1	# Harness: build spec
2	
3	**Text in, architecture out.** Harness is a diagram-first shell around real Claude Code. You talk to the agent in a chat pane; a domain × layer map of the target repo shows, live, what each turn plans and does to the architecture; and the agent stops to ask you before it crosses a rule. Decisions you make become rules that later sessions are checked against.
4	
5	The theme is giving people time back. Agents made writing code nearly free, but understanding and checking it did not get cheaper. Every feature below exists to cut reading, rework or re-explaining, and the time ledger counts those savings.
6	
7	## 1. Repos
8	
9	Two separate git repos, side by side:
10	
11	```
12	workspace/
13	  harness/        this tool (npm workspaces monorepo)
14	  scout-agent/    the demo target, built separately from DEMO_REPO_SPEC.md
15	```
16	
17	The target must be its own repo. The coding agent runs with its working directory there, the map is computed over it, and `domains.yaml` plus `decisions/` are committed into it. The tool's own code must never appear on the map.
18	
19	```
20	harness/
21	  package.json              npm workspaces
22	  packages/core/            pure TypeScript, no I/O beyond fs reads; fully unit-tested
23	    src/schema.ts           zod schema for domains.yaml
24	    src/events.ts           event types and the reducer
25	    src/mapper.ts           path → cell, table → owner
26	    src/imports.ts          regex import parser + relative-path resolver
27	    src/writes.ts           db.insert / db.update scanner
28	    src/facts.ts            whole-repo scan: files, imports, writes, cross-domain edges
29	    src/rules.ts            the invariant checker (one function, three call sites)
30	    src/plan.ts             plan → ghost footprint
31	    src/ledger.ts           per-turn and session counters
32	    test/                   uses fixtures/scout-agent.domains.yaml
33	  apps/server/              Node + Hono + ws + @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk
34	    src/index.ts            HTTP + websocket; serves the shell in production
35	    src/bus.ts              append-only event log (.harness/events.jsonl in the target) + broadcast
36	    src/repo.ts             load, full scan, file watcher
37	    src/session.ts          the coding session (streaming input, modes, hooks, canUseTool)
38	    src/harness-tools.ts    in-process MCP server: submit_plan, cell_for, domain, who_writes, decisions_for
39	    src/turns.ts            turn lifecycle, git baselines, turn records
40	    src/decisions.ts        decisions/DR-n.md, invariant updates, Alike instructions
41	    src/cartographer.ts     one-shot map proposal
42	  apps/shell/               Vite + React + Zustand
43	  fixtures/scout-agent.domains.yaml
44	```
45	
46	Run: `HARNESS_REPO=../scout-agent npm run dev` (server on 4310, shell on 5173).
47	
48	## 2. Hard rules
49	
50	1. **No model calls in the hot path.** Hooks, the mapper, the import parser and the rule checker are deterministic and fast. Model calls (the cartographer) never block the coding session.
51	2. **Every piece of UI state is a pure reduction of the event log.** Footprint, ghosts, ledger, summary, provenance and replay are all `reduce(events)`. Replay is "reduce up to index i".
52	3. **Harness writes to the target repo only in three places:** `domains.yaml`, `decisions/`, `.harness/` (gitignored). The coding session is the only thing that edits product code.
53	4. **Facts win on structure, the user wins on meaning, the agent wins only on stated intent**, and intent is always checked against facts.
54	
55	## 3. The map (`domains.yaml`)
56	
57	Schema: see `fixtures/scout-agent.domains.yaml`. Domains are columns, layers are rows (rows come from the file, not hard-coded). Each cell lists path globs and, for data cells, owned tables. `neutral` paths never create edges; `ignore` paths are skipped. Files that match no cell land in an **Unassigned** column.
58	
59	**Edges are derived, never declared.** A cross-domain edge exists when a file in domain A imports a file in domain B. Flow down a column is implied and not drawn. The import parser handles `import … from '…'`, `import('…')` and `export … from '…'`, resolves relative paths with `.ts`, `.tsx`, `/index.ts` fallbacks, and ignores bare package imports (Scout has none that matter).
60	
61	**Writes:** a regex scan for `db.insert("<table>"` and `db.update("<table>"` gives `{file, table}` pairs.
62	
63	## 4. Invariants: one checker, three call sites
64	
65	```ts
66	type Violation = { invariant: string; reason: string; file: string; detail: string; options: [string, string] };
67	function check(map: DomainMap, delta: FactDelta): Violation[];
68	```
69	
70	`FactDelta` is a set of added imports and added writes, each with its source file. The three kinds:
71	
72	| Kind | Fires when |
73	| --- | --- |
74	| `only_via` | a file outside `allowed_from` domains imports a `targets` path |
75	| `owns_writes` | a file outside the owner domain writes the table |
76	| `no_edge` | a file in `from` imports a file in `to` |
77	
78	Exceptions (paths) suppress a violation. Each violation carries two options: **A** comply (for `only_via` on Scout: "route through `gateway.complete()`"), **B** add an exception for this path and record why.
79	
80	The three call sites, all using the same function:
81	
82	1. **Load:** full repo scan. On Scout, finds exactly one: DR-1 in `src/tools/news-summarize.ts`. It shows red on load.
83	2. **Plan:** run on the declared dependencies and files in `submit_plan`.
84	3. **Edit:** run in the `PreToolUse` hook on the imports and writes that the edit would add (diff the `new_string`/`content` against the current file).
85	
86	## 5. Events
87	
88	```ts
89	type HarnessEvent = {
90	  id: string; t: number;
91	  session: string;          // coding session id
92	  turn: string | null;
93	  kind:
94	    | 'repo_scanned' | 'map_proposed' | 'map_confirmed' | 'file_assigned'
95	    | 'violation_found'
96	    | 'turn_started' | 'looked' | 'cursor'
97	    | 'planned' | 'plan_violation' | 'fork_asked' | 'fork_answered' | 'plan_approved'
98	    | 'gate_blocked' | 'edited' | 'edge_added' | 'edge_removed'
99	    | 'test_result' | 'decision_recorded' | 'turn_ended';
100	  cell?: { domain: string; layer: string };
101	  path?: string;
102	  data?: Record<string, unknown>;   // e.g. { step: 2 }, { added: 18, removed: 2 }, { invariant: 'DR-1' }
103	};
104	```
105	
106	The server appends every event to `.harness/events.jsonl` and broadcasts it over the websocket. The shell holds the array and derives everything from it.
107	
108	## 6. The coding session
109	
110	One long-lived streaming session:
111	
112	```ts
113	query({
114	  prompt: chatMessages(),                     // AsyncIterable<SDKUserMessage> fed by the chat pane
115	  options: {
116	    cwd: REPO,
117	    permissionMode: 'plan',
118	    systemPrompt: { type: 'preset', preset: 'claude_code', append: brief() },
119	    mcpServers: { harness: harnessTools },    // createSdkMcpServer; user-scope MCP servers (Alike) still load
120	    allowedTools: ['mcp__harness__*', 'mcp__alike__record_decision', 'mcp__alike__resolve_work_item', 'mcp__alike__describe_entity_kind'],
121	    hooks: { PreToolUse: [...], PostToolUse: [...] },
122	    canUseTool,                                // intercepts ExitPlanMode for approval
123	  },
124	});
125	```
126	
127	**`brief()`** contains: the map (domains, purposes, cell paths), active invariants, standing decisions from `decisions/`, and these rules:
128	
129	> Before editing anything, call `mcp__harness__submit_plan` with numbered steps. Each step lists the exact file paths it will create or modify and any new imports it adds (from path → to path). If the result contains violations, stop and ask the user to choose between the two options it gives, in one short message, then wait. Never work around a violation. After the user answers, resubmit the plan, then exit plan mode.
130	
131	**Turn flow:**
132	
133	1. User message → `turn_started` (record `git rev-parse HEAD` and a `git stash create` snapshot as the baseline).
134	2. Plan mode: Claude reads (`looked`, `cursor`), then calls `submit_plan`. The server maps paths to cells, builds ghost cells and ghost edges, and runs the checker → `planned` (+ `plan_violation`). The tool result returns the ghost summary and, if violated, the reason plus options A/B with an instruction to ask.
135	3. Claude asks → `fork_asked`. The user answers in chat → `fork_answered` → decision written (§8). Claude resubmits.
136	4. Claude calls `ExitPlanMode` → `canUseTool` holds it, the shell shows an **Approve plan** button (typing "approve" also works) → `plan_approved` → allow, then `session.setPermissionMode('acceptEdits')`.
137	5. Edits: hooks emit `cursor`, `gate_blocked`, `edited`, `edge_added` / `edge_removed`. Ghost cells fill as their files are edited; the step counter advances.
138	6. Result message → `turn_ended` with the plan-versus-built diff and git `--numstat` totals; write `.harness/turns/<id>.json`; `setPermissionMode('plan')` for the next turn.
139	
140	**Hooks:**
141	
142	| Hook | Matcher | Does | Blocking |
143	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
144	| PreToolUse | `Read\|Grep\|Glob` | `looked` + `cursor` for the file or search path | no (return `{ async: true }`) |
145	| PreToolUse | `Edit\|Write\|MultiEdit` | run the checker on the added imports/writes; on a hit return `permissionDecision: 'deny'` with the reason, options and "ask the user"; emit `gate_blocked` | yes, deterministic, < 20 ms |
146	| PostToolUse | `Edit\|Write\|MultiEdit` | `edited` (+/− lines), recompute that file's imports → edge events | no |
147	| PostToolUse | `Bash` | if the command ran `vitest`, parse results → `test_result` per test domain (stretch) | no |
148	
149	**File watcher** (chokidar on the target, minus `ignore`): any write not already reported by a hook becomes an `edited` event marked `unattributed`. Hooks give attribution and gating; the watcher guarantees completeness, since shell commands can write files without passing through the edit hooks.
150	
151	**Harness MCP tools** (all read-only except `submit_plan`, which only records intent): `submit_plan(steps[{ n, text, files[], imports[{ from, to }] }])`, `cell_for(path)`, `domain(id)`, `who_writes(table)`, `decisions_for(paths[])`.
152	
153	## 7. Plan versus built
154	
155	- **Ghosts:** planned cells are drawn dashed with their step numbers; planned edges are dashed; a ghost that violates an invariant is red.
156	- **Fill-in:** a ghost cell turns solid when a file mapped to it is edited.
157	- **End-of-turn diff:** planned and done is solid; planned and not done stays a ghost; **done but not planned is amber**, which is how the map shows the agent straying from its own plan.
158	
159	## 8. Design memory
160	
161	When a fork is answered:
162	
163	1. Write `decisions/DR-<n>.md` with front matter `{ id, title, outcome, status: made, type: standing, invariant, anchors: { paths }, rejected: "<option B text>" }` and a short rationale body.
164	2. Update `domains.yaml`: link the decision to the invariant (option A), or add the path to the invariant's `exceptions` with the DR id (option B). Commit both files.
165	3. Tell Claude, in the next tool result, to record it in Alike with `mcp__alike__record_decision`: title, outcome, rationale (including the rejected option), type `standing`, and code anchors `{ repository, branch, paths }`. Once at session start, have Claude run Alike's `describe_entity_kind` on `decision` to confirm the field names. Emit `decision_recorded` when the call succeeds.
166	
167	Memory is then used three ways:
168	
169	- **Provenance:** clicking an edge or cell shows the decisions and turns behind it ("added in turn 3, DR-4").
170	- **Session brief:** standing decisions on in-scope cells go into `brief()` for every new session.
171	- **Rejected options stay rejected:** when a plan or edit hits an invariant that has a linked decision, the violation reason says "You decided this in DR-4: <title>," and the ledger counts it as a rejected option blocked.
172	
173	## 9. Time ledger and turn summary
174	
175	Counts only; minutes appear only in the pitch, taken from the baseline run (§12).
176	
177	| Counter | Definition |
178	| --- | --- |
179	| Lines changed | git `--numstat` added + removed, turn baseline → turn end |
180	| Cells to review | cells with a finding of severity 1–3 below |
181	| Forks caught before code | `plan_violation` events resolved before any `edited` event in the turn |
182	| Rejected options blocked | violations that cited an existing decision |
183	
184	Severity for the turn summary, loudest first: **1** invariant hit (red) · **2** new cross-domain edge or new external (amber, one glance) · **3** unplanned edit (amber) · **4** everything else in the plan (quiet).
185	
186	## 10. Load and the cartographer
187	
188	1. `repo_scanned`: full fact scan (§3).
189	2. If `domains.yaml` is missing, run the **cartographer**: a separate one-shot `query()` with read-only tools, a smaller model, and `outputFormat` set to the `domains.yaml` JSON schema. Input: the file tree, the import edges and the table writes. Ask it for 5–9 domains in product language, layers suited to the repo, and invariants it can infer from the facts (sole importers of a vendor, sole writers of a table, absent edges). → `map_proposed`.
190	3. The shell plays the map assembling (`file_assigned` events, staggered about 15 ms apart) and shows the proposal; the user clicks **Confirm** → `map_confirmed`, file written. If the proposal is off, load `fixtures/scout-agent.domains.yaml` instead.
191	4. Full rule scan → `violation_found` (Scout: DR-1 in `news-summarize.ts`, red).
192	
193	## 11. The shell
194	
195	- **Layout:** chat pane on the left (380 px); the grid fills the rest; the turn summary and replay scrubber sit under the grid; the ledger sits top right. The mockups are in Figma, "v2 · Domain grid" page.
196	- **Cell states:** looked = dashed indigo outline · edited = indigo fill · unplanned = amber · invariant hit = red · ghost = dashed outline at 50% opacity with step badges.
197	- **Agent cursor:** a small avatar pinned to the current cell, labeled "Claude · reading `retrieve.ts`", easing between cells in 250 ms.
198	- **Edges:** SVG overlay routed through the gaps between cells; new edges draw in with a stroke-dashoffset animation.
199	- **Diff counts:** a +/− badge on each edited cell, ticking up.
200	- **Inspector:** click a cell or edge to see its paths, tables, invariants and provenance.
201	- **Replay:** a scrubber over the event index; dragging re-reduces the log.
202	- **Motion rule:** animate only state changes; nothing loops.
203	
204	## 12. Baseline run, for the pitch
205	
206	Copy `scout-agent` at the demo commit. In plain Claude Code, run "Add a tool that summarizes a prospect's latest 10-K." Time it, then run `npm run proof`. If the new tool leaks personal data, time a follow-up turn that finds and fixes it. Those minutes are the "without" numbers the pitch converts the ledger into. If the baseline doesn't make the mistake, drop that comparison and lean on lines-to-review and memory.

````text
1	# Scout: demo codebase spec
2	
3	Build a small but realistic agentic product called **Scout**, in its own git repo named `scout-agent`. It is the demo subject for a separate architecture-observability tool, so its **structure, tests and git history matter more than polish**. It should read like a product that a team built over a couple of weeks of ordinary agent-assisted work.
4	
5	**Never mention** the observability tool, invariants, rules, "planted", "violation" or "demo" anywhere in code, comments, commit messages or the README.
6	
7	## The product
8	
9	Scout is a B2B sales research agent. Given a prospect company, a contact and a goal, it:
10	
11	1. researches the company (web search, profile enrichment, recent news, SEC filings),
12	2. stores notes in memory and retrieves past notes about the same company,
13	3. writes a short research brief with a language model,
14	4. syncs the contact to the CRM and drafts an outreach email (optionally sends it).
15	
16	## Tech constraints
17	
18	- TypeScript, Node 22, ESM. Run with `tsx`. Test with `vitest`.
19	- **No network, no API keys, no native modules, no database server.** Everything runs offline and deterministically.
20	- **Relative imports only.** No path aliases, no barrel files that re-export `vendor/` modules. Each file imports a vendor module by its direct path.
21	- Target size: **2,500–3,500 lines** across `src/`, `vendor/` and `scripts/`, excluding fixtures and the lockfile.
22	- Storage is a tiny in-memory store with JSON snapshot, in `src/shared/db.ts`. **Every write goes through `db.insert("<table>", row)` or `db.update("<table>", id, patch)` with the table name as a string literal**, so writes are greppable.
23	
24	## Directory layout (follow exactly)
25	
26	```
27	scout-agent/
28	  package.json  tsconfig.json  vitest.config.ts  README.md  .gitignore
29	  vendor/                         fake external services, in-process
30	    _calllog.ts                   in-memory log of every vendor call: { vendor, method, payload, ts }
31	    llm-openai/index.ts           fake OpenAI-style chat client
32	    llm-anthropic/index.ts        fake Anthropic-style messages client
33	    embeddings/index.ts           fake embeddings (deterministic hash vectors)
34	    search/index.ts               fake web search
35	    news/index.ts                 fake news API
36	    sec-edgar/index.ts            fake SEC filings API (returns 10-K text from fixtures)
37	    enrichment/index.ts           fake company/person enrichment
38	    crm/index.ts                  fake HubSpot-style CRM
39	    email/index.ts                fake SendGrid-style email
40	  fixtures/                       canned JSON/text responses, keyed by input
41	  src/
42	    shared/      db.ts  config.ts  logger.ts  types.ts  ids.ts
43	    channels/    routes.ts (node:http server)  webhook.ts  cli.ts  validate.ts
44	    orchestrator/ agent.ts (run loop)  planner.ts  tool-registry.ts  run-state.ts
45	    tools/       index.ts  web-search.ts  company-profile.ts  news-digest.ts  news-summarize.ts
46	    gateway/     complete.ts  embed.ts  redact.ts  cost-ledger.ts  providers.ts
47	    memory/      notes-store.ts  vector-index.ts  retrieve.ts
48	    outreach/    draft-email.ts  crm-sync.ts  send.ts  outreach-log.ts
49	  scripts/       proof.ts  seed.ts
50	  test/          channels/  orchestrator/  tools/  gateway/  memory/  outreach/
51	```
52	
53	## Tables and their owners
54	
55	| Table | Written only from |
56	| --- | --- |
57	| `runs` | `src/orchestrator/` |
58	| `cost_log` | `src/gateway/` |
59	| `notes`, `embeddings` | `src/memory/` |
60	| `contacts`, `outreach_log` | `src/outreach/` |
61	
62	## How the parts fit
63	
64	- **Gateway** (`src/gateway/`): the only intended path to models. `complete({ purpose, messages })` redacts emails, phone numbers and known contact names (from `contacts`) into tokens like `[EMAIL_1]`, sends to `vendor/llm-openai`, falls back to `vendor/llm-anthropic` when the fake returns a 429 (deterministically: any prompt containing `#fallback`), and appends a row to `cost_log` (tokens = characters / 4, fixed price table). `embed(text)` wraps `vendor/embeddings` the same way.
65	- **Tools** (`src/tools/`): each tool is registered in `tool-registry.ts` as `{ name, tags, description, run(input, ctx) }`. Tools only read. They use their vendors directly (search, news, sec-edgar, enrichment) and call models through the gateway. `tools/index.ts` registers them all.
66	- **Orchestrator** (`src/orchestrator/`): a simple loop of at most 6 steps. The planner calls `gateway.complete` to pick tools (the fake model's canned answer is fine), and also selects every registered tool whose `tags` match keywords in the goal. Run state goes to `runs`.
67	- **Memory** (`src/memory/`): stores notes per company, indexes them with `gateway.embed`, retrieves the top 3 for the brief.
68	- **Outreach** (`src/outreach/`): drafts an email via the gateway, upserts the contact in the fake CRM, writes `contacts` and `outreach_log`, and sends via the fake email vendor only when `send: true`.
69	- **Channels** (`src/channels/`): `POST /runs` and a webhook endpoint on `node:http`, plus a CLI (`npm run scout -- --company Acme --contact jane@acme.com --goal "..."`). Validation lives in `validate.ts`.
70	
71	Every fake vendor returns deterministic output from `fixtures/` (keyed by a hash of the input, with a generic default) and appends to `vendor/_calllog.ts`.
72	
73	## Architecture rules the code follows
74	
75	The code follows all of these, **with exactly one exception**:
76	
77	1. Only `src/gateway/**` imports `vendor/llm-*` or `vendor/embeddings`.
78	2. Each table is written only by its owner (table above).
79	3. `src/tools/**` never imports `src/outreach/**`.
80	
81	**The one exception:** `src/tools/news-summarize.ts` imports `vendor/llm-openai` directly and calls it with the raw news text and contact context, with no redaction and no cost logging. It must look like an ordinary, slightly hurried feature, not a bug: no comment, no TODO. Register it with tags `["news", "summary"]`.
82	
83	This matters for the demo: later, an agent is asked to "add a tool that summarizes a prospect's latest 10-K," and `news-summarize.ts` is the nearest example to copy.
84	
85	## Proof script (`npm run proof`)
86	
87	- Runs the 20 requests in `fixtures/proof-requests.json` through the agent. Their contacts and goals contain personal data (emails, phone numbers, contact names), and goals mention news, filings and annual reports.
88	- Then, for each request, also invokes **every registered tool directly** once with that request's input, so any tool added later is exercised without editing the script.
89	- Reads the vendor call log and prints a large banner:
90	  - `PII reaching model providers: N of M model calls`
91	  - `Model calls missing from the cost log: K`
92	- With the exception above present, **N > 0**, all coming from `news-summarize`. A tool added later that routes through the gateway adds 0.
93	- Exit code 0 regardless; this is a report, not a test.
94	
95	## Tests
96	
97	`vitest`, 2–4 tests per domain under `test/<domain>/`, about 20 in total, all passing in under 5 seconds. Each test file imports only from its own domain plus `shared` and `vendor`, so a test maps cleanly to one domain.
98	
99	## Git history
100	
101	Initialize a repo and commit in about 12 steps that read like real feature work, using conventional commit messages, in this order: scaffold → shared → vendor fakes and fixtures → gateway → memory → tools (search, profile, news digest) → orchestrator → channels → outreach → tests → proof script → finally `feat(tools): summarize recent news for the brief` (the exception) as the last commit.
102	
103	## README
104	
105	Product description, how to run (`npm i`, `npm run dev`, `npm test`, `npm run proof`, the CLI), a folder overview, and a short "Adding a tool" section that explains the registry and tags and says "see `src/tools/` for examples." Do **not** describe the architecture rules.
106	
107	## Acceptance checks
108	
109	- [ ] `npm i && npm test` passes offline.
110	- [ ] `npm run proof` prints the banner with N > 0, and every leaking call comes from `news-summarize`.
111	- [ ] Imports of `vendor/llm-` or `vendor/embeddings` outside `src/gateway/` appear in **exactly one file**: `src/tools/news-summarize.ts`.
112	- [ ] Every `db.insert(` / `db.update(` table literal matches its owner directory.
113	- [ ] No file in `src/tools/` imports from `src/outreach/`.
114	- [ ] 2,500–3,500 lines in `src/`, `vendor/`, `scripts/`.
115	- [ ] None of the forbidden words appear in code, comments, commits or the README.
116	- [ ] `git log --oneline` shows about 12 feature commits, with the news summarizer last.

6	
7	**For the build, two specs are the source of truth as of Oct 11:** `SPEC.md` (the harness) and `DEMO_REPO_SPEC.md` (Scout, the demo repo). This doc keeps the reasoning behind them.

10

37	
38	## Idea and selling point
39	
40	You keep talking to your coding agent in text; a live map of your product shows what each turn did to its architecture, and the agent stops before crossing a line you drew.
41	
42	**One-liner:** Text in, architecture out.
43	
44	**Contrast line:** Graphify gives the agent a map of your code; this gives you a map of what the agent is doing to it.
45	
46	**The bottleneck (theme: give people their time back).** Agents now change code faster than people can follow. The time goes to re-reading diffs, re-explaining context, and untangling structure that drifted while nobody was looking. Chat shows what the agent said, not what it did to your system.
47	
48	**Thesis.** Chat is the right input and the wrong output. Text has no skill tax, so it stays the way you give instructions. But a transcript can't show you that a change you asked for in Checkout also touched Accounts. The human's role has shifted from author to supervisor, and a supervisor needs a map, not a log.
49	
50	**Time.** Before AI tools, professional developers already spent about 58% of their time on program comprehension ([Xia et al., IEEE TSE 2018](https://ink.library.smu.edu.sg/sis_research/3779)). In METR's 2025 trial, experienced open-source developers using AI took 19% longer and still believed they had been sped up; the time went to prompting, reviewing and integrating ([InfoQ](https://www.infoq.com/news/2025/07/ai-productivity)). The product removes three time sinks: reading diffs to see what changed (the footprint), redoing work after a wrong direction is found (the fork before code), and re-explaining decisions to each new session (design memory).
51	
52	**What makes it different**
53	
54	- **It observes the agent, not the codebase.** Static maps (Graphify, DeepWiki) describe code. This shows each turn's footprint, where the agent looked, and how far it strayed from what you asked.
55	- **Exception-driven.** Quiet when a turn stays in its stripe; loud on new coupling, writes into another domain's data, or edits outside scope.
56	- **Readable by anyone.** Boxes are named in product language (Checkout, Seat inventory) with the code underneath.
57	- **Works with the agent you already use.** Real Claude Code runs underneath; adapters for Cursor and Codex come later.
58	
59	**Pitch lines:** "Chat is the right input and the wrong output." · "A normal change is a vertical stripe. Sideways spread is news."
60	
61	## What the human does
62	
63	The human supervises instead of authoring: four cheap actions, none of which need architectural vocabulary. Every instruction still goes through chat; there is no gesture grammar.
64	
65	- **Point.** Click cells to make them nouns in your next message ("make these two stop talking"). Text is good at saying what you want and bad at saying which thing.
66	- **Judge.** Each turn ends with its footprint and a ranked summary. Approve or push back in chat.
67	- **Fence.** Mark a scope or a "don't touch" cell. The gate enforces it.
68	- **Interrupt.** See the agent wander into another domain and stop it before it writes code.
69	
70	### What a block represents
71	
72	A block is the smallest unit you'd have an opinion about: columns are product domains, rows are layers, so a normal change is a vertical stripe and sideways spread is news.
73	
74	- **Size test:** 5–9 domains on screen, and a typical turn lights up 1–3 cells. If every turn lights everything, the map carries no signal; if there are 40 boxes, nobody reads it.
75	- **Why not layers:** Web, API and DB boxes light up on every feature. Quick-buy lit 3 of 3 in the first mockup.
76	- **Naming:** product language on the box; files and endpoints live in the inspector.
77	- **Depth is local:** you only see deeper wiring inside the thing you zoomed into, never the whole system at class level. Files appear only as evidence on what a turn touched. See the levels below.
78	- **Edges:** only edges between domains are drawn. Flow down a column is implied.
79	
80	Scout, the demo repo (rows are read from the map, so an agent system gets Entry / Logic / Data / External):
81	
82	|  | Channels | Agent loop | Research tools | Model gateway | Memory | Outreach |
83	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
84	| Entry | HTTP, webhook, CLI | — | — | — | — | — |
85	| Logic | Validation | Run loop, planner, tool registry | Search, profile, news digest, news summary | complete(), embed(), redaction, fallback | Retrieval, vector index | Draft email, send |
86	| Data | — | runs | — | cost\_log | notes, embeddings | contacts, outreach\_log |
87	| External | — | — | Search, News, SEC EDGAR, Enrichment | OpenAI, Anthropic, Embeddings | — | CRM, Email |
88	
89	### Levels of abstraction
90	
91	Five levels, each a rollup of the same fact graph, and the agent's footprint carries through all of them: an edited cell is an edited endpoint is an edited function.
92	
93	| Level | Shows | Built from |
94	| --- | --- | --- |
95	| Journeys | A user flow such as "buy a ticket" as a path across domains | Routes and UI entry points traced through the fact graph, named by the cartographer |
96	| Domains | The domain × layer grid | `domains.yaml` mapping over the fact graph |
97	| Inside a domain | Endpoints, tables, jobs | Parsed routes, the Prisma schema, job config |
98	| Wiring | One call chain across cells, e.g. EventCard → POST /orders/quick → reserve() → prisma.seat.update | Graphify's symbol graph, drawn as a trace; calls leaving the component are stubs labeled with their cell |
99	| Code | The file itself | — |
100	
101	The wiring level is a trace rather than a full class graph because the question people have at that depth is "how does this get there?" Sunday ships Domains and Inside a domain; Journeys and the wiring trace are stretch.
102	
103	### Signals, loudest first
104	
105	1. A new dependency between domains (new coupling).
106	2. A write into data another domain owns (the invariant case).
107	3. Edits outside the domains the request named, or outside the agent's own plan.
108	4. A new external service or package.
109	5. Edits inside the requested stripe, which stay quiet.
110	
111	Cell states on the map: looked at (dashed), edited (filled), edited outside scope (amber), touches an invariant (red). Mockups: [Figma, v2 page](https://www.figma.com/design/PsNVwSXxGSerMVsNnbomKu).
112	
113	## What the agent gets
114	
115	The agent is ordinary Claude Code. The harness adds the domain map as context, observes every tool call, and gates edits that cross an invariant.
116	
117	- **Context, once per session.** The domain map and invariants are appended to Claude Code's system prompt. Scope is inferred from each prompt in the background for the canvas; it never delays the agent.
118	- **Plan.** Each turn starts in plan mode: the agent explores read-only, then calls `submit_plan` with the cells it will touch, the edges it will add, and numbered steps. Invariant checks run on the plan, so a fork surfaces before any code exists.
119	- **Graph tools (read-only MCP).** `cell_for(path)`, `domain(id)` (cells, invariants, files) and `who_writes(table)`, so the agent can check ownership while planning.
120	- **Observe.** Hooks on Read, Grep and Glob mark cells as looked at and move the agent cursor. Hooks after Edit and Write fill cells and recompute that file's cross-domain imports. These hooks return async, so they never slow the agent.
121	- **Gate (the backstop).** A pre-edit hook runs the same deterministic checks during editing: writes into data another domain owns, new imports across domains, edits outside a fence. On a hit it returns `permissionDecision: "deny"` with a reason that names the options and tells Claude to ask you.
122	- **Record.** Each answered fork becomes a decision (DR-n) in `decisions/` and in Alike, so later sessions inherit it.
123	
124	## Plan versus built
125	
126	Planning and implementation share one map: the plan draws a ghost footprint, edits fill it in, and anything done without being planned shows amber.
127	
128	- **Plan.** Claude Code's plan mode explores without editing. `submit_plan` returns cells, edges and steps, drawn as dashed ghosts with step numbers. A ghost that crosses an invariant is red, and the agent asks you A or B before writing any code.
129	- **Approve.** You approve in chat, and the session switches from plan mode to editing.
130	- **Build.** As edits land, ghost cells fill solid and the step counter advances. That's progress, laid out on the architecture.
131	- **End-of-turn diff.** This is the overfitting detector: it shows when the agent strays from its own plan.
132	
133	|  | Planned | Not planned |
134	| --- | --- | --- |
135	| Done | Solid | Amber: did something it didn't say it would |
136	| Not done | Ghost stays | — |
137	
138	## Live activity
139	
140	Every visual here comes from the same hook event stream, so each one is cheap once events flow. Each motion encodes a state change; nothing loops for decoration.
141	
142	- **Agent cursor.** An avatar sits on the cell the agent is reading or editing and moves with it, like a collaborator's cursor in Figma. Teammates' agents later become more cursors.
143	- **Fill-in progress.** Ghosts fill as steps complete, with a step counter ("3 of 6").
144	- **Live diff counts.** Lines added and removed tick up on each cell.
145	- **Edge draw-in.** A new cross-domain edge draws itself when the import appears.
146	- **Tests on the map.** When the agent runs tests, the cells they cover flash green or red.
147	- **Replay scrubber.** Every event is logged, so you can scrub a turn to watch it again or catch up on what happened while you were away.
148	
149	Priority for Sunday: cursor and pulse, then plan ghosts with the drift diff, then replay, then edge draw-in. Tests on cells and the wiring trace are stretch.
150	
151	## Who maintains the graph
152	
153	Three owners, split by the kind of knowledge each layer needs.
154	
155	| Layer | Holds | Updated by | When |
156	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
157	| Facts | Files, symbols, imports, calls, table writes | Code: Graphify or tree-sitter, an import scan, an ORM scan. No LLM | Every edit, incrementally; full check at commit |
158	| Meaning | Domains, names, purposes, journeys, invariants | A cartographer agent, async. It proposes, you confirm | At setup, then on drift triggers |
159	| Intent | Plans, decisions | The coding agent (`submit_plan`) and you (your answers) | Every turn |
160	
161	- **Levels are rollups.** One fact graph plus one mapping (`domains.yaml`); every level is that graph aggregated through the mapping, so nothing is maintained twice. An agent is needed only when the mapping itself is wrong or incomplete.
162	- **Why not the coding agent.** It's the thing being observed, and a self-reported map drifts. Bookkeeping also costs its context and gets skipped. Its only job is to state intent, which the facts then check.
163	- **Why not a parallel LLM for everything.** The parts that change on every edit are exactly what code computes precisely. An LLM there adds latency and cost, and makes the map flicker.
164	- **The cartographer.** A separate Agent SDK session with read-only tools and a cheaper model that never blocks the coding session. At setup it turns Graphify's communities and the folder structure into 5–9 proposed domains with names, purposes and suggested invariants. Drift triggers: files landing in Unassigned, a cell past a size limit, a dense new cluster of cross-domain edges. Each produces a proposal drawn as ghosts and accepted in chat, the same UI as plans.
165	- **Conflicts.** Facts win on structure, you win on meaning, and the agent wins only on intent, which is checked.
166	- **Sunday.** Facts run live; intent comes from `submit_plan`; the cartographer runs once for Scout, plus a "re-map" button. Drift triggers are a slide.
167	
168	### What Graphify does, and where we differ
169	
170	Graphify builds its graph when the skill is called (`/graphify .`), refreshes changed files with `--update`, and can rebuild on commit and branch checkout through git hooks. Its agent hooks don't update the graph; they fire before searches and file reads to steer the agent toward querying the graph instead. Nodes are symbols linked by calls, imports and inheritance, clustered into communities, with no hierarchy or zoom. A PR tool flags pull requests that touch the same community.
171	
172	So Graphify is a commit-time snapshot built for agent retrieval. We use it as the fact extractor for the wiring level and the domain proposal. The gap we fill is live, per-turn, plan-versus-built, and layered for humans.
173	
174	## Architecture
175	
176	Own the shell, borrow the harness: a diagram-first web app whose chat pane drives real Claude Code through the Agent SDK, with a local graph server in between that watches and gates every tool call.
177	
178	&#91;embedded content: architecture · shell, graph server, Claude Code\]
179	
180	Your chat goes through the graph server to Claude Code, and every tool call Claude makes comes back through it. That's how the grid updates live and how the gate can stop an edit, without anyone rebuilding the agent.
181	
182	### The pieces
183	
184	- **Shell (web app).** The grid takes two-thirds of the screen, the chat pane the rest, with the turn summary and replay scrubber under the grid. It's the only window you need.
185	- **Graph server (the product core).** Holds `domains.yaml`, a path → cell index, cross-domain edges and invariant checks, the plan overlay, the per-turn footprint and the event log. Pushes every change to the shell over a websocket.
186	- **Claude Code via the Agent SDK.** Your agent, unchanged: same loop, tools, login, CLAUDE.md and settings. The server adds hooks, a small MCP server, and plan mode at the start of each turn.
187	- **Cartographer.** A second, read-only SDK session on a cheaper model that proposes domains and map changes. It never blocks the coding session.
188	- **Graphify.** The fact extractor for symbols and calls, run at setup and on commit. Its `graph.json` feeds the wiring level and the cartographer.
189	- **Repo.** `domains.yaml`, `decisions/DR-*.md`, Graphify's output, and the source.
190	
191	This is not a new harness. The expensive part, the agent, stays Claude Code; only the window around it is ours.
192	
193	### Latency: fast path and slow path
194	
195	The graph is never the slow part as long as no model call sits in the blocking path.
196	
197	- **Fast path (synchronous, in hooks, deterministic):** map a path to a cell, re-read one file's imports, regex-check an edit against invariants. Milliseconds, so the grid updates before the agent's next step and the gate can block instantly.
198	- **Slow path (asynchronous, never blocks):** anything that needs a model. That's inferring scope from your prompt, which starts when you hit enter, and naming domains, which happens once at setup.
199	- The only intentional wait is when the gate stops the agent and asks you.
200	
201	### Representation
202	
203	One config file in the repo describes the map; everything else is derived from the code.
204	
205	```yaml
206	layers: [ui, api, data, jobs]
207	domains:
208	  - id: checkout
209	    name: Checkout
210	    purpose: Reserve seats, place orders
211	    cells:
212	      ui:   [apps/web/src/checkout/**]
213	      api:  [apps/api/src/orders/**]
214	      data: [seats, orders, holds]
215	      jobs: [apps/api/src/jobs/holds.ts]
216	    invariants:
217	      - id: DR-12
218	        rule: only Checkout writes seats
219	        check: { table: seats, writers: [checkout] }
220	```
221	
222	- **Domains:** the agent proposes them once when a repo loads, and you confirm. Unmapped files land in an "Unassigned" column.
223	- **Cells:** files map to cells by glob; tables by name.
224	- **Edges:** derived, not declared. Cross-domain imports come from an import-graph tool; table writes come from scanning ORM calls (Prisma, so writes are greppable).
225	- **Decisions:** `decisions/DR-*.md` in git, mirrored to Alike.
226	
227	### Stack
228	
229	| Layer | Choice | Why |
230	| --- | --- | --- |
231	| Shell | Vite + React + Zustand | Fast to scaffold |
232	| Grid | CSS grid + SVG overlay for edges | Fixed layout, so no graph layout engine |
233	| Motion | CSS transitions + SVG stroke animation | Agent cursor, fill-in, edge draw-in |
234	| Server | Node + Hono + `ws` | Holds graph, plan and turn state; logs events for replay |
235	| Per-edit facts | `dependency-cruiser` (or `madge`) + Prisma call scan | Deterministic imports and table writes in milliseconds |
236	| Commit-time facts | Graphify (`uv tool install graphifyy`) | Symbol graph across about 40 languages; communities seed domains |
237	| Agent | `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` | Real Claude Code: `query()`, plan mode, hooks, MCP |
238	| Cartographer | Second SDK session, read-only, smaller model | Proposes meaning without touching the coding session |
239	| Decisions | `decisions/*.md` + Alike MCP | In git and in every later session |
240	
241	### One turn, end to end
242	
243	1. You type in the chat pane. The server opens a turn and infers scope in the background; a scope band appears on the grid.
244	2. Claude starts in plan mode and reads. The agent cursor moves and cells are marked looked at. It submits a plan: ghost cells, ghost edges, numbered steps.
245	3. Invariant checks run on the plan. A ghost that crosses one turns red, and Claude asks you A or B in chat before writing code.
246	4. You answer and approve in text. The session switches to editing.
247	5. Edits fill ghosts solid, diff counts tick, and new imports draw in as edges. The gate stays armed for anything unplanned that crosses an invariant.
248	6. When the result message arrives: the plan-versus-built diff (amber for unplanned work), the ranked summary, a decision written to `decisions/` and Alike, and the turn joins the replay log.
249	
250	### Session wiring
251	
252	```ts
253	import { query, type HookCallback, type PreToolUseHookInput } from "@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk";
254	
255	const observeRead: HookCallback = async (input) => {
256	  graph.looked((input as PreToolUseHookInput).tool_input); // path → cell → shell
257	  return { async: true };                                  // never delays the agent
258	};
259	
260	const gate: HookCallback = async (input) => {
261	  const v = graph.check((input as PreToolUseHookInput).tool_input); // owned data, cross-domain import, fence
262	  if (!v) return {};
263	  shell.flag(v);
264	  return {
265	    hookSpecificOutput: {
266	      hookEventName: "PreToolUse",
267	      permissionDecision: "deny",
268	      permissionDecisionReason: `${v.reason}. Stop and ask the user to choose: ${v.options.join(" / ")}.`,
269	    },
270	  };
271	};
272	
273	const session = query({
274	  prompt: chatPane.messages(), // AsyncIterable<SDKUserMessage> fed by the chat pane
275	  options: {
276	    cwd: REPO,
277	    permissionMode: "plan",               // explore read-only, then call submit_plan
278	    planModeInstructions: PLAN_RULES,     // "submit cells, edges and steps before asking to edit"
279	    systemPrompt: { type: "preset", preset: "claude_code", append: graph.domainBrief() },
280	    mcpServers: { graph: graphTools },
281	    hooks: {
282	      PreToolUse: [
283	        { matcher: "Read|Grep|Glob", hooks: [observeRead] },
284	        { matcher: "Edit|Write", hooks: [gate] },
285	      ],
286	      PostToolUse: [{ matcher: "Edit|Write", hooks: [markEditedAndRecheckImports] }],

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-11 18:31:11Z)**_

Scout hasn't been built yet: `../scout-agent` doesn't exist. So everything below reviews the spec in `DEMO_REPO_SPEC.md` as written.

## What Scout does, per the spec

Scout is a fake B2B sales-research agent that runs fully offline on canned vendor responses:

```
channels (HTTP / webhook / CLI)
  → orchestrator: run loop, at most 6 steps; planner picks tools by tag keywords
    → tools: web-search, company-profile, news-digest, news-summarize
        → vendors: search / news / sec-edgar / enrichment
        → gateway.complete(): redacts PII, calls the OpenAI fake (Anthropic fake as fallback), logs cost
    → memory: stores notes, embeds them via the gateway, retrieves the top 3
    → outreach: drafts an email via the gateway, syncs the CRM, optionally sends
```

The deliberate fault is that `news-summarize.ts` calls `vendor/llm-openai` directly. `npm run proof` sends 20 requests containing personal data through the agent, then calls every registered tool directly. It prints how many model calls carried PII and how many are missing from the cost log, and attributes the leaks to that one file.

The parts that work well for us: the gateway rule is easy to grasp at a glance, the faulty file is the obvious one to copy for a "summarize X" tool, and the proof script automatically exercises any tool added later.

## Faults that matter for the demo

**1. The brief removes the reason to fork.** This is the biggest problem. SPEC §6 puts the active rules into Claude's system prompt, including "Model providers are only called through the model gateway." Three of the four existing tools already use the gateway. With that rule stated up front, Claude will almost certainly plan the 10-K tool through the gateway, and the red ghost and the A/B question never happen.

Even if the fork does fire, it's a fake choice. Option B is "keep leaking PII to the model provider", which nobody would pick. The fix is a genuine conflict that a rule in the prompt can't settle. For example, `redact.ts` uses a phone-number pattern that also mangles figures in a 10-K's financial tables (`(212) 555-0100` versus `$1,234,567`). Claude then has a real reason to ask:
- **A:** go through the gateway and add a filing-specific redaction mode.
- **B:** exempt filings, since they're public documents.

Both options are defensible. That also makes the decision recorded as DR-4 say something DR-1 doesn't already say, which fixes the weak memory beat in point 3.

**2. The new fault lands where the map already shows red.** The tools Logic cell is `src/tools/**`, so it's red from the moment Scout loads. The edge from tools to the gateway's External cell is already drawn too, because of `news-summarize`. So the plan's "new red ghost" lands on a red cell and repeats an existing edge, and the most important moment of the demo barely changes the picture. The grid needs a way to show a new violation as distinct from an old one: a file-level badge, a second edge lane, or a ghost style that overrides the red.

**3. The second-session prompt has no data source.** "Summarize earnings call transcripts" needs transcripts, and none of the vendors provide them. Claude would create `vendor/earnings/**`, which matches no cell, so it would land in the Unassigned column mid-demo. Either give the `news` or `sec-edgar` fake a transcripts endpoint, or change the prompt to one the existing vendors can serve, such as "summarize the latest 10-Q". On top of that, "session two didn't ask again" proves little when DR-1 alone already tells Claude what to do. Point 1's fix addresses this.

**4. Hidden edges the spec doesn't control.**
- **Gateway → outreach.** Redaction needs contact names from the `contacts` table. If the gateway gets them by importing `crm-sync.ts`, the model gateway depends on outreach, which is noise at best and a real code smell. Specify a read through `shared/db.ts`, which is neutral.
- **Tools ↔ orchestrator in both directions.** `tool-registry.ts` lives in the orchestrator, `tools/index.ts` imports it to register tools, and the orchestrator imports the tools back. That draws a two-way edge on every load. Moving the `Tool` type into `shared/` and having the orchestrator import the tool list makes it one way.

**5. Things that break "exactly one violation on load"** (from my earlier list):
- Tests are allowed to import `vendor/`, so a memory test that imports `vendor/embeddings` would trip DR-1.
- The resolver doesn't handle ESM `.js` import specifiers.
- The write regex only matches double quotes.

# Scout: demo codebase spec

Build a small but realistic agentic product called **Scout**, in its own git repo named `scout-agent`. It is the demo subject for a separate architecture-observability tool, so its **structure, tests and git history matter more than polish**. It should read like a product that a team built over a couple of weeks of ordinary agent-assisted work.

**Never mention** the observability tool, invariants, rules, "planted", "violation" or "demo" anywhere in code, comments, commit messages or the README.

## The product

Scout is a B2B sales research agent. Given a prospect company, a contact and a goal, it:

1. researches the company (web search, profile enrichment, recent news, SEC filings),
2. stores notes in memory and retrieves past notes about the same company,
3. writes a short research brief with a language model,
4. syncs the contact to the CRM and drafts an outreach email (optionally sends it).

## Tech constraints

- TypeScript, Node 22, ESM. Run with `tsx`. Test with `vitest`. `tsconfig.json` uses `"module": "esnext"` and `"moduleResolution": "bundler"`.
- **No network, no API keys, no native modules, no database server.** Everything runs offline and deterministically.
- **Relative imports only, written without a file extension** (`import { complete } from "../gateway/complete"`). No `.js` or `.ts` specifiers, no path aliases, no barrel files that re-export `vendor/` modules. Each file imports a vendor module by its direct path, including `index` (`../../vendor/llm-openai/index`).
- Target size: **2,500–3,500 lines** across `src/`, `vendor/` and `scripts/`, excluding fixtures and the lockfile.
- Storage is a tiny in-memory store with JSON snapshot, in `src/shared/db.ts`. **Every write goes through `db.insert("<table>", row)` or `db.update("<table>", id, patch)` with the table name as a double-quoted string literal**, so writes are greppable. Reads go through `db.get`, `db.all` and `db.find`, which any domain may call.

## Directory layout (follow exactly)

```
scout-agent/
  package.json  tsconfig.json  vitest.config.ts  README.md  .gitignore
  vendor/                         fake external services, in-process
    _calllog.ts                   in-memory log of every vendor call: { vendor, method, payload, ts }
    llm-openai/index.ts           fake OpenAI-style chat client (default provider)
    llm-anthropic/index.ts        fake Anthropic-style messages client (selected by config)
    embeddings/index.ts           fake embeddings (deterministic hash vectors)
    search/index.ts               fake web search
    news/index.ts                 fake news API: headlines and earnings call transcripts
    sec-edgar/index.ts            fake SEC filings API (10-K and 10-Q text from fixtures)
    enrichment/index.ts           fake company/person enrichment
    crm/index.ts                  fake HubSpot-style CRM
    email/index.ts                fake SendGrid-style email
  fixtures/                       canned JSON/text responses, keyed by input
  src/
    shared/      db.ts  config.ts  logger.ts  types.ts (incl. Tool, ToolContext)  ids.ts
    channels/    routes.ts (node:http server)  cli.ts  validate.ts
    orchestrator/ agent.ts (run loop)  planner.ts  tool-registry.ts  run-state.ts
    tools/       index.ts (the tool list)  web-search.ts  company-profile.ts  news-digest.ts  news-summarize.ts
    gateway/     complete.ts  embed.ts  redact.ts  cost-ledger.ts  providers.ts
    memory/      notes-store.ts  vector-index.ts  retrieve.ts
    outreach/    draft-email.ts  crm-sync.ts  send.ts  outreach-log.ts
  scripts/       proof.ts  seed.ts
  test/          channels/  orchestrator/  tools/  gateway/  memory/  outreach/
```

## Tables and their owners

| Table | Written only from |
| --- | --- |
| `runs` | `src/orchestrator/` |
| `cost_log` | `src/gateway/` |
| `notes`, `embeddings` | `src/memory/` |
| `contacts`, `outreach_log` | `src/outreach/` |

## How the parts fit

- **Gateway** (`src/gateway/`): the only intended path to models. `complete({ purpose, messages })`, where `purpose` is one of `"plan" | "profile" | "summary" | "brief" | "email"`, redacts emails, phone numbers and known contact names into tokens like `[EMAIL_1]`, sends to the provider chosen in `providers.ts` (`vendor/llm-openai` by default, `vendor/llm-anthropic` when `SCOUT_MODEL_PROVIDER=anthropic`), and appends a row to `cost_log` (tokens = characters / 4, fixed price table). Contact names come from `db.all("contacts")`; the gateway imports no other domain. `embed(text)` wraps `vendor/embeddings` the same way. No retries and no fallback between providers.
- **Redaction** (`src/gateway/redact.ts`): the phone pattern treats any run of seven or more digits separated by spaces, dots, dashes, commas or parentheses as a phone number. It catches every phone format in the fixtures, and it also turns full-precision figures such as `$4,512,300` into `$[PHONE_3]`. Every redaction applies to every purpose; there is no option to skip one. Nothing in the existing product checks figures: enrichment fixtures write money as `$4.5B`, and the gateway tests cover phone numbers, emails and names only.
- **Fake models** (`vendor/llm-*`): canned answers from fixtures, keyed by a hash of the prompt, for the prompts the product relies on (the planner's tool choice, email drafts). Any other prompt gets a deterministic extractive answer: the first three sentences of the last user message. Whatever the gateway sends is what comes back, tokens included.
- **Tools** (`src/tools/`): each tool is a `Tool` (`{ name, tags, description, run(input, ctx) }`, typed in `src/shared/types.ts`). `tools/index.ts` exports the list of all tools; tools never import the orchestrator. Tools only read. They use their vendors directly (search, news, sec-edgar, enrichment) and call models through the gateway. `news-digest` groups and formats headlines without a model call.
- **Orchestrator** (`src/orchestrator/`): `tool-registry.ts` imports the list from `../tools/index` and indexes it by name and tag. The run loop takes at most 6 steps. The planner calls `gateway.complete` with purpose `"plan"` to pick tools (the fake model's canned answer is fine), and also selects every registered tool whose `tags` match keywords in the goal. Run state goes to `runs`.
- **Memory** (`src/memory/`): stores notes per company, indexes them with `gateway.embed`, retrieves the top 3 for the brief.
- **Outreach** (`src/outreach/`): drafts an email via the gateway, upserts the contact in the fake CRM, writes `contacts` and `outreach_log`, and sends via the fake email vendor only when `send: true`.
- **Channels** (`src/channels/`): `POST /runs` on `node:http`, plus a CLI (`npm run scout -- --company Acme --contact jane@acme.com --goal "..."`). Validation lives in `validate.ts`.

Every fake vendor returns deterministic output from `fixtures/` (keyed by a hash of the input, with a generic default) and appends to `vendor/_calllog.ts`.

**Fixtures that later work depends on.** For each fixture company, `sec-edgar` has a 10-K and a 10-Q, each with an MD&A section and a financial table in full-precision figures. `news` has headlines that quote figures the same way, and one earnings call transcript (prepared remarks plus Q&A, with figures) that no tool uses yet.

## Architecture rules the code follows

The code follows all of these, **with exactly one exception**:

1. Only `src/gateway/**` imports `vendor/llm-*` or `vendor/embeddings`. In `test/`, only `test/gateway/**` does.
2. Each table is written only by its owner (table above).
3. `src/tools/**` never imports `src/outreach/**`.
4. Dependencies point one way: channels → orchestrator → tools, memory, outreach → gateway. Nothing imports `src/channels/`; tools, memory and outreach never import the orchestrator; the gateway imports no other domain.

**The one exception:** `src/tools/news-summarize.ts` imports `vendor/llm-openai/index` directly and calls it with the raw news text and contact context, with no redaction and no cost logging. It must look like an ordinary, slightly hurried feature, not a bug: no comment, no TODO. Register it with tags `["news", "summary"]`. Its commit message gives the reason in one line of body, the way a hurried developer would: "Call the model client directly so revenue and deal figures in headlines come through intact."

This matters for the demo. Later, an agent is asked to "add a tool that summarizes a prospect's latest 10-K," and `news-summarize.ts` is the nearest example to copy. Its shortcut has a real reason: a 10-K summarized through the gateway comes back with its figures replaced by tokens. So the agent faces a genuine choice between copying the shortcut and teaching the gateway about figures, which is real work in another domain, and both are reasonable to put to a person. A second request later asks for a tool that summarizes earnings call transcripts, which `vendor/news` already serves.

## Proof script (`npm run proof`)

- Runs the 20 requests in `fixtures/proof-requests.json` through the agent. Their contacts and goals contain personal data (emails, phone numbers, contact names), and goals mention news, filings and annual reports.
- Then, for each request, also invokes **every registered tool directly** once with that request's input, so any tool added later is exercised without editing the script.
- Reads the vendor call log and prints a large banner:
  - `PII reaching model providers: N of M model calls`
  - `Model calls missing from the cost log: K`
- With the exception above present, **N > 0**, all coming from `news-summarize`. A tool added later that routes through the gateway adds 0.
- Exit code 0 regardless; this is a report, not a test.

## Tests

`vitest`, 2–4 tests per domain under `test/<domain>/`, about 20 in total, all passing in under 5 seconds. Each test file imports only from its own domain plus `shared` and `vendor`, so a test maps cleanly to one domain. Only `test/gateway/` may import `vendor/llm-*` or `vendor/embeddings`; tests in other domains that need a model call go through the gateway.

## Git history

Initialize a repo and commit in about 12 steps that read like real feature work, using conventional commit messages, in this order: scaffold → shared → vendor fakes and fixtures → gateway → memory → tools (search, profile, news digest) → orchestrator → channels → outreach → tests → proof script → finally `feat(tools): summarize recent news for the brief` (the exception, with the one-line body above) as the last commit.

## README

Product description, how to run (`npm i`, `npm run dev`, `npm test`, `npm run proof`, the CLI), a folder overview, and a short "Adding a tool" section that explains the tool list in `src/tools/index.ts` and tags and says "see `src/tools/` for examples." Do **not** describe the architecture rules.

- [ ] `npm run proof` prints the banner with N > 0, and every leaking call comes from `news-summarize`.
- [ ] Imports of `vendor/llm-` or `vendor/embeddings` outside `src/gateway/` and `test/gateway/` appear in **exactly one file**: `src/tools/news-summarize.ts`.
- [ ] Every `db.insert(` / `db.update(` uses a double-quoted table literal that matches its owner directory.
- [ ] No file in `src/tools/` imports from `src/outreach/` or `src/orchestrator/`; no file in `src/gateway/` imports from another `src/` domain.
- [ ] Every relative import is extensionless; no `.js` specifiers anywhere.
- [ ] Passing a 10-K fixture through `complete()` returns text in which figures like `4,512,300` are replaced by `[PHONE_n]` tokens.
- [ ] `vendor/news` returns an earnings call transcript for each fixture company.
- [ ] 2,500–3,500 lines in `src/`, `vendor/`, `scripts/`.
- [ ] None of the forbidden words appear in code, comments, commits or the README.
- [ ] `git log --oneline` shows about 12 feature commits, with the news summarizer last.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-11 18:44:18Z)**_

Use the other agent. Splitting the work across two sessions is better than me running both, and the two jobs barely overlap.

**Split it this way:**
- **This session builds Scout** in `../scout-agent`. It's the smaller, fully specified job, and the harness needs it from step 5 on, as well as for the baseline run. Building it first gets it out of the way.
- **The fork builds the harness** in this repo, starting with the step 0 checks (now including the Alike hooks question). It can get through steps 0–4 against the small copy of Scout in `packages/core/test/fixture-repo/` without waiting for the real Scout.

**Why not one session doing both:** the harness work needs your judgment as it goes. The step 0 results decide which fallbacks the build uses, and the plan flow has to be watched with real Claude. If I ran it through a subagent, you'd only see a summary afterwards. Two sessions also never write to the same files, because they work in different repos.

1	# Harness: build spec
2	
3	**Text in, architecture out.** Harness is a diagram-first shell around real Claude Code. You talk to the agent in a chat pane; a domain × layer map of the target repo shows, live, what each turn plans and does to the architecture; and the agent stops to ask you before it crosses a rule. Decisions you make become rules that later sessions are checked against.
4	
5	The theme is giving people time back. Agents made writing code nearly free, but understanding and checking it did not get cheaper. Every feature below exists to cut reading, rework or re-explaining, and the time ledger counts those savings.
6	
7	## 1. Repos
8	
9	Two separate git repos, side by side:
10	
11	```
12	workspace/
13	  harness/        this tool (npm workspaces monorepo)
14	  scout-agent/    the demo target, built separately from DEMO_REPO_SPEC.md
15	```
16	
17	The target must be its own repo. The coding agent runs with its working directory there, the map is computed over it, and `domains.yaml` plus `decisions/` are committed into it. The tool's own code must never appear on the map.
18	
19	```
20	harness/
21	  package.json              npm workspaces
22	  packages/core/            pure TypeScript, no I/O beyond fs reads; fully unit-tested
23	    src/schema.ts           zod schema for domains.yaml
24	    src/events.ts           event types and the reducer
25	    src/mapper.ts           path → cell, table → owner
26	    src/imports.ts          regex import parser + relative-path resolver
27	    src/writes.ts           db.insert / db.update scanner
28	    src/facts.ts            whole-repo scan: files, imports, writes, cross-domain edges
29	    src/rules.ts            the invariant checker (one function, three call sites)
30	    src/plan.ts             plan → ghost footprint
31	    src/ledger.ts           per-turn and session counters
32	    test/                   uses fixtures/scout-agent.domains.yaml
33	  apps/server/              Node + Hono + ws + @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk
34	    src/index.ts            HTTP + websocket; serves the shell in production
35	    src/bus.ts              append-only event log (.harness/events.jsonl in the target) + broadcast
36	    src/repo.ts             load, full scan, file watcher
37	    src/session.ts          the coding session (streaming input, modes, hooks, canUseTool)
38	    src/harness-tools.ts    in-process MCP server: submit_plan, cell_for, domain, who_writes, decisions_for
39	    src/turns.ts            turn lifecycle, git baselines, turn records
40	    src/decisions.ts        decisions/DR-n.md, invariant updates, Alike instructions
41	    src/cartographer.ts     one-shot map proposal
