```typescript
/**
 * npm run proof
 *
 * Runs every request in fixtures/proof-requests.json through the agent, then
 * calls every registered tool directly with each request's input. Afterwards
 * it reads the vendor call log and reports how many model calls carried a
 * contact's personal data and how many never reached the cost log.
 *
 * This is a report, not a test: it always exits 0.
 */
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { calls, clearCalls, lastSeq, type VendorCall } from "../vendor/_calllog";
import { resetCrm } from "../vendor/crm/index";
import { resetOutbox } from "../vendor/email/index";
import { runAgent } from "../src/orchestrator/agent";
import { registry } from "../src/orchestrator/tool-registry";
import { db } from "../src/shared/db";
import { createLogger } from "../src/shared/logger";
import type { RunRequest, Tool } from "../src/shared/types";

const MODEL_VENDORS = new Set(["llm-openai", "llm-anthropic", "embeddings"]);
const AGENT = "(agent: planner, memory, brief, email)";

interface Span {
  source: string;
  fromSeq: number;
  toSeq: number;
  costBefore: number;
  costAfter: number;
}

const spans: Span[] = [];

/** Wraps a tool's run() to remember which vendor calls and cost rows happened inside it. */
function instrument(tool: Tool): void {
  const run = tool.run.bind(tool);
  tool.run = async (input, ctx) => {
    const fromSeq = lastSeq();
    const costBefore = db.count("cost_log");
    try {
      return await run(input, ctx);
    } finally {
      spans.push({ source: tool.name, fromSeq, toSeq: lastSeq(), costBefore, costAfter: db.count("cost_log") });
    }
  };
}

function sourceOf(call: VendorCall): string {
  return spans.find((s) => call.seq > s.fromSeq && call.seq <= s.toSeq)?.source ?? AGENT;
}

function personalData(requests: RunRequest[]): string[] {
  const values = new Set<string>();
  for (const { contact } of requests) {
    for (const value of [contact.email, contact.phone, contact.name]) if (value) values.add(value);
  }
  return [...values];
}

function leaks(call: VendorCall, pii: string[]): string[] {
  const payload = JSON.stringify(call.payload);
  return pii.filter((value) => payload.includes(value));
}

async function main(): Promise<void> {
  const requests = JSON.parse(
    readFileSync(new URL("../fixtures/proof-requests.json", import.meta.url), "utf8"),
  ) as RunRequest[];
  const log = createLogger("proof", { level: "error" });

  db.reset();
  clearCalls();
  resetCrm();
  resetOutbox();
  for (const tool of registry.list()) instrument(tool);

  let failedRuns = 0;
  for (const request of requests) {
    try {
      await runAgent(request, { log });
    } catch (err) {
      failedRuns++;
      console.error(`run failed for ${request.company}: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : err}`);
    }
  }

  let failedTools = 0;
  for (const [i, request] of requests.entries()) {
    for (const tool of registry.list()) {
      try {
        await tool.run(
          { company: request.company, contact: request.contact, goal: request.goal },
          { runId: `proof_${String(i + 1).padStart(2, "0")}`, log },
        );
      } catch {
        failedTools++;
      }
    }
  }

  const pii = personalData(requests);
  const modelCalls = calls().filter((c) => MODEL_VENDORS.has(c.vendor));
  const leaking = modelCalls.filter((c) => leaks(c, pii).length > 0);
  const missingFromCostLog = Math.max(0, modelCalls.length - db.count("cost_log"));

  const rows = new Map<string, { calls: number; leaking: number; unlogged: number }>();
  const row = (source: string) => {
    let r = rows.get(source);
    if (!r) rows.set(source, (r = { calls: 0, leaking: 0, unlogged: 0 }));
    return r;
  };
  for (const call of modelCalls) {
    const r = row(sourceOf(call));
    r.calls++;
    if (leaking.includes(call)) r.leaking++;
  }
  for (const span of spans) {
    const inSpan = modelCalls.filter((c) => c.seq > span.fromSeq && c.seq <= span.toSeq).length;
    row(span.source).unlogged += Math.max(0, inSpan - (span.costAfter - span.costBefore));
  }
  const toolUnlogged = [...rows.entries()].filter(([s]) => s !== AGENT).reduce((n, [, r]) => n + r.unlogged, 0);
  row(AGENT).unlogged = Math.max(0, missingFromCostLog - toolUnlogged);

  const width = 64;
  const bar = "=".repeat(width);
  console.log(`\n${bar}`);
  console.log(`  PII reaching model providers: ${leaking.length} of ${modelCalls.length} model calls`);
  console.log(`  Model calls missing from the cost log: ${missingFromCostLog}`);
  console.log(`${bar}\n`);

  console.log(`${"Source".padEnd(40)}${"calls".padStart(8)}${"with PII".padStart(10)}${"unlogged".padStart(10)}`);
  console.log("-".repeat(width + 4));
  for (const [source, r] of [...rows.entries()].sort((a, b) => b[1].leaking - a[1].leaking || a[0].localeCompare(b[0]))) {
    console.log(`${source.padEnd(40)}${String(r.calls).padStart(8)}${String(r.leaking).padStart(10)}${String(r.unlogged).padStart(10)}`);
  }

  console.log(
    `\n${requests.length} requests, ${registry.list().length} tools, ${db.count("runs")} runs` +
      (failedRuns || failedTools ? ` (${failedRuns} failed runs, ${failedTools} failed tool calls)` : ""),
  );
}

main()
  .catch((err: unknown) => {
    console.error(err instanceof Error ? (err.stack ?? err.message) : err);
  })
  .finally(() => {
    process.exitCode = 0;
  });
```

```typescript
/**
 * npm run seed
 *
 * Loads a few contacts and earlier research notes into the local snapshot so
 * the CLI and server have history to draw on.
 */
import { addNote } from "../src/memory/notes-store";
import { indexNotes } from "../src/memory/vector-index";
import { syncContact } from "../src/outreach/crm-sync";
import { loadConfig } from "../src/shared/config";
import { db } from "../src/shared/db";

const CONTACTS = [
  { company: "Acme Robotics", contact: { name: "Jane Doe", email: "jane.doe@acmerobotics.com", title: "VP Operations" } },
  { company: "Northwind Freight", contact: { name: "Priya Raman", email: "priya.raman@northwindfreight.com", title: "Head of Procurement" } },
  { company: "Halcyon Health", contact: { name: "Sam Okafor", email: "sam.okafor@halcyonhealth.com", title: "Director, IT Partnerships" } },
  { company: "Brightline Software", contact: { name: "Lena Fischer", email: "lena.fischer@brightline.io", title: "VP Revenue Operations" } },
];

const NOTES: Array<{ company: string; text: string }> = [
  { company: "Acme Robotics", text: "Ops team is measured on time to first pick; deployments are the bottleneck, not hardware." },
  { company: "Acme Robotics", text: "Procurement is consolidating field service and planning tools this year." },
  { company: "Northwind Freight", text: "New TMS rollout runs through next year; they are wary of adding vendors mid-migration." },
  { company: "Northwind Freight", text: "Cross-border lanes are the growth story; Laredo terminal just opened." },
  { company: "Halcyon Health", text: "Buying committee includes nursing informatics; time to go-live matters more than price." },
  { company: "Brightline Software", text: "RevOps owns tooling budget; they want fewer tools after the Series E." },
];

async function main(): Promise<void> {
  const { snapshotPath } = loadConfig();
  if (!snapshotPath) throw new Error("SCOUT_SNAPSHOT is off; nothing to seed into");
  db.restore(snapshotPath);

  for (const { company, contact } of CONTACTS) await syncContact(contact, company);
  const notes = NOTES.map((n) => addNote({ ...n, source: "seed" }));
  await indexNotes(notes);

  db.snapshot(snapshotPath);
  console.log(`seeded ${CONTACTS.length} contacts and ${notes.length} notes into ${snapshotPath}`);
}

main().catch((err: unknown) => {
  console.error(err instanceof Error ? err.message : err);
  process.exitCode = 1;
});
```

```typescript
import { existsSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { join, resolve, dirname } from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import { Hono } from 'hono';
import { serve } from '@hono/node-server';
import { serveStatic } from '@hono/node-server/serve-static';
import { WebSocketServer, type WebSocket } from 'ws';
import { parseDomainMap } from '@harness/core';
import { Bus } from './bus';
import { Repo } from './repo';
import { Session } from './session';
import { commitPaths } from './git';
import { proposeMap } from './cartographer';

const here = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
const REPO = process.env.HARNESS_REPO ? resolve(process.cwd(), process.env.HARNESS_REPO) : '';
if (!REPO || !existsSync(REPO)) {
  console.error(`Set HARNESS_REPO to the target repo (got "${process.env.HARNESS_REPO ?? ''}").`);
  process.exit(1);
}
const PORT = Number(process.env.PORT ?? 4310);
const FALLBACK_MAP = resolve(here, '../../../fixtures/scout-agent.domains.yaml');

const bus = new Bus(REPO, { fresh: process.env.HARNESS_FRESH === '1' });
const sockets = new Set<WebSocket>();
const broadcast = (msg: unknown) => {
  const s = JSON.stringify(msg);
  for (const ws of sockets) if (ws.readyState === ws.OPEN) ws.send(s);
};
bus.on((event) => broadcast({ type: 'event', event }));

const repo = new Repo(REPO, bus);
let session: Session | null = null;
let proposal: { yaml: string; source: 'cartographer' | 'fixture' } | null = null;
let busy = false;

function startSession() {
  repo.scan();
  repo.startWatcher();
  session = new Session(repo, bus, (m) => {
    if (m.type === 'busy') busy = m.busy;
    broadcast(m);
  });
  session.start();
}

/** Load: use domains.yaml if present; otherwise propose one (cartographer, else the fixture) and wait for Confirm. */
async function load() {
  if (repo.hasMap()) {
    repo.loadMapFile();
    bus.emit('map_confirmed', { map: repo.map, source: 'file' }, { turn: null });
    startSession();
    return;
  }
  let yaml: string;
  let source: 'cartographer' | 'fixture' = 'cartographer';
  try {
    if (process.env.HARNESS_CARTOGRAPHER === '0') throw new Error('disabled');
    yaml = await proposeMap(repo, bus);
  } catch (e) {
    if ((e as Error).message !== 'disabled') bus.emit('error', { message: `Cartographer failed, using the reference map: ${(e as Error).message}` }, { turn: null });
    yaml = readFileSync(FALLBACK_MAP, 'utf8');
    source = 'fixture';
  }
  showProposal(yaml, source);
}

function showProposal(yaml: string, source: 'cartographer' | 'fixture') {
  repo.setMap(yaml);
  proposal = { yaml, source };
  bus.emit('map_proposed', { map: repo.map, yaml }, { turn: null });
  // The shell plays the map assembling: one file_assigned per file, ~15 ms apart.
  const files = repo.listFiles();
  files.forEach((path, i) => setTimeout(() => bus.emit('file_assigned', { placement: repo.place(path) }, { path, turn: null }), i * 15));
}

const app = new Hono();
app.get('/api/info', (c) => c.json({ repo: REPO, session: bus.session, busy, proposal: !!proposal }));
app.get('/api/events', (c) => c.json(bus.events));
app.post('/api/chat', async (c) => {
  const { text } = await c.req.json<{ text: string }>();
  if (!session) return c.json({ error: 'Confirm the map first.' }, 409);
  session.userMessage(text);
  return c.json({ ok: true });
});
app.post('/api/approve', (c) => { session?.approve(); return c.json({ ok: true }); });
app.post('/api/interrupt', (c) => { session?.interrupt(); return c.json({ ok: true }); });
app.post('/api/map/confirm', (c) => {
  if (!proposal) return c.json({ error: 'No proposal pending.' }, 409);
  writeFileSync(repo.mapPath, proposal.yaml);
  try { commitPaths(repo.root, ['domains.yaml'], 'docs: add domains.yaml architecture map'); }
  catch (e) { bus.emit('error', { message: `Could not commit domains.yaml: ${(e as Error).message}` }, { turn: null }); }
  repo.setMap(proposal.yaml);
  bus.emit('map_confirmed', { map: repo.map, source: proposal.source }, { turn: null });
  proposal = null;
  startSession();
  return c.json({ ok: true });
});
app.post('/api/map/fallback', (c) => {
  if (!proposal) return c.json({ error: 'No proposal pending.' }, 409);
  showProposal(readFileSync(FALLBACK_MAP, 'utf8'), 'fixture');
  return c.json({ ok: true });
});
app.get('/api/file', (c) => {
  const p = c.req.query('path') ?? '';
  const rel = repo.rel(p);
  if (!rel || !existsSync(join(repo.root, rel))) return c.json({ error: 'not found' }, 404);
  return c.text(readFileSync(join(repo.root, rel), 'utf8'));
});

const shellDist = resolve(here, '../../shell/dist');
if (existsSync(shellDist)) app.use('/*', serveStatic({ root: shellDist }));

const server = serve({ fetch: app.fetch, port: PORT }, () => console.log(`Harness server on http://localhost:${PORT} · repo ${REPO}`));
const wss = new WebSocketServer({ server: server as never, path: '/ws' });
wss.on('connection', (ws) => {
  sockets.add(ws);
  ws.send(JSON.stringify({ type: 'hello', events: bus.events, busy, session: bus.session }));
  ws.on('close', () => sockets.delete(ws));
});

parseDomainMap; // keep the import tree-shake-safe for tsx watch reloads
void load();

const shutdown = async () => { await repo.close(); process.exit(0); };
process.on('SIGINT', shutdown);
process.on('SIGTERM', shutdown);
```

```text
import { z } from 'zod';
import YAML from 'yaml';

const LayerSchema = z.object({ id: z.string(), name: z.string() });

const CellSchema = z.object({
  paths: z.array(z.string()).optional(),
  tables: z.array(z.string()).optional(),
});

const DomainSchema = z.object({
  id: z.string(),
  name: z.string(),
  purpose: z.string(),
  cells: z.record(z.string(), CellSchema),
  tests: z.array(z.string()).optional(),
});

/** An exception may be written as a bare path string; it is normalized to `{ path }`. */
const ExceptionSchema = z.union([
  z.string().transform((path): { path: string; decision?: string } => ({ path })),
  z.object({ path: z.string(), decision: z.string().optional() }),
]);

const InvariantBase = z.object({
  id: z.string(),
  rule: z.string(),
  exceptions: z.array(ExceptionSchema).default([]),
  source: z.string().optional(),
  /** Decision records (DR ids) that confirmed this invariant. */
  decisions: z.array(z.string()).optional(),
});

const InvariantSchema = z.discriminatedUnion('kind', [
  InvariantBase.extend({
    kind: z.literal('only_via'),
    targets: z.array(z.string()),
    allowed_from: z.array(z.string()),
  }),
  InvariantBase.extend({
    kind: z.literal('owns_writes'),
    owners: z.record(z.string(), z.string()),
  }),
  InvariantBase.extend({
    kind: z.literal('no_edge'),
    from: z.string(),
    to: z.string(),
  }),
]);

/** Schema for a target repo's `domains.yaml`. */
export const DomainMapSchema = z
  .object({
    version: z.number(),
    layers: z.array(LayerSchema),
    neutral: z.array(z.string()).optional(),
    ignore: z.array(z.string()).optional(),
    domains: z.array(DomainSchema),
    invariants: z.array(InvariantSchema).default([]),
  })
  .superRefine((map, ctx) => {
    const layers = new Set(map.layers.map((l) => l.id));
    const domains = new Set(map.domains.map((d) => d.id));
    const issue = (path: (string | number)[], message: string) => ctx.addIssue({ code: 'custom', path, message });
    map.domains.forEach((d, i) => {
      for (const layer of Object.keys(d.cells)) {
        if (!layers.has(layer)) issue(['domains', i, 'cells', layer], `unknown layer "${layer}"`);
      }
    });
    map.invariants.forEach((inv, i) => {
      const refs =
        inv.kind === 'only_via' ? inv.allowed_from : inv.kind === 'owns_writes' ? Object.values(inv.owners) : [inv.from, inv.to];
      for (const ref of refs) {
        if (!domains.has(ref)) issue(['invariants', i], `${inv.id} refers to unknown domain "${ref}"`);
      }
    });
  });

export type DomainMap = z.output<typeof DomainMapSchema>;
export type Layer = DomainMap['layers'][number];
```

```typescript
import { query } from '@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk';
import { stringify } from 'yaml';
import { scanRepo, DomainMapSchema, type DomainMap } from '@harness/core';
import type { Repo } from './repo';
import type { Bus } from './bus';

const DEFAULT_IGNORE = ['node_modules/**', '.git/**', '.harness/**', 'decisions/**', '*.json', '*.md', '*.config.ts', '.gitignore', 'domains.yaml'];

/** Flat shape for structured output; converted to the domains.yaml schema afterwards. */
const OUTPUT_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  additionalProperties: false,
  required: ['layers', 'neutral', 'ignore', 'domains', 'invariants'],
  properties: {
    layers: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', additionalProperties: false, required: ['id', 'name'], properties: { id: { type: 'string' }, name: { type: 'string' } } } },
    neutral: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' }, description: 'Globs for shared code that belongs to no domain (types, db helpers, logging).' },
    ignore: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' }, description: 'Globs to skip entirely (fixtures, scripts, build output, config).' },
    domains: {
      type: 'array',
      items: {
        type: 'object',
        additionalProperties: false,
        required: ['id', 'name', 'purpose', 'cells', 'tests'],
        properties: {
          id: { type: 'string' }, name: { type: 'string', description: 'Product language, 1–3 words.' }, purpose: { type: 'string' },
          cells: {
            type: 'array',
            items: {
              type: 'object', additionalProperties: false, required: ['layer', 'paths', 'tables'],
              properties: { layer: { type: 'string' }, paths: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } }, tables: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } } },
            },
          },
          tests: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
        },
      },
    },
    invariants: {
      type: 'array',
      items: {
        type: 'object',
        additionalProperties: false,
        required: ['id', 'rule', 'kind', 'targets', 'allowed_from', 'owners', 'from', 'to'],
        properties: {
          id: { type: 'string', description: 'DR-1, DR-2, …' },
          rule: { type: 'string', description: 'One plain sentence.' },
          kind: { type: 'string', enum: ['only_via', 'owns_writes', 'no_edge'] },
          targets: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' }, description: 'only_via: globs of the guarded files (e.g. vendor clients).' },
          allowed_from: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' }, description: 'only_via: domain ids allowed to import the targets.' },
          owners: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', additionalProperties: false, required: ['table', 'domain'], properties: { table: { type: 'string' }, domain: { type: 'string' } } }, description: 'owns_writes: table → owning domain id.' },
          from: { type: 'string', description: 'no_edge: domain id (empty otherwise).' },
          to: { type: 'string', description: 'no_edge: domain id (empty otherwise).' },
        },
      },
    },
  },
} as const;

type Out = {
  layers: { id: string; name: string }[];
  neutral: string[];
  ignore: string[];
  domains: { id: string; name: string; purpose: string; cells: { layer: string; paths: string[]; tables: string[] }[]; tests: string[] }[];
  invariants: { id: string; rule: string; kind: 'only_via' | 'owns_writes' | 'no_edge'; targets: string[]; allowed_from: string[]; owners: { table: string; domain: string }[]; from: string; to: string }[];
};

function toMap(o: Out): DomainMap {
  const raw = {
    version: 1,
    layers: o.layers,
    neutral: o.neutral,
    ignore: [...new Set([...DEFAULT_IGNORE, ...o.ignore])],
    domains: o.domains.map((d) => ({
      id: d.id, name: d.name, purpose: d.purpose,
      cells: Object.fromEntries(d.cells.map((c) => [c.layer, { ...(c.paths.length ? { paths: c.paths } : {}), ...(c.tables.length ? { tables: c.tables } : {}) }])),
      ...(d.tests.length ? { tests: d.tests } : {}),
    })),
    invariants: o.invariants.map((i) => {
      const base = { id: i.id, rule: i.rule, kind: i.kind, exceptions: [], source: 'cartographer' };
      if (i.kind === 'only_via') return { ...base, targets: i.targets, allowed_from: i.allowed_from };
      if (i.kind === 'owns_writes') return { ...base, owners: Object.fromEntries(i.owners.map((x) => [x.table, x.domain])) };
      return { ...base, from: i.from, to: i.to };
    }),
  };
  return DomainMapSchema.parse(raw);
}

/**
 * One-shot map proposal (SPEC §10): a separate read-only query on a smaller model, given the file tree,
 * import edges and table writes. Never runs inside the coding session. Returns domains.yaml text.
 */
export async function proposeMap(repo: Repo, bus: Bus): Promise<string> {
  const bare: DomainMap = { version: 1, layers: [{ id: 'x', name: 'x' }], ignore: DEFAULT_IGNORE, domains: [], invariants: [] } as DomainMap;
  const facts = scanRepo(repo.root, bare);
  const prompt = [
    'Propose an architecture map for this repo as a domain × layer grid that a product person can read.',
    '- 5–9 domains named in product language (e.g. "Model gateway", not "src/gateway"). Every source file should land in exactly one cell or in `neutral`/`ignore`.',
    '- Layers suited to this repo, top to bottom (for an agent system: entry, logic, data, external). Data cells list the tables that domain writes. External cells hold vendor/third-party client code.',
    '- Prefer explicit file paths for cells that share a folder with other cells, globs otherwise. Map test folders with `tests` globs.',
    '- Invariants (ids DR-1, DR-2, …) you can infer from the facts below: sole importers of a vendor (only_via), sole writers of a table (owns_writes), and dependencies that are absent between two domains (no_edge). Note: the code may already break one of them in a single place; that is expected, still propose the rule.',
    'You may read files to understand purposes. Do not modify anything.',
    '',
    `Files (${facts.files.length}):`, ...facts.files,
    '',
    'Import edges (from → to):', ...facts.imports.map((i) => `${i.from} → ${i.to}`),
    '',
    'Table writes (file: table):', ...facts.writes.map((w) => `${w.file}: ${w.table}`),
  ].join('\n');

  const q = query({
    prompt,
    options: {
      cwd: repo.root,
      model: process.env.HARNESS_CARTOGRAPHER_MODEL ?? 'claude-haiku-5-5',
      tools: ['Read', 'Grep', 'Glob'],
      permissionMode: 'dontAsk',
      allowedTools: ['Read', 'Grep', 'Glob'],
      settingSources: [],
      strictMcpConfig: true,
      outputFormat: { type: 'json_schema', schema: OUTPUT_SCHEMA as unknown as Record<string, unknown> },
      maxTurns: 20,
    },
  });
  for await (const m of q) {
    if (m.type === 'result') {
      if (m.subtype !== 'success' || !m.structured_output) throw new Error(`cartographer ${m.subtype}`);
      const map = toMap(m.structured_output as Out);
      const header = '# Proposed by the Harness cartographer and confirmed by the user.\n# Domains are columns, layers are rows. Edges are derived from imports, never declared.\n\n';
      bus.emit('chat', { role: 'system', text: `Cartographer proposed ${map.domains.length} domains and ${map.invariants.length} rules.` }, { turn: null });
      return header + stringify(map, { flowLevel: 3 });
    }
  }
  throw new Error('cartographer returned no result');
}
```

```bash
describe("news_digest", () => {
  it("groups headlines by topic without calling a model", async () => {
    const result = await newsDigest.run(input, ctx);
    expect(result.summary).toMatch(/^4 recent headlines for Northwind Freight/);
    expect(result.facts[0]).toMatch(/^\[deals\] Northwind Freight signs/);
    expect(callsFor("llm-openai")).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  it("puts unrecognized headlines under 'other'", () => {
    const groups = groupByTopic([{ title: "Weather delays shipments", source: "", url: "", publishedAt: "", summary: "" }]);
    expect([...groups.keys()]).toEqual(["other"]);
  });
});

describe("company_profile", () => {
  it("combines company and contact enrichment and logs the model cost", async () => {
    const result = await companyProfile.run(input, ctx);
    expect(result.facts).toContain("Revenue: $2.1B");
    expect(result.facts).toContain("Title: Head of Procurement");
    expect(db.count("cost_log")).toBe(1);
  });
});

describe("web_search", () => {
  it("biases the query toward the goal and returns sources", async () => {
    const result = await webSearch.run(input, ctx);
    expect(callsFor("search")[0]?.payload).toMatchObject({ query: "Northwind Freight procurement" });
    expect(result.sources[0]).toBe("https://northwindfreight.com");
  });
});
```

````markdown
# Scout

Scout is a research agent for B2B sales. Give it a prospect company, a contact and a goal, and it:

1. researches the company: web search, firmographics, recent news, SEC filings;
2. recalls notes from earlier research on the same company and saves new ones;
3. writes a short research brief with a language model;
4. syncs the contact to the CRM and drafts an outreach email (and sends it if you ask).

Everything runs offline. External services (model providers, search, news, SEC EDGAR, enrichment, CRM, email) are in-process fakes under `vendor/` that answer from `fixtures/`, so runs are fast and deterministic and need no API keys.

## Running it

Requires Node 20+ (22 recommended).

```sh
npm i
npm test            # vitest, about 25 tests, under a second
npm run dev         # HTTP server on http://localhost:8787 (restarts on change)
npm run proof       # runs 20 sample requests and reports on model traffic
npm run seed        # loads sample contacts and notes into .scout/db.json
```

From the command line:

```sh
npm run scout -- --company "Acme Robotics" --contact jane.doe@acmerobotics.com \
  --name "Jane Doe" --goal "Prep for a renewal call; check recent news"
```

Add `--send` to send the drafted email, or `--json` for the full result. State is kept in `.scout/db.json` between runs (`SCOUT_SNAPSHOT=off` disables it).

Over HTTP:

```sh
curl -X POST localhost:8787/runs -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{
  "company": "Acme Robotics",
  "contact": { "email": "jane.doe@acmerobotics.com", "name": "Jane Doe" },
  "goal": "Prep for a renewal call; check recent news"
}'
curl localhost:8787/runs/run_0001
```

### Configuration

| Variable | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SCOUT_MODEL_PROVIDER` | `openai` | `openai` or `anthropic` |
| `SCOUT_OPENAI_MODEL` / `SCOUT_ANTHROPIC_MODEL` | `gpt-4o-mini` / `claude-3-5-haiku` | |
| `SCOUT_SNAPSHOT` | `.scout/db.json` | path, or `off` |
| `SCOUT_LOG_LEVEL` | `warn` | `debug`, `info`, `warn`, `error` |
| `PORT` | `8787` | |

## How it's organized

```
src/
  channels/       HTTP routes, CLI, request validation
  orchestrator/   run loop, planner, tool registry, run state
  tools/          research tools (one file each) and the tool list
  gateway/        model calls: complete(), embed(), redaction, cost ledger, providers
  memory/         notes, vector index, retrieval
  outreach/       CRM sync, email drafting, sending, outreach log
  shared/         db, config, logger, types, ids
vendor/           offline fakes of external services; every call is recorded in vendor/_calllog.ts
fixtures/         canned vendor responses and sample requests
scripts/          proof report and seed data
test/             tests, one folder per area of src/
```

A run goes: validate the request, sync the contact, recall earlier notes, plan which tools to use, run them (at most six steps), save the findings as notes, write the brief, then draft the email.

Storage is an in-memory table store with JSON snapshots (`src/shared/db.ts`). Writes go through `db.insert("<table>", row)` and `db.update("<table>", id, patch)`.

## Adding a tool

A tool is an object with a `name`, some `tags`, a `description` and an async `run(input, ctx)` that returns a summary, facts and sources (the `Tool` type in `src/shared/types.ts`). To add one:

1. Create a file in `src/tools/` that exports the tool.
2. Add it to the list in `src/tools/index.ts`.

The planner picks tools two ways: the model chooses from the descriptions, and any tool whose tag appears as a word in the goal is added too (plurals don't matter, so a `filing` tag matches "filings"). Pick tags a rep would actually type. `npm run proof` calls every registered tool, so new tools are covered automatically.

See `src/tools/` for examples.
````

## What it is
A diagram-first shell around Claude Code: chat pane on the left (380px), a domain × layer grid of the target repo filling the rest, turn summary + replay scrubber under the grid, ledger top right. Product: "Text in, architecture out." The demo judges see it on a projector for ~3 minutes, so legibility and calm, purposeful motion matter more than chrome. The Figma mockups are not accessible to you; design from the spec.

## Hard rule: UI state is a pure reduction of the event log
Import from `@harness/core/view` (browser-safe; no node builtins — never import `@harness/core` root in the shell): `reduce(events, upTo?)`, `apply`, `initialState`, `cellViews(state, turnId?)`, `edgeViews(state, turnId?)`, `provenance(state, {edge}|{cell})`, `ledger(state)`, `turnLedger`, `turnFindings`, `cellKey`, `edgeKey`, and types (`HarnessEvent`, `UIState`, `TurnState`, `CellView`, `EdgeView`, `Finding`, `DomainMap`, `Violation`, …). Read `packages/core/src/events.ts` and `packages/core/src/ledger.ts` fully — they define the event payloads and every derived view; do not re-derive footprint/ghosts/ledger yourself and do not keep separate mutable copies of them. The store holds `events: HarnessEvent[]`, the replay index (null = live), and purely ephemeral things (streaming text delta buffer, busy flag, input draft, selection, hover). Everything else = `reduce(events, replayIndex ?? events.length)`, memoized. Live mode may use `apply` incrementally for performance but must equal `reduce`.

## Server contract (apps/server, port 4310; already written — read `apps/server/src/index.ts` and `session.ts` to confirm)
- WebSocket `/ws`: on connect `{type:'hello', events, busy, session}`; then `{type:'event', event}`, `{type:'delta', text}` (assistant text streaming; clear the buffer when a `chat` event with role assistant arrives), `{type:'busy', busy}`. Reconnect with backoff.
- `POST /api/chat {text}`, `POST /api/approve`, `POST /api/interrupt`, `POST /api/map/confirm`, `POST /api/map/fallback`, `GET /api/file?path=` (raw text, for the inspector), `GET /api/info`.
- Vite dev server on 5173 proxies `/api` and `/ws` (ws: true) to 4310. Root `package.json` runs both via `npm run dev` (script `dev` in `@harness/shell` must start Vite on 5173). Add `apps/shell/package.json` (name `@harness/shell`, scripts dev/build/preview), `tsconfig.json` extending `../../tsconfig.base.json` (add DOM libs, jsx react-jsx), `vite.config.ts`, `index.html`.

## UI spec
- **Grid**: columns = `map.domains` in order (name in product language as header, purpose on hover), plus an **Unassigned** column only if any file is unassigned; rows = `map.layers` in file order (row labels on the left). A cell exists only where the domain has that layer in `cells`; empty slots are quiet blank space. Cell shows a small file count and, when edited this turn, a +added/−removed badge ticking up.
- **Cell states** (from `cellViews`): looked = dashed indigo outline · edited = indigo fill · unplanned (amber, done but not planned) · violation `existing` = red with a badge counting files · violation `new` = red plus a distinct **new** badge naming the file (must look different from an existing violation even in an already-red cell) · ghost = dashed outline at 50% opacity with step-number badges. Ghosts turn solid as they're edited.
- **Agent cursor**: small avatar pinned to `state.cursor.cell`, labelled "Claude · reading `retrieve.ts`" (verb + basename), easing between cells in 250 ms. Hidden when null.
- **Edges** (`edgeViews`): SVG overlay routed through the gaps between cells, from source domain column to target domain column (use the cells involved in the edge's files when possible: source cell = cell of `files[0].from`, target = cell of `files[0].to`; fall back to column centers). Existing = thin neutral; `new` (added this turn) draws in with a stroke-dashoffset animation; `ghost` = dashed, in its own lane offset from any solid edge between the same domains; `violation` = red. Arrowheads. Keep it legible with ~8–10 edges; don't build a layout engine — fixed grid, simple orthogonal or gentle curved routing through gutters.
- **Chat pane**: messages from `state.chat` (user / assistant / system), assistant markdown rendered simply (code spans, bold, lists, fenced code), streaming delta shown as a live trailing assistant bubble while busy. Input with Enter to send, Shift+Enter newline, Stop button while busy (`/api/interrupt`). When `state.awaitingApproval`: show the plan text and an **Approve plan** button (typing "approve" also works server-side). When `state.pendingFork`: show the violation reason and two buttons, **A** and **B**, labelled with `options[0]`/`options[1]`; clicking prefills the input with `A — ` / `B — ` and focuses it so the user can add their reason, Enter sends. Errors from `state.errors` as quiet system notes.
- **Map proposal** (load): when the latest `map_proposed` is not followed by `map_confirmed`, show a banner "Proposed map: N domains, M rules" with **Confirm** and **Use reference map** buttons; animate the grid assembling as `file_assigned` events arrive (cells' file counts tick up, a brief highlight per assignment).
- **Turn summary** under the grid for the selected turn (default latest): prompt, step counter "3 of 6 steps" (steps whose cells are all edited / total plan steps), and ranked findings from `turnFindings` — severity 1 red, 2–3 amber, 4 quiet — each clickable to select its cell.
- **Ledger** top right: Lines changed · Cells to review · Forks caught before code · Rejected options blocked, for the session (`ledger(state).session`) with the current turn's values small beneath. Counts only — **never display minutes or any time estimate**.
- **Replay scrubber**: a range over event indices with turn boundaries marked (ticks at `turn_started` indices) and a Live button; dragging re-reduces the log (`reduce(events, i)`). While replaying, disable sending.
- **Inspector**: click a cell or edge → side panel/popover with: cell paths & tables (from `map`), files currently placed there (from `state.files`), invariants that involve this domain, violations, provenance (`provenance(state, …)`: "added in turn 3 · DR-4"), and for a file, a code preview from `/api/file`. Click on empty space closes it.
- **Motion rule**: animate only state changes; nothing loops or pulses continuously. Respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- Empty/error states: server down (reconnecting), no map yet, no turns yet (a short hint: "Ask Claude to change something; the map shows what it plans and does").

````text
# Harness: build spec

**Text in, architecture out.** Harness is a diagram-first shell around real Claude Code. You talk to the agent in a chat pane; a domain × layer map of the target repo shows, live, what each turn plans and does to the architecture; and the agent stops to ask you before it crosses a rule. Decisions you make become rules that later sessions are checked against.

The theme is giving people time back. Agents made writing code nearly free, but understanding and checking it did not get cheaper. Every feature below exists to cut reading, rework or re-explaining, and the time ledger counts those savings.

## 1. Repos

Two separate git repos, side by side:

```
workspace/
  harness/        this tool (npm workspaces monorepo)
  scout-agent/    the demo target, built separately from DEMO_REPO_SPEC.md
```

The target must be its own repo. The coding agent runs with its working directory there, the map is computed over it, and `domains.yaml` plus `decisions/` are committed into it. The tool's own code must never appear on the map.

```
harness/
  package.json              npm workspaces
  packages/core/            pure TypeScript, no I/O beyond fs reads; fully unit-tested
    src/schema.ts           zod schema for domains.yaml
    src/events.ts           event types and the reducer
    src/mapper.ts           path → cell, table → owner
    src/imports.ts          regex import parser + relative-path resolver
    src/writes.ts           db.insert / db.update scanner
    src/facts.ts            whole-repo scan: files, imports, writes, cross-domain edges
    src/rules.ts            the invariant checker (one function, three call sites)
    src/plan.ts             plan → ghost footprint
    src/ledger.ts           per-turn and session counters
    test/                   uses fixtures/scout-agent.domains.yaml
  apps/server/              Node + Hono + ws + @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk
    src/index.ts            HTTP + websocket; serves the shell in production
    src/bus.ts              append-only event log (.harness/events.jsonl in the target) + broadcast
    src/repo.ts             load, full scan, file watcher
    src/session.ts          the coding session (streaming input, modes, hooks, canUseTool)
    src/harness-tools.ts    in-process MCP server: submit_plan, cell_for, domain, who_writes, decisions_for
    src/turns.ts            turn lifecycle, git baselines, turn records
    src/decisions.ts        decisions/DR-n.md, invariant updates, Alike instructions
    src/cartographer.ts     one-shot map proposal
  apps/shell/               Vite + React + Zustand
  fixtures/scout-agent.domains.yaml
```

Run: `HARNESS_REPO=../scout-agent npm run dev` (server on 4310, shell on 5173).

## 2. Hard rules

1. **No model calls in the hot path.** Hooks, the mapper, the import parser and the rule checker are deterministic and fast. Model calls (the cartographer) never block the coding session.
2. **Every piece of UI state is a pure reduction of the event log.** Footprint, ghosts, ledger, summary, provenance and replay are all `reduce(events)`. Replay is "reduce up to index i".
3. **Harness writes to the target repo only in three places:** `domains.yaml`, `decisions/`, `.harness/` (gitignored). The coding session is the only thing that edits product code.
4. **Facts win on structure, the user wins on meaning, the agent wins only on stated intent**, and intent is always checked against facts.

## 3. The map (`domains.yaml`)

Schema: see `fixtures/scout-agent.domains.yaml`. Domains are columns, layers are rows (rows come from the file, not hard-coded). Each cell lists path globs and, for data cells, owned tables. `neutral` paths never create edges; `ignore` paths are skipped. Files that match no cell land in an **Unassigned** column.

**Tests** are assigned to a domain by its `tests` globs. A test file counts as part of that domain for the rule checker and the footprint and is listed in the inspector, but it is not drawn in a cell and draws no edges.

**Edges are derived, never declared.** A cross-domain edge exists when a file in domain A imports a file in domain B. Flow down a column is implied and not drawn. The import parser handles `import … from '…'`, `import('…')` and `export … from '…'`. It resolves relative paths by trying the specifier as written, then `.ts`, `.tsx`, `/index.ts`, `/index.tsx`, and maps a `.js` specifier to `.ts`. It ignores bare package and `node:` imports (Scout has none that matter).

**Writes:** a regex scan for `db.insert(` and `db.update(` followed by a string literal in any quote style gives `{file, table}` pairs.

## 4. Invariants: one checker, three call sites

```ts
type Violation = { invariant: string; reason: string; file: string; detail: string; options: [string, string] };
function check(map: DomainMap, delta: FactDelta): Violation[];
```

`FactDelta` is a set of added imports and added writes, each with its source file. The three kinds:

| Kind | Fires when |
| --- | --- |
| `only_via` | a file outside `allowed_from` domains imports a `targets` path |
| `owns_writes` | a file outside the owner domain writes the table |
| `no_edge` | a file in `from` imports a file in `to` |

Exceptions (paths) suppress a violation. Each violation carries two options: **A** comply (for `only_via` on Scout: "route through `gateway.complete()`"), **B** add an exception for this path and record why.

The three call sites, all using the same function:

1. **Load:** full repo scan. On Scout, finds exactly one: DR-1 in `src/tools/news-summarize.ts`. It shows red on load.
2. **Plan:** run on the declared dependencies and files in `submit_plan`.
3. **Edit:** run in the `PreToolUse` hook on the imports and writes that the edit would add (diff the `new_string`/`content` against the current file).

## 5. Events

```ts
type HarnessEvent = {
  id: string; t: number;
  session: string;          // coding session id
  turn: string | null;
  kind:
    | 'repo_scanned' | 'map_proposed' | 'map_confirmed' | 'file_assigned'
    | 'violation_found'
    | 'turn_started' | 'looked' | 'cursor'
    | 'planned' | 'plan_violation' | 'fork_asked' | 'fork_answered' | 'plan_approved'
    | 'gate_blocked' | 'edited' | 'edge_added' | 'edge_removed'
    | 'test_result' | 'decision_recorded' | 'turn_ended';
  cell?: { domain: string; layer: string };
  path?: string;
  data?: Record<string, unknown>;   // e.g. { step: 2 }, { added: 18, removed: 2 }, { invariant: 'DR-1' }
};
```

The server appends every event to `.harness/events.jsonl` and broadcasts it over the websocket. The shell holds the array and derives everything from it.

## 6. The coding session

One long-lived streaming session:

```ts
query({
  prompt: chatMessages(),                     // AsyncIterable<SDKUserMessage> fed by the chat pane
  options: {
    cwd: REPO,
    permissionMode: 'plan',
    systemPrompt: { type: 'preset', preset: 'claude_code', append: brief() },
    mcpServers: { harness: harnessTools },    // createSdkMcpServer; user-scope MCP servers (Alike) still load
    allowedTools: ['mcp__harness__*', 'mcp__alike__record_decision', 'mcp__alike__resolve_work_item', 'mcp__alike__describe_entity_kind'],
    hooks: { PreToolUse: [...], PostToolUse: [...] },
    canUseTool,                                // intercepts ExitPlanMode for approval
  },
});
```

**`brief()`** contains: the map (domains, purposes, cell paths), every standing decision from `decisions/` (with the invariant it qualifies and the option it rejected), and these rules:

> Before editing anything, call `mcp__harness__submit_plan` with numbered steps. Each step lists the exact file paths it will create or modify and any new imports it adds (from path → to path). If the result contains violations, stop and ask the user to choose between the two options it gives, in one short message, then wait. Never work around a violation. After the user answers, resubmit the plan, then exit plan mode.

The brief does **not** list the seeded invariants (`source: cartographer`). They are enforced at plan and edit time instead. Stated up front, they would make the agent comply silently, so the user never sees the choice and nothing gets recorded. Once the user answers a fork, the resulting decision is in every later brief, and the next session follows it without asking. That contrast, asked once and then remembered, is the memory beat of the demo.

**Turn flow:**

1. User message → `turn_started` (record `git rev-parse HEAD` and a `git stash create` snapshot as the baseline).
2. Plan mode: Claude reads (`looked`, `cursor`), then calls `submit_plan`. The server maps paths to cells, builds ghost cells and ghost edges, and runs the checker → `planned` (+ `plan_violation`). The tool result returns the ghost summary and, if violated, the reason plus options A/B with an instruction to ask.
3. Claude asks → `fork_asked`. The user answers in chat → `fork_answered` → decision written (§8). Claude resubmits.
4. Claude calls `ExitPlanMode` → `canUseTool` holds it, the shell shows an **Approve plan** button (typing "approve" also works) → `plan_approved` → allow, then `session.setPermissionMode('acceptEdits')`.
5. Edits: hooks emit `cursor`, `gate_blocked`, `edited`, `edge_added` / `edge_removed`. Ghost cells fill as their files are edited; the step counter advances.
6. Result message → `turn_ended` with the plan-versus-built diff and git `--numstat` totals; write `.harness/turns/<id>.json`; `setPermissionMode('plan')` for the next turn.

**Hooks:**

| Hook | Matcher | Does | Blocking |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| PreToolUse | `Read\|Grep\|Glob` | `looked` + `cursor` for the file or search path | no (return `{ async: true }`) |
| PreToolUse | `Edit\|Write\|MultiEdit` | run the checker on the added imports/writes; on a hit return `permissionDecision: 'deny'` with the reason, options and "ask the user"; emit `gate_blocked` | yes, deterministic, < 20 ms |
| PostToolUse | `Edit\|Write\|MultiEdit` | `edited` (+/− lines), recompute that file's imports → edge events | no |
| PostToolUse | `Bash` | if the command ran `vitest`, parse results → `test_result` per test domain (stretch) | no |

**File watcher** (chokidar on the target, minus `ignore`): any write not already reported by a hook becomes an `edited` event marked `unattributed`. Hooks give attribution and gating; the watcher guarantees completeness, since shell commands can write files without passing through the edit hooks.

**Harness MCP tools** (all read-only except `submit_plan`, which only records intent): `submit_plan(steps[{ n, text, files[], imports[{ from, to }] }])`, `cell_for(path)`, `domain(id)`, `who_writes(table)`, `decisions_for(paths[])`.

## 7. Plan versus built

- **Ghosts:** planned cells are drawn dashed with their step numbers; planned edges are dashed; a ghost that violates an invariant is red.
- **Fill-in:** a ghost cell turns solid when a file mapped to it is edited.
- **End-of-turn diff:** planned and done is solid; planned and not done stays a ghost; **done but not planned is amber**, which is how the map shows the agent straying from its own plan.
- **New versus existing violations:** a violation found on load is drawn red, with a badge on its cell counting the files involved. A violation raised by this turn's plan or edits must look different from the map before the turn, even when it repeats an existing one (on Scout, the 10-K plan copies `news-summarize.ts` into the same red cell and toward the same provider). Its ghost edge gets its own lane, offset from any solid edge between the same cells, and the cell gets a separate **new** badge naming the file.

## 8. Design memory

When a fork is answered:

1. Write `decisions/DR-<n>.md` with front matter `{ id, title, outcome, status: made, type: standing, invariant, anchors: { paths }, rejected: "<option B text>" }` and a short rationale body.
2. Update `domains.yaml`: link the decision to the invariant (option A), or add the path to the invariant's `exceptions` with the DR id (option B). Commit both files and only those (`git commit -- domains.yaml decisions/DR-<n>.md`), so the coding session's uncommitted edits stay out of the commit.
3. Tell Claude, in the next tool result, to record it in Alike with `mcp__alike__record_decision`: title, outcome, rationale (including the rejected option), type `standing`, and code anchors `{ repository, branch, paths }`. Once at session start, have Claude run Alike's `describe_entity_kind` on `decision` to confirm the field names. Emit `decision_recorded` when the call succeeds.

Memory is then used three ways:

- **Provenance:** clicking an edge or cell shows the decisions and turns behind it ("added in turn 3, DR-4").
- **Session brief:** every standing decision goes into `brief()` for every new session (§6).
- **Rejected options stay rejected:** when a plan or edit hits an invariant that has a linked decision, the violation reason says "You decided this in DR-4: <title>," and the ledger counts it as a rejected option blocked.

## 9. Time ledger and turn summary

Counts only; minutes appear only in the pitch, taken from the baseline run (§12).

| Counter | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Lines changed | git `--numstat` added + removed, turn baseline → turn end |
| Cells to review | cells with a finding of severity 1–3 below |
| Forks caught before code | `plan_violation` events resolved before any `edited` event in the turn |
| Rejected options blocked | violations that cited an existing decision |

Severity for the turn summary, loudest first: **1** invariant hit (red) · **2** new cross-domain edge or new external (amber, one glance) · **3** unplanned edit (amber) · **4** everything else in the plan (quiet).

## 10. Load and the cartographer

1. `repo_scanned`: full fact scan (§3).
2. If `domains.yaml` is missing, run the **cartographer**: a separate one-shot `query()` with read-only tools, a smaller model, and `outputFormat` set to the `domains.yaml` JSON schema. Input: the file tree, the import edges and the table writes. Ask it for 5–9 domains in product language, layers suited to the repo, and invariants it can infer from the facts (sole importers of a vendor, sole writers of a table, absent edges). → `map_proposed`.
3. The shell plays the map assembling (`file_assigned` events, staggered about 15 ms apart) and shows the proposal; the user clicks **Confirm** → `map_confirmed`, file written. If the proposal is off, load `fixtures/scout-agent.domains.yaml` instead.
4. Full rule scan → `violation_found` (Scout: DR-1 in `news-summarize.ts`, red).

## 11. The shell

- **Layout:** chat pane on the left (380 px); the grid fills the rest; the turn summary and replay scrubber sit under the grid; the ledger sits top right. The mockups are in Figma, "v2 · Domain grid" page.
- **Cell states:** looked = dashed indigo outline · edited = indigo fill · unplanned = amber · invariant hit = red · ghost = dashed outline at 50% opacity with step badges.
- **Agent cursor:** a small avatar pinned to the current cell, labeled "Claude · reading `retrieve.ts`", easing between cells in 250 ms.
- **Edges:** SVG overlay routed through the gaps between cells; new edges draw in with a stroke-dashoffset animation.
- **Diff counts:** a +/− badge on each edited cell, ticking up.
- **Inspector:** click a cell or edge to see its paths, tables, invariants and provenance.
- **Replay:** a scrubber over the event index; dragging re-reduces the log.
- **Motion rule:** animate only state changes; nothing loops.

## 12. Baseline run, for the pitch

Copy `scout-agent` at the demo commit. In plain Claude Code, run "Add a tool that summarizes a prospect's latest 10-K." Time it, then run `npm run proof`. If the new tool leaks personal data, time a follow-up turn that finds and fixes it. Those minutes are the "without" numbers the pitch converts the ledger into. If the baseline doesn't make the mistake, drop that comparison and lean on lines-to-review and memory.

## 13. Build order and acceptance checks
````

```text
import type { DomainMap } from './schema';
import type { Placement } from './mapper';
import type { ImportEdge, WriteFact, DomainEdge } from './facts';
import type { Violation } from './rules';
import type { PlanStep } from './plan';

export type Cell = { domain: string; layer: string };

export type EventKind =
  | 'repo_scanned' | 'map_proposed' | 'map_confirmed' | 'file_assigned'
  | 'violation_found'
  | 'turn_started' | 'looked' | 'cursor'
  | 'planned' | 'plan_violation' | 'fork_asked' | 'fork_answered' | 'plan_approved'
  | 'gate_blocked' | 'edited' | 'edge_added' | 'edge_removed'
  | 'test_result' | 'decision_recorded' | 'turn_ended'
  // Additions to SPEC §5 so the chat pane and approval button are also reductions of the log.
  | 'chat' | 'approval_requested' | 'error';

export type HarnessEvent = {
  id: string;
  t: number;
  session: string;
  turn: string | null;
  kind: EventKind;
  cell?: Cell;
  path?: string;
  data?: Record<string, unknown>;
};

/** Typed payloads, by kind. The server builds events with `ev()`; the reducer reads them back. */
export type EventData = {
  repo_scanned: { files: { path: string; placement: Placement }[]; imports: ImportEdge[]; writes: WriteFact[]; edges: DomainEdge[] };
  map_proposed: { map: DomainMap; yaml: string };
  map_confirmed: { map: DomainMap; source: 'file' | 'cartographer' | 'fixture' };
  file_assigned: { placement: Placement };
  violation_found: { violations: Violation[] }; // the full current set (replaces)
  turn_started: { prompt: string; head: string; baseline: string };
  looked: { tool: string };
  cursor: { verb: 'reading' | 'searching' | 'editing' };
  planned: {
    steps: PlanStep[];
    cells: { domain: string; layer: string; steps: number[]; files: string[] }[];
    edges: { from: string; to: string; steps: number[]; imports: ImportEdge[] }[];
    unassigned: string[];
  };
  plan_violation: { violation: Violation };
  fork_asked: { violations: Violation[]; text: string };
  fork_answered: { option: 'A' | 'B'; text: string; violations: Violation[] };
  plan_approved: Record<string, never>;
  gate_blocked: { violation: Violation; tool: string };
  edited: { added: number; removed: number; created: boolean; unattributed?: boolean; tool?: string };
  edge_added: { edge: ImportEdge; from: string; to: string };
  edge_removed: { edge: ImportEdge; from: string; to: string };
  test_result: { domain: string; passed: number; failed: number };
  decision_recorded: { id: string; title: string; invariant: string; option: 'A' | 'B'; paths: string[]; alike?: boolean };
  turn_ended: { added: number; removed: number; files: string[]; reason: string };
  chat: { role: 'user' | 'assistant' | 'system'; text: string };
  approval_requested: { plan: string };
  error: { message: string };
};

export const cellKey = (c: Cell) => `${c.domain}/${c.layer}`;
export const edgeKey = (from: string, to: string) => `${from}->${to}`;

export type PlannedCell = { cell: Cell; steps: number[]; files: string[] };
export type PlannedEdge = { from: string; to: string; steps: number[]; imports: ImportEdge[] };

export type TurnState = {
  id: string;
  prompt: string;
  startedAt: number;
  endedAt: number | null;
  steps: PlanStep[];
  planned: Record<string, PlannedCell>;
  plannedEdges: Record<string, PlannedEdge>;
  planViolations: Violation[];
  gateBlocks: Violation[];
  looked: Record<string, string[]>; // cellKey → paths
  edited: Record<string, { added: number; removed: number; files: string[]; created: string[]; unattributed: boolean }>;
  tests: Record<string, string[]>; // domain → test files edited
  unassigned: string[];
  edgesAdded: { from: string; to: string; edge: ImportEdge }[];
  edgesRemoved: { from: string; to: string; edge: ImportEdge }[];
  forks: { asked: number; answered: number | null; option: 'A' | 'B' | null; violations: Violation[]; beforeCode: boolean }[];
  decisions: string[];
  approved: boolean;
  firstEditAt: number | null; // event index of first `edited`
  numstat: { added: number; removed: number } | null;
};

export type DomainEdgeState = { from: string; to: string; files: ImportEdge[] };

export type Decision = EventData['decision_recorded'] & { turn: string | null; at: number };

export type UIState = {
  map: DomainMap | null;
  files: Record<string, Placement>;
  edges: Record<string, DomainEdgeState>;
  violations: Violation[];
  turns: TurnState[];
  current: string | null;
  cursor: { cell: Cell | null; path: string; verb: string } | null;
  chat: { role: 'user' | 'assistant' | 'system'; text: string; turn: string | null; t: number }[];
  awaitingApproval: { turn: string | null; plan: string } | null;
  pendingFork: { turn: string | null; violations: Violation[] } | null;
  decisions: Decision[];
  errors: string[];
  /** event index → provenance lookups */
  edgeOrigin: Record<string, { turn: string | null; at: number }[]>;
  cellOrigin: Record<string, { turn: string | null; at: number }[]>;
};

export function initialState(): UIState {
  return {
    map: null, files: {}, edges: {}, violations: [], turns: [], current: null, cursor: null, chat: [],
    awaitingApproval: null, pendingFork: null, decisions: [], errors: [], edgeOrigin: {}, cellOrigin: {},
  };
}

function newTurn(id: string, prompt: string, t: number): TurnState {
  return {
    id, prompt, startedAt: t, endedAt: null, steps: [], planned: {}, plannedEdges: {}, planViolations: [], gateBlocks: [],
    looked: {}, edited: {}, tests: {}, unassigned: [], edgesAdded: [], edgesRemoved: [], forks: [], decisions: [],
    approved: false, firstEditAt: null, numstat: null,
  };
}

const push = <T>(rec: Record<string, T[]>, k: string, v: T) => { (rec[k] ??= []).push(v); };

/** Fold one event into the state. Mutates and returns `s`; callers that need immutability use `reduce`. */
export function apply(s: UIState, e: HarnessEvent, index: number): UIState {
  const turn = e.turn ? s.turns.find((x) => x.id === e.turn) ?? null : null;
  const d = (e.data ?? {}) as never;

  switch (e.kind) {
    case 'map_confirmed':
    case 'map_proposed': {
      const { map } = d as EventData['map_confirmed'];
      s.map = map;
      break;
    }
    case 'repo_scanned': {
      const { files, edges } = d as EventData['repo_scanned'];
      s.files = {};
      for (const f of files) s.files[f.path] = f.placement;
      s.edges = {};
      for (const ed of edges) s.edges[edgeKey(ed.from, ed.to)] = { from: ed.from, to: ed.to, files: [...ed.files] };
      break;
    }
    case 'file_assigned': {
      if (e.path) s.files[e.path] = (d as EventData['file_assigned']).placement;
      break;
    }
    case 'violation_found':
      s.violations = (d as EventData['violation_found']).violations;
      break;
    case 'turn_started': {
      const t = newTurn(e.turn ?? e.id, (d as EventData['turn_started']).prompt, e.t);
      s.turns.push(t);
      s.current = t.id;
      s.cursor = null;
      break;
    }
    case 'chat': {
      const { role, text } = d as EventData['chat'];
      s.chat.push({ role, text, turn: e.turn, t: e.t });
      break;
    }
    case 'looked':
    case 'cursor': {
      if (e.path) s.cursor = { cell: e.cell ?? null, path: e.path, verb: e.kind === 'cursor' ? (d as EventData['cursor']).verb : 'reading' };
      if (e.kind === 'looked' && turn && e.cell && e.path) {
        const k = cellKey(e.cell);
        const list = (turn.looked[k] ??= []);
        if (!list.includes(e.path)) list.push(e.path);
      }
      break;
    }
    case 'planned': {
      if (!turn) break;
      const p = d as EventData['planned'];
      turn.steps = p.steps;
      turn.planned = {};
      for (const c of p.cells) turn.planned[cellKey(c)] = { cell: { domain: c.domain, layer: c.layer }, steps: c.steps, files: c.files };
      turn.plannedEdges = {};
      for (const ed of p.edges) turn.plannedEdges[edgeKey(ed.from, ed.to)] = ed;
      turn.unassigned = p.unassigned;
      turn.planViolations = []; // a resubmitted plan replaces the previous one's violations
      break;
    }
    case 'plan_violation':
      turn?.planViolations.push((d as EventData['plan_violation']).violation);
      break;
    case 'gate_blocked':
      turn?.gateBlocks.push((d as EventData['gate_blocked']).violation);
      break;
    case 'fork_asked': {
      const { violations } = d as EventData['fork_asked'];
      s.pendingFork = { turn: e.turn, violations };
      turn?.forks.push({ asked: index, answered: null, option: null, violations, beforeCode: turn.firstEditAt === null });
      break;
    }
    case 'fork_answered': {
      const { option } = d as EventData['fork_answered'];
      s.pendingFork = null;
      const f = turn?.forks.findLast((x) => x.answered === null);
      if (f) { f.answered = index; f.option = option; f.beforeCode = f.beforeCode && turn!.firstEditAt === null; }
      break;
    }
    case 'approval_requested':
      s.awaitingApproval = { turn: e.turn, plan: (d as EventData['approval_requested']).plan };
      break;
    case 'plan_approved':
      s.awaitingApproval = null;
      if (turn) turn.approved = true;
      break;
    case 'edited': {
      const ed = d as EventData['edited'];
      if (s.cursor && e.path && !ed.unattributed) s.cursor = { cell: e.cell ?? null, path: e.path, verb: 'editing' };
      if (!turn || !e.path) break;
      if (turn.firstEditAt === null) turn.firstEditAt = index;
      const placement = s.files[e.path];
      if (placement?.kind === 'test') { push(turn.tests, placement.domain, e.path); break; }
      if (!e.cell) { if (!turn.unassigned.includes(e.path)) turn.unassigned.push(e.path); break; }
      const k = cellKey(e.cell);
      const c = (turn.edited[k] ??= { added: 0, removed: 0, files: [], created: [], unattributed: false });
      c.added += ed.added;
      c.removed += ed.removed;
      if (!c.files.includes(e.path)) c.files.push(e.path);
      if (ed.created && !c.created.includes(e.path)) c.created.push(e.path);
      if (ed.unattributed) c.unattributed = true;
      push(s.cellOrigin, k, { turn: e.turn, at: index });
      break;
    }
    case 'edge_added': {
      const { edge, from, to } = d as EventData['edge_added'];
      const k = edgeKey(from, to);
      const cur = (s.edges[k] ??= { from, to, files: [] });
      if (!cur.files.some((f) => f.from === edge.from && f.to === edge.to)) cur.files.push(edge);
      push(s.edgeOrigin, k, { turn: e.turn, at: index });
      turn?.edgesAdded.push({ from, to, edge });
      break;
    }
    case 'edge_removed': {
      const { edge, from, to } = d as EventData['edge_removed'];
      const k = edgeKey(from, to);
      const cur = s.edges[k];
      if (cur) {
        cur.files = cur.files.filter((f) => !(f.from === edge.from && f.to === edge.to));
        if (!cur.files.length) delete s.edges[k];
      }
      turn?.edgesRemoved.push({ from, to, edge });
      break;
    }
    case 'decision_recorded': {
      const dec = d as EventData['decision_recorded'];
      const existing = s.decisions.find((x) => x.id === dec.id);
      if (existing) Object.assign(existing, dec); // the Alike confirmation re-emits with alike: true
      else s.decisions.push({ ...dec, turn: e.turn, at: index });
      if (turn && !turn.decisions.includes(dec.id)) turn.decisions.push(dec.id);
      break;
    }
    case 'turn_ended': {
      if (!turn) break;
      const { added, removed } = d as EventData['turn_ended'];
      turn.endedAt = e.t;
      turn.numstat = { added, removed };
      s.awaitingApproval = null;
      if (s.current === turn.id) s.cursor = null;
      break;
    }
    case 'error':
      s.errors.push((d as EventData['error']).message);
      break;
    case 'test_result':
      break;
  }
  return s;
}

/** UI state = reduce(events). Replay is `reduce(events, i)`: the state after the first `i` events. */
export function reduce(events: readonly HarnessEvent[], upTo = events.length): UIState {
  const s = initialState();
  const n = Math.min(upTo, events.length);
  for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) apply(s, events[i]!, i);
  return s;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- derived views

export type CellView = {
  cell: Cell;
  looked: boolean;
  edited: boolean;
  ghost: number[] | null; // planned step numbers while not yet edited
  unplanned: boolean; // amber: edited but not in this turn's plan
  violation: 'existing' | 'new' | null;
  violationFiles: string[];
  newViolationFiles: string[];
  added: number;
  removed: number;
};

/** Per-cell visual state for one turn (defaults to the latest), plus load-time violations. */
export function cellViews(s: UIState, turnId: string | null = s.turns.at(-1)?.id ?? null): Record<string, CellView> {
  const out: Record<string, CellView> = {};
  const map = s.map;
  if (!map) return out;
  const turn = turnId ? s.turns.find((t) => t.id === turnId) ?? null : null;
  const hasPlan = !!turn && Object.keys(turn.planned).length > 0;

  for (const dom of map.domains) {
    for (const layer of map.layers) {
      if (!(layer.id in dom.cells)) continue;
      const cell = { domain: dom.id, layer: layer.id };
      const k = cellKey(cell);
      const edited = turn?.edited[k];
      const planned = turn?.planned[k];
      out[k] = {
        cell,
        looked: !!turn?.looked[k]?.length,
        edited: !!edited,
        ghost: planned && !edited ? planned.steps : null,
        unplanned: hasPlan && !!edited && !planned,
        violation: null,
        violationFiles: [],
        newViolationFiles: [],
        added: edited?.added ?? 0,
        removed: edited?.removed ?? 0,
      };
    }
  }
  const mark = (file: string, isNew: boolean, planCell?: Cell) => {
    const p = s.files[file];
    const cell = p?.kind === 'cell' ? { domain: p.domain, layer: p.layer } : planCell;
    if (!cell) return;
    const v = out[cellKey(cell)];
    if (!v) return;
    if (isNew) {
      v.violation = 'new';
      if (!v.newViolationFiles.includes(file)) v.newViolationFiles.push(file);
    } else {
      v.violation ??= 'existing';
      if (!v.violationFiles.includes(file)) v.violationFiles.push(file);
    }
  };
  for (const v of s.violations) mark(v.file, false);
  if (turn) {
    const plannedCellOf = (file: string) => Object.values(turn.planned).find((c) => c.files.includes(file))?.cell;
    for (const v of [...turn.planViolations, ...turn.gateBlocks]) {
      if (s.violations.some((x) => x.file === v.file && x.invariant === v.invariant)) continue; // already on the map before this turn
      mark(v.file, true, plannedCellOf(v.file));
    }
  }
  return out;
}

export type EdgeView = {
  from: string;
  to: string;
  state: 'existing' | 'ghost' | 'new';
  violation: boolean;
  steps: number[];
  files: ImportEdge[];
};

/**
 * Edges for one turn. A planned edge always gets its own `ghost` entry, even when a solid edge between the same
 * domains exists, so a plan that repeats an existing violation still looks different from the map before the turn.
 */
export function edgeViews(s: UIState, turnId: string | null = s.turns.at(-1)?.id ?? null): EdgeView[] {
  const turn = turnId ? s.turns.find((t) => t.id === turnId) ?? null : null;
  const violating = (from: string, files: ImportEdge[], list: Violation[]) =>
    list.some((v) => files.some((f) => f.from === v.file && (!v.target || v.target === f.to)));
  const out: EdgeView[] = [];
  const addedThisTurn = new Set(turn?.edgesAdded.map((x) => edgeKey(x.from, x.to)) ?? []);
  for (const [k, e] of Object.entries(s.edges)) {
    out.push({ from: e.from, to: e.to, state: addedThisTurn.has(k) ? 'new' : 'existing', violation: violating(e.from, e.files, s.violations), steps: [], files: e.files });
  }
  if (turn) {
    for (const pe of Object.values(turn.plannedEdges)) {
      const built = pe.imports.every((imp) => s.edges[edgeKey(pe.from, pe.to)]?.files.some((f) => f.from === imp.from && f.to === imp.to));
      if (built) continue;
      out.push({ from: pe.from, to: pe.to, state: 'ghost', violation: violating(pe.from, pe.imports, turn.planViolations), steps: pe.steps, files: pe.imports });
    }
  }
  return out;
}

/** Decisions and turns behind an edge or a cell, for the inspector. */
export function provenance(s: UIState, target: { edge: string } | { cell: string }) {
  const origins = 'edge' in target ? s.edgeOrigin[target.edge] ?? [] : s.cellOrigin[target.cell] ?? [];
  const turnIds = [...new Set(origins.map((o) => o.turn).filter((x): x is string => !!x))];
  const turns = turnIds.map((id) => ({ id, index: s.turns.findIndex((t) => t.id === id) + 1, prompt: s.turns.find((t) => t.id === id)?.prompt ?? '' }));
  const decisions = s.decisions.filter((d) => d.turn && turnIds.includes(d.turn));
  return { turns, decisions };
}
import { cellKey, type Cell, type TurnState, type UIState } from './events';
import type { Violation } from './rules';

export type Severity = 1 | 2 | 3 | 4;

export type Finding = {
  severity: Severity;
  kind: 'invariant' | 'new_edge' | 'new_external' | 'unplanned' | 'planned';
  cell: Cell | null;
  text: string;
  files: string[];
  invariant?: string;
};

export type TurnLedger = {
  turn: string;
  linesChanged: number | null; // null until turn_ended brings the git numstat
  cellsToReview: number;
  forksCaughtBeforeCode: number;
  rejectedOptionsBlocked: number;
  findings: Finding[];
};

export type Ledger = {
  turns: TurnLedger[];
  session: { linesChanged: number; cellsToReview: number; forksCaughtBeforeCode: number; rejectedOptionsBlocked: number };
};

const vkey = (v: Violation) => `${v.invariant}|${v.file}|${v.target ?? ''}`;

function cellOf(s: UIState, turn: TurnState, file: string): Cell | null {
  const p = s.files[file];
  if (p?.kind === 'cell') return { domain: p.domain, layer: p.layer };
  return Object.values(turn.planned).find((c) => c.files.includes(file))?.cell ?? null;
}

/** Severity-ranked findings for one turn (SPEC §9): 1 invariant hit · 2 new edge / new external · 3 unplanned · 4 planned. */
export function turnFindings(s: UIState, turn: TurnState): Finding[] {
  const out: Finding[] = [];
  const seen = new Set<string>();
  for (const v of [...turn.planViolations, ...turn.gateBlocks]) {
    if (seen.has(vkey(v))) continue;
    seen.add(vkey(v));
    out.push({ severity: 1, kind: 'invariant', cell: cellOf(s, turn, v.file), text: v.reason, files: [v.file], invariant: v.invariant });
  }
  const edges = new Map<string, { from: string; to: string; files: string[] }>();
  for (const e of turn.edgesAdded) {
    const k = `${e.from}->${e.to}`;
    const cur = edges.get(k) ?? { from: e.from, to: e.to, files: [] };
    if (!cur.files.includes(e.edge.from)) cur.files.push(e.edge.from);
    edges.set(k, cur);
  }
  for (const e of edges.values()) {
    const p = s.files[e.files[0]!];
    const cell = p?.kind === 'cell' ? { domain: p.domain, layer: p.layer } : null;
    out.push({ severity: 2, kind: 'new_edge', cell, text: `New dependency: ${name(s, e.from)} → ${name(s, e.to)}`, files: e.files });
  }
  const hasPlan = Object.keys(turn.planned).length > 0;
  for (const [k, c] of Object.entries(turn.edited)) {
    const [domain, layer] = k.split('/') as [string, string];
    const cell = { domain, layer };
    if (layer === 'external' && c.created.length) {
      out.push({ severity: 2, kind: 'new_external', cell, text: `New external service in ${name(s, domain)}`, files: c.created });
    }
    if (hasPlan && !turn.planned[k]) {
      out.push({ severity: 3, kind: 'unplanned', cell, text: `Edited ${name(s, domain)} · ${layer} without planning it`, files: c.files });
    } else {
      out.push({ severity: 4, kind: 'planned', cell, text: `${name(s, domain)} · ${layer}: ${c.files.length} file(s), +${c.added} −${c.removed}`, files: c.files });
    }
  }
  for (const file of turn.unassigned) {
    if (hasPlan && !Object.values(turn.planned).some((c) => c.files.includes(file))) {
      out.push({ severity: 3, kind: 'unplanned', cell: null, text: `Edited ${file}, which belongs to no domain`, files: [file] });
    }
  }
  return out.sort((a, b) => a.severity - b.severity);
}

function name(s: UIState, domain: string) {
  return s.map?.domains.find((d) => d.id === domain)?.name ?? domain;
}

export function turnLedger(s: UIState, turn: TurnState): TurnLedger {
  const findings = turnFindings(s, turn);
  const review = new Set(findings.filter((f) => f.severity <= 3).map((f) => (f.cell ? cellKey(f.cell) : `file:${f.files[0]}`)));
  // A fork counts once per distinct plan violation it resolved, if it was answered before any edit in the turn.
  let forks = 0;
  for (const f of turn.forks) {
    if (f.answered === null || !f.beforeCode) continue;
    forks += f.violations.filter((v) => turn.planViolations.some((p) => vkey(p) === vkey(v))).length;
  }
  const rejected = new Set([...turn.planViolations, ...turn.gateBlocks].filter((v) => v.decision).map(vkey)).size;
  return {
    turn: turn.id,
    linesChanged: turn.numstat ? turn.numstat.added + turn.numstat.removed : null,
    cellsToReview: review.size,
    forksCaughtBeforeCode: forks,
    rejectedOptionsBlocked: rejected,
    findings,
  };
}

export function ledger(s: UIState): Ledger {
  const turns = s.turns.map((t) => turnLedger(s, t));
  const sum = (f: (t: TurnLedger) => number) => turns.reduce((a, t) => a + f(t), 0);
  return {
    turns,
    session: {
      linesChanged: sum((t) => t.linesChanged ?? 0),
      cellsToReview: sum((t) => t.cellsToReview),
      forksCaughtBeforeCode: sum((t) => t.forksCaughtBeforeCode),
      rejectedOptionsBlocked: sum((t) => t.rejectedOptionsBlocked),
    },
  };
}
// Browser-safe entry for the shell: the reducer, derived views and ledger, with no node builtins.

export * from './ledger';

export type { Placement } from './mapper';
export type { ImportEdge, WriteFact, DomainEdge } from './facts';
export type { Violation } from './rules';
export type { PlanStep } from './plan';
```
