```text
## Idea and selling point

You keep talking to your coding agent in text; a live map of your product shows what each turn did to its architecture, and the agent stops before crossing a line you drew.

**One-liner:** Text in, architecture out.

**Contrast line:** Graphify gives the agent a map of your code; this gives you a map of what the agent is doing to it.

**The bottleneck (theme: give people their time back).** Agents now change code faster than people can follow. The time goes to re-reading diffs, re-explaining context, and untangling structure that drifted while nobody was looking. Chat shows what the agent said, not what it did to your system.

**Thesis.** Chat is the right input and the wrong output. Text has no skill tax, so it stays the way you give instructions. But a transcript can't show you that a change you asked for in Checkout also touched Accounts. The human's role has shifted from author to supervisor, and a supervisor needs a map, not a log.

**Time.** Before AI tools, professional developers already spent about 58% of their time on program comprehension ([Xia et al., IEEE TSE 2018](https://ink.library.smu.edu.sg/sis_research/3779)). In METR's 2025 trial, experienced open-source developers using AI took 19% longer and still believed they had been sped up; the time went to prompting, reviewing and integrating ([InfoQ](https://www.infoq.com/news/2025/07/ai-productivity)). The product removes three time sinks: reading diffs to see what changed (the footprint), redoing work after a wrong direction is found (the fork before code), and re-explaining decisions to each new session (design memory).

**What makes it different**

- **It observes the agent, not the codebase.** Static maps (Graphify, DeepWiki) describe code. This shows each turn's footprint, where the agent looked, and how far it strayed from what you asked.
- **Exception-driven.** Quiet when a turn stays in its stripe; loud on new coupling, writes into another domain's data, or edits outside scope.
- **Readable by anyone.** Boxes are named in product language (Checkout, Seat inventory) with the code underneath.
- **Works with the agent you already use.** Real Claude Code runs underneath; adapters for Cursor and Codex come later.

**Pitch lines:** "Chat is the right input and the wrong output." · "A normal change is a vertical stripe. Sideways spread is news."

## What the human does

The human supervises instead of authoring: four cheap actions, none of which need architectural vocabulary. Every instruction still goes through chat; there is no gesture grammar.

- **Point.** Click cells to make them nouns in your next message ("make these two stop talking"). Text is good at saying what you want and bad at saying which thing.
- **Judge.** Each turn ends with its footprint and a ranked summary. Approve or push back in chat.
- **Fence.** Mark a scope or a "don't touch" cell. The gate enforces it.
- **Interrupt.** See the agent wander into another domain and stop it before it writes code.

### What a block represents

A block is the smallest unit you'd have an opinion about: columns are product domains, rows are layers, so a normal change is a vertical stripe and sideways spread is news.

- **Size test:** 5–9 domains on screen, and a typical turn lights up 1–3 cells. If every turn lights everything, the map carries no signal; if there are 40 boxes, nobody reads it.
- **Why not layers:** Web, API and DB boxes light up on every feature. Quick-buy lit 3 of 3 in the first mockup.
- **Naming:** product language on the box; files and endpoints live in the inspector.
- **Depth is local:** you only see deeper wiring inside the thing you zoomed into, never the whole system at class level. Files appear only as evidence on what a turn touched. See the levels below.
- **Edges:** only edges between domains are drawn. Flow down a column is implied.

Scout, the demo repo (rows are read from the map, so an agent system gets Entry / Logic / Data / External):

|  | Channels | Agent loop | Research tools | Model gateway | Memory | Outreach |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Entry | HTTP, webhook, CLI | — | — | — | — | — |
| Logic | Validation | Run loop, planner, tool registry | Search, profile, news digest, news summary | complete(), embed(), redaction, fallback | Retrieval, vector index | Draft email, send |
| Data | — | runs | — | cost\_log | notes, embeddings | contacts, outreach\_log |
| External | — | — | Search, News, SEC EDGAR, Enrichment | OpenAI, Anthropic, Embeddings | — | CRM, Email |

### Levels of abstraction

Five levels, each a rollup of the same fact graph, and the agent's footprint carries through all of them: an edited cell is an edited endpoint is an edited function.

| Level | Shows | Built from |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Journeys | A user flow such as "buy a ticket" as a path across domains | Routes and UI entry points traced through the fact graph, named by the cartographer |
| Domains | The domain × layer grid | `domains.yaml` mapping over the fact graph |
| Inside a domain | Endpoints, tables, jobs | Parsed routes, the Prisma schema, job config |
| Wiring | One call chain across cells, e.g. EventCard → POST /orders/quick → reserve() → prisma.seat.update | Graphify's symbol graph, drawn as a trace; calls leaving the component are stubs labeled with their cell |
| Code | The file itself | — |

The wiring level is a trace rather than a full class graph because the question people have at that depth is "how does this get there?" Sunday ships Domains and Inside a domain; Journeys and the wiring trace are stretch.

### Signals, loudest first

1. A new dependency between domains (new coupling).
2. A write into data another domain owns (the invariant case).
3. Edits outside the domains the request named, or outside the agent's own plan.
4. A new external service or package.
5. Edits inside the requested stripe, which stay quiet.

Cell states on the map: looked at (dashed), edited (filled), edited outside scope (amber), touches an invariant (red). Mockups: [Figma, v2 page](https://www.figma.com/design/PsNVwSXxGSerMVsNnbomKu).

## What the agent gets

The agent is ordinary Claude Code. The harness adds the domain map as context, observes every tool call, and gates edits that cross an invariant.

- **Context, once per session.** The domain map and invariants are appended to Claude Code's system prompt. Scope is inferred from each prompt in the background for the canvas; it never delays the agent.
- **Plan.** Each turn starts in plan mode: the agent explores read-only, then calls `submit_plan` with the cells it will touch, the edges it will add, and numbered steps. Invariant checks run on the plan, so a fork surfaces before any code exists.
- **Graph tools (read-only MCP).** `cell_for(path)`, `domain(id)` (cells, invariants, files) and `who_writes(table)`, so the agent can check ownership while planning.
- **Observe.** Hooks on Read, Grep and Glob mark cells as looked at and move the agent cursor. Hooks after Edit and Write fill cells and recompute that file's cross-domain imports. These hooks return async, so they never slow the agent.
- **Gate (the backstop).** A pre-edit hook runs the same deterministic checks during editing: writes into data another domain owns, new imports across domains, edits outside a fence. On a hit it returns `permissionDecision: "deny"` with a reason that names the options and tells Claude to ask you.
- **Record.** Each answered fork becomes a decision (DR-n) in `decisions/` and in Alike, so later sessions inherit it.

## Plan versus built

Planning and implementation share one map: the plan draws a ghost footprint, edits fill it in, and anything done without being planned shows amber.

- **Plan.** Claude Code's plan mode explores without editing. `submit_plan` returns cells, edges and steps, drawn as dashed ghosts with step numbers. A ghost that crosses an invariant is red, and the agent asks you A or B before writing any code.
- **Approve.** You approve in chat, and the session switches from plan mode to editing.
- **Build.** As edits land, ghost cells fill solid and the step counter advances. That's progress, laid out on the architecture.
- **End-of-turn diff.** This is the overfitting detector: it shows when the agent strays from its own plan.

|  | Planned | Not planned |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Done | Solid | Amber: did something it didn't say it would |
| Not done | Ghost stays | — |

## Live activity

Every visual here comes from the same hook event stream, so each one is cheap once events flow. Each motion encodes a state change; nothing loops for decoration.

- **Agent cursor.** An avatar sits on the cell the agent is reading or editing and moves with it, like a collaborator's cursor in Figma. Teammates' agents later become more cursors.
- **Fill-in progress.** Ghosts fill as steps complete, with a step counter ("3 of 6").
- **Live diff counts.** Lines added and removed tick up on each cell.
- **Edge draw-in.** A new cross-domain edge draws itself when the import appears.
- **Tests on the map.** When the agent runs tests, the cells they cover flash green or red.
- **Replay scrubber.** Every event is logged, so you can scrub a turn to watch it again or catch up on what happened while you were away.

Priority for Sunday: cursor and pulse, then plan ghosts with the drift diff, then replay, then edge draw-in. Tests on cells and the wiring trace are stretch.

7:**For the build, two specs are the source of truth as of Oct 11:** `SPEC.md` (the harness) and `DEMO_REPO_SPEC.md` (Scout, the demo repo). This doc keeps the reasoning behind them.
15:| Demo repo is Scout, an agentic sales research system with mocked APIs | Representative of what an AI audience builds; the gateway rule reads instantly; one existing gateway bypass shows red on load | TicketDrop, a ticketing web app |
16:| Two repos: harness and the demo target | The agent works inside the target, and the tool's own code must not appear on the map | One monorepo |
34:| Build-first demo around one fork | The difference is deciding before code is written | Rescuing a messy repo |
80:Scout, the demo repo (rows are read from the map, so an agent system gets Entry / Logic / Data / External):
322:Every fork you answer becomes an Alike decision, so the next session, yours or a teammate's, gets the rule before it edits. Alike's demo shows exactly this "stopped before the rework" moment, which makes it a natural pairing.
344:Get the live footprint and agent cursor working by hour 3, plan ghosts by 4 and the gate by 5, then freeze features an hour before demos.
348:The riskiest piece, the gate stopping Claude and Claude asking in chat, sits mid-day, once there's a grid to show it on. Test early that Claude reliably asks after a deny instead of trying another route; the demo rests on it. Edit the rows to match the event's real start and demo times.
359:**Demo script (about 3 minutes)**
381:- [ ] Dispatch the Scout build from `DEMO_REPO_SPEC.md` in its own repo
```

```text
import { existsSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { join, resolve, dirname } from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import { Hono } from 'hono';
import { serve } from '@hono/node-server';
import { serveStatic } from '@hono/node-server/serve-static';
import { WebSocketServer, type WebSocket } from 'ws';
import { Bus } from './bus';
import { Repo } from './repo';
import { Session } from './session';
import { commitPaths } from './git';
import { proposeMap } from './cartographer';

const here = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
const REPO = process.env.HARNESS_REPO ? resolve(process.cwd(), process.env.HARNESS_REPO) : '';
if (!REPO || !existsSync(REPO)) {
  console.error(`Set HARNESS_REPO to the target repo (got "${process.env.HARNESS_REPO ?? ''}").`);
  process.exit(1);
}
const PORT = Number(process.env.PORT ?? 4310);
const FALLBACK_MAP = resolve(here, '../../../fixtures/scout-agent.domains.yaml');

const bus = new Bus(REPO, { fresh: process.env.HARNESS_FRESH === '1' });
const sockets = new Set<WebSocket>();
const broadcast = (msg: unknown) => {
  const s = JSON.stringify(msg);
  for (const ws of sockets) if (ws.readyState === ws.OPEN) ws.send(s);
};
bus.on((event) => broadcast({ type: 'event', event }));

const repo = new Repo(REPO, bus);
let session: Session | null = null;
let proposal: { yaml: string; source: 'cartographer' | 'fixture' } | null = null;
let busy = false;

function startSession() {
  repo.scan();
  repo.startWatcher();
  session = new Session(repo, bus, (m) => {
    if (m.type === 'busy') busy = m.busy;
    broadcast(m);
  });
  session.start();
}

/** Load: use domains.yaml if present; otherwise propose one (cartographer, else the fixture) and wait for Confirm. */
async function load() {
  if (repo.hasMap()) {
    repo.loadMapFile();
    bus.emit('map_confirmed', { map: repo.map, source: 'file' }, { turn: null });
    startSession();
    return;
  }
  let yaml: string;
  let source: 'cartographer' | 'fixture' = 'cartographer';
  try {
    if (process.env.HARNESS_CARTOGRAPHER === '0') throw new Error('disabled');
    yaml = await proposeMap(repo, bus);
  } catch (e) {
    if ((e as Error).message !== 'disabled') bus.emit('error', { message: `Cartographer failed, using the reference map: ${(e as Error).message}` }, { turn: null });
    yaml = readFileSync(FALLBACK_MAP, 'utf8');
    source = 'fixture';
  }
  showProposal(yaml, source);
}

function showProposal(yaml: string, source: 'cartographer' | 'fixture') {
  repo.setMap(yaml);
  proposal = { yaml, source };
  bus.emit('map_proposed', { map: repo.map, yaml }, { turn: null });
  // The shell plays the map assembling: one file_assigned per file, ~15 ms apart.
  const files = repo.listFiles();
  files.forEach((path, i) => setTimeout(() => bus.emit('file_assigned', { placement: repo.place(path) }, { path, turn: null }), i * 15));
}

const app = new Hono();
app.get('/api/info', (c) => c.json({ repo: REPO, session: bus.session, busy, proposal: !!proposal }));
app.get('/api/events', (c) => c.json(bus.events));
app.post('/api/chat', async (c) => {
  const { text } = await c.req.json<{ text: string }>();
  if (!session) return c.json({ error: 'Confirm the map first.' }, 409);
  session.userMessage(text);
  return c.json({ ok: true });
});
app.post('/api/approve', (c) => { session?.approve(); return c.json({ ok: true }); });
app.post('/api/interrupt', (c) => { session?.interrupt(); return c.json({ ok: true }); });
app.post('/api/map/confirm', (c) => {
  if (!proposal) return c.json({ error: 'No proposal pending.' }, 409);
  writeFileSync(repo.mapPath, proposal.yaml);
  try { commitPaths(repo.root, ['domains.yaml'], 'docs: add domains.yaml architecture map'); }
  catch (e) { bus.emit('error', { message: `Could not commit domains.yaml: ${(e as Error).message}` }, { turn: null }); }
  repo.setMap(proposal.yaml);
  bus.emit('map_confirmed', { map: repo.map, source: proposal.source }, { turn: null });
  proposal = null;
  startSession();
  return c.json({ ok: true });
});
app.post('/api/map/fallback', (c) => {
  if (!proposal) return c.json({ error: 'No proposal pending.' }, 409);
  showProposal(readFileSync(FALLBACK_MAP, 'utf8'), 'fixture');
  return c.json({ ok: true });
});
app.get('/api/file', (c) => {
  const p = c.req.query('path') ?? '';
  const rel = repo.rel(p);
  if (!rel || !existsSync(join(repo.root, rel))) return c.json({ error: 'not found' }, 404);
  return c.text(readFileSync(join(repo.root, rel), 'utf8'));
});

const shellDist = resolve(here, '../../shell/dist');
if (existsSync(shellDist)) app.use('/*', serveStatic({ root: shellDist }));

const server = serve({ fetch: app.fetch, port: PORT }, () => console.log(`Harness server on http://localhost:${PORT} · repo ${REPO}`));
const wss = new WebSocketServer({ server: server as never, path: '/ws' });
wss.on('connection', (ws) => {
  sockets.add(ws);
  ws.send(JSON.stringify({ type: 'hello', events: bus.events, busy, session: bus.session }));
  ws.on('close', () => sockets.delete(ws));
});

void load();

# Reference map for the Scout demo repo.
# Live, the cartographer proposes this on load and the user confirms it.
# This copy is the test fixture for packages/core and the fallback if the
# cartographer's proposal is off on stage.

version: 1

layers:
  - { id: entry,    name: Entry }
  - { id: logic,    name: Logic }
  - { id: data,     name: Data }
  - { id: external, name: External }

# Paths that belong to no domain and never create cross-domain edges.
neutral: ["src/shared/**", "vendor/_calllog.ts"]
ignore: ["node_modules/**", ".git/**", ".harness/**", "fixtures/**", "scripts/**", "decisions/**", "*.json", "*.md", "*.config.ts", ".gitignore", "domains.yaml"]

domains:
  - id: channels
    name: Channels
    purpose: Take requests from HTTP and the CLI
    cells:
      entry: { paths: ["src/channels/routes.ts", "src/channels/cli.ts"] }
      logic: { paths: ["src/channels/validate.ts"] }
    tests: ["test/channels/**"]

  - id: orchestrator
    name: Agent loop
    purpose: Plan each run and call tools in order
    cells:
      logic: { paths: ["src/orchestrator/agent.ts", "src/orchestrator/planner.ts", "src/orchestrator/tool-registry.ts"] }
      data:  { paths: ["src/orchestrator/run-state.ts"], tables: ["runs"] }
    tests: ["test/orchestrator/**"]

  - id: tools
    name: Research tools
    purpose: Look up companies, news and filings
    cells:
      logic:    { paths: ["src/tools/**"] }
      external: { paths: ["vendor/search/**", "vendor/news/**", "vendor/sec-edgar/**", "vendor/enrichment/**"] }
    tests: ["test/tools/**"]

  - id: gateway
    name: Model gateway
    purpose: Every model call, with redaction and cost logging
    cells:
      logic:    { paths: ["src/gateway/complete.ts", "src/gateway/embed.ts", "src/gateway/redact.ts", "src/gateway/providers.ts"] }
      data:     { paths: ["src/gateway/cost-ledger.ts"], tables: ["cost_log"] }
      external: { paths: ["vendor/llm-openai/**", "vendor/llm-anthropic/**", "vendor/embeddings/**"] }
    tests: ["test/gateway/**"]

  - id: memory
    name: Memory
    purpose: Store and retrieve notes about each company
    cells:
      logic: { paths: ["src/memory/retrieve.ts", "src/memory/vector-index.ts"] }
      data:  { paths: ["src/memory/notes-store.ts"], tables: ["notes", "embeddings"] }
    tests: ["test/memory/**"]

  - id: outreach
    name: Outreach
    purpose: Draft emails and keep the CRM in sync
    cells:
      logic:    { paths: ["src/outreach/draft-email.ts", "src/outreach/send.ts"] }
      data:     { paths: ["src/outreach/crm-sync.ts", "src/outreach/outreach-log.ts"], tables: ["contacts", "outreach_log"] }
      external: { paths: ["vendor/crm/**", "vendor/email/**"] }
    tests: ["test/outreach/**"]

# Seeded by the cartographer on load (source: cartographer), confirmed by the user.
# Runtime decisions get the next free id (DR-4, DR-5, ...) and live in decisions/.
invariants:
  - id: DR-1
    rule: Model providers are only called through the model gateway
    kind: only_via
    targets: ["vendor/llm-*/**", "vendor/embeddings/**"]
    allowed_from: [gateway]
    exceptions: []
    source: cartographer

  - id: DR-2
    rule: Each table is written only by the domain that owns it
    kind: owns_writes
    owners: { runs: orchestrator, cost_log: gateway, notes: memory, embeddings: memory, contacts: outreach, outreach_log: outreach }
    exceptions: []
    source: cartographer

  - id: DR-3
    rule: Research tools never depend on outreach
    kind: no_edge
    from: tools
    to: outreach
    exceptions: []
    source: cartographer
import { z } from 'zod';
import YAML from 'yaml';

const LayerSchema = z.object({ id: z.string(), name: z.string() });

const CellSchema = z.object({
  paths: z.array(z.string()).optional(),
  tables: z.array(z.string()).optional(),
});

const DomainSchema = z.object({
  id: z.string(),
  name: z.string(),
  purpose: z.string(),
  cells: z.record(z.string(), CellSchema),
  tests: z.array(z.string()).optional(),
});

/** An exception may be written as a bare path string; it is normalized to `{ path }`. */
const ExceptionSchema = z.union([
  z.string().transform((path): { path: string; decision?: string } => ({ path })),
  z.object({ path: z.string(), decision: z.string().optional() }),
]);

const InvariantBase = z.object({
  id: z.string(),
  rule: z.string(),
  exceptions: z.array(ExceptionSchema).default([]),
  source: z.string().optional(),
  /** Decision records (DR ids) that confirmed this invariant. */
  decisions: z.array(z.string()).optional(),
});

const InvariantSchema = z.discriminatedUnion('kind', [
  InvariantBase.extend({
    kind: z.literal('only_via'),
    targets: z.array(z.string()),
    allowed_from: z.array(z.string()),
  }),
  InvariantBase.extend({
    kind: z.literal('owns_writes'),
    owners: z.record(z.string(), z.string()),
  }),
  InvariantBase.extend({
    kind: z.literal('no_edge'),
    from: z.string(),
    to: z.string(),
  }),
]);

/** Schema for a target repo's `domains.yaml`. */
export const DomainMapSchema = z
  .object({
    version: z.number(),
    layers: z.array(LayerSchema),
    neutral: z.array(z.string()).optional(),
    ignore: z.array(z.string()).optional(),
    domains: z.array(DomainSchema),
    invariants: z.array(InvariantSchema).default([]),
  })
  .superRefine((map, ctx) => {
    const layers = new Set(map.layers.map((l) => l.id));
    const domains = new Set(map.domains.map((d) => d.id));
    const issue = (path: (string | number)[], message: string) => ctx.addIssue({ code: 'custom', path, message });
    map.domains.forEach((d, i) => {
      for (const layer of Object.keys(d.cells)) {
        if (!layers.has(layer)) issue(['domains', i, 'cells', layer], `unknown layer "${layer}"`);
      }
    });
    map.invariants.forEach((inv, i) => {
      const refs =
        inv.kind === 'only_via' ? inv.allowed_from : inv.kind === 'owns_writes' ? Object.values(inv.owners) : [inv.from, inv.to];
      for (const ref of refs) {
        if (!domains.has(ref)) issue(['invariants', i], `${inv.id} refers to unknown domain "${ref}"`);
      }
    });
  });

export type DomainMap = z.output<typeof DomainMapSchema>;
export type Layer = DomainMap['layers'][number];
export type Domain = DomainMap['domains'][number];
export type Invariant = DomainMap['invariants'][number];
export type InvariantException = Invariant['exceptions'][number];

/** Parse and validate `domains.yaml` text. Throws an Error with a readable message. */
export function parseDomainMap(yamlText: string): DomainMap {
  let raw: unknown;
  try {
    raw = YAML.parse(yamlText);
  } catch (err) {
    throw new Error(`domains.yaml is not valid YAML: ${(err as Error).message}`);
  }
  const result = DomainMapSchema.safeParse(raw);
  if (!result.success) throw new Error(`domains.yaml is invalid:\n${z.prettifyError(result.error)}`);
  return result.data;
}
import picomatch from 'picomatch';
import type { DomainMap } from './schema';

export type Placement =
  | { kind: 'cell'; domain: string; layer: string }
  | { kind: 'test'; domain: string }
  | { kind: 'neutral' }
  | { kind: 'ignored' }
  | { kind: 'unassigned' };

export type Mapper = ReturnType<typeof createMapper>;

const globCache = new Map<string, (path: string) => boolean>();

/** Compiled, cached picomatch matcher for a single glob (exact paths match themselves). */
export function globMatcher(glob: string): (path: string) => boolean {
  let m = globCache.get(glob);
  if (!m) {
    m = picomatch(glob, { dot: true });
    globCache.set(glob, m);
  }
  return m;
}

/** True if `path` matches any of `globs`. */
export function matchesAny(globs: readonly string[] | undefined, path: string): boolean {
  return !!globs && globs.some((g) => globMatcher(g)(path));
}

/** Path → placement on the domain × layer grid, and table → owning cell. */
export function createMapper(map: DomainMap) {
  const ignore = map.ignore ?? [];
  const neutral = map.neutral ?? [];
  const layerOrder = map.layers.map((l) => l.id);
  const tests = map.domains.map((d) => ({ domain: d.id, globs: d.tests ?? [] }));
  const cells = map.domains.flatMap((d) =>
    layerOrder.flatMap((layer) => {
      const cell = d.cells[layer];
      return cell ? [{ domain: d.id, layer, globs: cell.paths ?? [], tables: cell.tables ?? [] }] : [];
    }),
  );
  const cache = new Map<string, Placement>();

  function place(path: string): Placement {
    let p = cache.get(path);
    if (p) return p;
    if (matchesAny(ignore, path)) p = { kind: 'ignored' };
    else if (matchesAny(neutral, path)) p = { kind: 'neutral' };
    else {
      const t = tests.find((t) => matchesAny(t.globs, path));
      const c = t ? undefined : cells.find((c) => matchesAny(c.globs, path));
      p = t
        ? { kind: 'test', domain: t.domain }
        : c
```

```text
import { appendFileSync, existsSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { join } from 'node:path';
import { randomUUID } from 'node:crypto';
import type { HarnessEvent, EventKind, EventData, Cell } from '@harness/core';

type Listener = (e: HarnessEvent) => void;

/** Append-only event log: `.harness/events.jsonl` in the target repo, broadcast to every listener. */
export class Bus {
  readonly events: HarnessEvent[] = [];
  readonly session = randomUUID().slice(0, 8);
  turn: string | null = null;
  private listeners = new Set<Listener>();
  private file: string;

  constructor(repo: string, opts: { fresh?: boolean } = {}) {
    const dir = join(repo, '.harness');
    mkdirSync(join(dir, 'turns'), { recursive: true });
    // Keep .harness/ out of the target's git without touching its .gitignore.
    if (!existsSync(join(dir, '.gitignore'))) writeFileSync(join(dir, '.gitignore'), '*\n');
    this.file = join(dir, 'events.jsonl');
    if (opts.fresh) writeFileSync(this.file, '');
    else if (existsSync(this.file)) {
      for (const line of readFileSync(this.file, 'utf8').split('\n')) {
        if (line.trim()) this.events.push(JSON.parse(line) as HarnessEvent);
      }
    }
  }

  emit<K extends EventKind>(kind: K, data: K extends keyof EventData ? EventData[K] : never, extra: { cell?: Cell | null; path?: string; turn?: string | null } = {}): HarnessEvent {
    const e: HarnessEvent = {
      id: randomUUID().slice(0, 12),
      t: Date.now(),
      session: this.session,
      turn: extra.turn === undefined ? this.turn : extra.turn,
      kind,
      ...(extra.cell ? { cell: extra.cell } : {}),
      ...(extra.path ? { path: extra.path } : {}),
      data: data as Record<string, unknown>,
    };
    this.events.push(e);
    appendFileSync(this.file, JSON.stringify(e) + '\n');
    for (const l of this.listeners) l(e);
    return e;
  }

  on(l: Listener) {
    this.listeners.add(l);
    return () => this.listeners.delete(l);
  }
}
```

```text
          ],
        },
        canUseTool: this.canUseTool,
        stderr: (d) => { if (process.env.HARNESS_DEBUG) process.stderr.write(d); },
      },
    });
    void this.loop();
  }

  private async loop() {
    try {
      for await (const m of this.q!) {
        if (m.type === 'stream_event') {
          const ev = m.event as { type: string; delta?: { type: string; text?: string } };
          if (ev.type === 'content_block_delta' && ev.delta?.type === 'text_delta' && ev.delta.text) this.ephemeral({ type: 'delta', text: ev.delta.text });
        } else if (m.type === 'assistant' && !m.parent_tool_use_id) {
          const t = m.message.content.filter((b) => b.type === 'text').map((b) => (b as { text: string }).text).join('\n').trim();
          if (t) {
            this.bus.emit('chat', { role: 'assistant', text: t });
            if (this.turn) this.turn.lastText = t;
          }
        } else if (m.type === 'result') {
          this.onResult(m.subtype);
        }
      }
    } catch (e) {
      this.bus.emit('error', { message: `Session ended: ${(e as Error).message}` });
    }
  }

  // ---------------------------------------------------------------- chat input

  userMessage(text: string) {
    const t = text.trim();
    if (!t) return;
    if (this.approval) {
      this.bus.emit('chat', { role: 'user', text: t });
      if (/^(approve|approved|lgtm|yes|ok|go|ship it)\b/i.test(t)) this.approve();
      else this.rejectPlan(t);
      return;
    }
    if (this.turn?.forkOpen) {
      const violations = this.turn.forkOpen;
      const option = parseOption(t);
      this.bus.emit('chat', { role: 'user', text: t });
      this.bus.emit('fork_answered', { option, text: t, violations });
      this.turn.forkOpen = null;
      this.turn.planViolations = [];
      this.turn.gateBlocks = [];
      const { decisions, alikeInstruction } = recordFork(this.repo, this.bus, violations, option, t, this.turn.prompt);
      if (alikeInstruction && process.env.HARNESS_ALIKE !== '0') this.notes.push(alikeInstruction);
      const ids = decisions.map((d) => d.id).join(', ');
      this.send(`${t}\n\n[Harness: recorded as ${ids || 'a decision'} in decisions/ and domains.yaml. ` +
        (option === 'B' ? `${violations[0]?.file} is now an exception. ` : '') +
        'Resubmit the plan with mcp__harness__submit_plan, then exit plan mode.]');
      return;
    }
    if (!this.turn) this.startTurn(t);
    this.bus.emit('chat', { role: 'user', text: t });
    this.send(t);
  }

  private send(text: string) {
    this.busy = true;
    this.ephemeral({ type: 'busy', busy: true });
    this.inbox.push(text);
  }

  private startTurn(prompt: string) {
    const id = `t${randomUUID().slice(0, 6)}`;
    this.turn = { id, prompt, base: baseline(this.repo.root), planned: false, steps: [], planViolations: [], gateBlocks: [], forkOpen: null, lastText: '' };
    this.bus.turn = id;
    this.bus.emit('turn_started', { prompt, head: this.turn.base.head, baseline: this.turn.base.snapshot });
  }

  approve() {
    if (!this.approval) return;
    const { resolve, input } = this.approval;
    this.approval = null;
    this.bus.emit('plan_approved', {} as never);
    resolve({ behavior: 'allow', updatedInput: input });
    void this.q?.setPermissionMode('acceptEdits');
  }

  private rejectPlan(feedback: string) {
    if (!this.approval) return;
    const { resolve } = this.approval;
    this.approval = null;
    resolve({ behavior: 'deny', message: `The user did not approve the plan yet. Their feedback: ${feedback}` });
  }

  private onPlan(steps: PlanStep[], violations: Violation[]) {
    if (!this.turn) return;
    this.turn.planned = true;
    this.turn.steps = steps;
    this.turn.planViolations = violations;
  }

  private onResult(subtype: string) {
    this.busy = false;
    this.ephemeral({ type: 'busy', busy: false });
    const turn = this.turn;
    if (!turn) return;
    if (subtype !== 'success') this.bus.emit('error', { message: `Turn ended with ${subtype}` });
    const open = [...turn.planViolations, ...turn.gateBlocks];
    if (open.length && subtype === 'success') {
      // Claude stopped to ask: the turn stays open until the user answers.
      turn.forkOpen = open;
      this.bus.emit('fork_asked', { violations: open, text: turn.lastText });
      return;
    }
    this.endTurn(subtype);
  }

  private endTurn(reason: string) {
    const turn = this.turn!;
    const stat = numstat(this.repo.root, turn.base);
    this.bus.emit('turn_ended', { ...stat, reason });
    const events = this.bus.events.filter((e) => e.turn === turn.id);
    writeFileSync(join(this.repo.root, '.harness/turns', `${turn.id}.json`), JSON.stringify({ id: turn.id, prompt: turn.prompt, baseline: turn.base, steps: turn.steps, numstat: stat, events }, null, 2));
    this.turn = null;
    this.bus.turn = null;
    this.repo.recheck();
    void this.q?.setPermissionMode('plan');
  }

  // ---------------------------------------------------------------- hooks

  private observeRead: HookCallback = async (input) => {
    const i = input as PreToolUseHookInput;
    const ti = i.tool_input as { file_path?: string; path?: string };
    if (i.tool_name === 'Read' && ti.file_path) {
      const rel = this.repo.rel(ti.file_path);
      if (rel) this.bus.emit('looked', { tool: 'Read' }, { path: rel, cell: this.repo.cellOf(rel) });
    } else {
      const rel = this.repo.rel(ti.path ?? this.repo.root);
      if (rel) this.bus.emit('cursor', { verb: 'searching' }, { path: rel, cell: this.repo.cellOf(rel) ?? this.repo.cellForDir(rel) });
    }
    return { async: true };
  };

  /** The edit gate: same checker as load and plan, on the imports/writes this edit would add. */
  private gate: HookCallback = async (input) => {
    const i = input as PreToolUseHookInput;
    const ti = i.tool_input as { file_path?: string; content?: string; old_string?: string; new_string?: string; replace_all?: boolean };
    if (!ti.file_path) return {};
    const rel = this.repo.rel(ti.file_path);
    if (!rel) return {}; // outside the repo, e.g. Claude's own plan file
    const old = this.repo.current(rel);
    let next: string;
    try {
      next = i.tool_name === 'Write' ? ti.content ?? '' : applyEdit(old ?? '', ti.old_string ?? '', ti.new_string ?? '', ti.replace_all);
    } catch {
      return {}; // the Edit will fail on its own
    }
    const delta = deltaForEdit(rel, old, next, withExtra(this.repo.exists, [rel]));
    const violations = check(this.repo.map, delta, this.repo.mapper);
    this.bus.emit('cursor', { verb: 'editing' }, { path: rel, cell: this.repo.cellOf(rel) });
    if (!violations.length) {
      this.repo.markPending(rel);
      return {};
    }
    for (const v of violations) this.bus.emit('gate_blocked', { violation: v, tool: i.tool_name }, { path: rel, cell: this.repo.cellOf(rel) });
    this.turn?.gateBlocks.push(...violations);
    return {
      hookSpecificOutput: {
        hookEventName: 'PreToolUse',
        permissionDecision: 'deny',
        permissionDecisionReason: `Harness blocked this edit.\n${violationText(violations)}\n${ASK_RULE}`,
      },
    };
  };

  private afterEdit: HookCallback = async (input) => {
    const i = input as PostToolUseHookInput;
    const ti = i.tool_input as { file_path?: string };
    const rel = ti.file_path ? this.repo.rel(ti.file_path) : null;
    if (rel) setImmediate(() => this.repo.fileChanged(rel, { tool: i.tool_name }));
    return { async: true };
  };

  private afterAlike: HookCallback = async (input) => {
    const i = input as PostToolUseHookInput;
    const res = JSON.stringify(i.tool_response ?? '');
    const ids = new Set(JSON.stringify(i.tool_input).match(/DR-\d+/g) ?? []);
    if (/error|failed|unauthori[sz]ed/i.test(res) && !/"id"/.test(res)) return { async: true };
    for (const d of this.bus.events.filter((e) => e.kind === 'decision_recorded')) {
      const data = d.data as { id: string };
      if (ids.has(data.id)) this.bus.emit('decision_recorded', { ...(d.data as EventData['decision_recorded']), alike: true });
    }
    return { async: true };
  };

  private canUseTool: CanUseTool = async (name, input) => {
    if (name === 'ExitPlanMode') {
      const turn = this.turn;
      if (turn && !turn.planned) {
        return { behavior: 'deny', message: 'Call mcp__harness__submit_plan with your numbered steps before exiting plan mode.' };
      }
      if (turn?.planViolations.length) {
        return { behavior: 'deny', message: `The plan has unresolved violations.\n${violationText(turn.planViolations)}\n${ASK_RULE}` };
      }
      const plan = String((input as { plan?: unknown }).plan ?? '');
      this.bus.emit('approval_requested', { plan });
      return new Promise<PermissionResult>((resolve) => { this.approval = { resolve, input }; });
    }
    return { behavior: 'allow', updatedInput: input };
  };

  interrupt() { void this.q?.interrupt(); }
}
```

# Frontend Design

Approach this as the design lead at a design studio known for giving every client a distinct visual identity that is not mistaken for anyone else's. This client has already rejected proposals that felt cliché or templated, and is paying for a distinctive point of view: make deliberate, opinionated choices about palette, typography, and layout that are specific to this brief, and take aesthetic risk if justified.

## Ground your designs in the subject matter

If the brief does not identify what the product or subject matter is, identify it yourself before designing, and confirm with the client. You can come up with one concrete subject, the design's audience, and the design's primary job, as a proposal. If there's any information in your memory about the client's preferences or context about what they're building, use that as a hint. The subject's industry, subject matter, materials, and vernacular are where distinctive visual choices come from — a design for a toy for girls aged 8–11 will be very aesthetically different from a dashboard for financial analysts. Build with the brief's real content and subject matter throughout.

## Design principles

For web designs, the hero is the first thing viewers will see. Open with the most characteristic thing in the subject's world, in the form that is most appropriate: a headline, an image, an animation, a live demo, an interactive moment, or other treatments. Be deliberate with your choice: a big number with a small label, supporting stats, and a gradient accent is the default treatment, so only use it if that's truly the best option.

Typography carries the personality of the page. You don't need a different typeface for display or headline text and body content: use one family or two, and if two, make them clearly distinct.

Choose your typefaces deliberately, not the default families you would reach for on any other project, and set a clear type scale following the default guidance of The Elements of Typographic Style with intentional weights, widths, and spacing. When type is used as a headline or visual element, use the type treatment itself as an active part of the design, not a neutral delivery vehicle for the content.

Default to line lengths of less than 80 characters. Serif typefaces can have slightly longer line lengths; give serif body text slightly more line-height than a sans-serif.

Avoid these default typographic treatments; they are the commonest tells of a generated page:
- Accenting just a single word or phrase in a headline, like putting one word in italic/bold or a different color.
- Using all caps for labels.
- Adding unnecessary typographic labels above content.

Visual structure is information. Structural devices like outlines, borders, numbering, eyebrows, dividers, labels, etc., encode useful information about the content rather than decorate it. Many generic designs use numbered markers (01 / 02 / 03), but that's only appropriate if the content actually is a sequence — like a stepped process or a timeline. Before adding numbered markers, check the content really is a sequence.

Use non-user-triggered motion sparingly and deliberately, only to draw attention. A single orchestrated moment — one page-load sequence or one reveal — lands better than scattered effects; fade-and-slide-up entrances on each section and hover transitions on every card are the generic default and read as AI-generated. Motion that answers a person's action (opening, expanding, confirming) is welcome when it shows what changed.

Consider written content carefully. Often a design brief may not contain real content, and it's up to you to come up with copy and placeholder content. Copy can make a design feel as templated as the design itself. See the below section on writing for more guidance.

## Process: plan, review against the brief, build, critique

For calibration, AI-generated design right now clusters around some traits:
1. a warm cream background (near #F4F1EA) with a high-contrast serif display and a terracotta or warm-clay accent (often near #D97757 — Anthropic's own Claude-interaction accent, so on a user's brief it reads as a tell);
2. a near-black background with a single bright acid-green or vermilion accent;
3. a broadsheet-style layout with hairline rules, zero border-radius, and dense newspaper-like columns;
4. the SaaS-card kit: content chopped into identical rounded cards, one border-radius on everything regardless of hierarchy, the same soft grey shadow (rgba(0,0,0,.1)) under each, and gradient washes as decoration;
5. template chrome that appears whatever the subject: a tracked-out ALL-CAPS eyebrow label above every heading; meta strings joined with middle dots ('A · B · C'); labels built as 'WORD — fragment' with a spaced em dash; tinted near-black (#0B0B0B, #111) standing in for black; a monospace face for small data labels; a '→' appended to link and button text.

All traits are legitimate for some briefs, but they are defaults rather than choices, and they appear regardless of subject. Where the brief pins down a visual direction, follow it exactly — the brief's own words always win, including when it asks for one of these looks. Where it leaves an axis free, don't spend that freedom on one of these defaults. As with a hired human designer, there's often a careful balance between doing what you're good at and taking each project as a chance to experiment and learn.

Work in two passes. First, brainstorm a short design plan based on the client's design brief: create a compact token system with color, type, layout, and principles.
- Color: describe the core base palette as 4–6 named hex values.
- Type: the typefaces and their roles.
- Layout: a layout concept, using one-sentence prose descriptions and ASCII wireframes to ideate and compare. Include alignment guidance; should the content be left aligned, center aligned, justified?
- Principles: the high-level guidance for what makes this page unique.

Then review that plan against the brief before building: if any part of it reads like the generic default you would produce for any similar page (work through a similar prompt to see if you arrive somewhere similar) rather than a choice made for this specific brief — revise that part, say what you changed and why. Only after you've confirmed the relative uniqueness of your design plan should you start to write the code, following the revised plan.

When writing the code, be careful of structuring your CSS selector specificities. It's easy to generate CSS classes that cancel each other out (especially with a type-based selector like .section and an element-based selector like .cta). This can happen often with padding/margin between sections.

## Restraint and self-critique

Spend your boldness in one place. Let one element be the memorable thing, keep everything around it quiet and disciplined, and cut any decoration that does not serve the brief. Build to a quality floor without announcing it: responsive down to mobile, visible keyboard focus, reduced motion respected, visually accessible, harmonious color palettes. Critique your own work as you build, taking screenshots to review if your environment supports it — a picture is worth 1000 tokens. Consider Chanel's advice: before leaving the house, take a look in the mirror and remove one accessory. Human creatives have memory and always try to do something new, so if you have a space to quickly jot down notes about what you've tried, it can help you in future passes.

## More on writing in design

Words appear in a design for one reason: to make it easier to understand and use. They are design content, not decoration. Bring the same intentionality and minimalism to copywriting that you would bring to spacing and color. Before writing anything, ask what the design needs to say, and how it can best be said to help the person navigate the experience.

Write from the end user's perspective. Name things by what users will understand in simple language, not by how the system is built. A user manages notifications, not webhook config. Describe what something is or does in plain terms rather than selling it. Being specific and legible to new users is always better than being clever.

Use active voice as default. A CTA says exactly what happens when it is used: "Save changes," not "Submit." An action keeps the same name through the whole flow, so the button that says "Publish" produces a toast that says "Published." The vocabulary of an interface is the signposting for someone navigating the product. Cohesion and consistency are how people learn their way around.

Treat failure and emptiness as moments for direction, not mood. Explain what went wrong and how to fix it, in the interface's voice rather than a person's. Errors don't apologize, and they are never vague about what happened. An empty screen is an invitation to act.

Keep the tone conversational: plain verbs, sentence case, no filler, with tone matched to the brand and the audience. Let each written element do exactly one job.

```typescript
import { check } from '../src/rules';
import { createMapper } from '../src/mapper';
import { domainEdges, fileExistsIn, scanRepo, withExtra } from '../src/facts';
import { planFootprint, type PlanStep } from '../src/plan';
import type { EventData, EventKind, HarnessEvent } from '../src/events';
import { fixtureRepo, loadMap } from './helpers';

/** Builds a realistic event log for the demo turn from real core computations over the fixture repo. */
export function demoLog() {
  const map = loadMap();
  const mapper = createMapper(map);
  const facts = scanRepo(fixtureRepo, map);
  const events: HarnessEvent[] = [];
  let turn: string | null = null;
  let n = 0;
  const ev = <K extends EventKind>(kind: K, data: K extends keyof EventData ? EventData[K] : never, extra: Partial<HarnessEvent> = {}) => {
    events.push({ id: `e${n}`, t: 1000 + n++, session: 's1', turn, kind, data: data as Record<string, unknown>, ...extra });
    return events.length - 1;
  };
  const cell = (path: string) => {
    const p = mapper.place(path);
    return p.kind === 'cell' ? { domain: p.domain, layer: p.layer } : undefined;
  };
  const plan = (steps: PlanStep[]) => {
    const fp = planFootprint(map, steps, withExtra(fileExistsIn(fixtureRepo), steps.flatMap((s) => s.files)), mapper);
    ev('planned', { steps, cells: fp.cells, edges: fp.edges, unassigned: fp.unassigned });
    for (const v of fp.violations) ev('plan_violation', { violation: v }, { path: v.file });
    return fp.violations;
  };
  const tenK = (model: string): PlanStep[] => [
    { n: 1, text: 'Add the 10-K tool', files: ['src/tools/filing-summary.ts'], imports: [{ from: 'src/tools/filing-summary.ts', to: model }] },
    { n: 2, text: 'Register it', files: ['src/tools/index.ts'], imports: [] },
  ];

  ev('map_confirmed', { map, source: 'file' });
  ev('repo_scanned', { files: facts.files.map((path) => ({ path, placement: mapper.place(path) })), imports: facts.imports, writes: facts.writes, edges: domainEdges(facts, mapper) });
  ev('violation_found', { violations: check(map, facts, mapper) });

  turn = 't1';
  ev('turn_started', { prompt: "Add a tool that summarizes a prospect's latest 10-K", head: 'abc', baseline: 'abc' });
  ev('looked', { tool: 'Read' }, { path: 'src/tools/news-summarize.ts', cell: cell('src/tools/news-summarize.ts') });
  ev('looked', { tool: 'Read' }, { path: 'src/gateway/complete.ts', cell: cell('src/gateway/complete.ts') });
  const violations = plan(tenK('vendor/llm-openai/index'));
  ev('fork_asked', { violations, text: 'A or B?' });
  ev('fork_answered', { option: 'A', text: 'A, through the gateway', violations });
  ev('decision_recorded', { id: 'DR-4', title: 'Filings go through the gateway', invariant: 'DR-1', option: 'A', paths: ['src/tools/filing-summary.ts'] });
  plan(tenK('src/gateway/complete'));
  ev('approval_requested', { plan: '1. add tool 2. register' });
  ev('plan_approved', {} as never);
  const firstEdit = ev('edited', { added: 12, removed: 0, created: true }, { path: 'src/tools/filing-summary.ts', cell: { domain: 'tools', layer: 'logic' } });
  ev('edge_added', { edge: { from: 'src/tools/filing-summary.ts', to: 'src/gateway/complete.ts' }, from: 'tools', to: 'gateway' }, { path: 'src/tools/filing-summary.ts' });
  ev('edited', { added: 2, removed: 0, created: false }, { path: 'src/tools/index.ts', cell: { domain: 'tools', layer: 'logic' } });
  ev('edited', { added: 3, removed: 1, created: false }, { path: 'src/outreach/draft-email.ts', cell: { domain: 'outreach', layer: 'logic' } });
  ev('turn_ended', { added: 17, removed: 1, files: ['src/tools/filing-summary.ts', 'src/tools/index.ts', 'src/outreach/draft-email.ts'], reason: 'success' });
  turn = null;
  return { map, events, firstEdit };
}
```

```typescript
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { apply, cellViews, edgeViews, initialState, provenance, reduce } from '../src/events';
import { demoLog } from './turn-log';

describe('reduce', () => {
  const { events, firstEdit } = demoLog();
  const s = reduce(events);

  it('is a pure fold: incremental apply equals reduce', () => {
    const inc = initialState();
    events.forEach((e, i) => apply(inc, e, i));
    expect(JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(inc))).toEqual(JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(reduce(events))));
  });

  it('carries the load-time violation as existing and the map edges', () => {
    expect(s.violations).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(s.violations[0]!.file).toBe('src/tools/news-summarize.ts');
    expect(s.edges['tools->gateway']).toBeDefined();
  });

  it('replays: before the fork answer the plan ghost is red and new, after the turn it is solid', () => {
    const forkAsked = events.findIndex((e) => e.kind === 'fork_asked');
    const mid = reduce(events, forkAsked + 1);
    expect(mid.pendingFork?.violations[0]?.invariant).toBe('DR-1');
    const tools = cellViews(mid)['tools/logic']!;
    expect(tools.ghost).toEqual([1, 2]);
    expect(tools.violation).toBe('new'); // differs from the map before the turn even though the cell was already red
    expect(tools.newViolationFiles).toEqual(['src/tools/filing-summary.ts']);
    const ghost = edgeViews(mid).find((e) => e.state === 'ghost');
    expect(ghost).toMatchObject({ from: 'tools', to: 'gateway', violation: true });
    expect(edgeViews(mid).some((e) => e.state === 'existing' && e.from === 'tools' && e.to === 'gateway')).toBe(true);

    const end = cellViews(s);
    expect(end['tools/logic']).toMatchObject({ edited: true, ghost: null, added: 14 });
    expect(end['outreach/logic']).toMatchObject({ unplanned: true });
    expect(end['gateway/logic']).toMatchObject({ looked: false, edited: false });
    expect(reduce(events, firstEdit).turns[0]!.approved).toBe(true);
  });

  it('records the decision and provenance', () => {
    expect(s.decisions.map((d) => d.id)).toEqual(['DR-4']);
    const p = provenance(s, { edge: 'tools->gateway' });
    expect(p.turns.map((t) => t.index)).toEqual([1]);
    expect(p.decisions.map((d) => d.id)).toEqual(['DR-4']);
  });
});
```

```typescript
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { reduce, type HarnessEvent } from '../src/events';
import { ledger, turnFindings } from '../src/ledger';
import type { Violation } from '../src/rules';
import { demoLog } from './turn-log';

describe('ledger (SPEC §9)', () => {
  it('counts the demo turn exactly', () => {
    const { events } = demoLog();
    const l = ledger(reduce(events));
    expect(l.turns).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(l.turns[0]).toMatchObject({ linesChanged: 18, forksCaughtBeforeCode: 1, rejectedOptionsBlocked: 0 });
    // invariant hit (tools/logic) · unplanned edit (outreach/logic); the tools→gateway edge already existed
    // at domain level but is new this turn, and lands in tools/logic too.
    expect(l.turns[0]!.cellsToReview).toBe(2);
    expect(l.session).toEqual({ linesChanged: 18, cellsToReview: 2, forksCaughtBeforeCode: 1, rejectedOptionsBlocked: 0 });
  });

  it('ranks findings loudest first', () => {
    const { events } = demoLog();
    const s = reduce(events);
    const f = turnFindings(s, s.turns[0]!);
    expect(f.map((x) => x.severity)).toEqual([...f.map((x) => x.severity)].sort());
    expect(f[0]).toMatchObject({ severity: 1, kind: 'invariant', invariant: 'DR-1' });
    expect(f.some((x) => x.kind === 'unplanned' && x.cell?.domain === 'outreach')).toBe(true);
  });

  it('lines changed is null until the turn ends', () => {
    const { events } = demoLog();
    const l = ledger(reduce(events, events.length - 1));
    expect(l.turns[0]!.linesChanged).toBeNull();
    expect(l.session.linesChanged).toBe(0);
  });

  it('does not count a fork answered after code was written', () => {
    const { events, firstEdit } = demoLog();
    // Move the fork question and answer after the first edit.
    const fork = events.filter((e) => e.kind === 'fork_asked' || e.kind === 'fork_answered');
    const rest = events.filter((e) => !fork.includes(e));
    const at = rest.findIndex((e) => e === events[firstEdit]) + 1;
    const reordered: HarnessEvent[] = [...rest.slice(0, at), ...fork, ...rest.slice(at)];
    expect(ledger(reduce(reordered)).turns[0]!.forksCaughtBeforeCode).toBe(0);
  });

  it('counts violations that cite an existing decision as rejected options blocked', () => {
    const { events } = demoLog();
    const v: Violation = { invariant: 'DR-1', kind: 'only_via', reason: 'You decided this in DR-4. …', file: 'src/tools/earnings.ts', detail: '', options: ['A', 'B'], target: 'vendor/llm-openai/index.ts', decision: 'DR-4' };
    const t2: HarnessEvent[] = [
      { id: 'x1', t: 1, session: 's1', turn: 't2', kind: 'turn_started', data: { prompt: 'earnings calls', head: '', baseline: '' } },
      { id: 'x2', t: 2, session: 's1', turn: 't2', kind: 'gate_blocked', path: v.file, data: { violation: v, tool: 'Write' } },
      { id: 'x3', t: 3, session: 's1', turn: 't2', kind: 'gate_blocked', path: v.file, data: { violation: v, tool: 'Write' } },
      { id: 'x4', t: 4, session: 's1', turn: 't2', kind: 'turn_ended', data: { added: 0, removed: 0, files: [], reason: 'success' } },
    ];
    const l = ledger(reduce([...events, ...t2]));
    expect(l.turns[1]).toMatchObject({ rejectedOptionsBlocked: 1, linesChanged: 0, forksCaughtBeforeCode: 0 });
    expect(l.session.rejectedOptionsBlocked).toBe(1);
  });
});
```

```bash
SP=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-johnzhang-Documents-GitHub-Speedhacks-project/4bfd5c1a-5a5b-44a6-ad19-d157d19da66d/scratchpad && cd /Users/johnzhang/Documents/GitHub/Speedhacks-project && scripts/sandbox.sh $SP/e2e-repo >/dev/null && cat > $SP/drive.mjs <<'EOF'
// Drives one demo turn against a running server: prompt → (fork → answer A) → approve → wait for turn_ended.
const base = process.argv[2] ?? 'http://localhost:4320';
const prompt = process.argv[3] ?? "Add a tool that summarizes a prospect's latest 10-K. Base it on src/tools/news-summarize.ts, which is the closest existing example.";
const answer = process.argv[4] ?? 'A — route it through the gateway like the other tools.';
const post = (p, b) => fetch(base + p, { method: 'POST', headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' }, body: JSON.stringify(b ?? {}) });
let seen = 0;
const t0 = Date.now();
const show = (e) => {
  const d = e.data ?? {};
  const extra = e.kind === 'chat' ? `${d.role}: ${String(d.text).slice(0, 300).replace(/\n/g, ' ⏎ ')}`
    : e.kind === 'planned' ? `cells=${d.cells.map((c) => `${c.domain}/${c.layer}[${c.steps}]`).join(',')} edges=${d.edges.map((x) => `${x.from}->${x.to}`).join(',')} unassigned=${d.unassigned}`
    : e.kind.includes('violation') || e.kind === 'gate_blocked' ? (d.violation ? d.violation.reason : `${(d.violations ?? []).length} violations`)
    : e.kind === 'edited' ? `${e.path} +${d.added} -${d.removed}${d.unattributed ? ' UNATTRIBUTED' : ''} cell=${e.cell ? e.cell.domain + '/' + e.cell.layer : '-'}`
    : e.kind === 'turn_ended' ? `+${d.added} -${d.removed} ${d.files} (${d.reason})`
    : e.kind === 'decision_recorded' ? `${d.id} ${d.title} alike=${d.alike}`
    : ['edge_added', 'edge_removed'].includes(e.kind) ? `${d.from}->${d.to} ${d.edge.from}`
    : e.path ? `${e.path} ${e.cell ? e.cell.domain + '/' + e.cell.layer : ''}` : '';
  console.log(`${((Date.now() - t0) / 1000).toFixed(1).padStart(6)}s ${e.kind.padEnd(18)} ${extra}`);
};
const sleep = (ms) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms));
async function poll(until) {
  while (true) {
    const ev = await (await fetch(base + '/api/events')).json();
    for (const e of ev.slice(seen)) { show(e); const r = until(e); if (r) { seen = ev.indexOf(e) + 1; return r; } }
    seen = ev.length;
    await sleep(500);
  }
}
await poll((e) => e.kind === 'violation_found');
await post('/api/chat', { text: prompt });
let answered = false;
while (true) {
  const e = await poll((e) => ['fork_asked', 'approval_requested', 'turn_ended', 'error'].includes(e.kind) && e);
  if (e.kind === 'fork_asked' && !answered) { answered = true; await sleep(300); console.log('>>> answering', answer); await post('/api/chat', { text: answer }); }
  else if (e.kind === 'approval_requested') { await sleep(300); console.log('>>> approve'); await post('/api/approve'); }
  else if (e.kind === 'turn_ended') break;
  else if (e.kind === 'error' && /Session ended/.test(e.data.message)) break;
}
process.exit(0);
EOF
(cd $SP/e2e-repo && git log --oneline | head -2)
```

Scout is built in `../scout-agent` and every acceptance check in `DEMO_REPO_SPEC.md` passes. It's a fresh local repo with no remote, and nothing has been pushed.

**What it does:**
- **Tests:** `npm test` runs 24 tests offline in about 0.6 seconds.
- **Proof report:** `npm run proof` prints `PII reaching model providers: 36 of 212 model calls` and `Model calls missing from the cost log: 36`. All 36 come from `news_summarize`. At the commit just before it, the report shows 0 of 176.
- **The redaction conflict:** Acme's 10-K sent through `complete()` comes back as "Total revenue … was $[PHONE_1] thousand", with 17 redactions. So an agent writing the 10-K tool has a real reason to copy the shortcut in `news_summarize`.
- **Code checks:** only `src/tools/news-summarize.ts` imports a model vendor outside the gateway. Every database write uses a double-quoted table name in its owner's folder. Every import is extensionless, and the one-way dependency direction holds.
- **Size:** 2,757 lines across `src/`, `vendor/` and `scripts/`.
- **Banned words:** none in the code, commits or README.
- **Also working:** the CLI, the HTTP server and the seed script.

**History:** 12 commits in the spec's order, each of which typechecks on its own. The last is `feat(tools): summarize recent news for the brief`, with the one-line reason in its body.

**Decisions you might want changed:**
- **Backdated commits.** I dated them Sep 21 – Oct 6 so the history reads like two weeks of work. They're authored as you and carry the Claude co-author line. Say if you'd rather have today's dates.
- **Node version.** `engines` says Node ≥ 20 rather than 22, because you're on 20.19.5. A `.nvmrc` recommends 22.
- **Fixture lookup.** The search, news, filings and enrichment fakes look companies up by name (`acme`) rather than by a hash of the input, which keeps the fixture files readable. Only the canned model answers are keyed by hash, as the spec says.
- **`RunResult.email` is optional.** That way the orchestrator commit, which comes before outreach, still compiles.
- **No type arguments on `db.update(...)` calls.** Writing `db.update<RunRow>("runs", …)` would break the harness's write scan, which expects the table name right after `(`.

**Worth knowing:** your home directory is a git repository (`~/.git`). Until I ran `git init` in `scout-agent`, any git command there would have hit your home repo. Any new folder outside a repo behaves the same way, so you may want to check whether that home repo is intentional.

**For the harness session:**
- Scout is ready at `../scout-agent`, so the copy under `packages/core/test/fixture-repo/` is only needed for unit tests.
- With the real repo, the load scan should find exactly one violation.
- We still don't know whether Claude notices the mangled figures while planning. That's the first thing to test once the plan flow works.

```typescript
import { create } from 'zustand';
import type { HarnessEvent } from '@harness/core/view';

export type Selection = { cell: string } | { edge: string; pair: string } | { unassigned: true };

export type Conn = 'connecting' | 'open' | 'down' | 'fake';

/**
 * The store holds the event log and purely ephemeral UI state. Everything the map, ledger, summary and chat show
 * is derived from `events` (see derive.ts); nothing here is a second copy of footprint, ghosts or ledger.
 */
type Store = {
  events: HarnessEvent[];
  /** null = live; otherwise the number of events to reduce (replay). */
  replay: number | null;
  /** Streaming assistant text not yet committed as a `chat` event. */
  delta: string;
  busy: boolean;
  conn: Conn;
  repo: string;
  draft: string;
  focusTick: number;
  selection: Selection | null;
  /** null = latest turn. */
  turn: string | null;
  hover: string | null;

  hello(events: HarnessEvent[], busy: boolean): void;
  append(e: HarnessEvent): void;
  addDelta(text: string): void;
  setBusy(b: boolean): void;
  setConn(c: Conn): void;
  setRepo(r: string): void;
  setDraft(d: string, focus?: boolean): void;
  select(s: Selection | null): void;
  setTurn(id: string | null): void;
  setReplay(i: number | null): void;
  setHover(h: string | null): void;
};

export const useStore = create<Store>((set) => ({
  events: [],
  replay: null,
  delta: '',
  busy: false,
  conn: 'connecting',
  repo: '',
  draft: '',
  focusTick: 0,
  selection: null,
  turn: null,
  hover: null,

  hello: (events, busy) => set({ events, busy, delta: '' }),
  append: (e) =>
    set((s) => {
      if (s.events.length && s.events[s.events.length - 1]!.id === e.id) return s;
      const clear = e.kind === 'chat' && (e.data as { role?: string } | undefined)?.role === 'assistant';
      return { events: [...s.events, e], ...(clear ? { delta: '' } : {}) };
    }),
  addDelta: (text) => set((s) => ({ delta: s.delta + text })),
  setBusy: (busy) => set(busy ? { busy } : { busy, delta: '' }),
  setConn: (conn) => set({ conn }),
  setRepo: (repo) => set({ repo }),
  setDraft: (draft, focus) => set((s) => ({ draft, focusTick: focus ? s.focusTick + 1 : s.focusTick })),
  select: (selection) => set({ selection }),
  setTurn: (turn) => set({ turn }),
  setReplay: (replay) => set({ replay }),
  setHover: (hover) => set({ hover }),
}));
```

```typescript
import type { HarnessEvent } from '@harness/core/view';
import { useStore } from './store';

type ServerMsg =
  | { type: 'hello'; events: HarnessEvent[]; busy: boolean; session: string }
  | { type: 'event'; event: HarnessEvent }
  | { type: 'delta'; text: string }
  | { type: 'busy'; busy: boolean };

const params = new URLSearchParams(location.search);
/** Dev-only: `?fake=1` loads /fake-events.json at once, `?fake=play` streams it; `&at=N` opens the replay at N. */
export const fakeMode = params.get('fake');

export function connect() {
  if (fakeMode) return loadFake(fakeMode === 'play');
  void fetch('/api/info')
    .then((r) => r.json() as Promise<{ repo: string }>)
    .then((i) => useStore.getState().setRepo(i.repo))
    .catch(() => {});
  openSocket(500);
}

function openSocket(delay: number) {
  const st = useStore.getState();
  st.setConn(st.conn === 'open' ? 'down' : st.conn);
  const ws = new WebSocket(`${location.protocol === 'https:' ? 'wss' : 'ws'}://${location.host}/ws`);
  let opened = false;
  ws.onopen = () => {
    opened = true;
    useStore.getState().setConn('open');
  };
  ws.onmessage = (m) => {
    const msg = JSON.parse(String(m.data)) as ServerMsg;
    const s = useStore.getState();
    if (msg.type === 'hello') s.hello(msg.events, msg.busy);
    else if (msg.type === 'event') s.append(msg.event);
    else if (msg.type === 'delta') s.addDelta(msg.text);
    else if (msg.type === 'busy') s.setBusy(msg.busy);
  };
  ws.onclose = () => {
    useStore.getState().setConn('down');
    const next = opened ? 500 : Math.min(delay * 2, 8000);
    setTimeout(() => openSocket(next), opened ? 500 : delay);
  };
}

async function loadFake(play: boolean) {
  const st = useStore.getState();
  st.setConn('fake');
  st.setRepo('scout-agent (fake turn)');
  const events = (await (await fetch('/fake-events.json')).json()) as HarnessEvent[];
  const at = params.get('at');
  if (!play) {
    st.hello(events, false);
    if (at !== null) st.setReplay(Math.max(0, Math.min(events.length, Number(at))));
    return;
  }
  st.hello([], false);
  for (let i = 0; i < events.length; i++) {
    const e = events[i]!;
    const prev = events[i - 1];
    const gap = prev ? Math.max(20, Math.min(900, (e.t - prev.t) / 3)) : 0;
    await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, e.kind === 'file_assigned' ? 15 : gap));
    useStore.getState().append(e);
  }
}

async function post(path: string, body?: unknown) {
  if (fakeMode) return;
  await fetch(path, { method: 'POST', headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' }, body: JSON.stringify(body ?? {}) });
}

export const api = {
  chat: (text: string) => post('/api/chat', { text }),
  approve: () => post('/api/approve'),
  interrupt: () => post('/api/interrupt'),
  confirmMap: () => post('/api/map/confirm'),
  fallbackMap: () => post('/api/map/fallback'),
  async file(path: string): Promise<string | null> {
    const r = await fetch(`/api/file?path=${encodeURIComponent(path)}`);
    return r.ok ? r.text() : null;
  },
};
```

```typescript
import {
  cellKey, cellViews, edgeViews, ledger, reduce, turnLedger,
  type CellView, type EdgeView, type HarnessEvent, type Ledger, type TurnLedger, type TurnState, type UIState, type Violation,
} from '@harness/core/view';
import { useStore } from './store';

/** Everything the UI shows, as a pure function of (events, replay index, selected turn). */
export type View = {
  ui: UIState;
  upTo: number;
  live: boolean;
  turn: TurnState | null;
  turnIndex: number; // 1-based, 0 when no turn
  cells: Record<string, CellView>;
  edges: EdgeView[];
  ledger: Ledger;
  turnLedger: TurnLedger | null;
  /** cellKey → files placed there (product files only; tests are listed under their domain). */
  cellFiles: Record<string, string[]>;
  testFiles: Record<string, string[]>;
  unassigned: string[];
  proposal: { domains: number; rules: number } | null;
  steps: { done: number; total: number };
  turnStarts: number[];
};

let reduceCache: { events: readonly HarnessEvent[]; upTo: number; ui: UIState } | null = null;
let viewCache: { ui: UIState; turnSel: string | null; view: View } | null = null;

function reduced(events: readonly HarnessEvent[], upTo: number): UIState {
  if (reduceCache && reduceCache.events === events && reduceCache.upTo === upTo) return reduceCache.ui;
  const ui = reduce(events, upTo);
  reduceCache = { events, upTo, ui };
  return ui;
}

export function deriveView(events: readonly HarnessEvent[], replay: number | null, turnSel: string | null): View {
  const upTo = replay ?? events.length;
  const ui = reduced(events, upTo);
  if (viewCache && viewCache.ui === ui && viewCache.turnSel === turnSel) return viewCache.view;

  const turn = (turnSel && ui.turns.find((t) => t.id === turnSel)) || ui.turns.at(-1) || null;
  const cellFiles: Record<string, string[]> = {};
  const testFiles: Record<string, string[]> = {};
  const unassigned: string[] = [];
  for (const [path, p] of Object.entries(ui.files)) {
    if (p.kind === 'cell') (cellFiles[cellKey(p)] ??= []).push(path);
    else if (p.kind === 'test') (testFiles[p.domain] ??= []).push(path);
    else if (p.kind === 'unassigned') unassigned.push(path);
  }
  for (const list of Object.values(cellFiles)) list.sort();

  let proposed = -1;
  let confirmed = -1;
  const turnStarts: number[] = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < events.length; i++) {
    const k = events[i]!.kind;
    if (k === 'turn_started') turnStarts.push(i);
    if (i >= upTo) continue;
    if (k === 'map_proposed') proposed = i;
    if (k === 'map_confirmed') confirmed = i;
  }
  const proposal = proposed > confirmed && ui.map ? { domains: ui.map.domains.length, rules: ui.map.invariants.length } : null;

  const l = ledger(ui);
  const view: View = {
    ui,
    upTo,
    live: replay === null,
    turn,
    turnIndex: turn ? ui.turns.indexOf(turn) + 1 : 0,
    cells: cellViews(ui, turn?.id ?? null),
    edges: edgeViews(ui, turn?.id ?? null),
    ledger: l,
    turnLedger: turn ? turnLedger(ui, turn) : null,
    cellFiles,
    testFiles,
    unassigned,
    proposal,
    steps: turn ? stepProgress(turn) : { done: 0, total: 0 },
    turnStarts,
  };
  viewCache = { ui, turnSel, view };
  return view;
}

/** "3 of 6 steps": a step is done when every cell it plans has been edited (or, for a step with no cells, its files). */
function stepProgress(turn: TurnState) {
  const editedFiles = new Set([
    ...Object.values(turn.edited).flatMap((c) => c.files),
    ...Object.values(turn.tests).flat(),
    ...turn.unassigned,
  ]);
  let done = 0;
  for (const step of turn.steps) {
    const cells = Object.entries(turn.planned).filter(([, c]) => c.steps.includes(step.n)).map(([k]) => k);
    const ok = cells.length ? cells.every((k) => !!turn.edited[k]) : step.files.length > 0 && step.files.every((f) => editedFiles.has(f));
    if (ok) done++;
  }
  return { done, total: turn.steps.length };
}

export function useView(): View {
  const events = useStore((s) => s.events);
  const replay = useStore((s) => s.replay);
  const turnSel = useStore((s) => s.turn);
  return deriveView(events, replay, turnSel);
}

/** Violations relevant to the selected turn (load-time plus this turn's plan and gate), for the inspector. */
export function turnViolations(v: View): { v: Violation; source: 'load' | 'plan' | 'gate' }[] {
  const out: { v: Violation; source: 'load' | 'plan' | 'gate' }[] = v.ui.violations.map((x) => ({ v: x, source: 'load' as const }));
  for (const x of v.turn?.planViolations ?? []) out.push({ v: x, source: 'plan' });
  for (const x of v.turn?.gateBlocks ?? []) out.push({ v: x, source: 'gate' });
  return out;
}

export const basename = (p: string) => p.split('/').pop() ?? p;
export const stem = (p: string) => {
  const parts = p.split('/');
  const last = parts.pop() ?? p;
  // vendor/<name>/index.ts reads better as its folder name
  if (/^index\.[tj]sx?$/.test(last) && parts.length) return parts.pop()!;
  return last.replace(/\.[tj]sx?$/, '');
};
```
