## Stop Reasons

The `stop_reason` field in the response indicates why the model stopped generating:

| Value           | Meaning                                                         |
| --------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `end_turn`      | Claude finished its response naturally                          |
| `max_tokens`    | Hit the `max_tokens` limit - increase it or use streaming       |
| `stop_sequence` | Hit a custom stop sequence                                      |
| `tool_use`      | Claude wants to call a tool - execute it and continue           |
| `pause_turn`    | Model paused and can be resumed (agentic flows)                 |
| `refusal`       | Claude refused for safety reasons - check `stop_details`        |

### Structured Stop Details

When `stop_reason` is `"refusal"`, the response includes a `stop_details` object with structured information about the refusal:

```typescript
if (response.stop_reason === "refusal" && response.stop_details) {
  console.log(`Category: ${response.stop_details.category}`); // e.g. "cyber", "bio", "reasoning_extraction", "frontier_llm", or null - see docs for the full set
  console.log(`Explanation: ${response.stop_details.explanation}`);
}
```

### Refusal Fallbacks (Claude Fable 5.1) - opt in by default

Fallbacks are **opt-in**: without them a refused request simply stops. Include the server-side `fallbacks` parameter in `claude-fable-5-1` code by default - on a policy decline the API re-runs the same request on the fallback model inside the same call. A mid-stream decline is billed at normal rates, and the rescue bills at the fallback model's own rates, with cache repricing applied automatically; for a decline before any output, see [How refusals are billed](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/refusals-and-fallback#how-refusals-are-billed).

```typescript
const response = await client.beta.messages.create({
  model: "claude-fable-5-1",
  max_tokens: 16000,
  betas: ["server-side-fallback-2026-06-01"],
  fallbacks: [{ model: "claude-opus-4-8" }],
  messages: [{ role: "user", content: "..." }],
});

// Switch points: one fallback block per model that ran and declined this turn
for (const block of response.content) {
  if (block.type === "fallback") {
    console.log(`${block.from.model} declined; ${block.to.model} continued`);
  }
}

// Served-by signal - covers sticky turns, which carry no fallback block.
// Pair with stop_reason: the fallback model can itself refuse.
const fallbackRan = (response.usage.iterations ?? []).some(
  (entry) => entry.type === "fallback_message",
);
if (fallbackRan && response.stop_reason !== "refusal") {
  console.log(`Served by ${response.model}`);
}
```

A `stop_reason: "refusal"` on the final response means the whole chain refused. The header must be exactly `server-side-fallback-2026-06-01` **for this array form**; the newer `fallbacks: "default"` scalar form uses `server-side-fallback-2026-07-01` instead (see `shared/model-migration.md` -> Migrating to Claude Opus 5 -> New API features), and pairing either header with the other form returns a 400. The parameter is rejected on the Batches API and unavailable on Amazon Bedrock, Vertex AI, and Microsoft Foundry - register the client-side `betaRefusalFallbackMiddleware` on the client there instead. Full semantics (sticky routing, billing, streaming, echoing fallback turns back): `shared/model-migration.md` -> Migrating to Claude Fable 5.1 -> `refusal` stop reason.

## Cost Optimization Strategies

### 1. Use Prompt Caching for Repeated Context

```typescript
// Automatic caching (simplest - caches the last cacheable block)
const response = await client.messages.create({
  model: "claude-opus-5-5",
  max_tokens: 16000,
  cache_control: { type: "ephemeral" },
  system: largeDocumentText, // e.g., 50KB of context
  messages: [{ role: "user", content: "Summarize the key points" }],
});

// First request: full cost
// Subsequent requests: ~90% cheaper for cached portion
```

### 2. Use Token Counting Before Requests

```typescript
const countResponse = await client.messages.countTokens({
  model: "claude-opus-5-5",
  messages: messages,
  system: system,
});

const estimatedInputCost = countResponse.input_tokens * 0.000004; // $4/1M tokens
console.log(`Estimated input cost: $${estimatedInputCost.toFixed(4)}`);
```

1173-Claude Sonnet 5 substantially improves on Sonnet 4.6 for coding and agentic work, reaching what was previously Opus-tier quality on many tasks. Its API surface aligns with Opus 4.7/4.8: manual extended thinking is removed (adaptive or disabled only, adaptive is the default), and non-default sampling parameters are rejected. This section is layered on top of the Sonnet 4.6 migration above - if the caller is jumping from Sonnet 4.5 or older, apply the 4.6 changes first, then this one.

1175-**TL;DR for someone already on Sonnet 4.6:** swap the model ID to `claude-sonnet-5`. Replace any remaining `thinking: {type: "enabled", budget_tokens: N}` with `thinking: {type: "adaptive"}` (the transitional escape hatch is gone - it now 400s), and note that omitting `thinking` now runs adaptive (4.6 ran thinking-off). Strip non-default `temperature`/`top_p`/`top_k`. Re-run `count_tokens()` against `claude-sonnet-5` - the new tokenizer produces ~30% more tokens for the same text, so token-budgeted limits and cost baselines shift (per-token pricing is also lower than Sonnet 4.6: $2/$10 vs $3/$15 per MTok). `effort` defaults to `high`, the same as Sonnet 4.6 - raise to `xhigh` for the hardest coding and agentic tasks (Claude Sonnet 5 supports the full `low`/`medium`/`high`/`xhigh`/`max` range), and give `max_tokens` headroom at `xhigh`/`max` (the new tokenizer means a Sonnet-4.6-tuned `max_tokens` may truncate equivalent output). Then re-tune prompts: Claude Sonnet 5 interprets instructions more literally than 4.6 - holdover style/tone directives now apply at face value; it is more agentic by default and reaches for tools and self-verification loops more readily (with thinking disabled it is less tool-eager - add an explicit nudge); it gives better in-progress updates by default (drop forced "summarize every N tool calls" scaffolding); and code-review harnesses with conservative-reporting instructions may see lower recall (tell it to report everything and filter downstream).

## Anthropic-Defined Tools

Version-suffixed `type` literals; `name` is fixed per interface. Web search and code execution are server-executed; bash and text editor are client-executed (you handle the `tool_use` locally - see `shared/tool-use-concepts.md`). Pass plain object literals - the `ToolUnion` type is satisfied structurally. **The `name`/`type` pair must match the interface**: mixing `str_replace_based_edit_tool` (20250728 name) with `text_editor_20250124` (which expects `str_replace_editor`) is a TS2322.

**Don't type-annotate as `Tool[]`** - `Tool` is just the custom-tool variant. Let structural typing infer from the `tools` param, or annotate as `Anthropic.Messages.ToolUnion[]` if you must:

```typescript
// Good: let inference work - no annotation
const response = await client.messages.create({
  model: "claude-opus-5-5",
  max_tokens: 16000,
  tools: [
    { type: "text_editor_20250728", name: "str_replace_based_edit_tool" },
    { type: "bash_20250124", name: "bash" },
    { type: "web_search_20260209", name: "web_search" },
    { type: "code_execution_20260120", name: "code_execution" },
  ],
  messages: [{ role: "user", content: "..." }],
});

// Bad: this is a TS2352 - Tool is the CUSTOM tool variant only
// const tools: Anthropic.Tool[] = [{ type: "text_editor_20250728", ... }]
```

| `ToolTextEditor20250124` | `str_replace_editor` | `text_editor_20250124` |

| `ToolTextEditor20250728` | `str_replace_based_edit_tool` | `text_editor_20250728` |
| `ToolBash20250124` | `bash` | `bash_20250124` |
| `WebSearchTool20260209` | `web_search` | `web_search_20260209` |

import { existsSync } from "node:fs";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";

export type ModelProviderName = "openai" | "anthropic";

/** `live` calls real services (Claude, web search, SEC EDGAR); `offline` uses the fakes in vendor/. */
export type ScoutMode = "live" | "offline";

export interface ScoutConfig {
  mode: ScoutMode;
  modelProvider: ModelProviderName;
  openaiModel: string;
  anthropicModel: string;
  embeddingModel: string;
  port: number;
  snapshotPath: string | null;
  cacheDir: string;
  secUserAgent: string;
  maxSteps: number;
  fromAddress: string;
  senderName: string;
}

const DEFAULTS: ScoutConfig = {
  mode: "live",
  modelProvider: "anthropic",
  openaiModel: "gpt-4o-mini",
  anthropicModel: "claude-opus-5-5",
  embeddingModel: "local-hash-64",
  port: 8787,
  snapshotPath: ".scout/db.json",
  cacheDir: ".scout/cache",
  secUserAgent: "Scout Research research@scout.local",
  maxSteps: 6,
  fromAddress: "research@scout.local",
  senderName: "Scout",
};

let envFileLoaded = false;

/** Reads `.env` at the repo root once. Variables already set in the environment win. */
function loadEnvFile(): void {
  if (envFileLoaded) return;
  envFileLoaded = true;
  const path = fileURLToPath(new URL("../../.env", import.meta.url));
  if (existsSync(path)) process.loadEnvFile(path);
}

/** Reads config from the environment on every call, so tests can change it per case. */
export function loadConfig(env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv = process.env): ScoutConfig {
  if (env === process.env) loadEnvFile();
  const provider = env.SCOUT_MODEL_PROVIDER || undefined;
  if (provider !== undefined && provider !== "openai" && provider !== "anthropic") {
    throw new Error(`SCOUT_MODEL_PROVIDER must be "openai" or "anthropic", got "${provider}"`);
  }
  return {
    ...DEFAULTS,
    mode: env.SCOUT_MODE === "offline" ? "offline" : "live",
    modelProvider: provider ?? DEFAULTS.modelProvider,
    openaiModel: env.SCOUT_OPENAI_MODEL ?? DEFAULTS.openaiModel,
    anthropicModel: env.SCOUT_ANTHROPIC_MODEL ?? DEFAULTS.anthropicModel,
    port: env.PORT ? Number(env.PORT) : DEFAULTS.port,
    snapshotPath: env.SCOUT_SNAPSHOT === "off" ? null : (env.SCOUT_SNAPSHOT ?? DEFAULTS.snapshotPath),
    secUserAgent: env.SCOUT_SEC_USER_AGENT ?? DEFAULTS.secUserAgent,
    fromAddress: env.SCOUT_FROM ?? DEFAULTS.fromAddress,
  };
}

/** True when live model calls can authenticate. */
export function hasAnthropicCredentials(env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv = process.env): boolean {
  if (env === process.env) loadEnvFile();
  return Boolean(env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY || env.ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN);
}

import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import AnthropicSDK from "@anthropic-ai/sdk";
import { recordCall } from "../_calllog";
import { hasAnthropicCredentials, loadConfig } from "../../src/shared/config";
import { stableHash } from "../../src/shared/ids";

/**
 * Anthropic messages client. In live mode it calls the Claude API (with
 * server-side refusal fallbacks on); in offline mode it answers from
 * fixtures/llm/canned.json (keyed by system prompt hash) or with the first
 * three prose sentences of the last user message.
 *
 * Every call is recorded in the vendor call log either way.
 */

export interface MessageParam {
  role: "user" | "assistant";
  content: string;
}

export interface MessageCreateParams {
  model: string;
  max_tokens: number;
  system?: string;
  messages: MessageParam[];
  /** How hard the model should think. Claude Opus 5.5 defaults to medium. */
  effort?: "low" | "medium" | "high";
}

export interface Message {
  id: string;
  type: "message";
  role: "assistant";
  model: string;
  content: Array<{ type: "text"; text: string }>;
  stop_reason: "end_turn" | "max_tokens";
  usage: { input_tokens: number; output_tokens: number };
}

export class AnthropicError extends Error {
  constructor(
    readonly status: number,
    message: string,
  ) {
    super(message);
    this.name = "AnthropicError";
  }
}

// ---- Live ------------------------------------------------------------------

let sdk: AnthropicSDK | null = null;

function liveClient(): AnthropicSDK {
  if (!hasAnthropicCredentials()) {
    throw new AnthropicError(
      401,
      "Live mode needs an Anthropic API key. Add ANTHROPIC_API_KEY to .env, or set SCOUT_MODE=offline.",
    );
  }
  sdk ??= new AnthropicSDK();
  return sdk;
}

async function createLive(params: MessageCreateParams): Promise<Message> {
  const response = await liveClient().beta.messages.create({
    model: params.model,
    max_tokens: params.max_tokens,
    system: params.system,
    messages: params.messages,
    output_config: params.effort ? { effort: params.effort } : undefined,
    betas: ["server-side-fallback-2026-07-01"],
    fallbacks: "default",
  });
  if (response.stop_reason === "refusal") {
    throw new AnthropicError(422, "The model declined this request.");
  }
  const text = response.content.map((block) => (block.type === "text" ? block.text : "")).join("");
  return {
    id: response.id,
    type: "message",
    role: "assistant",
    model: response.model,
    content: [{ type: "text", text }],
    stop_reason: response.stop_reason === "max_tokens" ? "max_tokens" : "end_turn",
    usage: { input_tokens: response.usage.input_tokens, output_tokens: response.usage.output_tokens },
  };
}

// ---- Offline ---------------------------------------------------------------

let canned: Record<string, string> | null = null;

function cannedAnswers(): Record<string, string> {
  canned ??= JSON.parse(readFileSync(new URL("../../fixtures/llm/canned.json", import.meta.url), "utf8")) as Record<
    string,
    string
  >;
  return canned;
}

function leadingSentences(text: string, count: number): string {
  const prose = text
    .split("\n")
    .map((line) => line.trim().replace(/^[-*•]\s+/, ""))
    .map((line) => /^[A-Z][\w ()/&,.'-]{0,40}:\s+(.*)$/.exec(line)?.[1] ?? line)
    .filter((line) => line.split(/\s+/).length >= 6);
  const parts = (prose.length ? prose.join(" ") : text).replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim().split(/(?<=[.!?])\s+/);
  return parts.filter(Boolean).slice(0, count).join(" ");
}

let counter = 0;

function createOffline(params: MessageCreateParams): Message {
  const lastUser = [...params.messages].reverse().find((m) => m.role === "user")?.content ?? "";
  let text = cannedAnswers()[stableHash(params.system ?? "")] ?? leadingSentences(lastUser, 3);
  let stop: Message["stop_reason"] = "end_turn";
  if (Math.ceil(text.length / 4) > params.max_tokens) {
    text = text.slice(0, params.max_tokens * 4);
    stop = "max_tokens";
  }
  const inputChars = (params.system ?? "").length + params.messages.reduce((n, m) => n + m.content.length, 0);
  return {
    id: `msg_${String(++counter).padStart(6, "0")}`,
    type: "message",
    role: "assistant",
    model: params.model,
    content: [{ type: "text", text }],
    stop_reason: stop,
    usage: { input_tokens: Math.ceil(inputChars / 4), output_tokens: Math.ceil(text.length / 4) },
  };
}

// ---- Client ----------------------------------------------------------------

export class Anthropic {
  readonly messages = {
    create: (params: MessageCreateParams) => this.createMessage(params),
  };

  private async createMessage(params: MessageCreateParams): Promise<Message> {
    recordCall("llm-anthropic", "messages.create", params);
    if (!params.model) throw new AnthropicError(400, "model: field required");
    if (!params.max_tokens) throw new AnthropicError(400, "max_tokens: field required");
    if (!params.messages?.length) throw new AnthropicError(400, "messages: at least one message is required");
    if (params.messages[0]?.role !== "user") throw new AnthropicError(400, "messages: first message must use the user role");
    return loadConfig().mode === "live" ? createLive(params) : createOffline(params);
  }
}

import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import AnthropicSDK from "@anthropic-ai/sdk";
import { recordCall } from "../_calllog";
import { hasAnthropicCredentials, loadConfig } from "../../src/shared/config";
import { slugify } from "../../src/shared/ids";

/**
 * Web search. Live mode uses Claude's web search tool: Claude runs the
 * searches and cites what it read, and each cited page becomes a result with
 * the cited text as its snippet. Offline mode answers from fixtures/search.json.
 *
 * Only the query leaves the process; callers pass company names and topics,
 * never contact details.
 */

export interface SearchResult {
  title: string;
  url: string;
  snippet: string;
  rank: number;
}

export interface SearchOptions {
  limit?: number;
}

/** A page Claude found, with when it was published (if the search index knows). */
export interface WebPage {
  title: string;
  url: string;
  snippet: string;
  pageAge: string | null;
}

export class SearchError extends Error {
  constructor(message: string) {
    super(message);
    this.name = "SearchError";
  }
}

// ---- Live ------------------------------------------------------------------

const MAX_CONTINUATIONS = 3;

let sdk: AnthropicSDK | null = null;

function liveClient(): AnthropicSDK {
  if (!hasAnthropicCredentials()) {
    throw new SearchError("Live search needs an Anthropic API key. Add ANTHROPIC_API_KEY to .env, or set SCOUT_MODE=offline.");
  }
  sdk ??= new AnthropicSDK();
  return sdk;
}

/**
 * Asks Claude to search the web and returns the pages it cited, in the order
 * the search returned them. `instructions` steers what to look for.
 */
export async function searchWeb(query: string, options: { limit: number; instructions?: string }): Promise<WebPage[]> {
  const client = liveClient();
  const messages: AnthropicSDK.Beta.BetaMessageParam[] = [
    {
      role: "user",
      content: `Search the web for: ${query}\n\n${options.instructions ?? "Find the most relevant, recent pages."} Then write one sentence about each of the ${options.limit} most useful results, citing it.`,
    },
  ];

  const found = new Map<string, WebPage>();
  const cited = new Map<string, string>();
  for (let turn = 0; turn <= MAX_CONTINUATIONS; turn++) {
    const response = await client.beta.messages.create({
      model: loadConfig().anthropicModel,
      max_tokens: 4000,
      output_config: { effort: "low" },
      tools: [{ type: "web_search_20260209", name: "web_search", max_uses: 3 }],
      messages,
      betas: ["server-side-fallback-2026-07-01"],
      fallbacks: "default",
    });

    for (const block of response.content) {
      if (block.type === "web_search_tool_result" && Array.isArray(block.content)) {
        for (const page of block.content) {
          if (!found.has(page.url)) found.set(page.url, { title: page.title, url: page.url, snippet: "", pageAge: page.page_age ?? null });
        }
      } else if (block.type === "text") {
        for (const citation of block.citations ?? []) {
          if (citation.type === "web_search_result_location" && !cited.has(citation.url)) cited.set(citation.url, citation.cited_text);
        }
      }
    }

    if (response.stop_reason !== "pause_turn") break;
    messages.push({ role: "assistant", content: response.content });
  }

  // Pages Claude actually cited come first; they're the ones it judged relevant.
  const pages = [...found.values()].map((p) => ({ ...p, snippet: cited.get(p.url) ?? "" }));
  pages.sort((a, b) => Number(Boolean(b.snippet)) - Number(Boolean(a.snippet)));
  return pages.slice(0, options.limit);
}

// ---- Offline ---------------------------------------------------------------

type FixtureResult = Omit<SearchResult, "rank">;

let fixtures: Record<string, FixtureResult[]> | null = null;

function load(): Record<string, FixtureResult[]> {
  fixtures ??= JSON.parse(readFileSync(new URL("../../fixtures/search.json", import.meta.url), "utf8")) as Record<
    string,
    FixtureResult[]
  >;
  return fixtures;
}

function keyFor(query: string, keys: string[]): string | undefined {
  const slug = slugify(query);
  return keys.find((k) => k !== "_default" && (slug === k || slug.startsWith(`${k}-`) || slug.includes(`-${k}-`)));
}

function searchOffline(query: string, limit: number): FixtureResult[] {
  const data = load();
  const key = keyFor(query, Object.keys(data));
  const subject = query.split(/\s+/).slice(0, 2).join(" ");
  return key
    ? (data[key] ?? [])
    : (data._default ?? []).map((r) => ({
        title: r.title.replaceAll("{query}", subject),
        url: r.url.replaceAll("{slug}", slugify(subject)),
        snippet: r.snippet.replaceAll("{query}", subject),
      }));
}

// ---- API -------------------------------------------------------------------

export async function search(query: string, options: SearchOptions = {}): Promise<SearchResult[]> {
  const limit = Math.max(1, Math.min(options.limit ?? 5, 10));
  recordCall("search", "search", { query, limit });
  if (!query.trim()) return [];

  const results =
    loadConfig().mode === "live"
      ? (await searchWeb(query, { limit })).map(({ title, url, snippet }) => ({ title, url, snippet }))
      : searchOffline(query, limit);
  return results.slice(0, limit).map((r, i) => ({ ...r, rank: i + 1 }));
}

```typescript
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import AnthropicSDK from "@anthropic-ai/sdk";
import { recordCall } from "../_calllog";
import { searchWeb } from "../search/index";
import { hasAnthropicCredentials, loadConfig } from "../../src/shared/config";
import { slugify } from "../../src/shared/ids";

/**
 * News: recent headlines per company, plus the latest earnings call
 * transcript. Live mode finds both with Claude's web search (transcripts also
 * use web fetch to read the page); offline mode reads fixtures/news.json.
 */

export interface Headline {
  title: string;
  source: string;
  url: string;
  publishedAt: string;
  summary: string;
}

export interface Transcript {
  company: string;
  quarter: string;
  heldOn: string;
  participants: string[];
  text: string;
}

// ---- Live ------------------------------------------------------------------

/** "September 18, 2026" / "3 days ago" / ISO -> "2026-09-18"; unknown -> "". */
export function toIsoDate(pageAge: string | null, now = new Date()): string {
  if (!pageAge) return "";
  const relative = /(\d+)\s+(day|week|month)s?\s+ago/i.exec(pageAge);
  if (relative) {
    const days = Number(relative[1]) * ({ day: 1, week: 7, month: 30 }[relative[2]!.toLowerCase() as "day"] ?? 1);
    return new Date(now.getTime() - days * 86_400_000).toISOString().slice(0, 10);
  }
  const parsed = Date.parse(pageAge);
  return Number.isNaN(parsed) ? "" : new Date(parsed).toISOString().slice(0, 10);
}

function sourceOf(url: string): string {
  try {
    return new URL(url).hostname.replace(/^www\./, "");
  } catch {
    return "";
  }
}

async function headlinesLive(company: string, limit: number): Promise<Headline[]> {
  const pages = await searchWeb(`${company} news`, {
    limit,
    instructions: `Find news articles about ${company} from the last three months: deals, results, leadership changes, launches and expansion. Skip the company's own marketing pages.`,
  });
  return pages.map((p) => ({
    title: p.title,
    source: sourceOf(p.url),
    url: p.url,
    publishedAt: toIsoDate(p.pageAge),
    summary: p.snippet,
  }));
}

const TRANSCRIPT_SYSTEM =
  "You retrieve earnings call transcripts. Find the company's most recent earnings call transcript, read it, and reply with exactly this layout: a first line 'Quarter: <fiscal quarter>; Date: <YYYY-MM-DD>; Participants: <names and roles, separated by semicolons>', a blank line, then the prepared remarks and the Q&A quoted as faithfully as you can, up to about 1,500 words. If you can't find a transcript, reply with the single word NONE.";

async function transcriptLive(company: string): Promise<Transcript | null> {
  if (!hasAnthropicCredentials()) {
    throw new Error("Live news needs an Anthropic API key. Add ANTHROPIC_API_KEY to .env, or set SCOUT_MODE=offline.");
  }
  const client = new AnthropicSDK();
  const messages: AnthropicSDK.Beta.BetaMessageParam[] = [{ role: "user", content: `Company: ${company}` }];
  let text = "";
  for (let turn = 0; turn <= 3; turn++) {
    const response = await client.beta.messages.create({
      model: loadConfig().anthropicModel,
      max_tokens: 8000,
      system: TRANSCRIPT_SYSTEM,
      output_config: { effort: "low" },
      tools: [
        { type: "web_search_20260209", name: "web_search", max_uses: 3 },
        { type: "web_fetch_20260209", name: "web_fetch", max_uses: 2 },
      ],
      messages,
      betas: ["server-side-fallback-2026-07-01"],
      fallbacks: "default",
    });
    text += response.content.map((b) => (b.type === "text" ? b.text : "")).join("");
    if (response.stop_reason !== "pause_turn") break;
    messages.push({ role: "assistant", content: response.content });
  }

  const trimmed = text.trim();
  if (!trimmed || trimmed === "NONE") return null;
  const [header = "", ...body] = trimmed.split("\n");
  const field = (name: string) => new RegExp(`${name}:\\s*([^;]+)`, "i").exec(header)?.[1]?.trim() ?? "";
  const participants = /Participants:\s*(.*)$/i.exec(header)?.[1]?.split(";").map((p) => p.trim()).filter(Boolean) ?? [];
  return { company, quarter: field("Quarter"), heldOn: field("Date"), participants, text: body.join("\n").trim() };
}

// ---- Offline ---------------------------------------------------------------

interface CompanyNews {
  name: string;
  headlines: Headline[];
  transcript: Omit<Transcript, "company">;
}

let fixtures: Record<string, CompanyNews> | null = null;

function load(): Record<string, CompanyNews> {
  fixtures ??= JSON.parse(readFileSync(new URL("../../fixtures/news.json", import.meta.url), "utf8")) as Record<
    string,
    CompanyNews
  >;
  return fixtures;
}

function lookup(company: string): { entry: CompanyNews; generic: boolean } {
  const data = load();
  const slug = slugify(company);
  const key = Object.keys(data).find((k) => k !== "_default" && (slug === k || slug.startsWith(`${k}-`)));
  const entry = key ? data[key] : data._default;
  if (!entry) throw new Error("news fixtures are missing a _default entry");
  return { entry, generic: !key };
}

function fill(text: string, company: string): string {
  return text.replaceAll("{company}", company);
}

function headlinesOffline(company: string, limit: number): Headline[] {
  const { entry, generic } = lookup(company);
  return [...entry.headlines]
    .sort((a, b) => b.publishedAt.localeCompare(a.publishedAt))
    .slice(0, limit)
    .map((h) =>
      generic
        ? { ...h, title: fill(h.title, company), summary: fill(h.summary, company), url: fill(h.url, slugify(company)) }
        : h,
    );
}

// ---- API -------------------------------------------------------------------

export async function latestHeadlines(company: string, options: { limit?: number } = {}): Promise<Headline[]> {
  const limit = options.limit ?? 5;
  recordCall("news", "headlines", { company, limit });
  if (loadConfig().mode === "offline") return headlinesOffline(company, limit);
  const headlines = await headlinesLive(company, limit);
  return headlines.sort((a, b) => b.publishedAt.localeCompare(a.publishedAt));
}

export async function earningsTranscript(company: string): Promise<Transcript | null> {
  recordCall("news", "transcripts.latest", { company });
  if (loadConfig().mode === "live") return transcriptLive(company);
  const { entry, generic } = lookup(company);
  if (generic) return null;
  return { company: entry.name, ...entry.transcript };
}

```typescript
import { existsSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync, statSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { dirname, join } from "node:path";
import { recordCall } from "../_calllog";
import { loadConfig } from "../../src/shared/config";
import { slugify } from "../../src/shared/ids";

/**
 * SEC EDGAR. Live mode reads the public EDGAR APIs (no key; the SEC asks for a
 * descriptive User-Agent), turns the filing's HTML into text and splits it
 * into the usual sections. Responses are cached under .scout/cache/sec.
 * Offline mode reads fixtures/sec-edgar/<company>.json.
 */

export type FormType = "10-K" | "10-Q";

export interface FilingSections {
  business?: string;
  mdna: string;
  financials: string;
  risks?: string;
}

export interface Filing {
  company: string;
  cik: string;
  form: FormType;
  period: string;
  filedAt: string;
  accession: string;
  sections: FilingSections;
}

export interface FilingSummary {
  form: FormType;
  period: string;
  filedAt: string;
  accession: string;
}

/** What EDGAR knows about a registrant, plus its latest annual revenue. */
export interface CompanyFacts {
  name: string;
  cik: string;
  tickers: string[];
  industry: string;
  headquarters: string;
  website: string | null;
  annualRevenue: number | null;
  fiscalYear: number | null;
}

export class EdgarError extends Error {
  constructor(message: string) {
    super(message);
    this.name = "EdgarError";
  }
}

// ---- Live: HTTP with a small disk cache ------------------------------------

const DAY = 86_400_000;
const MAX_SECTION_CHARS = 100_000;
let lastRequestAt = 0;

async function secFetch(url: string, cacheFile: string, maxAgeMs: number): Promise<string> {
  const path = join(loadConfig().cacheDir, "sec", cacheFile);
  if (existsSync(path) && Date.now() - statSync(path).mtimeMs < maxAgeMs) return readFileSync(path, "utf8");

  // The SEC allows 10 requests a second; stay well under it.
  const wait = lastRequestAt + 150 - Date.now();
  if (wait > 0) await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, wait));
  lastRequestAt = Date.now();

  const res = await fetch(url, { headers: { "User-Agent": loadConfig().secUserAgent, Accept: "*/*" } });
  if (!res.ok) throw new EdgarError(`SEC EDGAR returned ${res.status} for ${url}`);
  const body = await res.text();
  mkdirSync(dirname(path), { recursive: true });
  writeFileSync(path, body);
  return body;
}

interface TickerEntry {
  cik_str: number;
  ticker: string;
  title: string;
}

const SUFFIXES = /\b(incorporated|inc|corporation|corp|company|co|holdings|group|ltd|plc|llc|lp|the)\b/g;

function normalizeName(name: string): string {
  return slugify(name).replace(/-/g, " ").replace(SUFFIXES, "").replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim();
}

async function resolveCik(company: string): Promise<{ cik: string; title: string } | null> {
  const tickers = Object.values(
    JSON.parse(await secFetch("https://www.sec.gov/files/company_tickers.json", "company_tickers.json", DAY)) as Record<
      string,
      TickerEntry
    >,
  );
  const wanted = normalizeName(company);
  const byTicker = tickers.find((t) => t.ticker === company.trim().toUpperCase());
  const exact = tickers.find((t) => normalizeName(t.title) === wanted);
  const prefix = tickers.find((t) => normalizeName(t.title).startsWith(`${wanted} `));
  const hit = exact ?? byTicker ?? prefix;
  return hit ? { cik: String(hit.cik_str).padStart(10, "0"), title: hit.title } : null;
}

interface Submissions {
  name: string;
  tickers: string[];
  sicDescription: string;
  website?: string;
  addresses: { business: { city: string | null; stateOrCountry: string | null } };
  filings: {
    recent: {
      form: string[];
      filingDate: string[];
      reportDate: string[];
      accessionNumber: string[];
      primaryDocument: string[];
    };
  };
}

async function submissions(cik: string): Promise<Submissions> {
  return JSON.parse(await secFetch(`https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK${cik}.json`, `submissions-${cik}.json`, DAY)) as Submissions;
}

function recentFilings(sub: Submissions): Array<FilingSummary & { document: string }> {
  const r = sub.filings.recent;
  const out: Array<FilingSummary & { document: string }> = [];
  r.form.forEach((form, i) => {
    if (form !== "10-K" && form !== "10-Q") return;
    out.push({
      form,
      period: r.reportDate[i] ?? "",
      filedAt: r.filingDate[i] ?? "",
      accession: r.accessionNumber[i] ?? "",
      document: r.primaryDocument[i] ?? "",
    });
  });
  return out.sort((a, b) => b.filedAt.localeCompare(a.filedAt));
}

const ENTITIES: Record<string, string> = { "&amp;": "&", "&lt;": "<", "&gt;": ">", "&quot;": '"', "&#39;": "'", "&nbsp;": " " };

/** Filing HTML (inline XBRL) to plain text, one block per line. */
export function htmlToText(html: string): string {
  return html
    .replace(/<(script|style|ix:header)[^>]*>[\s\S]*?<\/\1>/gi, " ")
    .replace(/<br\s*\/?>|<\/(p|div|tr|li|h\d|table)>/gi, "\n")
    .replace(/<\/t[dh]>/gi, " ")
    .replace(/<[^>]+>/g, " ")
    .replace(/&#(\d+);/g, (_, n: string) => String.fromCharCode(Number(n)))
    .replace(/&#x([0-9a-f]+);/gi, (_, n: string) => String.fromCharCode(parseInt(n, 16)))
    .replace(/&[a-z]+;/gi, (e) => ENTITIES[e.toLowerCase()] ?? " ")
    .replace(/[ \t ]+/g, " ")
    .replace(/\n\s*\n+/g, "\n")
    .trim();
}

/**
 * The longest span from a `start` heading to the next `end` heading. Taking
 * the longest skips the table of contents, where headings sit next to each other.
 */
export function section(text: string, start: RegExp, end: RegExp): string {
  let best = "";
  for (const match of text.matchAll(new RegExp(start.source, "gi"))) {
    const stop = new RegExp(end.source, "gi");
    stop.lastIndex = (match.index ?? 0) + match[0].length;
    const hit = stop.exec(text);
    const span = text.slice(match.index ?? 0, hit ? hit.index : undefined);
    if (hit && span.length > best.length) best = span;
  }
  if (best.length <= MAX_SECTION_CHARS) return best.trim();
  return `${best.slice(0, MAX_SECTION_CHARS).trim()}\n[Section continues; cut at ${MAX_SECTION_CHARS.toLocaleString("en-US")} characters.]`;
}

function splitSections(form: FormType, text: string): FilingSections {
  if (form === "10-K") {
    return {
      business: section(text, /item\s*1\.?\s*business/, /item\s*1a\.?\s*risk\s*factors/),
      risks: section(text, /item\s*1a\.?\s*risk\s*factors/, /item\s*1b\.?\s*unresolved/),
      mdna: section(text, /item\s*7\.?\s*management.s\s*discussion/, /item\s*7a\.?\s*quantitative/),
      financials: section(text, /item\s*8\.?\s*financial\s*statements/, /item\s*9\.?\s*changes\s*in/),
    };
  }
  return {
    mdna: section(text, /item\s*2\.?\s*management.s\s*discussion/, /item\s*3\.?\s*quantitative/),
    financials: section(text, /item\s*1\.?\s*financial\s*statements/, /item\s*2\.?\s*management.s\s*discussion/),
    risks: section(text, /item\s*1a\.?\s*risk\s*factors/, /item\s*2\.?\s*unregistered/),
  };
}

async function latestFilingLive(company: string, form: FormType): Promise<Filing | null> {
  const resolved = await resolveCik(company);
  if (!resolved) return null;
  const sub = await submissions(resolved.cik);
  const latest = recentFilings(sub).find((f) => f.form === form);
  if (!latest) return null;

  const folder = latest.accession.replace(/-/g, "");
  const html = await secFetch(
    `https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/${Number(resolved.cik)}/${folder}/${latest.document}`,
    `${folder}.htm`,
    365 * DAY,
  );
  return {
    company: sub.name,
    cik: resolved.cik,
    form,
    period: latest.period,
    filedAt: latest.filedAt,
    accession: latest.accession,
    sections: splitSections(form, htmlToText(html)),
  };
}

interface FactUnit {
  val: number;
  fy: number;
  fp: string;
  form: string;
  end: string;
}

const REVENUE_CONCEPTS = ["Revenues", "RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax", "SalesRevenueNet"];

async function companyFactsLive(company: string): Promise<CompanyFacts | null> {
  const resolved = await resolveCik(company);
  if (!resolved) return null;
  const sub = await submissions(resolved.cik);
  const facts = JSON.parse(
    await secFetch(`https://data.sec.gov/api/xbrl/companyfacts/CIK${resolved.cik}.json`, `facts-${resolved.cik}.json`, DAY),
  ) as { facts?: { "us-gaap"?: Record<string, { units?: { USD?: FactUnit[] } }> } };

  let annual: FactUnit | undefined;
  for (const concept of REVENUE_CONCEPTS) {
    const values = facts.facts?.["us-gaap"]?.[concept]?.units?.USD ?? [];
    const latest = values.filter((v) => v.form === "10-K" && v.fp === "FY").sort((a, b) => b.end.localeCompare(a.end))[0];
    if (latest && (!annual || latest.end > annual.end)) annual = latest;
  }

  const { city, stateOrCountry } = sub.addresses.business;
  return {
    name: sub.name,
    cik: resolved.cik,
    tickers: sub.tickers,
    industry: sub.sicDescription,
    headquarters: [city, stateOrCountry].filter(Boolean).join(", "),
    website: sub.website || null,
    annualRevenue: annual?.val ?? null,
    fiscalYear: annual ? Number(annual.end.slice(0, 4)) : null,
  };
}

// ---- Offline ---------------------------------------------------------------

interface CompanyFilings {
  name: string;
  cik: string;
  filings: Array<Omit<Filing, "company" | "cik">>;
}

const offlineCache = new Map<string, CompanyFilings | null>();

function loadOffline(company: string): CompanyFilings | null {
  const slug = slugify(company).split("-")[0] ?? "";
  if (!offlineCache.has(slug)) {
    const url = new URL(`../../fixtures/sec-edgar/${slug}.json`, import.meta.url);
    offlineCache.set(slug, slug && existsSync(url) ? (JSON.parse(readFileSync(url, "utf8")) as CompanyFilings) : null);
  }
  return offlineCache.get(slug) ?? null;
}

// ---- API -------------------------------------------------------------------

const live = () => loadConfig().mode === "live";

export async function listFilings(company: string): Promise<FilingSummary[]> {
  recordCall("sec-edgar", "filings.list", { company });
  if (live()) {
    const resolved = await resolveCik(company);
    if (!resolved) return [];
    return recentFilings(await submissions(resolved.cik)).map(({ form, period, filedAt, accession }) => ({ form, period, filedAt, accession }));
  }
  const data = loadOffline(company);
  if (!data) return [];
  return data.filings
    .map(({ form, period, filedAt, accession }) => ({ form, period, filedAt, accession }))
    .sort((a, b) => b.filedAt.localeCompare(a.filedAt));
}

/** Most recent filing of the given form, or null if the company has none on file. */
export async function latestFiling(company: string, form: FormType): Promise<Filing | null> {
  recordCall("sec-edgar", "filings.latest", { company, form });
  if (live()) return latestFilingLive(company, form);
  const data = loadOffline(company);
  if (!data) return null;
  const match = data.filings.filter((f) => f.form === form).sort((a, b) => b.filedAt.localeCompare(a.filedAt))[0];
  return match ? { company: data.name, cik: data.cik, ...match } : null;
}

/** Registrant details and latest annual revenue. Live mode only; offline returns null. */
export async function companyFacts(company: string): Promise<CompanyFacts | null> {
  recordCall("sec-edgar", "companyfacts", { company });
  return live() ? companyFactsLive(company) : null;
}

/** The filing as one text document, sections in the order they appear in the form. */
export function filingText(filing: Filing): string {
  const { business, mdna, financials, risks } = filing.sections;
  return [
    business && `Item 1. Business\n${business}`,
    risks && `Item 1A. Risk Factors\n${risks}`,
    `Management's Discussion and Analysis\n${mdna}`,
    `Financial Statements\n${financials}`,
  ]
    .filter(Boolean)
    .join("\n\n");
}

```typescript
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { recordCall } from "../_calllog";
import { companyFacts } from "../sec-edgar/index";
import { loadConfig } from "../../src/shared/config";
import { slugify } from "../../src/shared/ids";

/**
 * Company and person enrichment (Clearbit-style). Live mode builds company
 * profiles from SEC EDGAR registrant data and XBRL revenue; people are matched
 * against our own records only. Offline mode reads fixtures/enrichment.json.
 */

export interface CompanyProfile {
  name: string;
  domain: string | null;
  industry: string;
  employees: number | null;
  revenue: string | null;
  founded: number | null;
  headquarters: string;
  description: string;
  tech: string[];
}

export interface PersonProfile {
  email: string;
  name: string | null;
  title: string | null;
  seniority: "executive" | "director" | "manager" | "individual" | null;
  linkedin: string | null;
  company: string | null;
}

interface Fixtures {
  companies: Record<string, CompanyProfile>;
  people: Record<string, Omit<PersonProfile, "email">>;
}

let fixtures: Fixtures | null = null;

function load(): Fixtures {
  fixtures ??= JSON.parse(readFileSync(new URL("../../fixtures/enrichment.json", import.meta.url), "utf8")) as Fixtures;
  return fixtures;
}

/** 4_512_300_000 -> "$4.5B" */
export function formatRevenue(usd: number): string {
  if (usd >= 1e9) return `$${(usd / 1e9).toFixed(1).replace(/\.0$/, "")}B`;
  if (usd >= 1e6) return `$${Math.round(usd / 1e6)}M`;
  return `$${Math.round(usd / 1e3)}K`;
}

function titleCase(value: string): string {
  return value.toLowerCase().replace(/\b[a-z]/g, (c) => c.toUpperCase());
}

async function enrichCompanyLive(name: string): Promise<CompanyProfile | null> {
  const facts = await companyFacts(name);
  if (!facts) return null;
  const industry = titleCase(facts.industry || "Unknown industry");
  return {
    name: titleCase(facts.name.replace(/[,.]?\s*(inc|corp|corporation|incorporated)\.?$/i, "")),
    domain: facts.website ? facts.website.replace(/^https?:\/\//, "").replace(/\/.*$/, "") : null,
    industry,
    employees: null,
    revenue: facts.annualRevenue ? formatRevenue(facts.annualRevenue) : null,
    founded: null,
    headquarters: titleCase(facts.headquarters),
    description: `${industry} company${facts.tickers.length ? ` listed as ${facts.tickers.join(", ")}` : ""}${
      facts.fiscalYear ? `; revenue figure is for fiscal ${facts.fiscalYear}` : ""
    }.`,
    tech: [],
  };
}

export async function enrichCompany(nameOrDomain: string): Promise<CompanyProfile | null> {
  recordCall("enrichment", "companies.find", { query: nameOrDomain });
  if (loadConfig().mode === "live") return enrichCompanyLive(nameOrDomain);
  const { companies } = load();
  const query = nameOrDomain.toLowerCase().trim();
  const slug = slugify(nameOrDomain);
  const hit = Object.entries(companies).find(
    ([key, c]) => c.domain === query || slug === key || slug.startsWith(`${key}-`) || slugify(c.name) === slug,
  );
  return hit ? hit[1] : null;
}

export async function enrichPerson(email: string): Promise<PersonProfile> {
  recordCall("enrichment", "people.find", { email });
  const { people, companies } = load();
  const normalized = email.toLowerCase().trim();
  const known = people[normalized];
  if (known) return { email: normalized, ...known };

  const domain = normalized.split("@")[1] ?? "";
  const company = Object.values(companies).find((c) => c.domain === domain);
  return { email: normalized, name: null, title: null, seniority: null, linkedin: null, company: company?.name ?? null };
}

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-11 19:46:24Z)**_

Most of what's built is real and works on any repo, but it has only been exercised on Scout. Here's the split.

## Real, and works on any repo

- **A live map that follows a real Claude Code session.** You point Harness at a local git repo (`HARNESS_REPO=…`). It scans the files, places each one in a domain × layer cell, and works out which domains depend on which from the actual imports. While Claude works, the map updates live: reads mark cells and move the agent cursor, edits fill cells with +/− counts, and new imports draw new edges. A file watcher catches changes no hook reported.
- **The plan step.** Every turn starts in plan mode. Claude submits numbered steps, and they show on the map as dashed "ghost" cells and edges before any code exists. You approve in the UI; edits then fill the ghosts, and anything Claude does that wasn't in its plan shows amber.
- **The rule checks.** Three kinds of rule: only some domains may import X, only one domain may write a table, and two domains must not depend on each other. The same check runs on load, on each submitted plan, and before every edit, including edits Claude tries to make through Bash. A hit makes Claude stop and ask you A or B.
- **Decision memory.** Your answer becomes a `decisions/DR-n.md` file plus a `domains.yaml` update, committed to the target repo, and is recorded in Alike. Later sessions get your decisions up front and are blocked with "You decided this in DR-n" if they go against one.
- **The cartographer.** If the repo has no map, a separate one-shot model call proposes domains, layers and three rules, and you confirm it.
- **The interface.** The grid, chat, A/B fork card, Approve button, ledger counters, turn summary, inspector and replay scrubber all work on any map.

## Demo-specific or scaffolding

- **The scripted turn behind `?fake=play`.** It's recorded data, not a session.
- **The sandbox script and reference map** (`scripts/sandbox.sh`, `fixtures/scout-agent.domains.yaml`). The sandbox is a stub copy of Scout's layout, and the reference map is the fallback if the cartographer misfires on stage.
- **Detecting table writes.** It only recognizes Scout's convention, `db.insert("table")` and `db.update("table")`. Prisma, SQL and other ORMs aren't detected, so the table-ownership rule does nothing on most real codebases.
- **Default ignore rules** (root `*.json`, `*.md`, config files) are tuned to keep Scout's map clean.
- **The demo prompt** names the shortcut on purpose, because Claude usually avoids the fork by itself.

## What stops it being a general tool today

- **TS/JS only, relative imports only.** Path aliases like `@/components` and package imports are skipped, so many Next.js and monorepo codebases would show few or no edges.
- **The cartographer won't scale.** It puts every file and import into one prompt, so on a repo with thousands of files it will be slow or fail. It has only run on Scout-shaped code.
- **One fixed repo and one session per server run.** There's no repo picker, no "new session" button and no re-map button. Starting a fresh Claude session means restarting the server, and Claude loses its conversation; the event history and decisions survive.
- **Only the domain grid is built.** The plan's other levels (journeys, inside-a-domain views, wiring traces) and showing test results on cells aren't built.
- **Scale is untested.** It's been run on about 50 files, and the scan takes about 30 ms there. Behaviour on large repos is unknown.
- **After you approve a plan, Claude can run any command without asking.**

## What's been tested, and what hasn't

- **Tested with real Claude** against a copy of the real Scout, driven by a script through the server's API, many times:
  - planning, the fork and its answer, approval and the build;
  - session memory;
  - the option-B exception;
  - the Bash write gate;
  - the cartographer;
  - writing to Alike.

  I also took screenshots of the interface showing a real turn.
- **Not yet tested:** typing in the chat box and clicking the A/B, Approve and Confirm buttons during a live session. They call the same endpoints the script used, so the risk is low, but nobody has done it end to end.

In short, it's a working, deterministic "live map of what the agent is doing" for TS/JS repos that use relative imports and have a `domains.yaml`, or one the cartographer can propose. Turning it into a general tool would take, in order: path-alias resolution, real ORM write detection, a cartographer that samples big repos instead of reading everything, and a repo, session and re-map control in the UI.

/** Reloads a resource every `ms` while `active` is true, e.g. while a run is still going. */
export function usePolling(resource: Resource<unknown>, active: boolean, ms = 1500): void {
  const { loading, reload } = resource;
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!active || loading) return;
    const timer = window.setTimeout(reload, ms);
    return () => window.clearTimeout(timer);
  }, [active, loading, reload, ms]);
}'''),

/** The tools a run used, in order, as waypoints on a line. While running, planned tools wait at the end. */
export function Trail({ steps, planned = [], running = false }: { steps: Step[]; planned?: string[]; running?: boolean }) {
  const pending = running ? planned.slice(steps.length) : [];
  if (steps.length === 0 && pending.length === 0) {
    return <p className="muted">{running ? "Planning which tools to use" : "No tools ran."}</p>;
  }
  return (
    <ol className="trail">
      {steps.map((step) => (
        <Waypoint key={step.index} step={step} />
      ))}
      {pending.map((tool, i) => (
        <PendingWaypoint key={`${tool}-${i}`} index={steps.length + i + 1} tool={tool} current={i === 0} />
      ))}
    </ol>
  );
}'''),

 * npm run seed
 *

 * snapshot so the app has history to draw on. Live mode seeds contacts at real
 * public companies; offline mode uses the sample companies in fixtures/.
 */
import { addNote } from "../src/memory/notes-store";
import { indexNotes } from "../src/memory/vector-index";
import { syncContact } from "../src/outreach/crm-sync";
import { loadConfig } from "../src/shared/config";
import { db } from "../src/shared/db";

const LIVE_CONTACTS = [
  { company: "Symbotic", contact: { name: "Maya Ortiz", email: "maya.ortiz@symbotic.com", title: "VP Operations" } },
  { company: "Old Dominion Freight Line", contact: { name: "Ben Carter", email: "ben.carter@odfl.com", title: "Director of Procurement" } },
  { company: "Veeva Systems", contact: { name: "Priya Nair", email: "priya.nair@veeva.com", title: "VP, IT Partnerships" } },
  { company: "Snowflake", contact: { name: "Sam Whitaker", email: "sam.whitaker@snowflake.com", title: "VP Revenue Operations" } },
];

const OFFLINE_CONTACTS = [
  { company: "Acme Robotics", contact: { name: "Jane Doe", email: "jane.doe@acmerobotics.com", title: "VP Operations" } },
  { company: "Northwind Freight", contact: { name: "Priya Raman", email: "priya.raman@northwindfreight.com", title: "Head of Procurement" } },
  { company: "Halcyon Health", contact: { name: "Sam Okafor", email: "sam.okafor@halcyonhealth.com", title: "Director, IT Partnerships" } },
  { company: "Brightline Software", contact: { name: "Lena Fischer", email: "lena.fischer@brightline.io", title: "VP Revenue Operations" } },
];

const OFFLINE_NOTES: Array<{ company: string; text: string }> = [
  { company: "Acme Robotics", text: "Ops team is measured on time to first pick; deployments are the bottleneck, not hardware." },
  { company: "Acme Robotics", text: "Procurement is consolidating field service and planning tools this year." },
  { company: "Northwind Freight", text: "New TMS rollout runs through next year; they are wary of adding vendors mid-migration." },
  { company: "Northwind Freight", text: "Cross-border lanes are the growth story; Laredo terminal just opened." },
  { company: "Halcyon Health", text: "Buying committee includes nursing informatics; time to go-live matters more than price." },
  { company: "Brightline Software", text: "RevOps owns tooling budget; they want fewer tools after the Series E." },
];

async function main(): Promise<void> {
  const { snapshotPath, mode } = loadConfig();
  if (!snapshotPath) throw new Error("SCOUT_SNAPSHOT is off; nothing to seed into");
  db.restore(snapshotPath);

  const contacts = mode === "live" ? LIVE_CONTACTS : OFFLINE_CONTACTS;
  for (const { company, contact } of contacts) await syncContact(contact, company);
  const notes = mode === "live" ? [] : OFFLINE_NOTES.map((n) => addNote({ ...n, source: "seed" }));
  await indexNotes(notes);

  db.snapshot(snapshotPath);
  console.log(`seeded ${contacts.length} contacts and ${notes.length} notes into ${snapshotPath} (${mode})`);
}

main().catch((err: unknown) => {
  console.error(err instanceof Error ? err.message : err);
  process.exitCode = 1;
});
EOF

```typescript
import { Anthropic } from "../../vendor/llm-anthropic/index";
import { latestHeadlines } from "../../vendor/news/index";
import { loadConfig } from "../shared/config";
import type { Tool } from "../shared/types";

const client = new Anthropic();

export const newsSummarize: Tool = {
  name: "news_summarize",
  tags: ["news", "summary"],
  description: "Turns the company's latest headlines into talking points for the contact.",

  async run(input, ctx) {
    const headlines = await latestHeadlines(input.company, { limit: 6 });
    if (headlines.length === 0) {
      return { tool: this.name, summary: "", facts: [], sources: [] };
    }

    const contact = [input.contact.name, input.contact.title, input.contact.email, input.contact.phone]
      .filter(Boolean)
      .join(", ");
    const news = headlines.map((h) => `- ${h.title} (${h.publishedAt}). ${h.summary}`).join("\n");

    const response = await client.messages.create({
      model: loadConfig().anthropicModel,
      max_tokens: 2000,
      effort: "low",
      system: `Turn recent news about ${input.company} into two or three talking points for a call with ${contact}. Their goal: ${input.goal}. Keep every figure exact.`,
      messages: [{ role: "user", content: news }],
    });
    ctx.log.debug("summarized news", { headlines: headlines.length });

    return {
      tool: this.name,
      summary: response.content.map((block) => block.text).join(""),
      facts: headlines.map((h) => h.title),
      sources: headlines.map((h) => h.url),
    };
  },
};

```

````text
1	# Scout
2	
3	Scout is a research agent for B2B sales. Give it a prospect company, a contact and a goal, and it:
4	
5	1. researches the company: web search, firmographics, recent news, SEC filings;
6	2. recalls notes from earlier research on the same company and saves new ones;
7	3. writes a short research brief with a language model;
8	4. syncs the contact to the CRM and drafts an outreach email (and sends it if you ask).
9	
10	It comes with a web app for the whole workflow: start research, read the brief and the trail of tools behind it, review and send the email, browse what Scout remembers about each account, and see model usage.
11	
12	Everything runs offline. External services (model providers, search, news, SEC EDGAR, enrichment, CRM, email) are in-process fakes under `vendor/` that answer from `fixtures/`, so runs are fast and deterministic and need no API keys.
13	
14	## Running it
15	
16	Requires Node 20+ (22 recommended).
17	
18	```sh
19	npm i
20	npm run seed        # optional: sample contacts and notes in .scout/db.json
21	npm run build       # builds the web app into web/dist
22	npm start           # app and API on http://localhost:8787
23	```
24	
25	For development, `npm run dev` runs the API on :8787 (restarting on change) and the web app with hot reload on http://localhost:5173.
26	
27	```sh
28	npm test            # vitest, about 25 tests, under a second
29	npm run typecheck   # server and web app
30	npm run proof       # runs 20 sample requests and reports on model traffic
31	```
32	
33	From the command line:
34	
35	```sh
36	npm run scout -- --company "Acme Robotics" --contact jane.doe@acmerobotics.com \
37	  --name "Jane Doe" --goal "Prep for a renewal call; check recent news"
38	```
39	
40	Add `--send` to send the drafted email, or `--json` for the full result. State is kept in `.scout/db.json` between runs (`SCOUT_SNAPSHOT=off` disables it).
41	
42	Over HTTP (the same API the web app uses):
43	
44	```sh
45	curl -X POST localhost:8787/api/runs -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{
46	  "company": "Acme Robotics",
47	  "contact": { "email": "jane.doe@acmerobotics.com", "name": "Jane Doe" },
48	  "goal": "Prep for a renewal call; check recent news"
49	}'
50	curl localhost:8787/api/runs/run_0001
51	```
52	
53	### Configuration
54	
55	| Variable | Default | |
56	| --- | --- | --- |
57	| `SCOUT_MODEL_PROVIDER` | `openai` | `openai` or `anthropic` |
58	| `SCOUT_OPENAI_MODEL` / `SCOUT_ANTHROPIC_MODEL` | `gpt-4o-mini` / `claude-3-5-haiku` | |
59	| `SCOUT_SNAPSHOT` | `.scout/db.json` | path, or `off` |
60	| `SCOUT_LOG_LEVEL` | `warn` | `debug`, `info`, `warn`, `error` |
61	| `PORT` | `8787` | |
62	
63	## How it's organized
64	
65	```
66	src/
67	  channels/       HTTP routes, CLI, request validation
68	  orchestrator/   run loop, planner, tool registry, run state
69	  tools/          research tools (one file each) and the tool list
70	  gateway/        model calls: complete(), embed(), redaction, cost ledger, providers
71	  memory/         notes, vector index, retrieval
72	  outreach/       CRM sync, email drafting, sending, outreach log
73	  shared/         db, config, logger, types, ids
74	web/              the web app (React + Vite)
75	  src/app/        shell: layout, navigation, routing
76	  src/features/   one folder per area: runs, notes, outreach, usage, tools
77	  src/shared/     API client, formatting, shared components, styles
78	vendor/           offline fakes of external services; every call is recorded in vendor/_calllog.ts
79	fixtures/         canned vendor responses and sample requests
80	scripts/          dev runner, proof report and seed data
81	test/             tests, one folder per area of src/
82	```
83	
84	A run goes: validate the request, sync the contact, recall earlier notes, plan which tools to use, run them (at most six steps), save the findings as notes, write the brief, then draft the email.
85	
86	Storage is an in-memory table store with JSON snapshots (`src/shared/db.ts`). Writes go through `db.insert("<table>", row)` and `db.update("<table>", id, patch)`.
87	
88	## Adding a tool
89	
90	A tool is an object with a `name`, some `tags`, a `description` and an async `run(input, ctx)` that returns a summary, facts and sources (the `Tool` type in `src/shared/types.ts`). To add one:
91	
92	1. Create a file in `src/tools/` that exports the tool.
93	2. Add it to the list in `src/tools/index.ts`.
94	
95	The planner picks tools two ways: the model chooses from the descriptions, and any tool whose tag appears as a word in the goal is added too (plurals don't matter, so a `filing` tag matches "filings"). Pick tags a rep would actually type. `npm run proof` calls every registered tool, so new tools are covered automatically.
96	
97	See `src/tools/` for examples.
98	
99	### API
100	
101	| Method | Path | |
102	| --- | --- | --- |
103	| `POST` | `/api/runs` | start a run; returns the brief, steps and email |
104	| `GET` | `/api/runs`, `/api/runs/:id` | recent runs; one run with its email and model cost |
105	| `GET` | `/api/accounts`, `/api/accounts/:company/notes` | companies with notes; a company's notes |
106	| `GET` | `/api/contacts` | contacts synced to the CRM |
107	| `GET` | `/api/outreach` | drafted and sent emails |
108	| `POST` | `/api/outreach/:id/send` | send a drafted email |
109	| `GET` | `/api/usage` | model calls and cost |
110	| `GET` | `/api/tools` | registered tools |
111
````

Not the one running now. It points at the throwaway sandbox in `/var/folders/.../harness-sandbox`, so anything Claude does there never touches Scout.

Restarted against Scout, it can change Scout for real:
```
! lsof -ti tcp:4310,5173 | xargs kill; HARNESS_REPO=../scout-agent npm run dev
```

What happens in `../scout-agent` once you do:
- **First load:** there's no `domains.yaml` yet, so the cartographer proposes a map. Clicking **Confirm** writes it and commits it.
- **Each turn:** after you approve a plan, Claude edits Scout's real files. Those edits stay uncommitted, so `git diff` shows them and `git checkout .` undoes them.
- **Each fork you answer:** Harness writes `decisions/DR-n.md`, updates `domains.yaml`, and commits just those two files.
- **Always:** Harness keeps its event log in `.harness/`, which it hides from git.

Before you start:
- **Make it easy to undo:** run `git -C ../scout-agent checkout -b harness-demo` first, and you can throw the whole run away afterwards.
- **Expect an Unassigned column:** the map doesn't cover Scout's new `web/` app yet, so those 31 files land there. I can fix that in the map first if you want a clean grid.
- **It costs usage:** each chat message runs Claude on your Claude Code login.

**The deeper levels are bigger jobs.** Wiring needs real call-graph extraction (roughly a day), and Journeys needs flow tracing plus naming by the cartographer. Both are past hackathon scope, as SPEC already says.

let reduceCache: { events: readonly HarnessEvent[]; upTo: number; ui: UIState } | null = null;

function reduced(events: readonly HarnessEvent[], upTo: number): UIState {
  if (reduceCache && reduceCache.events === events && reduceCache.upTo === upTo) return reduceCache.ui;
  const ui = reduce(events, upTo);

export function deriveView(events: readonly HarnessEvent[], replay: number | null, turnSel: string | null): View {

  for (const [path, p] of Object.entries(ui.files)) {

    else if (p.kind === 'test') (testFiles[p.domain] ??= []).push(path);
    else if (p.kind === 'unassigned') unassigned.push(path);

  let confirmed = -1;

    const k = events[i]!.kind;
    if (k === 'turn_started') turnStarts.push(i);

import { cellKey, type DomainMap, type EdgeView, type ImportEdge, type TurnState, type UIState, type Violation } from '@harness/core/view';

export type Rect = { x: number; y: number; w: number; h: number };

export type GridLayout = {
  width: number;
  height: number;
  labelW: number;
  headerH: number;
  gapX: number;
  gapY: number;
  colW: number;
  rowH: number;
  cols: { id: string; name: string; purpose: string; x: number; index: number }[];
  rows: { id: string; name: string; y: number; index: number }[];
  cells: Record<string, Rect & { col: number; row: number }>;
  unassigned: Rect | null;
};

/** Fixed grid: a gutter on both sides of every column and row, so edges can route around cells. */
export function gridLayout(map: DomainMap, size: { w: number; h: number }, withUnassigned: boolean): GridLayout {
  const labelW = 64;
  const headerH = 46;
  const n = map.domains.length + (withUnassigned ? 1 : 0);
  const r = map.layers.length;
  const gapX = Math.max(28, Math.min(44, size.w * 0.032));
  const gapY = 26;
  const colW = Math.max(96, (size.w - labelW - gapX * (n + 1)) / n);
  const rowH = Math.max(72, Math.min(150, (size.h - headerH - gapY * (r + 1)) / r));
  const colX = (i: number) => labelW + gapX + i * (colW + gapX);
  const rowY = (j: number) => headerH + gapY + j * (rowH + gapY);
  const cols = map.domains.map((d, i) => ({ id: d.id, name: d.name, purpose: d.purpose, x: colX(i), index: i }));
  const rows = map.layers.map((l, j) => ({ id: l.id, name: l.name, y: rowY(j), index: j }));
  const cells: GridLayout['cells'] = {};
  map.domains.forEach((d, i) => {
    map.layers.forEach((l, j) => {
      if (l.id in d.cells) cells[cellKey({ domain: d.id, layer: l.id })] = { x: colX(i), y: rowY(j), w: colW, h: rowH, col: i, row: j };
    });
  });
  const unassigned = withUnassigned ? { x: colX(n - 1), y: rowY(0), w: colW, h: rowY(r - 1) + rowH - rowY(0) } : null;
  if (withUnassigned) cols.push({ id: '__unassigned', name: 'Unassigned', purpose: 'Files that match no cell in domains.yaml', x: colX(n - 1), index: n - 1 });
  return {
    width: labelW + gapX * (n + 1) + colW * n,
    height: headerH + gapY * (r + 1) + rowH * r,
    labelW, headerH, gapX, gapY, colW, rowH, cols, rows, cells, unassigned,
  };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- edges

export type EdgeSegment = {
  key: string; // stable React key
  edgeKey: string; // `${from}->${to}`
  pair: string; // `${srcCell}=>${dstCell}`
  from: string;
  to: string;
  src: string; // cellKey
  dst: string; // cellKey
  state: EdgeView['state'];
  violation: boolean;
  steps: number[];
  files: ImportEdge[];
};

/** Which cell a file sits in: its placement, else the cell a plan put it in. */
function cellForFile(s: UIState, turn: TurnState | null, file: string): string | null {
  const p = s.files[file];
  if (p?.kind === 'cell') return cellKey(p);
  const planned = turn && Object.values(turn.planned).find((c) => c.files.includes(file));
  return planned ? cellKey(planned.cell) : null;
}

function fallbackCell(map: DomainMap, domain: string): string | null {
  const d = map.domains.find((x) => x.id === domain);
  const layer = d && map.layers.find((l) => l.id in d.cells);
  return d && layer ? cellKey({ domain, layer: layer.id }) : null;
}

````text
# Harness: build spec

**Text in, architecture out.** Harness is a diagram-first shell around real Claude Code. You talk to the agent in a chat pane; a domain × layer map of the target repo shows, live, what each turn plans and does to the architecture; and the agent stops to ask you before it crosses a rule. Decisions you make become rules that later sessions are checked against.

The theme is giving people time back. Agents made writing code nearly free, but understanding and checking it did not get cheaper. Every feature below exists to cut reading, rework or re-explaining, and the time ledger counts those savings.

## 1. Repos

Two separate git repos, side by side:

```
workspace/
  harness/        this tool (npm workspaces monorepo)
  scout-agent/    the demo target, built separately from DEMO_REPO_SPEC.md
```

The target must be its own repo. The coding agent runs with its working directory there, the map is computed over it, and `domains.yaml` plus `decisions/` are committed into it. The tool's own code must never appear on the map.

```
harness/
  package.json              npm workspaces
  packages/core/            pure TypeScript, no I/O beyond fs reads; fully unit-tested
    src/schema.ts           zod schema for domains.yaml
    src/events.ts           event types and the reducer
    src/mapper.ts           path → cell, table → owner
    src/imports.ts          regex import parser + relative-path resolver
    src/writes.ts           db.insert / db.update scanner
    src/facts.ts            whole-repo scan: files, imports, writes, cross-domain edges
    src/rules.ts            the invariant checker (one function, three call sites)
    src/plan.ts             plan → ghost footprint
    src/ledger.ts           per-turn and session counters
    test/                   uses fixtures/scout-agent.domains.yaml
  apps/server/              Node + Hono + ws + @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk
    src/index.ts            HTTP + websocket; serves the shell in production
    src/bus.ts              append-only event log (.harness/events.jsonl in the target) + broadcast
    src/repo.ts             load, full scan, file watcher
    src/session.ts          the coding session (streaming input, modes, hooks, canUseTool)
    src/harness-tools.ts    in-process MCP server: submit_plan, cell_for, domain, who_writes, decisions_for
    src/turns.ts            turn lifecycle, git baselines, turn records
    src/decisions.ts        decisions/DR-n.md, invariant updates, Alike instructions
    src/cartographer.ts     one-shot map proposal
  apps/shell/               Vite + React + Zustand
  fixtures/scout-agent.domains.yaml
```

Run: `HARNESS_REPO=../scout-agent npm run dev` (server on 4310, shell on 5173).

## 2. Hard rules

1. **No model calls in the hot path.** Hooks, the mapper, the import parser and the rule checker are deterministic and fast. Model calls (the cartographer) never block the coding session.
2. **Every piece of UI state is a pure reduction of the event log.** Footprint, ghosts, ledger, summary, provenance and replay are all `reduce(events)`. Replay is "reduce up to index i".
3. **Harness writes to the target repo only in three places:** `domains.yaml`, `decisions/`, `.harness/` (gitignored). The coding session is the only thing that edits product code.
4. **Facts win on structure, the user wins on meaning, the agent wins only on stated intent**, and intent is always checked against facts.

## 3. The map (`domains.yaml`)

Schema: see `fixtures/scout-agent.domains.yaml`. Domains are columns, layers are rows (rows come from the file, not hard-coded). Each cell lists path globs and, for data cells, owned tables. `neutral` paths never create edges; `ignore` paths are skipped. Files that match no cell land in an **Unassigned** column.

**Tests** are assigned to a domain by its `tests` globs. A test file counts as part of that domain for the rule checker's import rules and the footprint and is listed in the inspector, but it is not drawn in a cell and draws no edges. Tests may write any table: seeding fixture rows is setup, not a product write, so `owns_writes` skips them.

**Edges are derived, never declared.** A cross-domain edge exists when a file in domain A imports a file in domain B. Flow down a column is implied and not drawn. The import parser handles `import … from '…'`, `import('…')` and `export … from '…'`. It resolves relative paths by trying the specifier as written, then `.ts`, `.tsx`, `/index.ts`, `/index.tsx`, and maps a `.js` specifier to `.ts`. It ignores bare package and `node:` imports (Scout has none that matter).

**Writes:** a regex scan for `db.insert(` and `db.update(` followed by a string literal in any quote style gives `{file, table}` pairs.

## 4. Invariants: one checker, three call sites

```ts
type Violation = { invariant: string; reason: string; file: string; detail: string; options: [string, string] };
function check(map: DomainMap, delta: FactDelta): Violation[];
```

`FactDelta` is a set of added imports and added writes, each with its source file. The three kinds:

| Kind | Fires when |
| --- | --- |
| `only_via` | a file outside `allowed_from` domains imports a `targets` path |
| `owns_writes` | a file outside the owner domain writes the table |
| `no_edge` | a file in `from` imports a file in `to` |

Exceptions (paths) suppress a violation. Each violation carries two options: **A** comply (for `only_via` on Scout: "route through `gateway.complete()`"), **B** add an exception for this path and record why.

The three call sites, all using the same function:

1. **Load:** full repo scan. On Scout, finds exactly one: DR-1 in `src/tools/news-summarize.ts`. It shows red on load.
2. **Plan:** run on the declared dependencies and files in `submit_plan`.
3. **Edit:** run in the `PreToolUse` hook on the imports and writes that the edit would add (diff the `new_string`/`content` against the current file).

## 5. Events

```ts
type HarnessEvent = {
  id: string; t: number;
  session: string;          // coding session id
  turn: string | null;
  kind:
    | 'repo_scanned' | 'map_proposed' | 'map_confirmed' | 'file_assigned'
    | 'violation_found'
    | 'turn_started' | 'looked' | 'cursor'
    | 'planned' | 'plan_violation' | 'fork_asked' | 'fork_answered' | 'plan_approved'
    | 'gate_blocked' | 'edited' | 'edge_added' | 'edge_removed'
    | 'test_result' | 'decision_recorded' | 'turn_ended';
  cell?: { domain: string; layer: string };
  path?: string;
  data?: Record<string, unknown>;   // e.g. { step: 2 }, { added: 18, removed: 2 }, { invariant: 'DR-1' }
};
```

The server appends every event to `.harness/events.jsonl` and broadcasts it over the websocket. The shell holds the array and derives everything from it.

## 6. The coding session

One long-lived streaming session:

```ts
query({
  prompt: chatMessages(),                     // AsyncIterable<SDKUserMessage> fed by the chat pane
  options: {
    cwd: REPO,
    permissionMode: 'plan',
    systemPrompt: { type: 'preset', preset: 'claude_code', append: brief() },
    mcpServers: { harness: harnessTools },    // createSdkMcpServer; user-scope MCP servers (Alike) still load
    allowedTools: ['mcp__harness__*', 'mcp__alike__record_decision', 'mcp__alike__resolve_work_item', 'mcp__alike__describe_entity_kind'],
    hooks: { PreToolUse: [...], PostToolUse: [...] },
    canUseTool,                                // intercepts ExitPlanMode for approval
  },
});
```

**`brief()`** contains: the map (domains, purposes, cell paths), every standing decision from `decisions/` (with the invariant it qualifies and the option it rejected), and these rules:

> Before editing anything, call `mcp__harness__submit_plan` with numbered steps. Each step lists the exact file paths it will create or modify and any new imports it adds (from path → to path). If the result contains violations, stop and ask the user to choose between the two options it gives, in one short message, then wait. Never work around a violation. After the user answers, resubmit the plan, then exit plan mode.

The brief does **not** list the seeded invariants (`source: cartographer`). They are enforced at plan and edit time instead. Stated up front, they would make the agent comply silently, so the user never sees the choice and nothing gets recorded. Once the user answers a fork, the resulting decision is in every later brief, and the next session follows it without asking. That contrast, asked once and then remembered, is the memory beat of the demo.

**Turn flow:**

1. User message → `turn_started` (record `git rev-parse HEAD` and a `git stash create` snapshot as the baseline).
2. Plan mode: Claude reads (`looked`, `cursor`), then calls `submit_plan`. The server maps paths to cells, builds ghost cells and ghost edges, and runs the checker → `planned` (+ `plan_violation`). The tool result returns the ghost summary and, if violated, the reason plus options A/B with an instruction to ask.
3. Claude asks → `fork_asked`. The user answers in chat → `fork_answered` → decision written (§8). Claude resubmits.
4. Claude calls `ExitPlanMode` → `canUseTool` holds it, the shell shows an **Approve plan** button (typing "approve" also works) → `plan_approved` → allow, then `session.setPermissionMode('acceptEdits')`.
5. Edits: hooks emit `cursor`, `gate_blocked`, `edited`, `edge_added` / `edge_removed`. Ghost cells fill as their files are edited; the step counter advances.
6. Result message → `turn_ended` with the plan-versus-built diff and git `--numstat` totals; write `.harness/turns/<id>.json`; `setPermissionMode('plan')` for the next turn.

**Hooks:**

| Hook | Matcher | Does | Blocking |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| PreToolUse | `Read\|Grep\|Glob` | `looked` + `cursor` for the file or search path | no (return `{ async: true }`) |
| PreToolUse | `Edit\|Write\|MultiEdit` | run the checker on the added imports/writes; on a hit return `permissionDecision: 'deny'` with the reason, options and "ask the user"; emit `gate_blocked` | yes, deterministic, < 20 ms |
| PostToolUse | `Edit\|Write\|MultiEdit` | `edited` (+/− lines), recompute that file's imports → edge events | no |
| PostToolUse | `Bash` | if the command ran `vitest`, parse results → `test_result` per test domain (stretch) | no |

**File watcher** (chokidar on the target, minus `ignore`): any write not already reported by a hook becomes an `edited` event marked `unattributed`. Hooks give attribution and gating; the watcher guarantees completeness, since shell commands can write files without passing through the edit hooks.

**Harness MCP tools** (all read-only except `submit_plan`, which only records intent): `submit_plan(steps[{ n, text, files[], imports[{ from, to }] }])`, `cell_for(path)`, `domain(id)`, `who_writes(table)`, `decisions_for(paths[])`.

## 7. Plan versus built

- **Ghosts:** planned cells are drawn dashed with their step numbers; planned edges are dashed; a ghost that violates an invariant is red.
- **Fill-in:** a ghost cell turns solid when a file mapped to it is edited.
- **End-of-turn diff:** planned and done is solid; planned and not done stays a ghost; **done but not planned is amber**, which is how the map shows the agent straying from its own plan.
- **New versus existing violations:** a violation found on load is drawn red, with a badge on its cell counting the files involved. A violation raised by this turn's plan or edits must look different from the map before the turn, even when it repeats an existing one (on Scout, the 10-K plan copies `news-summarize.ts` into the same red cell and toward the same provider). Its ghost edge gets its own lane, offset from any solid edge between the same cells, and the cell gets a separate **new** badge naming the file.

## 8. Design memory

When a fork is answered:

1. Write `decisions/DR-<n>.md` with front matter `{ id, title, outcome, status: made, type: standing, invariant, anchors: { paths }, rejected: "<option B text>" }` and a short rationale body.
2. Update `domains.yaml`: link the decision to the invariant (option A), or add the path to the invariant's `exceptions` with the DR id (option B). Commit both files and only those (`git commit -- domains.yaml decisions/DR-<n>.md`), so the coding session's uncommitted edits stay out of the commit.
3. Tell Claude, in the next tool result, to record it in Alike with `mcp__alike__record_decision`, giving it the exact arguments: `title`, `outcome`, `rationale` (including the rejected option), `decision_type: standing`, `status: made`, and one path anchor per governed file, `{ kind: path, label: governs, path, repository: owner/name }` (field names checked with `describe_entity_kind`, see VERIFY.md). Emit `decision_recorded` when the call succeeds.

Memory is then used three ways:

- **Provenance:** clicking an edge or cell shows the decisions and turns behind it ("added in turn 3, DR-4").
- **Session brief:** every standing decision goes into `brief()` for every new session (§6).
- **Rejected options stay rejected:** when a plan or edit hits an invariant that has a linked decision, the violation reason says "You decided this in DR-4: <title>," and the ledger counts it as a rejected option blocked.

## 9. Time ledger and turn summary

Counts only; minutes appear only in the pitch, taken from the baseline run (§12).

| Counter | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Lines changed | git `--numstat` added + removed, turn baseline → turn end |
| Cells to review | cells with a finding of severity 1–3 below |
| Forks caught before code | `plan_violation` events resolved before any `edited` event in the turn |
| Rejected options blocked | violations that cited an existing decision |

Severity for the turn summary, loudest first: **1** invariant hit (red) · **2** new cross-domain edge or new external (amber, one glance) · **3** unplanned edit (amber) · **4** everything else in the plan (quiet).

## 10. Load and the cartographer

1. `repo_scanned`: full fact scan (§3).
2. If `domains.yaml` is missing, run the **cartographer**: a separate one-shot `query()` with read-only tools, a smaller model, and `outputFormat` set to the `domains.yaml` JSON schema. Input: the file tree, the import edges and the table writes. Ask it for 5–9 domains in product language, layers suited to the repo, and invariants it can infer from the facts (sole importers of a vendor, sole writers of a table, absent edges). → `map_proposed`.
3. The shell plays the map assembling (`file_assigned` events, staggered about 15 ms apart) and shows the proposal; the user clicks **Confirm** → `map_confirmed`, file written. If the proposal is off, load `fixtures/scout-agent.domains.yaml` instead.
