````text
## 11. The shell

- **Layout:** chat pane on the left (380 px); the grid fills the rest; the turn summary and replay scrubber sit under the grid; the ledger sits top right. The mockups are in Figma, "v2 · Domain grid" page.
- **Cell states:** looked = dashed indigo outline · edited = indigo fill · unplanned = amber · invariant hit = red · ghost = dashed outline at 50% opacity with step badges.
- **Agent cursor:** a small avatar pinned to the current cell, labeled "Claude · reading `retrieve.ts`", easing between cells in 250 ms.
- **Edges:** SVG overlay routed through the gaps between cells; new edges draw in with a stroke-dashoffset animation.
- **Diff counts:** a +/− badge on each edited cell, ticking up.
- **Inspector:** click a cell or edge to see its paths, tables, invariants and provenance.
- **Replay:** a scrubber over the event index; dragging re-reduces the log.
- **Motion rule:** animate only state changes; nothing loops.

Copy `scout-agent` at the demo commit. In plain Claude Code, run "Add a tool that summarizes a prospect's latest 10-K." Time it, then run `npm run proof`. If the new tool leaks personal data, time a follow-up turn that finds and fixes it. Those minutes are the "without" numbers the pitch converts the ledger into. const REGEX_PRECEDERS = new Set('(,=:[!&|?{};+-*%<>~^'.split(''));
````
```text
const REGEX_KEYWORDS = /(?:^|[^\w$])(?:return|typeof|case|do|else|in|of|void|yield|await|delete|throw|new)$/;

/**
 * Replace `//` and `/* *\/` comments with spaces (newlines kept), leaving strings,
 * template literals and regex literals intact, so offsets and line numbers still match.
 */
export function stripComments(src: string): string {
  const n = src.length;
  let out = '';
  let i = 0;

  const copyQuoted = (quote: string) => {
    out += src[i++];
    while (i < n && src[i] !== quote && src[i] !== '\n') {
      if (src[i] === '\\') out += src[i++];
      if (i < n) out += src[i++];
    }
    if (i < n && src[i] === quote) out += src[i++];
  };

  const copyRegex = () => {
    let inClass = false;
    out += src[i++];
    while (i < n && src[i] !== '\n') {
      const c = src[i]!;
      if (c === '\\') {
        out += src.slice(i, i + 2);
        i += 2;
        continue;
      }
      out += c;
      i++;
      if (c === '[') inClass = true;
      else if (c === ']') inClass = false;
      else if (c === '/' && !inClass) break;
    }
  };

  const copyTemplate = () => {
    out += src[i++];
    while (i < n && src[i] !== '`') {
      if (src[i] === '\\') {
        out += src.slice(i, i + 2);
        i += 2;
      } else if (src[i] === '$' && src[i + 1] === '{') {
        out += '${';
        i += 2;
        code(true);
      } else out += src[i++];
    }
    if (i < n) out += src[i++];
  };

  // Scan code; when `inTemplate`, stop after the `}` that closes the `${`.
  function code(inTemplate: boolean) {
    let depth = 0;
    while (i < n) {
      const c = src[i]!;
      const next = src[i + 1];
      if (c === '/' && next === '/') {
        while (i < n && src[i] !== '\n') {
          out += ' ';
          i++;
        }
      } else if (c === '/' && next === '*') {
        const end = src.indexOf('*/', i + 2);
        const stop = end === -1 ? n : end + 2;
        out += src.slice(i, stop).replace(/[^\n]/g, ' ');
        i = stop;
      } else if (c === '"' || c === "'") copyQuoted(c);
      else if (c === '`') copyTemplate();
      else if (c === '/') {
        const before = out.trimEnd();
        const prev = before[before.length - 1];
        if (prev === undefined || REGEX_PRECEDERS.has(prev) || REGEX_KEYWORDS.test(before)) copyRegex();
        else out += src[i++];
      } else {
        if (c === '{') depth++;
        else if (c === '}') {
          if (inTemplate && depth === 0) {
            out += src[i++];
            return;
          }
          depth--;
        }
        out += src[i++];
      }
    }
  }

  code(false);
  return out;
}

const STATIC_FROM = /(?<![\w$.])(?:import|export)\s+(?:type\s+)?[\w$\s{},*]*?\bfrom\s*(['"])([^'"\n]+)\1/g;
const SIDE_EFFECT = /(?<![\w$.])import\s*(['"])([^'"\n]+)\1/g;
const DYNAMIC = /(?<![\w$.])import\s*\(\s*(['"`])([^'"`$\n]+)\1\s*\)/g;

/** Module specifiers imported or re-exported by `source`, in source order. Comments are ignored. */
export function parseImports(source: string): string[] {
  const code = stripComments(source);
  const found: { at: number; spec: string }[] = [];
  for (const re of [STATIC_FROM, SIDE_EFFECT, DYNAMIC]) {
    for (const m of code.matchAll(re)) found.push({ at: m.index, spec: m[2]! });
  }
  return found.sort((a, b) => a.at - b.at).map((f) => f.spec);
}

/** Normalize a repo-relative path: POSIX separators, no `./`, `.`/`..` resolved. Null if it escapes the root. */
export function normalizePath(path: string): string | null {
  const parts: string[] = [];
  for (const seg of path.replace(/\\/g, '/').split('/')) {
    if (seg === '' || seg === '.') continue;
    if (seg === '..') {
      if (parts.length === 0) return null;
      parts.pop();
    } else parts.push(seg);
  }
  return parts.join('/');
}

/** Directory part of a repo-relative path ('' for root files). */
export function dirname(path: string): string {
  const i = path.lastIndexOf('/');
  return i === -1 ? '' : path.slice(0, i);
}

const EXT_SWAPS: Record<string, string[]> = { '.js': ['.ts', '.tsx'], '.jsx': ['.tsx'], '.mjs': ['.mts'] };

/** First existing file for a repo path written the way an import would be: as is, swapped JS extension, `.ts`, `.tsx`, `/index.ts`, `/index.tsx`. */
export function resolvePath(path: string, exists: (path: string) => boolean): string | null {
  const base = normalizePath(path);
  if (!base) return null;
  const candidates = [base];
  const ext = base.match(/\.(?:js|jsx|mjs)$/)?.[0];
  if (ext) for (const swap of EXT_SWAPS[ext]!) candidates.push(base.slice(0, -ext.length) + swap);
  candidates.push(`${base}.ts`, `${base}.tsx`, `${base}/index.ts`, `${base}/index.tsx`);
  return candidates.find((c) => exists(c)) ?? null;
}

/** Resolve a relative specifier imported by `fromFile` to an existing repo file. Bare and `node:` specifiers give null. */
export function resolveImport(fromFile: string, specifier: string, exists: (path: string) => boolean): string | null {
  if (!isRelative(specifier)) return null;
  const dir = dirname(normalizePath(fromFile) ?? '');
  return resolvePath(dir ? `${dir}/${specifier}` : specifier, exists);
}

export function isRelative(specifier: string): boolean {
  return specifier === '.' || specifier === '..' || specifier.startsWith('./') || specifier.startsWith('../');
}
import * as fs from 'node:fs';
import { normalizePath, parseImports, resolveImport } from './imports';
import { createMapper, type Mapper } from './mapper';
import type { DomainMap } from './schema';
import { scanWrites } from './writes';

/** File → file import. */
export type ImportEdge = { from: string; to: string };
export type WriteFact = { file: string; table: string };
/** Cross-domain dependency (domain ids) with the file imports behind it. */
export type DomainEdge = { from: string; to: string; files: ImportEdge[] };
export type Facts = { files: string[]; imports: ImportEdge[]; writes: WriteFact[] };
export type FactDelta = { imports: ImportEdge[]; writes: WriteFact[] };

export type Exists = (path: string) => boolean;

export const CODE_EXTENSIONS = ['.ts', '.tsx', '.js', '.jsx', '.mjs', '.cjs', '.mts'];

export function isCodeFile(path: string): boolean {
  return CODE_EXTENSIONS.some((ext) => path.endsWith(ext));
}

/** File-existence check against a repo root, cached. Call `clear()` after files are created or deleted. */
export function fileExistsIn(root: string): Exists & { clear(): void } {
  const cache = new Map<string, boolean>();
  const exists = (path: string) => {
    let hit = cache.get(path);
    if (hit === undefined) {
      try {
        hit = fs.statSync(`${root}/${path}`).isFile();
      } catch {
        hit = false;
      }
      cache.set(path, hit);
    }
    return hit;
  };
  return Object.assign(exists, { clear: () => cache.clear() });
}

/** `exists`, plus `paths` that will exist (e.g. files a plan creates). */
export function withExtra(exists: Exists, paths: readonly string[]): Exists {
  const extra = new Set(paths.map((p) => normalizePath(p) ?? p));
  return (path) => extra.has(path) || exists(path);
}

/** Full fact scan of a repo: every non-ignored file, plus resolved imports and table writes of code files. */
export function scanRepo(root: string, map: DomainMap): Facts {
  const mapper = createMapper(map);
  const files: string[] = [];
  const walk = (dir: string) => {
    for (const entry of fs.readdirSync(dir ? `${root}/${dir}` : root, { withFileTypes: true })) {
      if (entry.name === 'node_modules' || entry.name === '.git') continue;
      const path = dir ? `${dir}/${entry.name}` : entry.name;
      if (mapper.isIgnored(path)) continue;
      if (entry.isDirectory()) walk(path);
      else if (entry.isFile()) files.push(path);
    }
  };
  walk('');
  files.sort();

  const known = new Set(files);
  const onDisk = fileExistsIn(root);
  const exists: Exists = (p) => known.has(p) || onDisk(p);
  const imports: ImportEdge[] = [];
  const writes: WriteFact[] = [];
  for (const file of files) {
    if (!isCodeFile(file)) continue;
    const delta = factsForSource(file, fs.readFileSync(`${root}/${file}`, 'utf8'), exists);
    imports.push(...delta.imports);
    writes.push(...delta.writes);
  }
  return { files, imports, writes };
}

function counts(path: string, source: string, exists: Exists) {
  const imports = new Map<string, number>();
  for (const spec of parseImports(source)) {
    const to = resolveImport(path, spec, exists);
    if (to) imports.set(to, (imports.get(to) ?? 0) + 1);
  }
  const writes = new Map<string, number>();
  for (const table of scanWrites(source)) writes.set(table, (writes.get(table) ?? 0) + 1);
  return { imports, writes };
}

/** One file's resolved imports and table writes (each target/table once). */
export function factsForSource(path: string, source: string, exists: Exists): FactDelta {
  return deltaForEdit(path, null, source, exists);
}

/** Imports and writes that `newSource` adds over `oldSource` (multiset difference by target/table). */
export function deltaForEdit(path: string, oldSource: string | null, newSource: string, exists: Exists): FactDelta {
  const file = normalizePath(path) ?? path;
  const before = oldSource === null ? null : counts(file, oldSource, exists);
  const after = counts(file, newSource, exists);
  const added = (key: string, n: number, old: Map<string, number> | undefined) => n > (old?.get(key) ?? 0);
  return {
    imports: [...after.imports].filter(([to, n]) => added(to, n, before?.imports)).map(([to]) => ({ from: file, to })),
    writes: [...after.writes].filter(([t, n]) => added(t, n, before?.writes)).map(([table]) => ({ file, table })),
  };
}

/** Apply a Claude Code `Edit` to file text. Throws if `oldString` is not found. */
export function applyEdit(current: string, oldString: string, newString: string, replaceAll = false): string {
  if (!current.includes(oldString)) throw new Error('old_string not found in file');
  return replaceAll ? current.split(oldString).join(newString) : current.replace(oldString, () => newString);
}

/** Cross-domain edges between cell files. Neutral, ignored, unassigned and test files, and same-domain imports, draw none. */
export function domainEdges(facts: Facts | FactDelta, mapper: Mapper): DomainEdge[] {
  const edges = new Map<string, DomainEdge>();
  for (const imp of facts.imports) {
    const a = mapper.place(imp.from);
    const b = mapper.place(imp.to);
    if (a.kind !== 'cell' || b.kind !== 'cell' || a.domain === b.domain) continue;
    const key = `${a.domain}\u0000${b.domain}`;
    let edge = edges.get(key);
    if (!edge) edges.set(key, (edge = { from: a.domain, to: b.domain, files: [] }));
    edge.files.push(imp);
  }
  return [...edges.values()].sort((x, y) => x.from.localeCompare(y.from) || x.to.localeCompare(y.to));
}
import picomatch from 'picomatch';
import type { DomainMap } from './schema';

export type Placement =
  | { kind: 'cell'; domain: string; layer: string }
  | { kind: 'test'; domain: string }
  | { kind: 'neutral' }
  | { kind: 'ignored' }
  | { kind: 'unassigned' };

export type Mapper = ReturnType<typeof createMapper>;

const globCache = new Map<string, (path: string) => boolean>();

/** Compiled, cached picomatch matcher for a single glob (exact paths match themselves). */
export function globMatcher(glob: string): (path: string) => boolean {
  let m = globCache.get(glob);
  if (!m) {
    m = picomatch(glob, { dot: true });
    globCache.set(glob, m);
  }
  return m;
}

/** True if `path` matches any of `globs`. */
export function matchesAny(globs: readonly string[] | undefined, path: string): boolean {
  return !!globs && globs.some((g) => globMatcher(g)(path));
}

/** Path → placement on the domain × layer grid, and table → owning cell. */
export function createMapper(map: DomainMap) {
  const ignore = map.ignore ?? [];
  const neutral = map.neutral ?? [];
  const layerOrder = map.layers.map((l) => l.id);
  const tests = map.domains.map((d) => ({ domain: d.id, globs: d.tests ?? [] }));
  const cells = map.domains.flatMap((d) =>
    layerOrder.flatMap((layer) => {
      const cell = d.cells[layer];
      return cell ? [{ domain: d.id, layer, globs: cell.paths ?? [], tables: cell.tables ?? [] }] : [];
    }),
  );
  const cache = new Map<string, Placement>();

  function place(path: string): Placement {
    let p = cache.get(path);
    if (p) return p;
    if (matchesAny(ignore, path)) p = { kind: 'ignored' };
    else if (matchesAny(neutral, path)) p = { kind: 'neutral' };
    else {
      const t = tests.find((t) => matchesAny(t.globs, path));
      const c = t ? undefined : cells.find((c) => matchesAny(c.globs, path));
      p = t
        ? { kind: 'test', domain: t.domain }
        : c
          ? { kind: 'cell', domain: c.domain, layer: c.layer }
          : { kind: 'unassigned' };
    }
    cache.set(path, p);
    return p;
  }

  return {
    place,
    /** Domain of a cell or test file; null for neutral, ignored and unassigned files. */
    domainOf(path: string): string | null {
      const p = place(path);
      return p.kind === 'cell' || p.kind === 'test' ? p.domain : null;
    },
    /** The cell that lists `table`, if any. */
    ownerOf(table: string): { domain: string; layer: string } | null {
      const c = cells.find((c) => c.tables.includes(table));
      return c ? { domain: c.domain, layer: c.layer } : null;
    },
    isIgnored: (path: string) => place(path).kind === 'ignored',
    isNeutral: (path: string) => place(path).kind === 'neutral',
  };
}

import { createMapper, matchesAny, type Mapper } from './mapper';
import type { DomainMap, Invariant } from './schema';

export type Violation = {

  file: string;
  /** Short fact, e.g. `src/a.ts → vendor/b/index.ts` or `src/a.ts writes "runs"`. */

/**

export function check(map: DomainMap, delta: FactDelta, mapper: Mapper = createMapper(map)): Violation[] {
  const domainName = (id: string) => map.domains.find((d) => d.id === id)?.name ?? id;
  const found = new Map<string, Violation>();

  const add = (inv: Invariant, file: string, target: string, fact: string, detail: string, optionA: string) => {
    if (inv.exceptions.some((e) => matchesAny([e.path], file))) return;
    const decision = inv.decisions?.at(-1);
    const v: Violation = {
      invariant: inv.id,
      kind: inv.kind,
      reason: `${decision ? `You decided this in ${decision}. ` : ''}${file} ${fact}, but ${inv.id}: ${inv.rule}.`,
      file,
      detail,
      options: [optionA, `Add an exception for ${file} and record why`],

      for (const w of delta.writes) {

        if (!owner || mapper.isIgnored(w.file) || mapper.place(w.file).kind === 'test' || mapper.domainOf(w.file) === owner) continue;
        add(inv, w.file, w.table, `writes "${w.table}"`, `${w.file} writes "${w.table}"`,

      }

    for (const imp of delta.imports) {
      const p = mapper.place(imp.from);
```

```text
import { existsSync, readFileSync, realpathSync } from 'node:fs';
import { join, relative, isAbsolute } from 'node:path';
import { watch, type FSWatcher } from 'chokidar';
import { diffLines } from 'diff';
import {
  parseDomainMap, createMapper, scanRepo, factsForSource, domainEdges, check, fileExistsIn,
  type DomainMap, type Facts, type ImportEdge, type Violation, type Placement,
} from '@harness/core';
import type { Bus } from './bus';

const CODE = /\.(ts|tsx|js|jsx|mjs|cjs|mts)$/;

export class Repo {
  readonly root: string;
  map!: DomainMap;
  mapText = '';
  mapper!: ReturnType<typeof createMapper>;
  facts: Facts = { files: [], imports: [], writes: [] };
  violations: Violation[] = [];
  private contents = new Map<string, string>();
  private pending = new Map<string, NodeJS.Timeout>(); // paths a hook is editing; the watcher leaves them alone
  private watcher: FSWatcher | null = null;
  exists: ReturnType<typeof fileExistsIn>;

  constructor(root: string, private bus: Bus) {
    this.root = realpathSync(root);
    this.exists = fileExistsIn(this.root);
  }

  get mapPath() { return join(this.root, 'domains.yaml'); }
  hasMap() { return existsSync(this.mapPath); }

  /** Load (or reload) domains.yaml text. */
  setMap(text: string) {
    this.mapText = text;
    this.map = parseDomainMap(text);
    this.mapper = createMapper(this.map);
  }

  loadMapFile() { this.setMap(readFileSync(this.mapPath, 'utf8')); }

  /** Repo-relative POSIX path for an absolute path from a hook, or null if it is outside the repo. */
  rel(p: string): string | null {
    let abs = isAbsolute(p) ? p : join(this.root, p);
    try { abs = realpathSync(abs); } catch {
      // New file: resolve the parent instead.
      const i = abs.lastIndexOf('/');
      try { abs = join(realpathSync(abs.slice(0, i)), abs.slice(i + 1)); } catch { /* keep as is */ }
    }
    const r = relative(this.root, abs);
    if (!r || r.startsWith('..') || isAbsolute(r)) return null;
    return r.split('\\').join('/');
  }

  place(path: string): Placement { return this.mapper.place(path); }

  cellOf(path: string) {
    const p = this.place(path);
    return p.kind === 'cell' ? { domain: p.domain, layer: p.layer } : null;
  }

  /** Placement for a directory (Grep/Glob path): the single cell all known files under it share, if any. */
  cellForDir(dir: string) {
    const prefix = dir.replace(/\/$/, '') + '/';
    let found: { domain: string; layer: string } | null = null;
    for (const f of this.facts.files) {
      if (!f.startsWith(prefix)) continue;
      const c = this.cellOf(f);
      if (!c) continue;
      if (found && (found.domain !== c.domain || found.layer !== c.layer)) return null;
      found = c;
    }
    return found;
  }

  /** Every non-ignored file under the current map. */
  listFiles() { return scanRepo(this.root, this.map).files; }

  /** Full fact scan → `repo_scanned` + `violation_found`. */
  scan() {
    this.facts = scanRepo(this.root, this.map);
    this.contents.clear();
    for (const f of this.facts.files) {
      if (CODE.test(f)) this.contents.set(f, readFileSync(join(this.root, f), 'utf8'));
    }
    this.bus.emit('repo_scanned', {
      files: this.facts.files.map((path) => ({ path, placement: this.place(path) })),
      imports: this.facts.imports,
      writes: this.facts.writes,
      edges: domainEdges(this.facts, this.mapper),
    }, { turn: null });
    this.recheck();
  }

  /** Re-run the checker over the whole repo (load call site) and publish the current set. */
  recheck() {
    this.violations = check(this.map, this.facts, this.mapper);
    this.bus.emit('violation_found', { violations: this.violations }, { turn: null });
  }

  current(path: string): string | null {
    if (this.contents.has(path)) return this.contents.get(path)!;
    const abs = join(this.root, path);
    return existsSync(abs) ? readFileSync(abs, 'utf8') : null;
  }

  markPending(path: string) {
    clearTimeout(this.pending.get(path));
    this.pending.set(path, setTimeout(() => this.pending.delete(path), 10_000));
  }

  /**
   * A file changed on disk: emit `edited` (+/− lines) and edge events from its import diff, and update facts.
   * Called by the PostToolUse hook (attributed) and the watcher (unattributed). No-op if the content is unchanged.
   */
  fileChanged(path: string, attr: { tool?: string; unattributed?: boolean }) {
    if (this.mapper.isIgnored(path)) return;
    const abs = join(this.root, path);
    const deleted = !existsSync(abs);
    const next = deleted ? '' : readFileSync(abs, 'utf8');
    const prev = this.contents.get(path);
    const known = this.facts.files.includes(path);
    if (prev === next && known) return;
    if (!attr.unattributed) { clearTimeout(this.pending.get(path)); this.pending.delete(path); }

    let added = 0, removed = 0;
    for (const part of diffLines(prev ?? '', next)) {
      if (part.added) added += part.count ?? 0;
      else if (part.removed) removed += part.count ?? 0;
    }
    const created = !known && !deleted;
    if (created) {
      this.facts.files.push(path);
      this.bus.emit('file_assigned', { placement: this.place(path) }, { path });
    }
    if (deleted) this.facts.files = this.facts.files.filter((f) => f !== path);
    if (created || deleted) this.exists.clear();

    // Import and write facts for this one file.
    const before = this.facts.imports.filter((i) => i.from === path);
    const after = CODE.test(path) && !deleted ? factsForSource(path, next, this.exists) : { imports: [], writes: [] };
    this.facts.imports = [...this.facts.imports.filter((i) => i.from !== path), ...after.imports];
    this.facts.writes = [...this.facts.writes.filter((w) => w.file !== path), ...after.writes];
    if (deleted) this.contents.delete(path); else if (CODE.test(path)) this.contents.set(path, next);

    this.bus.emit('edited', { added, removed, created, ...(attr.unattributed ? { unattributed: true } : {}), ...(attr.tool ? { tool: attr.tool } : {}) }, { path, cell: this.cellOf(path) });

    const key = (i: ImportEdge) => `${i.from}→${i.to}`;
    const beforeKeys = new Set(before.map(key));
    const afterKeys = new Set(after.imports.map(key));
    const gained = after.imports.filter((i) => !beforeKeys.has(key(i)));
    const lost = before.filter((i) => !afterKeys.has(key(i)));
    for (const de of domainEdges({ imports: gained, writes: [] }, this.mapper)) {
      for (const edge of de.files) this.bus.emit('edge_added', { edge, from: de.from, to: de.to }, { path });
    }
    for (const de of domainEdges({ imports: lost, writes: [] }, this.mapper)) {
      for (const edge of de.files) this.bus.emit('edge_removed', { edge, from: de.from, to: de.to }, { path });
    }
  }

  /** Completeness: any write that no hook reported (e.g. from Bash) becomes an unattributed `edited` event. */
  startWatcher() {
    const ignored = (p: string) => {
      const r = relative(this.root, p);
      if (!r || r.startsWith('..')) return false;
      return /(^|\/)(node_modules|\.git|\.harness)(\/|$)/.test(r) || this.mapper.isIgnored(r.split('\\').join('/'));
    };
    this.watcher = watch(this.root, { ignored, ignoreInitial: true, awaitWriteFinish: { stabilityThreshold: 120, pollInterval: 40 } });
    const handle = (abs: string) => {
      const r = this.rel(abs);
      if (!r || this.pending.has(r) || r === 'domains.yaml') return;
      this.fileChanged(r, { unattributed: true });
    };
    this.watcher.on('add', handle).on('change', handle).on('unlink', handle);
  }

  async close() { await this.watcher?.close(); }
}
import { writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { join } from 'node:path';
import { randomUUID } from 'node:crypto';
import {
  query, type Query, type SDKUserMessage, type HookCallback, type PreToolUseHookInput, type PostToolUseHookInput,
  type CanUseTool, type PermissionResult, type McpServerConfig,
} from '@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk';
import { applyEdit, deltaForEdit, check, withExtra, type PlanStep, type Violation, type EventData } from '@harness/core';
import { harnessTools, violationText, ASK_RULE } from './harness-tools';
import { listDecisions, parseOption, recordFork } from './decisions';
import { baseline, numstat, type Baseline } from './git';
import type { Repo } from './repo';
import type { Bus } from './bus';

const PLAN_RULES = [
  'Explore read-only, briefly. Then, before editing anything, call mcp__harness__submit_plan with numbered steps.',
  'Each step lists the exact repo-relative file paths it will create or modify, and every new import it adds as { from: path, to: path }.',
  'If the result contains violations: ' + ASK_RULE,
  'After the user answers, resubmit the plan with mcp__harness__submit_plan, then call ExitPlanMode.',
  'If there are no violations, call ExitPlanMode with a short plan.',
].join('\n');

/** Push-based prompt stream fed by the chat pane. */
class Inbox implements AsyncIterable<SDKUserMessage> {
  private queue: SDKUserMessage[] = [];
  private wake: (() => void) | null = null;
  push(text: string) {
    this.queue.push({ type: 'user', message: { role: 'user', content: text }, parent_tool_use_id: null });
    this.wake?.();
  }
  async *[Symbol.asyncIterator]() {
    while (true) {
      while (this.queue.length) yield this.queue.shift()!;
      await new Promise<void>((r) => (this.wake = r));
      this.wake = null;
    }
  }
}

type Turn = {
  id: string;
  prompt: string;
  base: Baseline;
  planned: boolean;
  steps: PlanStep[];
  planViolations: Violation[]; // from the latest submit_plan
  gateBlocks: Violation[]; // since the last answer
  forkOpen: Violation[] | null; // asked, awaiting the user's A/B
  lastText: string;
};

/** If a shell command writes a file inside the repo, a short description of how; otherwise null. */
export function bashWriteTarget(cmd: string, rel: (p: string) => string | null): string | null {
  const inRepo = (p: string) => !!p && !p.startsWith('/dev/') && rel(p.replace(/^['"]|['"]$/g, '')) !== null;
  // Redirects to a file: `> f`, `>> f`, `cat <<EOF > f` (not 2>&1, >&2, >/dev/null).
  for (const m of cmd.matchAll(/(?:^|[^0-9&>])>>?\s*([^\s;&|<>()]+)/g)) if (!m[1]!.startsWith('&') && inRepo(m[1]!)) return `redirect to ${m[1]}`;
  for (const m of cmd.matchAll(/\btee\s+(?:-a\s+)?([^\s;&|<>()]+)/g)) if (inRepo(m[1]!)) return `tee ${m[1]}`;
  if (/\b(sed|perl)\s+(-[a-zA-Z]*\s+)*-[a-zA-Z]*i/.test(cmd)) return 'in-place edit';
  if (/\b(python3?|node|ruby|perl|deno|bun)\b[\s\S]*(open\([^)]*['"][wa]\+?['"]|write_text|writeFileSync|appendFileSync|\.write\(|fs\.write)/.test(cmd)) return 'script that writes files';
  return null;
}

export type Ephemeral = (msg: { type: 'delta'; text: string } | { type: 'busy'; busy: boolean }) => void;

export class Session {
  private inbox = new Inbox();
  private q: Query | null = null;
  private turn: Turn | null = null;
  private approval: { resolve: (r: PermissionResult) => void; input: Record<string, unknown> } | null = null;
  private notes: string[] = [];
  busy = false;

  constructor(private repo: Repo, private bus: Bus, private ephemeral: Ephemeral) {}

  brief(): string {
    const m = this.repo.map;
    const domains = m.domains.map((d) => {
      const cells = Object.entries(d.cells).map(([layer, c]) => `    ${layer}: ${[...(c.paths ?? []), ...(c.tables ?? []).map((t) => `table ${t}`)].join(', ')}`);
      return `- ${d.name} (${d.id}): ${d.purpose}\n${cells.join('\n')}`;
    });
    const decisions = listDecisions(this.repo.root).map((d) =>
      `- ${d.id}: ${d.title}\n  Outcome: ${d.outcome}\n  Rejected: ${d.rejected}\n  ${d.rationale.replace(/\n+/g, '\n  ')}`);
    // Seeded invariants are deliberately not listed (SPEC §6): they are enforced at plan and edit time.
    return [
      '# Harness',
      'You are working inside Harness, which shows the user a live domain × layer map of this repo and checks every plan and edit against its architecture rules.',
      '',
      '## Map (domains.yaml)',
      `Layers: ${m.layers.map((l) => l.id).join(', ')}`,
      ...domains,
      '',
      '## Standing decisions the user has made',
      decisions.length ? decisions.join('\n') : '(none yet)',
      '',
      '## Rules',
      PLAN_RULES,
      'Change files only with the Edit and Write tools, never through Bash (no heredocs, `sed -i` or scripts that write files): Harness checks each Edit/Write against the rules.',
      'If an edit is denied with options A and B: ' + ASK_RULE,
    ].join('\n');
  }

  start() {
    const alike: Record<string, McpServerConfig> = process.env.HARNESS_ALIKE === '0' ? {} : { alike: { type: 'http', url: 'https://alike.network/api-general/mcp' } };
    this.q = query({
      prompt: this.inbox,
      options: {
        cwd: this.repo.root,
        permissionMode: 'plan',
        planModeInstructions: PLAN_RULES,
        // User settings carry Alike's own hooks (network calls); keep the hot path deterministic. See VERIFY.md.
        settingSources: ['project', 'local'],
        strictMcpConfig: true,
        systemPrompt: { type: 'preset', preset: 'claude_code', append: this.brief() },
        mcpServers: {
          harness: harnessTools(this.repo, this.bus, {
            onPlan: (steps, violations) => this.onPlan(steps, violations),
            takeNotes: () => this.notes.splice(0),
          }),
          ...alike,
        },
        // No allowedTools: canUseTool approves everything except ExitPlanMode, which waits for the user.
        disallowedTools: ['AskUserQuestion'],
        includePartialMessages: true,
        hooks: {
          PreToolUse: [
            { matcher: 'Read|Grep|Glob', hooks: [this.observeRead] },
            { matcher: 'Bash', hooks: [this.observeBash, this.gateBash] },
            { matcher: 'Edit|Write', hooks: [this.gate] },
          ],
          PostToolUse: [
            { matcher: 'Edit|Write', hooks: [this.afterEdit] },
            { matcher: 'mcp__alike__record_decision', hooks: [this.afterAlike] },
          ],
        },
        canUseTool: this.canUseTool,
        stderr: (d) => { if (process.env.HARNESS_DEBUG) process.stderr.write(d); },
      },
    });
    void this.loop();
  }

  private async loop() {
    try {
      for await (const m of this.q!) {
        if (m.type === 'stream_event') {
          const ev = m.event as { type: string; delta?: { type: string; text?: string } };
          if (ev.type === 'content_block_delta' && ev.delta?.type === 'text_delta' && ev.delta.text) this.ephemeral({ type: 'delta', text: ev.delta.text });
        } else if (m.type === 'assistant' && !m.parent_tool_use_id) {
          const t = m.message.content.filter((b) => b.type === 'text').map((b) => (b as { text: string }).text).join('\n').trim();
          if (t) {
            this.bus.emit('chat', { role: 'assistant', text: t });
            if (this.turn) this.turn.lastText = t;
          }
        } else if (m.type === 'result') {
          this.onResult(m.subtype);
        }
      }
    } catch (e) {
      this.bus.emit('error', { message: `Session ended: ${(e as Error).message}` });
    }
  }

  // ---------------------------------------------------------------- chat input

  userMessage(text: string) {
    const t = text.trim();
    if (!t) return;
    if (this.approval) {
      this.bus.emit('chat', { role: 'user', text: t });
      if (/^(approve|approved|lgtm|yes|ok|go|ship it)\b/i.test(t)) this.approve();
      else this.rejectPlan(t);
      return;
    }
    if (this.turn?.forkOpen) {
      const violations = this.turn.forkOpen;
      const option = parseOption(t);
      this.bus.emit('chat', { role: 'user', text: t });
      this.bus.emit('fork_answered', { option, text: t, violations });
      this.turn.forkOpen = null;
      this.turn.planViolations = [];
      this.turn.gateBlocks = [];
      const { decisions, alikeInstruction } = recordFork(this.repo, this.bus, violations, option, t, this.turn.prompt);
      if (alikeInstruction && process.env.HARNESS_ALIKE !== '0') this.notes.push(alikeInstruction);
      const ids = decisions.map((d) => d.id).join(', ');
      this.send(`${t}\n\n[Harness: recorded as ${ids || 'a decision'} in decisions/ and domains.yaml. ` +
        (option === 'B' ? `${violations[0]?.file} is now an exception. ` : '') +
        'Resubmit the plan with mcp__harness__submit_plan, then exit plan mode.]');
      return;
    }
    if (!this.turn) this.startTurn(t);
    this.bus.emit('chat', { role: 'user', text: t });
    this.send(t);
  }

  private send(text: string) {
    this.busy = true;
    this.ephemeral({ type: 'busy', busy: true });
    this.inbox.push(text);
  }

  private startTurn(prompt: string) {
    const id = `t${randomUUID().slice(0, 6)}`;
    this.turn = { id, prompt, base: baseline(this.repo.root), planned: false, steps: [], planViolations: [], gateBlocks: [], forkOpen: null, lastText: '' };
    this.bus.turn = id;
    this.bus.emit('turn_started', { prompt, head: this.turn.base.head, baseline: this.turn.base.snapshot });
  }

  approve() {
    if (!this.approval) return;
    const { resolve, input } = this.approval;
    this.approval = null;
    this.bus.emit('plan_approved', {} as never);
    resolve({ behavior: 'allow', updatedInput: input });
    void this.q?.setPermissionMode('acceptEdits');
  }

  private rejectPlan(feedback: string) {
    if (!this.approval) return;
    const { resolve } = this.approval;
    this.approval = null;
    resolve({ behavior: 'deny', message: `The user did not approve the plan yet. Their feedback: ${feedback}` });
  }

  private onPlan(steps: PlanStep[], violations: Violation[]) {
    if (!this.turn) return;
    this.turn.planned = true;
    this.turn.steps = steps;
    this.turn.planViolations = violations;
  }

  private onResult(subtype: string) {
    this.busy = false;
    this.ephemeral({ type: 'busy', busy: false });
    const turn = this.turn;
    if (!turn) return;
    if (subtype !== 'success') this.bus.emit('error', { message: `Turn ended with ${subtype}` });
    const open = [...turn.planViolations, ...turn.gateBlocks];
    if (open.length && subtype === 'success') {
      // Claude stopped to ask: the turn stays open until the user answers.
      turn.forkOpen = open;
      this.bus.emit('fork_asked', { violations: open, text: turn.lastText });
      return;
    }
    this.endTurn(subtype);
  }

  private endTurn(reason: string) {
    const turn = this.turn!;
    const stat = numstat(this.repo.root, turn.base);
    this.bus.emit('turn_ended', { ...stat, reason });
    const events = this.bus.events.filter((e) => e.turn === turn.id);
    writeFileSync(join(this.repo.root, '.harness/turns', `${turn.id}.json`), JSON.stringify({ id: turn.id, prompt: turn.prompt, baseline: turn.base, steps: turn.steps, numstat: stat, events }, null, 2));
    this.turn = null;
    this.bus.turn = null;
    this.repo.recheck();
    void this.q?.setPermissionMode('plan');
  }

  // ---------------------------------------------------------------- hooks

  private observeRead: HookCallback = async (input) => {
    const i = input as PreToolUseHookInput;
    const ti = i.tool_input as { file_path?: string; path?: string };
    if (i.tool_name === 'Read' && ti.file_path) {
      const rel = this.repo.rel(ti.file_path);
      if (rel) this.bus.emit('looked', { tool: 'Read' }, { path: rel, cell: this.repo.cellOf(rel) });
    } else {
      const rel = this.repo.rel(ti.path ?? this.repo.root);
      if (rel) this.bus.emit('cursor', { verb: 'searching' }, { path: rel, cell: this.repo.cellOf(rel) ?? this.repo.cellForDir(rel) });
    }
    return { async: true };
  };

  /** Claude often reads with `cat`/`sed`/`grep` in Bash: any repo file named in the command counts as looked at. */
  private observeBash: HookCallback = async (input) => {
    const cmd = String((input as PreToolUseHookInput & { tool_input: { command?: string } }).tool_input.command ?? '');
    if (/(^|[;&|]\s*)(cat|head|tail|sed|grep|rg|less|wc|nl|awk)\b/.test(cmd)) {
      for (const token of new Set(cmd.split(/[\s'";|&()<>]+/))) {
        const rel = /[\w-]\.\w+$/.test(token) ? this.repo.rel(token) : null;
        if (rel && this.repo.facts.files.includes(rel)) this.bus.emit('looked', { tool: 'Bash' }, { path: rel, cell: this.repo.cellOf(rel) });
      }
    }
    return { async: true };
  };

  /**
   * Edits made through Bash (heredocs, `sed -i`, inline scripts) would skip the edit gate. Deny commands that
   * write files inside the repo and ask for Edit/Write instead; tests, git and reads pass. The watcher still
   * records anything that slips through, as an unattributed edit.
   */
  private gateBash: HookCallback = async (input) => {
    const cmd = String((input as PreToolUseHookInput & { tool_input: { command?: string } }).tool_input.command ?? '');
    const target = bashWriteTarget(cmd, (p) => this.repo.rel(p));
    if (!target) return {};
    return {
      hookSpecificOutput: {
        hookEventName: 'PreToolUse',
        permissionDecision: 'deny',
        permissionDecisionReason: `Harness: change files in this repo with the Edit or Write tool, not through Bash (${target}), so every edit can be checked against the architecture rules. Make this change with Edit/Write instead.`,
      },
    };
  };

  /** The edit gate: same checker as load and plan, on the imports/writes this edit would add. */
  private gate: HookCallback = async (input) => {
    const i = input as PreToolUseHookInput;
    const ti = i.tool_input as { file_path?: string; content?: string; old_string?: string; new_string?: string; replace_all?: boolean };
    if (!ti.file_path) return {};
    const rel = this.repo.rel(ti.file_path);
    if (!rel) return {}; // outside the repo, e.g. Claude's own plan file
    const old = this.repo.current(rel);
    let next: string;
    try {
      next = i.tool_name === 'Write' ? ti.content ?? '' : applyEdit(old ?? '', ti.old_string ?? '', ti.new_string ?? '', ti.replace_all);
    } catch {
      return {}; // the Edit will fail on its own
    }
    const delta = deltaForEdit(rel, old, next, withExtra(this.repo.exists, [rel]));
    const violations = check(this.repo.map, delta, this.repo.mapper);
    this.bus.emit('cursor', { verb: 'editing' }, { path: rel, cell: this.repo.cellOf(rel) });
    if (!violations.length) {
      this.repo.markPending(rel);
      return {};
    }
    for (const v of violations) this.bus.emit('gate_blocked', { violation: v, tool: i.tool_name }, { path: rel, cell: this.repo.cellOf(rel) });
    this.turn?.gateBlocks.push(...violations);
    return {
      hookSpecificOutput: {
        hookEventName: 'PreToolUse',
        permissionDecision: 'deny',
        permissionDecisionReason: `Harness blocked this edit.\n${violationText(violations)}\n${ASK_RULE}`,
      },
    };
  };

  private afterEdit: HookCallback = async (input) => {
    const i = input as PostToolUseHookInput;
    const ti = i.tool_input as { file_path?: string };
    const rel = ti.file_path ? this.repo.rel(ti.file_path) : null;
    if (rel) setImmediate(() => this.repo.fileChanged(rel, { tool: i.tool_name }));
    return { async: true };
  };

  private afterAlike: HookCallback = async (input) => {
    const i = input as PostToolUseHookInput;
    const res = JSON.stringify(i.tool_response ?? '');
    const ids = new Set(JSON.stringify(i.tool_input).match(/DR-\d+/g) ?? []);
    if (/error|failed|unauthori[sz]ed/i.test(res) && !/"id"/.test(res)) return { async: true };
    for (const d of this.bus.events.filter((e) => e.kind === 'decision_recorded')) {
      const data = d.data as { id: string };
      if (ids.has(data.id)) this.bus.emit('decision_recorded', { ...(d.data as EventData['decision_recorded']), alike: true });
    }
    return { async: true };
  };

  private canUseTool: CanUseTool = async (name, input) => {
    if (name === 'ExitPlanMode') {
      const turn = this.turn;
      if (turn && !turn.planned) {
        return { behavior: 'deny', message: 'Call mcp__harness__submit_plan with your numbered steps before exiting plan mode.' };
      }
      if (turn?.planViolations.length) {
        return { behavior: 'deny', message: `The plan has unresolved violations.\n${violationText(turn.planViolations)}\n${ASK_RULE}` };
      }
      const plan = String((input as { plan?: unknown }).plan ?? '');
      this.bus.emit('approval_requested', { plan });
      return new Promise<PermissionResult>((resolve) => { this.approval = { resolve, input }; });
    }
    return { behavior: 'allow', updatedInput: input };
  };

  interrupt() { void this.q?.interrupt(); }
}
```

```text
import { existsSync, readFileSync, statSync } from "node:fs";
import { createServer, type IncomingMessage, type Server, type ServerResponse } from "node:http";
import { extname, join, normalize } from "node:path";
import { fileURLToPath, pathToFileURL } from "node:url";
import { costSummary, recentCosts } from "../gateway/cost-ledger";
import { listAccounts, notesFor } from "../memory/notes-store";
import { runAgent } from "../orchestrator/agent";
import { getRun, listRuns } from "../orchestrator/run-state";
import { registry } from "../orchestrator/tool-registry";
import { contactByEmail, listContacts } from "../outreach/crm-sync";
import { draftForRun, recentOutreach } from "../outreach/outreach-log";
import { OutreachError, sendDraft } from "../outreach/send";
import { hasAnthropicCredentials, loadConfig } from "../shared/config";
import { db } from "../shared/db";
import { createLogger } from "../shared/logger";
import type { ContactRow, RunRow } from "../shared/types";
import { validateRunRequest } from "./validate";

const log = createLogger("http");
const MAX_BODY_BYTES = 64 * 1024;
const WEB_ROOT = fileURLToPath(new URL("../../web/dist/", import.meta.url));

const MIME: Record<string, string> = {
  ".html": "text/html; charset=utf-8",
  ".js": "text/javascript; charset=utf-8",
  ".css": "text/css; charset=utf-8",
  ".svg": "image/svg+xml",
  ".woff2": "font/woff2",
  ".png": "image/png",
  ".ico": "image/x-icon",
  ".json": "application/json; charset=utf-8",
};

class HttpError extends Error {
  constructor(
    readonly status: number,
    message: string,
    readonly details?: unknown,
  ) {
    super(message);
  }
}

function send(res: ServerResponse, status: number, body: unknown): void {
  const payload = JSON.stringify(body);
  res.writeHead(status, { "content-type": "application/json; charset=utf-8", "content-length": Buffer.byteLength(payload) });
  res.end(payload);
}

async function readJson(req: IncomingMessage): Promise<unknown> {
  const chunks: Buffer[] = [];
  let size = 0;
  for await (const chunk of req) {
    size += (chunk as Buffer).length;
    if (size > MAX_BODY_BYTES) throw new HttpError(413, "request body too large");
    chunks.push(chunk as Buffer);
  }
  if (size === 0) return undefined;
  try {
    return JSON.parse(Buffer.concat(chunks).toString("utf8"));
  } catch {
    throw new HttpError(400, "body is not valid JSON");
  }
}

function persist(): void {
  const path = loadConfig().snapshotPath;
  if (path) db.snapshot(path);
}

function withContact(run: RunRow): RunRow & { contact: ContactRow | null } {
  return { ...run, contact: contactByEmail(run.contactEmail) ?? null };
}

type Handler = (params: string[], req: IncomingMessage, url: URL) => Promise<[number, unknown]> | [number, unknown];

import { Anthropic } from "../../vendor/llm-anthropic/index";
import { latestHeadlines } from "../../vendor/news/index";
import { loadConfig } from "../shared/config";
import type { Tool } from "../shared/types";

const client = new Anthropic();

export const newsSummarize: Tool = {
  name: "news_summarize",
  tags: ["news", "summary"],
  description: "Turns the company's latest headlines into talking points for the contact.",

  async run(input, ctx) {
    const headlines = await latestHeadlines(input.company, { limit: 6 });
    if (headlines.length === 0) {
      return { tool: this.name, summary: "", facts: [], sources: [] };
    }

    const contact = [input.contact.name, input.contact.title, input.contact.email, input.contact.phone]
      .filter(Boolean)
      .join(", ");
    const news = headlines.map((h) => `- ${h.title} (${h.publishedAt}). ${h.summary}`).join("\n");

    const response = await client.messages.create({
      model: loadConfig().anthropicModel,
      max_tokens: 2000,
      effort: "low",
      system: `Turn recent news about ${input.company} into two or three talking points for a call with ${contact}. Their goal: ${input.goal}. Keep every figure exact.`,
      messages: [{ role: "user", content: news }],
    });
    ctx.log.debug("summarized news", { headlines: headlines.length });

    return {
      tool: this.name,
      summary: response.content.map((block) => block.text).join(""),
      facts: headlines.map((h) => h.title),
      sources: headlines.map((h) => h.url),
    };
  },
};

import { existsSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { dirname } from "node:path";
import { nextId, observeId, resetIds } from "./ids";
import type { TableName } from "./types";

/**
 * A tiny in-memory store with JSON snapshots. Rows are plain objects with a
 * string `id`. Reads return copies, so callers can't mutate stored rows.
 */

type StoredRow = { id: string } & Record<string, unknown>;
type Store = Record<TableName, Map<string, StoredRow>>;

const TABLES: TableName[] = ["runs", "cost_log", "notes", "embeddings", "contacts", "outreach_log"];

const ID_PREFIX: Record<TableName, string> = {
  runs: "run",
  cost_log: "cost",
  notes: "note",
  embeddings: "emb",
  contacts: "ct",
  outreach_log: "out",
};

function emptyStore(): Store {
  return Object.fromEntries(TABLES.map((t) => [t, new Map()])) as Store;
}

let store: Store = emptyStore();

function table(name: TableName): Map<string, StoredRow> {
  const rows = store[name];
  if (!rows) throw new Error(`unknown table: ${name}`);
  return rows;
}

function copy<T>(row: StoredRow): T {
  return structuredClone(row) as unknown as T;
}

export class NotFoundError extends Error {
  constructor(tableName: TableName, id: string) {
    super(`${tableName}: no row with id ${id}`);
    this.name = "NotFoundError";
  }
}

export const db = {
  insert<T extends object>(tableName: TableName, row: T): T & { id: string } {
    const rows = table(tableName);
    const given = (row as { id?: unknown }).id;
    const id = typeof given === "string" && given ? given : nextId(ID_PREFIX[tableName]);
    if (rows.has(id)) throw new Error(`${tableName}: duplicate id ${id}`);
    observeId(id);
    const stored = { ...structuredClone(row), id } as StoredRow;
    rows.set(id, stored);
    return copy(stored);
  },

  /** Merges `patch` into the row. The return type comes from the call site, e.g. `const run: RunRow = db.update(...)`. */
```

```text
**Zoom levels and drill-down**
- IcePanel's docs say its diagram hierarchy follows the C4 model with 3 levels of connected diagrams (instead of Level 4 diagrams, we allow you to link objects to reality).
- To drill down, you can use the 🔎 icon at the top-right of an object in a diagram, or the Level dropdown in the navigation bar. A numeric indicator will show how many objects are nested within the object. If there are no nested objects, a blank diagram will be created at a lower level when you click on it.
- An older IcePanel blog post describes the same flow: create a system in the top-level diagram, zoom in with the magnifying glass, then add apps or stores inside it.

**Connections across levels**
- The blog notes that the official guidance says you should avoid mixing scopes at lower levels, but IcePanel lets you break that restriction. Bounding areas are automatically added to show the parts of the hierarchy that belong in other scopes. You can now create connections between scopes.
- The diagramming docs state that connections to and from the object are part of an object's details, and that connections are stored in the model as relationships.

Sources: docs.icepanel.io/features/diagramming, docs.icepanel.io/getting-started, icepanel.io/blog/top-5-tips-for-using-icepanel, icepanel.io/blog/how-to-create-interactive-zoomable-software-architecture-diagrams. Graphify is an open-source tool that turns a codebase (plus docs, schemas, and other files) into a queryable knowledge graph, and it integrates with Claude Code as a skill plus an MCP server.
```

```text
- **What it does:** One source describes it as turning code, docs, PDFs, and images into a graph you can explore instead of grepping files ([dev.co](https://dev.co/ai/rag/graphify)). Code is parsed locally with tree-sitter, so no model call is needed for source files ([graphify.com](https://graphify.com/blog/how-to-give-claude-code-a-code-knowledge-graph)).
- **Setup:** The package is named `graphifyy` (two y's), and the CLI is `graphify` ([CodeConductor](https://codeconductor.ai/blog/graphify-review/)). Running `graphify install` wires in the `/graphify` slash command and an MCP server with eight tools ([graphify.com](https://graphify.com/blog/how-to-give-claude-code-a-code-knowledge-graph)).
- **Outputs:** The tool produces an interactive `graph.html`, a `GRAPH_REPORT.md` summary, and the raw `graph.json` ([graphify.com](https://graphify.com/blog/how-to-give-claude-code-a-code-knowledge-graph)).
- **Claude Code behavior:** A PreToolUse hook nudges Claude to consult the graph report before broad Grep or Glob calls, but it doesn't replace reading source files ([CodeConductor](https://codeconductor.ai/blog/graphify-review/)).
- **Token savings:** One guide claims a 71.5x reduction on a 52-file repo ([emelia.io](https://emelia.io/es/hub/knowledge-graph-graphify-guide)). A hands-on test by another author reports a more modest 5–10x figure and flags caveats ([mejba.me](https://www.mejba.me/graphify-knowledge-graph-codebase-claude-code)). Treat the headline number as unverified.
- **Discrepancies:** Sources disagree on the license (MIT in one, Apache-2.0 in another) and on GitHub stars (79.8k in one, about 116k in another). Check the upstream repo at github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify for current values.
```

```text
- **Community clustering:** Communities come from Leiden clustering, and the README says the graph is "split into subsystems (Leiden), with LLM-free labels." You can tune granularity with `--cluster-only --resolution 1.5`.

**Claude Code integration:**
- Install with `uv tool install graphifyy`, then run `graphify install` to register the skill.
- In Claude Code, run `/graphify .` to build the graph. Output goes to `graphify-out/` as graph.html, GRAPH_REPORT.md, and graph.json.
- Running `graphify claude install` in a project makes the assistant query the graph first. On Claude Code, a hook "fires automatically before search-style tool calls," nudging the assistant toward graph queries.
```

<tool-use data-tool-type="read" data-tool-name="WebFetch"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **WebFetch**</summary>
 `https://cognition.com/blog/codemaps`

```text
**Structure and levels of abstraction**
Codemaps are "first-of-its-kind AI-annotated structured maps of your code." The article describes them as grouped, nested sections. Each section can be expanded with "See more," which opens a "trace guide" explaining what connects the discovered lines. The article doesn't describe further abstraction levels beyond these nested groups.

**Navigation and linking to code**
You open Codemaps with a task prompt or one of the suggested prompts, then pick a Fast (SWE-1.5) or Smart (Sonnet 4.5) model. The list view links grouped sections to exact lines of code, which the article contrasts with Cascade answers that are "not as densely linked to the exact lines of code."

**List vs. visualization**
A visual mode is available. Clicking a node "send[s] you to the exact part of the codebase you clicked on," and the article says it works the same way as the list view. The article doesn't say how nodes are laid out or how edges (connections between nodes) are drawn.

**Use in Cascade**
You can reference a codemap, or a subsection of one, in a Cascade prompt with @{codemap}, which the article says improves agent performance on a task.

**Design rationale**
The core idea is that AI tools should keep engineers engaged rather than separate them from their code. The article argues that "To understand is to be accountable," and that the engineer's role is shifting toward accountability for what ships. Codemaps is meant to give humans and AI a shared picture of the system's structure, data flow, and dependencies. The article also frames the goal as helping engineers avoid shipping code they don't understand.

**Limitations and open items**
- The article says Codemaps are "a snapshot of your code" that respects ZDR, but it doesn't describe how often they update.
- The article says it hasn't yet benchmarked how much Codemaps improve Devin or Cascade on hard tasks.
- Sharing across teams works today, but connecting and annotating codemaps and an open .codemap protocol are described as future opportunities.
- The article reports that Codemaps work best on your own codebase and for specific "how or where" questions. Its effectiveness claims come from Cognition's own demos and dogfooding.
```

```text
Here's what the search turned up, grouped by topic.

**Double-click navigation:** In the Structurizr viewer, double-clicking an element with a "+" symbol opens the first diagram at the next level of detail, such as a container diagram for a software system. Double-click on an element with a + symbol to open the first diagram at the next level of detail (e.g. a container diagram for a software system). The viewer docs add that double-clicking can also open documentation, decisions, or a configured URL. Open documentation associated with the element. Open decisions associated with the element. Open the URL that is configured by the element's url property. Double-clicking a container goes to its first Component diagram, if one exists. Double-clicking a container will take you to the first Component diagram for that container, if one exists.

**Implied relationships:** The DSL creates these by default. If a person has a relationship to a container inside a software system, the DSL also creates a relationship between that person and the software system. By default, the Structurizr DSL will create "implied relationships" automatically. You can turn this off with the `!impliedRelationships false` keyword. This functionality can be disabled using the !impliedRelationships keyword. The DSL creates only one implied relationship per pair of elements. The Structurizr DSL uses the CreateImpliedRelationshipsUnlessAnyRelationshipExistsStrategy from the Structurizr for Java library when creating implied relationships, which prevents multiple implied relationships from being created.

**Java library difference:** The Java library does not do this automatically. Unlike the Structurizr DSL, the Structurizr for Java library will not create implied relationships.

**Tutorial:** The DSL tutorial uses the same idea to explain drill-down. It notes that a software system's relationships can be inferred from its inner containers, so a user relationship to a web app implies one to the system. There is an explicit relationship from the user to the web application, and because the web application is a container inside the software system, there is an implicit (or implied) relationship between the user and the software system itself.

The search did not turn up a source that connects double-click drill-down directly to implied relationships. The two features are separate: drill-down is a viewer interaction, and implied relationships are a DSL modeling behavior. The drill-down behavior is what shows the implied relationships at the system level when a diagram is opened.
```

```text
The search turned up mostly third-party write-ups and a few marketplace listings. Official AppMap documentation didn't appear, so I couldn't confirm details against the docs themselves.

- **What AppMap is:** It's an open-source runtime code analysis tool for Ruby, Java, Python, and Node.js. It records execution traces and displays them as interactive diagrams (AppMap is a versatile open-source runtime code analysis tool compatible with Ruby, Java, Python, and Node.js. It records code execution traces, gathering data about how your code works and behaves.).
- **Dependency map:** A developer-focused tutorial describes it as showing the high-level picture of the code packages and how they relate to each other.
- **Trace view:** The same tutorial says the Trace view shows the detailed execution path through the code, with parameters, return values, exceptions, etc.
- **Sequence diagrams:** A DEV Community post by AppMap's creator explains that you generate them by first recording a run, either running a test case or running your app and interacting with it through its UI or by sending API requests. The post notes that a newer version is fully interactive and doesn't require Java or PlantUML.
- **Recording:** One guide lists the workflow as installing the VS Code extension, running a test program with recording enabled, opening the AppMap, and then exploring it through the dependency map and execution trace (Open the AppMap in VS Code. 6. Explore and learn the code using the dependency map and execution trace.).
- **Other features:** A third-party summary mentions interactive flame graphs and anti-patterns like N+1 queries.
```

The research agents are still running. While they work, here's how the current shell divides up:
- The map renderer (`MapGrid` and `layout.ts`, about 450 lines) is what gets replaced.
- The chat pane, ledger, inspector, scrubber and derived-view layer (about 900 lines) mostly carry over.

The rule that all UI state is reduced from the event log still holds. Whichever level you're viewing, the same events drive it.

My working shape for the plan, which the research will confirm or change:
- **One graph, one projection.** Core builds a single containment tree: domain → cell → file → symbol, plus tables, vendors and routes. All the low-level relationships (imports, calls, table writes) are attached at the bottom of that tree. Each view is a pure function of that graph, which nodes are expanded, and the agent's activity, with edges rolled up to the nearest visible ancestor. Every level, from journeys down to symbols, is then just a different set of expanded nodes, rather than a separate graph to keep in sync.
- **The grid stays the top level.** Expanding a domain widens its column, while the other columns compress into narrow strips that still show their activity. That domain's cells become containers of files, keeping the layer rows, so "a normal change is a vertical stripe" holds at every depth.
- **Navigation that knows about the agent.** A "follow Claude" camera, indicators for activity outside the viewport, and ⌘K jump. Clicking nodes adds them as context to your next chat message, and paths in Claude's replies become links that fly the map to them.
- **Two speeds of fact extraction.** The fast per-file scan the edit gate needs stays as it is. Function and call extraction runs separately and never blocks the session.

When the three reports land, I'll write it up as `NAVIGATION_PLAN.md` in the repo, in the same style as `SPEC.md`: phases, acceptance checks, and the few decisions that are yours. The main ones are the navigation model and the visual direction.

 `https://githubnext.com/projects/repo-visualization/`

```text
**Design rationale**

The goal is a "fingerprint" of a repo that shows its structure at a glance. The author argues that a visual overview is faster to read than a directory tree: "Can we do better?" Once viewers learn the visual language, they can compare codebases side by side and spot similarities and differences.

**Techniques**

- **Circles and size:** Each file and folder is drawn as a circle, and "the circle’s size represents the size of the file." The article calls these "dots," and says each is "sized by file size." It doesn't name the layout algorithm, so it never mentions circle packing.
- **Color by file type:** Color encodes file type, so the viewer can see, for example, that most package code is JavaScript and that the `tasks` folder is mostly `.sh` files.
- **Folder labels:** Folder names appear in the diagram and help locate the nested structure, such as tests inside `react-dev-utils`. The article doesn't describe a labeling rule.
- **Depth limits:** The article doesn't discuss depth limits.
- **Integration:** A GitHub Action regenerates the diagram on each change. The React component is rendered with `renderToStaticMarkup` and saved as SVG, so the diagram can live in the README: "we can see it every time we work on the codebase."

**Problems and limitations**

The article mentions few explicit problems. For import connections, it notes that "there are often too many connections happening at once," so it shows links only on hover. It also calls the work a timeboxed exploration.

**Possible next steps**

- **Import graph:** Link files that import each other, to show data flow and standalone files.
- **Change frequency:** Show which files change most, to find key files or stale code.
- **Recency:** Highlight recently edited areas to help re-orient after a break.
- **History over time:** Track how structure grows and whether changes are scoped or sweeping across commits.
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
- **How it works:** Precise navigation depends on the open source SCIP Code Intelligence Protocol, a language-agnostic protocol for indexing source code. It uses compile-time information, and Sourcegraph uses precise navigation whenever it is available, falling back to search-based navigation otherwise.
- **Setup:** Indexes must be generated and uploaded per repository. Sourcegraph suggests auto-indexing as a fast way to get started, but recommends running SCIP indexing in your CI pipeline for complex or authenticated builds.

- **Cross-repo:** This works out-of-the-box when both the dependent repository and the dependency repository have indexes at the correct commits or versions.
- **2025 changes:** A changelog entry says the precise code navigation logic has been rewritten for better correctness and performance. It states that Go to Definition and Find References operations are faster, with significantly improved accuracy across complex codebases. The changelog does not give a date in the snippet, and it notes that this enhancement is available exclusively on the web interface.
- **Governance:** A Sourcegraph resource page says SCIP is transitioning to an independent project with open governance. That page is promotional, and its March 2026 date falls after the 2025 timeframe in the query, so verify it against the original announcement.

Language coverage varies. The current docs list indexers for Go, TypeScript/JavaScript, Python, Java, Kotlin, Scala, C/C++, Rust, Ruby, and C#/VB, with some marked as partially available. One older docs page still names lsif-go for Go, so the indexer naming may differ across doc versions.
```

```text
# Graphify: Summary from the Repository Page

**Overview.** Graphify (Graphify-Labs/graphify) turns a codebase, its docs, and other files into a knowledge graph that you query instead of grepping. It is invoked as a `/graphify` skill in AI coding assistants. The page describes it as "Turn any codebase, with its docs, SQL schemas, configs, and PDFs, into a queryable knowledge graph."

**What it extracts**
- **Nodes:** Concepts, such as classes and functions. Rationale comments (`# NOTE:` / `# WHY:`) and ADR/RFC citations "become first-class nodes linked to the code."
- **Edges:** The page names `calls`, `imports`, `inherits`, `mixes_in`, `uses`, `references`, and `method`. So call edges are described, though the page does not give a complete list of node or edge types.
- **Confidence tags:** Each edge is `EXTRACTED` ("explicit in the source") or `INFERRED` ("resolved by graphify").
- **Other structure:** Communities (subsystems found with Leiden clustering, labeled without an LLM) and "god nodes," the most-connected concepts.

**Languages and inputs**
- Code: "~40 languages via tree-sitter AST," per the features table. Full list is on docs.graphify.com, which I can't verify from this page.
- Optional extras add Terraform, Pascal, OCaml, Common Lisp, Robot Framework, SQL schemas, and live PostgreSQL introspection.
- Docs, PDFs, images, and video/audio are also mapped into the graph.

**How it parses**
- **Code:** Deterministic tree-sitter AST parsing with no LLM. "nothing leaves your machine."
- **Docs, PDFs, images:** A semantic pass through the assistant's model or a configured API key. Headless `graphify extract` supports several backends, including Gemini, Claude, OpenAI, DeepSeek, Bedrock, and Ollama.
- **Video/audio:** Transcribed locally with faster-whisper (optional `video` extra).
- **Retrieval:** No embeddings or vector store. Queries traverse the graph.

**Output formats**
- `graph.html`: interactive, browser-viewable graph.
- `GRAPH_REPORT.md`: god nodes, communities, surprising connections, suggested questions.
- `graph.json`: full graph, including `graph.schema_version` and `graph.graphify_version` fields.
- Optional: a markdown wiki (`--wiki`), Mermaid call-flow HTML (`graphify export callflow-html`), SVG export, and Neo4j/FalkorDB push.

**Speed claims.** The page gives no build-time or query-time speed figures. The "80%" figure ("Cut agent token spend by 80%") is attached to the paid Graphify Cloud product, not the open-source tool. - `/graphify ./docs --update` is described as one that will "re-extract only changed files."

- PyPI package: `graphifyy` (double-y). The page warns that other `graphify*` packages are unaffiliated. The CLI command is `graphify`.

- No npm package is mentioned.
- Python 3.10+ is required.

- The page shows the `v8` branch, 2,238 commits, 706 open issues, 862 pull requests, 125.5k stars, 12.1k forks, and 397 watchers.
```

```text
**Composite nodes**

- The page doesn't explain how collapsing works or how edges to and from a collapsed composite node are drawn, so I can't confirm whether they're aggregated.
- You can also focus a composite node. The docs say you can "focus" it "to render a graph of just the projects inside that node."

**Focus, proximity, and group by folder**

- Focusing on a project lets you use the sidebar's proximity and group-by-folder controls to "modify the graph around that project." You can also start with a project focused using `nx graph --focus <project-name>`.
- The page names proximity and group by folder as sidebar controls but doesn't define them further.

**Task graph**

- The task graph shows the tasks Nx runs and their dependencies. It's based on the project graph. Pass `--graph` to view it, for example `nx build myreactapp --graph`.
- Clicking a task node shows details such as the executor, the inputs used for the computation hash, and a link to the project's details.
- The docs note that Nx "will need to wait for all task dependencies to complete successfully before running the task."
```

```text
Cognition's DeepWiki is a hosted service, and the Mermaid detail comes mainly from open-source clones, not Cognition's own docs.

- **Official service:** Replacing github.com with deepwiki.com in a public repo URL brings up an auto-generated wiki with architecture diagrams, module summaries, and prose explanations of how the pieces fit together. Cognition launched it on May 5, 2025 as "the free public version of Devin Wiki and Devin Search". Per one guide, when a repo carries a DeepWiki badge, the wiki auto-refreshes on updates. A Cognition-linked guide says private repos require a Devin AI organization to index the repo first.
- **How it builds the wiki:** One source describes the pipeline as walking the directory tree, identifying entry points and top-level packages, summarising each module's purpose from the source plus the README, and stitching those summaries into a navigable structure. A separate guide says it ingests a repository's code files, README, and configuration, then passes them through large language models to produce structured documentation with real links back to the source.
- **Mermaid diagrams:** The Mermaid-specific description comes from the open-source reimplementation, deepwiki-open. Its README says the tool clones and analyzes the repository, creates embeddings of the code for smart retrieval, generates documentation with context-aware AI, and creates visual diagrams to explain code relationships. Its feature list includes automatic Mermaid diagrams to visualize architecture and data flow. I did not find a source confirming that the official deepwiki.com output uses Mermaid specifically.
- **Q&A layer:** A third-party summary says the "Ask" feature uses a Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) approach to let users query the repository's code.

Most of these sources are third-party blogs, so verify details against Cognition's official documentation before relying on them.
```

```text
Several open-source tools match this, and the closest fit to "live map of AI agent activity" is CodeMap Hotel and JamsusMaximus/codemap.

- **JamsusMaximus/codemap** is a browser-based tool that visualizes AI coding agent activity in real time. It targets Claude Code and Cursor. It has 130 GitHub stars with 19 forks as of the most recent article. The visualization updates via WebSocket as hooks capture file operations, thinking states, and completion events.
- **CodeMap Hotel** is a similar project that renders agents as pixel-art characters. Folders become hotel rooms, files transform into desks with glowing screens, and agents appear as pixel-art developers.
- **OpenVisio** is an MIT-licensed codebase map with a 3D city view, a 2D graph, and an MCP server for agents. It runs locally, and its engine uses tree-sitter with no LLM. It is positioned as an open-source alternative to CodeSee, which was sunset after the GitKraken acquisition.
- **Understand-Anything** is an open-source plugin in which a pipeline of five specialized AI agents analyzes a project and builds a graph where each file, function, and class is a node.
- **Depwire** is a dependency graph tool that serves the graph to AI tools over MCP. It has a `depwire viz` command for visualization.

Other options include codedocent (code visualization for non-programmers) and codemap for VS Code (a D3.js force-directed graph). GitHub topic pages list many more small projects, so star counts and maintenance status should be checked before adoption. Note that the search results are mostly vendor pages and blog posts, so the claims about features and performance were not independently verified.
```

```text
**JamsusMaximus/codemap** is an open-source TypeScript tool that shows AI coding agent activity as a pixel-art hotel in the browser. It targets Claude Code and Cursor.

**Views**
- **Hotel view (`/hotel`):** The main pixel-art view. The article describes the project's core idea as "rooms are folders, desks are files."
- **Force-directed graph (root `/`):** An alternative view that, per the article, "serves a force-directed graph view as an alternative to" the hotel view.

**Hooks**
Four shell scripts capture activity: `file-activity-hook.sh`, `thinking-hook.sh`, `cursor-stop-hook.sh`, and `git-post-commit.sh`. Updates are pushed over WebSocket as the hooks capture file operations and thinking states. The article also mentions a hook log at `/tmp/codemap-hook.log`.

**What's shown during reads and edits**
- Agents walk between rooms as they switch files.
- Screens glow yellow when an agent reads and green when it writes.
- Speech bubbles show the active tool and target file.
- Stuck agents bounce, which signals that they're waiting on input or permission. The article says "stuck agents bounce until you notice them."
- Up to 10 agents can appear at once.

**Hierarchy and zoom**
- Folders map to rooms and files map to desks.
- Rooms are ranked by git activity, and the layout refreshes on each commit.
- Rooms are color-coded by file type. The article gives Components (blue), Server (green), and Tests (peach) as examples.
- The article doesn't describe any zoom or drill-down controls.

**Setup and source**
- Quick start: `npx github:JamsusMaximus/codemap`, run inside a project.
- Local development runs the client on port 5173 and the server on 5174.
- Health and debugging endpoints include `/api/health` and `/api/thinking`.
- GitHub: https://github.com/JamsusMaximus/codemap
```

```text
GitNexus is an open-source tool that builds a code knowledge graph entirely in the browser, with no backend server. Sources describe it as a client-side engine that indexes a codebase into an interactive graph, plus a built-in Graph RAG agent for questions about the code. Its Web UI is said to run without server-side components, so code stays on the user's machine.

Input works through a GitHub repo URL or an uploaded ZIP. One source says the web app is at gitnexus.vercel.app and also accepts GitLab and Azure DevOps repos. Another describes a local setup where you clone the repo, run `npm install` and `npm run dev`, then open localhost:5173.

The browser stack uses WebAssembly, with Tree-sitter for parsing and KuzuDB for graph storage and vector indexing. Indexing happens in two phases: the graph first, then embeddings in the background. Language support is currently TypeScript, JavaScript, and Python, with Go, Java, and C in progress.

The sources disagree on some details. A GitHub star count appears as 25,000+ in one article and 33,463 in another. Sources also differ on whether the project is primarily the browser app or the CLI/MCP server for AI assistants like Claude Code and Cursor. The search results were mostly secondary blogs and directory listings, so I'd check the GitHub repo (abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus) for current specifics.
```

```text
- **How it works:** A multi-agent pipeline extracts files, functions, classes, and dependencies, then an LLM adds the semantic layer. Tree-sitter handles deterministic parsing, and LLM agents assign architectural layers and write plain-English summaries.

- **Other views:** A domain view maps code to business processes, and guided tours walk through the architecture in dependency order.
- **Usage:** Install via the Claude Code plugin marketplace, run `/understand` to build the graph, and run `/understand-dashboard` to explore it.
- **Scale:** Figures vary by source. One cites about 12.9k GitHub stars, while another cites about 71.7k stars for the Egonex-AI repo, and the latest release is listed as v2.7.3 from May 19, 2026.
```

<tool-use data-tool-type="read" data-tool-name="WebFetch"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **WebFetch**</summary>
 `https://reactflow.dev/learn/advanced-use/performance`

```text
The page gives **no node count limits, benchmarks, or mention of `onlyRenderVisibleElements`.** Its guidance covers these areas:

**What causes re-renders**
- Node movement triggers frequent state updates, which can create bottlenecks in larger diagrams.
- Components that read the `nodes` or `edges` arrays re-render on every change during dragging, panning, or zooming, even when the change is unrelated to them.

**Memoization**
- Custom node and edge components passed to `<ReactFlow>` should be wrapped in `React.memo` or declared outside the parent component.
- Callback functions passed as props should be wrapped in `useCallback`.
- Objects and arrays such as `defaultEdgeOptions` and `snapGrid` should be wrapped in `useMemo`.

**Store access patterns**
- Avoid selecting the full `nodes` array and filtering it inside a component. This is the page's main example of an anti-pattern.
- Instead, keep derived data, such as selected node IDs, in its own state field (using Zustand, Redux, or similar) so components re-render only when that data changes.

**Large node trees**
- For deeply nested trees, show a limited set of nodes and let users expand the rest.
- Toggle each node's `hidden` property to control visibility rather than rendering everything at once.

**CSS and styling**
- If other optimizations aren't enough, reduce style complexity. The page singles out animations, shadows, and gradients as costly when many nodes are present.

**Further reading**
- The page links three external resources: a Synergy Codes guide, a LiamBx post on tuning edge animations, and a YouTube video titled "5 Ways to Optimize React Flow in 10 minutes."
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
The page confirms several dashboard views and some visual choices, but it doesn't describe layout, hierarchy, zoom mechanics, or how edges are drawn.

- **Structural graph:** The default view. Nodes are files, functions, and classes. "every file, function, and class is a node you can click, search, and explore." Selecting a node shows summaries and relationships.
- **Domain view:** Maps code to business processes. It's a horizontal layout of "domains, flows, and steps laid out as a horizontal graph."
- **Layer view:** Groups nodes by architectural layer (API, Service, Data, UI, Utility) with a "color-coded legend."
- **Guided tours:** "Auto-generated walkthroughs of the architecture, ordered by dependency."
- **Diff impact:** Shows which parts of the system a change affects, via `/understand-diff`. It is described as "See which parts of the system your changes affect before you commit."
- **Knowledge-base view:** For LLM wikis, the page describes "a force-directed knowledge graph with community clustering."

**Layout, hierarchy, and zoom**

The page doesn't explain how hierarchy is represented or how nested levels expand. It only says the live demo lets you "pan, zoom, search, and explore" in the browser.

**Edges**

Edges are mentioned only as "relationships" and dependency ordering. The page doesn't cover edge styling, direction, or filtering.

**Visual design and adaptation**

- Color is used for architectural layers, with a legend.
- The dashboard is "color-coded by architectural layer, searchable, and clickable."
- Detail level adapts to the user: "The dashboard adjusts its detail level based on who you are."
- Output language can be set with `--language`, which changes labels, buttons, and tooltips.
- The read-only viewer runs locally: "Everything is served read-only from local disk."

For specifics on layout algorithms, zoom behavior, or edge rendering, the repository's dashboard source or docs would be needed.
```
