```text
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { apply, cellViews, edgeViews, initialState, provenance, reduce } from '../src/events';
import { demoLog } from './turn-log';

describe('reduce', () => {
  const { events, firstEdit } = demoLog();
  const s = reduce(events);

  it('is a pure fold: incremental apply equals reduce', () => {
    const inc = initialState();
    events.forEach((e, i) => apply(inc, e, i));
    expect(JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(inc))).toEqual(JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(reduce(events))));
  });

  it('carries the load-time violation as existing and the map edges', () => {
    expect(s.violations).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(s.violations[0]!.file).toBe('src/tools/news-summarize.ts');
    expect(s.edges['tools->gateway']).toBeDefined();
  });

  it('replays: before the fork answer the plan ghost is red and new, after the turn it is solid', () => {
    const forkAsked = events.findIndex((e) => e.kind === 'fork_asked');
    const mid = reduce(events, forkAsked + 1);
    expect(mid.pendingFork?.violations[0]?.invariant).toBe('DR-1');
    const tools = cellViews(mid)['tools/logic']!;
    expect(tools.ghost).toEqual([1, 2]);
    expect(tools.violation).toBe('new'); // differs from the map before the turn even though the cell was already red
    expect(tools.newViolationFiles).toEqual(['src/tools/filing-summary.ts']);
    const ghost = edgeViews(mid).find((e) => e.state === 'ghost');
    expect(ghost).toMatchObject({ from: 'tools', to: 'gateway', violation: true });
    expect(edgeViews(mid).some((e) => e.state === 'existing' && e.from === 'tools' && e.to === 'gateway')).toBe(true);

    const end = cellViews(s);
    expect(end['tools/logic']).toMatchObject({ edited: true, ghost: null, added: 14 });
    expect(end['outreach/logic']).toMatchObject({ unplanned: true });
    expect(end['gateway/logic']).toMatchObject({ looked: true, edited: false });
    expect(reduce(events, firstEdit).turns[0]!.approved).toBe(true);
  });

  it('records the decision and provenance', () => {
    expect(s.decisions.map((d) => d.id)).toEqual(['DR-4']);
    const p = provenance(s, { edge: 'tools->gateway' });
    expect(p.turns.map((t) => t.index)).toEqual([1]);
    expect(p.decisions.map((d) => d.id)).toEqual(['DR-4']);
  });
});
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { reduce, type HarnessEvent } from '../src/events';
import { ledger, turnFindings } from '../src/ledger';
import type { Violation } from '../src/rules';
import { demoLog } from './turn-log';

describe('ledger (SPEC §9)', () => {
  it('counts the demo turn exactly', () => {
    const { events } = demoLog();
    const l = ledger(reduce(events));
    expect(l.turns).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(l.turns[0]).toMatchObject({ linesChanged: 18, forksCaughtBeforeCode: 1, rejectedOptionsBlocked: 0 });
    // invariant hit (tools/logic) · unplanned edit (outreach/logic); the tools→gateway edge already existed
    // at domain level but is new this turn, and lands in tools/logic too.
    expect(l.turns[0]!.cellsToReview).toBe(2);
    expect(l.session).toEqual({ linesChanged: 18, cellsToReview: 2, forksCaughtBeforeCode: 1, rejectedOptionsBlocked: 0 });
  });

  it('ranks findings loudest first', () => {
    const { events } = demoLog();
    const s = reduce(events);
    const f = turnFindings(s, s.turns[0]!);
    expect(f.map((x) => x.severity)).toEqual([...f.map((x) => x.severity)].sort());
    expect(f[0]).toMatchObject({ severity: 1, kind: 'invariant', invariant: 'DR-1' });
    expect(f.some((x) => x.kind === 'unplanned' && x.cell?.domain === 'outreach')).toBe(true);
  });

  it('lines changed is null until the turn ends', () => {
    const { events } = demoLog();
    const l = ledger(reduce(events, events.length - 1));
    expect(l.turns[0]!.linesChanged).toBeNull();
    expect(l.session.linesChanged).toBe(0);
  });

  it('does not count a fork answered after code was written', () => {
    const { events, firstEdit } = demoLog();
    // Move the fork question and answer after the first edit.
    const fork = events.filter((e) => e.kind === 'fork_asked' || e.kind === 'fork_answered');
    const rest = events.filter((e) => !fork.includes(e));
    const at = rest.findIndex((e) => e === events[firstEdit]) + 1;
    const reordered: HarnessEvent[] = [...rest.slice(0, at), ...fork, ...rest.slice(at)];
    expect(ledger(reduce(reordered)).turns[0]!.forksCaughtBeforeCode).toBe(0);
  });

  it('counts violations that cite an existing decision as rejected options blocked', () => {
    const { events } = demoLog();
    const v: Violation = { invariant: 'DR-1', kind: 'only_via', reason: 'You decided this in DR-4. …', file: 'src/tools/earnings.ts', detail: '', options: ['A', 'B'], target: 'vendor/llm-openai/index.ts', decision: 'DR-4' };
    const t2: HarnessEvent[] = [
      { id: 'x1', t: 1, session: 's1', turn: 't2', kind: 'turn_started', data: { prompt: 'earnings calls', head: '', baseline: '' } },
      { id: 'x2', t: 2, session: 's1', turn: 't2', kind: 'gate_blocked', path: v.file, data: { violation: v, tool: 'Write' } },
      { id: 'x3', t: 3, session: 's1', turn: 't2', kind: 'gate_blocked', path: v.file, data: { violation: v, tool: 'Write' } },
      { id: 'x4', t: 4, session: 's1', turn: 't2', kind: 'turn_ended', data: { added: 0, removed: 0, files: [], reason: 'success' } },
    ];
    const l = ledger(reduce([...events, ...t2]));
    expect(l.turns[1]).toMatchObject({ rejectedOptionsBlocked: 1, linesChanged: 0, forksCaughtBeforeCode: 0 });
    expect(l.session.rejectedOptionsBlocked).toBe(1);
  });
});
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { reduce, type HarnessEvent } from '../src/events';
import { fileOf, cellId, domainId, edgeId, symbolId } from '../src/contracts/graph';
import type { MapProposal } from '../src/contracts/cartography';
import { parseDomainMap } from '../src/schema';
import { demoLog } from './turn-log';
import { scoutFacts } from './scout-facts';
import { mapYaml } from './helpers';

const ev = (i: number, kind: HarnessEvent['kind'], data: Record<string, unknown>, extra: Partial<HarnessEvent> = {}): HarnessEvent =>
  ({ id: `c${i}`, t: 5000 + i, session: 's1', turn: null, kind, data, ...extra });

describe('contract ids', () => {
  it('build and invert stable ids', () => {
    expect(domainId('tools')).toBe('domain:tools');
    expect(cellId('tools', 'logic')).toBe('cell:tools/logic');
    expect(symbolId('src/a.ts', 'f.g')).toBe('src/a.ts#f.g');
    expect(edgeId('calls', 'src/a.ts#f', 'src/b.ts#g')).toBe('calls|src/a.ts#f|src/b.ts#g');
    expect(fileOf('src/a.ts#f.g')).toBe('src/a.ts');
    expect(fileOf('src/a.ts')).toBe('src/a.ts');
    expect(fileOf('cell:tools/logic')).toBeNull();
    expect(fileOf('table:runs')).toBeNull();
  });
});

describe('schema extensions', () => {
  it('accepts components and cartography settings', () => {
    const yaml = mapYaml.replace(
      'logic:    { paths: ["src/tools/**"] }',
      'logic:    { paths: ["src/tools/**"], components: [{ id: news, name: News, paths: ["src/tools/news-*.ts"] }] }',
    ) + '\ncartography:\n  thresholds: { wideTurnsMedian: 4 }\n';
    const map = parseDomainMap(yaml);
    expect(map.domains.find((d) => d.id === 'tools')!.cells.logic!.components![0]!.name).toBe('News');
    expect(map.cartography?.thresholds?.wideTurnsMedian).toBe(4);
  });
});

describe('reducer: facts and living-map events', () => {
  const { events } = demoLog();

  it('derives per-file facts from an older scan and tracks per-path activity', () => {
    const s = reduce(events);
    expect(s.facts['src/tools/news-summarize.ts']!.imports.map((i) => i.to)).toContain('vendor/llm-openai/index.ts');
    expect(s.facts['src/gateway/cost-ledger.ts']!.writes.map((w) => w.table)).toEqual(['cost_log']);
    const t = s.turns[0]!;
    expect(t.paths['src/tools/news-summarize.ts']!.looked).toBe(true);
    expect(t.paths['src/tools/filing-summary.ts']).toMatchObject({ created: true, added: 12, edits: 1 });
  });

  it('replaces facts on facts_changed, drops stale Tier 2 results, merges symbol diffs', () => {
    const facts = scoutFacts();
    const f = { ...facts['src/tools/news-summarize.ts']!, hash: 'h2' };
    const extra: HarnessEvent[] = [
      ev(1, 'turn_started', { prompt: 'x', head: '', baseline: '' }, { turn: 't9' }),
      ev(2, 'facts_changed', { facts: f }, { turn: 't9', path: f.path }),
      ev(3, 'facts_resolved', { facts: { path: f.path, hash: 'old', calls: [], implements: [] } }),
      ev(4, 'facts_resolved', { facts: { path: f.path, hash: 'h2', calls: [{ from: 'a', to: 'b', confidence: 'typed', count: 1 }], implements: [] } }),
      ev(5, 'edited', { added: 1, removed: 0, created: false, symbols: { added: ['a'], removed: [], sig: [], body: ['b'], renamed: [] } }, { turn: 't9', path: f.path, cell: { domain: 'tools', layer: 'logic' } }),
      ev(6, 'edited', { added: 2, removed: 1, created: false, symbols: { added: [], removed: [], sig: ['c'], body: ['b'], renamed: [] } }, { turn: 't9', path: f.path, cell: { domain: 'tools', layer: 'logic' } }),
      ev(7, 'call_added', { from: 'a', to: 'b', confidence: 'syntactic' }, { turn: 't9' }),
      ev(8, 'facts_changed', { facts: null }, { turn: 't9', path: 'src/tools/web-search.ts' }),
    ];
    const s = reduce([...events, ...extra]);
    expect(s.facts[f.path]!.hash).toBe('h2');
    expect(s.semantic[f.path]!.calls).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(s.facts['src/tools/web-search.ts']).toBeUndefined();
    const pa = s.turns.at(-1)!.paths[f.path]!;
    expect(pa).toMatchObject({ added: 3, removed: 1, edits: 2 });
    expect(pa.symbols).toEqual({ added: ['a'], removed: [], sig: ['c'], body: ['b'], renamed: [] });
    expect(s.turns.at(-1)!.callsAdded).toEqual([{ from: 'a', to: 'b' }]);
  });

  it('keeps living-map proposals out of the map until accepted, and tracks labels, findings, drift', () => {
    const before = reduce(events);
    const proposal: MapProposal = {
      id: 'MP-1', trigger: [], scope: ['domain:billing'], candidates: [], chosen: 0,
      current: { cellsLitMean: 0, cellsLitMedian: 0, modularity: 0, unassigned: 0, cellSizeGini: 0, decisionsBroken: 0, churnFiles: 0, churnIds: 0, total: 0 },
      changes: [{ kind: 'add_domain', domain: 'billing', name: 'Billing' }], rationale: 'new folder',
    };
    const extra: HarnessEvent[] = [
      ev(1, 'drift_detected', { signals: [{ signal: 'unassigned', metric: 'files in Unassigned', value: 3, threshold: 0, scope: ['unassigned'], persisted: 2 }] }),
      ev(2, 'map_proposed', { map: { ...before.map!, domains: [] }, yaml: '', proposal }),
      ev(3, 'labels_updated', { labels: [{ target: 'group:tools/logic/news', kind: 'group', text: 'News', hash: 'h', confirmed: false }] }),
      ev(4, 'audit_finding', { finding: { id: 'AF-1', decision: 'DR-4', files: ['src/a.ts'], lines: [{ path: 'src/a.ts', line: 3 }], text: 'x', confidence: 'high' } }),
      ev(5, 'map_proposal_resolved', { proposal: 'MP-1', outcome: 'rejected', decision: 'DR-9' }),
      ev(6, 'audit_resolved', { id: 'AF-1', outcome: 'dismissed' }),
      ev(7, 'maintenance_run', { agent: 'cartographer', trigger: 'unassigned', ms: 1200, cost: 0.4, ok: true }),
    ];
    const s = reduce([...events, ...extra]);
    expect(s.map!.domains.length).toBe(before.map!.domains.length); // not replaced by the candidate
    expect(s.proposals['MP-1']).toMatchObject({ status: 'rejected', decision: 'DR-9' });
    expect(s.drift[0]!.signal).toBe('unassigned');
    expect(s.labels['group:group:tools/logic/news']!.text).toBe('News');
    expect(s.findings['AF-1']!.status).toBe('dismissed');
    expect(s.maintenance).toHaveLength(1);
  });
});

import { check } from '../src/rules';
import { createMapper } from '../src/mapper';
import { domainEdges, fileExistsIn, scanRepo, withExtra } from '../src/facts';
import { planFootprint, type PlanStep } from '../src/plan';
import type { EventData, EventKind, HarnessEvent } from '../src/events';
import { fixtureRepo, loadMap } from './helpers';

/** Builds a realistic event log for the demo turn from real core computations over the fixture repo. */
export function demoLog() {
  const map = loadMap();
  const mapper = createMapper(map);
  const facts = scanRepo(fixtureRepo, map);
  const events: HarnessEvent[] = [];
  let turn: string | null = null;
  let n = 0;
  const ev = <K extends EventKind>(kind: K, data: K extends keyof EventData ? EventData[K] : never, extra: Partial<HarnessEvent> = {}) => {
    events.push({ id: `e${n}`, t: 1000 + n++, session: 's1', turn, kind, data: data as Record<string, unknown>, ...extra });
    return events.length - 1;
  };
  const cell = (path: string) => {
    const p = mapper.place(path);
    return p.kind === 'cell' ? { domain: p.domain, layer: p.layer } : undefined;
  };
  const plan = (steps: PlanStep[]) => {
    const fp = planFootprint(map, steps, withExtra(fileExistsIn(fixtureRepo), steps.flatMap((s) => s.files)), mapper);
    ev('planned', { steps, cells: fp.cells, edges: fp.edges, unassigned: fp.unassigned });
    for (const v of fp.violations) ev('plan_violation', { violation: v }, { path: v.file });
    return fp.violations;
  };
  const tenK = (model: string): PlanStep[] => [
    { n: 1, text: 'Add the 10-K tool', files: ['src/tools/filing-summary.ts'], imports: [{ from: 'src/tools/filing-summary.ts', to: model }] },
    { n: 2, text: 'Register it', files: ['src/tools/index.ts'], imports: [] },
  ];

  ev('map_confirmed', { map, source: 'file' });
  ev('repo_scanned', { files: facts.files.map((path) => ({ path, placement: mapper.place(path) })), imports: facts.imports, writes: facts.writes, edges: domainEdges(facts, mapper) });
  ev('violation_found', { violations: check(map, facts, mapper) });

  turn = 't1';
  ev('turn_started', { prompt: "Add a tool that summarizes a prospect's latest 10-K", head: 'abc', baseline: 'abc' });
  ev('looked', { tool: 'Read' }, { path: 'src/tools/news-summarize.ts', cell: cell('src/tools/news-summarize.ts') });
  ev('looked', { tool: 'Read' }, { path: 'src/gateway/complete.ts', cell: cell('src/gateway/complete.ts') });
  const violations = plan(tenK('vendor/llm-openai/index'));
  ev('fork_asked', { violations, text: 'A or B?' });
  ev('fork_answered', { option: 'A', text: 'A, through the gateway', violations });
  ev('decision_recorded', { id: 'DR-4', title: 'Filings go through the gateway', invariant: 'DR-1', option: 'A', paths: ['src/tools/filing-summary.ts'] });
  plan(tenK('src/gateway/complete'));
  ev('approval_requested', { plan: '1. add tool 2. register' });
  ev('plan_approved', {} as never);
  ev('file_assigned', { placement: mapper.place('src/tools/filing-summary.ts') }, { path: 'src/tools/filing-summary.ts' });
  const firstEdit = ev('edited', { added: 12, removed: 0, created: true }, { path: 'src/tools/filing-summary.ts', cell: { domain: 'tools', layer: 'logic' } });
  ev('edge_added', { edge: { from: 'src/tools/filing-summary.ts', to: 'src/gateway/complete.ts' }, from: 'tools', to: 'gateway' }, { path: 'src/tools/filing-summary.ts' });
  ev('edited', { added: 2, removed: 0, created: false }, { path: 'src/tools/index.ts', cell: { domain: 'tools', layer: 'logic' } });
  ev('edited', { added: 3, removed: 1, created: false }, { path: 'src/outreach/draft-email.ts', cell: { domain: 'outreach', layer: 'logic' } });
  ev('turn_ended', { added: 17, removed: 1, files: ['src/tools/filing-summary.ts', 'src/tools/index.ts', 'src/outreach/draft-email.ts'], reason: 'success' });
  turn = null;
  return { map, events, firstEdit };
}
// Shared fixture for the NAVIGATION_PLAN lanes: FileFacts for test/fixture-repo (mirrors Scout).
// Imports and writes come from the real scanner; symbols, calls and routes are hand-written for the files the
// demo turns touch, until the Facts lane's extractor replaces them (its tests must reproduce these).
import { scanRepo } from '../src/facts';
import type { FileFacts, SymbolFact, CallFact, RouteFact } from '../src/contracts/facts';
import { fixtureRepo, loadMap } from './helpers';

const sym = (file: string, name: string, kind: SymbolFact['kind'], exported = true, parent: string | null = null): SymbolFact => ({
  id: `${file}#${name}`, file, name, kind, exported, parent, span: { start: 0, end: 0 }, sigHash: `sig:${name}`, bodyHash: `body:${file}#${name}`,
});
const call = (from: string, to: string, confidence: CallFact['confidence'] = 'syntactic'): CallFact => ({ from, to, confidence, count: 1 });

const SYMBOLS: Record<string, SymbolFact[]> = {
  'src/tools/news-summarize.ts': [sym('src/tools/news-summarize.ts', 'newsSummarize', 'const'), sym('src/tools/news-summarize.ts', 'newsSummarize.run', 'method', false, 'src/tools/news-summarize.ts#newsSummarize')],
  'src/tools/company-profile.ts': [sym('src/tools/company-profile.ts', 'companyProfile', 'const'), sym('src/tools/company-profile.ts', 'companyProfile.run', 'method', false, 'src/tools/company-profile.ts#companyProfile')],
  'src/tools/index.ts': [sym('src/tools/index.ts', 'tools', 'const')],
  'src/gateway/complete.ts': [sym('src/gateway/complete.ts', 'complete', 'function')],
  'src/gateway/redact.ts': [sym('src/gateway/redact.ts', 'redact', 'function')],
  'src/gateway/providers.ts': [sym('src/gateway/providers.ts', 'provider', 'function')],
  'src/gateway/cost-ledger.ts': [sym('src/gateway/cost-ledger.ts', 'logCost', 'function')],
  'src/orchestrator/tool-registry.ts': [sym('src/orchestrator/tool-registry.ts', 'registry', 'const')],
  'src/orchestrator/agent.ts': [sym('src/orchestrator/agent.ts', 'runAgent', 'function')],
  'src/channels/routes.ts': [sym('src/channels/routes.ts', 'server', 'const')],
  'vendor/llm-openai/index.ts': [sym('vendor/llm-openai/index.ts', 'chat', 'function')],
  'vendor/news/index.ts': [sym('vendor/news/index.ts', 'call', 'function')],
  'vendor/enrichment/index.ts': [sym('vendor/enrichment/index.ts', 'call', 'function')],
  'vendor/sec-edgar/index.ts': [sym('vendor/sec-edgar/index.ts', 'call', 'function')],
};

const CALLS: Record<string, CallFact[]> = {
  'src/tools/news-summarize.ts': [
    call('src/tools/news-summarize.ts#newsSummarize.run', 'vendor/news/index.ts#call'),
    call('src/tools/news-summarize.ts#newsSummarize.run', 'vendor/llm-openai/index.ts#chat'),
  ],
  'src/tools/company-profile.ts': [
    call('src/tools/company-profile.ts#companyProfile.run', 'src/gateway/complete.ts#complete'),
    call('src/tools/company-profile.ts#companyProfile.run', 'vendor/enrichment/index.ts#call'),
    call('src/tools/company-profile.ts#companyProfile.run', 'vendor/sec-edgar/index.ts#call'),
  ],
  'src/gateway/complete.ts': [
    call('src/gateway/complete.ts#complete', 'src/gateway/redact.ts#redact'),
    call('src/gateway/complete.ts#complete', 'src/gateway/providers.ts#provider'),
    call('src/gateway/complete.ts#complete', 'src/gateway/cost-ledger.ts#logCost'),
  ],
  'src/channels/routes.ts': [call('src/channels/routes.ts#server', 'src/orchestrator/agent.ts#runAgent')],
};

const ROUTES: Record<string, RouteFact[]> = {
  'src/channels/routes.ts': [{ id: 'route:POST /runs', method: 'POST', path: '/runs', file: 'src/channels/routes.ts', handler: 'src/channels/routes.ts#server' }],
};

/** FileFacts for every code file in the fixture repo (hash = 'fixture'). */
export function scoutFacts(): Record<string, FileFacts> {
  const map = loadMap();
  const facts = scanRepo(fixtureRepo, map);
  const out: Record<string, FileFacts> = {};
  for (const path of facts.files.filter((f) => /\.(ts|tsx|js|mjs)$/.test(f))) {
    out[path] = {
      path,
      hash: 'fixture',
      imports: facts.imports.filter((i) => i.from === path).map((i) => ({ to: i.to, typeOnly: false })),
      writes: facts.writes.filter((w) => w.file === path).map((w) => ({ table: w.table, symbol: null, via: 'db' })),
      symbols: SYMBOLS[path] ?? [],
      calls: CALLS[path] ?? [],
      routes: ROUTES[path] ?? [],
      entries: path === 'src/channels/cli.ts' ? [{ id: 'entry:cli:scout', kind: 'cli', file: path, symbol: null, label: 'scout' }] : [],
    };
  }
  return out;
}
```

```text
import { create } from 'zustand';
import type { HarnessEvent } from '@harness/core/view';

export type Selection = { cell: string } | { edge: string; pair: string } | { unassigned: true };

export type Conn = 'connecting' | 'open' | 'down' | 'fake';

/**
 * The store holds the event log and purely ephemeral UI state. Everything the map, ledger, summary and chat show
 * is derived from `events` (see derive.ts); nothing here is a second copy of footprint, ghosts or ledger.
 */
type Store = {
  events: HarnessEvent[];
  /** null = live; otherwise the number of events to reduce (replay). */
  replay: number | null;
  /** Streaming assistant text not yet committed as a `chat` event. */
  delta: string;
  busy: boolean;
  conn: Conn;
  repo: string;
  draft: string;
  focusTick: number;
  selection: Selection | null;
  /** null = latest turn. */
  turn: string | null;
  hover: string | null;

  hello(events: HarnessEvent[], busy: boolean): void;
  append(e: HarnessEvent): void;
  addDelta(text: string): void;
  setBusy(b: boolean): void;
  setConn(c: Conn): void;
  setRepo(r: string): void;
  setDraft(d: string, focus?: boolean): void;
  select(s: Selection | null): void;
  setTurn(id: string | null): void;
  setReplay(i: number | null): void;
  setHover(h: string | null): void;
};

export const useStore = create<Store>((set) => ({
  events: [],
  replay: null,
  delta: '',
  busy: false,
  conn: 'connecting',
  repo: '',
  draft: '',
  focusTick: 0,
  selection: null,
  turn: null,
  hover: null,

  hello: (events, busy) => set({ events, busy, delta: '' }),
  append: (e) =>
    set((s) => {
      if (s.events.length && s.events[s.events.length - 1]!.id === e.id) return s;
      const clear = e.kind === 'chat' && (e.data as { role?: string } | undefined)?.role === 'assistant';
      return { events: [...s.events, e], ...(clear ? { delta: '' } : {}) };
    }),
  addDelta: (text) => set((s) => ({ delta: s.delta + text })),
  setBusy: (busy) => set(busy ? { busy } : { busy, delta: '' }),
  setConn: (conn) => set({ conn }),
  setRepo: (repo) => set({ repo }),
  setDraft: (draft, focus) => set((s) => ({ draft, focusTick: focus ? s.focusTick + 1 : s.focusTick })),
  select: (selection) => set({ selection }),
  setTurn: (turn) => set({ turn }),
  setReplay: (replay) => set({ replay }),
  setHover: (hover) => set({ hover }),
}));
import {
  cellKey, cellViews, edgeViews, ledger, reduce, turnLedger,
  type CellView, type EdgeView, type HarnessEvent, type Ledger, type TurnLedger, type TurnState, type UIState, type Violation,
} from '@harness/core/view';
import { useStore } from './store';

/** Everything the UI shows, as a pure function of (events, replay index, selected turn). */
export type View = {
  ui: UIState;
  upTo: number;
  live: boolean;
  turn: TurnState | null;
  turnIndex: number; // 1-based, 0 when no turn
  cells: Record<string, CellView>;
  edges: EdgeView[];
  ledger: Ledger;
  turnLedger: TurnLedger | null;
  /** cellKey → files placed there (product files only; tests are listed under their domain). */
  cellFiles: Record<string, string[]>;
  testFiles: Record<string, string[]>;
  unassigned: string[];
  proposal: { domains: number; rules: number } | null;
  steps: { done: number; total: number };
  turnStarts: number[];
};

let reduceCache: { events: readonly HarnessEvent[]; upTo: number; ui: UIState } | null = null;
let viewCache: { ui: UIState; turnSel: string | null; view: View } | null = null;

function reduced(events: readonly HarnessEvent[], upTo: number): UIState {
  if (reduceCache && reduceCache.events === events && reduceCache.upTo === upTo) return reduceCache.ui;
  const ui = reduce(events, upTo);
  reduceCache = { events, upTo, ui };
  return ui;
}

export function deriveView(events: readonly HarnessEvent[], replay: number | null, turnSel: string | null): View {
  const upTo = replay ?? events.length;
  const ui = reduced(events, upTo);
  if (viewCache && viewCache.ui === ui && viewCache.turnSel === turnSel) return viewCache.view;

  const turn = (turnSel && ui.turns.find((t) => t.id === turnSel)) || ui.turns.at(-1) || null;
  const cellFiles: Record<string, string[]> = {};
  const testFiles: Record<string, string[]> = {};
  const unassigned: string[] = [];
  for (const [path, p] of Object.entries(ui.files)) {
    if (p.kind === 'cell') (cellFiles[cellKey(p)] ??= []).push(path);
    else if (p.kind === 'test') (testFiles[p.domain] ??= []).push(path);
    else if (p.kind === 'unassigned') unassigned.push(path);
  }
  for (const list of Object.values(cellFiles)) list.sort();

  let proposed = -1;
  let confirmed = -1;
  const turnStarts: number[] = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < events.length; i++) {
    const k = events[i]!.kind;
    if (k === 'turn_started') turnStarts.push(i);
    if (i >= upTo) continue;
    if (k === 'map_proposed') proposed = i;
    if (k === 'map_confirmed') confirmed = i;
  }
  const proposal = proposed > confirmed && ui.map ? { domains: ui.map.domains.length, rules: ui.map.invariants.length } : null;

  const l = ledger(ui);
  const view: View = {
    ui,
    upTo,
    live: replay === null,
    turn,
    turnIndex: turn ? ui.turns.indexOf(turn) + 1 : 0,
    cells: cellViews(ui, turn?.id ?? null),
    edges: edgeViews(ui, turn?.id ?? null),
    ledger: l,
    turnLedger: turn ? turnLedger(ui, turn) : null,
    cellFiles,
    testFiles,
    unassigned,
    proposal,
    steps: turn ? stepProgress(turn) : { done: 0, total: 0 },
    turnStarts,
  };
  viewCache = { ui, turnSel, view };
  return view;
}

/** "3 of 6 steps": a step is done when every cell it plans has been edited (or, for a step with no cells, its files). */
function stepProgress(turn: TurnState) {
  const editedFiles = new Set([
    ...Object.values(turn.edited).flatMap((c) => c.files),
    ...Object.values(turn.tests).flat(),
    ...turn.unassigned,
  ]);
  let done = 0;
  for (const step of turn.steps) {
    const cells = Object.entries(turn.planned).filter(([, c]) => c.steps.includes(step.n)).map(([k]) => k);
    const ok = cells.length ? cells.every((k) => !!turn.edited[k]) : step.files.length > 0 && step.files.every((f) => editedFiles.has(f));
    if (ok) done++;
  }
  return { done, total: turn.steps.length };
}

export function useView(): View {
  const events = useStore((s) => s.events);
  const replay = useStore((s) => s.replay);
  const turnSel = useStore((s) => s.turn);
  return deriveView(events, replay, turnSel);
}

/** Violations relevant to the selected turn (load-time plus this turn's plan and gate), for the inspector. */
export function turnViolations(v: View): { v: Violation; source: 'load' | 'plan' | 'gate' }[] {
  const out: { v: Violation; source: 'load' | 'plan' | 'gate' }[] = v.ui.violations.map((x) => ({ v: x, source: 'load' as const }));
  for (const x of v.turn?.planViolations ?? []) out.push({ v: x, source: 'plan' });
  for (const x of v.turn?.gateBlocks ?? []) out.push({ v: x, source: 'gate' });
  return out;
}

export const basename = (p: string) => p.split('/').pop() ?? p;
export const stem = (p: string) => {
  const parts = p.split('/');
  const last = parts.pop() ?? p;
  // vendor/<name>/index.ts reads better as its folder name
  if (/^index\.[tj]sx?$/.test(last) && parts.length) return parts.pop()!;
  return last.replace(/\.[tj]sx?$/, '');
};
import { cellKey, type DomainMap, type EdgeView, type ImportEdge, type TurnState, type UIState, type Violation } from '@harness/core/view';

export type Rect = { x: number; y: number; w: number; h: number };

export type GridLayout = {
  width: number;
  height: number;
  labelW: number;
  headerH: number;
  gapX: number;
  gapY: number;
  colW: number;
  rowH: number;
  cols: { id: string; name: string; purpose: string; x: number; index: number }[];
  rows: { id: string; name: string; y: number; index: number }[];
  cells: Record<string, Rect & { col: number; row: number }>;
  unassigned: Rect | null;
};

/** Fixed grid: a gutter on both sides of every column and row, so edges can route around cells. */
export function gridLayout(map: DomainMap, size: { w: number; h: number }, withUnassigned: boolean): GridLayout {
  const labelW = 64;
  const headerH = 46;
  const n = map.domains.length + (withUnassigned ? 1 : 0);
  const r = map.layers.length;
  const gapX = Math.max(28, Math.min(44, size.w * 0.032));
  const gapY = 26;
  const colW = Math.max(96, (size.w - labelW - gapX * (n + 1)) / n);
  const rowH = Math.max(72, Math.min(150, (size.h - headerH - gapY * (r + 1)) / r));
  const colX = (i: number) => labelW + gapX + i * (colW + gapX);
  const rowY = (j: number) => headerH + gapY + j * (rowH + gapY);
  const cols = map.domains.map((d, i) => ({ id: d.id, name: d.name, purpose: d.purpose, x: colX(i), index: i }));
  const rows = map.layers.map((l, j) => ({ id: l.id, name: l.name, y: rowY(j), index: j }));
  const cells: GridLayout['cells'] = {};
  map.domains.forEach((d, i) => {
    map.layers.forEach((l, j) => {
      if (l.id in d.cells) cells[cellKey({ domain: d.id, layer: l.id })] = { x: colX(i), y: rowY(j), w: colW, h: rowH, col: i, row: j };
    });
  });
  const unassigned = withUnassigned ? { x: colX(n - 1), y: rowY(0), w: colW, h: rowY(r - 1) + rowH - rowY(0) } : null;
  if (withUnassigned) cols.push({ id: '__unassigned', name: 'Unassigned', purpose: 'Files that match no cell in domains.yaml', x: colX(n - 1), index: n - 1 });
  return {
    width: labelW + gapX * (n + 1) + colW * n,
    height: headerH + gapY * (r + 1) + rowH * r,
    labelW, headerH, gapX, gapY, colW, rowH, cols, rows, cells, unassigned,
  };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- edges

export type EdgeSegment = {
  key: string; // stable React key
  edgeKey: string; // `${from}->${to}`
  pair: string; // `${srcCell}=>${dstCell}`
  from: string;
  to: string;
  src: string; // cellKey
  dst: string; // cellKey
  state: EdgeView['state'];
  violation: boolean;
  steps: number[];
  files: ImportEdge[];
};

/** Which cell a file sits in: its placement, else the cell a plan put it in. */
function cellForFile(s: UIState, turn: TurnState | null, file: string): string | null {
  const p = s.files[file];
  if (p?.kind === 'cell') return cellKey(p);
  const planned = turn && Object.values(turn.planned).find((c) => c.files.includes(file));
  return planned ? cellKey(planned.cell) : null;
}

function fallbackCell(map: DomainMap, domain: string): string | null {
  const d = map.domains.find((x) => x.id === domain);
  const layer = d && map.layers.find((l) => l.id in d.cells);
  return d && layer ? cellKey({ domain, layer: layer.id }) : null;
}

/**
 * Splits each domain edge from `edgeViews` into one segment per (source cell, target cell) pair, so a gateway
 * bypass to the provider (tools·logic → gateway·external) is drawn apart from calls to complete() (→ gateway·logic).
 * The edge's `violation` flag is kept only on the segments whose files are the violating imports.
 */
export function edgeSegments(s: UIState, turn: TurnState | null, edges: EdgeView[]): EdgeSegment[] {
  const map = s.map;
  if (!map) return [];
  const out: EdgeSegment[] = [];
  for (const e of edges) {
    const groups = new Map<string, { src: string; dst: string; files: ImportEdge[] }>();
    for (const f of e.files.length ? e.files : [{ from: '', to: '' }]) {
      const src = (f.from && cellForFile(s, turn, f.from)) || fallbackCell(map, e.from);
      const dst = (f.to && cellForFile(s, turn, f.to)) || fallbackCell(map, e.to);
      if (!src || !dst) continue;
      const k = `${src}=>${dst}`;
      const g = groups.get(k) ?? { src, dst, files: [] };
      if (f.from) g.files.push(f);
      groups.set(k, g);
    }
    const list: Violation[] = e.state === 'ghost' ? turn?.planViolations ?? [] : s.violations;
    const added = turn?.edgesAdded ?? [];
    for (const [pair, g] of groups) {
      const violation = e.violation && (groups.size === 1 || g.files.some((f) => list.some((v) => v.file === f.from && (!v.target || v.target === f.to))));
      const edgeKey = `${e.from}->${e.to}`;
      // `new` is per domain pair in edgeViews; only the cell pairs whose imports were added this turn draw in as new.
      const state = e.state === 'new' && !g.files.some((f) => added.some((a) => a.edge.from === f.from && a.edge.to === f.to)) ? 'existing' : e.state;
      out.push({ key: `${state}:${pair}`, edgeKey, pair, from: e.from, to: e.to, src: g.src, dst: g.dst, state, violation, steps: e.steps, files: g.files });
    }
  }
  // Existing edges first, then new, then ghosts: lanes are assigned in this order and stay stable as a turn adds edges.
  const rank = { existing: 0, new: 1, ghost: 2 } as const;
  return out.sort((a, b) => rank[a.state] - rank[b.state] || a.key.localeCompare(b.key));
}

type Pt = [number, number];

/** Alternating lane offsets around a gutter's center: 0, +s, −s, +2s, … */
const lane = (i: number, s: number) => (i === 0 ? 0 : (i % 2 ? 1 : -1) * Math.ceil(i / 2) * s);

export type RoutedSegment = EdgeSegment & { d: string; length: number };

/** Orthogonal routes through the gutters, with a separate lane per segment in every gutter it uses. */
export function routeEdges(L: GridLayout, segs: EdgeSegment[]): RoutedSegment[] {
  const used = new Map<string, number>();
  const take = (k: string) => {
    const n = used.get(k) ?? 0;
    used.set(k, n + 1);
    return n;
  };
  const colGutterX = (g: number) => L.labelW + g * (L.colW + L.gapX) + L.gapX / 2;
  const rowGutterY = (g: number) => L.headerH + g * (L.rowH + L.gapY) + L.gapY / 2;
  const laneX = Math.min(7, L.gapX / 6);
  const laneY = Math.min(6, L.gapY / 5);
  const out: RoutedSegment[] = [];

  for (const seg of segs) {
    const S = L.cells[seg.src];
    const T = L.cells[seg.dst];
    if (!S || !T || S === T) continue;
    const dir = T.col > S.col ? 1 : T.col < S.col ? -1 : 0;
    let pts: Pt[];
    const sideY = (c: typeof S, port: string) => c.y + c.h / 2 + lane(take(`port:${port}`), 9);
    if (dir === 0) {
      // Same column (only possible for odd placements): loop out through the right gutter.
      const gx = colGutterX(S.col + 1) + lane(take(`col:${S.col + 1}`), laneX);
      const ey = sideY(S, `${seg.src}:r`);
      const ty = sideY(T, `${seg.dst}:r`);
      pts = [[S.x + S.w, ey], [gx, ey], [gx, ty], [T.x + T.w, ty]];
    } else {
      const sx = dir > 0 ? S.x + S.w : S.x;
      const tx = dir > 0 ? T.x : T.x + T.w;
      const gS = dir > 0 ? S.col + 1 : S.col;
      const gT = dir > 0 ? T.col : T.col + 1;
      const ey = sideY(S, `${seg.src}:${dir > 0 ? 'r' : 'l'}`);
      const ty = sideY(T, `${seg.dst}:${dir > 0 ? 'l' : 'r'}`);
      if (gS === gT) {
        if (S.row === T.row) {
          const y = (ey + ty) / 2;
          pts = [[sx, y], [tx, y]];
        } else {
          const gx = colGutterX(gS) + lane(take(`col:${gS}`), laneX);
          pts = [[sx, ey], [gx, ey], [gx, ty], [tx, ty]];
        }
      } else {
        let rg: number;
        if (T.row > S.row) rg = S.row + 1;
        else if (T.row < S.row) rg = S.row;
        else rg = (used.get(`row:${S.row + 1}`) ?? 0) <= (used.get(`row:${S.row}`) ?? 0) ? S.row + 1 : S.row;
        const gy = rowGutterY(rg) + lane(take(`row:${rg}`), laneY);
        const gx1 = colGutterX(gS) + lane(take(`col:${gS}`), laneX);
        const gx2 = colGutterX(gT) + lane(take(`col:${gT}`), laneX);
        pts = [[sx, ey], [gx1, ey], [gx1, gy], [gx2, gy], [gx2, ty], [tx, ty]];
      }
    }
    const { d, length } = roundedPath(pts, 7);
    out.push({ ...seg, d, length });
  }
  return out;
}

function roundedPath(pts: Pt[], r: number) {
  let length = 0;
  for (let i = 1; i < pts.length; i++) length += Math.hypot(pts[i]![0] - pts[i - 1]![0], pts[i]![1] - pts[i - 1]![1]);
  let d = `M${pts[0]![0].toFixed(1)},${pts[0]![1].toFixed(1)}`;
  for (let i = 1; i < pts.length - 1; i++) {
    const [px, py] = pts[i - 1]!;
    const [cx, cy] = pts[i]!;
    const [nx, ny] = pts[i + 1]!;
    const d1 = Math.hypot(cx - px, cy - py);
    const d2 = Math.hypot(nx - cx, ny - cy);
    const rr = Math.min(r, d1 / 2, d2 / 2);
    if (rr < 0.5) {
      d += `L${cx.toFixed(1)},${cy.toFixed(1)}`;
      continue;
    }
    const ax = cx - ((cx - px) / d1) * rr;
    const ay = cy - ((cy - py) / d1) * rr;
    const bx = cx + ((nx - cx) / d2) * rr;
    const by = cy + ((ny - cy) / d2) * rr;
    d += `L${ax.toFixed(1)},${ay.toFixed(1)}Q${cx.toFixed(1)},${cy.toFixed(1)} ${bx.toFixed(1)},${by.toFixed(1)}`;
  }
  const last = pts[pts.length - 1]!;
  d += `L${last[0].toFixed(1)},${last[1].toFixed(1)}`;
  return { d, length };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- invariants

/** Glob → RegExp for the subset domains.yaml uses (`**`, `*`, `?`). */
export function globRe(glob: string): RegExp {
  let re = '';
  for (let i = 0; i < glob.length; i++) {
    const c = glob[i]!;
    if (c === '*' && glob[i + 1] === '*') {
      if (glob[i + 2] === '/') { re += '(?:.*/)?'; i += 2; } else { re += '.*'; i++; }
    } else if (c === '*') re += '[^/]*';
    else if (c === '?') re += '[^/]';
    else re += c.replace(/[.+^${}()|[\]\\]/g, '\\$&');
  }
  return new RegExp(`^${re}$`);
}

/** Invariants that involve a domain (and, for `only_via`, files of a given cell). */
export function invariantsFor(map: DomainMap, domain: string, files: string[]) {
  return map.invariants.filter((inv) => {
    if (inv.kind === 'only_via') return inv.allowed_from.includes(domain) || files.some((f) => inv.targets.some((t) => globRe(t).test(f)));
    if (inv.kind === 'owns_writes') return Object.values(inv.owners).includes(domain);
    return inv.from === domain || inv.to === domain;
  });
}
import { useEffect, useRef, useState } from 'react';

export const reducedMotion = () => typeof matchMedia !== 'undefined' && matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches;

/** Counts up (or down) to `value` over ~400 ms whenever it changes. */
export function useTween(value: number, ms = 400): number {
  const [shown, setShown] = useState(value);
  const from = useRef(value);
  useEffect(() => {
    if (reducedMotion() || from.current === value) {
      from.current = value;
      setShown(value);
      return;
    }
    const start = performance.now();
    const a = from.current;
    let raf = 0;
    const step = (now: number) => {
      const k = Math.min(1, (now - start) / ms);
      const eased = 1 - (1 - k) ** 3;
      setShown(Math.round(a + (value - a) * eased));
      if (k < 1) raf = requestAnimationFrame(step);
      else from.current = value;
    };
    raf = requestAnimationFrame(step);
    return () => {
      cancelAnimationFrame(raf);
      from.current = value;
    };
  }, [value, ms]);
  return shown;
}

/** True for a moment after `key` changes (not on mount). */
export function useFlash(key: unknown, ms = 650): boolean {
  const [on, setOn] = useState(false);
  const first = useRef(true);
  useEffect(() => {
    if (first.current) {
      first.current = false;
      return;
    }
    setOn(true);
    const t = setTimeout(() => setOn(false), ms);
    return () => clearTimeout(t);
  }, [key, ms]);
  return on;
}

export function useSize<T extends HTMLElement>() {
  const ref = useRef<T>(null);
  const [size, setSize] = useState({ w: 0, h: 0 });
  useEffect(() => {
    const el = ref.current;
    if (!el) return;
    const ro = new ResizeObserver(([e]) => {
      if (e) setSize({ w: e.contentRect.width, h: e.contentRect.height });
    });
    ro.observe(el);
    return () => ro.disconnect();
  }, []);
  return [ref, size] as const;
}
```
</details></tool-use>

````text
# Harness

A diagram-first shell around real Claude Code: chat on the left, a live domain × layer map of the target repo on the right, and a gate that makes the agent ask before it crosses an architecture rule. **Read `SPEC.md` before starting**, and follow its build order (§13), starting with the verification step.

## Rules

- **No model calls in the hot path.** Hooks, the mapper, the import parser and the rule checker must be deterministic and fast. The only model call Harness makes itself is the cartographer, and it never blocks the coding session.
- **UI state is a pure reduction of the event log** (`packages/core/src/events.ts`). Don't keep separate mutable state for footprint, ghosts, ledger or replay.
- **The rule checker is one function with three call sites** (load scan, `submit_plan`, edit hook). Don't fork its logic.
- **Harness writes to the target repo only** in `domains.yaml`, `decisions/` and `.harness/`. Product code in the target is edited only by the coding session.
- **Don't guess Agent SDK APIs.** Check https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/typescript and https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/hooks.
- TypeScript strict. `packages/core` has vitest tests for the mapper, import parser, write scanner, checker, plan mapping and ledger, all against `fixtures/scout-agent.domains.yaml`.
- Local only: no auth, no deployment, no database.

## Commands

```
npm i
HARNESS_REPO=../scout-agent npm run dev    # server :4310, shell :5173
npm test                                   # packages/core
```

## Context

- The target repo is built separately from `DEMO_REPO_SPEC.md`. Until it exists, test core against a small fixture repo under `packages/core/test/fixture-repo/` that mirrors its layout, including the one gateway bypass in `src/tools/news-summarize.ts`.
- Visual reference: Figma file "Diagram-first harness — product mockup", page "v2 · Domain grid".
- The demo is about time saved: keep the ledger counters exact (SPEC §9) and never display estimated minutes in the UI.
# Harness: build spec

**Text in, architecture out.** Harness is a diagram-first shell around real Claude Code. You talk to the agent in a chat pane; a domain × layer map of the target repo shows, live, what each turn plans and does to the architecture; and the agent stops to ask you before it crosses a rule. Decisions you make become rules that later sessions are checked against.

The theme is giving people time back. Agents made writing code nearly free, but understanding and checking it did not get cheaper. Every feature below exists to cut reading, rework or re-explaining, and the time ledger counts those savings.

## 1. Repos

Two separate git repos, side by side:

```
workspace/
  harness/        this tool (npm workspaces monorepo)
  scout-agent/    the demo target, built separately from DEMO_REPO_SPEC.md
```

The target must be its own repo. The coding agent runs with its working directory there, the map is computed over it, and `domains.yaml` plus `decisions/` are committed into it. The tool's own code must never appear on the map.

```
harness/
  package.json              npm workspaces
  packages/core/            pure TypeScript, no I/O beyond fs reads; fully unit-tested
    src/schema.ts           zod schema for domains.yaml
    src/events.ts           event types and the reducer
    src/mapper.ts           path → cell, table → owner
    src/imports.ts          regex import parser + relative-path resolver
    src/writes.ts           db.insert / db.update scanner
    src/facts.ts            whole-repo scan: files, imports, writes, cross-domain edges
    src/rules.ts            the invariant checker (one function, three call sites)
    src/plan.ts             plan → ghost footprint
    src/ledger.ts           per-turn and session counters
    test/                   uses fixtures/scout-agent.domains.yaml
  apps/server/              Node + Hono + ws + @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk
    src/index.ts            HTTP + websocket; serves the shell in production
    src/bus.ts              append-only event log (.harness/events.jsonl in the target) + broadcast
    src/repo.ts             load, full scan, file watcher
    src/session.ts          the coding session (streaming input, modes, hooks, canUseTool)
    src/harness-tools.ts    in-process MCP server: submit_plan, cell_for, domain, who_writes, decisions_for
    src/turns.ts            turn lifecycle, git baselines, turn records
    src/decisions.ts        decisions/DR-n.md, invariant updates, Alike instructions
    src/cartographer.ts     one-shot map proposal
  apps/shell/               Vite + React + Zustand
  fixtures/scout-agent.domains.yaml
```

Run: `HARNESS_REPO=../scout-agent npm run dev` (server on 4310, shell on 5173).

## 2. Hard rules

1. **No model calls in the hot path.** Hooks, the mapper, the import parser and the rule checker are deterministic and fast. Model calls (the cartographer) never block the coding session.
2. **Every piece of UI state is a pure reduction of the event log.** Footprint, ghosts, ledger, summary, provenance and replay are all `reduce(events)`. Replay is "reduce up to index i".
3. **Harness writes to the target repo only in three places:** `domains.yaml`, `decisions/`, `.harness/` (gitignored). The coding session is the only thing that edits product code.
4. **Facts win on structure, the user wins on meaning, the agent wins only on stated intent**, and intent is always checked against facts.

## 3. The map (`domains.yaml`)

Schema: see `fixtures/scout-agent.domains.yaml`. Domains are columns, layers are rows (rows come from the file, not hard-coded). Each cell lists path globs and, for data cells, owned tables. `neutral` paths never create edges; `ignore` paths are skipped. Files that match no cell land in an **Unassigned** column.

**Tests** are assigned to a domain by its `tests` globs. A test file counts as part of that domain for the rule checker's import rules and the footprint and is listed in the inspector, but it is not drawn in a cell and draws no edges. Tests may write any table: seeding fixture rows is setup, not a product write, so `owns_writes` skips them.

**Edges are derived, never declared.** A cross-domain edge exists when a file in domain A imports a file in domain B. Flow down a column is implied and not drawn. The import parser handles `import … from '…'`, `import('…')` and `export … from '…'`. It resolves relative paths by trying the specifier as written, then `.ts`, `.tsx`, `/index.ts`, `/index.tsx`, and maps a `.js` specifier to `.ts`. It ignores bare package and `node:` imports (Scout has none that matter).

**Writes:** a regex scan for `db.insert(` and `db.update(` followed by a string literal in any quote style gives `{file, table}` pairs.

## 4. Invariants: one checker, three call sites

```ts
type Violation = { invariant: string; reason: string; file: string; detail: string; options: [string, string] };
function check(map: DomainMap, delta: FactDelta): Violation[];
```

`FactDelta` is a set of added imports and added writes, each with its source file. The three kinds:

| Kind | Fires when |
| --- | --- |
| `only_via` | a file outside `allowed_from` domains imports a `targets` path |
| `owns_writes` | a file outside the owner domain writes the table |
| `no_edge` | a file in `from` imports a file in `to` |

Exceptions (paths) suppress a violation. Each violation carries two options: **A** comply (for `only_via` on Scout: "route through `gateway.complete()`"), **B** add an exception for this path and record why.

The three call sites, all using the same function:

1. **Load:** full repo scan. On Scout, finds exactly one: DR-1 in `src/tools/news-summarize.ts`. It shows red on load.
2. **Plan:** run on the declared dependencies and files in `submit_plan`.
3. **Edit:** run in the `PreToolUse` hook on the imports and writes that the edit would add (diff the `new_string`/`content` against the current file).

## 5. Events

```ts
type HarnessEvent = {
  id: string; t: number;
  session: string;          // coding session id
  turn: string | null;
  kind:
    | 'repo_scanned' | 'map_proposed' | 'map_confirmed' | 'file_assigned'
    | 'violation_found'
    | 'turn_started' | 'looked' | 'cursor'
    | 'planned' | 'plan_violation' | 'fork_asked' | 'fork_answered' | 'plan_approved'
    | 'gate_blocked' | 'edited' | 'edge_added' | 'edge_removed'
    | 'test_result' | 'decision_recorded' | 'turn_ended';
  cell?: { domain: string; layer: string };
  path?: string;
  data?: Record<string, unknown>;   // e.g. { step: 2 }, { added: 18, removed: 2 }, { invariant: 'DR-1' }
};
```

The server appends every event to `.harness/events.jsonl` and broadcasts it over the websocket. The shell holds the array and derives everything from it.

## 6. The coding session

One long-lived streaming session:

```ts
query({
  prompt: chatMessages(),                     // AsyncIterable<SDKUserMessage> fed by the chat pane
  options: {
    cwd: REPO,
    permissionMode: 'plan',
    systemPrompt: { type: 'preset', preset: 'claude_code', append: brief() },
    mcpServers: { harness: harnessTools },    // createSdkMcpServer; user-scope MCP servers (Alike) still load
    allowedTools: ['mcp__harness__*', 'mcp__alike__record_decision', 'mcp__alike__resolve_work_item', 'mcp__alike__describe_entity_kind'],
    hooks: { PreToolUse: [...], PostToolUse: [...] },
    canUseTool,                                // intercepts ExitPlanMode for approval
  },
});
```

**`brief()`** contains: the map (domains, purposes, cell paths), every standing decision from `decisions/` (with the invariant it qualifies and the option it rejected), and these rules:

> Before editing anything, call `mcp__harness__submit_plan` with numbered steps. Each step lists the exact file paths it will create or modify and any new imports it adds (from path → to path). If the result contains violations, stop and ask the user to choose between the two options it gives, in one short message, then wait. Never work around a violation. After the user answers, resubmit the plan, then exit plan mode.

The brief does **not** list the seeded invariants (`source: cartographer`). They are enforced at plan and edit time instead. Stated up front, they would make the agent comply silently, so the user never sees the choice and nothing gets recorded. Once the user answers a fork, the resulting decision is in every later brief, and the next session follows it without asking. That contrast, asked once and then remembered, is the memory beat of the demo.

**Turn flow:**

1. User message → `turn_started` (record `git rev-parse HEAD` and a `git stash create` snapshot as the baseline).
2. Plan mode: Claude reads (`looked`, `cursor`), then calls `submit_plan`. The server maps paths to cells, builds ghost cells and ghost edges, and runs the checker → `planned` (+ `plan_violation`). The tool result returns the ghost summary and, if violated, the reason plus options A/B with an instruction to ask.
3. Claude asks → `fork_asked`. The user answers in chat → `fork_answered` → decision written (§8). Claude resubmits.
4. Claude calls `ExitPlanMode` → `canUseTool` holds it, the shell shows an **Approve plan** button (typing "approve" also works) → `plan_approved` → allow, then `session.setPermissionMode('acceptEdits')`.
5. Edits: hooks emit `cursor`, `gate_blocked`, `edited`, `edge_added` / `edge_removed`. Ghost cells fill as their files are edited; the step counter advances.
6. Result message → `turn_ended` with the plan-versus-built diff and git `--numstat` totals; write `.harness/turns/<id>.json`; `setPermissionMode('plan')` for the next turn.

**Hooks:**

| Hook | Matcher | Does | Blocking |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| PreToolUse | `Read\|Grep\|Glob` | `looked` + `cursor` for the file or search path | no (return `{ async: true }`) |
| PreToolUse | `Edit\|Write\|MultiEdit` | run the checker on the added imports/writes; on a hit return `permissionDecision: 'deny'` with the reason, options and "ask the user"; emit `gate_blocked` | yes, deterministic, < 20 ms |
| PostToolUse | `Edit\|Write\|MultiEdit` | `edited` (+/− lines), recompute that file's imports → edge events | no |
| PostToolUse | `Bash` | if the command ran `vitest`, parse results → `test_result` per test domain (stretch) | no |

**File watcher** (chokidar on the target, minus `ignore`): any write not already reported by a hook becomes an `edited` event marked `unattributed`. Hooks give attribution and gating; the watcher guarantees completeness, since shell commands can write files without passing through the edit hooks.

**Harness MCP tools** (all read-only except `submit_plan`, which only records intent): `submit_plan(steps[{ n, text, files[], imports[{ from, to }] }])`, `cell_for(path)`, `domain(id)`, `who_writes(table)`, `decisions_for(paths[])`.

## 7. Plan versus built

- **Ghosts:** planned cells are drawn dashed with their step numbers; planned edges are dashed; a ghost that violates an invariant is red.
- **Fill-in:** a ghost cell turns solid when a file mapped to it is edited.
- **End-of-turn diff:** planned and done is solid; planned and not done stays a ghost; **done but not planned is amber**, which is how the map shows the agent straying from its own plan.
- **New versus existing violations:** a violation found on load is drawn red, with a badge on its cell counting the files involved. A violation raised by this turn's plan or edits must look different from the map before the turn, even when it repeats an existing one (on Scout, the 10-K plan copies `news-summarize.ts` into the same red cell and toward the same provider). Its ghost edge gets its own lane, offset from any solid edge between the same cells, and the cell gets a separate **new** badge naming the file.

## 8. Design memory

When a fork is answered:

1. Write `decisions/DR-<n>.md` with front matter `{ id, title, outcome, status: made, type: standing, invariant, anchors: { paths }, rejected: "<option B text>" }` and a short rationale body.
2. Update `domains.yaml`: link the decision to the invariant (option A), or add the path to the invariant's `exceptions` with the DR id (option B). Commit both files and only those (`git commit -- domains.yaml decisions/DR-<n>.md`), so the coding session's uncommitted edits stay out of the commit.
3. Tell Claude, in the next tool result, to record it in Alike with `mcp__alike__record_decision`, giving it the exact arguments: `title`, `outcome`, `rationale` (including the rejected option), `decision_type: standing`, `status: made`, and one path anchor per governed file, `{ kind: path, label: governs, path, repository: owner/name }` (field names checked with `describe_entity_kind`, see VERIFY.md). Emit `decision_recorded` when the call succeeds.

Memory is then used three ways:

- **Provenance:** clicking an edge or cell shows the decisions and turns behind it ("added in turn 3, DR-4").
- **Session brief:** every standing decision goes into `brief()` for every new session (§6).
- **Rejected options stay rejected:** when a plan or edit hits an invariant that has a linked decision, the violation reason says "You decided this in DR-4: <title>," and the ledger counts it as a rejected option blocked.

## 9. Time ledger and turn summary

Counts only; minutes appear only in the pitch, taken from the baseline run (§12).

| Counter | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Lines changed | git `--numstat` added + removed, turn baseline → turn end |
| Cells to review | cells with a finding of severity 1–3 below |
| Forks caught before code | `plan_violation` events resolved before any `edited` event in the turn |
| Rejected options blocked | violations that cited an existing decision |

Severity for the turn summary, loudest first: **1** invariant hit (red) · **2** new cross-domain edge or new external (amber, one glance) · **3** unplanned edit (amber) · **4** everything else in the plan (quiet).

## 10. Load and the cartographer

1. `repo_scanned`: full fact scan (§3).
2. If `domains.yaml` is missing, run the **cartographer**: a separate one-shot `query()` with read-only tools, a smaller model, and `outputFormat` set to the `domains.yaml` JSON schema. Input: the file tree, the import edges and the table writes. Ask it for 5–9 domains in product language, layers suited to the repo, and invariants it can infer from the facts (sole importers of a vendor, sole writers of a table, absent edges). → `map_proposed`.
3. The shell plays the map assembling (`file_assigned` events, staggered about 15 ms apart) and shows the proposal; the user clicks **Confirm** → `map_confirmed`, file written. If the proposal is off, load `fixtures/scout-agent.domains.yaml` instead.
4. Full rule scan → `violation_found` (Scout: DR-1 in `news-summarize.ts`, red).

## 11. The shell

- **Layout:** chat pane on the left (380 px); the grid fills the rest; the turn summary and replay scrubber sit under the grid; the ledger sits top right. The mockups are in Figma, "v2 · Domain grid" page.
- **Cell states:** looked = dashed indigo outline · edited = indigo fill · unplanned = amber · invariant hit = red · ghost = dashed outline at 50% opacity with step badges.
- **Agent cursor:** a small avatar pinned to the current cell, labeled "Claude · reading `retrieve.ts`", easing between cells in 250 ms.
- **Edges:** SVG overlay routed through the gaps between cells; new edges draw in with a stroke-dashoffset animation.
- **Diff counts:** a +/− badge on each edited cell, ticking up.
- **Inspector:** click a cell or edge to see its paths, tables, invariants and provenance.
- **Replay:** a scrubber over the event index; dragging re-reduces the log.
- **Motion rule:** animate only state changes; nothing loops.

## 12. Baseline run, for the pitch

Copy `scout-agent` at the demo commit. In plain Claude Code, run "Add a tool that summarizes a prospect's latest 10-K." Time it, then run `npm run proof`. If the new tool leaks personal data, time a follow-up turn that finds and fixes it. Those minutes are the "without" numbers the pitch converts the ledger into. If the baseline doesn't make the mistake, drop that comparison and lean on lines-to-review and memory.

## 13. Build order and acceptance checks

| # | Build | Done when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **Verify first** (30 min) | (a) a custom MCP tool can be called in plan mode; (b) `canUseTool` receives `ExitPlanMode`; (c) after a hook deny with "ask the user," Claude asks instead of retrying; (d) the Alike MCP login from Claude Code is available inside an SDK session. Write results in `VERIFY.md`. Fallbacks: (a) require the plan as a fenced JSON block in the `ExitPlanMode` plan text and parse it; (b) approve via a chat message and switch mode on the next message. |
| 1 | `packages/core` | Unit tests pass; scanning Scout (or a small fixture copy until it exists) finds exactly one violation, DR-1 in `src/tools/news-summarize.ts`, and none in test files. The fixture covers extensionless, `.js` and directory-index imports. |
| 2 | Server + chat pane | Chatting with Claude Code from the browser works, with responses streaming. |
| 3 | Grid from the fixture map | Grid renders Scout with derived cross-domain edges; the DR-1 cell is red. |
| 4 | Live footprint | Reads move the cursor and mark cells; edits fill cells; a new import draws a new edge. |
| 5 | Plan flow | "Add a tool that summarizes a prospect's latest 10-K. Do it the way news-summarize does, so the figures come through exactly." produces ghosts (the bare prompt usually goes through the gateway with no fork; this one forked 3 of 3 on Scout); a gateway bypass in the plan shows red, distinct from the existing DR-1 edge, and Claude asks A/B; answering, approving and building fills the ghosts; anything unplanned ends amber. If Claude plans through the gateway without noticing that redaction mangles the filing's figures, the fork can't happen: note it in `VERIFY.md` and fall back to the edit gate, which fires when it reaches for the provider during the build. |
| 6 | Edit gate | An edit that adds a forbidden import is denied and Claude asks. |
| 7 | Memory | Answering writes the DR file and updates `domains.yaml`; Alike `record_decision` succeeds; edge provenance shows the DR; a fresh session asked to "add a tool that summarizes earnings call transcripts" (served by `vendor/news`) either follows DR-4 without asking, citing it, or gets blocked with "You decided this in DR-4." |
| 8 | Ledger, summary, replay | Counters match §9; the scrubber replays a full turn. |
| 9 | Cartographer + load animation | Loading Scout without `domains.yaml` proposes a usable map and DR-1 to DR-3; confirm writes the file. |
| 10 | Polish | Edge draw-in, easing, empty and error states. Record the backup video and the baseline run. |

## 14. Not today

Gestures, the editor extension, adapters for other agents, multiplayer, Keewano, Sparta, Graphify, the journeys and wiring-trace levels, cartographer drift triggers, scope inference from the prompt.
````

```text
import * as fs from 'node:fs';
import { normalizePath, parseImports, resolveImport } from './imports';
import { createMapper, type Mapper } from './mapper';
import type { DomainMap } from './schema';
import { scanWrites } from './writes';

/** File → file import. */
export type ImportEdge = { from: string; to: string };
export type WriteFact = { file: string; table: string };
/** Cross-domain dependency (domain ids) with the file imports behind it. */
export type DomainEdge = { from: string; to: string; files: ImportEdge[] };
export type Facts = { files: string[]; imports: ImportEdge[]; writes: WriteFact[] };
export type FactDelta = { imports: ImportEdge[]; writes: WriteFact[] };

export type Exists = (path: string) => boolean;

export const CODE_EXTENSIONS = ['.ts', '.tsx', '.js', '.jsx', '.mjs', '.cjs', '.mts'];

export function isCodeFile(path: string): boolean {
  return CODE_EXTENSIONS.some((ext) => path.endsWith(ext));
}

/** File-existence check against a repo root, cached. Call `clear()` after files are created or deleted. */
export function fileExistsIn(root: string): Exists & { clear(): void } {
  const cache = new Map<string, boolean>();
  const exists = (path: string) => {
    let hit = cache.get(path);
    if (hit === undefined) {
      try {
        hit = fs.statSync(`${root}/${path}`).isFile();
      } catch {
        hit = false;
      }
      cache.set(path, hit);
    }
    return hit;
  };
  return Object.assign(exists, { clear: () => cache.clear() });
}

/** `exists`, plus `paths` that will exist (e.g. files a plan creates). */
export function withExtra(exists: Exists, paths: readonly string[]): Exists {
  const extra = new Set(paths.map((p) => normalizePath(p) ?? p));
  return (path) => extra.has(path) || exists(path);
}

/** Full fact scan of a repo: every non-ignored file, plus resolved imports and table writes of code files. */
export function scanRepo(root: string, map: DomainMap): Facts {
  const mapper = createMapper(map);
  const files: string[] = [];
  const walk = (dir: string) => {
    for (const entry of fs.readdirSync(dir ? `${root}/${dir}` : root, { withFileTypes: true })) {
      if (entry.name === 'node_modules' || entry.name === '.git') continue;
      const path = dir ? `${dir}/${entry.name}` : entry.name;
      if (mapper.isIgnored(path)) continue;
      if (entry.isDirectory()) walk(path);
      else if (entry.isFile()) files.push(path);
    }
  };
  walk('');
  files.sort();

  const known = new Set(files);
  const onDisk = fileExistsIn(root);
  const exists: Exists = (p) => known.has(p) || onDisk(p);
  const imports: ImportEdge[] = [];
  const writes: WriteFact[] = [];
  for (const file of files) {
    if (!isCodeFile(file)) continue;
    const delta = factsForSource(file, fs.readFileSync(`${root}/${file}`, 'utf8'), exists);
    imports.push(...delta.imports);
    writes.push(...delta.writes);
  }
  return { files, imports, writes };
}

function counts(path: string, source: string, exists: Exists) {
  const imports = new Map<string, number>();
  for (const spec of parseImports(source)) {
    const to = resolveImport(path, spec, exists);
    if (to) imports.set(to, (imports.get(to) ?? 0) + 1);
  }
  const writes = new Map<string, number>();
  for (const table of scanWrites(source)) writes.set(table, (writes.get(table) ?? 0) + 1);
  return { imports, writes };
}

/** One file's resolved imports and table writes (each target/table once). */
export function factsForSource(path: string, source: string, exists: Exists): FactDelta {
  return deltaForEdit(path, null, source, exists);
}

/** Imports and writes that `newSource` adds over `oldSource` (multiset difference by target/table). */
export function deltaForEdit(path: string, oldSource: string | null, newSource: string, exists: Exists): FactDelta {
  const file = normalizePath(path) ?? path;
  const before = oldSource === null ? null : counts(file, oldSource, exists);
  const after = counts(file, newSource, exists);
  const added = (key: string, n: number, old: Map<string, number> | undefined) => n > (old?.get(key) ?? 0);
  return {
    imports: [...after.imports].filter(([to, n]) => added(to, n, before?.imports)).map(([to]) => ({ from: file, to })),
    writes: [...after.writes].filter(([t, n]) => added(t, n, before?.writes)).map(([table]) => ({ file, table })),
  };
}

/** Apply a Claude Code `Edit` to file text. Throws if `oldString` is not found. */
export function applyEdit(current: string, oldString: string, newString: string, replaceAll = false): string {
  if (!current.includes(oldString)) throw new Error('old_string not found in file');
  return replaceAll ? current.split(oldString).join(newString) : current.replace(oldString, () => newString);
}

/** Cross-domain edges between cell files. Neutral, ignored, unassigned and test files, and same-domain imports, draw none. */
export function domainEdges(facts: Facts | FactDelta, mapper: Mapper): DomainEdge[] {
  const edges = new Map<string, DomainEdge>();
  for (const imp of facts.imports) {
    const a = mapper.place(imp.from);
    const b = mapper.place(imp.to);
    if (a.kind !== 'cell' || b.kind !== 'cell' || a.domain === b.domain) continue;
    const key = `${a.domain}\u0000${b.domain}`;
    let edge = edges.get(key);
    if (!edge) edges.set(key, (edge = { from: a.domain, to: b.domain, files: [] }));
    edge.files.push(imp);
  }
  return [...edges.values()].sort((x, y) => x.from.localeCompare(y.from) || x.to.localeCompare(y.to));
}
const REGEX_PRECEDERS = new Set('(,=:[!&|?{};+-*%<>~^'.split(''));
const REGEX_KEYWORDS = /(?:^|[^\w$])(?:return|typeof|case|do|else|in|of|void|yield|await|delete|throw|new)$/;

/**
 * Replace `//` and `/* *\/` comments with spaces (newlines kept), leaving strings,
 * template literals and regex literals intact, so offsets and line numbers still match.
 */
export function stripComments(src: string): string {
  const n = src.length;
  let out = '';
  let i = 0;

  const copyQuoted = (quote: string) => {
    out += src[i++];
    while (i < n && src[i] !== quote && src[i] !== '\n') {
      if (src[i] === '\\') out += src[i++];
      if (i < n) out += src[i++];
    }
    if (i < n && src[i] === quote) out += src[i++];
  };

  const copyRegex = () => {
    let inClass = false;
    out += src[i++];
    while (i < n && src[i] !== '\n') {
      const c = src[i]!;
      if (c === '\\') {
        out += src.slice(i, i + 2);
        i += 2;
        continue;
      }
      out += c;
      i++;
      if (c === '[') inClass = true;
      else if (c === ']') inClass = false;
      else if (c === '/' && !inClass) break;
    }
  };

  const copyTemplate = () => {
    out += src[i++];
    while (i < n && src[i] !== '`') {
      if (src[i] === '\\') {
        out += src.slice(i, i + 2);
        i += 2;
      } else if (src[i] === '$' && src[i + 1] === '{') {
        out += '${';
        i += 2;
        code(true);
      } else out += src[i++];
    }
    if (i < n) out += src[i++];
  };

  // Scan code; when `inTemplate`, stop after the `}` that closes the `${`.
  function code(inTemplate: boolean) {
    let depth = 0;
    while (i < n) {
      const c = src[i]!;
      const next = src[i + 1];
      if (c === '/' && next === '/') {
        while (i < n && src[i] !== '\n') {
          out += ' ';
          i++;
        }
      } else if (c === '/' && next === '*') {
        const end = src.indexOf('*/', i + 2);
        const stop = end === -1 ? n : end + 2;
        out += src.slice(i, stop).replace(/[^\n]/g, ' ');
        i = stop;
      } else if (c === '"' || c === "'") copyQuoted(c);
      else if (c === '`') copyTemplate();
      else if (c === '/') {
        const before = out.trimEnd();
        const prev = before[before.length - 1];
        if (prev === undefined || REGEX_PRECEDERS.has(prev) || REGEX_KEYWORDS.test(before)) copyRegex();
        else out += src[i++];
      } else {
        if (c === '{') depth++;
        else if (c === '}') {
          if (inTemplate && depth === 0) {
            out += src[i++];
            return;
          }
          depth--;
        }
        out += src[i++];
      }
    }
  }

  code(false);
  return out;
}

const STATIC_FROM = /(?<![\w$.])(?:import|export)\s+(?:type\s+)?[\w$\s{},*]*?\bfrom\s*(['"])([^'"\n]+)\1/g;
const SIDE_EFFECT = /(?<![\w$.])import\s*(['"])([^'"\n]+)\1/g;
const DYNAMIC = /(?<![\w$.])import\s*\(\s*(['"`])([^'"`$\n]+)\1\s*\)/g;

/** Module specifiers imported or re-exported by `source`, in source order. Comments are ignored. */
export function parseImports(source: string): string[] {
  const code = stripComments(source);
  const found: { at: number; spec: string }[] = [];
  for (const re of [STATIC_FROM, SIDE_EFFECT, DYNAMIC]) {
    for (const m of code.matchAll(re)) found.push({ at: m.index, spec: m[2]! });
  }
  return found.sort((a, b) => a.at - b.at).map((f) => f.spec);
}

/** Normalize a repo-relative path: POSIX separators, no `./`, `.`/`..` resolved. Null if it escapes the root. */
export function normalizePath(path: string): string | null {
  const parts: string[] = [];
  for (const seg of path.replace(/\\/g, '/').split('/')) {
    if (seg === '' || seg === '.') continue;
    if (seg === '..') {
      if (parts.length === 0) return null;
      parts.pop();
    } else parts.push(seg);
  }
  return parts.join('/');
}

/** Directory part of a repo-relative path ('' for root files). */
export function dirname(path: string): string {
  const i = path.lastIndexOf('/');
  return i === -1 ? '' : path.slice(0, i);
}

const EXT_SWAPS: Record<string, string[]> = { '.js': ['.ts', '.tsx'], '.jsx': ['.tsx'], '.mjs': ['.mts'] };

/** First existing file for a repo path written the way an import would be: as is, swapped JS extension, `.ts`, `.tsx`, `/index.ts`, `/index.tsx`. */
export function resolvePath(path: string, exists: (path: string) => boolean): string | null {
  const base = normalizePath(path);
  if (!base) return null;
  const candidates = [base];
  const ext = base.match(/\.(?:js|jsx|mjs)$/)?.[0];
  if (ext) for (const swap of EXT_SWAPS[ext]!) candidates.push(base.slice(0, -ext.length) + swap);
  candidates.push(`${base}.ts`, `${base}.tsx`, `${base}/index.ts`, `${base}/index.tsx`);
  return candidates.find((c) => exists(c)) ?? null;
}

/** Resolve a relative specifier imported by `fromFile` to an existing repo file. Bare and `node:` specifiers give null. */
export function resolveImport(fromFile: string, specifier: string, exists: (path: string) => boolean): string | null {
  if (!isRelative(specifier)) return null;
  const dir = dirname(normalizePath(fromFile) ?? '');
  return resolvePath(dir ? `${dir}/${specifier}` : specifier, exists);
}

export function isRelative(specifier: string): boolean {
  return specifier === '.' || specifier === '..' || specifier.startsWith('./') || specifier.startsWith('../');
}
import { stripComments } from './imports';

const WRITE = /(?<![\w$])db\s*\.\s*(?:insert|update)\s*\(\s*(?:"([^"\\\n]+)"|'([^'\\\n]+)'|`([^`\\$]+)`)/g;

/** Tables written via `db.insert("t", …)` / `db.update("t", …)` with a literal table name, in source order. */
export function scanWrites(source: string): string[] {
  return [...stripComments(source).matchAll(WRITE)].map((m) => (m[1] ?? m[2] ?? m[3])!);
}
```

```text
import type { HarnessEvent } from '@harness/core/view';
import { useStore } from './store';

type ServerMsg =
  | { type: 'hello'; events: HarnessEvent[]; busy: boolean; session: string }
  | { type: 'event'; event: HarnessEvent }
  | { type: 'delta'; text: string }
  | { type: 'busy'; busy: boolean };

const params = new URLSearchParams(location.search);
/** Dev-only: `?fake=1` loads /fake-events.json at once, `?fake=play` streams it; `&at=N` opens the replay at N. */
export const fakeMode = params.get('fake');

export function connect() {
  if (fakeMode) return loadFake(fakeMode === 'play');
  void fetch('/api/info')
    .then((r) => r.json() as Promise<{ repo: string }>)
    .then((i) => useStore.getState().setRepo(i.repo))
    .catch(() => {});
  openSocket(500);
}

function openSocket(delay: number) {
  const ws = new WebSocket(`${location.protocol === 'https:' ? 'wss' : 'ws'}://${location.host}/ws`);
  let opened = false;
  ws.onopen = () => {
    opened = true;
    useStore.getState().setConn('open');
  };
  ws.onmessage = (m) => {
    const msg = JSON.parse(String(m.data)) as ServerMsg;
    const s = useStore.getState();
    if (msg.type === 'hello') s.hello(msg.events, msg.busy);
    else if (msg.type === 'event') s.append(msg.event);
    else if (msg.type === 'delta') s.addDelta(msg.text);
    else if (msg.type === 'busy') s.setBusy(msg.busy);
  };
  ws.onclose = () => {
    useStore.getState().setConn('down');
    const next = opened ? 500 : Math.min(delay * 2, 8000);
    setTimeout(() => openSocket(next), opened ? 500 : delay);
  };
}

async function loadFake(play: boolean) {
  const st = useStore.getState();
  st.setConn('fake');
  st.setRepo('scout-agent (fake turn)');
  const events = (await (await fetch('/fake-events.json')).json()) as HarnessEvent[];
  const at = params.get('at');
  if (!play) {
    st.hello(events, false);
    if (at !== null) st.setReplay(Math.max(0, Math.min(events.length, Number(at))));
    return;
  }
  st.hello([], false);
  for (let i = 0; i < events.length; i++) {
    const e = events[i]!;
    const prev = events[i - 1];
    const gap = prev ? Math.max(20, Math.min(900, (e.t - prev.t) / 3)) : 0;
    await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, e.kind === 'file_assigned' ? 15 : gap));
    useStore.getState().append(e);
  }
}

async function post(path: string, body?: unknown) {
  if (fakeMode) return;
  await fetch(path, { method: 'POST', headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' }, body: JSON.stringify(body ?? {}) });
}

export const api = {
  chat: (text: string) => post('/api/chat', { text }),
  approve: () => post('/api/approve'),
  interrupt: () => post('/api/interrupt'),
  confirmMap: () => post('/api/map/confirm'),
  fallbackMap: () => post('/api/map/fallback'),
  async file(path: string): Promise<string | null> {
    const r = await fetch(`/api/file?path=${encodeURIComponent(path)}`);
    return r.ok ? r.text() : null;
  },

  const name = repo.split('/').filter(Boolean).pop() ?? '';
  return (
    <header className="top">
      <div className="brand">
        <span className="brand-mark" aria-hidden="true">
          <span /><span /><span /><span />
        </span>
        <span className="brand-name">Harness</span>
        {name && <span className="brand-repo">{name}</span>}
        {conn === 'down' && <span className="conn-down">Server not reachable. Reconnecting…</span>}
      </div>
      <Ledger />
    </header>
  );
}

function Ledger() {
  const v = useView();
  const s = v.ledger.session;
  const t = v.turnLedger;
  const items: { label: string; value: number; turn: number | null }[] = [
    { label: 'Lines changed', value: s.linesChanged, turn: t ? t.linesChanged : null },
    { label: 'Cells to review', value: s.cellsToReview, turn: t?.cellsToReview ?? null },
    { label: 'Forks caught before code', value: s.forksCaughtBeforeCode, turn: t?.forksCaughtBeforeCode ?? null },
    { label: 'Rejected options blocked', value: s.rejectedOptionsBlocked, turn: t?.rejectedOptionsBlocked ?? null },
  ];
  return (
    <dl className="ledger" aria-label="Session ledger">
      {items.map((it) => (
        <Counter key={it.label} {...it} turnIndex={v.turnIndex} />
      ))}
    </dl>
  );
}

function Counter({ label, value, turn, turnIndex }: { label: string; value: number; turn: number | null; turnIndex: number }) {
  const shown = useTween(value, 600);
  return (
    <div className="counter">
      <dd className="counter-value">{shown.toLocaleString()}</dd>
      <dt className="counter-label">{label}</dt>
      {turnIndex > 0 && <dd className="counter-turn">{turn === null ? '–' : turn.toLocaleString()} in turn {turnIndex}</dd>}
    </div>
  );
}
```

```text
export * from './ledger';
```
