# Frontend Design

Approach this as the design lead at a design studio known for giving every client a distinct visual identity that is not mistaken for anyone else's. This client has already rejected proposals that felt cliché or templated, and is paying for a distinctive point of view: make deliberate, opinionated choices about palette, typography, and layout that are specific to this brief, and take aesthetic risk if justified.

## Ground your designs in the subject matter

If the brief does not identify what the product or subject matter is, identify it yourself before designing, and confirm with the client. You can come up with one concrete subject, the design's audience, and the design's primary job, as a proposal. If there's any information in your memory about the client's preferences or context about what they're building, use that as a hint. The subject's industry, subject matter, materials, and vernacular are where distinctive visual choices come from — a design for a toy for girls aged 8–11 will be very aesthetically different from a dashboard for financial analysts. Build with the brief's real content and subject matter throughout.

## Design principles

For web designs, the hero is the first thing viewers will see. Open with the most characteristic thing in the subject's world, in the form that is most appropriate: a headline, an image, an animation, a live demo, an interactive moment, or other treatments. Be deliberate with your choice: a big number with a small label, supporting stats, and a gradient accent is the default treatment, so only use it if that's truly the best option.

Typography carries the personality of the page. You don't need a different typeface for display or headline text and body content: use one family or two, and if two, make them clearly distinct.

Choose your typefaces deliberately, not the default families you would reach for on any other project, and set a clear type scale following the default guidance of The Elements of Typographic Style with intentional weights, widths, and spacing. When type is used as a headline or visual element, use the type treatment itself as an active part of the design, not a neutral delivery vehicle for the content.

Default to line lengths of less than 80 characters. Serif typefaces can have slightly longer line lengths; give serif body text slightly more line-height than a sans-serif.

Avoid these default typographic treatments; they are the commonest tells of a generated page:
- Accenting just a single word or phrase in a headline, like putting one word in italic/bold or a different color.
- Using all caps for labels.
- Adding unnecessary typographic labels above content.

Visual structure is information. Structural devices like outlines, borders, numbering, eyebrows, dividers, labels, etc., encode useful information about the content rather than decorate it. Many generic designs use numbered markers (01 / 02 / 03), but that's only appropriate if the content actually is a sequence — like a stepped process or a timeline. Before adding numbered markers, check the content really is a sequence.

Use non-user-triggered motion sparingly and deliberately, only to draw attention. A single orchestrated moment — one page-load sequence or one reveal — lands better than scattered effects; fade-and-slide-up entrances on each section and hover transitions on every card are the generic default and read as AI-generated. Motion that answers a person's action (opening, expanding, confirming) is welcome when it shows what changed.

Consider written content carefully. Often a design brief may not contain real content, and it's up to you to come up with copy and placeholder content. Copy can make a design feel as templated as the design itself. See the below section on writing for more guidance.

## Process: plan, review against the brief, build, critique

For calibration, AI-generated design right now clusters around some traits:
1. a warm cream background (near #F4F1EA) with a high-contrast serif display and a terracotta or warm-clay accent (often near #D97757 — Anthropic's own Claude-interaction accent, so on a user's brief it reads as a tell);
2. a near-black background with a single bright acid-green or vermilion accent;
3. a broadsheet-style layout with hairline rules, zero border-radius, and dense newspaper-like columns;
4. the SaaS-card kit: content chopped into identical rounded cards, one border-radius on everything regardless of hierarchy, the same soft grey shadow (rgba(0,0,0,.1)) under each, and gradient washes as decoration;
5. template chrome that appears whatever the subject: a tracked-out ALL-CAPS eyebrow label above every heading; meta strings joined with middle dots ('A · B · C'); labels built as 'WORD — fragment' with a spaced em dash; tinted near-black (#0B0B0B, #111) standing in for black; a monospace face for small data labels; a '→' appended to link and button text.

All traits are legitimate for some briefs, but they are defaults rather than choices, and they appear regardless of subject. Where the brief pins down a visual direction, follow it exactly — the brief's own words always win, including when it asks for one of these looks. Where it leaves an axis free, don't spend that freedom on one of these defaults. As with a hired human designer, there's often a careful balance between doing what you're good at and taking each project as a chance to experiment and learn.

Work in two passes. First, brainstorm a short design plan based on the client's design brief: create a compact token system with color, type, layout, and principles.
- Color: describe the core base palette as 4–6 named hex values.
- Type: the typefaces and their roles.
- Layout: a layout concept, using one-sentence prose descriptions and ASCII wireframes to ideate and compare. Include alignment guidance; should the content be left aligned, center aligned, justified?
- Principles: the high-level guidance for what makes this page unique.

Then review that plan against the brief before building: if any part of it reads like the generic default you would produce for any similar page (work through a similar prompt to see if you arrive somewhere similar) rather than a choice made for this specific brief — revise that part, say what you changed and why. Only after you've confirmed the relative uniqueness of your design plan should you start to write the code, following the revised plan.

When writing the code, be careful of structuring your CSS selector specificities. It's easy to generate CSS classes that cancel each other out (especially with a type-based selector like .section and an element-based selector like .cta). This can happen often with padding/margin between sections.

## Restraint and self-critique

Spend your boldness in one place. Let one element be the memorable thing, keep everything around it quiet and disciplined, and cut any decoration that does not serve the brief. Build to a quality floor without announcing it: responsive down to mobile, visible keyboard focus, reduced motion respected, visually accessible, harmonious color palettes. Critique your own work as you build, taking screenshots to review if your environment supports it — a picture is worth 1000 tokens. Consider Chanel's advice: before leaving the house, take a look in the mirror and remove one accessory. Human creatives have memory and always try to do something new, so if you have a space to quickly jot down notes about what you've tried, it can help you in future passes.

## More on writing in design

Words appear in a design for one reason: to make it easier to understand and use. They are design content, not decoration. Bring the same intentionality and minimalism to copywriting that you would bring to spacing and color. Before writing anything, ask what the design needs to say, and how it can best be said to help the person navigate the experience.

Write from the end user's perspective. Name things by what users will understand in simple language, not by how the system is built. A user manages notifications, not webhook config. Describe what something is or does in plain terms rather than selling it. Being specific and legible to new users is always better than being clever.

Use active voice as default. A CTA says exactly what happens when it is used: "Save changes," not "Submit." An action keeps the same name through the whole flow, so the button that says "Publish" produces a toast that says "Published." The vocabulary of an interface is the signposting for someone navigating the product. Cohesion and consistency are how people learn their way around.

Treat failure and emptiness as moments for direction, not mood. Explain what went wrong and how to fix it, in the interface's voice rather than a person's. Errors don't apologize, and they are never vague about what happened. An empty screen is an invitation to act.

Keep the tone conversational: plain verbs, sentence case, no filler, with tone matched to the brand and the audience. Let each written element do exactly one job.


ARGUMENTS: Three static high-fidelity design comps for a diagram-first coding harness (domain × layer architecture map with an expanded domain showing file nodes, live agent activity, violations, ledger, breadcrumbs): Atlas (light cartographic blueprint), Control Room (dark telemetry, no looping motion), Strata (depth-of-field). Must be legible on a projector.

```text
/* ------------------------------------------------------------ buttons */
.btn {
  border: 1px solid var(--rule);
  background: var(--paper);

.btn-primary { background: var(--agent); border-color: var(--agent); color: var(--agent-ink); }

  color: var(--agent-deep); text-align: left; font-family: var(--mono); font-size: 12.5px;
```

```text
}

function send(res: ServerResponse, status: number, body: unknown): void {
  const payload = JSON.stringify(body);
  res.writeHead(status, { "content-type": "application/json; charset=utf-8", "content-length": Buffer.byteLength(payload) });
  res.end(payload);
}

async function readJson(req: IncomingMessage): Promise<unknown> {
  const chunks: Buffer[] = [];
  let size = 0;
  for await (const chunk of req) {
    size += (chunk as Buffer).length;
    if (size > MAX_BODY_BYTES) throw new HttpError(413, "request body too large");
    chunks.push(chunk as Buffer);
  }
  if (size === 0) return undefined;
  try {
    return JSON.parse(Buffer.concat(chunks).toString("utf8"));
  } catch {
    throw new HttpError(400, "body is not valid JSON");
  }
}
```

I read `NAVIGATION_PLAN.md`. Scout already contains most of what the harness needs to show off. It mainly needs one visible bug, and two small fixes so its routes and UI read cleanly on the map.

Here's a storyline where each beat shows a different part of what you're building, all on one theme: where customer data goes.

| # | Beat | What you do | Harness capability shown | What Scout needs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Ask** | "Where does a contact's phone number go when a rep starts research?" | Journeys (N10), Trace through the tool registry (N8), the agent's graph tools | Exists already, plus a second finding (below). Needs a small change to `web/src/shared/api.ts` |
| 2 | **Fix a bug** | "Revenue in company profiles shows as 'phone 1'." | Plan ghosts down to individual functions (N6), shift-click to point (N7), redirecting a plan | Make the bug visible (below) |
| 3 | **Add a feature** | "The brief should say if we've already emailed this person." | Red ghost edge, the A/B fork, a recorded decision, memory in the next session | Nothing to add; the tempting wrong path already exists |
| 4 | **Living map** | "Let reps follow an account and get a daily digest of new filings." | New code with no home, the cartographer proposing a new domain with scores, accept or reject (N5) | Nothing to add; nothing in Scout fits it today |
| 5 | **Auditor** (recorded) | A later turn follows the letter of beat 3's decision but not its spirit | Advisory findings that cite a decision (N9) | Nothing to add; the loophole exists naturally |

**How each beat plays out on Scout:**

1. **Ask.**
   - The "Start research" journey runs: UI page → `POST /api/runs` → run loop → registry → tools → gateway → Claude.
   - The trace shows two ways a contact's details reach a model provider: through the gateway with redaction, and from `news-summarize.ts` straight to `vendor/llm-anthropic` (red).
   - **A second finding I hadn't flagged until now:** live web search and news call `@anthropic-ai/sdk` directly from `vendor/search` and `vendor/news`. Their costs never reach `cost_log`, so the Model usage page under-reports spend. The import rule can't see this, because it ignores package imports, but your plan's Tier 1 records `vendor:@anthropic-ai/sdk`. So "who talks to Anthropic?" finds three callers, not one. That's a good "the map told you what reading the code wouldn't" moment.
2. **Fix a bug.**
   - The agent's likely first plan is a workaround: format revenue as "$2.2B" in `vendor/enrichment#formatRevenue`, a ghost in Research tools › External.
   - You shift-click `src/gateway/redact.ts#PHONE_PATTERN` and say "fix the cause here". The ghost moves to the gateway column and the gateway tests come along.
   - No rule fires; this is review on human judgment.
3. **Add a feature.**
   - Following the README's "Adding a tool" guide, the obvious plan is a new tool that imports outreach code. That edge goes red under DR-3 ("research tools never depend on outreach").
   - You pick A: the run loop passes outreach history into the brief. That becomes a recorded decision.
   - Afterwards, "also mention prior calls" in a fresh session follows that decision without asking.
4. **Living map.**
   - Watchlists need a new folder (e.g. `src/watchlist/`), a scheduled job and a new table. It lands in Unassigned with an instant guess.
   - At turn end the cartographer proposes a "Watchlists" domain, shown as ghosts with scores. Accepting commits `domains.yaml`.
5. **Auditor.**
   - A later tool reads the `outreach_log` table directly through `src/shared/db`.
   - The rule checker can't catch it: reads aren't checked, and `shared` is neutral.
   - The auditor flags it, citing beat 3's decision and the line.

**What I'd change in Scout:**
1. **Make the beat 2 bug visible.** Enrichment shows exact revenue ("$2,247,195,000 (FY2025)", which is what EDGAR returns), so every company profile gets a `phone 1` chip today, both live and offline.
2. **Use full literal paths in `web/src/shared/api.ts`.** It builds URLs as `` fetch(`/api${path}`) ``, which journey discovery can't match to a route. Writing out paths like `"/api/runs"` costs nothing and makes beat 1 work.
3. **Move `router.tsx` into the neutral `web/src/shared/`**, removing the four UI edges that point back at the shell.
4. **Leave the search-and-news cost gap in.** It's real and makes beat 1 richer. It can become an extra bug-fix beat: the tempting fix, writing `cost_log` from the search adapter, breaks DR-2 (only the gateway writes `cost_log`).

**One trade-off to decide:** fixing the redaction bug in beat 2 removes the 10-K tool's reason to bypass the gateway, so beat 3 should be the outreach-history feature. If you'd rather keep the 10-K tool as the fork beat, beat 2 needs a different bug. Old Dominion's empty filing sections would do: a quiet, single-column fix.

**For the other session:**
- **Out-of-date references to `vendor/llm-openai`.** N8's trace check and the Journeys example still name it; the leak and the default provider are now `vendor/llm-anthropic`.
- **N9's example assumes a filings decision with a redaction profile.** If beat 3 becomes the outreach-history decision, N9's example should be the `outreach_log` read from beat 5.
- **Route adapter:** Scout's routes are a table of method, regex and handler, so beat 1 needs the "custom router pattern" from §3.1.
- **Map YAML:** the UI-row change is still waiting in `DEMO_REPO_SPEC.md`.

Should I go with beats 1–5 as above (outreach history as the fork) and make Scout changes 1–3? I'd then add a "Demo beats" section to `DEMO_REPO_SPEC.md` that you can hand to the other session.

```text
export function wrap(result) {
  let program, module, comments, errors;
  return {
    get program() {
      if (!program) program = jsonParseAst(result.program);
      return program;
    },
    get module() {
      if (!module) module = result.module;
      return module;
    },
    get comments() {
      if (!comments) comments = result.comments;
      return comments;
    },
    get errors() {
      if (!errors) errors = result.errors;
      return errors;
    },
  };
}

// Used by `napi/playground/scripts/patch.js`.
//
// Set `value` field of `Literal`s which are `BigInt`s or `RegExp`s.
//
// Returned JSON contains an array `fixes` with paths to these nodes
// e.g. for `123n; foo(/xyz/)`, `fixes` will be
// `[["body", 0, "expression"], ["body", 1, "expression", "arguments", 0]]`.
//
// Walk down the AST to these nodes and alter them.
// Compiling the list of fixes on Rust side avoids having to do a full AST traversal on JS side
// to locate the likely very few `Literal`s which need fixing.
export function jsonParseAst(programJson) {
  const { node: program, fixes } = JSON.parse(programJson);
  for (const fixPath of fixes) {
    applyFix(program, fixPath);
  }
  return program;
}

function applyFix(program, fixPath) {
  let node = program;
  for (const key of fixPath) {
    node = node[key];
  }

  if (node.bigint) {
    node.value = BigInt(node.bigint);
  } else {
    try {
      node.value = RegExp(node.regex.pattern, node.regex.flags);
    } catch {
      // Invalid regexp, or valid regexp using syntax not supported by this version of NodeJS
    }
  }
}
```

```text
import { parse as parseBinding, parseSync as parseSyncBinding } from "./bindings.js";
import { wrap } from "./wrap.js";

export { default as visitorKeys } from "./generated/visit/keys.js";
export { Visitor } from "./visit/index.js";

export {
  ExportExportNameKind,
  ExportImportNameKind,
  ExportLocalNameKind,
  ImportNameKind,
  ParseResult,
  Severity,
} from "./bindings.js";
export { rawTransferSupported } from "./raw-transfer/supported.js";

const require = createRequire(import.meta.url);

// Lazily loaded as needed
let parseSyncRaw = null,
  parseRaw,
  parseSyncLazy = null,
  parseLazy,
  LazyVisitor;

/**
 * Lazy-load code related to raw transfer.
 * @returns {undefined}
 */
function loadRawTransfer() {
  if (parseSyncRaw === null) {
    ({ parseSyncRaw, parse: parseRaw } = require("./raw-transfer/eager.js"));
  }
}

/**
 * Lazy-load code related to raw transfer lazy deserialization.
 * @returns {undefined}
 */
function loadRawTransferLazy() {
  if (parseSyncLazy === null) {
    ({ parseSyncLazy, parse: parseLazy, Visitor: LazyVisitor } = require("./raw-transfer/lazy.js"));
  }
}

/**
 * Parse JS/TS source synchronously on current thread.
 *
 * @param {string} filename - Filename
 * @param {string} sourceText - Source text of file
 * @param {Object|undefined} options - Parsing options
 * @returns {Object} - Object with property getters for `program`, `module`, `comments`, and `errors`
 * @throws {Error} - If `experimentalRawTransfer` or `experimentalLazy` option is enabled,
 *   and raw transfer is not supported on this platform
 */
export function parseSync(filename, sourceText, options) {
  if (options?.experimentalRawTransfer) {
    loadRawTransfer();
    return parseSyncRaw(filename, sourceText, options);
  }
  if (options?.experimentalLazy) {
    loadRawTransferLazy();
    return parseSyncLazy(filename, sourceText, options);
  }
  return wrap(parseSyncBinding(filename, sourceText, options));
}

/**
 * Parse JS/TS source asynchronously on a separate thread.
 *
 * Note that not all of the workload can happen on a separate thread.
 * Parsing on Rust side does happen in a separate thread, but deserialization of the AST to JS objects
 * has to happen on current thread. This synchronous deserialization work typically outweighs
 * the asynchronous parsing by a factor of between 3 and 20.
 *
 * i.e. the majority of the workload cannot be parallelized by using this method.
 *
 * Generally `parseSync` is preferable to use as it does not have the overhead of spawning a thread.
 * If you need to parallelize parsing multiple files, it is recommended to use worker threads.
 *
 * @param {string} filename - Filename
 * @param {string} sourceText - Source text of file
 * @param {Object|undefined} options - Parsing options
 * @returns {Object} - Object with property getters for `program`, `module`, `comments`, and `errors`
 * @throws {Error} - If `experimentalRawTransfer` or `experimentalLazy` option is enabled,
 *   and raw transfer is not supported on this platform
 */
export async function parse(filename, sourceText, options) {
  if (options?.experimentalRawTransfer) {
    loadRawTransfer();
    return await parseRaw(filename, sourceText, options);
  }
  if (options?.experimentalLazy) {
    loadRawTransferLazy();
    return await parseLazy(filename, sourceText, options);
  }
  return wrap(await parseBinding(filename, sourceText, options));
}

/**
 * Get `Visitor` class to construct visitors with.
 * @returns {function} - `Visitor` class
 */
export function experimentalGetLazyVisitor() {
  loadRawTransferLazy();
  return LazyVisitor;
}
```

```typescript
// Small pure helpers shared by the cartography modules. Browser-safe (no node builtins).
import type { Placement } from '../mapper';
import type { FileFacts } from '../contracts/facts';

/** Key of the cell a placement counts as for footprints: `domain/layer`, `UNASSIGNED_CELL`, or null (neutral, ignored, test). */
export const UNASSIGNED_CELL = '(unassigned)';
export function cellKeyOf(p: Placement): string | null {
  if (p.kind === 'cell') return `${p.domain}/${p.layer}`;
  if (p.kind === 'unassigned') return UNASSIGNED_CELL;
  return null;
}

/** Full placement key for churn: every kind, so a move between any two homes counts. */
export function placementKey(p: Placement): string {
  if (p.kind === 'cell') return `cell:${p.domain}/${p.layer}`;
  if (p.kind === 'test') return `test:${p.domain}`;
  return p.kind;
}

export const CODE_FILE = /\.(ts|tsx|js|jsx|mjs|cjs|mts)$/;
export const TEST_FILE = /(^|\/)(test|tests|__tests__|spec)\/|\.(test|spec)\.[cm]?[jt]sx?$/;

/** Repo-internal import targets of a file (drops `vendor:<pkg>` bare imports and self-imports). */
export function repoImports(f: FileFacts): string[] {
  return f.imports.map((i) => i.to).filter((to) => !to.startsWith('vendor:') && to !== f.path);
}

export function median(xs: readonly number[]): number {
  if (!xs.length) return 0;
  const s = [...xs].sort((a, b) => a - b);
  const m = s.length >> 1;
  return s.length % 2 ? s[m]! : (s[m - 1]! + s[m]!) / 2;
}

export const mean = (xs: readonly number[]) => (xs.length ? xs.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0) / xs.length : 0);

/** Gini coefficient of non-negative counts (0 = perfectly even). */
export function gini(xs: readonly number[]): number {
  const n = xs.length;
  const total = xs.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0);
  if (n < 2 || total === 0) return 0;
  const s = [...xs].sort((a, b) => a - b);
  let acc = 0;
  s.forEach((x, i) => { acc += (2 * (i + 1) - n - 1) * x; });
  return acc / (n * total);
}

/** FNV-1a 32-bit, hex. Deterministic content hash for label cache keys (not cryptographic). */
export function fnv1a(text: string): string {
  let h = 0x811c9dc5;
  for (let i = 0; i < text.length; i++) {
    h ^= text.charCodeAt(i);
    h = Math.imul(h, 0x01000193) >>> 0;
  }
  return h.toString(16).padStart(8, '0');
}

export const dirOf = (path: string) => (path.includes('/') ? path.slice(0, path.lastIndexOf('/')) : '');

/** "news-digest" → "News digest". */
export function titleCase(slug: string): string {
  const words = slug.replace(/[-_.]+/g, ' ').trim();
  return words ? words[0]!.toUpperCase() + words.slice(1) : slug;
}

/** Majority key (ties → lexically smallest), or null for an empty tally. */
export function majority(keys: readonly string[]): string | null {
  const tally = new Map<string, number>();
  for (const k of keys) tally.set(k, (tally.get(k) ?? 0) + 1);
  let best: string | null = null;
  let n = 0;
  for (const [k, c] of [...tally].sort(([a], [b]) => a.localeCompare(b))) if (c > n) { best = k; n = c; }
  return best;
}

export const round = (x: number, places = 3) => Math.round(x * 10 ** places) / 10 ** places;
```

```typescript
// History units (Harness turns and git commits) that maps are scored and drift is measured against.
import type { UIState } from '../events';
import type { HistoryTurn } from '../contracts/cartography';

/**
 * Harness turns as history units: the files each turn edited (attributed or not), in log order.
 * Turns that only read are skipped; they say nothing about where change lands.
 */
export function historyFromUI(ui: UIState): HistoryTurn[] {
  const out: HistoryTurn[] = [];
  for (const t of ui.turns) {
    const files = Object.entries(t.paths).filter(([, a]) => a.edits > 0).map(([p]) => p).sort();
    if (files.length) out.push({ id: t.id, source: 'turn', files });
  }
  return out;
}

/**
 * Bulk units (initial imports, mass reformatting) say nothing about boundaries and would swamp the means:
 * a unit is bulk when it touches more than 10 known files and more than 30% of them.
 */
export function isBulk(files: readonly string[], known: ReadonlySet<string>): boolean {
  const n = files.filter((f) => known.has(f)).length;
  return n > 10 && n > 0.3 * known.size;
}
```

```typescript
// THROWAWAY (N0 spike): a Projection-shaped value built straight from UIState, until the Graph lane's `project()` lands.
// Domains → cells → files (ui.files), file edges from ui.facts[path].imports plus this turn's planned imports as ghosts.
// Expanding a domain expands all of its cells (System → Domain level). Ports for edges that leave an expanded cell.
import {
  cellId, cellKey, domainId, ROOT_ID,
  type Port, type Projection, type Rollup, type TurnState, type UIState, type ViolationState, type VisibleEdge, type VisibleNode, type Violation,
} from '@harness/core/view';
import type { GridSpec, Scene } from '../scene';

const sev = (v: ViolationState) => (v === 'new' ? 2 : v === 'existing' ? 1 : 0);
export const maxViolation = (a: ViolationState, b: ViolationState): ViolationState => (sev(a) >= sev(b) ? a : b);

export const emptyRollup = (): Rollup => ({
  looked: false, edited: false, added: 0, removed: 0, ghostSteps: [], unplanned: false, violation: null,
  violationFiles: [], newViolationFiles: [], cursor: false, audit: 0, proposal: null, leaves: 0,
});

/** Booleans OR, counts sum, severity MAX (never averaged). */
export function mergeRollups(list: Rollup[]): Rollup {
  const r = emptyRollup();
  for (const x of list) {
    r.looked ||= x.looked;
    r.edited ||= x.edited;
    r.added += x.added;
    r.removed += x.removed;
    r.ghostSteps = [...new Set([...r.ghostSteps, ...x.ghostSteps])].sort((a, b) => a - b);
    r.unplanned ||= x.unplanned;
    r.violation = maxViolation(r.violation, x.violation);
    r.violationFiles.push(...x.violationFiles);
    r.newViolationFiles.push(...x.newViolationFiles);
    r.cursor ||= x.cursor;
    r.audit += x.audit;
    r.leaves += x.leaves;
  }
  return r;
}

export function fileLabel(path: string) {
  const parts = path.split('/');
  const last = parts.pop() ?? path;
  return /^index\.[tj]sx?$/.test(last) && parts.length ? `${parts.pop()}/` : last;
}

const hits = (list: readonly Violation[], from: string, to?: string) => list.some((v) => v.file === from && (!to || !v.target || v.target === to));

export function fakeScene(ui: UIState, turn: TurnState | null, expanded: readonly string[]): Scene | null {
  const map = ui.map;
  if (!map) return null;
  const grid: GridSpec = {
    domains: map.domains.map((d) => ({ id: d.id, name: d.name, purpose: d.purpose })),
    layers: map.layers.map((l) => ({ id: l.id, name: l.name })),
    cells: Object.fromEntries(map.domains.map((d) => [d.id, map.layers.filter((l) => l.id in d.cells).map((l) => l.id)])),
  };
  const domIndex = new Map(map.domains.map((d, i) => [d.id, i]));
  const layerIndex = new Map(map.layers.map((l, i) => [l.id, i]));

  // Files per cell, plus planned files that don't exist yet.
  const fileCell = new Map<string, { domain: string; layer: string }>();
  for (const [path, p] of Object.entries(ui.files)) if (p.kind === 'cell') fileCell.set(path, { domain: p.domain, layer: p.layer });
  const planned: string[] = [];
  for (const pc of Object.values(turn?.planned ?? {})) {
    for (const f of pc.files) if (!fileCell.has(f)) { fileCell.set(f, pc.cell); planned.push(f); }
  }
  const cellFiles = new Map<string, string[]>();
  for (const [path, c] of fileCell) {
    const k = cellKey(c);
    cellFiles.set(k, [...(cellFiles.get(k) ?? []), path]);
  }
  for (const list of cellFiles.values()) list.sort();

  const hasPlan = !!turn && Object.keys(turn.planned).length > 0;
  const editedFiles = new Set(Object.values(turn?.edited ?? {}).flatMap((e) => e.files));
  const lookedFiles = new Set([...Object.values(turn?.looked ?? {}).flat(), ...Object.entries(turn?.paths ?? {}).filter(([, p]) => p.looked).map(([k]) => k)]);
  const plannedFiles = new Set(Object.values(turn?.planned ?? {}).flatMap((p) => p.files));
  const newList = [...(turn?.planViolations ?? []), ...(turn?.gateBlocks ?? [])];

  const leaf = (path: string): Rollup => {
    const pa = turn?.paths[path];
    const edited = editedFiles.has(path);
    const steps = turn?.steps.filter((s) => s.files.includes(path)).map((s) => s.n) ?? [];
    const isNew = hits(newList, path);
    const existing = hits(ui.violations, path);
    return {
      looked: lookedFiles.has(path), edited, added: pa?.added ?? 0, removed: pa?.removed ?? 0,
      ghostSteps: edited ? [] : steps,
      unplanned: hasPlan && edited && !plannedFiles.has(path) && !steps.length,
      violation: isNew ? 'new' : existing ? 'existing' : null,
      violationFiles: existing ? [path] : [], newViolationFiles: isNew ? [path] : [],
      cursor: ui.cursor?.path === path, audit: 0, proposal: null, leaves: 1,
    };
  };

  const isOpen = (domain: string) => expanded.includes(domainId(domain));
  const nodes: VisibleNode[] = [];
  const preview: Record<string, string[]> = {};
  map.domains.forEach((d, di) => {
    const open = isOpen(d.id);
    const cellRollups: Rollup[] = [];
    const cellNodes: VisibleNode[] = [];
    const fileNodes: VisibleNode[] = [];
    map.layers.forEach((l, li) => {
      if (!(l.id in d.cells)) return;
      const files = cellFiles.get(cellKey({ domain: d.id, layer: l.id })) ?? [];
      const leaves = files.map((f) => [f, leaf(f)] as const);
      const rollup = mergeRollups(leaves.map(([, r]) => r));
      const id = cellId(d.id, l.id);
      cellRollups.push(rollup);
      cellNodes.push({ id, kind: 'cell', parent: domainId(d.id), label: l.name, depth: 2, expanded: open && files.length > 0, expandable: files.length > 0, order: li, domain: d.id, layer: l.id, rollup });
      if (open) {
        leaves.forEach(([f, r], i) => fileNodes.push({ id: f, kind: 'file', parent: id, label: fileLabel(f), depth: 3, expanded: false, expandable: false, order: i, domain: d.id, layer: l.id, path: f, rollup: r }));
      } else {
        const rank = (r: Rollup) => (r.violation ? 0 : r.edited ? 1 : r.ghostSteps.length ? 2 : 3);
        preview[id] = [...leaves].sort((a, b) => rank(a[1]) - rank(b[1]) || a[0].localeCompare(b[0])).map(([f]) => fileLabel(f));
      }
    });
    nodes.push({ id: domainId(d.id), kind: 'domain', parent: ROOT_ID, label: d.name, depth: 1, expanded: open, expandable: true, order: di, domain: d.id, rollup: mergeRollups(cellRollups) });
    nodes.push(...cellNodes, ...fileNodes);
  });

  // Leaf edges → nearest visible endpoints.
  const visibleOf = (path: string) => {
    const c = fileCell.get(path);
    if (!c) return null;
    return isOpen(c.domain) ? path : cellId(c.domain, c.layer);
  };
  const added = new Set((turn?.edgesAdded ?? []).map((a) => `${a.edge.from}|${a.edge.to}`));
  type Leaf = { from: string; to: string; status: VisibleEdge['status']; violation: ViolationState; steps: number[] };
  const leaves: Leaf[] = [];
  const built = new Set<string>();
  for (const [path, f] of Object.entries(ui.facts)) {
    for (const imp of f.imports) {
      if (!imp.to) continue;
      built.add(`${path}|${imp.to}`);
      const isNew = added.has(`${path}|${imp.to}`);
      const violation: ViolationState = isNew && hits(turn?.gateBlocks ?? [], path, imp.to) ? 'new' : hits(ui.violations, path, imp.to) ? 'existing' : null;
      leaves.push({ from: path, to: imp.to, status: isNew ? 'new' : 'existing', violation, steps: [] });
    }
  }
  for (const pe of Object.values(turn?.plannedEdges ?? {})) {
    for (const imp of pe.imports) {
      if (built.has(`${imp.from}|${imp.to}`)) continue;
      leaves.push({ from: imp.from, to: imp.to, status: 'ghost', violation: hits(turn?.planViolations ?? [], imp.from, imp.to) ? 'new' : null, steps: pe.steps });
    }
  }
  const agg = new Map<string, VisibleEdge>();
  for (const l of leaves) {
    const from = visibleOf(l.from);
    const to = visibleOf(l.to);
    if (!from || !to || from === to) continue;
    const a = fileCell.get(l.from)!;
    const b = fileCell.get(l.to)!;
    if (a.domain === b.domain && !isOpen(a.domain)) continue; // inside a collapsed domain: not drawn at System level
    const id = `${l.status}|${from}|${to}`;
    const e = agg.get(id) ?? { id, from, to, kinds: ['imports'], count: 0, status: l.status, violation: null, confidence: null, steps: [], leafEdges: [] };
    e.count++;
    e.violation = maxViolation(e.violation, l.violation);
    e.steps = [...new Set([...e.steps, ...l.steps])].sort((x, y) => x - y);
    e.leafEdges.push(`imports|${l.from}|${l.to}`);
    agg.set(id, e);
  }
  const edges = [...agg.values()].sort((x, y) => x.id.localeCompare(y.id));

  // Ports: where an edge leaves (or enters) an expanded cell.
  const byId = new Map(nodes.map((n) => [n.id, n]));
  const ports: Port[] = [];
  for (const e of edges) {
    for (const [self, other, direction] of [[e.from, e.to, 'out'], [e.to, e.from, 'in']] as const) {
      const s = byId.get(self);
      const o = byId.get(other);
      if (!s || !o || s.kind !== 'file' || s.parent === (o.kind === 'file' ? o.parent : o.id)) continue;
      const dd = domIndex.get(o.domain!)! - domIndex.get(s.domain!)!;
      const dl = layerIndex.get(o.layer!)! - layerIndex.get(s.layer!)!;
      const side: Port['side'] = dd > 0 ? 'right' : dd < 0 ? 'left' : dl > 0 ? 'bottom' : 'top';
      ports.push({ container: s.parent!, edge: e.id, side, direction });
    }
  }

  const projection: Projection = { nodes, edges, ports };
  const cur = ui.cursor;
  const curNode = cur ? (byId.has(cur.path) ? cur.path : (() => { const c = fileCell.get(cur.path); return c ? cellId(c.domain, c.layer) : null; })()) : null;
  return { grid, projection, cursor: cur && curNode ? { node: curNode, verb: cur.verb, path: cur.path } : null, preview, planned };
}
```

```typescript
// ELK layered, one run per container, off the main thread. elk.bundled runs synchronously inside this worker.
import ELK from 'elkjs/lib/elk.bundled.js';
import type { ElkNode } from 'elkjs/lib/elk-api';

const elk = new ELK();

self.onmessage = async (e: MessageEvent<{ id: number; graph: ElkNode }>) => {
  const { id, graph } = e.data;
  const t0 = performance.now();
  try {
    const out = await elk.layout(graph);
    self.postMessage({ id, out, ms: performance.now() - t0 });
  } catch (err) {
    self.postMessage({ id, error: String(err), ms: performance.now() - t0 });
  }
};
```

```text
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { parseImports, resolveImport, stripComments } from '../src/imports';

describe('parseImports', () => {
  it('reads every import syntax in source order', () => {
    const src = [
      `import a from "./a";`,
      `import type { T } from './types';`,
      `import {`,
      `  b,`,
      `  c as d,`,
      `} from "../b";`,
      `import * as ns from './ns';`,
      `import x, { y } from './xy';`,
      `import './side-effect';`,
      `export { e } from "./e";`,
      `export * from './star';`,
      `export type { F } from './f';`,
      `const m = await import('./dynamic');`,
      'const t = await import(`./tpl`);',
      `import { readFile } from "node:fs";`,
      `import { z } from 'zod';`,
    ].join('\n');
    expect(parseImports(src)).toEqual([
      './a', './types', '../b', './ns', './xy', './side-effect', './e', './star', './f', './dynamic', './tpl', 'node:fs', 'zod',
    ]);
  });
```

```typescript
// scoreMap (NAVIGATION_PLAN §4.5): candidates are judged by deterministic metrics, never by the model's opinion.
import { createMapper, type Mapper } from '../mapper';
import type { DomainMap } from '../schema';
import type { FileFacts } from '../contracts/facts';
import type { HistoryTurn, MapScore } from '../contracts/cartography';
import type { ScoreMap } from '../contracts/api';
import { isBulk } from './history';
import { cellKeyOf, gini, mean, median, placementKey, repoImports, round } from './util';

/**
 * Weights of `MapScore.total` (lower is better). Rationale:
 * - cells lit per unit is the headline ("a typical turn lights 1.8 cells"): 1 per cell on the mean, 0.5 on the median;
 * - modularity Q lives in [-0.5, 1]; ×2 makes a clearly better partition (+0.1 Q) worth 0.2, about one in five turns lighting one fewer cell;
 * - each unassigned file costs 0.5, so placing even one file clears the proposal margin unless it widens turns;
 * - Gini of cell sizes (0..1) is a mild evenness nudge;
 * - breaking a standing decision costs 3, more than any plausible gain, so candidates practically never do it;
 * - churn is small per moved file (0.1) and larger per removed id (0.5): moving files beats re-cutting domains.
 */
export const SCORE_WEIGHTS = {
  cellsLitMean: 1,
  cellsLitMedian: 0.5,
  modularity: -2,
  unassigned: 0.5,
  cellSizeGini: 1,
  decisionsBroken: 3,
  churnFiles: 0.1,
  churnIds: 0.5,
} as const;

/**
 * A candidate is proposed only if `current.total - candidate.total >= PROPOSAL_MARGIN`. 0.25 is a quarter of a
 * cell per turn: below that the improvement is within the noise of a few odd turns, and proposing would churn.
 */
export const PROPOSAL_MARGIN = 0.25;

/** Distinct cells each history unit lights under `map` (unassigned files share one "Unassigned" cell). Bulk and empty units are skipped. */
export function cellsLitPerUnit(map: DomainMap | Mapper, facts: Readonly<Record<string, FileFacts>>, history: readonly HistoryTurn[]): number[] {
  const mapper = 'place' in map ? map : createMapper(map);
  const known = new Set(Object.keys(facts));
  const out: number[] = [];
  for (const unit of history) {
    if (isBulk(unit.files, known)) continue;
    const cells = new Set<string>();
    for (const f of unit.files) {
      if (!known.has(f)) continue; // deleted or non-code files say nothing about the current map
      const k = cellKeyOf(mapper.place(f));
      if (k) cells.add(k);
    }
    if (cells.size) out.push(cells.size);
  }
  return out;
}

/**
 * Newman modularity Q of the undirected file import graph, partitioned by domain. Nodes are code files in a cell
 * or unassigned (each unassigned file is its own community, so leaving coupled files unplaced is penalized);
 * neutral, ignored and test files are left out, as they draw no edges on the map.
 */
export function modularity(mapper: Mapper, facts: Readonly<Record<string, FileFacts>>): number {
  const community = new Map<string, string>();
  for (const path of Object.keys(facts)) {
    const p = mapper.place(path);
    if (p.kind === 'cell') community.set(path, p.domain);
    else if (p.kind === 'unassigned') community.set(path, `?${path}`);
  }
  const edges = new Set<string>();
  for (const f of Object.values(facts)) {
    if (!community.has(f.path)) continue;
    for (const to of repoImports(f)) {
      if (!community.has(to)) continue;
      edges.add(f.path < to ? `${f.path}\u0000${to}` : `${to}\u0000${f.path}`);
    }
  }
  const m = edges.size;
  if (!m) return 0;
  const intra = new Map<string, number>();
  const degree = new Map<string, number>();
  for (const e of edges) {
    const [a, b] = e.split('\u0000') as [string, string];
    const ca = community.get(a)!, cb = community.get(b)!;
    degree.set(ca, (degree.get(ca) ?? 0) + 1);
    degree.set(cb, (degree.get(cb) ?? 0) + 1);
    if (ca === cb) intra.set(ca, (intra.get(ca) ?? 0) + 1);
  }
  let q = 0;
  for (const [c, d] of degree) q += (intra.get(c) ?? 0) / m - (d / (2 * m)) ** 2;
  return q;
}

/** Decision ids a candidate would break vs `current` (see `ScoreMap`). */
export function brokenDecisions(map: DomainMap, current: DomainMap, decisionPaths: Readonly<Record<string, string[]>>): string[] {
  const before = createMapper(current);
  const after = createMapper(map);
  const broken = new Set<string>();
  for (const [id, paths] of Object.entries(decisionPaths)) {
    if (paths.some((p) => { const d = before.domainOf(p); return d !== null && d !== after.domainOf(p); })) broken.add(id);
  }
  const kept = new Set(map.invariants.map((i) => i.id));
  for (const inv of current.invariants) {
    if (kept.has(inv.id)) continue;
    for (const d of [...(inv.decisions ?? []), ...inv.exceptions.flatMap((e) => (e.decision ? [e.decision] : []))]) broken.add(d);
  }
  return [...broken].sort();
}

/** Domain ids, cells (in surviving domains) and invariant ids that `current` has and `map` lacks. */
export function removedIds(map: DomainMap, current: DomainMap): string[] {
  const out: string[] = [];
  const next = new Map(map.domains.map((d) => [d.id, d]));
  for (const d of current.domains) {
    const n = next.get(d.id);
    if (!n) { out.push(`domain:${d.id}`); continue; }
    for (const layer of Object.keys(d.cells)) if (!(layer in n.cells)) out.push(`cell:${d.id}/${layer}`);
  }
  const inv = new Set(map.invariants.map((i) => i.id));
  for (const i of current.invariants) if (!inv.has(i.id)) out.push(`rule:${i.id}`);
  return out;
}

/**
 * Score a map against facts and history (deterministic). Churn counts files that move between homes (cells, tests,
 * neutral); placing a previously unassigned file is not churn, it is what `unassigned` rewards.
 */
export const scoreMap: ScoreMap = (map, facts, history, opts = {}) => {
  const mapper = createMapper(map);
  const lit = cellsLitPerUnit(mapper, facts, history);
  const paths = Object.keys(facts).sort();

  let unassigned = 0;
  const cellSizes = new Map<string, number>();
  for (const d of map.domains) for (const layer of Object.keys(d.cells)) cellSizes.set(`${d.id}/${layer}`, 0);
  for (const p of paths) {
    const pl = mapper.place(p);
    if (pl.kind === 'unassigned') unassigned++;
    else if (pl.kind === 'cell') cellSizes.set(`${pl.domain}/${pl.layer}`, (cellSizes.get(`${pl.domain}/${pl.layer}`) ?? 0) + 1);
  }

  let churnFiles = 0, churnIds = 0, decisionsBroken = 0;
  if (opts.current) {
    const before = createMapper(opts.current);
    for (const p of paths) {
      const a = before.place(p);
      if (a.kind === 'unassigned' || a.kind === 'ignored') continue;
      if (placementKey(a) !== placementKey(mapper.place(p))) churnFiles++;
    }
    churnIds = removedIds(map, opts.current).length;
    decisionsBroken = brokenDecisions(map, opts.current, opts.decisionPaths ?? {}).length;
  }

  const s: Omit<MapScore, 'total'> = {
    cellsLitMean: round(mean(lit)),
    cellsLitMedian: round(median(lit)),
    modularity: round(modularity(mapper, facts)),
    unassigned,
    cellSizeGini: round(gini([...cellSizes.values()])),
    decisionsBroken,
    churnFiles,
    churnIds,
  };
  const w = SCORE_WEIGHTS;
  const total =
    w.cellsLitMean * s.cellsLitMean + w.cellsLitMedian * s.cellsLitMedian + w.modularity * s.modularity +
    w.unassigned * s.unassigned + w.cellSizeGini * s.cellSizeGini + w.decisionsBroken * s.decisionsBroken +
    w.churnFiles * s.churnFiles + w.churnIds * s.churnIds;
  return { ...s, total: round(total) };
};

/** One line for the proposal card: "turns would light 1.2 cells instead of 1.5 · 3 files placed · no decisions broken". */
export function describeScores(current: MapScore, next: MapScore): string {
  const parts = [`turns would light ${next.cellsLitMean} cells instead of ${current.cellsLitMean}`];
  const placed = current.unassigned - next.unassigned;
  if (placed > 0) parts.push(`${placed} file${placed === 1 ? '' : 's'} placed`);
  if (next.churnFiles) parts.push(`${next.churnFiles} file${next.churnFiles === 1 ? '' : 's'} move`);
  parts.push(`modularity ${current.modularity} → ${next.modularity}`);
  parts.push(next.decisionsBroken ? `${next.decisionsBroken} decision${next.decisionsBroken === 1 ? '' : 's'} broken` : 'no decisions broken');
  return parts.join(' · ');
}
```

```typescript
// Per-container ELK layout: one layered run per expanded cell, in a worker, cached by the container's content.
import type { ElkExtendedEdge, ElkNode } from 'elkjs/lib/elk-api';
import type { Port } from '@harness/core/view';

export type Pt = { x: number; y: number };
export type Box = { x: number; y: number; w: number; h: number };

/** Fixed sizes per kind (layout never depends on zoom or content, so positions stay put). */
export const FILE_W = 184;
export const FILE_H = 40;
export const PAD = { top: 44, left: 18, right: 18, bottom: 18 };

export type ContainerInput = {
  id: string;
  children: string[]; // sorted by model order
  edges: { id: string; from: string; to: string }[];
  ports: (Port & { node: string })[]; // node = the child the edge attaches to
};

export type ContainerLayout = {
  id: string;
  w: number;
  h: number;
  nodes: Record<string, Box>; // relative to the container
  edges: Record<string, Pt[]>; // internal edges, relative
  ports: Record<string, { at: Pt; route: Pt[] }>; // by `${edge}|${container}`: border point + route from/to the child
  ms: number;
};

const SIDE = { top: 'NORTH', right: 'EAST', bottom: 'SOUTH', left: 'WEST' } as const;
export const portKey = (edge: string, container: string) => `${edge}|${container}`;

export function elkGraph(c: ContainerInput): ElkNode {
  const edges: ElkExtendedEdge[] = c.edges.map((e) => ({ id: e.id, sources: [e.from], targets: [e.to] }));
  const ports = c.ports.map((p, i) => {
    const pid = `port:${i}`;
    edges.push(p.direction === 'out' ? { id: `pe:${i}`, sources: [p.node], targets: [pid] } : { id: `pe:${i}`, sources: [pid], targets: [p.node] });
    return { id: pid, width: 2, height: 2, layoutOptions: { 'elk.port.side': SIDE[p.side], 'elk.port.index': String(i) } };
  });
  return {
    id: c.id,
    layoutOptions: {
      'elk.algorithm': 'layered',
      'elk.direction': 'RIGHT',
      'elk.edgeRouting': 'ORTHOGONAL',
      'elk.randomSeed': '1',
      'elk.portConstraints': 'FIXED_SIDE',
      'elk.layered.considerModelOrder.strategy': 'NODES_AND_EDGES',
      'elk.layered.crossingMinimization.forceNodeModelOrder': 'true',
      'elk.padding': `[top=${PAD.top},left=${PAD.left},bottom=${PAD.bottom},right=${PAD.right}]`,
      'elk.spacing.nodeNode': '12',
      'elk.spacing.componentComponent': '14',
      'elk.layered.spacing.nodeNodeBetweenLayers': '44',
      'elk.layered.spacing.edgeNodeBetweenLayers': '14',
      'elk.spacing.edgeEdge': '8',
      'elk.aspectRatio': '1.4',
    },
    ports,
    children: c.children.map((id) => ({ id, width: FILE_W, height: FILE_H })),
    edges,
  };
}

function sectionPoints(e: ElkExtendedEdge): Pt[] {
  const s = e.sections?.[0];
  if (!s) return [];
  return [s.startPoint, ...(s.bendPoints ?? []), s.endPoint].map((p) => ({ x: p.x, y: p.y }));
}

export function readLayout(c: ContainerInput, out: ElkNode, ms: number): ContainerLayout {
  const nodes: ContainerLayout['nodes'] = {};
  for (const n of out.children ?? []) nodes[n.id] = { x: n.x ?? 0, y: n.y ?? 0, w: n.width ?? FILE_W, h: n.height ?? FILE_H };
  const edges: ContainerLayout['edges'] = {};
  const ports: ContainerLayout['ports'] = {};
  const portAt = new Map((out.ports ?? []).map((p) => [p.id, { x: (p.x ?? 0) + (p.width ?? 0) / 2, y: (p.y ?? 0) + (p.height ?? 0) / 2 }]));
  for (const e of out.edges ?? []) {
    if (e.id.startsWith('pe:')) {
      const i = Number(e.id.slice(3));
      const p = c.ports[i]!;
      const at = portAt.get(`port:${i}`) ?? { x: 0, y: 0 };
      ports[portKey(p.edge, c.id)] = { at, route: sectionPoints(e) };
    } else edges[e.id] = sectionPoints(e);
  }
  return { id: c.id, w: out.width ?? 0, h: out.height ?? 0, nodes, edges, ports, ms };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- worker client

let worker: Worker | null = null;
let seq = 0;
const pending = new Map<number, (r: { out?: ElkNode; error?: string; ms: number }) => void>();
const cache = new Map<string, ContainerLayout>();

function getWorker() {
  if (!worker) {
    worker = new Worker(new URL('./elk.worker.ts', import.meta.url), { type: 'module' });
    worker.onmessage = (e: MessageEvent<{ id: number; out?: ElkNode; error?: string; ms: number }>) => {
      pending.get(e.data.id)?.(e.data);
      pending.delete(e.data.id);
    };
  }
  return worker;
}

/** Cached by the container's children, edges and ports (and the elkjs version, via the bundle). */
export function layoutContainer(c: ContainerInput): Promise<ContainerLayout> {
  const key = JSON.stringify(c);
  const hit = cache.get(key);
  if (hit) return Promise.resolve(hit);
  const graph = elkGraph(c);
  const id = ++seq;
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    pending.set(id, (r) => {
      if (!r.out) return reject(new Error(r.error ?? 'elk failed'));
      const l = readLayout(c, r.out, r.ms);
      cache.set(key, l);
      resolve(l);
    });
    getWorker().postMessage({ id, graph });
  });
}

export const clearLayoutCache = () => cache.clear();

```

````markdown
# Demo recording plan

Oct 11, 2026. This replaces the "Demo script" section of the Build Plan. It assumes the harness from `SPEC.md` plus the navigation work in `NAVIGATION_PLAN.md`, and Scout as built from `DEMO_REPO_SPEC.md` (live services, web app, 14 commits).

## The story

**You stay the architect; the agent does the typing.** Each beat starts the way real work does: a question, a bug you can see, a feature a rep asked for. Instead of "fix this" and hoping, you read the plan on the map, steer it, and only then let Claude build. Everything is about one theme in Scout: where customer data goes.

**The pitch**
- Hook: "Writing code got free. Understanding it didn't." Developers already spent about 58% of their time on comprehension (Xia et al., 2018). In METR's 2025 trial, experienced developers using AI were 19% slower and still believed they had been sped up.
- Close: "Chat is the right input and the wrong output."

**What each beat proves**

| # | Beat | You do | The harness shows | Built in |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Ask | Ask where a contact's phone number goes | A journey plays; a trace shows two paths to the model provider, one of them red | N8 Trace, N10 Journeys, graph tools |
| 2 | Fix a bug | Report "revenue shows as phone 1" | Plan ghosts down to functions; you point at the real cause; the plan moves | N6 Module level, N7 Point |
| 3 | Add a feature | Ask for the brief to mention earlier emails | A red ghost edge before any code; Claude asks A or B; a decision is recorded | SPEC v1 (gate, forks, memory) |
| 4 | Remember | Ask a follow-up in a fresh session | The plan follows the decision without asking | SPEC v1 (§8) |
| 5 | Living map | Ask for account watchlists | New code with no home; the cartographer proposes a domain with scores | N5 |
| 6 | Audit | (Recorded) a later turn reads outreach data the back way | An advisory finding that cites the decision | N9 |

## Cuts

| Cut | Length | Beats | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Core** | about 3:00 | Hook, Load, 1, 2, 3, 4, Close | The submission video and the live demo |
| **Extended** | about 4:30 | Core plus 5 and 6 | Judges' follow-up, a longer slot, the website |
| **Minimum** | about 2:00 | Hook, Load, 3, 4, Close | If N6–N10 aren't ready: everything here runs on SPEC v1 |

## Shot list (core cut)

Timings are for the edited video. Agent turns run 2–5 minutes in real time; speed them up 4–8x in the edit, but keep the fork moment (Claude asking A or B) in real time.

### 0:00–0:15 Hook

- **On screen:** title card, then the two numbers.
- **Say:** "Writing code got free. Understanding it didn't. Agents now change code faster than we can follow, so the time goes to reading diffs and redoing work."

### 0:15–0:40 Load: meet Scout

- **On screen:**
  1. Scout's app (pre-recorded clip, sped up). A live research run on Symbotic: the trail fills in, real Q3 revenue, a drafted email.
  2. Cut to Harness pointed at `scout-agent`. The skeleton appears instantly, then the cartographer's map assembles: 6 domains, 5 layers.
  3. One cell is red.
- **Say:** "This is Scout, a sales research agent. 3,600 lines, 6 domains, 7 external services, and I didn't write any of it. Here's its architecture in ten seconds, and one thing is already wrong."

### 0:40–1:05 Beat 1: Ask

- **Type:** "Where does a contact's phone number go when a rep starts research?"
- **On screen:**
  1. The "Start research" journey plays over the map: UI page → `POST /api/runs` → run loop → tool registry → tools → gateway → Claude.
  2. The trace forks. One path goes through the gateway (redaction). The other goes from `news-summarize.ts` straight to `vendor/llm-anthropic`, in red.
  3. Inset of Scout's app: the news talking points say "Maya Ortiz" in plain text, while the brief shows a `name 1` marker.
- **Say:** "Two ways out. One hides personal data, one sends it to the model provider as is. I found that by asking, not by reading."
- **Optional second finding:** "Who calls Anthropic?" finds three callers. Web search and news use the SDK directly, so their cost never reaches the cost log.

### 1:05–1:35 Beat 2: Fix a bug

- **On screen:** Scout's company profile for Symbotic shows revenue as a `phone 1` marker.
- **Type:** "Revenue shows as 'phone 1' in company profiles. Can you fix how revenue is displayed?"
- **Expected plan:** a ghost on `vendor/enrichment#formatRevenue` (Research tools › External). It's a formatting workaround.
- **You:** shift-click `src/gateway/redact.ts#PHONE_PATTERN` and say "Fix the cause here; figures shouldn't look like phone numbers to the redactor." The ghost moves to Model gateway › Logic, and the gateway tests join the plan.
- **Approve.** The build fills the ghost and the tests pass. Scout's profile now shows "$2,247,195,000".
- **Say:** "The first plan hid the symptom in the wrong place. The map showed me where, so I moved it before a line was written."

### 1:35–2:20 Beat 3: Add a feature

- **Type:** "Add a tool so the brief says whether we've already emailed this contact."
- **Expected plan:** a new `src/tools/outreach-history.ts` importing `src/outreach/outreach-log.ts`. The ghost edge Research tools → Outreach turns red (DR-3).
- **Claude asks:** "This breaks DR-3. A: the run loop passes outreach history into the brief. B: add an exception for this file."
- **You:** "A." `decisions/DR-4.md` is written and committed, `domains.yaml` links DR-4 to DR-3, and Alike records it.
- **Build:** the ghosts fill in Agent loop › Logic and Outreach › Logic, a vertical stripe with nothing amber. Scout's next brief says "you emailed Maya on Oct 11".
- **Say:** "The fork came before the code. Without this, I'd have found it in review, or not at all."

### 2:20–2:40 Beat 4: Remember

- **On screen:** a fresh session. Type: "Also mention any calls we've logged with this contact."
- **Expected plan:** it goes through the run loop, cites DR-4 and asks nothing.
- **Say:** "Session two didn't ask again. The decision lives in the repo and in Alike, not in my head."

### 2:40–3:00 Ledger and close

- **On screen:** the ledger for the session, then a replay scrub through beat 3.
- **Ledger counts:** lines changed, cells to review, forks caught before code, rejected options blocked.
- **Say:** "[N] lines changed, [K] cells to review, one fork caught before code. Chat is the right input and the wrong output."
- Minutes appear only in the voiceover, taken from the baseline runs below. Never put them on the UI.

## Extended beats

### Beat 5: Living map (about 45 s)

- **Type:** "Let reps follow an account and get a daily digest of new filings and news."
- **On screen:**
  1. New files appear in `src/watchlist/`, a scheduled job and a `watchlists` table. They land in Unassigned with a faint "probably a new domain?" guess.
  2. At turn end the cartographer proposes a **Watchlists** domain as ghosts, with scores ("turns would light 2 cells; 0 unassigned; no decisions broken").
  3. You accept, and `domains.yaml` is committed.
- **Say:** "The map keeps up with the code, but only changes when I say so."

### Beat 6: Audit (about 30 s, recorded)

- **Setup:** a later turn adds a tool that reads `outreach_log` directly through `src/shared/db`. No import edge is crossed (`shared` is neutral, and reads aren't checked), so the gate stays quiet.
- **On screen:** after the turn, an amber "audit" badge: "DR-4 says outreach history reaches the brief through the run loop; `src/tools/…:NN` reads `outreach_log` directly." Promote it to a rule, or dismiss it.
- **Say:** "Rules catch what they can express. The auditor catches the rest, and it cites what you decided."

| 2 | N6 symbol ghosts and N7 Point | Cell-level ghosts; type the path instead of shift-clicking |

**Notes for the harness**
- The leak and the default provider are now `vendor/llm-anthropic`. Update N8's trace acceptance check, which still names `vendor/llm-openai`.
- N9's example assumes a filings decision. With this storyline, DR-4 is the outreach-history decision and the audit case is beat 6.
- Apply the UI-row map from `DEMO_REPO_SPEC.md`, or the 11 web files land in Unassigned.

## Rehearsal: make the agent's first move predictable

The demo depends on Claude's first plan. Run each beat at least 3 times against a reset Scout and log what it proposed.

| Beat | Want first | If it goes straight to the right answer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2 | The formatting workaround in enrichment | Keep the phrasing "fix how revenue is displayed". If it still goes to the gateway, change the beat to "the map confirms the fix stays in one column", and point at the test file instead |
| 3 | A new tool importing outreach | Keep "Add a tool so…", which follows the README. If it plans the run loop directly, the gate never fires: fall back to the 10-K beat (needs a different bug for beat 2) |
| 4 | Follows DR-4 without asking | If it asks anyway, check that DR-4 is in the session brief |

## Baselines for the voiceover

Per SPEC §12, minutes come only from measured runs.

1. Copy `scout-agent` at `demo-start`.
2. In plain Claude Code, without the harness, run the beat 2 and beat 3 prompts exactly as typed above. Time each one.
3. Record what it built: did it take the workaround or bypass? How long did finding and fixing that take? How many lines would you have had to read?
4. If plain Claude Code gets it right first time, drop the minutes claim for that beat and lean on lines to review and memory.

## Recording setup

**Screen**
- 1920×1080 at 125% browser zoom, one browser window, no bookmarks bar. Do Not Disturb on, Dock hidden.
- Tabs: Harness shell (http://localhost:5173 in the harness repo), Scout app, Alike (for beat 3's decision).

**Scout during recording**
- Run `npm run dev` in `scout-agent`, so code the agent changes reloads on its own. The web app is on http://localhost:5173 there too, so give one of the two dev servers a different port before recording.
- Use live mode for the intro clip and the "after" shots. A run takes about 70 s, so start it and cut.
- Pre-run the Symbotic research once before recording, so the app has history.

**Takes**
- Record each beat as its own take. Do the voiceover afterwards.

**Reset between takes**
1. In `scout-agent`:
   ```
   git reset --hard demo-start && git clean -fd
   rm -rf .scout/db.json
   npm run seed
   ```
   This keeps `.env` and the EDGAR cache.
2. In the harness, clear `.harness/`, delete `decisions/DR-4*.md`, and restore `domains.yaml`. A `scripts/reset-demo.sh` in the harness repo should do all of this in one step.

**Cost:** a live Scout run costs about 2–3 cents, and the agent turns are the main spend. Budget about 10 takes.

## Risks

| Risk | Fallback |
| --- | --- |
| Claude's first plan is already right (beats 2, 3) | The rehearsal table above; keep the recorded best take |
| A live service is slow or down while recording | Scout's `SCOUT_MODE=offline`, using fixture companies (switch the whole recording, not one shot) |
| Navigation features (N6–N10) aren't ready | The Minimum cut runs on SPEC v1 alone |
| Alike sign-in doesn't carry over to SDK sessions | Show `decisions/DR-4.md` in git; Alike becomes a slide |
| The map is too busy at System level | The UI row and router fix keep edges at 12 domain pairs; use the turn lens during beats |
````

```typescript
// Drift signals (NAVIGATION_PLAN §4.4): deterministic, from facts plus the event log. A signal triggers the
// cartographer only once it has persisted for `thresholds.persist` consecutive surveys.
import { createMapper, type Mapper } from '../mapper';
import type { DomainMap } from '../schema';
import type { FileFacts } from '../contracts/facts';
import { cellId, domainId, fileOf } from '../contracts/graph';
import { DEFAULT_THRESHOLDS, type DriftSignal, type DriftSignalKind, type DriftThresholds, type Label } from '../contracts/cartography';
import type { DetectDrift } from '../contracts/api';
import { cellsLitPerUnit } from './score';
import { isBulk } from './history';
import { TEST_FILE, fnv1a, median, repoImports, round } from './util';

const KIND_ORDER: DriftSignalKind[] = ['unassigned', 'new_top_level', 'wide_turns', 'co_change', 'coupling_growth', 'rule_erosion', 'rule_reinforcement', 'bloated_cell', 'stale_label'];

/** DEFAULT_THRESHOLDS overridden by `cartography.thresholds` in domains.yaml (unknown keys ignored). */
export function thresholdsFor(map: DomainMap | null): DriftThresholds {
  const out = { ...DEFAULT_THRESHOLDS };
  for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(map?.cartography?.thresholds ?? {})) if (k in out) out[k as keyof DriftThresholds] = v;
  return out;
}

/** Folder a path's "top-level code" belongs to: `src/<x>`, `packages/<x>` etc., else the first segment; null for root files. */
export function topFolder(path: string): string | null {
  const parts = path.split('/');
  if (parts.length < 2) return null;
  if (parts.length >= 3 && ['src', 'lib', 'app', 'packages', 'apps', 'services', 'modules'].includes(parts[0]!)) return `${parts[0]}/${parts[1]}`;
  return parts[0]!;
}

/** Code files placed in one cell, sorted. */
export function cellFiles(mapper: Mapper, facts: Readonly<Record<string, FileFacts>>, domain: string, layer: string): string[] {
  return Object.keys(facts).filter((p) => { const pl = mapper.place(p); return pl.kind === 'cell' && pl.domain === domain && pl.layer === layer; }).sort();
}

/** Hash a group label is keyed by: the cell's sorted file list (content edits don't rename sub-groups; membership changes do). */
export const groupHash = (files: readonly string[]) => fnv1a([...files].sort().join('\n'));

/** Current hash of what `label` describes, or null if its target is gone (group: file left its cell; summary: symbol removed). */
export function labelHash(mapper: Mapper, facts: Readonly<Record<string, FileFacts>>, label: Label): string | null {
  if (label.kind === 'summary') {
    const file = fileOf(label.target);
    return (file && facts[file]?.symbols.find((s) => s.id === label.target)?.bodyHash) ?? null;
  }
  if (label.kind === 'group') {
    const p = mapper.place(label.target);
    return p.kind === 'cell' ? groupHash(cellFiles(mapper, facts, p.domain, p.layer)) : null;
  }
  return label.hash; // journeys are re-validated by the journeys lane
}

const overlaps = (a: readonly string[], b: readonly string[]) => (a.length === 0 && b.length === 0) || a.some((x) => b.includes(x));

/**
 * Every signal in §4.4. `persisted` = 1 + the previous survey's `persisted` for a signal of the same kind whose
 * scope overlaps (equal-empty scopes match), so a scope that grows by a file keeps its count.
 * Comparison per signal: counts that must exceed (`unassigned`, `wide_turns`, `bloated_cell`) use `>`; "at least"
 * thresholds (`co_change`, `coupling_growth`, `rule_*`) use `>=`.
 */
export const detectDrift: DetectDrift = (map, facts, ui, history, t, previous = []) => {
  const mapper = createMapper(map);
  const paths = Object.keys(facts).sort();
  const known = new Set(paths);
  const out: Omit<DriftSignal, 'persisted'>[] = [];

  // Unplaced code, one signal per folder; and folders the map knows nothing about.
  const unassignedByDir = new Map<string, string[]>();
  const byTop = new Map<string, { all: number; unassigned: string[] }>();
  for (const p of paths) {
    const pl = mapper.place(p);
    if (pl.kind === 'unassigned') {
      const dir = p.includes('/') ? p.slice(0, p.lastIndexOf('/')) : '.';
      unassignedByDir.set(dir, [...(unassignedByDir.get(dir) ?? []), p]);
    }
    const top = topFolder(p);
    if (top && !TEST_FILE.test(p) && pl.kind !== 'ignored') {
      const e = byTop.get(top) ?? { all: 0, unassigned: [] };
      e.all++;
      if (pl.kind === 'unassigned') e.unassigned.push(p);
      byTop.set(top, e);
    }
  }
  for (const [dir, files] of unassignedByDir) {
    if (files.length > t.unassigned) out.push({ signal: 'unassigned', metric: `files in Unassigned under ${dir}/`, value: files.length, threshold: t.unassigned, scope: files });
  }
  for (const [top, e] of byTop) {
    if (e.all > 0 && e.unassigned.length === e.all) out.push({ signal: 'new_top_level', metric: `new top-level folder ${top}/ (no file on the map)`, value: e.all, threshold: 0, scope: e.unassigned });
  }

  // Turns too wide: median cells lit over the last N Harness turns (needs min(3, N) turns).
  const turns = history.filter((h) => h.source === 'turn').slice(-t.wideTurnsWindow);
  const lit = cellsLitPerUnit(mapper, facts, turns);
  if (lit.length >= Math.min(3, t.wideTurnsWindow) && median(lit) > t.wideTurnsMedian) {
    const domains = new Set<string>();
    for (const u of turns) for (const f of u.files) { const d = known.has(f) ? mapper.domainOf(f) : null; if (d) domains.add(domainId(d)); }
    out.push({ signal: 'wide_turns', metric: `median cells lit per turn (last ${t.wideTurnsWindow})`, value: round(median(lit)), threshold: t.wideTurnsMedian, scope: [...domains].sort() });
  }

  // Co-change across a boundary: file pairs in different domains edited together in >= K of the last N units.
  const pairs = new Map<string, number>();
  for (const u of history.slice(-t.coChangeWindow)) {
    if (isBulk(u.files, known)) continue;
    const placed = [...new Set(u.files)].filter((f) => known.has(f)).map((f) => ({ f, d: mapper.place(f) }))
      .flatMap(({ f, d }) => (d.kind === 'cell' ? [{ f, domain: d.domain }] : [])).sort((a, b) => a.f.localeCompare(b.f));
    for (let i = 0; i < placed.length; i++) for (let j = i + 1; j < placed.length; j++) {
      if (placed[i]!.domain === placed[j]!.domain) continue;
      const k = `${placed[i]!.f}\u0000${placed[j]!.f}`;
      pairs.set(k, (pairs.get(k) ?? 0) + 1);
    }
  }
  [...pairs].filter(([, n]) => n >= t.coChangeTurns).sort(([a, x], [b, y]) => y - x || a.localeCompare(b)).slice(0, 10).forEach(([k, n]) => {
    const [a, b] = k.split('\u0000') as [string, string];
    out.push({ signal: 'co_change', metric: `${a} and ${b} changed together (last ${t.coChangeWindow} turns or commits)`, value: n, threshold: t.coChangeTurns, scope: [a, b] });
  });

  // Coupling growth: importing files per directed domain pair now, vs before this log's turns added edges.
  const current = new Map<string, Set<string>>();
  const pairOf = (from: string, to: string) => {
    const a = mapper.place(from), b = mapper.place(to);
    return a.kind === 'cell' && b.kind === 'cell' && a.domain !== b.domain ? `${a.domain}\u0000${b.domain}` : null;
  };
  for (const f of Object.values(facts)) for (const to of repoImports(f)) {
    const k = pairOf(f.path, to);
    if (k) (current.get(k) ?? current.set(k, new Set()).get(k)!).add(f.path);
  }
  const added = new Set<string>();
  for (const turn of ui.turns) {
    for (const e of turn.edgesAdded) added.add(`${e.edge.from}\u0000${e.edge.to}`);
    for (const e of turn.edgesRemoved) added.delete(`${e.edge.from}\u0000${e.edge.to}`);
  }
  const grown = new Map<string, Set<string>>();
  for (const key of added) {
    const [from, to] = key.split('\u0000') as [string, string];
    const k = pairOf(from, to);
    if (k && facts[from] && repoImports(facts[from]!).includes(to)) (grown.get(k) ?? grown.set(k, new Set()).get(k)!).add(from);
  }
  for (const [k, g] of [...grown].sort(([a], [b]) => a.localeCompare(b))) {
    const [a, b] = k.split('\u0000') as [string, string];
    const base = (current.get(k)?.size ?? 0) - g.size;
    const scope = [domainId(a), domainId(b)];
    if (g.size >= t.couplingGrowthFiles) out.push({ signal: 'coupling_growth', metric: `files importing ${a} → ${b} added since the map was confirmed`, value: g.size, threshold: t.couplingGrowthFiles, scope });
    else if (base > 0 && g.size / base >= t.couplingGrowthRatio) out.push({ signal: 'coupling_growth', metric: `growth of ${a} → ${b} importing files since the map was confirmed`, value: round(g.size / base), threshold: t.couplingGrowthRatio, scope });
  }

  // Rule erosion and reinforcement, from invariants and recorded decisions (deduped by id).
  const decisions = [...new Map(ui.decisions.map((d) => [d.id, d])).values()];
  for (const inv of map.invariants) {
    const b = decisions.filter((d) => d.invariant === inv.id && d.option === 'B').length;
    if (inv.exceptions.length >= t.ruleErosionExceptions) out.push({ signal: 'rule_erosion', metric: `exceptions to ${inv.id}`, value: inv.exceptions.length, threshold: t.ruleErosionExceptions, scope: [`rule:${inv.id}`] });
    else if (b >= t.ruleErosionB) out.push({ signal: 'rule_erosion', metric: `option B (exception) chosen for ${inv.id}`, value: b, threshold: t.ruleErosionB, scope: [`rule:${inv.id}`] });
  }
  const reinforce = new Map<string, number>();
  for (const d of decisions) {
    if (d.option !== 'A') continue;
    const k = `${d.invariant}\u0000${(d.paths[0] && mapper.domainOf(d.paths[0])) ?? 'unassigned'}`;
    reinforce.set(k, (reinforce.get(k) ?? 0) + 1);
  }
  for (const [k, n] of [...reinforce].sort(([a], [b]) => a.localeCompare(b))) {
    const [inv, dom] = k.split('\u0000') as [string, string];
    if (n >= t.ruleReinforcement) out.push({ signal: 'rule_reinforcement', metric: `option A chosen for ${inv} in ${dom}`, value: n, threshold: t.ruleReinforcement, scope: [`rule:${inv}`, domainId(dom)] });
  }

  // Bloated cells: > N files, or > share of the domain (share rule only above N/2 files, so tiny domains never fire).
  for (const d of map.domains) {
    const sizes = Object.keys(d.cells).map((layer) => ({ layer, n: cellFiles(mapper, facts, d.id, layer).length }));
    const total = sizes.reduce((a, s) => a + s.n, 0);
    for (const { layer, n } of sizes) {
      const scope = [cellId(d.id, layer)];
      if (n > t.bloatedCellFiles) out.push({ signal: 'bloated_cell', metric: `files in ${d.id}/${layer}`, value: n, threshold: t.bloatedCellFiles, scope });
      else if (n > Math.ceil(t.bloatedCellFiles / 2) && n / total > t.bloatedCellShare) out.push({ signal: 'bloated_cell', metric: `share of ${d.id}'s files in ${layer}`, value: round(n / total), threshold: t.bloatedCellShare, scope });
    }
  }

  // Stale labels: what a label describes changed since it was written.
  const stale = Object.values(ui.labels).filter((l) => labelHash(mapper, facts, l) !== l.hash).map((l) => l.target).sort();
  if (stale.length) out.push({ signal: 'stale_label', metric: 'labels whose target changed', value: stale.length, threshold: 0, scope: stale });

  return out
    .sort((a, b) => KIND_ORDER.indexOf(a.signal) - KIND_ORDER.indexOf(b.signal) || a.scope.join().localeCompare(b.scope.join()))
    .map((s) => ({ ...s, persisted: (previous.find((p) => p.signal === s.signal && overlaps(p.scope, s.scope))?.persisted ?? 0) + 1 }));
};
```

```text
// Contract (NAVIGATION_PLAN §1, §3.2): one containment tree plus leaf edges; every level is a projection.
// Browser-safe: types and id helpers only. Implementations live in src/graph/ (Graph lane).
import type { CallConfidence, SymbolDiff } from './facts';

export type NodeKind =
  | 'repo'
  | 'domain'
  | 'cell'
  | 'group' // a directory or confirmed component inside a cell
  | 'file'
  | 'symbol'
  | 'table'
  | 'vendor' // bare package or external service not claimed by a cell
  | 'route'
  | 'entry'
  | 'unassigned' // pseudo-domain for files that match no cell
  | 'neutral' // shared code (domains.yaml `neutral`): never creates edges
  | 'tests'; // a domain's test files

export type GraphNode = {
  id: string;
  kind: NodeKind;
  parent: string | null;
  label: string;
  order: number; // stable sort key among siblings (model order for layout)
  domain?: string; // domain id, for nodes inside a domain
  layer?: string; // layer id, for cells and everything inside them
  path?: string; // repo path for files and groups (directory)
  symbol?: { kind: string; exported: boolean };
};

export type EdgeKind = 'imports' | 'calls' | 'implements' | 'handles' | 'writes' | 'reads' | 'uses' | 'fetches' | 'starts';

export type GraphEdge = {
  id: string; // edgeId(kind, from, to)
  kind: EdgeKind;
  from: string; // leaf node id
  to: string;
  count: number;
  owner: string; // the file whose facts produced it; replaced when that file changes
  confidence?: CallConfidence;
  typeOnly?: boolean;
};

export type ContextGraph = {
  root: string; // 'repo'
  nodes: Record<string, GraphNode>;
  children: Record<string, string[]>; // parent id → child ids, sorted by `order`
  edges: GraphEdge[];
};

/** View-only state held by the shell (not in the event log unless D5 says so). */
export type ViewState = {
  expanded: readonly string[];
  focus: string | null;
  lens: { kinds: readonly EdgeKind[]; turnOnly: boolean };
  budget: number; // max detailed visible nodes for autoExpand (DOI)
  follow: boolean;
};

export type ViolationState = 'existing' | 'new' | null;
export type ProposalMark = 'add' | 'move_in' | 'move_out' | 'remove' | 'rename' | null;

export type LeafActivity = {

  removed: number;
  created: boolean;
  unattributed: boolean;
  ghostSteps: number[]; // planned in these steps and not yet edited
  planned: boolean;
  unplanned: boolean; // edited, the turn has a plan, and this leaf is not in it
  violation: ViolationState;
  cursor: boolean;
  symbols: SymbolDiff | null; // for files: which symbols the turn changed
  audit: number; // open advisory findings
  proposal: ProposalMark; // pending cartographer proposal touching this leaf
};
```
