describe('edit gate budget', () => {
  const exists = fileExistsIn(fixtureRepo);
  const forbidden = 'import { chat } from "../../vendor/llm-openai/index";\n';
  /** Best of 5 gate calls on texts that are new each run (`i`), so nothing comes from the record cache unless `prime`. */
  const gate = (path: string, text: string, prime: boolean) => {
    const runs: number[] = [];
    for (let i = 0; i <= 5; i++) {
      const old = text + '\n'.repeat(i);
      if (prime) moduleRecord(path, old); // what the server's PostToolUse extraction leaves behind for the next edit
      const t = performance.now();
      const delta = deltaForEdit(path, old, forbidden + old, exists);
      if (i > 0) runs.push(performance.now() - t); // run 0 warms the native binding and wasm
      expect(delta.imports).toEqual([{ from: path, to: 'vendor/llm-openai/index.ts' }]);
    }
    return Math.min(...runs);
  };

  it('deltaForEdit stays under 20 ms on a ~1 MB generated file (woff2-wasm style), parsing both texts', () => {
    const blob = Buffer.alloc(720_000, 7).toString('base64');

    expect(gate('src/tools/generated.ts', text, true)).toBeLessThan(20);
  });

```sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# A fresh, disposable copy of Scout for one harness session.
#
# The original (../scout-agent) is never touched: each run clones it at a tag
# (default demo-start) into ../scout-run, so whatever the session changes
# (code, domains.yaml, decisions/, .harness/, the database) is thrown away next time.
#
# Usage: scripts/fresh-scout.sh [--map] [--with-data] [--keep] [--offline]
#   --map        start from fixtures/scout-agent.domains.yaml (skip the cartographer)
#   --with-data  copy the original's database (its runs and notes) instead of seeding a fresh one
#   --keep       keep the previous run as ../scout-run-<time> instead of deleting it
#   --offline    seed the offline sample companies instead of the live ones
#
# Environment: SCOUT_SRC (original), SCOUT_RUN_DIR (copy), SCOUT_REF (tag or commit), SCOUT_PORT (default 8788)
set -euo pipefail

here="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
src="$(cd "${SCOUT_SRC:-$here/../scout-agent}" && pwd)"
dest="${SCOUT_RUN_DIR:-$(dirname "$src")/scout-run}"
ref="${SCOUT_REF:-demo-start}"
port="${SCOUT_PORT:-8788}"

map=0 with_data=0 keep=0 mode="live"
for arg in "$@"; do
  case "$arg" in
    --map) map=1 ;;
    --with-data) with_data=1 ;;
    --keep) keep=1 ;;
    --offline) mode="offline" ;;
    -h|--help) sed -n '2,15p' "$0"; exit 0 ;;
    *) echo "unknown option: $arg" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
done

[[ "$dest" != "$src" ]] || { echo "refusing: the run directory is the original" >&2; exit 1; }
git -C "$src" rev-parse -q --verify "$ref^{commit}" >/dev/null || { echo "no $ref in $src" >&2; exit 1; }

# Copy-on-write where the filesystem supports it (APFS, btrfs), plain copy otherwise.
clone_path() {
  [[ -e "$1" ]] || return 0
  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$2")"
  cp -cR "$1" "$2" 2>/dev/null || cp -R --reflink=auto "$1" "$2" 2>/dev/null || cp -R "$1" "$2"
}

# Stop anything still serving the previous copy.
if pids="$(lsof -ti "tcp:$port" 2>/dev/null)" && [[ -n "$pids" ]]; then
  echo "stopping the process on :$port"
  kill $pids 2>/dev/null || true
  sleep 1
fi

if [[ -d "$dest" ]]; then
  if (( keep )); then
    mv "$dest" "$dest-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
  else
    rm -rf "$dest"
  fi
fi

echo "cloning $src @ $ref -> $dest"
git clone -q "$src" "$dest"
git -C "$dest" checkout -q -B session "$ref"
# No remote: nothing in the session can push back into the original.
git -C "$dest" remote remove origin

# Things git doesn't carry: dependencies, the API key, the SEC cache, the built web app.
clone_path "$src/node_modules" "$dest/node_modules"
clone_path "$src/.env" "$dest/.env"
clone_path "$src/.scout/cache" "$dest/.scout/cache"
clone_path "$src/web/dist" "$dest/web/dist"

cd "$dest"
if (( with_data )) && [[ -d "$src/.scout/pgdata" ]]; then
  if lsof -ti tcp:8787 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "note: something is running on :8787; if it's the original Scout, stop it first so its database is copied cleanly"
  fi
  clone_path "$src/.scout/pgdata" "$dest/.scout/pgdata"
  echo "copied the original's database"
else
  SCOUT_MODE="$mode" npm run --silent seed
fi
[[ -d web/dist ]] || npm run --silent build >/dev/null

if (( map )); then
  cp "$here/fixtures/scout-agent.domains.yaml" domains.yaml
  git add domains.yaml
  git -c user.name="Harness" -c user.email="harness@localhost" commit -qm "chore: add domains map"
  echo "added domains.yaml from fixtures"
fi

cat <<EOF

Fresh Scout at $dest (branch "session" at $ref; the original is untouched).

  Harness:  cd $here && HARNESS_REPO=$dest HARNESS_REPO_SLUG=johnz4021/scout-agent npm run dev
  Scout:    cd $dest && PORT=$port npm run dev:api      # app + API on http://localhost:$port, reloads server code

Run this script again for a clean slate. The web app is served prebuilt; after the agent edits web/, run "npm run build" in the copy.
EOF

```

3. The model call (injectable `auditor` function; real one = separate Agent SDK `query`, read-only tools, `settingSources: []`, `strictMcpConfig: true`, structured output: findings with decision id, files, lines, text, confidence; strongest model via `HARNESS_AUDITOR_MODEL` default `claude-opus-5-5`). Prompt: flag only likely contradictions of a standing decision's *rationale* that the three rule kinds can't express; cite lines; never restate rule violations the checker already caught; empty is the expected answer most of the time.
4. Emit `audit_finding` per finding (`AF-<n>` ids), `maintenance_run`. Dismissed findings (`POST /api/findings/:id/dismiss`) are remembered (same decision+file+text signature never re-raised — persist under `.harness/audit/dismissed.json`); `POST /api/findings/:id/promote` turns a finding into a rule proposal: emit a living-map style `map_proposed { proposal }` with a `change_rule`/`add_rule` change built deterministically when possible (e.g. a decision about a gateway mode → an `only_via`-style suggestion is often impossible; then emit the proposal with the rule text and let acceptance be manual) — keep it simple and documented.
5. **Rule reinforcement** (NAVIGATION_PLAN §4.4): when the same invariant gets option A ≥ 3 times (from `decision_recorded` events), propose a standing rule via the same proposal path (deterministic, no model).

**Journeys (N10, computation only; the overlay UI is a later lane)** — `packages/core/src/journeys/` (pure) + `apps/server/src/journeys/` (naming):
6. `computeJourneys(graph, facts) → Journey[]` (pure, tested): entries (FileFacts.entries: bin/scripts/cli/main/routes/pages) → wiring traces over calls ∪ implements ∪ handles to sinks (vendors, tables) using core `trace`; UI pages → `fetch` call sites → API routes by matching URL string literals / template prefixes (e.g. Scout's ``fetch(`/api${path}`)`` — mark `confidence: 'inferred'`) → the route's handler trace; branches where paths diverge; stable ids `journey:<slug of entry>`; deterministic.
7. Naming: an injectable namer (real one: small model, `HARNESS_JOURNEY_MODEL` default `claude-haiku-5-5`) gives each journey a product-language name ("Start research"), cached by a hash of the step list under `.harness/journeys/`; `inferred: true` until `POST /api/journeys/:id/confirm` (and rename via body `{name}`). # Harness navigation: build plan for the context graph

**Text in, architecture out, at every depth.** Today the map is one fixed level: a domain × layer grid. This plan turns it into a navigable context graph. You can move from journeys to domains to files to functions to code without losing your place, and the agent's live activity (reading, planning, editing, getting blocked) stays visible and rolled up at whatever depth you are looking at.

This plan extends `SPEC.md`; it does not replace it. Every rule in `CLAUDE.md` still holds: no model calls in the hot path, UI state is a reduction of the event log, one checker with three call sites, and Harness writes only to `domains.yaml`, `decisions/` and `.harness/` in the target.

Research behind this plan (October 2026): three surveys covering interaction and visual references, rendering and layout tech with benchmarks, and code-fact extraction with benchmarks. Their key numbers are quoted inline. Their sources include Sourcetrail, Structurizr/C4, IcePanel, Nx, Kiali, Windsurf Codemaps, van Wijk & Nuij 2003, Heer & Robertson 2007, Furnas's degree of interest, Holten's edge bundling, and Wedge.

## 1. Principles

1. **One fact graph, one containment tree, many projections.** There is a single graph:
   - *containment*: repo → domain → cell → file → symbol, plus tables, vendors, routes and entries;
   - *leaf edges*: imports, calls, writes, handles, uses, implements.

   Every level is a projection of that graph through the current *view*, meaning which nodes are expanded and where the focus is. Nothing is maintained twice. The Build Plan already called the levels rollups of one fact graph; this makes it literal.
2. **One coordinate system.** The domain × layer grid stays the anchor at every depth.
   - Expanding a domain widens its column in place. The other columns compress into thin spines that keep their badges.
   - Cells open *inside* the cell. A normal change stays a vertical stripe at every depth.
...

````text
1	# Harness navigation: build plan for the context graph
2	
3	**Text in, architecture out, at every depth.** Today the map is one fixed level: a domain × layer grid. This plan turns it into a navigable context graph. You can move from journeys to domains to files to functions to code without losing your place, and the agent's live activity (reading, planning, editing, getting blocked) stays visible and rolled up at whatever depth you are looking at.
4	
5	This plan extends `SPEC.md`; it does not replace it. Every rule in `CLAUDE.md` still holds: no model calls in the hot path, UI state is a reduction of the event log, one checker with three call sites, and Harness writes only to `domains.yaml`, `decisions/` and `.harness/` in the target.
6	
7	Research behind this plan (October 2026): three surveys covering interaction and visual references, rendering and layout tech with benchmarks, and code-fact extraction with benchmarks. Their key numbers are quoted inline. Their sources include Sourcetrail, Structurizr/C4, IcePanel, Nx, Kiali, Windsurf Codemaps, van Wijk & Nuij 2003, Heer & Robertson 2007, Furnas's degree of interest, Holten's edge bundling, and Wedge.
8	
9	## 1. Principles
10	
11	1. **One fact graph, one containment tree, many projections.** There is a single graph:
12	   - *containment*: repo → domain → cell → file → symbol, plus tables, vendors, routes and entries;
13	   - *leaf edges*: imports, calls, writes, handles, uses, implements.
14	
15	   Every level is a projection of that graph through the current *view*, meaning which nodes are expanded and where the focus is. Nothing is maintained twice. The Build Plan already called the levels rollups of one fact graph; this makes it literal.
16	2. **One coordinate system.** The domain × layer grid stays the anchor at every depth.
17	   - Expanding a domain widens its column in place. The other columns compress into thin spines that keep their badges.
18	   - Cells open *inside* the cell. A normal change stays a vertical stripe at every depth.
19	   - Spatial memory is the point. Kuhn et al. found that layouts clustered by topic confuse people; a stable cartographic layout helps them. Separate pages per level, as in Structurizr, lose your place every time you drill down.
20	3. **Depth is local, formalized as degree of interest (DOI).** What is visible is decided by an interest score with a budget.
21	   - Interest = how important a node is (planned, violating, the agent is there, edited this turn) minus its distance from your focus.
22	   - Expand until the budget is spent: about 20–30 detailed nodes in focus and at most about 50 visible entities. Path-finding gets hard above 50 nodes in dense graphs.
23	   - DOI decides *what* is visible. It never distorts geometry: Cockburn found fisheye distortion hurts target acquisition.
24	4. **Edges and activity roll up to the nearest visible ancestor.**
25	   - A rolled-up edge carries a count and its kinds, and the worst status by **max, never average** (Elmqvist & Fekete's aggregation guidelines). A violation three levels down is red at System level.
26	   - The agent cursor sits on the deepest visible ancestor of the file it is touching.
27	   - Edges that cross out of an expanded container leave through *ports* on its border (stubs).
28	5. **Facts win on structure, determinism first.**
29	   - Syntax facts are synchronous and cheap, and feed the gate and the live map.
30	   - Semantic facts (typed calls) are asynchronous and never block.
31	   - Model output (cartographer labels and proposals, auditor findings) is labelled as inferred. Structural changes need your confirmation, and nothing a model produces is trusted silently (§4).
32	6. **Motion encodes state changes only.**
33	   - Transitions are staged and interruptible, about 650 ms total. Heer & Robertson recommend about 1 s and "as long as needed, but no longer".
34	   - Nothing loops.
35	   - `prefers-reduced-motion` is honoured.
36	
37	## 2. Levels
38	
39	| Level | What you see | Built from | Entered by |
40	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
41	| **Journeys** | A numbered flow drawn *over* the System map, e.g. "Start research: UI page → `POST /api/runs` → run loop → tools → gateway → OpenAI". It plays back step by step and can branch. | Entries (routes, CLI, UI pages, `bin`), fetch → route matching, wiring traces. The cartographer names journeys; you confirm them. | Journey list (left rail) or ⌘K |
42	| **System** | The domain × layer grid, as today. Edges between domains carry a count and the worst status. | `domains.yaml` + facts | Default |
43	| **Domain** | One column expanded. Its cells become containers holding files, tables, vendors and routes, with edges inside the domain. Ports lead to the other columns, which are compressed. | Facts within the domain, ELK layout per cell | Double-click a column or cell, Enter, ⌘K |
44	| **Module** | One file expanded into rows for its symbols (functions, classes, methods, exported consts, routes). Call, write and use edges, one hop out. | Symbols and calls (syntactic first, typed later) | Double-click a file |
45	| **Code** | A docked code pane (CodeMirror 6) opened at the symbol. Gutters show this turn's diff, plan step badges and inline violations. | File text, the turn baseline, events | Double-click a symbol, or a path link in chat |
46	
47	Two things cut across the levels:
48	- **Wiring trace.** Pick an entry or symbol and Harness computes the call chain to its sinks (vendors, tables). It expands only along that path and dims everything else.
49	- **Turn lens.** "This turn only" hides everything the current turn didn't plan, read or edit.
50	
51	## 3. Architecture
52	
53	```
54	target repo ──► Tier 1 facts (sync, oxc) ──┐                         ┌──► edit gate: check(map, delta)  (unchanged)
55	   │                                        ├──► ContextGraph (core) ─┤
56	   └──────────► Tier 2 facts (async, tsgo) ─┘        ▲                └──► project(graph, view, activity) ─► shell
57	                                                     │                          ▲
58	event log ── reduce ─► activity per leaf ────────────┘          view state: expanded, focus, lens, follow
59	     ▲
60	     └── cartographer + auditor (async agents, §4): drift → proposals, labels, findings ── you accept / reject
61	```
62	
63	### 3.1 Facts (server)
64	
65	**Tier 1: syntax facts.** Synchronous and per file. Target ≤ 5 ms per file, with a hard cap of 20 ms because the edit gate uses them.
66	
67	- **Parser: oxc-parser** replaces the regex parser.
68	  - Measured on Scout, hono and excalidraw: 0.09–0.26 ms mean per file for imports and exports, and 0.4–1 ms with a full walk for symbols and calls.
69	  - The current regex takes **42 ms on one 972 KB generated file, so the gate takes over 80 ms**. That is a live bug (fix in N1).
70	- **Resolver: oxc-resolver** handles tsconfig `paths`, package `exports`/`imports` and workspaces, at 3–6 µs per import.
71	  - On excalidraw it resolves 3,347 of 4,096 imports; today's resolver gets 2,396.
72	  - Planned files that don't exist yet fall back to get-tsconfig `createPathsMatcher` plus the current resolver.
73	- **One pass collects:** imports and exports (with type-only flags), symbols, call sites (enclosing symbol and callee shape), writes, routes, and SQL literals.
74	- **Syntactic call edges** come from import bindings. Against typed edges on Scout they score 91–97% precision and 68–88% recall; the misses are mostly method calls.
75	- **Adapters:**
76	  - Writes: Scout's `db.insert/update`, Prisma, Drizzle, Knex, raw SQL (TypeORM comes in Tier 2).
77	  - Routes: Express, Hono, Fastify, Koa, and Next.js `app/` and `pages/`.
78	  - Entries: package.json `bin`/`scripts`, routes, UI routes.
79	  - Custom routers (like Scout's table of routes) use a pattern the user confirms in `domains.yaml`.
80	- **Size cap:** files over ~500 KB or minified use only the import/export record (2.6 ms at 972 KB).
81	- **`check()` keeps its signature.** The gate still checks only imports and writes. A `calls` field can be added to `FactDelta` later.
82	
83	**Tier 2: semantic facts.** Asynchronous, in a child process, never blocking.
84	
85	- **TypeScript 7 `typescript/unstable/sync`** (tsgo), pinned to 7.0.2, behind a `SemanticResolver` interface. The fallback is the TS 6 LanguageService (ts-morph).
86	  - Measured: opens a project in 0.07–0.42 s, and re-resolves a changed file in 1–8 ms.
87	  - The 7.0 blog says the API officially arrives in 7.1, which is why it is pinned and wrapped.
88	- **Produces** `calls` edges with `confidence: typed`, plus `implements` edges. Implements links a registry like Scout's `Tool.run` to its implementations, so traces can pass through dispatch.
89	- **Per file:** debounce ~150 ms, then `updateSnapshot` and re-resolve.
90	- **Results arrive as events** keyed by content hash. The reducer ignores results for stale hashes.
91	- **Python and Go (N11):** web-tree-sitter for syntax; pyright or gopls for semantics only when that toolchain is installed.
92	- **Rejected:**
93	  - stack-graphs: archived in September 2025.
94	  - SCIP: batch only, so at most for CI.
95	  - Graphify: name heuristics written in Python. It is a reference, not a dependency.
96	
97	**Ids stay stable across edits.** They never contain line numbers.
98	
99	| Kind | Id example |
100	| --- | --- |
101	| file | `src/tools/news-summarize.ts` |
102	| symbol | `src/tools/news-summarize.ts#newsSummarize.run` (`~2` for duplicates, `<cb1>` for anonymous callbacks) |
103	| route | `route:POST /api/runs` |
104	| table | `table:runs` |
105	| vendor | `vendor:vendor/llm-openai` or `vendor:@anthropic-ai/sdk` |
106	| entry | `entry:bin/scout`, `entry:page:/runs/{}` |
107	| journey | `journey:<slug>` |
108	
109	Edge kinds:
110	- `contains`
111	- `imports` (with a typeOnly flag)
112	- `calls` (with `{ confidence: syntactic | typed | dispatch, count }`)
113	- `implements`
114	- `handles`
115	- `writes` and `reads`
116	- `uses`
117	- `fetches`
118	- `starts`
119	
120	**Which symbols an edit changed.** Each symbol gets two hashes:
121	- `sigHash`: its normalized signature;
122	- `bodyHash`: its whitespace-normalized body.
123	
124	Compare them before and after the edit to classify each symbol as added, removed, signature changed, body changed, or renamed. Renamed means removed plus added with the same `bodyHash`. Measured cost is 1.6–2.4 ms per file, done in PostToolUse, which doesn't block. `edited` events gain `symbols: { added, removed, sig, body, renamed }`. Diffing a file's outgoing edges gives `call_added` and `call_removed` events, which work like `edge_added`.
125	
126	**Facts in the log stay pure.** Large fact sets go into content-addressed blobs under `.harness/facts/<hash>.json`, and events reference those blobs. The blobs never change, so replay stays a reduction. Events are snapshotted every N events so replay stays fast (N11).
127	
128	### 3.2 Core model (`packages/core`, pure, tested)
129	
130	- `buildGraph(map, facts, semantic?) → ContextGraph` builds the containment tree and the leaf edges. Files group by directory inside a cell when a cell holds more than about 12 files.
131	- `ViewState = { expanded: Set<id>, focus: id | null, lens: { kinds, turnOnly }, budget, follow }` is view-only state that lives in the shell. Replay reproduces the graph and activity. It reproduces the camera too, if we choose to log view events (decision D5).
132	- `project(graph, view, activity) → Projection` returns:
133	  - visible nodes, with rolled-up activity: looked, edited, +/−, ghost steps, worst violation (new or existing), cursor present, and counts;
134	  - aggregated edges, with count, kinds, worst status, ghost or new, and their own lane;
135	  - ports for edges that cross a boundary.
136	- `autoExpand(graph, activity, focus, budget) → expanded`: the DOI expansion used by Follow mode and the opening view.
137	- `trace(graph, from, sinks) → path[]`: shortest paths over `calls ∪ implements ∪ handles`. Hops within one cell are collapsed, and interface dispatch shows as "via registry".
138	- **Parity:** today's `cellViews` and `edgeViews` become `project()` with nothing expanded. Property tests over the demo log prove they give identical output.
139	- The activity reducer adds per-file and per-symbol state alongside the per-cell state it already tracks.
140	
141	### 3.3 Renderer (`apps/shell`)
142	
143	- **React Flow 12.12** (pinned `~12.12`; 13 is in prerelease) hosts the viewport and the DOM nodes.
144	  - Node components are memoized per id and subscribe to their own slice of the projection.
145	  - Edges are one SVG layer of precomputed paths: the existing gutter router at System level, and ELK's orthogonal sections inside containers.
146	  - Measured: zooming 500 nodes and 750 edges takes 4.5 ms per frame at p50. MIT licence. LikeC4 does drill-down on the same stack.
147	- **Layout:**
148	  - The top grid keeps today's deterministic `layout.ts`, with track sizes driven by the expanded children.
149	  - Each expanded container is laid out by **elkjs layered, one run per container, in a Web Worker**, bottom-up. Measured at about 100 ms for 500 files. One global hierarchical run took 2.4 s at 500 files and 11.5 s at 2,000.
150	  - Edgeless leaf sets use a `d3-hierarchy` treemap or ELK `rectpacking`.
151	  - Stability:
152	    - fixed node sizes per kind and level of detail;
153	    - input sorted by stable id, with `considerModelOrder` / `forceNodeModelOrder`;
154	    - a fixed seed, and interactive strategies when files are added live;
155	    - a cache keyed by a hash of the container, its children, its edges and the elkjs version;
156	    - vitest checks on how far positions move.
157	- **Transitions:** an xstate-style machine (as LikeC4 uses), cancellable at any point.
158	  1. Request the layout; the old frame stays on screen.
159	  2. 0–150 ms: fade out the edges that will change and the collapsing children.
160	  3. 150–450 ms: commit once, then **FLIP** the nodes with the Web Animations API, while the camera runs `fitBounds` in parallel. Measured at 3.6 ms per frame, against 40 ms per frame for calling `setNodes` every frame.
161	  4. 450–650 ms: new children fade in and edges draw in.
162	- **Camera:**
163	  - It follows the van Wijk & Nuij smooth zoom-and-pan path (ρ ≈ √2, via `d3.interpolateZoom` or React Flow's `interpolate: 'smooth'`, to be verified).
164	  - It is recomputed every frame, so Follow mode can retarget it mid-flight.
165	- **Level of detail by zoom bucket:**
166	  - far: chips with a fill and a count;
167	  - mid: titles;
168	  - near: full content and symbol rows.
169	
170	  Domain and layer headers render in screen space so they stay crisp. Labels hide below 16 px, and only the focused node's children are labelled.
171	- **Navigation chrome:**
172	  - breadcrumbs (Journey › Domain › Cell › Module › Symbol);
173	  - back/forward history;
174	  - a hideable minimap (80% of users preferred having one);
175	  - ⌘K over domains, files, symbols, routes, decisions, turns and plan steps;
176	  - keyboard: arrows move between spatial neighbours, Enter dives, Esc goes up, `f` toggles Follow, `t` toggles the turn lens.
177	- **Off-screen activity** gets **Wedge** indicators, which were more accurate than Halo and arrows in the study.
178	- **Large views:**
179	  - above about 1,000 visible nodes, the least interesting containers auto-collapse and everything drops to chips;
180	  - above about 3,000, Harness switches to a **Sigma.js v4** read-only overview (WebGL) fed from the same layout cache (N11).
181	- **Rollout:** the old grid stays behind `?map=v1` until N3 reaches parity.
182	
183	### 3.4 Agent-aware navigation: the graph as shared context
184	
185	- **Follow Claude.** The view auto-expands around where the agent is working, and the camera follows it with hysteresis: it moves only when the agent's visible ancestor changes. Any manual navigation stops following, with a "Following Claude · Stop" pill as in Figma.
186	- **Point.** Shift-click nodes to add them as chips in the composer. The message then carries the resolved paths and symbols. This was the Build Plan's "click cells to make them nouns".
187	- **Links back.** Paths and symbols in Claude's replies become links that fly the camera there. Plan steps in the approval card do the same.
188	- **Plan ghosts at every depth.** `submit_plan` steps can name symbols (`path#symbol`), so ghosts appear at Module level too. The step counter tracks individual files, not cells.
189	- **Blocked is unmistakable.** `gate_blocked` and `fork_asked` stand out at every zoom level, and a Wedge points at them when they are off screen.
190	- **Agent tools.** Extend the read-only harness MCP tools with `graph_neighbors(id, kinds, hops)`, `trace(from, to?)` and `symbols_in(path)`, so Claude queries the same graph you look at. These answer from the graph without any model call, and nothing about them goes into the brief.
191	
192	## 4. The living map: mapping and updating in production
193	
194	The map has three owners, and only one of them is a model that maintains it:
195	
196	| Layer | Owner | Updated |
197	| --- | --- | --- |
198	| **Facts:** files, imports, calls, writes, routes | Deterministic code (Tier 1 and Tier 2) | On every edit, in milliseconds. Never a model. |
199	| **Intent:** plans, fork answers | The coding agent proposes, the checker verifies, you decide | Every turn |
200	| **Meaning:** domains, boundaries, names, rules, journeys | **The cartographer**, a dedicated agent that runs continuously and proposes; you confirm | When drift is detected, at turn end, and when the repo is idle |
201	
202	The coding agent never maintains the map: it is the thing being observed, and bookkeeping would cost its context. A second agent, the **auditor**, reads finished turns against your standing decisions and raises advisory findings. Neither agent ever blocks the coding session.
203	
204	### 4.1 Four clocks
205	
206	| Clock | What runs | Latency | Can block Claude? |
207	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
208	| **Per edit, sync** | Tier 1 facts for the edited file, the edit gate, map events (`edited`, `edge_added`, symbol diff) | ≤ 20 ms | Only the gate, deterministically |
209	| **Per edit, async** | Tier 2 typed calls for that file; label refresh for symbols whose `bodyHash` changed | 150 ms – 2 s | No |
210	| **Per turn end** | Drift metrics (deterministic); the cartographer, if a signal fired; the auditor's review of the turn | Seconds | No. Results queue as proposals and findings |
211	| **Idle or big change** | Full re-survey: the cartographer generates and scores candidate maps over all history. Triggered by idle time, a merge or branch switch, or a new package | Minutes | No |
212	
213	Your accept/reject of a proposal runs on human time and never holds up a turn.
214	
215	### 4.2 Onboarding a repo
216	
217	1. **Instant skeleton (under 1 s, no model).** Tier 1 scans the repo. A deterministic first map (one domain per top-level source folder, layers from folder-name heuristics) renders straight away, so you are never looking at a spinner.
218	2. **History mining (seconds, no model).** `git log` provides co-change pairs (files changed in the same commit) and "commit footprints". Commits act as stand-in turns, so the map can be scored before Harness has run a single turn.
219	3. **Cartographer proposal (about a minute, model).** It generates K candidate maps (default 4). Each is scored deterministically (§4.5), and the best is shown assembling on the grid with its scores, for example "a typical commit lights 1.8 cells; 0 files unassigned".
220	4. **You confirm** (or pick another candidate, or edit in chat: "merge Memory into Agent loop"). `domains.yaml` is committed.
221	5. **Background fill-in.** Tier 2 indexes typed calls. The cartographer adds inferred labels: sub-group names inside domains, one-line symbol summaries, journey names.
222	
223	### 4.3 Steady state while you build
224	
225	| Happens during a turn | Deterministic update (immediate) | Model follow-up (async) |
226	| --- | --- | --- |
227	| Edit to a file already in a cell | Facts, edges, symbol diff, activity | Re-summarize changed symbols (cached by `bodyHash`) |
228	| New file that matches a cell's globs | Placed in that cell | Label it, if it starts a new sub-group |
229	| New file that matches nothing | Unassigned, with an instant faint guess ("probably Billing?") from its folder siblings and the majority domain of what it imports | Placement proposal at turn end |
230	| New folder or workspace package | Unassigned, and the guess is shown | A proposal at turn end for a new domain or a new cell |
231	| `submit_plan` | Ghosts, plan check | The plan text goes to the cartographer as intent context (purposes, sub-group names) |
232	| Fork answered | DR file, `domains.yaml` update (committed) | The auditor and cartographer read the new decision |
233	| Turn ends | Drift metrics recomputed | If a signal fired: scoped cartographer run, then a proposal. Auditor review runs either way |
234	
235	The cartographer never runs on half-finished edits. Its proposals wait for `turn_ended`, and the only thing shown mid-turn is the instant deterministic guess.
236	
237	### 4.4 Drift signals
238	
239	These are deterministic and computed from facts plus the event log. Thresholds are configurable under a `cartography:` key in `domains.yaml`. A signal must persist across two turns before it triggers anything, so one odd turn doesn't cause churn.
240	
241	| Signal | Metric | Default threshold | Likely proposal |
242	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
243	| Unplaced code | Files in Unassigned after `turn_ended` | > 0 | Place them, or add a cell or domain |
244	| **Turns too wide** | Median cells lit per turn over the last 10 turns (the Build Plan's size test, now measured) | > 3 | Re-cut domains |
245	| **Co-change across a boundary** | File pairs in different domains edited together in ≥ 3 of the last 20 turns or commits | Any pair | Move a file, or merge two domains |
246	| Coupling growth | Cross-domain edges between one pair of domains | +50% or +5 files since the map was confirmed | Review that boundary |
247	| Rule erosion | An invariant's exceptions, or option B answers to it | ≥ 3 exceptions, or B chosen twice | Loosen, split or retire the rule |
248	| Rule reinforcement | The same decision pattern (A on the same invariant for similar files) | 3 times | Propose a standing rule (auditor) |
249	| Bloated cell | Files in a cell | > 25, or > 40% of its domain | Split the cell or add sub-groups |
250	| New top-level code | New top-level folder or workspace package | Any | New domain |
251	| Stale label | A symbol's `bodyHash` changed since its summary was written | Any | Regenerate automatically |
252	
253	### 4.5 The cartographer
254	
255	**Runtime.** A separate Agent SDK session out of process, on the strongest model at high effort.
256	- Tools: read-only file tools plus the harness graph tools (`graph_neighbors`, `trace`, `symbols_in`, and new `map_metrics` and `history`).
257	- Settings: no user settings and no write tools.
258	- It never edits product code, never touches the coding session, and never changes `domains.yaml` without your accept.
259	
260	**Input, scoped to the trigger:**
261	- the affected domains plus one hop;
262	- recent turns (prompts, plans, footprints);
263	- standing decisions and their rationale;
264	- git co-change;
265	- the current `domains.yaml`;
266	- **every proposal you have rejected**, which it must not repeat.
267	
268	**Output** is structured JSON. The schema covers:
269	- placements;
270	- cell moves;
271	- domain new, split, merge or rename;
272	- purpose rewrites;
273	- rule add, retire or loosen;
274	- labels: sub-groups, symbol summaries, journey names.
275	
276	**Candidates are scored deterministically, not by the model's own opinion.** Each candidate is scored by `scoreMap(map, facts, history)` in core, which is pure and tested:
277	- mean and median cells lit when past turns and commits are replayed against the candidate;
278	- modularity of the import graph across the candidate's domains;
279	- unassigned count, and how unevenly cell sizes are spread;
280	- how many existing decisions it would break;
281	- churn: how many files move, and how many ids change.
282	
283	Only a candidate that beats the current map by a margin is shown, and between similar scores the smaller change wins.
284	
285	**Stability rules:**
286	- A rename keeps the `id`; only the `name` changes.
287	- Moving files is preferred over re-cutting domains.
288	- At most one structural proposal is pending per domain.
289	- An accepted proposal never reshuffles layout outside its scope. The per-container layout cache (§3.3) guarantees this.
290	
291	**Proposals use the same UI as plans.**
292	- The change is shown as ghosts: a proposed column dashed, files sliding in preview to their proposed cells, a rule badge dashed.
293	- Scores sit next to it: "turns would light 2.1 cells instead of 4.3 · 3 files move · no decisions broken".
294	- In chat you can accept, reject or amend ("yes, but call it Billing").
295	- Accepting writes and commits `domains.yaml` and emits `map_confirmed`.
296	- Rejecting is recorded as a decision (`decisions/DR-n.md`, `status: rejected`), so the cartographer never proposes that change again. This is the same "rejected options stay rejected" memory that forks use.
297	
298	**Labels are applied automatically and marked as inferred.**
299	- Sub-group names, symbol summaries and journey names carry no rule weight. They are stored as content-addressed files under `.harness/labels/` and shown with an "inferred" marker.
300	- Confirming one moves it into `domains.yaml` (cells gain optional `components: [{ id, name, paths }]`).
301	- Each label is regenerated only when the hash of what it describes changes.
302	
303	### 4.6 The auditor
304	
305	**When it runs:**
306	- **after every turn**, on the turn's symbol-level diff, plan, decisions and fact delta;
307	- optionally **on each submitted plan**. Its note appears on the approval card while you read it; it never blocks Approve.
308	
309	**What it checks:** whether the work contradicts your standing decisions in ways the three rule kinds can't express. For example: "DR-4 says filings go through the gateway with `redaction: "filings"`; `src/tools/filing-summarize.ts:31` calls `complete()` without it."
310	
311	**Output:**
312	- **Advisory findings**, each with a confidence, the lines it refers to, and the decision it cites.
313	- They show as an "audit" badge (amber outline, inferred marker) at every level and are counted separately from the exact ledger.
314	- You can dismiss a finding (recorded, so it won't come back) or **promote** it into an enforced rule. Promoting goes through the cartographer's proposal flow.
315	
316	**Rule mining:** when the same choice keeps being made (reinforcement, §4.4), it proposes making that choice a standing rule.
317	
318	### 4.7 Events
319	
320	The new events are all in the log, so the UI is still a reduction and replay covers maintenance too. Large payloads such as candidate maps and label sets live in content-addressed blobs that events reference.
321	
322	- `drift_detected { signal, metric, value, threshold, scope }`
323	- `map_proposed` (extended): `{ proposal: id, trigger, candidates: blob, chosen, scores, changes, rationale }`
324	- `map_proposal_resolved { proposal, outcome: accepted | rejected | amended, decision? }`
325	- `labels_updated { blob, scope }`
326	- `audit_finding { id, decision?, files, lines, text, confidence }` and `audit_resolved { id, outcome: dismissed | promoted }`
327	- `maintenance_run { agent: cartographer | auditor, trigger, ms, cost }`. This feeds a separate Maintenance panel and never the ledger.
328	
329	### 4.8 Guarantees
330	
331	1. **Claude never waits on any model but itself.** The gate stays deterministic, and maintenance agents run out of process.
332	2. **The structure of the map changes only with your consent.** Every change is a commit to `domains.yaml` with a decision record, so it can be reviewed in a PR like any other change.
333	3. **Everything a model produced is marked inferred and cites its source.** Confidence is always visible.
334	4. **Map quality is measured, not asserted.** Turn width, co-change across boundaries and unassigned count show in a small map-health readout, and a trend over turns tells you when the map is going stale.
335	5. **It degrades gracefully.** If the cartographer or auditor is down, the map stays exact and live; only new labels, proposals and findings stop.
336	
337	### 4.9 Teams and branches
338	
339	- **The map lives in git.** `domains.yaml` and `decisions/` live in the repo, so each branch has its own map, and switching branches reloads it (an idle-clock trigger). Map changes from teammates arrive through ordinary PRs, with small diffs from the minimal-edit writer.
340	- **Conflicts are proposals.** Two people's accepted proposals that conflict in `domains.yaml` are resolved like any merge conflict. The cartographer can propose the merged map.
341	- **Multiplayer** (vision): one shared live map, with each teammate's agent as a separate cursor. The cartographer runs once per repo, not per person.
342	
343	## 5. Visual direction (decision D1)
344	
345	1. **Atlas (cartographic blueprint).** Calm and print-like.
346	   - Nested containers separated by hairlines, with one step of elevation per level.
347	   - A lightness ramp by depth (LCH theme from three inputs: base, accent and contrast).
348	   - Orthogonal edges routed through ports.
349	   - Map-style label placement with 300 ms fades.
350	   - **The agent is the only saturated colour.** Red and amber are reserved for rules.
351	   - Risk: it can look static, so liveness depends on small cues.
352	2. **Control Room (live telemetry).** Dark mission control in the spirit of Kiali and Datadog: dots flowing along active edges, arc rings showing each domain's status mix, glow on focus.
353	   - Risks: it turns into a Christmas tree, glow competes with violation red, and **continuous flow breaks the "nothing loops" rule**.
354	3. **Strata (depth-of-field canvas).** You literally fly into a cell.
355	   - Parent levels fade to about 10% opacity with a slight blur.
356	   - Typography changes with zoom.
357	   - The camera moves first, then the expansion happens, then edges appear.
358	   - Risks: blur is expensive, and it's easy to get lost without strong breadcrumbs and Wedges.
359	
360	**Recommendation:** use Atlas as the base system, add Strata's camera and depth fade for transitions, and borrow one thing from Control Room: a single pulse that travels once along an edge when it is used or added, never looping.
361	
362	## 6. Phases
363	
364	| # | Build | Done when |
365	| --- | --- | --- |
366	| N0 | **Spike** (1–2 days, alongside N1/N2) | React Flow + ELK in a worker + FLIP + the camera, on real Scout facts and real node components. Research Tools expands from System to Domain level with ports. Zooming 500 nodes stays under 16.7 ms per frame at p95; a transition commit takes under 50 ms; the camera path is verified. Three static design comps (Atlas, Control Room, Strata) go to you for D1. Go/no-go on the stack. |
367	| N1 | **Tier 1 facts on oxc** | oxc-parser and oxc-resolver replace the regex parser and resolver, keeping `check()`'s signature. The gate stays under 20 ms on the 972 KB file. Path aliases and workspaces resolve. Symbols, syntactic calls, routes and write adapters work. Edits report which symbols changed. All 49 existing tests pass, plus new ones. Scout still has exactly one violation on load. |
368	| N2 | **ContextGraph, `project`, `autoExpand`** in core | Pure and tested. Parity tests show that `project()` with nothing expanded gives exactly today's `cellViews` and `edgeViews` on the demo log. Rollups use max severity. Ports and edge aggregation are covered by unit tests. |
369	| N3 | **New renderer at System parity** | Every current state works on React Flow: looked, edited, ghost, unplanned, existing and new violations, cursor, diff badges, edge lanes, inspector, replay and ledger. The demo turn looks at least as good as v1, which stays behind `?map=v1`. |
370	| N4 | **Domain level** | Expand and collapse in place. Sibling columns compress into spines. Ports and stubs. Aggregated edges show counts and the worst status. Staged transitions. Breadcrumbs, history, ⌘K, keyboard, minimap. Positions move less than a set threshold across edits (vitest). |
371	| N5 | **Living map: drift signals + cartographer** | `scoreMap` and every drift metric in core, pure and tested, including replaying past turns and git history. On a Scout copy, adding `src/billing/` with three files gives an instant faint guess mid-turn, then at turn end a scored proposal ("new domain Billing") shown as ghosts. Accept commits `domains.yaml`. Reject records a decision and is never proposed again. Onboarding produces the instant skeleton, then K scored candidates. Inferred sub-group labels appear in Domain view. |
372	| N6 | **Module level + Code pane** | Symbol rows and call edges (syntactic). Each symbol shows its own state (edited, ghost, violation). The CodeMirror pane shows the turn diff and step badges. A plan that names `path#symbol` shows symbol ghosts. |
373	| N7 | **Agent-aware navigation** | Follow Claude with hysteresis. Wedge indicators. Point → chips in the composer. Path links in chat. Blocked and fork states are visible at every level. The demo turn can be watched hands-free in Follow mode. |
374	| N8 | **Tier 2 semantic facts + Trace** | A tsgo child process sends typed calls and implements as events keyed by content hash. Edges are styled by confidence. Trace mode finds `routes.ts → … → vendor/llm-openai` through the tool registry. The agent's graph tools work. |
375	| N9 | **Auditor** | After each turn, findings are checked against standing decisions. On Scout, a filings tool that calls `complete()` without `redaction: "filings"` produces an advisory finding that cites DR-4 and the line. Dismiss is recorded. Promote turns it into a rule proposal. The ledger counters don't change. Optional plan review shows a note on the approval card. |
376	| N10 | **Journeys** | Entries are discovered, fetches are matched to routes, and journeys are computed. The cartographer names them asynchronously and you confirm. Overlay with numbered steps and playback. "Start research" on Scout plays end to end. |
377	| N11 | **Real-world scale and languages** | tree-sitter for Python and Go. A cartographer for large repos that works from sampled directory summaries. The Sigma overview above 3,000 nodes. Log snapshots. Performance budgets checked in CI. Tried on hono and excalidraw-sized repos. |
378	
379	N0, N1 and N2 can run in parallel. N3 starts after the N0 go/no-go. N5 needs N4, because proposals render as ghosts in the expanded views; its scoring and metrics (core only) can start alongside N2. The hackathon demo keeps working on v1 throughout.
380	
381	## 7. Risks
382	
383	| Risk | Mitigation |
384	| --- | --- |
385	| Layout jumps on small changes, losing the mental map | Layout per container, model order, fixed sizes, cache, interactive strategies, and position-delta tests |
386	| TS 7's API is officially unstable until 7.1 | Pin 7.0.2 behind `SemanticResolver`, with a TS 6 fallback. Tier 2 is optional; everything works on Tier 1 |
387	| oxc is pre-1.0 and ships weekly | Pin it. Its AST follows the ESTree shape, which limits churn |
388	| Performance falls short of the headless benchmarks | N0 spike on target hardware with real node components; budgets checked in CI |
389	| Edge clutter at Domain level | Aggregate edges, show only the focused node's edges by default, add lenses, and show counts as stroke width |
390	| Dynamic dispatch (registries, DI, events) breaks traces | `implements` edges; show `dispatch`/`inferred` confidence; never present a trace as complete |
391	| The event log grows large | Content-addressed fact blobs and snapshots |
392	| Licences | elkjs is dual EPL-2.0/GPL-3.0; using it unmodified is fine (get a legal check before shipping). libavoid is LGPL, optional and dynamically loaded. Avoid Cosmograph's CC-BY-NC packages and tldraw, which needs a licence key |
393	| The cartographer churns the map (a constant stream of proposals, or boundaries that keep moving) | Signals must persist across two turns; a proposal must beat the current map's score by a margin; one pending proposal per domain; rejections are permanent; churn counts against a candidate's score |
394	| Auditor false positives cause alert fatigue | Advisory only, with confidence shown; dismissals are permanent; findings sit outside the ledger; tune it on recorded turns before turning it on by default |
395	| Maintenance agents' cost and time on big repos | Scoped runs (affected domains plus one hop); content-hash caches for labels; full re-survey only when idle |
396	| Scope | Each phase leaves something you can demo; v1 stays the fallback |
397	
398	## 8. Decisions for you
399	
400	- **D1 Visual direction:** Atlas, Control Room, Strata, or the recommended hybrid. N0 produces comps to choose from.
401	- **D2 Navigation model:** the recommended nested grid driven by DOI (one coordinate system, expand in place), or a free infinite canvas with continuous semantic zoom (more cinematic, easier to get lost in).
402	- **D3 Semantic tier:** accept TS 7's unstable API, pinned with a fallback (recommended), or stay on TS 6 / ts-morph (stable, slower, more memory).
403	- **D4 Order:** agent-aware navigation (N7) before or after the living map (N5) and the deep levels (N6)? Recommended: N5 first, because it closes the gap in keeping meaning current; move N7 up if the demo matters sooner.
404	- **D5 Camera in replay:** should replay reproduce where you were looking? That means logging view events, and the camera becomes part of the record.
405	- **D6 Motion rule:** keep SPEC §11's "nothing loops". This rules out continuous particle flow.
406	- **D7 Labels:** apply inferred labels automatically (recommended, marked as inferred), or require confirmation for every label too?
407	- **D8 Auditor on plans:** review each submitted plan, adding a few seconds before its note appears on the approval card without blocking Approve, or review only finished turns?
408	- **D9 Drift thresholds:** start with the defaults in §4.4 and tune them on recorded Scout turns, or keep proposals manual-only ("re-map" button) at first?

1	# Harness: build spec
2	
3	**Text in, architecture out.** Harness is a diagram-first shell around real Claude Code. You talk to the agent in a chat pane; a domain × layer map of the target repo shows, live, what each turn plans and does to the architecture; and the agent stops to ask you before it crosses a rule. Decisions you make become rules that later sessions are checked against.
4	
5	The theme is giving people time back. Agents made writing code nearly free, but understanding and checking it did not get cheaper. Every feature below exists to cut reading, rework or re-explaining, and the time ledger counts those savings.
6	
7	## 1. Repos
8	
9	Two separate git repos, side by side:
10	
11	```
12	workspace/
13	  harness/        this tool (npm workspaces monorepo)
14	  scout-agent/    the demo target, built separately from DEMO_REPO_SPEC.md
15	```
16	
17	The target must be its own repo. The coding agent runs with its working directory there, the map is computed over it, and `domains.yaml` plus `decisions/` are committed into it. The tool's own code must never appear on the map.
18	
19	```
20	harness/
21	  package.json              npm workspaces
22	  packages/core/            pure TypeScript, no I/O beyond fs reads; fully unit-tested
23	    src/schema.ts           zod schema for domains.yaml
24	    src/events.ts           event types and the reducer
25	    src/mapper.ts           path → cell, table → owner
26	    src/imports.ts          regex import parser + relative-path resolver
27	    src/writes.ts           db.insert / db.update scanner
28	    src/facts.ts            whole-repo scan: files, imports, writes, cross-domain edges
29	    src/rules.ts            the invariant checker (one function, three call sites)
30	    src/plan.ts             plan → ghost footprint
31	    src/ledger.ts           per-turn and session counters
32	    test/                   uses fixtures/scout-agent.domains.yaml
33	  apps/server/              Node + Hono + ws + @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk
34	    src/index.ts            HTTP + websocket; serves the shell in production
35	    src/bus.ts              append-only event log (.harness/events.jsonl in the target) + broadcast
36	    src/repo.ts             load, full scan, file watcher
37	    src/session.ts          the coding session (streaming input, modes, hooks, canUseTool)
38	    src/harness-tools.ts    in-process MCP server: submit_plan, cell_for, domain, who_writes, decisions_for
39	    src/turns.ts            turn lifecycle, git baselines, turn records
40	    src/decisions.ts        decisions/DR-n.md, invariant updates, Alike instructions
41	    src/cartographer.ts     one-shot map proposal
42	  apps/shell/               Vite + React + Zustand
43	  fixtures/scout-agent.domains.yaml
44	```
45	
46	Run: `HARNESS_REPO=../scout-agent npm run dev` (server on 4310, shell on 5173).
47	
48	## 2. Hard rules
49	
50	1. **No model calls in the hot path.** Hooks, the mapper, the import parser and the rule checker are deterministic and fast. Model calls (the cartographer) never block the coding session.
51	2. **Every piece of UI state is a pure reduction of the event log.** Footprint, ghosts, ledger, summary, provenance and replay are all `reduce(events)`. Replay is "reduce up to index i".
52	3. **Harness writes to the target repo only in three places:** `domains.yaml`, `decisions/`, `.harness/` (gitignored). The coding session is the only thing that edits product code.
53	4. **Facts win on structure, the user wins on meaning, the agent wins only on stated intent**, and intent is always checked against facts.
54	
55	## 3. The map (`domains.yaml`)
56	
57	Schema: see `fixtures/scout-agent.domains.yaml`. Domains are columns, layers are rows (rows come from the file, not hard-coded). Each cell lists path globs and, for data cells, owned tables. `neutral` paths never create edges; `ignore` paths are skipped. Files that match no cell land in an **Unassigned** column.
58	
59	**Tests** are assigned to a domain by its `tests` globs. A test file counts as part of that domain for the rule checker's import rules and the footprint and is listed in the inspector, but it is not drawn in a cell and draws no edges. Tests may write any table: seeding fixture rows is setup, not a product write, so `owns_writes` skips them.
60	
61	**Edges are derived, never declared.** A cross-domain edge exists when a file in domain A imports a file in domain B. Flow down a column is implied and not drawn. The import parser handles `import … from '…'`, `import('…')` and `export … from '…'`. It resolves relative paths by trying the specifier as written, then `.ts`, `.tsx`, `/index.ts`, `/index.tsx`, and maps a `.js` specifier to `.ts`. It ignores bare package and `node:` imports (Scout has none that matter).
62	
63	**Writes:** a regex scan for `db.insert(` and `db.update(` followed by a string literal in any quote style gives `{file, table}` pairs.
64	
65	## 4. Invariants: one checker, three call sites
66	
67	```ts
68	type Violation = { invariant: string; reason: string; file: string; detail: string; options: [string, string] };
69	function check(map: DomainMap, delta: FactDelta): Violation[];
70	```
71	
72	`FactDelta` is a set of added imports and added writes, each with its source file. The three kinds:
73	
74	| Kind | Fires when |
75	| --- | --- |
76	| `only_via` | a file outside `allowed_from` domains imports a `targets` path |
77	| `owns_writes` | a file outside the owner domain writes the table |
78	| `no_edge` | a file in `from` imports a file in `to` |
79	
80	Exceptions (paths) suppress a violation. Each violation carries two options: **A** comply (for `only_via` on Scout: "route through `gateway.complete()`"), **B** add an exception for this path and record why.
81	
82	The three call sites, all using the same function:
83	
84	1. **Load:** full repo scan. On Scout, finds exactly one: DR-1 in `src/tools/news-summarize.ts`. It shows red on load.
85	2. **Plan:** run on the declared dependencies and files in `submit_plan`.
86	3. **Edit:** run in the `PreToolUse` hook on the imports and writes that the edit would add (diff the `new_string`/`content` against the current file).
87	
88	## 5. Events
89	
90	```ts
91	type HarnessEvent = {
92	  id: string; t: number;
93	  session: string;          // coding session id
94	  turn: string | null;
95	  kind:
96	    | 'repo_scanned' | 'map_proposed' | 'map_confirmed' | 'file_assigned'
97	    | 'violation_found'
98	    | 'turn_started' | 'looked' | 'cursor'
99	    | 'planned' | 'plan_violation' | 'fork_asked' | 'fork_answered' | 'plan_approved'
100	    | 'gate_blocked' | 'edited' | 'edge_added' | 'edge_removed'
101	    | 'test_result' | 'decision_recorded' | 'turn_ended';
102	  cell?: { domain: string; layer: string };
103	  path?: string;
104	  data?: Record<string, unknown>;   // e.g. { step: 2 }, { added: 18, removed: 2 }, { invariant: 'DR-1' }
105	};
106	```
107	
108	The server appends every event to `.harness/events.jsonl` and broadcasts it over the websocket. The shell holds the array and derives everything from it.
109	
110	## 6. The coding session
111	
112	One long-lived streaming session:
113	
114	```ts
115	query({
116	  prompt: chatMessages(),                     // AsyncIterable<SDKUserMessage> fed by the chat pane
117	  options: {
118	    cwd: REPO,
119	    permissionMode: 'plan',
120	    systemPrompt: { type: 'preset', preset: 'claude_code', append: brief() },
121	    mcpServers: { harness: harnessTools },    // createSdkMcpServer; user-scope MCP servers (Alike) still load
122	    allowedTools: ['mcp__harness__*', 'mcp__alike__record_decision', 'mcp__alike__resolve_work_item', 'mcp__alike__describe_entity_kind'],
123	    hooks: { PreToolUse: [...], PostToolUse: [...] },
124	    canUseTool,                                // intercepts ExitPlanMode for approval
125	  },
126	});
127	```
128	
129	**`brief()`** contains: the map (domains, purposes, cell paths), every standing decision from `decisions/` (with the invariant it qualifies and the option it rejected), and these rules:
130	
131	> Before editing anything, call `mcp__harness__submit_plan` with numbered steps. Each step lists the exact file paths it will create or modify and any new imports it adds (from path → to path). If the result contains violations, stop and ask the user to choose between the two options it gives, in one short message, then wait. Never work around a violation. After the user answers, resubmit the plan, then exit plan mode.
132	
133	The brief does **not** list the seeded invariants (`source: cartographer`). They are enforced at plan and edit time instead. Stated up front, they would make the agent comply silently, so the user never sees the choice and nothing gets recorded. Once the user answers a fork, the resulting decision is in every later brief, and the next session follows it without asking. That contrast, asked once and then remembered, is the memory beat of the demo.
134	
135	**Turn flow:**
136	
137	1. User message → `turn_started` (record `git rev-parse HEAD` and a `git stash create` snapshot as the baseline).
138	2. Plan mode: Claude reads (`looked`, `cursor`), then calls `submit_plan`. The server maps paths to cells, builds ghost cells and ghost edges, and runs the checker → `planned` (+ `plan_violation`). The tool result returns the ghost summary and, if violated, the reason plus options A/B with an instruction to ask.
139	3. Claude asks → `fork_asked`. The user answers in chat → `fork_answered` → decision written (§8). Claude resubmits.
140	4. Claude calls `ExitPlanMode` → `canUseTool` holds it, the shell shows an **Approve plan** button (typing "approve" also works) → `plan_approved` → allow, then `session.setPermissionMode('acceptEdits')`.
141	5. Edits: hooks emit `cursor`, `gate_blocked`, `edited`, `edge_added` / `edge_removed`. Ghost cells fill as their files are edited; the step counter advances.
142	6. Result message → `turn_ended` with the plan-versus-built diff and git `--numstat` totals; write `.harness/turns/<id>.json`; `setPermissionMode('plan')` for the next turn.
143	
144	**Hooks:**
145	
146	| Hook | Matcher | Does | Blocking |
147	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
148	| PreToolUse | `Read\|Grep\|Glob` | `looked` + `cursor` for the file or search path | no (return `{ async: true }`) |
149	| PreToolUse | `Edit\|Write\|MultiEdit` | run the checker on the added imports/writes; on a hit return `permissionDecision: 'deny'` with the reason, options and "ask the user"; emit `gate_blocked` | yes, deterministic, < 20 ms |
150	| PostToolUse | `Edit\|Write\|MultiEdit` | `edited` (+/− lines), recompute that file's imports → edge events | no |
151	| PostToolUse | `Bash` | if the command ran `vitest`, parse results → `test_result` per test domain (stretch) | no |
152	
153	**File watcher** (chokidar on the target, minus `ignore`): any write not already reported by a hook becomes an `edited` event marked `unattributed`. Hooks give attribution and gating; the watcher guarantees completeness, since shell commands can write files without passing through the edit hooks.
154	
155	**Harness MCP tools** (all read-only except `submit_plan`, which only records intent): `submit_plan(steps[{ n, text, files[], imports[{ from, to }] }])`, `cell_for(path)`, `domain(id)`, `who_writes(table)`, `decisions_for(paths[])`.
156	
157	## 7. Plan versus built
158	
159	- **Ghosts:** planned cells are drawn dashed with their step numbers; planned edges are dashed; a ghost that violates an invariant is red.
160	- **Fill-in:** a ghost cell turns solid when a file mapped to it is edited.
161	- **End-of-turn diff:** planned and done is solid; planned and not done stays a ghost; **done but not planned is amber**, which is how the map shows the agent straying from its own plan.
162	- **New versus existing violations:** a violation found on load is drawn red, with a badge on its cell counting the files involved. A violation raised by this turn's plan or edits must look different from the map before the turn, even when it repeats an existing one (on Scout, the 10-K plan copies `news-summarize.ts` into the same red cell and toward the same provider). Its ghost edge gets its own lane, offset from any solid edge between the same cells, and the cell gets a separate **new** badge naming the file.

165	
166	When a fork is answered:
167	
168	1. Write `decisions/DR-<n>.md` with front matter `{ id, title, outcome, status: made, type: standing, invariant, anchors: { paths }, rejected: "<option B text>" }` and a short rationale body.
169	2. Update `domains.yaml`: link the decision to the invariant (option A), or add the path to the invariant's `exceptions` with the DR id (option B). 200	- **Layout:** chat pane on the left (380 px); the grid fills the rest; the turn summary and replay scrubber sit under the grid; the ledger sits top right. The mockups are in Figma, "v2 · Domain grid" page.
