# Frontend Design

Approach this as the design lead at a design studio known for giving every client a distinct visual identity that is not mistaken for anyone else's. This client has already rejected proposals that felt cliché or templated, and is paying for a distinctive point of view: make deliberate, opinionated choices about palette, typography, and layout that are specific to this brief, and take aesthetic risk if justified.

## Ground your designs in the subject matter

If the brief does not identify what the product or subject matter is, identify it yourself before designing, and confirm with the client. You can come up with one concrete subject, the design's audience, and the design's primary job, as a proposal. If there's any information in your memory about the client's preferences or context about what they're building, use that as a hint. The subject's industry, subject matter, materials, and vernacular are where distinctive visual choices come from — a design for a toy for girls aged 8–11 will be very aesthetically different from a dashboard for financial analysts. Build with the brief's real content and subject matter throughout.

## Design principles

For web designs, the hero is the first thing viewers will see. Open with the most characteristic thing in the subject's world, in the form that is most appropriate: a headline, an image, an animation, a live demo, an interactive moment, or other treatments. Be deliberate with your choice: a big number with a small label, supporting stats, and a gradient accent is the default treatment, so only use it if that's truly the best option.

Typography carries the personality of the page. You don't need a different typeface for display or headline text and body content: use one family or two, and if two, make them clearly distinct.

Choose your typefaces deliberately, not the default families you would reach for on any other project, and set a clear type scale following the default guidance of The Elements of Typographic Style with intentional weights, widths, and spacing. When type is used as a headline or visual element, use the type treatment itself as an active part of the design, not a neutral delivery vehicle for the content.

Default to line lengths of less than 80 characters. Serif typefaces can have slightly longer line lengths; give serif body text slightly more line-height than a sans-serif.

Avoid these default typographic treatments; they are the commonest tells of a generated page:
- Accenting just a single word or phrase in a headline, like putting one word in italic/bold or a different color.
- Using all caps for labels.
- Adding unnecessary typographic labels above content.

Visual structure is information. Structural devices like outlines, borders, numbering, eyebrows, dividers, labels, etc., encode useful information about the content rather than decorate it. Many generic designs use numbered markers (01 / 02 / 03), but that's only appropriate if the content actually is a sequence — like a stepped process or a timeline. Before adding numbered markers, check the content really is a sequence.

Use non-user-triggered motion sparingly and deliberately, only to draw attention. A single orchestrated moment — one page-load sequence or one reveal — lands better than scattered effects; fade-and-slide-up entrances on each section and hover transitions on every card are the generic default and read as AI-generated. Motion that answers a person's action (opening, expanding, confirming) is welcome when it shows what changed.

Consider written content carefully. Often a design brief may not contain real content, and it's up to you to come up with copy and placeholder content. Copy can make a design feel as templated as the design itself. See the below section on writing for more guidance.

## Process: plan, review against the brief, build, critique

For calibration, AI-generated design right now clusters around some traits:
1. a warm cream background (near #F4F1EA) with a high-contrast serif display and a terracotta or warm-clay accent (often near #D97757 — Anthropic's own Claude-interaction accent, so on a user's brief it reads as a tell);
2. a near-black background with a single bright acid-green or vermilion accent;
3. a broadsheet-style layout with hairline rules, zero border-radius, and dense newspaper-like columns;
4. the SaaS-card kit: content chopped into identical rounded cards, one border-radius on everything regardless of hierarchy, the same soft grey shadow (rgba(0,0,0,.1)) under each, and gradient washes as decoration;
5. template chrome that appears whatever the subject: a tracked-out ALL-CAPS eyebrow label above every heading; meta strings joined with middle dots ('A · B · C'); labels built as 'WORD — fragment' with a spaced em dash; tinted near-black (#0B0B0B, #111) standing in for black; a monospace face for small data labels; a '→' appended to link and button text.

All traits are legitimate for some briefs, but they are defaults rather than choices, and they appear regardless of subject. Where the brief pins down a visual direction, follow it exactly — the brief's own words always win, including when it asks for one of these looks. Where it leaves an axis free, don't spend that freedom on one of these defaults. As with a hired human designer, there's often a careful balance between doing what you're good at and taking each project as a chance to experiment and learn.

Work in two passes. First, brainstorm a short design plan based on the client's design brief: create a compact token system with color, type, layout, and principles.
- Color: describe the core base palette as 4–6 named hex values.
- Type: the typefaces and their roles.
- Layout: a layout concept, using one-sentence prose descriptions and ASCII wireframes to ideate and compare. Include alignment guidance; should the content be left aligned, center aligned, justified?
- Principles: the high-level guidance for what makes this page unique.

Then review that plan against the brief before building: if any part of it reads like the generic default you would produce for any similar page (work through a similar prompt to see if you arrive somewhere similar) rather than a choice made for this specific brief — revise that part, say what you changed and why. Only after you've confirmed the relative uniqueness of your design plan should you start to write the code, following the revised plan.

When writing the code, be careful of structuring your CSS selector specificities. It's easy to generate CSS classes that cancel each other out (especially with a type-based selector like .section and an element-based selector like .cta). This can happen often with padding/margin between sections.

## Restraint and self-critique

Spend your boldness in one place. Let one element be the memorable thing, keep everything around it quiet and disciplined, and cut any decoration that does not serve the brief. Build to a quality floor without announcing it: responsive down to mobile, visible keyboard focus, reduced motion respected, visually accessible, harmonious color palettes. Critique your own work as you build, taking screenshots to review if your environment supports it — a picture is worth 1000 tokens. Consider Chanel's advice: before leaving the house, take a look in the mirror and remove one accessory. Human creatives have memory and always try to do something new, so if you have a space to quickly jot down notes about what you've tried, it can help you in future passes.

## More on writing in design

Words appear in a design for one reason: to make it easier to understand and use. They are design content, not decoration. Bring the same intentionality and minimalism to copywriting that you would bring to spacing and color. Before writing anything, ask what the design needs to say, and how it can best be said to help the person navigate the experience.

Write from the end user's perspective. Name things by what users will understand in simple language, not by how the system is built. A user manages notifications, not webhook config. Describe what something is or does in plain terms rather than selling it. Being specific and legible to new users is always better than being clever.

Use active voice as default. A CTA says exactly what happens when it is used: "Save changes," not "Submit." An action keeps the same name through the whole flow, so the button that says "Publish" produces a toast that says "Published." The vocabulary of an interface is the signposting for someone navigating the product. Cohesion and consistency are how people learn their way around.

Treat failure and emptiness as moments for direction, not mood. Explain what went wrong and how to fix it, in the interface's voice rather than a person's. Errors don't apologize, and they are never vague about what happened. An empty screen is an invitation to act.

Keep the tone conversational: plain verbs, sentence case, no filler, with tone matched to the brand and the audience. Let each written element do exactly one job.

```typescript
// What one turn (or one submitted plan) touched, as the auditor sees it (NAVIGATION_PLAN §4.6). Pure: a reduction
// of the event log, so it replays like everything else.
import { reduce, type HarnessEvent, type EventData } from '../events';
import type { PlanStep } from '../plan';
import type { Violation } from '../rules';
import type { FileFacts } from '../contracts/facts';
import { fileOf } from '../contracts/graph';

export type FactDeltaPlus = {
  calls: { from: string; to: string }[];
  imports: { from: string; to: string }[];
  writes: { file: string; table: string }[];
};

export type TurnSurface = {
  turn: string;
  prompt: string;
  /** `turn_started.baseline` (a `git stash create` snapshot, or HEAD); null for a plan review. */
  baseline: string | null;
  source: 'turn' | 'plan';
  /** Files the turn changed (or the plan names), sorted. Harness's own files are never included. */
  files: string[];
  created: string[];
  /** Symbol ids the turn added or changed (renames count as their new id), sorted. */
  symbols: string[];
  /** New calls, imports and table writes in the changed files (facts at turn start → turn end). */
  delta: FactDeltaPlus;
  plan: PlanStep[];
  /** Violations the checker already raised this turn (plan and gate) or holds for these files. Never re-raised by the auditor. */
  violations: Violation[];
};

const HARNESS_OWN = (p: string) => p === 'domains.yaml' || p.startsWith('decisions/') || p.startsWith('.harness/');
const uniqSorted = (xs: Iterable<string>) => [...new Set(xs)].sort();
const pairKey = (a: string, b: string) => `${a}\u0000${b}`;

/** New imports, calls and writes of `after` relative to `before`, for `files`. */
export function factDelta(before: Readonly<Record<string, FileFacts>>, after: Readonly<Record<string, FileFacts>>, files: readonly string[]): FactDeltaPlus {
  const out: FactDeltaPlus = { calls: [], imports: [], writes: [] };
  for (const path of files) {
    const a = after[path];
    if (!a) continue;
    const b = before[path];
    const oldImports = new Set(b?.imports.map((i) => i.to) ?? []);
    for (const i of a.imports) if (!oldImports.has(i.to)) out.imports.push({ from: path, to: i.to });
    const oldCalls = new Set(b?.calls.map((c) => pairKey(c.from, c.to)) ?? []);
    for (const c of a.calls) if (!oldCalls.has(pairKey(c.from, c.to))) out.calls.push({ from: c.from, to: c.to });
    const oldWrites = new Set(b?.writes.map((w) => w.table) ?? []);
    for (const w of a.writes) if (!oldWrites.has(w.table)) out.writes.push({ file: path, table: w.table });
  }
  const sort = <T extends object>(xs: T[]) => [...new Map(xs.map((x) => [JSON.stringify(x), x])).values()].sort((x, y) => (JSON.stringify(x) < JSON.stringify(y) ? -1 : 1));
  return { calls: sort(out.calls), imports: sort(out.imports), writes: sort(out.writes) };
}

/**
 * The surface of a finished turn: files from the turn's `edited` events plus `turn_ended.files` (numstat), the symbols
 * its edits changed, and the fact delta between the facts at `turn_started` and at `turn_ended`. Null if the turn
 * has not ended (the auditor never reviews half-finished work).
 */
export function turnSurface(events: readonly HarnessEvent[], turnId: string): TurnSurface | null {
  const start = events.findIndex((e) => e.kind === 'turn_started' && e.turn === turnId);
  const end = events.findLastIndex((e) => e.kind === 'turn_ended' && e.turn === turnId);
  if (start < 0 || end < start) return null;
  const before = reduce(events, start);
  const after = reduce(events, end + 1);
  const turn = after.turns.find((t) => t.id === turnId);
  if (!turn) return null;
  const started = events[start]!.data as EventData['turn_started'];
  const ended = events[end]!.data as EventData['turn_ended'];

  const edited = Object.entries(turn.paths).filter(([, a]) => a.edits > 0).map(([p]) => p);
  const files = uniqSorted([...edited, ...ended.files].filter((p) => !HARNESS_OWN(p)));
  const created = uniqSorted(Object.entries(turn.paths).filter(([, a]) => a.created).map(([p]) => p));
  const symbols = uniqSorted(Object.values(turn.paths).flatMap((a) => (a.symbols ? [...a.symbols.added, ...a.symbols.sig, ...a.symbols.body, ...a.symbols.renamed.map(([, to]) => to)] : [])));
  const seen = turn.violationsSeen.map((x) => x.v);
  const standing = after.violations.filter((v) => files.includes(v.file));
  return {
    turn: turnId,
    prompt: turn.prompt,
    baseline: started.baseline || started.head || null,
    source: 'turn',
    files,
    created,
    symbols,
    delta: factDelta(before.facts, after.facts, files),
    plan: turn.steps,
    violations: dedupeViolations([...seen, ...standing]),
  };
}

/** The surface of the latest submitted plan of an open turn (plan review, behind HARNESS_AUDIT_PLANS=1). */
export function planSurface(events: readonly HarnessEvent[], turnId: string): TurnSurface | null {
  const ui = reduce(events);
  const turn = ui.turns.find((t) => t.id === turnId);
  if (!turn || !turn.steps.length) return null;
  const named = turn.steps.flatMap((s) => [...s.files, ...s.imports.map((i) => i.from)]);
  const files = uniqSorted(named.map((f) => fileOf(f) ?? f).filter((p) => !HARNESS_OWN(p)));
  const symbols = uniqSorted(named.filter((f) => f.includes('#')));
  const imports = turn.steps.flatMap((s) => s.imports.map((i) => ({ from: fileOf(i.from) ?? i.from, to: i.to })));
  return {
    turn: turnId,
    prompt: turn.prompt,
    baseline: null,
    source: 'plan',
    files,
    created: files.filter((f) => !ui.files[f]),
    symbols,
    delta: { calls: [], imports: [...new Map(imports.map((i) => [pairKey(i.from, i.to), i])).values()], writes: [] },
    plan: turn.steps,
    violations: dedupeViolations([...turn.planViolations, ...ui.violations.filter((v) => files.includes(v.file))]),
  };
}

function dedupeViolations(vs: Violation[]): Violation[] {
  return [...new Map(vs.map((v) => [`${v.invariant}\u0000${v.file}\u0000${v.target ?? ''}`, v])).values()];
}
```

```typescript
// The auditor's deterministic pre-filter (NAVIGATION_PLAN §4.6): only standing decisions that plausibly bear on what a
// turn touched are sent to the model; with none, the model call is skipped. Pure and cheap.
import { createMapper, matchesAny, type Mapper } from '../mapper';
import type { DomainMap, Invariant } from '../schema';
import { fileOf } from '../contracts/graph';
import type { TurnSurface } from './surface';

/** A standing decision as the auditor reads it (decisions/DR-n.md front matter + body). */
export type AuditDecision = { id: string; title: string; outcome: string; rationale: string; invariant: string; paths: string[] };

export type RelevanceReason = 'anchor' | 'invariant' | 'mention';
export type RelevantDecision = { decision: AuditDecision; reasons: { kind: RelevanceReason; detail: string }[] };

/** Words that read as identifiers but name nothing in particular. Only words of 4+ letters are ever compared. */
const STOP = new Set([
  'this', 'that', 'with', 'from', 'they', 'them', 'their', 'there', 'these', 'those', 'what', 'when', 'where', 'which', 'while', 'will', 'would',
  'should', 'could', 'must', 'have', 'been', 'into', 'only', 'also', 'each', 'every', 'other', 'than', 'then', 'some', 'more', 'most', 'make',
  'made', 'keep', 'kept', 'user', 'users', 'chose', 'choose', 'chosen', 'option', 'words', 'asked', 'during', 'rejected', 'triggered',
  'exception', 'rule', 'rules', 'file', 'files', 'path', 'paths', 'index', 'main', 'types', 'type', 'test', 'tests', 'shared', 'utils', 'util',
  'data', 'call', 'calls', 'called', 'calling', 'code', 'through', 'domain', 'domains', 'layer', 'cell', 'decision', 'decisions', 'standing',
  'outcome', 'title', 'rationale', 'imports', 'import', 'export', 'default', 'function', 'const', 'async', 'await', 'return', 'true', 'false',
  'null', 'undefined', 'string', 'number', 'here', 'just', 'like', 'because', 'instead', 'without', 'within', 'about', 'after', 'before', 'still',
  'goes', 'going', 'uses', 'used', 'using', 'need', 'needs', 'want', 'wants', 'does', 'done', 'into', 'onto', 'over', 'under', 'same', 'both',
]);

const words = (s: string) => (s.match(/[A-Za-z_$][\w$]*/g) ?? []).flatMap((w) => [w, ...w.split(/(?<=[a-z0-9])(?=[A-Z])|[_$]+/)]).map((w) => w.toLowerCase()).filter((w) => w.length >= 4 && !STOP.has(w));
const stemWords = (path: string) => (path.slice(path.lastIndexOf('/') + 1).replace(/\.[^.]+$/, '').match(/[A-Za-z0-9]+/g) ?? []).map((w) => w.toLowerCase()).filter((w) => w.length >= 4 && !STOP.has(w));
const symbolNames = (id: string) => {
  const i = id.indexOf('#');
  if (i < 0) return [];
  const q = id.slice(i + 1).replace(/~\d+$/, '');
  return [q, ...q.split('.')].map((w) => w.toLowerCase()).filter((w) => w.length >= 4 && !STOP.has(w) && !w.startsWith('<'));
};
/** Path-like tokens (`src/tools/x.ts`, `vendor/llm-openai`) in prose. */
const pathTokens = (s: string) => (s.match(/[\w.@-]+(?:\/[\w.@*-]+)+/g) ?? []).map((p) => p.replace(/[.,;:]+$/, '').replace(/^\.\//, ''));
const under = (path: string, token: string) => path === token || path.startsWith(`${token.replace(/\/$/, '')}/`) || path.startsWith(token.replace(/\.[cm]?[jt]sx?$/, ''));

/** Files the turn reaches: changed files plus the files of new import/call targets (vendors and tables excluded). */
function touchedTargets(s: TurnSurface): string[] {
  const out = new Set<string>();
  for (const i of s.delta.imports) if (!i.to.includes(':')) out.add(i.to);
  for (const c of s.delta.calls) { const f = fileOf(c.to); if (f) out.add(f); }
  return [...out].sort();
}

/** Does `inv` bear on what the turn touched? Returns a short reason, or null. */
function invariantTouches(inv: Invariant, s: TurnSurface, mapper: Mapper, targets: readonly string[]): string | null {
  const domainOf = (p: string) => mapper.domainOf(p);
  const changedDomains = new Set(s.files.map(domainOf).filter((d): d is string => !!d));
  const targetDomains = new Set(targets.map(domainOf).filter((d): d is string => !!d));
  const exception = inv.exceptions.find((e) => s.files.includes(e.path));
  if (exception) return `${exception.path} is an exception to ${inv.id}`;
  if (inv.kind === 'only_via') {
    const hit = [...s.files, ...targets].find((p) => matchesAny(inv.targets, p));
    if (hit) return `${hit} is a target of ${inv.id}`;
    const via = inv.allowed_from.find((d) => targetDomains.has(d) && [...changedDomains].some((c) => c !== d));
    if (via) return `the turn now reaches ${via}, the only way ${inv.id} allows`;
    const inside = inv.allowed_from.find((d) => changedDomains.has(d));
    if (inside) return `the turn changed ${inside}, the way ${inv.id} allows`;
    return null;
  }
  if (inv.kind === 'owns_writes') {
    const w = s.delta.writes.find((x) => x.table in inv.owners);
    if (w) return `${w.file} writes "${w.table}"`;
    const owner = Object.values(inv.owners).find((d) => changedDomains.has(d));
    return owner ? `the turn changed ${owner}, which owns tables under ${inv.id}` : null;
  }
  const end = [inv.from, inv.to].find((d) => changedDomains.has(d) || targetDomains.has(d));
  return end ? `the turn touches ${end}, an end of ${inv.id}` : null;
}

/**
 * Standing decisions relevant to a turn, sorted by DR number, each with why:
 * - **anchor**: an anchored path (exact, glob or directory) is a changed file or a file the turn newly imports/calls;
 * - **invariant**: the decision's invariant targets, exempts, or names a domain of what the turn changed or reaches;
 * - **mention**: its title, outcome or rationale names a path the turn touches, or a symbol/file name it changed or calls.
 */
export function relevantDecisions(decisions: readonly AuditDecision[], map: DomainMap, s: TurnSurface, mapper: Mapper = createMapper(map)): RelevantDecision[] {
  const targets = touchedTargets(s);
  const touched = [...new Set([...s.files, ...targets])];
  const names = new Map<string, string>(); // lowercased name → what it is
  for (const id of s.symbols) for (const n of symbolNames(id)) names.set(n, id);
  for (const c of s.delta.calls) for (const n of symbolNames(c.to)) if (!names.has(n)) names.set(n, c.to);
  for (const f of s.files) for (const n of stemWords(f)) if (!names.has(n)) names.set(n, f);

  const out: RelevantDecision[] = [];
  for (const d of decisions) {
    const reasons: RelevantDecision['reasons'] = [];
    const anchored = d.paths.flatMap((a) => touched.filter((p) => p === a || matchesAny([a], p) || under(p, a)).map((p) => `${a} ↔ ${p}`));
    if (anchored.length) reasons.push({ kind: 'anchor', detail: anchored.join(', ') });
    const inv = d.invariant ? map.invariants.find((i) => i.id === d.invariant) : undefined;
    const why = inv ? invariantTouches(inv, s, mapper, targets) : null;
    if (why) reasons.push({ kind: 'invariant', detail: why });
    const prose = `${d.title}\n${d.outcome}\n${d.rationale}`;
    const paths = pathTokens(prose).flatMap((t) => touched.filter((p) => under(p, t)).map((p) => `${t} ↔ ${p}`));
    const named = [...new Set(words(prose))].filter((w) => names.has(w)).map((w) => `"${w}" ↔ ${names.get(w)}`);
    if (paths.length || named.length) reasons.push({ kind: 'mention', detail: [...new Set(paths), ...named].join(', ') });
    if (reasons.length) out.push({ decision: d, reasons });
  }
  return out.sort((a, b) => num(a.decision.id) - num(b.decision.id) || (a.decision.id < b.decision.id ? -1 : 1));
}

const num = (id: string) => Number(/(\d+)$/.exec(id)?.[1] ?? 0);
```

```typescript
// Auditor findings after the model (NAVIGATION_PLAN §4.6): sanitized against what was asked, deduplicated, and
// checked against the dismissal memory so a dismissed finding never comes back. Pure.
import type { AuditFinding } from '../contracts/cartography';
import { fnv1a } from '../cartography/util';

/** A finding as the model returns it (no id yet). */
export type RawFinding = Omit<AuditFinding, 'id'>;

/** A dismissed finding, as remembered in `.harness/audit/dismissed.json`. */
export type DismissedFinding = { signature: string; decision: string | null; files: string[]; text: string; id?: string; at?: number };

const CONFIDENCE = new Set(['low', 'medium', 'high']);

/** Lowercased, line references and punctuation dropped, whitespace collapsed: rephrasing a line number is not a new finding. */
export function normalizeFindingText(text: string): string {
  return text.toLowerCase()
    .replace(/(?:\blines?\s*|:)\d+(?:\s*[-–]\s*\d+)?/g, ' ')
    .replace(/[^\p{L}\p{N}\s]+/gu, ' ')
    .replace(/\s+/g, ' ')
    .trim();
}

/** Same decision + same files + same (normalized) text = same finding. */
export function findingSignature(f: { decision: string | null; files: readonly string[]; text: string }): string {
  return fnv1a([f.decision ?? '', [...new Set(f.files)].sort().join(','), normalizeFindingText(f.text)].join('\u0000'));
}

const wordSet = (t: string) => new Set(normalizeFindingText(t).split(' ').filter((w) => w.length > 2));
/** Jaccard similarity of the two texts' word sets. */
export function textSimilarity(a: string, b: string): number {
  const x = wordSet(a), y = wordSet(b);
  if (!x.size && !y.size) return 1;
  let both = 0;
  for (const w of x) if (y.has(w)) both++;
  return both / (x.size + y.size - both);
}

/** Rephrasings of a dismissed finding (same decision, same files) at or above this similarity stay dismissed. */
export const DISMISS_SIMILARITY = 0.6;

/** True if `f` was dismissed: identical signature, or the same decision and files with near-identical text. */
export function isDismissed(f: { decision: string | null; files: readonly string[]; text: string }, dismissed: readonly DismissedFinding[]): boolean {
  const sig = findingSignature(f);
  const files = [...new Set(f.files)].sort().join(',');
  return dismissed.some((d) => d.signature === sig || (d.decision === f.decision && [...new Set(d.files)].sort().join(',') === files && textSimilarity(d.text, f.text) >= DISMISS_SIMILARITY));
}

/**
 * Keep only findings worth showing: they cite a decision that was sent (`decisions`), concern files the turn changed
 * (`files`; other files are dropped from the finding, and a finding left with none is dropped), have text, and are
 * neither dismissed nor a repeat of an open finding or of each other. Lines outside the finding's files are dropped;
 * an unknown confidence becomes `low`. Order is kept.
 */
export function acceptFindings(raw: readonly RawFinding[], ctx: { decisions: readonly string[]; files: readonly string[]; dismissed: readonly DismissedFinding[]; open: readonly { decision: string | null; files: readonly string[]; text: string }[] }): RawFinding[] {
  const sent = new Set(ctx.decisions);
  const changed = new Set(ctx.files);
  const norm = (p: string) => p.replace(/^\.\//, '');
  const seen = new Set(ctx.open.map(findingSignature));
  const out: RawFinding[] = [];
  for (const r of raw) {
    const text = (r.text ?? '').trim();
    if (!text || !r.decision || !sent.has(r.decision)) continue;
    const files = [...new Set((r.files ?? []).map(norm))].filter((f) => changed.has(f)).sort();
    for (const l of r.lines ?? []) if (changed.has(norm(l.path)) && !files.includes(norm(l.path))) files.push(norm(l.path));
    if (!files.length) continue;
    files.sort();
    const lines = (r.lines ?? [])
      .map((l) => ({ path: norm(l.path), line: Math.trunc(Number(l.line)) }))
      .filter((l) => files.includes(l.path) && Number.isFinite(l.line) && l.line > 0);
    const f: RawFinding = { decision: r.decision, files, lines: [...new Map(lines.map((l) => [`${l.path}:${l.line}`, l])).values()], text, confidence: CONFIDENCE.has(r.confidence) ? r.confidence : 'low' };
    const sig = findingSignature(f);
    if (seen.has(sig) || isDismissed(f, ctx.dismissed)) continue;
    seen.add(sig);
    out.push(f);
  }
  return out;
}

/** Next free `AF-n` above every existing finding id. */
export function nextFindingId(existing: Iterable<string>): string {
  let max = 0;
  for (const id of existing) max = Math.max(max, Number(/^AF-(\d+)$/.exec(id)?.[1] ?? 0));
  return `AF-${max + 1}`;
}
```

```typescript
// Unified diffs with new-file line numbers, so the auditor can cite exact lines. Pure.

/**
 * Rewrite a unified diff (`git diff` output, one or more files) so every line carries its line number in the new file:
 * `  31 + code` (added), `     - code` (removed), `  30   code` (context). File headers become `### path` (or
 * `### path (new file)`); hunk headers are dropped. At most `maxLines` body lines per file, then `… (n more lines)`.
 */
export function numberDiff(diff: string, maxLines = 300): string {
  const out: string[] = [];
  let line = 0;
  let count = 0;
  let skipped = 0;
  let isNew = false;
  const flush = () => { if (skipped) out.push(`     … (${skipped} more lines)`); skipped = 0; };
  for (const raw of diff.split('\n')) {
    if (raw.startsWith('diff --git')) { flush(); isNew = false; count = 0; continue; }
    if (raw.startsWith('new file mode') || raw.startsWith('--- /dev/null')) { isNew = true; continue; }
    if (raw.startsWith('+++ ')) {
      const path = raw.slice(4).replace(/^b\//, '').trim();
      out.push(`### ${path}${isNew ? ' (new file)' : ''}`);
      continue;
    }
    if (raw.startsWith('--- ') || raw.startsWith('index ') || raw.startsWith('similarity ') || raw.startsWith('rename ') || raw.startsWith('deleted file') || raw.startsWith('old mode') || raw.startsWith('new mode')) continue;
    const h = /^@@ -\d+(?:,\d+)? \+(\d+)(?:,\d+)? @@/.exec(raw);
    if (h) { line = Number(h[1]); if (count && count < maxLines) out.push('     ⋮'); continue; }
    if (raw.startsWith('\\')) continue; // "\ No newline at end of file"
    if (!line) continue;
    const kind = raw[0];
    if (kind !== '+' && kind !== '-' && kind !== ' ') continue;
    if (count >= maxLines) { skipped++; if (kind !== '-') line++; continue; }
    count++;
    if (kind === '+') out.push(`${String(line++).padStart(4)} + ${raw.slice(1)}`);
    else if (kind === '-') out.push(`     - ${raw.slice(1)}`);
    else out.push(`${String(line++).padStart(4)}   ${raw.slice(1)}`);
  }
  flush();
  return out.join('\n');
}
```

```typescript
// Rule proposals from the auditor (NAVIGATION_PLAN §4.4 "Rule reinforcement", §4.6 "promote"). Deterministic, no
// model: they go through the living map's proposal flow (`map_proposed { proposal }`), so accept/reject work the same.
//
// What can be built deterministically, and what can't:
// - The three rule kinds (only_via, owns_writes, no_edge) can't express most rationale-level constraints (e.g. "filings
//   calls pass `redaction: "filings"`"). When the cited decision is linked to an invariant, the proposal amends that
//   invariant's `rule` text with the decision (a `change_rule` with a ready candidate map: accepting commits it, and the
//   rule text then states the constraint wherever the rule is shown). The checker's behaviour is unchanged; the auditor
//   keeps checking the constraint.
// - Otherwise the proposal is manual: an `add_rule` change carrying the rule text and no candidate map. Accept is
//   refused (there is nothing to write); the user writes the rule into domains.yaml by hand, or rejects it.
import YAML, { isMap, isSeq, isScalar } from 'yaml';
import { createMapper } from '../mapper';
import { parseDomainMap, type DomainMap } from '../schema';
import type { Decision } from '../events';
import type { FileFacts } from '../contracts/facts';
import type { DriftSignal, HistoryTurn, MapProposal, ProposalChange } from '../contracts/cartography';
import { DEFAULT_THRESHOLDS } from '../contracts/cartography';
import { domainId } from '../contracts/graph';
import { scoreMap } from '../cartography/score';
import { diffMaps } from '../cartography/diff';

/** Replace invariant `invariantId`'s `rule:` scalar in place (only that value's text changes). */
export function setRuleText(yamlText: string, invariantId: string, rule: string): string {
  const doc = YAML.parseDocument(yamlText);
  const list = doc.get('invariants');
  const inv = isSeq(list) ? list.items.find((item) => isMap(item) && item.get('id') === invariantId) : undefined;
  const node = isMap(inv) ? inv.get('rule', true) : undefined;
  if (!isScalar(node) || !node.range) throw new Error(`domains.yaml has no rule text for ${invariantId}`);
  return yamlText.slice(0, node.range[0]) + JSON.stringify(rule) + yamlText.slice(node.range[1]);
}

/** The same invariant chosen with option A at least `threshold` times for files in the same domain. */
export type Reinforcement = { invariant: string; domain: string; decisions: string[]; paths: string[] };

/** Reinforced invariants from recorded decisions (deduped by id), grouped like the `rule_reinforcement` drift signal. */
export function reinforcements(decisions: readonly Pick<Decision, 'id' | 'invariant' | 'option' | 'paths'>[], map: DomainMap, threshold = DEFAULT_THRESHOLDS.ruleReinforcement): Reinforcement[] {
  const mapper = createMapper(map);
  const groups = new Map<string, Reinforcement>();
  for (const d of new Map(decisions.map((x) => [x.id, x])).values()) {
    if (d.option !== 'A' || !d.invariant) continue;
    const domain = (d.paths[0] && mapper.domainOf(d.paths[0])) ?? 'unassigned';
    const k = `${d.invariant}\u0000${domain}`;
    const g = groups.get(k) ?? { invariant: d.invariant, domain, decisions: [], paths: [] };
    g.decisions.push(d.id);
    g.paths.push(...d.paths);
    groups.set(k, g);
  }
  return [...groups.values()]
    .filter((g) => g.decisions.length >= threshold && map.invariants.some((i) => i.id === g.invariant))
    .map((g) => ({ ...g, paths: [...new Set(g.paths)].sort() }))
    .sort((a, b) => (a.invariant + a.domain < b.invariant + b.domain ? -1 : 1));
}

export type RuleProposalInput = {
  id: string; // MP-n
  yaml: string; // current domains.yaml text
  map: DomainMap;
  facts: Readonly<Record<string, FileFacts>>;
  history: readonly HistoryTurn[];
  trigger: DriftSignal[];
  scope: string[];
  rationale: string;
};

/** A `change_rule` proposal with one candidate: the current map with `invariant`'s rule text replaced by `rule`. */
export function changeRuleProposal(input: RuleProposalInput & { invariant: string; rule: string }): MapProposal {
  const yaml = setRuleText(input.yaml, input.invariant, input.rule);
  const next = parseDomainMap(yaml);
  const files = Object.keys(input.facts);
  const current = scoreMap(input.map, input.facts, input.history, { current: input.map });
  const score = scoreMap(next, input.facts, input.history, { current: input.map });
  const changes = diffMaps(input.map, next, files);
  return { id: input.id, trigger: input.trigger, scope: [...new Set(input.scope)].sort(), candidates: [{ yaml, score }], chosen: 0, current, changes, rationale: input.rationale };
}

/** A manual `add_rule` proposal: the rule text only, no candidate map (accept is refused; see the module comment). */
export function manualRuleProposal(input: RuleProposalInput & { invariant: string; rule: string }): MapProposal {
  const current = scoreMap(input.map, input.facts, input.history, { current: input.map });
  const changes: ProposalChange[] = [{ kind: 'add_rule', invariant: input.invariant, rule: input.rule }];
  return { id: input.id, trigger: input.trigger, scope: [...new Set(input.scope)].sort(), candidates: [], chosen: 0, current, changes, rationale: input.rationale };
}

/** Rule text for a reinforced invariant: the rule, plus the decisions that confirmed it. */
export function reinforcedRuleText(rule: string, r: Reinforcement, domainName: string): string {
  return `${stripClause(rule)} (confirmed ${r.decisions.length}× for ${domainName}: ${r.decisions.join(', ')})`;
}

/** Rule text that also states a decision's constraint: `<rule>; <decision id>: <title>`. */
export function amendedRuleText(rule: string, decision: { id: string; title: string }): string {
  const clause = `${decision.id}: ${decision.title.replace(/[.\s]+$/, '')}`;
  return rule.includes(clause) ? rule : `${rule.replace(/[.\s]+$/, '')}; ${clause}`;
}

const stripClause = (rule: string) => rule.replace(/\s*\(confirmed \d+× for [^)]*\)\s*$/, '');

/** The drift-style trigger for a reinforcement proposal (scope `rule:<id>` + the domain). */
export function reinforcementSignal(r: Reinforcement, threshold = DEFAULT_THRESHOLDS.ruleReinforcement): DriftSignal {
  return { signal: 'rule_reinforcement', metric: `option A chosen for ${r.invariant} in ${r.domain}`, value: r.decisions.length, threshold, scope: [`rule:${r.invariant}`, domainId(r.domain)], persisted: 1 };
}
```

```typescript
const params = new URLSearchParams(location.search);
const themeParam = params.get('theme');
export const initialTheme: Theme = themeParam === 'control' || themeParam === 'strata' ? themeParam : 'atlas';

/** Where you are: the containers you opened (domains, cells, groups) and the node you are on. View-only state. */
export type Place = { open: string[]; focus: string | null };

const readMinimap = () => {
  try { return localStorage.getItem('harness.minimap') !== '0'; } catch { return true; }
};

/**
 * View-only state for the v2 map: what is open, the focused node, history, chrome toggles. Plus the current
 * projection's nodes and edges published by id with structural sharing, so each node component re-renders only when
 * its own slice changes. Nothing here duplicates what the event log says.
 */
type V2Store = {
  open: string[];
  focus: string | null;
  back: Place[];
  forward: Place[];
  theme: Theme;
  minimap: boolean;
  palette: boolean;
  /** A node to fly the camera to once it is laid out (⌘K, breadcrumbs). */
  fly: string | null;
  nodes: Record<string, VisibleNode>;
  edges: Record<string, VisibleEdge>;
  hot: Record<string, string[]>;
  cursor: ProjectionCursor | null;

  /** Navigate to a place (pushes history unless it is the same place). */
  go(next: Partial<Place>, fly?: string | null): void;
  setFocus(id: string | null): void;
  goBack(): void;
  goForward(): void;
  setPalette(open: boolean): void;
  toggleMinimap(): void;
  publish(p: { nodes: VisibleNode[]; edges: VisibleEdge[]; hot: Record<string, string[]>; cursor: ProjectionCursor | null }): void;
};

const same = (a: unknown, b: unknown) => a === b || JSON.stringify(a) === JSON.stringify(b);
const samePlace = (a: Place, b: Place) => a.focus === b.focus && a.open.join() === b.open.join();
const HISTORY = 50;

export const useV2 = create<V2Store>((set, get) => ({
  open: (params.get('expand') ?? '').split(',').filter(Boolean).map((d) => (d.includes(':') ? d : `domain:${d}`)),
  focus: null,
  back: [],
  forward: [],
  theme: initialTheme,
  minimap: readMinimap(),
  palette: false,
  fly: null,
  nodes: {},
  edges: {},
  hot: {},
  cursor: null,

  go: (next, fly = null) => {
    const s = get();
    const cur: Place = { open: s.open, focus: s.focus };
    const to: Place = { open: next.open ?? s.open, focus: next.focus === undefined ? s.focus : next.focus };
    if (samePlace(cur, to)) { if (fly) set({ fly }); return; }
    set({ ...to, back: [...s.back, cur].slice(-HISTORY), forward: [], fly });
  },
  setFocus: (focus) => set({ focus }),
  goBack: () => {
    const s = get();
    const prev = s.back.at(-1);
    if (!prev) return;
    set({ ...prev, back: s.back.slice(0, -1), forward: [{ open: s.open, focus: s.focus }, ...s.forward], fly: prev.focus });
  },
  goForward: () => {
    const s = get();
    const next = s.forward[0];
    if (!next) return;
    set({ ...next, forward: s.forward.slice(1), back: [...s.back, { open: s.open, focus: s.focus }], fly: next.focus });
  },
  setPalette: (palette) => set({ palette }),
  toggleMinimap: () => set((s) => {
    try { localStorage.setItem('harness.minimap', s.minimap ? '0' : '1'); } catch { /* private mode */ }
    return { minimap: !s.minimap };
  }),
  publish: (p) => {
    const prev = get();
    const nodes: Record<string, VisibleNode> = {};
    for (const n of p.nodes) {
      const o = prev.nodes[n.id];
      nodes[n.id] = o && same(o, n) ? o : n;
    }
    const edges: Record<string, VisibleEdge> = {};
    for (const e of p.edges) {
      const o = prev.edges[e.id];
      edges[e.id] = o && same(o, e) ? o : e;
    }
    const hot: Record<string, string[]> = {};
    for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(p.hot)) hot[k] = prev.hot[k] && same(prev.hot[k], v) ? prev.hot[k]! : v;
    set({ nodes, edges, hot, cursor: same(prev.cursor, p.cursor) ? prev.cursor : p.cursor });
  },
}));
```

```typescript
// Tier 2 (NAVIGATION_PLAN §3.1): the semantic resolver interface. Two implementations sit behind it: TypeScript 7's
// `typescript/unstable/sync` (tsgo, pinned to 7.0.2) and the TS 6 LanguageService via ts-morph (fallback). Node-only;
// runs in the semantic child process, never in the server's main thread.

/** What a call site's callee (or a heritage/annotation type name) resolves to. */
export type DeclInfo =
  /** A declaration in a repo source file. `name` is qualified like Tier 1 symbol names (`Tool.run`, `Anthropic.messages.create`). */
  | { where: 'repo'; file: string; name: string; abstract: boolean }
  /** A declaration inside an installed package (`@types/x` is reported as `x`). */
  | { where: 'package'; pkg: string }
  /** The default library (`Array.prototype.map`, `Promise`, …) or anything else outside the repo. */
  | { where: 'lib' };

export type ResolverImpl = 'tsgo' | 'ts-morph';

export interface SemanticResolver {
  readonly impl: ResolverImpl;
  /**
   * For each UTF-16 offset in `file`'s text on disk, the declaration the identifier there resolves to (aliases followed),
   * or null when the checker can't resolve it (e.g. a member of an `any` value).
   */
  declarationsAt(file: string, positions: readonly number[]): (DeclInfo | null)[];
  /** Files changed, created or deleted on disk (repo-relative). The next `declarationsAt` sees the new program. */
  update(changes: FileChanges): void;
  close(): void;
}

export type FileChanges = { changed: readonly string[]; created: readonly string[]; deleted: readonly string[] };

export type ResolverOptions = {
  root: string; // absolute, real path
  /** Repo-relative code files to analyse (used when the repo has no root tsconfig.json). */
  files: readonly string[];
};
```

```typescript
// The real pipeline (NAVIGATION_PLAN §3): ui = reduce(events, upTo) → graph = graphOf(ui) (memoized on its inputs)
// → activity = activityFor(ui, graph, turn) → projection = project(graph, view, activity). Pure functions; the hook
// at the bottom wires them to the stores.
import { useMemo } from 'react';
import {
  activityFor, buildGraph, graphFacts, project,
  type ContextGraph, type FileFacts, type LeafActivity, type Projection, type TurnActivity, type UIState, type ViewState,
} from '@harness/core/view';
import { useView } from '../derive';
import { useV2 } from './store';

const sameImports = (a: FileFacts['imports'], b: FileFacts['imports']) =>
  a === b || (a.length === b.length && a.every((x, i) => x.to === b[i]!.to && x.typeOnly === b[i]!.typeOnly));

/** Same graph inputs: facts by content hash (stubs and edge-adjusted files compare their imports), map and Tier 2 by hash. */
export function sameInputs(a: Record<string, FileFacts>, b: Record<string, FileFacts>): boolean {
  const ka = Object.keys(a);
  if (ka.length !== Object.keys(b).length) return false;
  for (const k of ka) {
    const x = a[k]!;
    const y = b[k];
    if (!y) return false;
    if (x === y) continue;
    if (x.hash !== y.hash || !sameImports(x.imports, y.imports) || x.writes.length !== y.writes.length) return false;
  }
  return true;
}

const semKey = (ui: UIState) => Object.values(ui.semantic).map((s) => `${s.path}@${s.hash}`).sort().join('|');

/**
 * graphOf(ui), rebuilt only when what it is built from changes. Replay re-reduces the log, so UIState objects are
 * new on every event; the facts inside them are the events' own objects, so most comparisons are by reference.
 */
export function graphMemo() {
  let last: { map: unknown; mapJson: string; facts: Record<string, FileFacts>; sem: string; graph: ContextGraph } | null = null;
  return (ui: UIState): ContextGraph | null => {
    if (!ui.map) return (last = null);
    const facts = graphFacts(ui);
    const sem = semKey(ui);
    const mapJson = last && last.map === ui.map ? last.mapJson : JSON.stringify(ui.map);
    if (last && last.mapJson === mapJson && last.sem === sem && sameInputs(last.facts, facts)) {
      last.map = ui.map;
      return last.graph;
    }
    const graph = buildGraph(ui.map, facts, ui.semantic);
    last = { map: ui.map, mapJson, facts, sem, graph };
    return graph;
  };
}

/** Opened ids that still exist, each with the containers above it (a group needs its cell open). */
export function normalizeOpen(graph: ContextGraph, open: readonly string[]): string[] {
  const out = new Set<string>();
  for (const id of open) {
    const n = graph.nodes[id];
    if (!n || !(graph.children[id]?.length)) continue;
    if (n.kind !== 'domain' && n.kind !== 'cell' && n.kind !== 'group' && n.kind !== 'unassigned') continue;
    out.add(id);
  }
  return [...out];
}

/**
 * The projection's view for what is open. System level is "every domain expanded one level" (cells visible, the
 * parity view). Opening a domain opens all its cells; opening a cell or group opens it and the containers above it.
 */
export function viewFor(graph: ContextGraph, open: readonly string[]): ViewState {
  const expanded = new Set<string>();
  for (const id of graph.children[graph.root] ?? []) if (graph.nodes[id]!.kind === 'domain') expanded.add(id);
  for (const id of normalizeOpen(graph, open)) {
    const n = graph.nodes[id]!;
    if (n.kind === 'domain') for (const c of graph.children[id] ?? []) if (graph.nodes[c]!.kind === 'cell') expanded.add(c);
    for (let p: string | null = id; p && p !== graph.root; p = graph.nodes[p]?.parent ?? null) expanded.add(p);
  }
  return { expanded: [...expanded], focus: null, lens: { kinds: [], turnOnly: false }, budget: 50, follow: false };
}

/** Which column a node is drawn in: its domain, or the Unassigned column. */
export const columnOf = (graph: ContextGraph, id: string): string | null => {
  const n = graph.nodes[id];
  if (!n) return null;
  if (n.domain) return n.domain;
  for (let p: string | null = id; p; p = graph.nodes[p]?.parent ?? null) if (p === 'unassigned') return UNASSIGNED_COL;
  return null;
};
export const UNASSIGNED_COL = '__unassigned';

const heat = (l: LeafActivity | undefined) =>
  !l ? 9 : l.violation === 'new' ? 0 : l.violation ? 1 : l.cursor ? 2 : l.edited ? 3 : l.ghostSteps.length ? 4 : l.looked ? 5 : 9;

/** Collapsed cells list their children with the ones that matter this turn first (as v1 did), then by order. */
export function hotLabels(graph: ContextGraph, activity: TurnActivity, p: Projection, max = 8): Record<string, string[]> {
  const out: Record<string, string[]> = {};
  for (const n of p.nodes) {
    if (n.expanded || (n.kind !== 'cell' && n.kind !== 'unassigned')) continue;
    const kids = graph.children[n.id] ?? [];
    const ranked = kids.map((k, i) => ({ k, i, h: heat(activity.leaves[k]) })).sort((a, b) => a.h - b.h || a.i - b.i);
    out[n.id] = ranked.slice(0, max).map((x) => graph.nodes[x.k]!.label);
  }
  return out;
}

export type Scene = {
  ui: UIState;
  graph: ContextGraph;
  activity: TurnActivity;
  projection: Projection;
  open: string[];
  /** Layout key: what is open (positions depend on nothing else but content). */
  key: string;
};

export function sceneOf(ui: UIState, graph: ContextGraph, turn: string | null, open: readonly string[]): Scene {
  const activity = activityFor(ui, graph, turn);
  const opened = normalizeOpen(graph, open);
  const projection = project(graph, viewFor(graph, opened), activity);
  return { ui, graph, activity, projection, open: opened, key: opened.join(',') };
}

const memoGraph = graphMemo();

/** The scene for the current events, replay index, selected turn and open set. */
export function useScene(): Scene | null {
  const v = useView();
  const open = useV2((s) => s.open);
  const graph = useMemo(() => memoGraph(v.ui), [v.ui]);
  return useMemo(() => (graph ? sceneOf(v.ui, graph, v.turn?.id ?? null, open) : null), [v.ui, v.turn, graph, open]);
}
```

```typescript
// Shared by both resolvers: turn a declaration node into a Tier 1 style qualified name, decide whether it is an
// abstract member (calls through it are dispatch), and name the package a path belongs to.

const KIND_NAMES = [
  'SourceFile', 'FunctionDeclaration', 'ClassDeclaration', 'InterfaceDeclaration', 'TypeAliasDeclaration', 'EnumDeclaration',
  'MethodDeclaration', 'MethodSignature', 'PropertyDeclaration', 'PropertySignature', 'PropertyAssignment',
  'ShorthandPropertyAssignment', 'VariableDeclaration', 'GetAccessor', 'SetAccessor', 'Constructor', 'AbstractKeyword',
] as const;
export type KindName = (typeof KIND_NAMES)[number];

/** The parts of a compiler node (TS 6 or TS 7 remote node) the resolvers read. */
export type DeclNode = {
  readonly kind: number;
  readonly parent?: DeclNode | null;
  readonly name?: { readonly kind: number; readonly text?: string } | null;
  readonly modifiers?: ArrayLike<{ readonly kind: number }> | null;
};

/** Number → name for the kinds above, from a `SyntaxKind` enum object (TS 6 and 7 number them differently). */
export function kindTable(syntaxKind: Record<string, unknown>): (kind: number) => KindName | null {
  const map = new Map<number, KindName>();
  for (const k of KIND_NAMES) if (typeof syntaxKind[k] === 'number') map.set(syntaxKind[k] as number, k);
  return (kind) => map.get(kind) ?? null;
}

/** Declarations that contribute a segment to the qualified name; namespaces and expressions don't (Tier 1 has none). */
const NAMED = new Set<KindName>([
  'FunctionDeclaration', 'ClassDeclaration', 'InterfaceDeclaration', 'TypeAliasDeclaration', 'EnumDeclaration',
  'MethodDeclaration', 'MethodSignature', 'PropertyDeclaration', 'PropertySignature', 'PropertyAssignment',
  'ShorthandPropertyAssignment', 'VariableDeclaration', 'GetAccessor', 'SetAccessor',
]);

/**
 * `Tool.run`, `Anthropic.messages.create`, `runAgent`: names of the enclosing named declarations, outermost first.
 * `settleCalls` later trims it to the deepest Tier 1 symbol that exists. Anonymous default exports are `default`.
 */
export function qualifiedName(node: DeclNode, kindOf: (kind: number) => KindName | null): string {
  const parts: string[] = [];
  for (let n: DeclNode | null | undefined = node; n; n = n.parent) {
    const k = kindOf(n.kind);
    if (k === 'SourceFile') break;
    if (k === 'Constructor') parts.unshift('constructor');
    else if (k && NAMED.has(k)) {
      const text = n.name?.text;
      if (text) parts.unshift(text);
    }
  }
  return parts.join('.') || 'default';
}

/** Interface and type-literal members, and abstract class members: a call through one is dispatched at runtime. */
export function isAbstract(node: DeclNode, kindOf: (kind: number) => KindName | null): boolean {
  const k = kindOf(node.kind);
  if (k === 'MethodSignature' || k === 'PropertySignature') return true;
  if (k !== 'MethodDeclaration' && k !== 'PropertyDeclaration') return false;
  const mods = node.modifiers;
  if (!mods) return false;
  for (let i = 0; i < mods.length; i++) if (kindOf(mods[i]!.kind) === 'AbstractKeyword') return true;
  return false;
}

/** Package a file path belongs to (after the last `node_modules/`); `@types/x` → `x`, `@types/a__b` → `@a/b`. */
export function packageOf(path: string): string | null {
  const i = path.lastIndexOf('/node_modules/');
  if (i === -1) return null;
  const parts = path.slice(i + 14).split('/');
  const name = parts[0]?.startsWith('@') ? `${parts[0]}/${parts[1] ?? ''}` : (parts[0] ?? '');
  if (!name) return null;
  if (!name.startsWith('@types/')) return name;
  const t = name.slice(7);
  return t.includes('__') ? `@${t.replace('__', '/')}` : t;
}
```

On Alike: yes, that's the value. Decisions you make in the harness travel to every other agent session, including teammates who never open it. And because the harness anchors each decision to exact files from the map, Alike gets precise memories rather than ones guessed from chat.

**On "mention any calls we've logged with this contact":** it's a feature request to the coding agent, not a lookup for a person. It means "make the brief also include the phone calls logged in the CRM for this contact". Scout's sandbox CRM can store calls alongside emails, so it's beat 3's feature again with a different kind of history.

The idea was a follow-up that falls under beat 3's decision (DR-4: outreach history reaches the brief through the run loop, never through a tool importing outreach code). Session two should build it that way without asking, and that shows the memory working.

**It's a weak choice, though, for two reasons:**
1. **It reads ambiguously,** as you just noticed. That's bad on camera.
2. **Nothing in Scout ever logs a call.** The sandbox CRM keeps its data in memory and starts empty every time the app starts, so the finished feature would have nothing to show. The "after" shot would be an empty brief.

**Better follow-up:** "Show when we last emailed the contact in the company profile step."
- **Unambiguous**, and it's something a rep would actually ask for.
- **A stronger test of memory:** the request names a tool (the company profile), so the tempting build is that tool importing outreach code, the same mistake beat 3's gate caught. Remembering DR-4 means the agent has the run loop hand the date to the tool instead, and you see it respect the decision in the exact spot where it would most likely slip.
- **Visible result:** every research run drafts an email, so the profile step will show "Last emailed Oct 11" in the app.
- **It works for both memory moments:** the same prompt in a fresh harness session, and in a teammate's plain Claude Code session for the Alike beat.

```typescript
// UI → API links for journeys (NAVIGATION_PLAN §2 "Journeys"): `fetch` call sites (direct, through a small wrapper
// such as Scout's `request(path)`, or axios/ky) with their URL literal, matched to route facts. Pure and browser-safe:
// it scans source text, using the file's symbol spans only to name the enclosing symbol.
import type { RouteFact, SymbolFact } from '../contracts/facts';

/** A call that sends an HTTP request to a URL known (at least in part) from the source text. */
export type FetchSite = {
  file: string;
  from: string; // enclosing symbol id, or the file path for top-level code
  method: string; // upper case; GET when the call doesn't say
  url: string; // path only, query dropped, `${…}` → `{}`
  exact: boolean; // the whole URL is literal text at the call (no template holes, no wrapper prefix)
  via: string | null; // wrapper or client the call goes through (`request`, `axios.post`), null for a direct fetch
};

export type SourceFile = { path: string; source: string; symbols: readonly SymbolFact[] };

const CLIENT = /(?<![\w$.])(?:(fetch|\$fetch|ofetch)|(axios|ky)\s*\.\s*(get|post|put|patch|delete|head|options))\s*(?:<[^()]*?>)?\s*\(/g;
const QUOTES = new Set(['"', "'", '`']);

/** Read a string or template literal starting at `i` (the quote). Template holes become `{}`; `holes` counts them. */
function readString(src: string, i: number): { value: string; end: number; holes: number; tail: string } | null {
  const q = src[i];
  if (!q || !QUOTES.has(q)) return null;
  let value = '';
  let holes = 0;
  let tail = ''; // literal text after the last hole
  for (let j = i + 1; j < src.length; j++) {
    const c = src[j]!;
    if (c === '\\') { value += src[j + 1] ?? ''; tail += src[j + 1] ?? ''; j++; continue; }
    if (c === q) return { value, end: j + 1, holes, tail: holes ? tail : value };
    if (q !== '`' && c === '\n') return null;
    if (q === '`' && c === '$' && src[j + 1] === '{') {
      let depth = 1;
      j += 2;
      for (; j < src.length && depth; j++) {
        const d = src[j]!;
        if (d === '{') depth++;
        else if (d === '}') depth--;
        else if (QUOTES.has(d)) { const s = readString(src, j); if (s) j = s.end - 1; }
      }
      j--;
      value += '{}';
      holes++;
      tail = '';
      continue;
    }
    value += c;
    tail += c;
  }
  return null;
}

/** Index just past the `)` that closes the call whose `(` is at `open - 1`, skipping strings; src.length if unbalanced. */
function argsEnd(src: string, open: number): number {
  let depth = 1;
  for (let j = open; j < src.length; j++) {
    const c = src[j]!;
    if (QUOTES.has(c)) { const s = readString(src, j); if (s) { j = s.end - 1; continue; } }
    if (c === '(' || c === '[' || c === '{') depth++;
    else if (c === ')' || c === ']' || c === '}') { depth--; if (!depth) return j + 1; }
  }
  return src.length;
}

const skipWs = (src: string, i: number) => { while (i < src.length && /\s/.test(src[i]!)) i++; return i; };

/** Path part of a URL: origin, query and hash dropped, slashes collapsed. Null unless it is a path (starts with `/`). */
export function urlPath(raw: string): string | null {
  let u = raw.trim().replace(/^https?:\/\/[^/]+/, '');
  u = u.replace(/[?#].*$/, '').replace(/\/{2,}/g, '/');
  if (!u.startsWith('/')) return null;
  return u.length > 1 ? u.replace(/\/$/, '') : u;
}

function enclosing(file: SourceFile, at: number): string {
  let best: SymbolFact | null = null;
  for (const s of file.symbols) {
    if (s.kind === 'type' || s.span.end <= s.span.start || at < s.span.start || at >= s.span.end) continue;
    if (!best || s.span.end - s.span.start < best.span.end - best.span.start) best = s;
  }
  return best?.id ?? file.path;
}

const shortName = (id: string) => (id.includes('#') ? id.slice(id.indexOf('#') + 1).split('.').at(-1)! : null);

type Wrapper = { name: string; prefix: string; method: string | null; symbol: string };

/**
 * Every fetch site in `files`:
 * 1. direct calls (`fetch`, `$fetch`, `ofetch`, `axios.<m>`, `ky.<m>`) whose first argument is a URL literal;
 * 2. wrappers: a function whose `fetch` takes a non-literal URL (`fetch(path)`, ``fetch(`/api${path}`)``) is a wrapper
 *    with that prefix; calls to it by name, anywhere, with a URL literal first argument are sites (`via` = its name).
 * The method comes from the client name (`axios.post`) or a `method: "POST"` in the call's arguments; else GET.
 * Sorted by file, then position.
 */
export function findFetchSites(files: readonly SourceFile[]): FetchSite[] {
  const wrappers = new Map<string, Wrapper>();
  const sites: (FetchSite & { at: number })[] = [];
  const methodIn = (src: string, from: number, to: number) => /\bmethod\s*:\s*["'`]([A-Za-z]+)["'`]/.exec(src.slice(from, to))?.[1]?.toUpperCase() ?? null;

  for (const f of files) {
    const src = f.source;
    if (!/fetch|axios|ky\s*\./.test(src)) continue;
    for (const m of src.matchAll(CLIENT)) {
      const open = m.index + m[0].length;
      const end = argsEnd(src, open);
      const a = skipWs(src, open);
      const str = readString(src, a);
      const client = m[1] ?? `${m[2]}.${m[3]}`;
      const fixed = m[3] ? m[3].toUpperCase() : null;
      const from = enclosing(f, m.index);
      if (str) {
        // `${…}` right after a literal prefix that doesn't end in `/` (e.g. `/api${path}`): a wrapper, not a site.
        const lead = str.value.indexOf('{}');
        if (str.holes && lead >= 0 && !str.value.slice(0, lead).endsWith('/') && str.tail === '' && str.holes === 1) {
          const name = shortName(from);
          if (name) wrappers.set(name, { name, prefix: str.value.slice(0, lead), method: fixed ?? methodIn(src, str.end, end), symbol: from });
          continue;
        }
        const url = urlPath(str.value);
        if (url) sites.push({ file: f.path, from, method: fixed ?? methodIn(src, str.end, end) ?? 'GET', url, exact: str.holes === 0, via: client === 'fetch' ? null : client, at: m.index });
      } else if (/^[A-Za-z_$][\w$]*\s*[,)]/.test(src.slice(a, a + 80))) {
        const name = shortName(from);
        if (name) wrappers.set(name, { name, prefix: '', method: fixed ?? methodIn(src, a, end), symbol: from });
      }
    }
  }

  if (wrappers.size) {
    const names = [...wrappers.keys()].map((n) => n.replace(/[$]/g, '\\$')).join('|');
    const call = new RegExp(`(?<![\\w$])(${names})\\s*(?:<[^()]*?>)?\\s*\\(`, 'g');
    for (const f of files) {
      const src = f.source;
      for (const m of src.matchAll(call)) {
        if (/\bfunction\s*\*?\s*$/.test(src.slice(Math.max(0, m.index - 12), m.index))) continue; // the definition
        const w = wrappers.get(m[1]!)!;
        const open = m.index + m[0].length;
        const a = skipWs(src, open);
        const str = readString(src, a);
        if (!str) continue;
        const url = urlPath(w.prefix + str.value);
        if (!url) continue;
        const from = enclosing(f, m.index);
        if (from === w.symbol) continue;
        sites.push({ file: f.path, from, method: w.method ?? methodIn(src, str.end, argsEnd(src, open)) ?? 'GET', url, exact: str.holes === 0 && w.prefix === '', via: w.name, at: m.index });
      }
    }
  }
  return sites
    .sort((x, y) => (x.file < y.file ? -1 : x.file > y.file ? 1 : x.at - y.at))
    .map(({ at: _at, ...s }) => s);
}

const segs = (p: string) => p.split('/').filter(Boolean);
const segRe = (s: string) => new RegExp(`^${s.split('{}').map((x) => x.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, '\\$&')).join('[^/]+')}$`);

/**
 * The route a site calls: same number of path segments, each equal or matched through a `{}` on either side, and the
 * same method (a route with method ANY matches any). Among matches the one with the fewest wildcards wins (then id).
 * `syntactic` when the site's URL is exact and matched a route segment-for-segment with no wildcard on the site side;
 * otherwise `inferred`.
 */
export function matchRoute(site: Pick<FetchSite, 'method' | 'url' | 'exact'>, routes: readonly RouteFact[]): { route: RouteFact; confidence: 'syntactic' | 'inferred' } | null {
  const want = segs(site.url);
  let best: { route: RouteFact; wild: number; siteWild: boolean } | null = null;
  for (const r of routes) {
    if (r.method !== site.method && r.method !== 'ANY') continue;
    const have = segs(r.path);
    if (have.length !== want.length) continue;
    let wild = 0;
    let siteWild = false;
    let ok = true;
    for (let i = 0; i < have.length && ok; i++) {
      const [h, w] = [have[i]!, want[i]!];
      if (h === w) continue;
      if (h === '{}') { wild++; continue; }
      if (w.includes('{}') && segRe(w).test(h)) { wild++; siteWild = true; continue; }
      if (h.includes('{}') && segRe(h).test(w)) { wild++; continue; }
      ok = false;
    }
    if (!ok) continue;
    if (!best || wild < best.wild || (wild === best.wild && r.id < best.route.id)) best = { route: r, wild, siteWild };
  }
  if (!best) return null;
  const exact = site.exact && !best.siteWild && best.route.method !== 'ANY';
  return { route: best.route, confidence: exact ? 'syntactic' : 'inferred' };
}
```

```typescript
// SemanticResolver on TypeScript 7's `typescript/unstable/sync` API (tsgo), pinned to exactly 7.0.2 and installed under
// the alias `typescript-7` so the repo's own `tsc` stays on 5.x. The API is officially unstable until 7.1, so only the
// handful of calls below are used, typed structurally here rather than through the package's own declarations.
import { existsSync } from 'node:fs';
import { join, relative, sep } from 'node:path';
import { isAbstract, kindTable, packageOf, qualifiedName, type DeclNode } from './names';
import type { DeclInfo, FileChanges, ResolverOptions, SemanticResolver } from './types';

type RemoteNode = DeclNode & { getSourceFile(): { fileName: string } };
type Handle = { readonly path: string; readonly index: number; resolve(project: Project): RemoteNode | undefined };
type Sym = { readonly flags: number; readonly declarations?: readonly Handle[]; readonly valueDeclaration?: Handle };
type Project = {
  readonly configFileName: string;
  readonly checker: { getSymbolAtPosition(file: string, positions: readonly number[]): (Sym | undefined)[]; getAliasedSymbol(s: Sym): Sym };
};
type Snapshot = { getProjects(): readonly Project[]; getDefaultProjectForFile(file: string): Project | undefined; dispose(): void };
type Api = { updateSnapshot(params?: Record<string, unknown>): Snapshot; close(): void };
type SyncModule = { API: new (options: { cwd: string }) => Api; SymbolFlags: Record<string, number> };
type AstModule = { SyntaxKind: Record<string, unknown> };

/** Module ids, held in variables so the TS 5 compiler of this repo doesn't type-check TS 7's declarations. */
const SYNC: string = 'typescript-7/unstable/sync';
const AST: string = 'typescript-7/unstable/ast';

const posix = (p: string) => p.split(sep).join('/');

export async function createTsgoResolver({ root, files }: ResolverOptions): Promise<SemanticResolver> {
  const sync = (await import(SYNC)) as SyncModule;
  const kindOf = kindTable(((await import(AST)) as AstModule).SyntaxKind);
  const ALIAS = sync.SymbolFlags.Alias ?? 0;
  const api = new sync.API({ cwd: root });
  const abs = (rel: string) => join(root, rel);
  const rootLower = `${root.toLowerCase()}/`;
  const tsconfig = join(root, 'tsconfig.json');

  let snap: Snapshot;
  try {
    snap = api.updateSnapshot(existsSync(tsconfig) ? { openProjects: [tsconfig] } : { openFiles: files.map(abs) });
  } catch (e) {
    api.close();
    throw e;
  }
  const decls = new Map<string, DeclInfo>(); // per snapshot: `${path}\0${index}` → info
  const opened = new Set<string>();
  const next = (params: Record<string, unknown>) => {
    const s = api.updateSnapshot(params);
    snap.dispose();
    snap = s;
    decls.clear();
  };

  /** The file's default project; files outside every tsconfig are opened once (inferred project). */
  const projectFor = (rel: string): Project | undefined => {
    const file = abs(rel);
    let p = snap.getDefaultProjectForFile(file);
    if (!p && !opened.has(rel)) {
      opened.add(rel);
      next({ openFiles: [file] });
      p = snap.getDefaultProjectForFile(file);
    }
    return p;
  };

  const classify = (h: Handle, project: Project): DeclInfo | null => {
    const lower = h.path.toLowerCase(); // tsgo canonicalizes paths (lower case on case-insensitive file systems)
    if (lower.includes('/node_modules/')) {
      const pkg = packageOf(lower);
      return pkg ? { where: 'package', pkg } : { where: 'lib' };
    }
    if (!lower.startsWith(rootLower)) return { where: 'lib' };
    const key = `${lower}\0${h.index}`;
    let info = decls.get(key);
    if (!info) {
      const node = h.resolve(project);
      if (!node) return null;
      info = { where: 'repo', file: posix(relative(root, node.getSourceFile().fileName)), name: qualifiedName(node, kindOf), abstract: isAbstract(node, kindOf) };
      decls.set(key, info);
    }
    return info;
  };

  return {
    impl: 'tsgo',
    declarationsAt(file, positions) {
      if (!positions.length) return [];
      const project = projectFor(file);
      if (!project) return positions.map(() => null);
      const syms = project.checker.getSymbolAtPosition(abs(file), positions);
      return syms.map((s0) => {
        if (!s0) return null;
        try {
          const s = s0.flags & ALIAS ? project.checker.getAliasedSymbol(s0) : s0;
          const h = s.declarations?.[0] ?? s.valueDeclaration;
          return h ? classify(h, project) : null;
        } catch {
          return null;
        }
      });
    },
    update({ changed, created, deleted }: FileChanges) {
      if (!changed.length && !created.length && !deleted.length) return;
      next({ fileChanges: { changed: changed.map(abs), created: created.map(abs), deleted: deleted.map(abs) } });
    },
    close() {
      try { snap.dispose(); } catch { /* already gone */ }
      api.close();
    },
  };
}
```

```typescript
// Per-container ELK layout (NAVIGATION_PLAN §3.3): one layered run per expanded container, bottom-up (an open group
// is laid out first and enters its cell's run as a fixed-size node with fixed ports), cached by the container's input.
// The ELK instance is injected: the browser uses elkjs's worker, tests use the bundled build in node.
import type { ElkExtendedEdge, ElkNode, ElkPort } from 'elkjs/lib/elk-api';

export type Pt = { x: number; y: number };
export type Box = { x: number; y: number; w: number; h: number };
export type Side = 'top' | 'right' | 'bottom' | 'left';

/** Fixed sizes per kind (layout never depends on zoom or text, so positions stay put). */
export const SIZE = {
  file: { w: 220, h: 42 },
  chip: { w: 220, h: 34 }, // tables, vendors, routes
  group: { w: 220, h: 50 }, // a collapsed group
} as const;
export const PAD = { top: 46, left: 18, right: 18, bottom: 18 };

export type ChildSpec = { id: string; w: number; h: number; ports: { id: string; at: Pt; side: Side }[] };
export type ContainerInput = {
  id: string;
  children: ChildSpec[]; // sorted by model order
  edges: { id: string; from: string; to: string }[]; // child ids, or a child's port id
  /** Edges leaving (out) or entering (in) this container; `node` is the child (or child port) inside it. */
  ports: { key: string; edge: string; node: string; side: Side; direction: 'out' | 'in' }[];
};

export type ContainerLayout = {
  id: string;
  w: number;
  h: number;
  nodes: Record<string, Box>; // relative to the container
  /** Every route this container draws, by projection edge id, in edge direction (child → port for out, port → child for in). */
  edges: Record<string, Pt[]>;
  ports: Record<string, { at: Pt; side: Side }>; // by port key, relative to the container
  ms: number;
};

export const portKey = (edge: string, container: string) => `${edge}|${container}`;

const ELK_SIDE = { top: 'NORTH', right: 'EAST', bottom: 'SOUTH', left: 'WEST' } as const;

export function elkGraph(c: ContainerInput): ElkNode {
  const edges: ElkExtendedEdge[] = c.edges.map((e) => ({ id: e.id, sources: [e.from], targets: [e.to] }));
  const ports: ElkPort[] = c.ports.map((p, i) => {
    edges.push(p.direction === 'out' ? { id: `pe:${i}`, sources: [p.node], targets: [p.key] } : { id: `pe:${i}`, sources: [p.key], targets: [p.node] });
    return { id: p.key, width: 2, height: 2, layoutOptions: { 'elk.port.side': ELK_SIDE[p.side], 'elk.port.index': String(i) } };
  });
  const node: ElkNode = {
    id: c.id,
    layoutOptions: {
      'elk.algorithm': 'layered',
      'elk.direction': 'RIGHT',
      'elk.edgeRouting': 'ORTHOGONAL',
      'elk.randomSeed': '1',
      'elk.portConstraints': 'FIXED_SIDE',
      'elk.layered.considerModelOrder.strategy': 'NODES_AND_EDGES',
      // Model order as a tie-break only: forcing it cost 2.6× on a 300-file cell for little extra stability.
      'elk.layered.crossingMinimization.forceNodeModelOrder': 'false',
      'elk.layered.thoroughness': c.children.length > 100 ? '3' : '7',
      'elk.padding': `[top=${PAD.top},left=${PAD.left},bottom=${PAD.bottom},right=${PAD.right}]`,
      'elk.spacing.nodeNode': '12',
      'elk.spacing.componentComponent': '14',
      'elk.layered.spacing.nodeNodeBetweenLayers': '44',
      'elk.layered.spacing.edgeNodeBetweenLayers': '14',
      'elk.spacing.edgeEdge': '8',
      'elk.aspectRatio': '1.4',
    },
    ports,
    children: c.children.map((ch) => ({
      id: ch.id,
      width: ch.w,
      height: ch.h,
      ...(ch.ports.length
        ? {
            layoutOptions: { 'elk.portConstraints': 'FIXED_POS' },
            ports: ch.ports.map((p) => ({ id: p.id, x: p.at.x - 1, y: p.at.y - 1, width: 2, height: 2, layoutOptions: { 'elk.port.side': ELK_SIDE[p.side] } })),
          }
        : {}),
    })),
    edges,
  };
  // Wrapped in a root so the container's ports are real external ports (ELK rejects edges to the root's own ports).
  return { id: `root:${c.id}`, layoutOptions: { 'elk.algorithm': 'layered', 'elk.padding': '[top=0,left=0,bottom=0,right=0]' }, children: [node] };
}

function sectionPoints(e: ElkExtendedEdge): Pt[] {
  const s = e.sections?.[0];
  if (!s) return [];
  return [s.startPoint, ...(s.bendPoints ?? []), s.endPoint].map((p) => ({ x: p.x, y: p.y }));
}

export function readLayout(c: ContainerInput, root: ElkNode, ms: number): ContainerLayout {
  const out = root.children?.[0] ?? root;
  const nodes: ContainerLayout['nodes'] = {};
  for (const n of out.children ?? []) nodes[n.id] = { x: n.x ?? 0, y: n.y ?? 0, w: n.width ?? 0, h: n.height ?? 0 };
  const edges: ContainerLayout['edges'] = {};
  const ports: ContainerLayout['ports'] = {};
  const portAt = new Map((out.ports ?? []).map((p) => [p.id, { x: (p.x ?? 0) + (p.width ?? 0) / 2, y: (p.y ?? 0) + (p.height ?? 0) / 2 }]));
  const w = out.width ?? 0;
  const h = out.height ?? 0;
  for (const p of c.ports) {
    const at = portAt.get(p.key) ?? { x: p.side === 'left' ? 0 : w, y: h / 2 };
    // snap to the border on the declared side (ELK centres a 2 px port on it)
    if (p.side === 'left') at.x = 0;
    if (p.side === 'right') at.x = w;
    if (p.side === 'top') at.y = 0;
    if (p.side === 'bottom') at.y = h;
    ports[p.key] = { at, side: p.side };
  }
  for (const e of out.edges ?? []) {
    if (e.id.startsWith('pe:')) {
      const p = c.ports[Number(e.id.slice(3))]!;
      const pts = sectionPoints(e);
      const at = ports[p.key]!.at;
      if (pts.length) pts[p.direction === 'out' ? pts.length - 1 : 0] = { ...at };
      edges[p.edge] = pts;
    } else edges[e.id] = sectionPoints(e);
  }
  return { id: c.id, w, h, nodes, edges, ports, ms };
}

export type ElkApi = { layout(g: ElkNode): Promise<ElkNode> };
export type LayoutFn = (c: ContainerInput) => Promise<ContainerLayout>;

/** A layout function over an ELK instance, cached by the container's whole input (children, sizes, edges, ports). */
export function cachedLayout(getElk: () => Promise<ElkApi>, cache = new Map<string, ContainerLayout>()): LayoutFn & { cache: Map<string, ContainerLayout> } {
  const fn = async (c: ContainerInput) => {
    const key = JSON.stringify(c);
    const hit = cache.get(key);
    if (hit) return hit;
    const api = await getElk();
    const t0 = performance.now();
    const out = await api.layout(elkGraph(c));
    const l = readLayout(c, out, performance.now() - t0);
    cache.set(key, l);
    return l;
  };
  return Object.assign(fn, { cache });
}
```
