```typescript
// The auditor loop (NAVIGATION_PLAN §4.6): after every `turn_ended` (never mid-turn), pre-filter the standing decisions
// against what the turn touched; if any bear on it, run the auditor out of band and emit advisory `audit_finding`s.
// Plan review (D8) runs on each `planned` event only with HARNESS_AUDIT_PLANS=1. Dismiss is remembered; promote and
// rule reinforcement become living-map proposals (`map_proposed { proposal }`). Nothing here touches the ledger.
import { Hono } from 'hono';
import {
  reduce, turnSurface, planSurface, relevantDecisions, acceptFindings, nextFindingId, reinforcements, reinforcementSignal,
  changeRuleProposal, manualRuleProposal, reinforcedRuleText, amendedRuleText, changeSignature, summarizeChanges, historyFromUI, thresholdsFor,
  type AuditFinding, type FileFacts, type MapProposal, type TurnSurface, type UIState,
} from '@harness/core';
import { listDecisions } from '../decisions';
import type { Bus } from '../bus';
import type { Repo } from '../repo';
import { sdkAuditor, type Auditor } from './runner';
import { loadDismissed, rememberDismissed, standingDecisions, turnDiff } from './records';

export type AuditorOptions = {
  bus: Bus;
  repo: Repo;
  auditor?: Auditor | null; // default: the Agent SDK auditor (null when HARNESS_AUDITOR=0)
  plans?: boolean; // review each submitted plan too (default: HARNESS_AUDIT_PLANS=1)
};

export type Result = { ok: true; proposal?: string; manual?: boolean } | { ok: false; status: 400 | 404 | 409; error: string };

const nextProposalId = (ui: UIState) => `MP-${Math.max(0, ...Object.keys(ui.proposals).map((id) => Number(/^MP-(\d+)$/.exec(id)?.[1] ?? 0))) + 1}`;

export function attachAuditor(opts: AuditorOptions) {
  const { bus, repo } = opts;
  const auditor = opts.auditor === undefined ? (process.env.HARNESS_AUDITOR === '0' ? null : sdkAuditor) : opts.auditor;
  const plans = opts.plans ?? process.env.HARNESS_AUDIT_PLANS === '1';
  const work = new Set<Promise<unknown>>();
  let chain: Promise<unknown> = Promise.resolve();
  /** Audits run one at a time, in order, off the emitter's stack. */
  const enqueue = (job: () => Promise<unknown> | unknown) => {
    const p = chain.then(() => new Promise<void>((r) => setImmediate(r))).then(job).catch((e: Error) => {
      bus.emit('error', { message: `Auditor failed: ${e.message}` }, { turn: null });
    });
    chain = p;
    work.add(p);
    void p.finally(() => work.delete(p));
    return p;
  };
  const facts = (): Record<string, FileFacts> => Object.fromEntries(repo.fileFacts);

  /** Pre-filter, then (only if a decision bears on the turn) the model, then accepted findings as events. */
  async function audit(surface: TurnSurface): Promise<{ sent: string[]; findings: AuditFinding[] }> {
    if (!repo.map || !surface.files.length) return { sent: [], findings: [] };
    const relevant = relevantDecisions(standingDecisions(repo.root), repo.map, surface, repo.mapper);
    if (!relevant.length || !auditor) return { sent: relevant.map((r) => r.decision.id), findings: [] };
    const trigger = surface.source;
    const t0 = Date.now();
    let result;
    try {
      result = await auditor({
        root: repo.root,
        surface,
        decisions: relevant,
        invariants: repo.map.invariants,
        diff: surface.source === 'turn' ? turnDiff(repo.root, surface.baseline, surface.files) : '',
      });
    } catch (e) {
      bus.emit('maintenance_run', { agent: 'auditor', trigger, ms: Date.now() - t0, cost: (e as { cost?: number }).cost ?? null, ok: false }, { turn: null });
      bus.emit('error', { message: `Auditor failed: ${(e as Error).message}` }, { turn: null });
      return { sent: relevant.map((r) => r.decision.id), findings: [] };
    }
    const ui = reduce(bus.events);
    const open = Object.values(ui.findings).filter((f) => f.status === 'open');
    const accepted = acceptFindings(result.findings, { decisions: relevant.map((r) => r.decision.id), files: surface.files, dismissed: loadDismissed(repo.root), open });
    const ids = Object.keys(ui.findings);
    const emitted: AuditFinding[] = [];
    for (const f of accepted) {
      const finding: AuditFinding = { id: nextFindingId(ids), ...f };
      ids.push(finding.id);
      bus.emit('audit_finding', { finding }, { turn: surface.turn, path: finding.files[0]! });
      emitted.push(finding);
    }
    bus.emit('maintenance_run', { agent: 'auditor', trigger, ms: Date.now() - t0, cost: result.cost, ok: true }, { turn: null });
    return { sent: relevant.map((r) => r.decision.id), findings: emitted };
  }

  function auditTurn(turnId: string) {
    const s = turnSurface(bus.events, turnId);
    return s ? audit(s) : Promise.resolve({ sent: [], findings: [] });
  }

  function auditPlan(turnId: string) {
    const s = planSurface(bus.events, turnId);
    return s ? audit(s) : Promise.resolve({ sent: [], findings: [] });
  }

  /** Signatures of every rejected map proposal on record, so a rejected rule proposal is never repeated. */
  const rejectedSignatures = () => new Set(listDecisions(repo.root).flatMap((d) => {
    const fm = d as unknown as { status?: string; type?: string; signature?: string };
    return fm.status === 'rejected' && fm.type === 'map_proposal' && fm.signature ? [fm.signature] : [];
  }));

  function emitProposal(proposal: MapProposal, chat: string) {
    bus.emit('map_proposed', { map: repo.map, yaml: repo.mapText, proposal }, { turn: null });
    bus.emit('chat', { role: 'system', text: chat }, { turn: null });
  }

  /** Rule reinforcement (§4.4): option A on the same invariant ≥ N times in one domain → propose stating it as standing. */
  function reinforce(): string[] {
    if (!repo.map || !repo.hasMap()) return [];
    const ui = reduce(bus.events);
    const t = thresholdsFor(repo.map);
    const made: string[] = [];
    const rejected = rejectedSignatures();
    for (const r of reinforcements(ui.decisions, repo.map, t.ruleReinforcement)) {
      const signal = reinforcementSignal(r, t.ruleReinforcement);
      const scopeKey = signal.scope.join('|');
      const seen = Object.values(ui.proposals).some((p) => p.proposal.trigger.some((s) => s.signal === 'rule_reinforcement' && s.scope.join('|') === scopeKey));
      if (seen) continue;
      const inv = repo.map.invariants.find((i) => i.id === r.invariant)!;
      const rule = reinforcedRuleText(inv.rule, r, repo.map.domains.find((d) => d.id === r.domain)?.name ?? r.domain);
      if (rule === inv.rule) continue;
      const proposal = changeRuleProposal({
        id: nextProposalId(reduce(bus.events)), yaml: repo.mapText, map: repo.map, facts: facts(), history: historyFromUI(ui),
        trigger: [signal], scope: [`rule:${r.invariant}`, `domain:${r.domain}`, ...r.paths], invariant: r.invariant, rule,
        rationale: `You chose to comply with ${r.invariant} ${r.decisions.length} times for ${r.domain} (${r.decisions.join(', ')}). Make it a standing rule: the rule text records the confirmations, so the next session reads it as settled.`,
      });
      if (rejected.has(changeSignature(proposal.changes))) continue;
      emitProposal(proposal, `Auditor proposal ${proposal.id} (rule reinforcement): ${summarizeChanges(proposal.changes)}`);
      made.push(proposal.id);
    }
    return made;
  }

  function dismiss(id: string): Result {
    const f = reduce(bus.events).findings[id];
    if (!f) return { ok: false, status: 404, error: `No finding ${id}.` };
    if (f.status !== 'open') return { ok: false, status: 409, error: `${id} is already ${f.status}.` };
    rememberDismissed(repo.root, f);
    bus.emit('audit_resolved', { id, outcome: 'dismissed' }, { turn: null });
    return { ok: true };
  }

  /**
   * Promote a finding into a rule proposal. If its decision is linked to an invariant, the proposal amends that rule's
   * text with the decision (a candidate map, so accept commits it); otherwise it is manual (rule text, no candidate).
   * See packages/core/src/audit/rules.ts for why the three rule kinds rarely express these.
   */
  function promote(id: string): Result {
    const ui = reduce(bus.events);
    const f = ui.findings[id];
    if (!f) return { ok: false, status: 404, error: `No finding ${id}.` };
    if (f.status !== 'open') return { ok: false, status: 409, error: `${id} is already ${f.status}.` };
    if (!repo.map || !repo.hasMap()) return { ok: false, status: 409, error: 'No confirmed map yet.' };
    const decision = f.decision ? standingDecisions(repo.root).find((d) => d.id === f.decision) : undefined;
    const inv = decision?.invariant ? repo.map.invariants.find((i) => i.id === decision.invariant) : undefined;
    const base = {
      id: nextProposalId(ui), yaml: repo.mapText, map: repo.map, facts: facts(), history: historyFromUI(ui), trigger: [],
      scope: [...(inv ? [`rule:${inv.id}`] : []), ...f.files],
    };
    const rule = inv && decision ? amendedRuleText(inv.rule, decision) : null;
    const proposal = inv && rule && rule !== inv.rule
      ? changeRuleProposal({ ...base, invariant: inv.id, rule, rationale: `Promoted from ${id}: ${f.text} The three rule kinds can't check ${decision!.id} directly; accepting states it in ${inv.id}'s rule text, and the auditor keeps checking it.` })
      : manualRuleProposal({ ...base, invariant: id, rule: decision ? `${decision.id}: ${decision.title}` : f.text, rationale: `Promoted from ${id}: ${f.text} No rule kind can express this, so there is no candidate map: write the rule into domains.yaml by hand, or reject.` });
    emitProposal(proposal, `Auditor proposal ${proposal.id} (from ${id}): ${summarizeChanges(proposal.changes)}${proposal.candidates.length ? '' : ' (manual)'}`);
    bus.emit('audit_resolved', { id, outcome: 'promoted' }, { turn: null });
    return { ok: true, proposal: proposal.id, manual: !proposal.candidates.length };
  }

  const off = bus.on((e) => {
    if (e.kind === 'turn_ended' && e.turn) {
      const turn = e.turn;
      enqueue(() => { reinforce(); return auditTurn(turn); });
    } else if (e.kind === 'planned' && plans && e.turn) {
      const turn = e.turn;
      enqueue(() => auditPlan(turn));
    }
  });

  return {
    /** Audit a finished turn now (also runs automatically at every turn end). */
    run(turnId: string) { return enqueue(() => auditTurn(turnId)) as Promise<unknown>; },
    auditTurn,
    auditPlan,
    reinforce,
    dismiss,
    promote,
    /** Resolves once no audit is queued or running (for tests and shutdown). */
    async idle() { while (work.size) await Promise.allSettled([...work]); },
    detach: off,
  };
}

export type AuditorLoop = ReturnType<typeof attachAuditor>;

/** HTTP endpoints, mounted under /api by the server. */
export function auditorRoutes(a: AuditorLoop) {
  const r = new Hono();
  const reply = (c: { json: (b: unknown, s?: 200 | 400 | 404 | 409) => Response }, res: Result) => (res.ok ? c.json(res) : c.json({ error: res.error }, res.status));
  r.post('/findings/:id/dismiss', (c) => reply(c, a.dismiss(c.req.param('id'))));
  r.post('/findings/:id/promote', (c) => reply(c, a.promote(c.req.param('id'))));
  r.post('/audit/turns/:turn', (c) => { void a.run(c.req.param('turn')); return c.json({ ok: true, queued: true }); });
  return r;
}
```

```typescript
// Custom React Flow nodes. Each is memoized and reads only its own slice of the projection from the v2 store, plus
// the zoom bucket, so a zoom re-renders a node only when its level of detail changes.
import { memo } from 'react';
import { useStore as useFlow, type NodeProps } from '@xyflow/react';
import type { Rollup, VisibleNode } from '@harness/core/view';
import { useTween } from '../hooks';
import { useStore } from '../store';
import { selectedNode } from './select';
import { useV2 } from './store';

export type Lod = 'far' | 'mid' | 'near';
export const lodOf = (zoom: number): Lod => (zoom < 0.36 ? 'far' : zoom < 0.72 ? 'mid' : 'near');
export const useLod = () => useFlow((s) => lodOf(s.transform[2]));

const base = (p: string) => p.split('/').pop() ?? p;

function stateClasses(r: Rollup, ghost: boolean) {
  const c: string[] = [];
  if (r.looked && !r.edited) c.push('is-looked');
  if (r.edited) c.push(r.unplanned ? 'is-unplanned' : 'is-edited');
  if (ghost) c.push('is-ghost');
  if (r.violation === 'existing') c.push('is-violation');
  if (r.violation === 'new') c.push('is-new-violation');
  if (r.cursor) c.push('is-cursor');
  return c.join(' ');
}

function useMarks(id: string) {
  const focus = useV2((s) => s.focus === id);
  const selected = useStore((s) => selectedNode(s.selection) === id);
  return `${focus ? 'is-focus' : ''} ${selected ? 'is-selected' : ''}`;
}

function Steps({ steps }: { steps: number[] }) {
  if (!steps.length) return null;
  return (
    <span className="v2-steps" aria-label={`Planned in step ${steps.join(', ')}`}>
      {steps.map((n) => <span key={n} className="v2-step">{n}</span>)}
    </span>
  );
}

/** +/− badge, ticking up as edits land. */
function Diff({ r }: { r: Rollup }) {
  const added = useTween(r.added);
  const removed = useTween(r.removed);
  if (!r.edited) return null;
  return (
    <span className="v2-diff">
      <span className="plus">+{added}</span>
      <span className="minus">−{removed}</span>
    </span>
  );
}

/** Existing crossings: a ring badge with the rule ids and file count. New crossings: a solid badge naming the file. */
function Violations({ r, compact = false }: { r: Rollup; compact?: boolean }) {
  if (!r.violation) return null;
  const existing = r.violationFiles.filter((f) => !r.newViolationFiles.includes(f));
  return (
    <span className="v2-vmarks">
      {r.newViolationFiles.length > 0 && (
        <span className="v2-vmark is-new" title={r.newViolationFiles.join('\n')}>
          <b>new</b>{!compact && <> {r.newViolationFiles.map(base).join(', ')}</>}
        </span>
      )}
      {(existing.length > 0 || (!r.newViolationFiles.length && r.rules.length > 0)) && (
        <span className="v2-vmark" title={[...r.rules, ...existing].join('\n')}>
          {compact ? existing.length || r.rules.length : `${r.rules.join(' ')}${existing.length > 1 ? ` · ${existing.length}` : ''}`}
        </span>
      )}
    </span>
  );
}

const useNode = (id: string) => useV2((s) => s.nodes[id]) as VisibleNode | undefined;

export const FileNode = memo(function FileNode({ id }: NodeProps) {
  const n = useNode(id);
  const lod = useLod();
  const marks = useMarks(id);
  const syms = useV2((s) => s.symbols[id] ?? 0);
  if (!n) return null;
  const r = n.rollup;
  const ghost = r.ghostSteps.length > 0;
  return (
    <div className={`v2-file ${stateClasses(r, ghost)} ${r.plannedNew ? 'is-planned-new' : ''} lod-${lod} ${marks}`} title={n.path ?? n.id}>
      {lod !== 'far' && <span className="v2-file-name">{n.label}</span>}
      {lod !== 'far' && (
        <span className="v2-file-meta">
          {syms > 0 && <span className="v2-syms" title={`${syms} symbol${syms === 1 ? '' : 's'} changed`}>ƒ{syms}</span>}
          <Diff r={r} />
        </span>
      )}
      <Steps steps={r.ghostSteps} />
      {lod !== 'far' && <Violations r={r} />}
    </div>
  );
});

export const CellNode = memo(function CellNode({ id }: NodeProps) {
  const n = useNode(id);
  const lod = useLod();
  const marks = useMarks(id);
  const hot = useV2((s) => s.hot[id]);
  if (!n) return null;
  const r = n.rollup;
  const ghost = r.ghostSteps.length > 0 && !r.edited;
  const names = hot ?? n.preview;
  const room = lod === 'near' ? 4 : 2;
  const shown = names.slice(0, room);
  const more = r.leaves - shown.length;
  return (
    <div className={`v2-cell ${stateClasses(r, ghost)} lod-${lod} ${marks}`}>
      {lod === 'far' ? (
        <span className="v2-cell-count is-big">{r.leaves}</span>
      ) : (
        <>
          <span className="v2-cell-files">
            {shown.map((f, i) => <span key={`${f}${i}`} className="v2-cell-file">{f}</span>)}
            {more > 0 && <span className="v2-cell-more">+{more} more</span>}
          </span>
          <span className="v2-cell-foot">
            <span className="v2-cell-count">{r.leaves} {r.leaves === 1 ? 'file' : 'files'}</span>
            <Diff r={r} />
          </span>
        </>
      )}
      {ghost && <Steps steps={r.ghostSteps} />}
      <Violations r={r} compact={lod === 'far'} />
    </div>
  );
});

/** A compressed column's cell: no text, only the state it carries (fill, ghost dash, rule marks, count). */
export const SpineNode = memo(function SpineNode({ id }: NodeProps) {
  const n = useNode(id);
  const marks = useMarks(id);
  if (!n) return null;
  const r = n.rollup;
  const ghost = r.ghostSteps.length > 0 && !r.edited;
  return (
    <div className={`v2-spine ${stateClasses(r, ghost)} ${marks}`} title={`${n.label}: ${r.leaves} files`}>
      <span className="v2-spine-count">{r.leaves}</span>
      {ghost && <Steps steps={r.ghostSteps} />}
      <Violations r={r} compact />
    </div>
  );
});

export const ContainerNode = memo(function ContainerNode({ id }: NodeProps) {
  const n = useNode(id);
  const lod = useLod();
  const marks = useMarks(id);
  if (!n) return null;
  const r = n.rollup;
  return (
    <div className={`v2-container is-${n.kind} ${r.violation ? `has-${r.violation}` : ''} ${r.edited ? 'has-edits' : ''} lod-${lod} ${marks}`}>
      <span className="v2-container-head">
        <span className="v2-container-name">{n.kind === 'group' ? n.label : n.label}</span>
        <span className="v2-container-count">{r.leaves} {r.leaves === 1 ? 'file' : 'files'}</span>
        <Diff r={r} />
      </span>
    </div>
  );
});

/** A collapsed directory or component inside an open cell. */
export const GroupNode = memo(function GroupNode({ id }: NodeProps) {
  const n = useNode(id);
  const lod = useLod();
  const marks = useMarks(id);
  if (!n) return null;
  const r = n.rollup;
  const ghost = r.ghostSteps.length > 0 && !r.edited;
  return (
    <div className={`v2-group ${stateClasses(r, ghost)} lod-${lod} ${marks}`} title={n.preview.join(', ')}>
      {lod !== 'far' && <span className="v2-group-name">{n.label}</span>}
      {lod !== 'far' && <span className="v2-group-count">{r.leaves} files <Diff r={r} /></span>}
      {ghost && <Steps steps={r.ghostSteps} />}
      {lod !== 'far' && <Violations r={r} compact />}
    </div>
  );
});

/** Tables, vendors and routes inside an open cell. */
export const ChipNode = memo(function ChipNode({ id }: NodeProps) {
  const n = useNode(id);
  const lod = useLod();
  const marks = useMarks(id);
  if (!n) return null;
  return (
    <div className={`v2-chip is-${n.kind} ${stateClasses(n.rollup, false)} ${marks}`}>
      {lod !== 'far' && <><span className="v2-chip-kind">{n.kind === 'table' ? 'table' : n.kind}</span><span className="v2-chip-name">{n.label}</span></>}
    </div>
  );
});

/** The open column: the next step down the depth lightness ramp. */
export const BandNode = memo(function BandNode() {
  return <div className="v2-band" />;
});

export const nodeTypes = { file: FileNode, cell: CellNode, spine: SpineNode, container: ContainerNode, group: GroupNode, chip: ChipNode, band: BandNode };
```

Here's how I'd frame what Alike plus the harness offers beyond basic memory.

**Basic memory (Alike on its own):** it remembers what you decided, attaches that to file paths, and puts it in front of any agent that works there. It's advisory: the agent reads it and usually follows it. It can't tell whether the code still follows the decision, and a new file that didn't exist when you decided has no anchor.

**Architectural memory (Alike plus the harness):** the decision is attached to the architecture, e.g. "research tools never touch outreach data", not to files. That gets you four things basic memory can't:
1. **It covers code that doesn't exist yet.** A tool written next month is still a research tool, so the decision still applies.
2. **It shapes the plan before any code.** The rejected approach shows on the map as blocked ("you decided this in DR-4"), and the agent builds the decided way.
3. **It's checked against the actual code**, both when the repo loads and through the auditor (beat 6). Basic memory can't tell you the code has drifted from what you decided.
4. **It shows where it came from:** click the edge and you see "decided in session 1, DR-4".

Alike's part stays essential: it carries the decision to agents and teammates who never open the harness.

**Line:** "Alike remembers what we decided. The harness makes it part of the architecture, so it holds for code nobody has written yet."

**Beats 3 and 4, reworked so they're obviously feature requests and memory changes what gets built:**

**Beat 3: the decision is made.**
- **You type:** "Can we add a research tool that checks whether we've already emailed this contact?"
- **Plan:** a new tool importing outreach code. The edge goes red (DR-3), and Claude asks A or B.
- **You pick A**, worded as a principle rather than a one-off fix: "Research tools never read outreach data. The run loop passes outreach context in."
- **Result:** DR-4 is recorded in git and Alike, and built the decided way.

**Beat 4: memory stops something being built.**
- **Fresh session. You type:** "Can we build a research tool that reads our past emails with this contact and suggests a personalized opener?"
- **What you see:**
  1. The plan comes back without the tool you asked for. The edge you'd expect (Research tools → Outreach) is drawn struck through: "rejected in DR-4, session 1".
  2. Claude says: "Per DR-4, I won't build this as a research tool. The run loop will pass a summary of past emails into the email draft."
  3. The ghosts form a clean stripe in Agent loop › Logic and Outreach › Logic.
  4. The ledger's "Rejected options blocked" counter goes to 1.
- **Why it's strong:** this is a different feature from beat 3, in a file that didn't exist when you decided. Memory that only knew which files were involved wouldn't stop it.
- **Say:** "I asked for a tool. It remembered we don't build it that way, and built the feature the way we agreed. Nobody had to remember, and I didn't have to re-explain."

**Optional teammate moment for Alike** (10–15 s): the same request in a teammate's plain Claude Code session. Alike puts DR-4 in front of their agent, which follows the same approach.
- **Say:** "Alike makes sure every agent hears the decision; the harness makes sure the code honors it."
- This frames the two as complementary rather than making Alike look weak, which matters since they're a sponsor.

**Two things to check in rehearsal:**
- **How beat 4's plan resolves.** It either avoids the tool from the start, because DR-4 is in the session brief, or plans it, gets blocked with "You decided this in DR-4", and replans without asking you. Both show memory working; the second is more visible on the map, since red appears and then resolves itself.
- **What beat 4 needs from the harness:** the struck-through rejected edge and the "rejected options blocked" counter. The counter is in SPEC §9. The struck-through drawing isn't specified anywhere yet, so the other session needs it.

```typescript
// Journeys (NAVIGATION_PLAN §2, phase N10), server side: compute journeys from the repo's Tier 1 facts and fetch sites
// (pure, in @harness/core), name them with a small model (cached under .harness/journeys/<hash>.json by the hash of
// the step list; inferred until confirmed), and publish `journeys_updated` on load, after turns that change them, and on
// confirm. The namer never blocks anything: placeholder names go out first, model names follow.
import { existsSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { join } from 'node:path';
import { Hono } from 'hono';
import { query } from '@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk';
import {
  buildGraph, computeJourneys, findFetchSites, journeyHash, reduce,
  type ContextGraph, type FileFacts, type Journey,
} from '@harness/core';
import type { Bus } from '../bus';
import type { Repo } from '../repo';

export type NamerInput = { root: string; journeys: { id: string; steps: string[] }[] };
export type Namer = (input: NamerInput) => Promise<{ names: { id: string; name: string }[]; cost: number | null }>;

const NAMES_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object', additionalProperties: false, required: ['names'],
  properties: {
    names: {
      type: 'array',
      items: { type: 'object', additionalProperties: false, required: ['id', 'name'], properties: { id: { type: 'string' }, name: { type: 'string' } } },
    },
  },
} as const;

export function namerPrompt(input: NamerInput): string {
  return [
    'Each block below is a user flow through a codebase: an entry point (UI page, HTTP route, CLI, script) followed by the code it runs, down to the services and tables it ends at.',
    'Give each flow a short product-language name a PM would use: 2–4 words, verb first, sentence case, no code names or URLs (e.g. "Start research", "Send a drafted email", "View usage").',
    'Return one name per id, using the exact ids given.',
    '',
    ...input.journeys.flatMap((j) => [`## ${j.id}`, ...j.steps.map((s, i) => `${i + 1}. ${s}`), '']),
  ].join('\n');
}

/** Real namer: a small, tool-less structured query. Model: `HARNESS_JOURNEY_MODEL` (default `claude-haiku-5-5`). */
export const sdkNamer: Namer = async (input) => {
  const q = query({
    prompt: namerPrompt(input),
    options: {
      cwd: input.root, model: process.env.HARNESS_JOURNEY_MODEL ?? 'claude-haiku-5-5', tools: [], settingSources: [], strictMcpConfig: true,
      outputFormat: { type: 'json_schema', schema: NAMES_SCHEMA as unknown as Record<string, unknown> }, maxTurns: 3,
    },
  });
  for await (const m of q) {
    if (m.type !== 'result') continue;
    if (m.subtype !== 'success' || !m.structured_output) throw Object.assign(new Error(`journey namer ${m.subtype}`), { cost: m.total_cost_usd });
    return { names: (m.structured_output as { names: { id: string; name: string }[] }).names ?? [], cost: m.total_cost_usd };
  }
  throw new Error('journey namer returned no result');
};

/** How a step reads in the namer's prompt: `<kind>: <label>` with the node's path or id for context. */
export function describeStep(graph: ContextGraph, step: Journey['steps'][number]): string {
  const n = graph.nodes[step.node];
  const where = step.node.includes('#') ? step.node : n?.path ?? step.node;
  return `${step.kind}: ${n?.label ?? step.node}${where !== n?.label ? ` (${where})` : ''}`;
}

/** Journeys for the repo's current facts and sources (deterministic; names are placeholders). */
export function journeysFor(repo: Repo): { journeys: Journey[]; graph: ContextGraph } {
  const facts: Record<string, FileFacts> = Object.fromEntries(repo.fileFacts);
  const sources = Object.values(facts).flatMap((f) => {
    const source = repo.current(f.path);
    return source === null ? [] : [{ path: f.path, source, symbols: f.symbols }];
  });
  const graph = buildGraph(repo.map, facts);
  return { journeys: computeJourneys(graph, facts, findFetchSites(sources)), graph };
}

type Cache = { id: string; hash: string; steps: string[]; name: string };
type Confirmed = Record<string, { name: string; at: number }>;

export type JourneysOptions = { bus: Bus; repo: Repo; namer?: Namer | null };
export type Result = { ok: true; journey: Journey } | { ok: false; status: 404 | 409; error: string };

export function attachJourneys(opts: JourneysOptions) {
  const { bus, repo } = opts;
  const namer = opts.namer === undefined ? (process.env.HARNESS_JOURNEYS === '0' ? null : sdkNamer) : opts.namer;
  const dir = join(repo.root, '.harness', 'journeys');
  const confirmedPath = join(dir, 'confirmed.json');
  const work = new Set<Promise<unknown>>();
  const track = <T>(p: Promise<T>) => { work.add(p); const off = () => { work.delete(p); }; p.then(off, off); return p; };
  let naming = false;
  let again = false;
  let current: { journeys: Journey[]; graph: ContextGraph } | null = null;

  const readJson = <T>(p: string, fallback: T): T => { try { return existsSync(p) ? (JSON.parse(readFileSync(p, 'utf8')) as T) : fallback; } catch { return fallback; } };
  const cached = (hash: string) => readJson<Cache | null>(join(dir, `${hash}.json`), null);
  const confirmed = () => readJson<Confirmed>(confirmedPath, {});

  /** Confirmed names win (inferred: false); then cached model names; else the placeholder (both inferred). */
  function named(js: Journey[]): { journeys: Journey[]; unnamed: Journey[] } {
    const conf = confirmed();
    const unnamed: Journey[] = [];
    const journeys = js.map((j) => {
      const c = conf[j.id];
      if (c) return { ...j, name: c.name, inferred: false };
      const hit = cached(journeyHash(j));
      if (hit) return { ...j, name: hit.name, inferred: true };
      unnamed.push(j);
      return j;
    });
    return { journeys, unnamed };
  }

  const lastEmitted = () => JSON.stringify(reduce(bus.events).journeys);

  function publish(js: Journey[]) {
    if (JSON.stringify(js) !== lastEmitted()) bus.emit('journeys_updated', { journeys: js }, { turn: null });
  }

  /** Recompute, publish if anything changed, and name new journeys in the background. */
  function refresh(): Journey[] {
    if (!repo.map || !repo.hasMap()) return [];
    current = journeysFor(repo);
    const { journeys, unnamed } = named(current.journeys);
    publish(journeys);
    if (unnamed.length && namer) {
      if (naming) again = true;
      else track(name(unnamed));
    }
    return journeys;
  }

  async function name(list: Journey[]) {
    naming = true;
    const t0 = Date.now();
    const graph = current!.graph;
    try {
      const input = { root: repo.root, journeys: list.map((j) => ({ id: j.id, steps: j.steps.map((s) => describeStep(graph, s)) })) };
      const r = await namer!(input);
      mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });
      const byId = new Map(r.names.map((n) => [n.id, n.name.trim()]));
      for (const j of list) {
        const n = byId.get(j.id);
        if (!n) continue;
        const hash = journeyHash(j);
        writeFileSync(join(dir, `${hash}.json`), JSON.stringify({ id: j.id, hash, steps: j.steps.map((s) => s.node), name: n } satisfies Cache, null, 2));
      }
      bus.emit('maintenance_run', { agent: 'cartographer', trigger: 'journeys', ms: Date.now() - t0, cost: r.cost, ok: true }, { turn: null });
      if (current) publish(named(current.journeys).journeys);
    } catch (e) {
      bus.emit('maintenance_run', { agent: 'cartographer', trigger: 'journeys', ms: Date.now() - t0, cost: (e as { cost?: number }).cost ?? null, ok: false }, { turn: null });
      bus.emit('error', { message: `Journey naming failed: ${(e as Error).message}` }, { turn: null });
    } finally {
      naming = false;
      if (again) { again = false; schedule(); }
    }
  }

  /** Confirm a journey (optionally renaming it): it is no longer inferred. */
  function confirm(id: string, name?: string): Result {
    const js = reduce(bus.events).journeys;
    const j = js.find((x) => x.id === id);
    if (!j) return { ok: false, status: 404, error: `No journey ${id}.` };
    const text = (name ?? j.name).trim();
    if (!text) return { ok: false, status: 409, error: 'A journey name cannot be empty.' };
    mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });
    writeFileSync(confirmedPath, JSON.stringify({ ...confirmed(), [id]: { name: text, at: Date.now() } }, null, 2));
    const next = js.map((x) => (x.id === id ? { ...x, name: text, inferred: false } : x));
    publish(next);
    return { ok: true, journey: next.find((x) => x.id === id)! };
  }

  function schedule() {
    track(new Promise<void>((resolve) => setImmediate(() => {
      try { refresh(); }
      catch (e) { bus.emit('error', { message: `Journeys failed: ${(e as Error).message}` }, { turn: null }); }
      finally { resolve(); }
    })));
  }

  // After a scan (load, map accepted) and after every turn: recompute; emit only when the journeys changed.
  const off = bus.on((e) => { if (e.kind === 'repo_scanned' || e.kind === 'turn_ended') schedule(); });

  return {
    refresh() { schedule(); },
    confirm,
    /** Resolves once no recompute or naming job is in flight (for tests and shutdown). */
    async idle() { while (work.size) await Promise.allSettled([...work]); },
    detach: off,
  };
}

export type JourneysLoop = ReturnType<typeof attachJourneys>;

/** HTTP endpoints, mounted under /api by the server. */
export function journeyRoutes(j: JourneysLoop) {
  const r = new Hono();
  r.post('/journeys/:id/confirm', async (c) => {
    const body = await c.req.json<{ name?: string }>().catch(() => ({} as { name?: string }));
    const res = j.confirm(decodeURIComponent(c.req.param('id')), body.name);
    return res.ok ? c.json(res) : c.json({ error: res.error }, res.status);
  });
  r.post('/journeys/refresh', (c) => { j.refresh(); return c.json({ ok: true }); });
  return r;
}
```

```typescript
import type { Tool } from './types';

export class Registry {
  private byName = new Map<string, Tool>();

  constructor(list: Tool[]) {
    for (const t of list) this.byName.set(t.name, t);
  }

  get(name: string): Tool | undefined {
    return this.byName.get(name);
  }

  async runAll(input: string): Promise<string[]> {
    const out: string[] = [];
    for (const t of this.byName.values()) out.push(await t.run(input));
    return out;
  }
}
```

```typescript
// Navigation over the containment tree (NAVIGATION_PLAN §3.3): dive, go up, jump, spatial neighbours. Pure: every
// function maps (graph, open, focus) to the next place; the store applies it and keeps history.
import { fileOf, type ContextGraph } from '@harness/core/view';
import type { Frame } from './layout/frame';
import type { Place } from './store';

const OPENABLE = new Set(['domain', 'cell', 'group', 'unassigned']);

export function ancestors(graph: ContextGraph, id: string): string[] {
  const out: string[] = [];
  for (let n: string | null = id; n && n !== graph.root; n = graph.nodes[n]?.parent ?? null) out.push(n);
  return out.reverse(); // top-down, including id
}

/** Is `id` drawn inside an open container (or is it one)? Domains open all of their cells. */
export function isOpen(graph: ContextGraph, open: readonly string[], id: string): boolean {
  if (open.includes(id)) return true;
  const n = graph.nodes[id];
  return n?.kind === 'cell' && !!n.domain && open.includes(`domain:${n.domain}`);
}

/** Remove a container (and anything opened inside it). Closing one cell of an open domain keeps its other cells open. */
export function close(graph: ContextGraph, open: readonly string[], id: string): string[] {
  const n = graph.nodes[id];
  let next = open.filter((o) => o !== id && !ancestors(graph, o).includes(id));
  if (n?.kind === 'cell' && n.domain && next.includes(`domain:${n.domain}`)) {
    const siblings = (graph.children[`domain:${n.domain}`] ?? []).filter((c) => c !== id && graph.nodes[c]!.kind === 'cell');
    next = [...next.filter((o) => o !== `domain:${n.domain}`), ...siblings];
  }
  return next;
}

/** Dive into a node: open it if it is a container (a domain replaces its cells), else just focus it. */
export function dive(graph: ContextGraph, place: Place, id: string): Place {
  const n = graph.nodes[id];
  if (!n || !OPENABLE.has(n.kind) || !(graph.children[id]?.length)) return { ...place, focus: id };
  if (isOpen(graph, place.open, id)) return { open: close(graph, place.open, id), focus: id };
  let open = [...place.open];
  if (n.kind === 'domain') open = open.filter((o) => graph.nodes[o]?.domain !== n.domain || o === id);
  return { open: [...open, id], focus: id };
}

/** Esc: close the deepest open container holding the focus and focus it; at the top, close the last opened. */
export function up(graph: ContextGraph, place: Place): Place {
  const { open, focus } = place;
  if (focus) {
    const path = ancestors(graph, focus);
    for (let i = path.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
      const a = path[i]!;
      if (a === focus && !isOpen(graph, open, a)) continue;
      if (!isOpen(graph, open, a)) continue;
      return { open: close(graph, open, a), focus: a };
    }
    if (graph.nodes[focus]?.kind !== 'domain') {
      const dom = path.find((p) => graph.nodes[p]?.kind === 'domain' || p === 'unassigned');
      if (dom && dom !== focus) return { open, focus: dom };
    }
    return { open, focus: null };
  }
  if (open.length) return { open: open.slice(0, -1), focus: null };
  return place;
}

/** ⌘K jump: open the containers on the way to a node (symbols and routes land on their file) and focus it. */
export function jump(graph: ContextGraph, place: Place, id: string): Place {
  let target = id;
  const n = graph.nodes[id];
  if (n && (n.kind === 'symbol' || n.kind === 'route' || n.kind === 'entry')) target = fileOf(id) ?? n.parent ?? id;
  const t = graph.nodes[target];
  if (!t) return place;
  if (t.kind === 'domain') return isOpen(graph, place.open, target) ? { ...place, focus: target } : dive(graph, place, target);
  const path = ancestors(graph, target);
  // the innermost container to open: the node itself when it is a cell or group, else its parent container
  const own = OPENABLE.has(t.kind) && t.kind !== 'domain' ? target : null;
  const inner = own ?? [...path].reverse().find((p) => p !== target && OPENABLE.has(graph.nodes[p]?.kind ?? '') && graph.nodes[p]!.kind !== 'domain');
  const open = [...place.open];
  if (inner && !path.some((p) => isOpen(graph, open, p) && p === inner)) open.push(inner);
  return { open, focus: target };
}

export type Dir = 'left' | 'right' | 'up' | 'down';
const FOCUSABLE = new Set(['cell', 'spine', 'container', 'file', 'group', 'chip']);

/** The nearest drawn node in a direction (cost: distance along it plus twice the sideways offset). */
export function neighbour(frame: Frame, from: string | null, dir: Dir): string | null {
  const nodes = frame.nodes.filter((n) => FOCUSABLE.has(n.type));
  const cur = from ? frame.boxes[from] : undefined;
  if (!cur) return nodes[0]?.id ?? null;
  const cx = cur.x + cur.w / 2;
  const cy = cur.y + cur.h / 2;
  const [dx, dy] = dir === 'left' ? [-1, 0] : dir === 'right' ? [1, 0] : dir === 'up' ? [0, -1] : [0, 1];
  let best: string | null = null;
  let cost = Infinity;
  for (const n of nodes) {
    if (n.id === from) continue;
    // never jump into or out of the current box's own container chain sideways: compare edges, not centres
    const nx = n.x + n.w / 2;
    const ny = n.y + n.h / 2;
    const ahead = dx ? (dx > 0 ? n.x - (cur.x + cur.w) : cur.x - (n.x + n.w)) : dy > 0 ? n.y - (cur.y + cur.h) : cur.y - (n.y + n.h);
    if (ahead < -1) continue;
    const side = dx ? Math.abs(ny - cy) : Math.abs(nx - cx);
    const c = Math.max(0, ahead) + 2 * side;
    if (c < cost) { cost = c; best = n.id; }
  }
  return best;
}
```

```text
import { existsSync, mkdirSync, readdirSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { basename, join } from 'node:path';
import { parse as parseYaml, stringify as stringifyYaml } from 'yaml';
import { linkDecision, addException, nextDecisionId, type Violation } from '@harness/core';
import { commitPaths, git } from './git';
import type { Repo } from './repo';
import type { Bus } from './bus';

export type DecisionRecord = {
  id: string;
  title: string;
  outcome: string;
  status: string;
  type: string;
  invariant: string;
  anchors: { paths: string[] };
  rejected: string;
  rationale: string;
};

/** Read `decisions/DR-*.md` (front matter + body). */
export function listDecisions(root: string): DecisionRecord[] {
  const dir = join(root, 'decisions');
  if (!existsSync(dir)) return [];
  const out: DecisionRecord[] = [];
  for (const f of readdirSync(dir).filter((f) => /^DR-\d+\.md$/.test(f))) {
    const text = readFileSync(join(dir, f), 'utf8');
    const m = /^---\n([\s\S]*?)\n---\n?([\s\S]*)$/.exec(text);
    if (!m) continue;
    const fm = parseYaml(m[1]!) as Omit<DecisionRecord, 'rationale'>;
    out.push({ ...fm, rationale: m[2]!.trim() });
  }
  return out.sort((a, b) => Number(a.id.slice(3)) - Number(b.id.slice(3)));
}

/** Parse which option the user picked. Explicit A/B wins; "exception" leans B; otherwise A (comply). */
export function parseOption(text: string): 'A' | 'B' {
  const t = text.trim();
  const m = /^\(?\s*(?:option\s+)?([ab])\b/i.exec(t) ?? /\b(?:option|choose|pick|go with)\s+\(?([ab])\b/i.exec(t);
  if (m) return m[1]!.toUpperCase() as 'A' | 'B';
  return /\bexception\b/i.test(t) ? 'B' : 'A';
}

/** The decision in the user's own words: their answer minus the "A —" prefix, first sentence, if it says something. */
export function titleFromAnswer(answer: string): string | null {
  const t = answer.trim().replace(/^\(?\s*(?:option\s+)?[ab]\b\)?\s*[—–:,.-]*\s*/i, '');
  const first = (t.split(/(?<=[.!?])\s/)[0] ?? '').replace(/[.!?]+$/, '').trim();
  if (first.length < 12) return null;
  const s = first[0]!.toUpperCase() + first.slice(1);
  return s.length > 100 ? s.slice(0, 99).replace(/\s+\S*$/, '') + '…' : s;
}

/**
 * `owner/name`, which Alike's path anchors require: HARNESS_REPO_SLUG, else the origin remote,
 * else `<git user>/<folder>` for a repo with no remote.
 */
function repoAnchor(root: string) {
  if (process.env.HARNESS_REPO_SLUG) return { repository: process.env.HARNESS_REPO_SLUG };
  try {
    const m = /[:/]([^/:]+\/[^/]+?)(?:\.git)?$/.exec(git(root, ['remote', 'get-url', 'origin']));
    if (m) return { repository: m[1]! };
  } catch { /* no remote */ }
  let owner = 'local';
  try { owner = git(root, ['config', 'user.name']).replace(/[^\w.-]+/g, '-') || owner; } catch { /* unset */ }
  return { repository: `${owner}/${basename(root)}` };
}

/**
 * An answered fork becomes a standing decision (SPEC §8): write decisions/DR-n.md, update domains.yaml
 * (A links the decision to the invariant, B adds an exception), commit just those two files, emit
 * `decision_recorded`, and return the instruction that asks Claude to record it in Alike.
 */
export function recordFork(repo: Repo, bus: Bus, violations: Violation[], option: 'A' | 'B', answer: string, prompt: string) {
  const existing = listDecisions(repo.root).map((d) => d.id);
  const byInvariant = new Map<string, Violation[]>();
  for (const v of violations) byInvariant.set(v.invariant, [...(byInvariant.get(v.invariant) ?? []), v]);

  const made: DecisionRecord[] = [];
  let yamlText = repo.mapText;
  for (const [invariantId, vs] of byInvariant) {
    const inv = repo.map.invariants.find((i) => i.id === invariantId);
    if (!inv) continue;
    const id = nextDecisionId(repo.map, [...existing, ...made.map((d) => d.id)]);
    const files = [...new Set(vs.map((v) => v.file))];
    const v0 = vs[0]!;
    const [chosen, rejected] = option === 'A' ? [v0.options[0], v0.options[1]] : [v0.options[1], v0.options[0]];
    const title = titleFromAnswer(answer) ?? (option === 'A'
      ? `${files.join(', ')} follows ${inv.id}: ${inv.rule}`
      : `Exception to ${inv.id} for ${files.join(', ')}`);
    const rec: DecisionRecord = {
      id, title, outcome: chosen, status: 'made', type: 'standing', invariant: inv.id,
      anchors: { paths: files }, rejected,
      rationale: [
        `The user chose ${option}, in their words: "${answer.trim()}"`,
        '',
        `Asked during: "${prompt.trim()}"`,
        '',
        `What triggered it: ${v0.reason}`,
        '',
        `Rejected: ${rejected}`,
      ].join('\n'),
    };
    made.push(rec);
    yamlText = option === 'A' ? linkDecision(yamlText, inv.id, id) : addException(yamlText, inv.id, files[0]!, id);
  }
  if (!made.length) return { decisions: [], alikeInstruction: '' };

  mkdirSync(join(repo.root, 'decisions'), { recursive: true });
  const paths: string[] = ['domains.yaml'];
  for (const d of made) {
    const { rationale, ...fm } = d;
    const rel = `decisions/${d.id}.md`;
    writeFileSync(join(repo.root, rel), `---\n${stringifyYaml(fm).trim()}\n---\n\n${rationale}\n`);
    paths.push(rel);
  }
  writeFileSync(repo.mapPath, yamlText);
  try { commitPaths(repo.root, paths, `docs(decisions): ${made.map((d) => d.id).join(', ')} ${made[0]!.title}`.slice(0, 100)); }
  catch (e) { bus.emit('error', { message: `Could not commit ${paths.join(', ')}: ${(e as Error).message}` }); }

  repo.setMap(yamlText);
  bus.emit('map_confirmed', { map: repo.map, source: 'file' });
  for (const d of made) {
    bus.emit('decision_recorded', { id: d.id, title: d.title, invariant: d.invariant, option, paths: d.anchors.paths, alike: false });
  }

  const anchor = repoAnchor(repo.root);
  // Field names checked against Alike's record_decision schema (VERIFY.md, step 0d).
  const alikeInstruction = made.map((d) => {
    const args = {
      title: `${d.id}: ${d.title}`,
      outcome: d.outcome,
      rationale: d.rationale.replace(/\n+/g, ' '),
      decision_type: 'standing',
      status: 'made',
      anchors: d.anchors.paths.map((path) => ({ kind: 'path', label: 'governs', path, repository: anchor.repository })),
    };
    return `Record ${d.id} in Alike now: call mcp__alike__record_decision with exactly these arguments: ${JSON.stringify(args)}. If the Alike tools are unavailable, skip this silently.`;
  }).join('\n');
  return { decisions: made, alikeInstruction };
}
```

```typescript
import { afterAll, describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { mkdirSync, mkdtempSync, readFileSync, rmSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';

import type { FileFacts, RouteFact } from '../src/contracts/facts';
import { fixtureRepo, loadMap } from './helpers';
import { scoutFacts } from './scout-facts';

const dirs: string[] = [];
afterAll(() => { for (const d of dirs) rmSync(d, { recursive: true, force: true }); });

const route = (method: string, path: string): RouteFact => ({ id: `route:${method} ${path}`, method, path, file: 'src/server.ts', handler: null });
const sitesOf = (files: Record<string, string>) => findFetchSites(Object.entries(files).map(([path, source]) => ({ path, source, symbols: [] })));

describe('findFetchSites', () => {
  it('finds direct fetches with literal and template URLs, axios/ky calls, and the method from the init or the client', () => {
    const sites = sitesOf({
      'web/a.ts': [
        'fetch("/api/runs");',
        'fetch(`/api/runs/${id}?full=1`, { method: "DELETE" });',
        "await fetch('https://example.com/api/x#frag', { headers: {}, method: 'put' });",
        'axios.post("/api/notes", body);',
        'ky.get(`/api/usage`);',
        'fetch(url);', // not a literal and not inside a named function: ignored
        'fetch(`${BASE}/api/runs`);', // dynamic origin: not a path
        'const s = "fetch(\\"/api/nope\\")";',
      ].join('\n'),
    });
    expect(sites.map((s) => `${s.method} ${s.url} ${s.exact} ${s.via}`)).toEqual([
      'GET /api/runs true null',
      'DELETE /api/runs/{} false null',
      'PUT /api/x true null',
      'POST /api/notes true axios.post',
      'GET /api/usage true ky.get',
    ]);
  });

  it('finds wrappers (fetch of a parameter, or `/api${path}`) and their literal call sites, in any file', () => {
    const sites = sitesOf({
      'web/api.ts': [
        'export async function request<T>(path: string, init?: RequestInit): Promise<T> {',
        '  const res = await fetch(path, { ...init });',
        '  return res.json();',
        '}',
        'export function apiGet(path: string) { return fetch(`/api${path}`); }',
        'export const api = { runs: () => request<{ runs: string[] }>("/api/runs?limit=25"), start: (b: unknown) => request("/api/runs", { method: "POST", body: JSON.stringify(b) }) };',
      ].join('\n'),
      'web/page.tsx': 'import { apiGet } from "./api";\nexport function Usage() { apiGet(`/usage/${month}`); return null; }\n',
    });
    expect(sites.map((s) => `${s.file} ${s.method} ${s.url} ${s.exact} ${s.via}`)).toEqual([
      'web/api.ts GET /api/runs true request',
      'web/api.ts POST /api/runs true request',
      'web/page.tsx GET /api/usage/{} false apiGet',
    ]);
  });

  it('names the innermost enclosing symbol from spans', () => {
    const source = 'export function A() {\n  return fetch("/api/a");\n}\n';
    const sym = (name: string, start: number, end: number) => ({ id: `w.ts#${name}`, file: 'w.ts', name, kind: 'function' as const, exported: true, parent: null, span: { start, end }, sigHash: '', bodyHash: '' });
    const [site] = findFetchSites([{ path: 'w.ts', source, symbols: [sym('A', 0, source.length), sym('Outer', 0, source.length + 10)] }]);
    expect(site!.from).toBe('w.ts#A');
    expect(urlPath('https://x.io')).toBeNull();
    expect(urlPath('/a//b/?q')).toBe('/a/b');
  });

describe('matchRoute', () => {

  const site = (method: string, url: string, exact = true): Pick<FetchSite, 'method' | 'url' | 'exact'> => ({ method, url, exact });
  it('matches by method and segments, preferring the fewest wildcards', () => {
    expect(matchRoute(site('POST', '/api/runs'), routes)).toEqual({ route: routes[1], confidence: 'syntactic' });
    expect(matchRoute(site('GET', '/api/runs/latest'), routes)).toEqual({ route: routes[3], confidence: 'syntactic' });
    expect(matchRoute(site('GET', '/api/runs/r-1'), routes)).toEqual({ route: routes[2], confidence: 'syntactic' });
    expect(matchRoute(site('GET', '/api/runs/{}', false), routes)).toEqual({ route: routes[2], confidence: 'inferred' });
    expect(matchRoute(site('GET', '/api/accounts/{}/notes', false), routes)?.route.id).toBe('route:GET /api/accounts/{}/notes');
    expect(matchRoute(site('PATCH', '/api/hook'), routes)).toEqual({ route: routes[4], confidence: 'inferred' });
    expect(matchRoute(site('DELETE', '/api/runs'), routes)).toBeNull();

    ]);

    expect(computeJourneys(g, facts)).toEqual(js);
    expect(journeySinks(g)).toContain('table:runs');
    expect(journeySinks(g)).toContain('vendor/llm-openai/index.ts#chat');
  });

  it("the Facts lane's extractor: the route and the CLI trace to the gateway's provider (Scout's real pattern)", () => {
    const map = loadMap();
    map.cartography = { routes: [{ file: 'src/channels/routes.ts', pattern: 'req\\.method === "(?<method>[A-Z]+)" && req\\.url === "(?<path>[^"]+)"' }] };
    const { fileFacts } = scanRepoFacts(fixtureRepo, map);
    const g = buildGraph(map, fileFacts);
    const sources = Object.values(fileFacts).map((f) => ({ path: f.path, source: readFileSync(join(fixtureRepo, f.path), 'utf8'), symbols: f.symbols }));
    const js = computeJourneys(g, fileFacts, findFetchSites(sources));
    expect(js.map((j) => j.id)).toEqual(['journey:cli-scout', 'journey:post-runs']);
    const run = js.find((j) => j.id === 'journey:post-runs')!;
    expect(run.steps[0]).toEqual({ node: 'route:POST /runs', kind: 'route', confidence: 'syntactic' });
    expect(run.steps.map((s) => s.node)).toContain('src/orchestrator/agent.ts#runAgent');
    for (const j of js) {
      const last = j.steps.at(-1)!;
      expect(['vendor', 'table']).toContain(last.kind); // every journey reaches a sink
      for (const b of j.branches) {
        expect(b.from).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0);
        expect(b.from).toBeLessThan(j.steps.length - 1);
        expect(b.steps.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
      }
    }
    const cli = js.find((j) => j.id === 'journey:cli-scout')!;
    expect(cli.steps.slice(0, 3).map((s) => s.kind)).toEqual(['entry', 'symbol', 'symbol']);
    expect(journeyHash(cli)).toBe(journeyHash({ steps: cli.steps.map((s) => ({ ...s })) }));
  });
});

/** A small web app + server: a page calls a wrapper (`/api${path}`), the server registers Express routes. */
const UI_REPO: Record<string, string> = {
  'package.json': '{ "name": "ui-fixture", "private": true, "type": "module", "dependencies": { "express": "4" } }',
  'web/src/api.ts': [
    'export async function request(path: string, init?: RequestInit) {',
    '  const res = await fetch(`/api${path}`, init);',
    '  return res.json();',
    '}',
    'export const startRun = (body: unknown) => request("/runs", { method: "POST", body: JSON.stringify(body) });',
    'export const getRun = (id: string) => request(`/runs/${id}`);',
    'export const health = () => fetch("/api/health");',
    '',
  ].join('\n'),
  'web/src/pages/ResearchPage.tsx': 'import { startRun } from "../api";\nexport function ResearchPage() {\n  void startRun({ company: "Acme" });\n  return <div>Research</div>;\n}\n',
  'src/server/routes.ts': [
    'import express from "express";',
    'import { runAgent, getRun } from "../agent/run";',
    'const app = express();',
    'app.post("/api/runs", async (req, res) => { res.json(await runAgent(req.body)); });',
    'app.get("/api/runs/:id", (req, res) => { res.json(getRun(req.params.id)); });',
    'export default app;',
    '',
  ].join('\n'),
  'src/agent/run.ts': [
    'import { chat } from "../../vendor/llm/index";',
    'import { db } from "../db";',
    'export async function runAgent(body: unknown) {',
    '  db.insert("runs", { body });',
    '  return chat(String(body));',
    '}',
    'export function getRun(id: string) { return id; }',
    '',
  ].join('\n'),
  'src/db.ts': 'export const db = { insert(table: string, row: unknown) { return [table, row]; } };\n',
  'vendor/llm/index.ts': 'export function chat(text: string) { return text; }\n',
};
const UI_MAP = `
version: 1
layers: [{ id: ui, name: UI }, { id: entry, name: Entry }, { id: logic, name: Logic }, { id: data, name: Data }, { id: external, name: External }]
neutral: ["src/db.ts"]
domains:
  - { id: web, name: Web, purpose: The app, cells: { ui: { paths: ["web/**"] } } }
  - { id: api, name: API, purpose: HTTP, cells: { entry: { paths: ["src/server/**"] } } }
  - { id: agent, name: Agent, purpose: Runs, cells: { logic: { paths: ["src/agent/**"] }, data: { tables: [runs] } } }
  - { id: llm, name: Model, purpose: Models, cells: { external: { paths: ["vendor/llm/**"] } } }
`;

describe('computeJourneys: UI page → fetch → route → handler trace', () => {
  const root = mkdtempSync(join(process.env.HARNESS_TEST_TMP ?? tmpdir(), 'harness-journeys-'));
  dirs.push(root);
  for (const [p, text] of Object.entries(UI_REPO)) { mkdirSync(dirname(join(root, p)), { recursive: true }); writeFileSync(join(root, p), text); }
  const map = parseDomainMap(UI_MAP);
  const { fileFacts } = scanRepoFacts(root, map);
  const sources = Object.values(fileFacts).map((f) => ({ path: f.path, source: UI_REPO[f.path]!, symbols: f.symbols }));
  const sites = findFetchSites(sources);
  const g = buildGraph(map, fileFacts);
  const js = computeJourneys(g, fileFacts, sites);

  it('links wrapper call sites to routes (the `/api${path}` prefix is inferred); unmatched fetches drop out', () => {
    expect(sites.map((s) => `${s.from} ${s.method} ${s.url} ${s.via}`)).toEqual([
      'web/src/api.ts#startRun POST /api/runs request',
      'web/src/api.ts#getRun GET /api/runs/{} request',
      'web/src/api.ts#health GET /api/health null',
    ]);
    expect(linkFetches(sites, fileFacts).map((l) => `${l.site.from} → ${l.route.id} (${l.confidence})`)).toEqual([
      'web/src/api.ts#startRun → route:POST /api/runs (inferred)',
      'web/src/api.ts#getRun → route:GET /api/runs/{} (inferred)',
    ]);
  });

  it('draws the start-research journey end to end, with a branch to the table', () => {
    expect(js.map((j) => j.id)).toEqual(['journey:get-api-runs-id', 'journey:post-api-runs']);
    const run = js.find((j) => j.id === 'journey:post-api-runs')!;
    expect(run.entry).toBe('entry:route:POST /api/runs');
    expect(run.name).toBe('POST /api/runs');
    const handler = fileFacts['src/server/routes.ts']!.routes.find((r) => r.id === 'route:POST /api/runs')!.handler!;
    expect(run.steps).toEqual([
      { node: 'web/src/pages/ResearchPage.tsx#ResearchPage', kind: 'page', confidence: 'syntactic' },
      { node: 'web/src/api.ts#startRun', kind: 'fetch', confidence: 'syntactic' },
      { node: 'route:POST /api/runs', kind: 'route', confidence: 'inferred' },
      { node: handler, kind: 'symbol', confidence: 'syntactic' },
      { node: 'src/agent/run.ts#runAgent', kind: 'symbol', confidence: 'syntactic' },
      { node: 'vendor/llm/index.ts#chat', kind: 'vendor', confidence: 'syntactic' },

    expect(run.branches).toEqual([{ from: 4, steps: ['table:runs'] }]);
    const get = js.find((j) => j.id === 'journey:get-api-runs-id')!;
    expect(get.steps.map((s) => `${s.kind}:${s.node}`).slice(0, 2)).toEqual(['fetch:web/src/api.ts#getRun', 'route:route:GET /api/runs/{}']);
    expect(get.steps[1]!.confidence).toBe('inferred');
  });

  it('is deterministic and slugs are stable', () => {
    expect(computeJourneys(buildGraph(map, fileFacts), fileFacts, findFetchSites([...sources].reverse()))).toEqual(js);
    expect(journeySlug({ kind: 'route', label: 'GET /api/accounts/{}/notes' })).toBe('get-api-accounts-id-notes');
    expect(journeySlug({ kind: 'bin', label: '@scope/x' })).toBe('bin-scope-x');
  });
});
```
