```typescript
// Tier 2 (NAVIGATION_PLAN §3.1): the SemanticResolver interface on a small TS fixture, for both implementations
// (TS 7 tsgo and TS 6 ts-morph), plus the engine's update and stale-hash logic.
import { afterAll, describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { join } from 'node:path';
import type { SemanticFacts } from '../src/contracts/facts';
import { SemanticEngine } from '../src/facts/semantic/engine';
import { packageOf } from '../src/facts/semantic/names';
import { semanticFacts } from '../src/facts/semantic/resolve';
import { scanSites } from '../src/facts/semantic/sites';
import type { ResolverImpl } from '../src/facts/semantic/types';
import { cleanTemps, factsFor, factsOf, semanticRepo, tempCopy, tryOpen } from './semantic-helpers';

afterAll(cleanTemps);

const show = (f: SemanticFacts) => [
  ...f.calls.map((c) => `${c.from} -> ${c.to} ${c.confidence}${c.count > 1 ? ` x${c.count}` : ''}`),
  ...f.implements.map((i) => `${i.from} => ${i.to}`),
];

/** What both resolvers must agree on (the fixture has emoji before call sites: offsets are UTF-16). */
const EXPECTED: Record<string, string[]> = {
  'src/main.ts': [
    'src/main.ts#main -> src/providers.ts#provider typed',
    'src/main.ts#main -> src/registry.ts#Registry typed',
    'src/main.ts#main -> src/registry.ts#Registry.get typed',
    'src/main.ts#main -> src/registry.ts#Registry.runAll typed',
    // `loose.whatever()` can't be resolved, so Tier 1's guesses in `main` stay (syntactic)
    'src/main.ts#main -> src/tools/echo.ts#echo.run syntactic',
    'src/main.ts#main -> src/types.ts#Provider.chat dispatch',
    'src/main.ts#main -> src/types.ts#Tool.run dispatch x2',
  ],
  'src/providers.ts': [
    'src/providers.ts#Base.hello -> src/providers.ts#Base.chat dispatch', // abstract member
    'src/providers.ts#Loud.chat -> src/util.ts#shout typed',
    'src/providers.ts#provider -> src/providers.ts#Loud typed',
    'src/providers.ts#Loud.chat => src/providers.ts#Base.chat', // extends an abstract class
    'src/providers.ts#Loud.chat => src/types.ts#Provider.chat', // implements clause, type-literal member
  ],
  'src/registry.ts': ['src/registry.ts#Registry.runAll -> src/types.ts#Tool.run dispatch'],
  'src/tools/echo.ts': ['src/tools/echo.ts#echo.run -> src/util.ts#shout typed', 'src/tools/echo.ts#echo.run => src/types.ts#Tool.run'],
  'src/tools/upper.ts': ['src/tools/upper.ts#upper.run => src/types.ts#Tool.run'], // `satisfies Tool`
  'src/tools/index.ts': [],
  'src/types.ts': [],
  'src/util.ts': [],
};

describe.each<ResolverImpl>(['tsgo', 'ts-morph'])('SemanticResolver (%s)', (impl) => {
  const facts = factsOf(semanticRepo);

  it('resolves typed calls, dispatch through interface members, and implements edges in Tier 1 ids', async (ctx) => {
    const resolver = await tryOpen(impl, semanticRepo, Object.keys(facts));
    if (!resolver) return ctx.skip(); // TS 7 has no native binary for this platform
    expect(resolver.impl).toBe(impl);
    const out: SemanticFacts[] = [];
    const engine = new SemanticEngine(semanticRepo, resolver, (f) => out.push(f));
    engine.setFacts(Object.values(facts));
    await engine.resolveAll();
    engine.close();
    const got = Object.fromEntries(out.map((f) => [f.path, show(f)]));
    expect(got).toEqual(EXPECTED);
    for (const f of out) expect(f.hash).toBe(facts[f.path]!.hash);
    expect(engine.totals).toMatchObject({ unresolved: 1, implements: 5 });
  });

  it('re-resolves an edited file and its importers after update(), and reports only what changed', async (ctx) => {
    const root = tempCopy();
    const all = factsOf(root);
    const resolver = await tryOpen(impl, root, Object.keys(all));
    if (!resolver) return ctx.skip();
    const out: SemanticFacts[] = [];
    const engine = new SemanticEngine(root, resolver, (f) => out.push(f));
    engine.setFacts(Object.values(all));
    await engine.resolveAll();
    out.length = 0;

    // util.ts gains `whisper`; echo.ts switches to it.
    const util = `${readFileSync(join(root, 'src/util.ts'), 'utf8')}\nexport function whisper(s: string): string {\n  return s.toLowerCase();\n}\n`;
    writeFileSync(join(root, 'src/util.ts'), util);
    all['src/util.ts'] = factsFor(root, 'src/util.ts', util, all);
    const echo = readFileSync(join(root, 'src/tools/echo.ts'), 'utf8').replace(/shout/g, 'whisper');
    writeFileSync(join(root, 'src/tools/echo.ts'), echo);
    all['src/tools/echo.ts'] = factsFor(root, 'src/tools/echo.ts', echo, all);

    const t = performance.now();
    const paths = engine.update([all['src/util.ts']!, all['src/tools/echo.ts']!]);
    const ms = performance.now() - t;
    engine.close();
    // The edited files first, then importers (re-resolved, emitted only if their result moved).
    expect(paths.slice(0, 2)).toEqual(['src/util.ts', 'src/tools/echo.ts']);
    expect(paths).toEqual(expect.arrayContaining(['src/providers.ts', 'src/tools/index.ts']));
    const echoOut = out.find((f) => f.path === 'src/tools/echo.ts')!;
    expect(echoOut.hash).toBe(all['src/tools/echo.ts']!.hash);
    expect(show(echoOut)).toContain('src/tools/echo.ts#echo.run -> src/util.ts#whisper typed');
    expect(out.map((f) => f.path).sort()).toEqual(['src/tools/echo.ts', 'src/util.ts']); // providers.ts unchanged: not re-emitted
    expect(ms).toBeLessThan(impl === 'tsgo' ? 500 : 2000);
  });
});

describe('Tier 2 helpers', () => {
  it('drops a result when the text on disk is not the text the Tier 1 facts describe (stale hash)', async () => {
    const facts = factsOf(semanticRepo);
    const f = facts['src/main.ts']!;
    const never = { impl: 'ts-morph' as const, declarationsAt: () => { throw new Error('not called'); }, update() {}, close() {} };
    expect(semanticFacts(never, f, `${readFileSync(join(semanticRepo, 'src/main.ts'), 'utf8')}\n// edited`, () => null)).toBeNull();
  });

  it('finds call sites at the callee name and attributes them to the innermost Tier 1 symbol', () => {
    const facts = factsOf(semanticRepo);
    const src = readFileSync(join(semanticRepo, 'src/main.ts'), 'utf8');
    const { calls } = scanSites('src/main.ts', src, facts['src/main.ts']!.symbols);
    expect(calls.map((c) => `${src.slice(c.at, c.at + 8)}@${c.from}`)).toEqual([
      'Registry@src/main.ts#main', 'runAll(\'@src/main.ts#main', 'run(\'y\')@src/main.ts#main', 'get(name@src/main.ts#main',
      'run(\'z\')@src/main.ts#main', 'chat(\'he@src/main.ts#main', 'provider@src/main.ts#main', 'whatever@src/main.ts#main',
    ]);
  });

  it('names packages from declaration paths (@types/x → x)', () => {
    expect(packageOf('/r/node_modules/@anthropic-ai/sdk/client.d.mts')).toBe('@anthropic-ai/sdk');
    expect(packageOf('/r/node_modules/a/node_modules/yaml/dist/index.d.ts')).toBe('yaml');
    expect(packageOf('/r/node_modules/@types/node/fs.d.ts')).toBe('node');
    expect(packageOf('/r/node_modules/@types/babel__core/index.d.ts')).toBe('@babel/core');
    expect(packageOf('/r/src/a.ts')).toBeNull();
  });
});
```

```text
The page covers only part of what you asked for. Here is what it says on each topic, with the rest marked as absent.

**Recording decisions**
- You can ask your agent to record a decision: "Ask your agent when you decide something."
- A decision should include a title, an outcome, a rationale, and code anchors.
- Agents can also record decisions unprompted when they notice you choosing between options. "It records only your own work."
- Decisions can be one-time (for one situation) or standing (a rule for all future work).

**Anchors**
- The page names these anchors: "the repository, branch, pull request, issue, or file paths that the decision applies to."
- It does not mention folder, glob, situation, tool, entity, repository identity, or machine_path anchors.

**How decisions reach other agents**
- Session start: when a session starts on the same work item, the brief lists that work's decisions.
- File touched: "When an agent is about to use a file in the decision's paths, Alike adds a short note." This works in Claude Code, Codex CLI, and Factory droid.
- On-demand search: any agent can search decisions.
- The page does not describe prompt or tool-call triggers.

**Status, updating, superseding, rejecting, retiring**
- Statuses are proposed, made (default), implemented, revisited, superseded, and rejected.
- Superseded: "Alike stops giving it to agents."
- Rejected: "Alike still shows it, marked as rejected, so that agents do not suggest it again."
- To replace a decision: "To replace a decision, ask your agent to record the new decision and mark the old one as superseded."
- For rejected alternatives, you can note them in the rationale or record them as separate decisions with the rejected status.
- The page does not describe retiring decisions.
- Decisions Alike finds start unconfirmed: "These start as not confirmed." You can dismiss a wrong one with the reason "incorrect."

**Stable URLs or links per decision**
- Not covered on this page.

**Sharing with teammates**
- Under the default High Sharing preset, "everyone in your workspace sees your decisions."
- The page links to "Who sees what" for more detail.

**Limits and budgets**
- Not covered on this page.

**Repository detection (git remote, no remote)**
- Not covered on this page.
```

```text
**Hooks and what each injects**

- **SessionStart:** "A brief about the current work: the task, recent decisions, related work, live sessions on the same work." The brief also covers questions waiting for your answer.
- **UserPromptSubmit:** "What changed since the last turn, and items that match your prompt."
- **PreToolUse:** "A short note if a decision or task is attached to that file." The page says this runs for Claude Code, Codex CLI, and Factory droid only. It also says "This check runs on your machine and sends nothing."
- **PostToolUse:** "Items that match your prompt or the work." The page limits this to Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, Factory droid, Devin CLI, and VS Code.
- **Stop:** "If a teammate or another of your sessions asked you something, the agent can continue for one more turn to tell you."

**Decisions anchored to paths, folders, situations, or tools**

The page covers only file-level anchoring, in the PreToolUse row. It does not describe folder, situation, or tool anchoring.

**Repository identification**

The page does not describe how repositories are identified. It says only that the agent links a session to a work item, "for example the git branch, the GitHub pull request, or the Linear issue."

**Budgets and limits**

- "Alike tries not to show the same item twice in one session."
- "If Alike does not answer within a few seconds, the hook stops and the agent continues without Alike's context."
- "After a few network failures in a row, the session-start and prompt hooks stop calling Alike for some minutes."
- "A work focus that has no activity for 5 minutes becomes idle."
- The first-use greeting happens "once in each workspace."

**The Alike CLI**

The only command the page names is "Alike auth expired — run `npx @alikeai/setup --doctor`", which the agent shows when your machine's credential stops working.

**HTTP API or token-based access**

The page does not describe an HTTP API or token access. It mentions Alike's MCP tools and links to a separate reference page, but does not document them here.
```

```text
export async function runTelemetry(mode, ctx) {
  const spec = TELEMETRY_MODES[mode];
  if (!spec) return { status: 'skipped' };
  let payload;
  try {
    payload = JSON.parse(ctx.raw);
  } catch {
    payload = {};
  }
  maybeDumpPayload(ctx.home, ctx.harnessId, mode, ctx.raw);
  const rec = readHookPayload(ctx.dialect, payload);
  const sessionKey = wireSessionKey(ctx.harnessId, rec.sessionKey);
  // A harness that exposes no session id (Junie) cannot be correlated to anything — drop rather
  // than invent a key. `--doctor` reports this honestly instead of implying coverage.
  if (!sessionKey) return { status: 'skipped' };

  // The hook fired, which is the fact `--doctor` cannot otherwise learn — record it even when the
  // event itself is unusable, since a gated-off hook never reaches this line at all.
  const nowIso = ctx.nowIso ?? new Date().toISOString();
  recordHookFire(ctx.home, ctx.harnessId, nowIso);

  const statePath = anchorStatePath(ctx.home);
  let event;
  if (spec.kind === 'session_start') {
    // Anchors need git, so they are read HERE (once per session) and never on the tool-call path.
    const anchors = readAnchors(payload?.cwd ?? null);
    // Cached under the WIRE key so the tool-call branch below can read them back without git, and
    // so the inject rail resolves the same anchors for the same session (see resolveAnchors).
    if (Object.keys(anchors).length > 0) writeLastAnchors(statePath, sessionKey, anchors);
    // The working set (changed files vs merge-base) rides session_start only — one more
    // bounded git call on a rail that already shells git (v0.65 §0.4).
    event = buildSessionStart(nowIso, {
      anchors,
      workingSetPaths: readWorkingSetPaths(payload?.cwd ?? null),
    });
  } else if (spec.kind === 'session_end') {
    event = buildSessionEnd(nowIso);
  } else if (spec.kind === 'turn_start') {
    // No prompt is a real state, not a failure: several harnesses fire a prompt-submit hook whose
    // payload carries no prompt field at all. Drop rather than send an empty turn.
    if (!rec.prompt) return { status: 'skipped' };
    event = buildTurnStart(nowIso, rec.prompt);
  } else if (spec.kind === 'turn_end') {
    if (!rec.response) return { status: 'skipped' };
    event = buildTurnEnd(nowIso, rec.response);
  } else {
    if (!rec.tool) return { status: 'skipped' };
    // The dialect's own success signal wins when it has one; otherwise the mode decides.
    const ok = typeof rec.ok === 'boolean' ? rec.ok : spec.ok;
    // ANCHORS ON THE TOOL CALL (ALI-2822 §4.9). The server opens a work session from the first
    // tool call of a session — but `buildToolCall` never emitted anchors, and the door read them
    // off that event alone, so `captureWorkSession` answered `no_anchor` on every request ever
    // made and §4.9 captured nothing. The schema's own comment anticipated this ("the branch
    // reaches it only on session_start and anchor_change, and the harnesses that emit neither
    // would have starved"); the client half was simply never written.
    //
    // Read from the cache, NOT from git: this fires inside the agent's loop and the whole contract
    // of this path is a parse plus a file append. A cold cache means no anchors on the event —
    // the same honest miss as before, not a new cost.
    event = buildToolCall(
      nowIso,
      rec.tool,
      ok,
      rec.ms,
      readLastAnchors(statePath, sessionKey),
      rec.input,
      rec.output,
      rec.toolUseId,
    );
  }
  // SYNCHRONOUS POST, no spool (DR-3). The harness label (baked as `--harness-label`) rides the
  // body so the server sees `client: "Claude Code"` rather than resolving the agent as "node".
  //
  // The read half (v0.4 B2): only where this mode's event can carry an envelope. The trigger
  // declaration names the boundary explicitly (outcome 1 — the server must not infer it from
  // event presence), and `seen_urns` gives the server's grounding pass the same dedup ledger
  // the prompt rail sends.
  const injectable = TELEMETRY_INJECTABLE[ctx.dialect]?.[mode] ?? null;
  // ONE expression for the wall, used twice — the same shape `runInject` uses for its own rails,
  // and for the same reason: DECLARED to the server in `budget_ms` below and ENFORCED on our own
  // fetch further down. The comment below already claimed this was one expression while the
  // constant was in fact spelled twice, which is precisely the drift `injectWallMs` exists to
  // prevent on the inject rail.
  //
  // `ctx.timeoutMs` is honoured here for consistency with every other rail — `runInject`,
  // `runStop` and the path-index read all take the caller's override, and this rail was the only
  // one ignoring it. It is also what lets the abort be driven in milliseconds instead of waiting
  // out the real 1.5s wall; the assertions still pin the production constant as the DEFAULT.
  const contentWallMs = ctx.timeoutMs ?? INJECT_CONTENT_TIMEOUT_MS;
  const ledgerPath = ctx.ledgerPath ?? groundingLedgerPath(ctx.home);
  // ALI-4686: the path index rides THIS hook at session start WHEN the harness runs it in the
  // background (`--async`; main() resolves `ctx.wantPathIndex` from that flag and the pretool
  // rail's kill-switch, `saveFlagEnabled`): the ~750KB of server-rendered text and the server's
  // time to build it then cost the person nothing, where on the synchronous SessionStart inject
  // they were 44% of a start the person waited on. A harness whose telemetry hook is synchronous
  // keeps the index on its inject, as before — moving it here would only move the wait, under a
  // wall equal to the kill.
  const wantPathIndex = spec.kind === 'session_start' && ctx.wantPathIndex === true;
  const extras = injectable
    ? {
      want: ['context'],
      [WIRE_TRIGGER_FIELD]: TRIGGER_TOOL_CALL,
      seen_urns: readSeenUrns(sessionKey, ledgerPath),
      // DECLARE the wall we are about to enforce, net of the transport the server cannot see
      // (declaredBudgetMs, the same rule as the inject and stop rails), so the server spends at
      // most what we will wait for. Derived from the same binding handed to sendEvents below, so
      // the declaration cannot drift from the enforcement.
      budget_ms: declaredBudgetMs(contentWallMs, readTransportMs(ctx.healthPath ?? injectHealthStatePath(ctx.home))),
    }
    : wantPathIndex
      ? { want: ['path_index'], budget_ms: INJECT_PATH_INDEX_TIMEOUT_MS }
      : {};
  // An injectable tool_call is a READ, not just an observation: the server runs content grounding
  // under CONTENT_GROUND_BUDGET_MS before answering. It therefore needs the content wall rather
  // than postTelemetry's telemetry default — a write rail's constant, free to move for reasons
  // that have nothing to do with grounding — or a completed serve is abandoned here after the
  // droplet has already paid for it and burned the URNs out of this session's ledger. The
  // path-index ask is a read too, and declares the wall it waits on for the same reason.
  const { outcome, body } = await sendEvents(
    ctx,
    sessionKey,
    [event],
    extras,
    injectable ? contentWallMs : wantPathIndex ? INJECT_PATH_INDEX_TIMEOUT_MS : undefined,
  );
  if (wantPathIndex) cachePathIndexFrom(ctx, sessionKey, body);
  const context = injectable && body && typeof body.context === 'string' ? body.context : '';
  const notice = injectable ? noticeFrom(body, ctx.harnessId) : null;
  if (!context && !notice) return { status: outcome };
  // Record BEFORE the caller prints (same order as the inject rail): a crash mid-turn must not
  // re-surface the same items on the next event. Only the server-named grounding URNs (C-6).
  const groundedUrns = Array.isArray(body?.grounded_urns)
    ? body.grounded_urns.filter((u) => typeof u === 'string')
    : [];
  if (groundedUrns.length > 0) recordSeenUrns(sessionKey, groundedUrns, ledgerPath);
  // The server's line for this hook (ALI-4606). A hook the harness runs `async: true` (`--async`,
  // baked by the installer) is never drawn to the person — Claude Code hands its output to the
  // model only — so its line is PARKED for the next synchronous hook and left out of this forward
  // (ALI-4686). A synchronous telemetry hook prints its own line and records it as printed, so the
  // Stop digest can recap the turn either way.
  if (notice) {
    const outbox = ctx.noticesDir ?? noticesDir(ctx.home);
    if (ctx.asyncHook) recordNotice(outbox, sessionKey, notice);
    else recordPrintedNotices(outbox, sessionKey, ctx.harnessId, [notice]);
  }
  const forwardNotice = ctx.asyncHook ? null : notice;
  if (!context && !forwardNotice) return { status: outcome };
  return { status: outcome, forward: { ccEvent: injectable.ccEvent, dialect: injectable.dialect, context, ...(forwardNotice ? { notice: forwardNotice } : {}) } };
}

/**
 * POST events to the merged door. Never throws — a hook that fails because Alike is unreachable is
 * a hook that broke someone's turn.
 *
 * There is no retry and no local queue: the retry IS the harness firing again, and the wire's
 * per-event `event_id` is what makes a re-send idempotent. That is the DR-3 trade — one lost event
 * on a flaky network, against a second durable copy of every session on the user's disk. The loss
 * is asymmetric, and worth being precise about: a repeating event (`tool_call`, `turn_*`) is
 * re-covered by the harness's next fire, but `session_end` fires ONCE — lose that POST and the
 * event itself is gone for good; the server's stall sweep recovers the CLOSE (brief, extraction),
 * not the event.
 *
 * Returns the parsed response `body` alongside the outcome (v0.4 outcome 7): the server's answer
 * to a `want` is what runTelemetry turns into a forward. A failed POST carries no body.
 *
 * `timeoutMs` is for the callers whose POST is also a READ: postTelemetry's default is sized for a
 * write-and-forget telemetry event, and a caller asking for `context` is waiting on a server-side
 * grounding read with a budget of its own. Omit it and the telemetry default applies.
 */
```

```typescript
// Tier 2 from the server's side: the per-file debounce, the child process (startSemantic) with its hash checks, and
// the edit gate staying within budget while the child is busy resolving.
import { afterAll, afterEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';
import { readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { join } from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import type { SemanticFacts } from '../src/contracts/facts';
import { deltaForEdit, fileExistsIn, scanRepoFacts } from '../src/facts';
import { startSemantic, type SemanticClient } from '../src/facts/semantic/client';
import { KeyedDebounce } from '../src/facts/semantic/debounce';
import { parseDomainMap } from '../src/schema';
import { cleanTemps, factsFor, factsOf, tempCopy } from './semantic-helpers';
import { fixtureRepo } from './helpers';

afterAll(cleanTemps);

describe('KeyedDebounce', () => {
  afterEach(() => { vi.useRealTimers(); });

  it('waits 150 ms after the last change per key, keeps the latest value, and flushes keys due together as one batch', () => {
    vi.useFakeTimers();
    const batches: [string, number][][] = [];
    const d = new KeyedDebounce<number>(150, (b) => batches.push([...b]));
    d.push('a', 1);
    vi.advanceTimersByTime(100);
    d.push('a', 2); // restarts a's wait
    d.push('b', 1);
    vi.advanceTimersByTime(140);
    expect(batches).toEqual([]);
    expect(d.pending).toBe(2);
    vi.advanceTimersByTime(20); // a and b both came due
    expect(batches).toEqual([[['a', 2], ['b', 1]]]);
    d.push('c', 1);
    vi.advanceTimersByTime(151);
    expect(batches).toHaveLength(2);
    expect(batches[1]).toEqual([['c', 1]]);
    expect(d.pending).toBe(0);
  });

  it('clear() drops everything queued', () => {
    vi.useFakeTimers();
    const batches: unknown[] = [];
    const d = new KeyedDebounce<number>(150, (b) => batches.push(b));
    d.push('a', 1);
    d.clear();
    vi.advanceTimersByTime(500);
    expect(batches).toEqual([]);
  });
});

describe('startSemantic (child process)', () => {
  const clients: SemanticClient[] = [];
  afterAll(async () => { await Promise.all(clients.map((c) => c.close())); });

  it('loads in the background, then debounces edits and only hands back results for the current hash', async () => {
    const root = tempCopy();
    const all = factsOf(root);
    const got: SemanticFacts[] = [];
    const client = startSemantic({ root, onResolved: (f) => got.push(f) });
    clients.push(client);
    client.load(Object.values(all));
    expect(client.status().state).toBe('opening'); // returns at once
    await client.idle();
    const st = client.status();
    expect(st).toMatchObject({ state: 'ready', total: 8, done: 8 });
    expect(st.impl === 'tsgo' || st.impl === 'ts-morph').toBe(true);
    expect(st.stats).toMatchObject({ unresolved: 1, implements: 4 });
    expect(got.map((f) => f.path).sort()).toEqual(Object.keys(all).sort());
    got.length = 0;

    // Two quick edits of echo.ts: one update after the debounce, for the second text only.
    const path = 'src/tools/echo.ts';
    const base = readFileSync(join(root, path), 'utf8');
    const v1 = base.replace('return shout(input);', 'return shout(input) + shout(input);');
    writeFileSync(join(root, path), v1);
    client.changed(path, factsFor(root, path, v1, all));
    const v2 = base.replace('return shout(input);', 'return input;');
    writeFileSync(join(root, path), v2);
    const f2 = factsFor(root, path, v2, all);
    client.changed(path, f2);
    await client.idle();
    const mine = got.filter((f) => f.path === path);
    expect(mine).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(mine[0]!.hash).toBe(f2.hash);
    expect(mine[0]!.calls).toEqual([]); // echo.run no longer calls shout
    expect(mine[0]!.implements).toEqual([{ from: 'src/tools/echo.ts#echo.run', to: 'src/types.ts#Tool.run' }]);
    expect(client.status().lastUpdateMs).not.toBeNull();

    // A result computed for an older hash is dropped: tell the client a newer text exists before the child answers.
    got.length = 0;
    const v3 = `${v2}\n// v3\n`;
    client.load(Object.values({ ...all, [path]: f2 })); // the child will resolve echo.ts against f2…
    writeFileSync(join(root, path), v3);
    client.changed(path, factsFor(root, path, v3, all)); // …but v3 is current now
    await client.idle();
    const hashes = got.filter((f) => f.path === path).map((f) => f.hash);
    expect(hashes).not.toContain(f2.hash);
  });

  it('keeps the edit gate under budget while the child is busy resolving', async () => {
    // Keep the child busy on a real project (this package's own sources) while the gate runs in this process.
    const root = fileURLToPath(new URL('..', import.meta.url));
    const map = parseDomainMap('version: 1\nlayers: [{ id: logic, name: Logic }]\nignore: ["node_modules/**", "test/**", "*.json"]\ndomains:\n  - { id: core, name: Core, purpose: x, cells: { logic: { paths: ["src/**"] } } }\n');
    const facts = Object.values(scanRepoFacts(root, map).fileFacts);
    const client = startSemantic({ root, onResolved: () => {} });
    clients.push(client);
    client.load(facts);

    const BUDGET = process.env.HARNESS_PERF_STRICT === '1' ? 20 : 60;
    const exists = fileExistsIn(fixtureRepo);
    const forbidden = 'import { chat } from "../../vendor/llm-openai/index";\n';
    let text = 'import { complete } from "../gateway/complete";\n';
    for (let i = 0; text.length < 1_000_000; i++) text += `export function f${i}(x: number): number {\n  const y = complete({ purpose: "p${i}", messages: [] });\n  return [1, 2].map((q) => q * x).length + Number(y);\n}\n`;
    const runs: number[] = [];
    let busy = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i <= 5; i++) {
      const old = text + '\n'.repeat(i);
      deltaForEdit('src/tools/generated.ts', null, old, exists); // the previous write's extraction leaves the old record cached
      if (client.status().state !== 'ready') busy++;
      const t = performance.now();
      const delta = deltaForEdit('src/tools/generated.ts', old, forbidden + old, exists);
      if (i > 0) runs.push(performance.now() - t);
      expect(delta.imports).toEqual([{ from: 'src/tools/generated.ts', to: 'vendor/llm-openai/index.ts' }]);
    }
    expect(busy).toBeGreaterThan(0); // measured while the child was opening/resolving
    expect(Math.min(...runs)).toBeLessThan(BUDGET);
    await client.idle();
    expect(client.status().state).toBe('ready');
  });
});
```

```bash
  since Tier 2 calls replace a file's syntactic ones in buildGraph.

  the background, per-file 150 ms debounce batched into one snapshot update, importers
  re-resolved, results handed back only for the file's current content hash.

  groups only when `path` is named, as documented in schema.ts.
- Tests: both resolvers on a small TS fixture (UTF-16 offsets, dispatch, implements, update),
```

```text
// The real pipeline wired to the stores: ui = reduce(events, upTo) → graph = graphOf(ui) (memoized) →
// activity = activityFor(ui, graph, turn) → projection = project(graph, view, activity).
import { useMemo } from 'react';
import { useView } from '../derive';
import { graphMemo, sceneOf, type Scene } from './scene';
import { useV2 } from './store';

export { hotLabels, type Scene } from './scene';

const memoGraph = graphMemo();

/** The scene for the current events, replay index, selected turn and open set. */
export function useScene(): Scene | null {
  const v = useView();
  const open = useV2((s) => s.open);
  const graph = useMemo(() => memoGraph(v.ui), [v.ui]);
  return useMemo(() => (graph ? sceneOf(v.ui, graph, v.turn?.id ?? null, open) : null), [v.ui, v.turn, graph, open]);
}
// The pipeline's pure half (NAVIGATION_PLAN §3): graph = graphOf(ui) memoized on its inputs, the view for what is
// open, activity and projection. No React and no stores, so the layout tests run it in node.
import {
  activityFor, buildGraph, graphFacts, project,
  type ContextGraph, type FileFacts, type LeafActivity, type Projection, type TurnActivity, type UIState, type ViewState,
} from '@harness/core/view';

const sameImports = (a: FileFacts['imports'], b: FileFacts['imports']) =>
  projection: Projection;
  open: string[];
  /** Layout key: what is open (positions depend on nothing else but content). */
  key: string;
};

export function sceneOf(ui: UIState, graph: ContextGraph, turn: string | null, open: readonly string[]): Scene {
  const activity = activityFor(ui, graph, turn);
  const opened = normalizeOpen(graph, open);
  const projection = project(graph, viewFor(graph, opened), activity);
  return { ui, graph, activity, projection, open: opened, key: opened.join(',') };
}
```

```typescript
    expect(out).toContain('← implements  src/tools/echo.ts#echo.run  [Tools · Logic]');
    expect(out).toContain('← implements  src/tools/upper.ts#upper.run  [Tools · Logic]');
  });

  it('filters by kind and follows more hops', () => {
    const out = neighborsText(graph, semanticMap, 'src/tools/echo.ts', ['calls', 'implements'], 2);
    expect(out).toContain('→ calls (typed)  src/util.ts#shout  [Providers · External]  (from src/tools/echo.ts#echo.run)');
    expect(out).not.toContain('imports');
    expect(out).toMatch(/2 hops \(\d+\):[\s\S]*src\/registry\.ts#Registry\.runAll/);
  });
});

describe('symbols_in', () => {
  it('lists a file\'s symbols with lines, calls and implemented members', () => {
    const out = symbolsText(graph, semanticMap, new Map(Object.entries(facts)), 'src/providers.ts', text);
    expect(out).toContain('src/providers.ts  [Providers · Logic] · 6 symbols');
    expect(out).toContain('    method Base.chat :5');
    expect(out).toContain('    method Loud.chat :12 · calls 1 · implements src/providers.ts#Base.chat, src/types.ts#Provider.chat');
  });

  it('lists the files under a directory', () => {
    expect(symbolsText(graph, semanticMap, new Map(Object.entries(facts)), 'src/tools/', text)).toContain('src/tools/echo.ts  2 symbols  [Tools · Logic]');
  });
});
```

```text
// Shared synthetic inputs for the cartography tests: Scout facts plus a new `src/billing/` folder.
import type { FileFacts } from '../src/contracts/facts';
import type { HarnessEvent } from '../src/events';
import { parseDomainMap } from '../src/schema';
import { mapYaml } from './helpers';
import { scoutFacts } from './scout-facts';

export const ff = (path: string, imports: string[] = [], writes: string[] = []): FileFacts => ({
  path, hash: `h:${path}`, imports: imports.map((to) => ({ to, typeOnly: false })),
  writes: writes.map((table) => ({ table, symbol: null, via: 'db' })), symbols: [], calls: [], routes: [], entries: [],
});

export const BILLING = ['src/billing/charge.ts', 'src/billing/invoice.ts', 'src/billing/refund.ts'];

/** Scout facts + three billing files that import each other and shared/db, two of which write `invoices`. */
export function billingFacts(): Record<string, FileFacts> {
  return {
    ...scoutFacts(),
    'src/billing/invoice.ts': ff('src/billing/invoice.ts', ['src/billing/charge.ts', 'src/shared/db.ts'], ['invoices']),
    'src/billing/charge.ts': ff('src/billing/charge.ts', ['src/shared/db.ts']),
    'src/billing/refund.ts': ff('src/billing/refund.ts', ['src/billing/charge.ts', 'src/billing/invoice.ts', 'src/shared/db.ts'], ['invoices']),
  };
}

export const billingBlock = `
  - id: billing
    name: Billing
    purpose: Invoices, charges and refunds
    cells:
      logic: { paths: ["src/billing/**"], tables: ["invoices"] }
db.ts
types.ts
import type { Tool } from "../shared/types";
import { webSearch } from "./web-search";
import { companyProfile } from "./company-profile";
import { newsDigest } from "./news-digest";
import { newsSummarize } from "./news-summarize";
export { webSearch } from "./web-search";
export type { Tool };
export const tools: Tool[] = [webSearch, companyProfile, newsDigest, newsSummarize];
import { db } from "../shared/db";
import { redact } from "./redact";
import { provider } from "./providers";
import { logCost } from "./cost-ledger";
export async function complete(req: { purpose: string; messages: string[] }): Promise<string> {
  const names = db.all("contacts");
  const text = redact(req.messages.join("\n"), names);
  logCost(req.purpose, text.length / 4);
  return provider()(text);
}
```

<tool-use data-tool-type="read" data-tool-name="WebFetch"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **WebFetch**</summary>
 `https://alike.help/help/limitations.md`

```text
The page doesn't cover decisions, anchors, paths, folders, repositories without a remote, the API, or rate limits. It does address the following related topics.

**Injection**
- "Injection settings have no page in the web app". To change them, you can "Ask your agent to change them."
- Windsurf, Zed, and Continue get no automatic context. Their agents can still call Alike's MCP tools.

**Editing and deleting items**
- "You cannot delete one session or one item." Instead, hide items with archive or dismiss. Deleting your account removes everything.

**CLI and devices**
- To remove a paired machine, run `--uninstall` on it. If you can't reach the machine, contact support.
- The installer does not run on Windows. Connect MCP clients by hand there.

**Capture and repositories**
- "You cannot pause capture for one repository or one session." For that work, use an agent without Alike.
- "Your transcript-capture choice does not stop the live hooks." To stop all sending, remove Alike from the agents.

**Sharing and workspaces**
- "You cannot hide one session and share the others." You can stop sharing all agent activity or choose Low Sharing.
- You can't view or cancel invite links, so create them with few uses and a short expiry.
- There is no list of workspace members, and you can't remove a member, change a role, or leave a workspace. Contact support for these.

**Secrets and export**
- Alike does not remove secrets from stored sessions. Keep secrets out of sessions, and rotate any secret that reaches one.
- The export does not include agent sessions.

**Other**
- The installer does not support HTTP proxies. Pair from a network without one.
- Disconnect in Settings → AI Agents signs you out of the browser rather than disconnecting one client. To disconnect a single client, remove the `alike` server from that client's settings.
- The dashboard tour shows once and can't be replayed.
- Sign-in supports email and password only.

For help, contact support@alike.work.
```
</details></tool-use>

<tool-use data-tool-type="read" data-tool-name="WebFetch"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **WebFetch**</summary>
 `https://alike.help/install/non-interactive.md`

```text
**Capture flags**
- The page documents `--capture=all` and `--capture=claude,codex`. It also shows `--capture=` (empty) to capture from no agent.
- Without a terminal and without `--capture=`, transcript capture is off by default. The installer prints a reminder to enable it.
- Capture uses agent IDs from the Supported agents page. Unknown IDs are ignored silently.
- Flags must use `=`. A flag written with a space, such as `--harness claude`, is ignored.

**`ALIKE_BASE_URL` and `ALIKE_TOKEN`**
- "When both variables are set in the environment, the hooks use them instead of `~/.alike/credentials.json`."
- While both are set, the installer does not pair the machine with a different server. It prints a message that begins with `! ALIKE_BASE_URL/ALIKE_TOKEN are exported`.
- To pair normally, clear them with `unset ALIKE_BASE_URL ALIKE_TOKEN`.

**Headless, CI, and server use**
- Without a TTY, the installer sets up detected agents automatically.
- Pairing still requires a person to approve a code. The installer waits up to 10 minutes.
- Some agent tools stop shell commands early. If that happens before approval, run `npx @alikeai/setup --doctor` in a terminal to finish pairing.
- `--dry-run` previews the install without writing files or pairing, but it still asks setup and capture questions.

**Tokens**
- The page does not explain how to create or rotate `ALIKE_TOKEN`. It only says the variable overrides `~/.alike/credentials.json` when both variables are set.
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
/**
 * Should this hook fire stay silent? The ONE gate every rail passes through, because content leaves
 * on three of them (telemetry-*, inject-prompt's prompt, stop's reply) and a gate on one is a gate
 * on none. Silent means no POST of any kind: injecting context needs the prompt sent.
 *
 * Two questions, both answered on this machine: did the user consent to capture for this harness
 * (`capture_harnesses`, the same list the sweep reads), and does a capture rule stop this session
 * (capture-rules.mjs)? A rule that fires is recorded, so the session stays silent afterwards.
 */
export function captureSilenced({ home, harnessId, input, nowIso, cwdFallback = process.cwd() }) {
  if (!readEnabledHarnesses(home).includes(harnessId)) return true;
  // The wire key, which is also the sweep's key for the transcript. It is '' for an id the server
  // would refuse; with a tool:/input: rule set, sessionSkipReason then stops the event outright.
  const sessionKey = wireSessionKey(harnessId, input.sessionId ?? '');
  // The directory the rules are scoped by. Hooks run in the project, so the process cwd is the
  // last resort for a harness whose payload names no directory at all.
  const cwd = input.cwd || input.workspace || cwdFallback;
  const reason = sessionSkipReason({
    home,
    sessionKey,
    transcriptKey: transcriptRecordKey(input.transcriptPath),
    live: true,
    nowIso,
    facts: {
      cwd,
      // Lazy, because only a `repo:` rule needs it — and it must be known BEFORE the first POST:
      // session_start is the event that fills the anchor cache, and it is itself an egress.
      get repository() {
        return sessionRepository(home, sessionKey, cwd);
      },
      toolName: input.tool,
      toolInput: input.toolInput,
    },
  });
  return reason !== null;
}

 * when nothing is left open, and bounded work leaves things open: an aborted fetch does not close a

 * on a bad link every prompt paid the whole backstop instead of INJECT_PROMPT_TIMEOUT_MS. An open
 * stdin pinned `read-payload` the same way. One exit here covers every handle at once.
 *
 * It rides the write callback: stdout under a harness is a pipe, and on macOS a pipe write past the

 * measured), which is why the no-output branch can exit at once: the stderr diagnostics main()
 * leaves behind are a few hundred bytes and are already in the pipe.
```

```typescript
// Position stability and edge declutter for the v2 layout (NAVIGATION_PLAN §3.3, N4), on the Scout fixture's real
// load events (Tier 1 facts from the sandbox scan) through the real pipeline, with ELK's bundled build in node.
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import ELK from 'elkjs/lib/elk.bundled.js';
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { reduce, type FileFacts, type HarnessEvent } from '@harness/core/view';
import { cachedLayout, type ElkApi } from '../layout/containers';
import { buildFrame, layoutAll, UNASSIGNED, type Frame } from '../layout/frame';
import { ancestors, dive, jump, up } from '../nav';
import { graphMemo, sceneOf, type Scene } from '../scene';

const base = JSON.parse(readFileSync(fileURLToPath(new URL('../../../scripts/base-events.json', import.meta.url)), 'utf8')) as HarnessEvent[];
const elk = new ELK() as unknown as ElkApi;
const layout = cachedLayout(async () => elk);

let n = 0;
const ev = (kind: HarnessEvent['kind'], data: Record<string, unknown>, extra: Partial<HarnessEvent> = {}): HarnessEvent =>
  ({ id: `x${n++}`, t: n, session: 's', turn: null, kind, data, ...extra });

/** A new file in a cell, as the server reports it: placed, with Tier 1 facts. */
function addFile(path: string, domain: string, layer: string, imports: string[]): HarnessEvent[] {
  const facts: FileFacts = { path, hash: `h-${path}`, imports: imports.map((to) => ({ to, typeOnly: false })), writes: [], symbols: [], calls: [], routes: [], entries: [] };
  return [ev('file_assigned', { placement: { kind: 'cell', domain, layer } }, { path }), ev('facts_changed', { facts }, { path })];
}

const memo = graphMemo();
function sceneFor(events: HarnessEvent[], open: string[]): Scene {
  const ui = reduce(events);
  return sceneOf(ui, memo(ui)!, null, open);
}

async function frameFor(scene: Scene, region: string[] | null = scene.open.length ? scene.open : null): Promise<Frame> {
  const layouts = await layoutAll(scene.projection, layout);
  const map = scene.ui.map!;
  const meta = { domains: map.domains.map((d) => ({ id: d.id, name: d.name, purpose: d.purpose })), layers: map.layers.map((l) => ({ id: l.id, name: l.name })) };
  return buildFrame({ projection: scene.projection, meta, layouts, region, key: scene.key });
}

/** Nodes of a frame inside a container (its children, transitively), with their box relative to the container. */
function inside(f: Frame, scene: Scene, container: string) {
  const out = new Map<string, { abs: { x: number; y: number }; rel: { x: number; y: number } }>();
  const c = f.boxes[container]!;
  for (const node of f.nodes) {
    if (node.id === container || !ancestors(scene.graph, node.id).includes(container)) continue;
    out.set(node.id, { abs: { x: node.x, y: node.y }, rel: { x: node.x - c.x, y: node.y - c.y } });
  }
  return out;
}

describe('v2 layout: position stability', () => {
  // Three open containers: Channels·Entry (left of and above the change), Research tools·Logic (the change) and
  // Memory·Logic (right of it, same row).
  const open = ['cell:channels/entry', 'cell:tools/logic', 'cell:memory/logic'];

  it('adding a file to one cell moves nodes in other containers by 0 px, and in its own container by a bounded amount', async () => {
    const before = sceneFor(base, open);
    const after = sceneFor([...base, ...addFile('src/tools/sec-filings.ts', 'tools', 'logic', ['src/gateway/complete.ts', 'vendor/sec-edgar/index.ts'])], open);
    const f0 = await frameFor(before);
    const f1 = await frameFor(after);
    expect(f1.boxes['src/tools/sec-filings.ts']).toBeDefined();

    // other containers: identical layout (cache hit), so every node keeps its place inside its container
    for (const c of ['cell:channels/entry', 'cell:memory/logic']) {
      const a = inside(f0, before, c);
      const b = inside(f1, after, c);
      expect(a.size).toBeGreaterThan(0);
      for (const [id, p] of a) expect(b.get(id)!.rel).toEqual(p.rel);
    }
    // and a container whose column is left of the change and whose row is above it does not move at all
    for (const [id, p] of inside(f0, before, 'cell:channels/entry')) expect(inside(f1, after, 'cell:channels/entry').get(id)!.abs).toEqual(p.abs);
    expect(f1.boxes['cell:channels/entry']).toEqual(f0.boxes['cell:channels/entry']);
    // collapsed cells left of the change keep their boxes too
    for (const id of ['cell:channels/logic', 'cell:orchestrator/logic']) expect(f1.boxes[id]).toEqual(f0.boxes[id]);

    // the changed container: existing nodes move by at most two file rows (and most stay put)
    const a = inside(f0, before, 'cell:tools/logic');
    const b = inside(f1, after, 'cell:tools/logic');
    const moves = [...a].map(([id, p]) => Math.hypot(b.get(id)!.rel.x - p.rel.x, b.get(id)!.rel.y - p.rel.y));
    expect(moves.length).toBeGreaterThan(3);
    expect(Math.max(...moves)).toBeLessThanOrEqual(2 * (42 + 12) + 1);
  });

  it('is deterministic: the same inputs give the same frame', async () => {
    const s = sceneFor(base, open);
    const [a, b] = [await frameFor(s), await frameFor(sceneFor(base, open))];
    expect(b.nodes).toEqual(a.nodes);
    expect(b.edges.map((e) => e.d)).toEqual(a.edges.map((e) => e.d));
  });

  it('a turn event that changes no structure keeps every node in place', async () => {
    const s0 = sceneFor(base, ['domain:tools']);
    const s1 = sceneFor([...base, ev('turn_started', { prompt: 'x', head: '', baseline: '' }, { turn: 't' }), ev('looked', { tool: 'Read' }, { turn: 't', path: 'src/tools/web-search.ts', cell: { domain: 'tools', layer: 'logic' } })], ['domain:tools']);
    expect((await frameFor(s1)).nodes).toEqual((await frameFor(s0)).nodes);
  });
});

describe('v2 layout: grid, ports and declutter', () => {
  it('System level: every cell on the grid, no containers, every edge drawn in full', async () => {
    const s = sceneFor(base, []);
    const f = await frameFor(s);
    expect(f.nodes.every((x) => x.type === 'cell')).toBe(true);
    expect(f.nodes.length).toBe(s.projection.grid.cells.length + (f.boxes[UNASSIGNED] ? 1 : 0));
    expect(f.edges.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    expect(f.edges.some((e) => e.faint)).toBe(false);
    // the gateway bypass on load is a red edge from Research tools·Logic to Model gateway·External
    expect(f.edges.find((e) => e.from === 'cell:tools/logic' && e.to === 'cell:gateway/external')?.violation).toBe('existing');
    // flow down a column is implied: no edge between two cells of one domain
    expect(f.edges.some((e) => e.from.startsWith('cell:') && e.to.startsWith('cell:') && e.from.split('/')[0] === e.to.split('/')[0])).toBe(false);
  });

  it('a domain open: its column widens, the others become spines, edges leave through the container border', async () => {
    const s = sceneFor(base, ['domain:tools']);
    const f = await frameFor(s);
    const tools = f.cols.find((c) => c.id === 'tools')!;
    expect(tools.open).toBe(true);
    expect(f.cols.filter((c) => c.id !== 'tools').every((c) => c.spine)).toBe(true);
    expect(f.boxes['cell:tools/logic']!.type).toBe('container');
    expect(f.boxes['src/tools/news-summarize.ts']!.type).toBe('file');
    // the existing bypass now starts at the file, inside the container
    const bypass = f.edges.find((e) => e.from === 'src/tools/news-summarize.ts' && e.violation === 'existing')!;
    expect(bypass).toBeDefined();
    const box = f.boxes['src/tools/news-summarize.ts']!;
    const [x0, y0] = bypass.d.slice(1).split(/[LQ ]/)[0]!.split(',').map(Number) as [number, number];
    expect(x0).toBeCloseTo(box.x + box.w, 0);
    expect(y0).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(box.y);
    expect(y0).toBeLessThanOrEqual(box.y + box.h);
  });

  it('declutters: edges away from the open region merge into faint trunks with a count; loud edges stay', async () => {
    const s = sceneFor(base, ['domain:tools']);
    const f = await frameFor(s);
    const trunks = f.edges.filter((e) => e.trunk);
    expect(trunks.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    for (const t of trunks) {
      expect(t.faint).toBe(true);
      expect(t.count).toBe(t.trunk!.reduce((sum, id) => sum + s.projection.edges.find((e) => e.id === id)!.count, 0));
      // nothing in a trunk touches the open domain
      for (const id of t.trunk!) {
        const e = s.projection.edges.find((x) => x.id === id)!;
        expect([e.from, e.to].some((x) => s.projection.nodes.find((nn) => nn.id === x)!.domain === 'tools')).toBe(false);
      }
    }
    expect(f.edges.filter((e) => e.violation).every((e) => !e.faint)).toBe(true);
    // a selected node narrows the region further: edges not touching it fade, its own stay
    const sel = await frameFor(s, ['src/tools/news-summarize.ts']);
    expect(sel.edges.filter((e) => !e.faint).every((e) => e.from === 'src/tools/news-summarize.ts' || e.to === 'src/tools/news-summarize.ts' || e.violation || e.status !== 'existing')).toBe(true);
  });
});

describe('v2 navigation', () => {
  const s = sceneFor(base, []);
  const g = s.graph;

  it('dives into cells and domains, and Esc goes back up one level at a time', () => {
    let p = dive(g, { open: [], focus: null }, 'cell:tools/logic');
    expect(p).toEqual({ open: ['cell:tools/logic'], focus: 'cell:tools/logic' });
    p = { ...p, focus: 'src/tools/news-summarize.ts' };
    p = up(g, p);
    expect(p).toEqual({ open: [], focus: 'cell:tools/logic' });
    p = up(g, p);
    expect(p).toEqual({ open: [], focus: 'domain:tools' });
    expect(up(g, p)).toEqual({ open: [], focus: null });
    // opening the domain replaces its cells; closing one cell keeps the others open
    const d = dive(g, { open: ['cell:tools/logic'], focus: null }, 'domain:tools');
    expect(d.open).toEqual(['domain:tools']);
    const back = up(g, { ...d, focus: 'src/tools/web-search.ts' });
    expect(back.focus).toBe('cell:tools/logic');
    expect(back.open).toEqual(['cell:tools/entry', 'cell:tools/external'].filter((c) => g.nodes[c]));
  });

  it('jumps to a symbol by opening its cell and focusing its file', () => {
    const sym = Object.keys(g.nodes).find((id) => id.startsWith('src/memory/retrieve.ts#'))!;
    expect(jump(g, { open: [], focus: null }, sym)).toEqual({ open: ['cell:memory/logic'], focus: 'src/memory/retrieve.ts' });
    expect(jump(g, { open: ['domain:memory'], focus: null }, 'src/memory/retrieve.ts')).toEqual({ open: ['domain:memory'], focus: 'src/memory/retrieve.ts' });
  });
});
```

```text
// ---- API -------------------------------------------------------------------

export interface WhereOptions {
  orderBy?: string;
  limit?: number;
}

export const db = {
  async insert<T extends object>(table: TableName, row: T): Promise<T & { id: string }> {
    const pg = await connection();
    const known = tableColumns(table);
    const entries = Object.entries(row).filter(([, value]) => value !== undefined);
    const names = entries.map(([key]) => toColumn(key));
    const values = entries.map(([key, value]) => encode(value, known.get(toColumn(key))));
    const placeholders = values.map((_, i) => `$${i + 1}`);
    const result = await pg.query<Row>(
      `insert into ${table} (${names.join(", ")}) values (${placeholders.join(", ")}) returning *`,
      values,
    );
    return decode(result.rows[0] ?? {}, table);
  },

  async update<T = Row>(table: TableName, id: string, patch: Row): Promise<T> {
    const pg = await connection();
    const known = tableColumns(table);
    const entries = Object.entries(patch).filter(([key, value]) => value !== undefined && key !== "id");
    const sets = entries.map(([key], i) => `${toColumn(key)} = $${i + 1}`);
    const values = entries.map(([key, value]) => encode(value, known.get(toColumn(key))));
    const result = await pg.query<Row>(
      `update ${table} set ${sets.join(", ")} where id = $${values.length + 1} returning *`,
      [...values, id],
    );
    if (!result.rows[0]) throw new NotFoundError(table, id);
    return decode(result.rows[0], table);
  },

  async get<T>(table: TableName, id: string): Promise<T | undefined> {
    const rows = await db.where<T>(table, { id }, { limit: 1 });
    return rows[0];
  },

  /** Rows whose columns equal every value in `criteria` (null matches IS NULL). */
  async where<T>(table: TableName, criteria: Row = {}, options: WhereOptions = {}): Promise<T[]> {
    const pg = await connection();
    tableColumns(table);
    const conditions: string[] = [];
    const values: unknown[] = [];
    for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(criteria)) {
      if (value === null) {
        conditions.push(`${toColumn(key)} is null`);
      } else {
        values.push(value);
        conditions.push(`${toColumn(key)} = $${values.length}`);
      }
    }
    const sql = [
      `select * from ${table}`,
      conditions.length ? `where ${conditions.join(" and ")}` : "",
      options.orderBy ? `order by ${orderClause(options.orderBy)}` : "",
      options.limit ? `limit ${Math.max(1, Math.floor(options.limit))}` : "",
    ].join(" ");
    const result = await pg.query<Row>(sql, values);
    return result.rows.map((row) => decode<T>(row, table));
  },

  async all<T>(table: TableName, options: WhereOptions = {}): Promise<T[]> {
    return db.where<T>(table, {}, options);
  },

  async count(table: TableName, criteria: Row = {}): Promise<number> {
    return (await db.where(table, criteria)).length;
  },

  /** A read-only query for joins and aggregates. Writes go through insert/update. */
  async query<T>(sql: string, params: unknown[] = []): Promise<T[]> {
    if (!/^\s*(select|with)\b/i.test(sql)) throw new Error("db.query only runs reads; use db.insert or db.update");
    const pg = await connection();
    const result = await pg.query<Row>(sql, params);
    return result.rows.map((row) => decode<T>(row));
  },

  /** Empties every table and restarts id sequences. Used by tests and the proof script. */
  async reset(): Promise<void> {
```

```typescript
const sleep = (ms: number) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms));

  git(dir, 'config', 'user.name', 'test');
  git(dir, 'add', '-A');
  git(dir, 'commit', '-qm', 'fixture');
  return dir;
}

function setup(extra: Record<string, string> = {}) {
  const root = sandbox(mapYaml, extra);
  const bus = new Bus(root, { fresh: true });
  const repo = new Repo(root, bus);
  repo.loadMapFile();
  bus.emit('map_confirmed', { map: repo.map, source: 'file' }, { turn: null });
  closers.push(() => repo.close());
  const of = <K extends keyof EventData>(kind: K) => bus.events.filter((e): e is HarnessEvent & { data: EventData[K] } => e.kind === kind);
  return { root, bus, repo, of };
}

describe('Tier 2 on the server', () => {
  it('emits facts_resolved per file after a scan, re-resolves edits, and the graph store follows the current hashes', async () => {
    const { root, bus, repo, of } = setup();
    const semantic = attachSemantic(bus, repo)!;
    closers.push(() => semantic.close());
    repo.scan();
    await semantic.idle();
    const resolved = of('facts_resolved');
    expect(resolved.length).toBe(repo.fileFacts.size);
    expect(new Set(resolved.map((e) => e.path)).size).toBe(repo.fileFacts.size);
    const ui = reduce(bus.events);
    expect(Object.keys(ui.semantic).length).toBe(repo.fileFacts.size); // every hash matched in the reducer too
    const ns = ui.semantic['src/tools/news-summarize.ts']!;
    expect(ns.implements).toEqual([{ from: 'src/tools/news-summarize.ts#newsSummarize.run', to: 'src/shared/types.ts#Tool.run' }]);
    expect(ns.calls.map((c) => `${c.to} ${c.confidence}`)).toEqual(['vendor/llm-openai/index.ts#chat typed', 'vendor/news/index.ts#call typed']);

    const store = semanticStore(repo, bus);
    expect(store.coverage()).toEqual({ typed: repo.fileFacts.size, files: repo.fileFacts.size });
    const g1 = store.graph();
    expect(store.graph()).toBe(g1); // cached until something changes
    expect(g1.edges.some((e) => e.kind === 'implements' && e.to === 'src/shared/types.ts#Tool.run')).toBe(true);

    // An edit: the stale entry drops at once; the new one arrives after the debounce, for the new hash.
    const path = 'src/tools/news-summarize.ts';
    appendFileSync(join(root, path), '\nexport function extra() { return 1; }\n');
    const t0 = performance.now();
    repo.fileChanged(path, { tool: 'Edit' });
    expect(store.facts[path]).toBeUndefined();
    expect(store.graph()).not.toBe(g1);
    await semantic.idle();
    const ms = performance.now() - t0;
    const last = of('facts_resolved').at(-1)!;
    expect(last.path).toBe(path);
    expect(last.data.facts.hash).toBe(repo.fileFacts.get(path)!.hash);
    expect(store.facts[path]?.hash).toBe(repo.fileFacts.get(path)!.hash);
    expect(ms).toBeLessThan(1500); // 150 ms debounce + one snapshot update + re-resolve
    expect(semantic.status().state).toBe('ready');
  });

  it('is off with HARNESS_SEMANTIC=0', () => {
    const { bus, repo } = setup();
    process.env.HARNESS_SEMANTIC = '0';
    try { expect(attachSemantic(bus, repo)).toBeNull(); } finally { delete process.env.HARNESS_SEMANTIC; }
  });
});

describe('config-file rescans', () => {
  it('rescans on package.json / tsconfig changes and user edits of domains.yaml, never on Harness\'s own writes', () => {
    const { root, repo, of } = setup();
    repo.scan();
    const scans = () => of('repo_scanned').length;
    expect(scans()).toBe(1);

    // Harness writes domains.yaml the way decisions/accept do: file, then setMap with the same text.
    const own = `${mapYaml}\n# exception recorded by Harness\n`;
    writeFileSync(repo.mapPath, own);
    repo.setMap(own);
    expect(repo.applyConfigChanges(['domains.yaml'])).toBe(false);
    expect(scans()).toBe(1);

    // The user edits it by hand: reload the map and rescan once.
    writeFileSync(repo.mapPath, `${own}# edited by hand\n`);
    expect(repo.applyConfigChanges(['domains.yaml'])).toBe(true);
    expect(scans()).toBe(2);
    expect(of('map_confirmed').at(-1)!.data.source).toBe('file');

    // An invalid hand edit keeps the old map and doesn't rescan.
    writeFileSync(repo.mapPath, 'domains: [');
    expect(repo.applyConfigChanges(['domains.yaml'])).toBe(false);
    expect(of('error').at(-1)!.data.message).toMatch(/keeping the previous map/);
    writeFileSync(repo.mapPath, repo.mapText);

    // package.json gains a bin: entries come from a fresh index after the rescan.
    const pkg = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'), 'utf8')) as Record<string, unknown>;
    writeFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'), JSON.stringify({ ...pkg, bin: { scoutctl: 'src/channels/cli.ts' } }));
    expect(repo.applyConfigChanges(['package.json'])).toBe(true);
    expect(scans()).toBe(3);
    expect(repo.fileFacts.get('src/channels/cli.ts')!.entries.map((e) => e.id)).toContain('entry:bin:scoutctl');
  });

  it('the watcher triggers them (tsconfig.json), and ignores Harness\'s own domains.yaml write', async () => {
    const { root, repo, of } = setup();
    repo.scan();
    repo.startWatcher();
    await sleep(300); // chokidar's initial crawl
    const scans = () => of('repo_scanned').length;
    writeFileSync(join(root, 'tsconfig.json'), '{ "compilerOptions": { "strict": true } }\n');
    for (let i = 0; i < 40 && scans() < 2; i++) await sleep(100);
    expect(scans()).toBe(2);

    const own = `${repo.mapText}\n# written by Harness\n`;
    writeFileSync(repo.mapPath, own);
    repo.setMap(own);
    await sleep(900);
    expect(scans()).toBe(2);
  });
});

describe('barrel relink', () => {
  const LIB = {
    'src/lib/a.ts': 'export function alpha() {\n  return 1;\n}\n',
    'src/lib/b.ts': 'export function beta() {\n  return 2;\n}\n',
    'src/lib/index.ts': "export { alpha } from './a';\n",
    'src/use.ts': "import { alpha } from './lib';\nexport function run() {\n  return alpha();\n}\n",
  };
  const callsOf = (repo: Repo, p: string) => repo.fileFacts.get(p)!.calls.map((c) => `${c.from} -> ${c.to}`);

  it('re-links importers when a barrel re-points an export, and through barrels when a symbol disappears', () => {
    const { root, repo, of } = setup(LIB);
    repo.scan();
    expect(callsOf(repo, 'src/use.ts')).toEqual(['src/use.ts#run -> src/lib/a.ts#alpha']);

    writeFileSync(join(root, 'src/lib/index.ts'), "export { beta as alpha } from './b';\n");
    repo.fileChanged('src/lib/index.ts', { tool: 'Write' });
    expect(callsOf(repo, 'src/use.ts')).toEqual(['src/use.ts#run -> src/lib/b.ts#beta']);
    const changed = of('facts_changed').filter((e) => e.path === 'src/use.ts');
    expect(changed).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(of('call_added').filter((e) => e.path === 'src/use.ts').map((e) => e.data.to)).toEqual(['src/lib/b.ts#beta']);
    expect(of('call_removed').filter((e) => e.path === 'src/use.ts').map((e) => e.data.to)).toEqual(['src/lib/a.ts#alpha']);

    // Back to `export *`, then a.ts renames alpha: use.ts (behind the barrel) now points at the file only.
    writeFileSync(join(root, 'src/lib/index.ts'), "export * from './a';\n");
    repo.fileChanged('src/lib/index.ts', { tool: 'Write' });
    expect(callsOf(repo, 'src/use.ts')).toEqual(['src/use.ts#run -> src/lib/a.ts#alpha']);
    writeFileSync(join(root, 'src/lib/a.ts'), 'export function alpha2() {\n  return 1;\n}\n');
    repo.fileChanged('src/lib/a.ts', { tool: 'Write' });
    expect(callsOf(repo, 'src/use.ts')).toEqual(['src/use.ts#run -> src/lib/a.ts']);

    // A body-only edit relinks nothing.
    const before = of('facts_changed').length;
    writeFileSync(join(root, 'src/lib/a.ts'), 'export function alpha2() {\n  return 42;\n}\n');
    repo.fileChanged('src/lib/a.ts', { tool: 'Write' });
    expect(of('facts_changed').length).toBe(before + 1); // a.ts itself only
  });
});

describe('onboarding (no domains.yaml)', () => {
  it('scores the cartographer\'s K candidates and returns the best; invalid ones are dropped', async () => {
    const root = sandbox(null);
    const bus = new Bus(root, { fresh: true });
    const inputs: ProposeInput[] = [];
    const weak = mapYaml.replace(/paths: \[[^\]]*\]/g, 'paths: ["nowhere/**"]');
    const proposer: Proposer = async (input) => {
      inputs.push(input);
      return { cost: 0, candidates: [
        { title: 'Broken.', rationale: '', yaml: 'domains: [' },
        { title: 'Nothing placed.', rationale: '', yaml: weak },
        { title: 'Scout map.', rationale: 'Product domains.', yaml: mapYaml },
      ] };
    };
    const best = await proposeOnboarding({ root, bus, proposer, k: 4, gitLimit: 20 });
    expect(best).not.toBeNull();
    expect(best!.candidate.title).toBe('Scout map.');
    expect(best!.scored).toBe(2);
    expect(best!.score.unassigned).toBeLessThan(best!.skeleton.unassigned + 1);
    expect(parseDomainMap(best!.yaml).domains.map((d) => d.id)).toEqual(parseDomainMap(mapYaml).domains.map((d) => d.id));

    const input = inputs[0]!;
    expect(input).toMatchObject({ mode: 'onboard', k: 4, signals: [], turns: [] });
    expect(input.yaml).toBe(onboardingSkeleton(root).replace(/^#.*\n\n/, ''));
    expect(input.facts['src/tools/news-summarize.ts']!.symbols.length).toBeGreaterThan(0); // real Tier 1 facts
    const prompt = buildPrompt(input);
    expect(prompt).toContain('There is no confirmed map yet');
    expect(prompt).not.toContain('## Signals');
    const runs = bus.events.filter((e) => e.kind === 'maintenance_run').map((e) => e.data);
    expect(runs).toEqual([expect.objectContaining({ agent: 'cartographer', trigger: 'onboarding', ok: true, cost: 0 })]);
  });

  it('returns null when no candidate is valid', async () => {
    const root = sandbox(null);
    const bus = new Bus(root, { fresh: true });
    const proposer: Proposer = async () => ({ cost: null, candidates: [{ title: 'x', rationale: '', yaml: 'nope: [' }] });
    expect(await proposeOnboarding({ root, bus, proposer, k: 4 })).toBeNull();
  });
});

describe('living map facts', () => {
  it('hands the cartographer real Tier 1 facts (symbols, calls, hashes), with Tier 2 calls where current', async () => {
    const { root, bus, repo } = setup();
    repo.scan();
    const store = semanticStore(repo, bus);
    // Pretend Tier 2 resolved one file: its calls replace Tier 1's in what the living map sees.
    const f = repo.fileFacts.get('src/orchestrator/agent.ts')!;
    bus.emit('facts_resolved', { facts: { path: f.path, hash: f.hash, calls: [{ from: `${f.path}#runAgent`, to: 'src/memory/retrieve.ts#retrieve', confidence: 'typed', count: 1 }], implements: [] } }, { path: f.path, turn: null });
    bus.emit('facts_resolved', { facts: { path: 'src/tools/web-search.ts', hash: 'stale', calls: [], implements: [] } }, { turn: null });
    expect(Object.keys(store.facts)).toEqual(['src/orchestrator/agent.ts']);

    const inputs: ProposeInput[] = [];
    const lm = attachLivingMap({ bus, repo, proposer: async (i) => { inputs.push(i); return { cost: 0, candidates: [] }; }, labeler: null, gitLimit: 20 });
    const turn = (id: string, files: Record<string, string>) => {
      bus.turn = id;
      bus.emit('turn_started', { prompt: id, head: '', baseline: '' });
      for (const [p, text] of Object.entries(files)) {
        mkdirSync(join(root, p, '..'), { recursive: true });
        writeFileSync(join(root, p), text);
        repo.fileChanged(p, { tool: 'Write' });
      }
      bus.emit('turn_ended', { added: 1, removed: 0, files: [], reason: 'success' });
      bus.turn = null;
    };
    turn('t1', { 'src/billing/invoice.ts': 'export function invoice() {\n  return 1;\n}\n' });
    await lm.idle();
    turn('t2', { 'src/billing/invoice.ts': 'export function invoice() {\n  return 2;\n}\n' });
    await lm.idle();
    lm.detach();
    expect(inputs).toHaveLength(1);
    const facts = inputs[0]!.facts;
    expect(facts['src/tools/news-summarize.ts']!.symbols.map((s) => s.id)).toContain('src/tools/news-summarize.ts#newsSummarize.run');
    expect(facts['src/tools/news-summarize.ts']!.hash).not.toBe('');
    expect(facts['src/billing/invoice.ts']!.symbols.map((s) => s.name)).toEqual(['invoice']);
    expect(facts['src/orchestrator/agent.ts']!.calls).toEqual([{ from: 'src/orchestrator/agent.ts#runAgent', to: 'src/memory/retrieve.ts#retrieve', confidence: 'typed', count: 1 }]);
  });
});
```

```bash
new='''function invariantTouches(inv: Invariant, s: TurnSurface, mapper: Mapper, targets: readonly string[]): string | null {
  const domainOf = (p: string) => mapper.domainOf(p);
  const changedDomains = new Set(s.files.map(domainOf).filter((d): d is string => !!d));
  const targetDomains = new Set(targets.map(domainOf).filter((d): d is string => !!d));
  // Tables the turn newly reads or writes (reads are invisible to the gate), with the domain whose cell lists them.
  const tables = [...s.delta.reads.map((r) => ({ ...r, how: 'reads' })), ...s.delta.writes.map((w) => ({ ...w, how: 'writes' }))]
    .map((t) => ({ ...t, owner: mapper.ownerOf(t.table)?.domain ?? null }));
  const tableOf = (domains: readonly string[]) => tables.find((t) => t.owner && domains.includes(t.owner));
  const say = (t: { file: string; how: string; table: string; owner: string | null }) => `${t.file} newly ${t.how} "${t.table}" (owned by ${t.owner})`;
  const exception = inv.exceptions.find((e) => s.files.includes(e.path));
  if (exception) return `${exception.path} is an exception to ${inv.id}`;
  if (inv.kind === 'only_via') {
    const hit = [...s.files, ...targets].find((p) => matchesAny(inv.targets, p));
    if (hit) return `${hit} is a target of ${inv.id}`;
    const via = inv.allowed_from.find((d) => targetDomains.has(d) && [...changedDomains].some((c) => c !== d));
    if (via) return `the turn now reaches ${via}, the only way ${inv.id} allows`;
    const inside = inv.allowed_from.find((d) => changedDomains.has(d));
    if (inside) return `the turn changed ${inside}, the way ${inv.id} allows`;
    const t = tableOf(inv.allowed_from);
    return t ? say(t) : null;
  }
  if (inv.kind === 'owns_writes') {
    const t = tables.find((x) => x.table in inv.owners);
    return t ? `${t.file} newly ${t.how} "${t.table}" (owned by ${inv.owners[t.table]})` : null;
  }
  // no_edge: the turn touches files in either domain, or reads/writes a table one of them owns. The checker only sees
  // a direct import edge; the decision's rationale may cover indirect routes (e.g. a read through neutral shared code).
  const t = tableOf([inv.from, inv.to]);
  if (t) return say(t);
  const end = [inv.from, inv.to].find((d) => changedDomains.has(d));
  return end ? `the turn changed files in ${end}, an end of ${inv.id} (${inv.from} → ${inv.to})` : null;
}

'''
```

```text
1	# Demo recording plan
2	
3	Oct 11, 2026. This replaces the "Demo script" section of the Build Plan. It assumes the harness from `SPEC.md` plus the navigation work in `NAVIGATION_PLAN.md`, and Scout as built from `DEMO_REPO_SPEC.md`: live services (Claude, Claude web search, SEC EDGAR), embedded Postgres (PGlite with pgvector), a web app, and 17 commits tagged `demo-start`.
4	
5	## The story
6	
7	**You stay the architect; the agent does the typing.** Each beat starts the way real work does: a question, a bug you can see, a feature a rep asked for. Instead of "fix this" and hoping, you read the plan on the map, steer it, and only then let Claude build. Everything is about one theme in Scout: where customer data goes.
8	
9	**The pitch**
10	
11	- Hook: "Writing code got free. Understanding it didn't." Developers already spent about 58% of their time on comprehension (Xia et al., 2018). In METR's 2025 trial, experienced developers using AI were 19% slower and still believed they had been sped up.
12	- Close: "Chat is the right input and the wrong output."
```

```text
  const plannedEdges: TurnActivity['plannedEdges'] = [];
  if (turn) {
    for (const pe of Object.values(turn.plannedEdges)) {
      if (pe.imports.every((i) => ids.has(edgeId('imports', i.from, i.to)))) continue;
      for (const i of pe.imports) {
        const hit = turn.planViolations.find((v) => v.file === i.from && (!v.target || v.target === i.to));
        const violation: ViolationState = !hit ? null : known(hit.file, hit.invariant) ? 'existing' : 'new';
        plannedEdges.push({ from: i.from, to: i.to, steps: [...pe.steps], violation });
      }
    }
    // an import the edit gate blocked is a would-be edge: a ghost carrying the new violation
    for (const v of turn.gateBlocks) {
      if (!v.target || !has(v.file) || !has(v.target) || ids.has(edgeId('imports', v.file, v.target))) continue;
      const kind = graph.nodes[v.target]!.kind;
      if (kind !== 'file' && kind !== 'vendor') continue;
      if (plannedEdges.some((p) => p.from === v.file && p.to === v.target)) continue;
      plannedEdges.push({ from: v.file, to: v.target, steps: [], violation: 'new' });
    }
    plannedEdges.sort((a, b) => byId(a.from, b.from) || byId(a.to, b.to));
  }

  const added = new Set<string>();
  for (const e of turn?.edgesAdded ?? []) added.add(edgeId('imports', e.edge.from, e.edge.to));
  for (const c of turn?.callsAdded ?? []) added.add(edgeId('calls', c.from, c.to));

  return {
    turn: turn?.id ?? null,
    leaves,
    plannedEdges,
    addedEdges: [...added].filter((id) => ids.has(id)).sort(byId),
    cursor,
    verb: cursor ? ui.cursor!.verb : null,
    violations: { files: [...files].sort(byId), edges: [...edges].sort(byId) },

    plannedNew: plannedNew.sort(byId),
```

```text
1	# Demo recording plan
2	
3	Oct 11, 2026. This replaces the "Demo script" section of the Build Plan. It assumes the harness from `SPEC.md` plus the navigation work in `NAVIGATION_PLAN.md`, and Scout as built from `DEMO_REPO_SPEC.md`: live services (Claude, Claude web search, SEC EDGAR), embedded Postgres (PGlite with pgvector), a web app, and 17 commits tagged `demo-start`.
4	
5	## The story
6	
7	**You stay the architect; the agent does the typing.** Each beat starts the way real work does: a question, a bug you can see, a feature a rep asked for. Instead of "fix this" and hoping, you read the plan on the map, steer it, and only then let Claude build. Everything is about one theme in Scout: where customer data goes.
8	
9	**The pitch**
10	
11	- Hook: "Writing code got free. Understanding it didn't." Developers already spent about 58% of their time on comprehension (Xia et al., 2018). In METR's 2025 trial, experienced developers using AI were 19% slower and still believed they had been sped up.
12	- Close: "Chat is the right input and the wrong output."
13	
14	**What each beat proves**
15	
16	
17	| #   | Beat          | You do                                                   | The harness shows                                                               | Built in                            |
18	| --- | ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
19	| 1   | Ask           | Ask where a contact's phone number goes                  | A journey plays; a trace shows two paths to the model provider, one of them red | N8 Trace, N10 Journeys, graph tools |
20	| 2   | Fix a bug     | Report "revenue shows as phone 1"                        | Plan ghosts down to functions; you point at the real cause; the plan moves      | N6 Module level, N7 Point           |
21	| 3   | Add a feature | "Can we add a research tool that checks whether we've already emailed this contact?" | A red ghost edge before any code; Claude asks A or B; your answer becomes an architectural decision (git + Alike) | SPEC v1 (gate, forks, decisions) |
22	| 4   | Remember | "Can we build a research tool that reads our past emails and suggests a personalized opener?" | The tool you asked for is not built: its edge shows struck through, "rejected in DR-4"; the feature is built the decided way | SPEC v1 (§8) + struck-through rejected edge |
23	| 5   | Living map    | Ask for account watchlists                               | New code with no home; the cartographer proposes a domain with scores           | N5                                  |
```

```text
// Write adapters: table writes found in comment-free code. Text-based so the edit gate needs no AST, and the
// gate, the load scan and extractFacts all see the same writes. Browser-safe.

export type WriteHit = { table: string; via: string; at: number };

type Adapter = { via: string; guard: RegExp; find: (code: string, out: WriteHit[]) => void };

const each = (re: RegExp, code: string, fn: (m: RegExpMatchArray) => void) => {
  for (const m of code.matchAll(re)) fn(m);
};

/** Scout: `db.insert("t", …)` / `db.update("t", …)` with a literal table name. */
const SCOUT = /(?<![\w$])db\s*\.\s*(?:insert|update)\s*\(\s*(?:"([^"\\\n]+)"|'([^'\\\n]+)'|`([^`\\$]+)`)/g;
/** Prisma: `prisma.user.create(…)`, `tx.post.updateMany(…)`. */
const PRISMA = /(?<![\w$])(?:prisma|tx)\s*\.\s*([a-z][\w$]*)\s*\.\s*(?:create|createMany|createManyAndReturn|update|updateMany|updateManyAndReturn|upsert|delete|deleteMany)\s*\(/g;
/** Drizzle: `db.insert(users).values(…)`, `.update(users).set(…)`, `.delete(users).where(…)`. */
const DRIZZLE = /\.\s*(?:insert|update|delete)\s*\(\s*([A-Za-z_$][\w$]*)\s*\)\s*\.\s*(?:values|set|where|returning|onConflictDoNothing|onConflictDoUpdate)\s*\(/g;
/** Knex: `knex("t")…insert(…)`, `trx("t").update(…)`, `knex.table("t").del()`. */
const KNEX = /(?<![\w$])(?:knex|trx)\s*(?:\.\s*(?:table|into|from)\s*)?\(\s*(['"`])([\w.]+)\1\s*\)/g;
const KNEX_WRITE = /^[^;]{0,400}?\.\s*(?:insert|update|del|delete|upsert|merge|increment|decrement)\s*\(/;
/** Kysely: `db.insertInto("t")`, `.updateTable("t")`, `.deleteFrom("t")`. */
const KYSELY = /\.\s*(?:insertInto|replaceInto|updateTable|deleteFrom|mergeInto)\s*\(\s*(['"`])([\w.]+)\1/g;
/** Raw SQL (upper-case keywords, so prose like "Delete from cart" is skipped) at the start of a string or template literal. */
const SQL = /(['"`])\s*(?:(?:INSERT|REPLACE)\s+(?:OR\s+\w+\s+)?INTO|DELETE\s+FROM|MERGE\s+INTO|UPDATE)\s+[`"[]?([A-Za-z_][\w.]*)[`"\]]?(\s+SET\b)?/g;

const ADAPTERS: Adapter[] = [
  { via: 'db', guard: /\bdb\s*\./, find: (code, out) => each(SCOUT, code, (m) => out.push({ table: (m[1] ?? m[2] ?? m[3])!, via: 'db', at: m.index! })) },
  { via: 'prisma', guard: /\b(?:prisma|tx)\s*\./, find: (code, out) => each(PRISMA, code, (m) => out.push({ table: m[1]!, via: 'prisma', at: m.index! })) },
  { via: 'drizzle', guard: /\.\s*(?:insert|update|delete)\s*\(/, find: (code, out) => each(DRIZZLE, code, (m) => out.push({ table: m[1]!, via: 'drizzle', at: m.index! })) },
  {
    via: 'knex',
    guard: /\b(?:knex|trx)\b/,
    find: (code, out) => each(KNEX, code, (m) => {
      const after = code.slice(m.index! + m[0].length, m.index! + m[0].length + 400);
      if (KNEX_WRITE.test(after)) out.push({ table: m[2]!, via: 'knex', at: m.index! });
    }),
  },
  { via: 'kysely', guard: /\.\s*(?:insertInto|replaceInto|updateTable|deleteFrom|mergeInto)\b/, find: (code, out) => each(KYSELY, code, (m) => out.push({ table: m[2]!, via: 'kysely', at: m.index! })) },
  {
    via: 'sql',
    guard: /\b(?:INSERT|REPLACE|DELETE|MERGE|UPDATE)\s/,
    find: (code, out) => each(SQL, code, (m) => {
      if (/^\s*UPDATE/.test(code.slice(m.index! + 1, m.index! + 12)) && !m[3]) return; // UPDATE needs SET
      out.push({ table: m[2]!, via: 'sql', at: m.index! });
    }),
  },
];

/** Table writes in `code` (comments already blanked), in source order. */
export function findWrites(code: string): WriteHit[] {
  const out: WriteHit[] = [];
  for (const a of ADAPTERS) if (a.guard.test(code)) a.find(code, out);
  return out.sort((x, y) => x.at - y.at);
}

/** `source` with the given comment spans replaced by spaces (offsets kept). */
export function maskComments(source: string, comments: readonly { start: number; end: number }[]): string {
  if (comments.length === 0) return source;
  let out = '';
  let at = 0;
  for (const c of comments) {
    out += source.slice(at, c.start) + source.slice(c.start, c.end).replace(/[^\n]/g, ' ');
    at = c.end;
  }
  return out + source.slice(at);
}
```
