```text
import { existsSync, mkdirSync, readdirSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { basename, join } from 'node:path';
import { parse as parseYaml, stringify as stringifyYaml } from 'yaml';
import { linkDecision, addException, nextDecisionId, type Violation } from '@harness/core';
import { commitPaths, git } from './git';
import type { Repo } from './repo';
import type { Bus } from './bus';

export type DecisionRecord = {
  id: string;
  title: string;
  outcome: string;
  status: string;
  type: string;
  invariant: string;
  anchors: { paths: string[] };
  rejected: string;
  rationale: string;
};

/** Read `decisions/DR-*.md` (front matter + body). */
export function listDecisions(root: string): DecisionRecord[] {
  const dir = join(root, 'decisions');
  if (!existsSync(dir)) return [];
  const out: DecisionRecord[] = [];
  for (const f of readdirSync(dir).filter((f) => /^DR-\d+\.md$/.test(f))) {
    const text = readFileSync(join(dir, f), 'utf8');
    const m = /^---\n([\s\S]*?)\n---\n?([\s\S]*)$/.exec(text);
    if (!m) continue;
    const fm = parseYaml(m[1]!) as Omit<DecisionRecord, 'rationale'>;
    out.push({ ...fm, rationale: m[2]!.trim() });
  }
  return out.sort((a, b) => Number(a.id.slice(3)) - Number(b.id.slice(3)));
}

/** Parse which option the user picked. Explicit A/B wins; "exception" leans B; otherwise A (comply). */
export function parseOption(text: string): 'A' | 'B' {
  const t = text.trim();
  const m = /^\(?\s*(?:option\s+)?([ab])\b/i.exec(t) ?? /\b(?:option|choose|pick|go with)\s+\(?([ab])\b/i.exec(t);
  if (m) return m[1]!.toUpperCase() as 'A' | 'B';
  return /\bexception\b/i.test(t) ? 'B' : 'A';
}

/** The decision in the user's own words: their answer minus the "A —" prefix, first sentence, if it says something. */
export function titleFromAnswer(answer: string): string | null {
  const t = answer.trim().replace(/^\(?\s*(?:option\s+)?[ab]\b\)?\s*[—–:,.-]*\s*/i, '');
  const first = (t.split(/(?<=[.!?])\s/)[0] ?? '').replace(/[.!?]+$/, '').trim();
  if (first.length < 12) return null;
  const s = first[0]!.toUpperCase() + first.slice(1);
  return s.length > 100 ? s.slice(0, 99).replace(/\s+\S*$/, '') + '…' : s;
}

/**
 * `owner/name`, which Alike's path anchors require: HARNESS_REPO_SLUG, else the origin remote,
 * else `<git user>/<folder>` for a repo with no remote.
 */

  if (process.env.HARNESS_REPO_SLUG) return { repository: process.env.HARNESS_REPO_SLUG };
  try {
```

```text
/**
 * An answered fork becomes a standing decision (SPEC §8): write decisions/DR-n.md, update domains.yaml
 * (A links the decision to the invariant, B adds an exception), commit just those two files, emit
 * `decision_recorded`, and return the instruction that asks Claude to record it in Alike.
 */
export function recordFork(repo: Repo, bus: Bus, violations: Violation[], option: 'A' | 'B', answer: string, prompt: string) {
  const existing = listDecisions(repo.root).map((d) => d.id);
  const byInvariant = new Map<string, Violation[]>();
  for (const v of violations) byInvariant.set(v.invariant, [...(byInvariant.get(v.invariant) ?? []), v]);

  const made: DecisionRecord[] = [];
  let yamlText = repo.mapText;
  for (const [invariantId, vs] of byInvariant) {
    const inv = repo.map.invariants.find((i) => i.id === invariantId);
    if (!inv) continue;
    const id = nextDecisionId(repo.map, [...existing, ...made.map((d) => d.id)]);
    const files = [...new Set(vs.map((v) => v.file))];
    const v0 = vs[0]!;
    const [chosen, rejected] = option === 'A' ? [v0.options[0], v0.options[1]] : [v0.options[1], v0.options[0]];
    const title = titleFromAnswer(answer) ?? (option === 'A'
      ? `${files.join(', ')} follows ${inv.id}: ${inv.rule}`
      : `Exception to ${inv.id} for ${files.join(', ')}`);
    const rec: DecisionRecord = {
      id, title, outcome: chosen, status: 'made', type: 'standing', invariant: inv.id,
      anchors: { paths: files }, rejected,
      rationale: [
        `The user chose ${option}, in their words: "${answer.trim()}"`,
        '',
        `Asked during: "${prompt.trim()}"`,
        '',
        `What triggered it: ${v0.reason}`,
        '',
        `Rejected: ${rejected}`,
      ].join('\n'),
    };
    made.push(rec);
    yamlText = option === 'A' ? linkDecision(yamlText, inv.id, id) : addException(yamlText, inv.id, files[0]!, id);
  }
  if (!made.length) return { decisions: [], alikeInstruction: '' };

  mkdirSync(join(repo.root, 'decisions'), { recursive: true });
  const paths: string[] = ['domains.yaml'];
  for (const d of made) {
    const { rationale, ...fm } = d;
    const rel = `decisions/${d.id}.md`;
    writeFileSync(join(repo.root, rel), `---\n${stringifyYaml(fm).trim()}\n---\n\n${rationale}\n`);
    paths.push(rel);
  }
  writeFileSync(repo.mapPath, yamlText);
  try { commitPaths(repo.root, paths, `docs(decisions): ${made.map((d) => d.id).join(', ')} ${made[0]!.title}`.slice(0, 100)); }
  catch (e) { bus.emit('error', { message: `Could not commit ${paths.join(', ')}: ${(e as Error).message}` }); }

  repo.setMap(yamlText);
  bus.emit('map_confirmed', { map: repo.map, source: 'file' });
  for (const d of made) {
    bus.emit('decision_recorded', { id: d.id, title: d.title, invariant: d.invariant, option, paths: d.anchors.paths, alike: false });
  }

  const anchor = repoAnchor(repo.root);
  // Field names checked against Alike's record_decision schema (VERIFY.md, step 0d).
  const alikeInstruction = made.map((d) => {
    const args = {
      title: `${d.id}: ${d.title}`,
      outcome: d.outcome,
      rationale: d.rationale.replace(/\n+/g, ' '),
      decision_type: 'standing',
      status: 'made',
      anchors: d.anchors.paths.map((path) => ({ kind: 'path', label: 'governs', path, repository: anchor.repository })),
    };
    return `Record ${d.id} in Alike now: call mcp__alike__record_decision with exactly these arguments: ${JSON.stringify(args)}. If the Alike tools are unavailable, skip this silently.`;
  }).join('\n');
  return { decisions: made, alikeInstruction };
}
```

```text
/** Every company we hold notes on, most recently researched first. */
export async function listAccounts(): Promise<AccountSummary[]> {
  return db.query<AccountSummary>(
    `select company, count(*)::int as notes, max(created_at) as last_note_at,
            array_agg(distinct source order by source) as sources
       from notes
      group by company
      order by last_note_at desc, company`,
  );
}
export async function searchNotes(company: string, query: string, k: number, runId?: string): Promise<ScoredNote[]> {
  const slug = slugify(company);
  const [{ count } = { count: 0 }] = await db.query<{ count: number }>(
    "select count(*)::int as count from embeddings where company = $1",
    [slug],
  );
  if (count === 0) return [];

  const queryVector = await embed(query, { runId });
  if (queryVector.every((v) => v === 0)) return [];
  const rows = await db.query<NoteRow & { score: number }>(
    `select n.*, 1 - (e.vector <=> $2) as score
       from embeddings e
       join notes n on n.id = e.note_id
      where e.company = $1
      order by e.vector <=> $2, n.id
      limit $3`,
    [slug, `[${queryVector.join(",")}]`, k],
  );
  return rows.map(({ score, ...note }) => ({ note, score }));
}
/** Totals for one run, or for everything when no run is given. */

            sum(output_tokens)::int as output_tokens, sum(usd) as usd
       from cost_log
      where $1::text is null or run_id = $1
      group by purpose`,
    [runId ?? null],
  );
```

```typescript
// Alike integration (ALIKE_INTEGRATION.md, redesigned against Alike's verified capabilities):
// the server records each decision itself through the paired CLI (`alike it`), off the hot path and with no
// model step; anchors are architectural (cell folders, never globs — Alike matches folder prefixes only);
// the URN goes back into the DR file so a decision is recorded once. The MCP instruction is only a fallback.
import { execFile } from 'node:child_process';
import { homedir } from 'node:os';
import { join } from 'node:path';
import type { DomainMap, Invariant } from '@harness/core';
import { git } from './git';

export type AlikeAnchor =
  | { kind: 'path'; label: string; path: string; repository: string }
  | { kind: 'situation'; label: string; text: string };

export type AlikeDecision = {
  title: string;
  outcome: string;
  rationale: string;
  decision_type: 'standing';
  status: 'made';
  anchors: AlikeAnchor[];
};

/** What Harness knows about a decision when it records it. */
export type DecisionInput = {
  id: string;
  title: string;
  outcome: string;
  rejected: string;
  option: 'A' | 'B';
  invariant: Invariant;
  files: string[]; // files the fork was about
  answer: string;
  session: number; // 1-based Harness session number
};

const MAX_PATH_ANCHORS = 20; // Alike: at most 20 path + machine_path anchors

/**
 * `owner/name` as Alike's hooks see it: HARNESS_REPO_SLUG, else the origin remote, lowercased.
 * Null when there is neither — Alike's own fallback (the bare folder name) can't hold path anchors.
 */
export function repoSlug(root: string): string | null {
  if (process.env.HARNESS_REPO_SLUG) return process.env.HARNESS_REPO_SLUG.toLowerCase();
  try {
    const m = /[:/]([^/:]+\/[^/]+?)(?:\.git)?\/?$/.exec(git(root, ['remote', 'get-url', 'origin']));
    if (m) return m[1]!.toLowerCase();
  } catch { /* no remote */ }
  return null;
}

/** A cell path glob as Alike anchors: `src/tools/**` → `src/tools/`; plain files stay; other wildcards → null. */
export function anchorPath(glob: string): string | null {
  if (glob.endsWith('/**')) {
    const dir = glob.slice(0, -3);
    return /[*?[{]/.test(dir) ? null : `${dir}/`;
  }
  return /[*?[{]/.test(glob) ? null : glob;
}

/** Folder/file anchors for a domain's cells, logic first (it's where rules usually bite). */
function domainPaths(map: DomainMap, domainId: string, expand: (glob: string) => string[]): string[] {
  const d = map.domains.find((x) => x.id === domainId);
  if (!d) return [];
  const order = (layer: string) => (layer === 'logic' ? 0 : layer === 'data' ? 1 : layer === 'ui' ? 2 : 3);
  const out: string[] = [];
  for (const [, cell] of Object.entries(d.cells).sort(([a], [b]) => order(a) - order(b))) {
    for (const g of cell.paths ?? []) {
      const p = anchorPath(g);
      out.push(...(p ? [p] : expand(g)));
    }
  }
  return out;
}

/**
 * The architecture a decision governs, as Alike anchors: for `no_edge`, both domains' cells (the `from` side
 * governs, the `to` side is context); for `only_via`, the guarded targets plus the allowed domains; for
 * `owns_writes`, the owners' data cells. An exception (option B) also anchors the excepted file.
 * `expand` turns a glob Alike can't take (e.g. `vendor/llm-*` + `/**`) into concrete folders.
 */
export function decisionAnchors(map: DomainMap, d: DecisionInput, repository: string | null, expand: (glob: string) => string[] = () => []): AlikeAnchor[] {
  const governs = new Set<string>();
  const context = new Set<string>();
  const inv = d.invariant;
  if (inv.kind === 'no_edge') {
    for (const p of domainPaths(map, inv.from, expand)) governs.add(p);
    for (const p of domainPaths(map, inv.to, expand)) context.add(p);
  } else if (inv.kind === 'only_via') {
    for (const g of inv.targets) for (const p of anchorPath(g) ? [anchorPath(g)!] : expand(g)) governs.add(p);
    for (const dom of inv.allowed_from) for (const p of domainPaths(map, dom, expand)) context.add(p);
  } else {
    for (const owner of new Set(Object.values(inv.owners))) {
      const cell = map.domains.find((x) => x.id === owner)?.cells.data;
      for (const g of cell?.paths ?? []) for (const p of anchorPath(g) ? [anchorPath(g)!] : expand(g)) governs.add(p);
    }
  }
  if (d.option === 'B') for (const f of d.files) governs.add(f);

  const anchors: AlikeAnchor[] = [];
  if (repository) {
    const push = (path: string, label: string) => {
      if (anchors.length < MAX_PATH_ANCHORS && !anchors.some((a) => a.kind === 'path' && a.path === path)) anchors.push({ kind: 'path', label, path, repository });
    };
    for (const p of governs) push(p, 'governs');
    for (const p of context) push(p, 'context');
  }
  anchors.push({ kind: 'situation', label: 'applies_when', text: situationFor(map, inv) });
  return anchors;
}

function situationFor(map: DomainMap, inv: Invariant): string {
  const name = (id: string) => map.domains.find((d) => d.id === id)?.name ?? id;
  if (inv.kind === 'no_edge') return `Adding or changing code in ${name(inv.from)} that would depend on ${name(inv.to)}`;
  if (inv.kind === 'only_via') return `Adding code that calls ${inv.targets.join(', ')} from outside ${inv.allowed_from.map(name).join(', ')}`;
  return `Adding code that writes ${Object.keys(inv.owners).join(', ')}`;
}

/** The principle, not the incident: title and rationale an agent elsewhere can act on. */
export function alikeDecision(map: DomainMap, d: DecisionInput, repository: string | null, expand?: (glob: string) => string[]): AlikeDecision {
  return {
    title: `${d.id}: ${d.title}`,
    outcome: d.outcome,
    rationale: [
      `Refines ${d.invariant.id} (${d.invariant.rule}).`,
      `Chosen: ${d.outcome}.`,
      `Rejected: ${d.rejected}.`,
      `In the user's words: "${d.answer.trim()}".`,
      `Decided in Harness session ${d.session}.`,
    ].join(' '),
    decision_type: 'standing',
    status: 'made',
    anchors: decisionAnchors(map, d, repository, expand),
  };
}

export type ExecFn = (file: string, args: string[]) => Promise<{ stdout: string }>;

const defaultExec: ExecFn = (file, args) =>
  new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    execFile(file, args, { timeout: 30_000, maxBuffer: 1 << 20 }, (err, stdout, stderr) => {
      if (err) reject(Object.assign(err, { stderr: String(stderr) }));
      else resolve({ stdout: String(stdout) });
    });
  });

export const alikeCli = () => process.env.HARNESS_ALIKE_CLI ?? join(homedir(), '.alike', 'bin', 'alike');

/** Record one decision with the paired CLI. Resolves to its URN, or rejects with the CLI's error. */
export async function recordDecision(decision: AlikeDecision, exec: ExecFn = defaultExec): Promise<string> {
  const { title, ...rest } = decision;
  const { stdout } = await exec(alikeCli(), ['it', title, '--json', JSON.stringify(rest)]);
  const urn = /urn:alike:decision:[0-9a-f]+/.exec(stdout)?.[0];
  if (!urn) throw new Error(`alike it returned no decision URN: ${stdout.slice(0, 200)}`);
  return urn;
}

/** The old path, kept as a fallback when the CLI is missing or fails: ask the coding session to call MCP. */
export function mcpInstruction(decision: AlikeDecision): string {
  return `Record this decision in Alike now: call mcp__alike__record_decision with exactly these arguments: ${JSON.stringify(decision)}. If the Alike tools are unavailable, skip this silently.`;
}
```

```typescript
// Table reads in code, and tables defined by `.sql` schema files. Text-based like the write adapters; browser-safe.
import type { FileFacts } from '../contracts/facts';
import type { WriteHit } from './adapters';
import { hashText } from './hash';

const each = (re: RegExp, code: string, fn: (m: RegExpMatchArray) => void) => {
  for (const m of code.matchAll(re)) fn(m);
};
const LIT = String.raw`(?:"([^"\\\n]+)"|'([^'\\\n]+)'|\`([^\`\\$]+)\`)`;
/** Type arguments between a method name and its call: `db.get<RunRow>(`, `db.query<Pick<Row, "name">>(`. */
const TARGS = String.raw`(?:<[^()]*?>\s*)?`;

/** Scout: `db.get("t", id)`, `db.where("t", …)`, `db.all("t")`, `db.count("t")`. */
const SCOUT = new RegExp(String.raw`(?<![\w$])db\s*\.\s*(?:get|where|all|count)\s*${TARGS}\(\s*${LIT}`, 'g');
/** `db.query(sql)` / `pool.query(sql)` / `sql.unsafe(sql)`: the first argument's text is SQL whatever its case. */
const QUERY = new RegExp(String.raw`(?<![\w$])(?:db|pool|client|conn|connection|knex\.raw|sql\.unsafe)\s*\.?\s*(?:query|execute|raw|unsafe|all|get)?\s*${TARGS}\(\s*(["'\`])`, 'g');
/** A string or template literal that starts like a read (upper-case keywords, so prose is skipped). */
const SQL_LITERAL = /(["'`])\s*(?:SELECT|WITH)\s/g;
/** Table names after FROM / JOIN in SQL text; `from (subquery)` and functions are skipped. */
const FROM = /\b(?:from|join)\s+(?:only\s+)?["`]?([A-Za-z_]\w*(?:\.[A-Za-z_]\w*)?)["`]?(?!\s*\()/gi;
/** Prisma: `prisma.user.findMany(…)`. */
const PRISMA = /(?<![\w$])(?:prisma|tx)\s*\.\s*([a-z][\w$]*)\s*\.\s*(?:findMany|findUnique|findUniqueOrThrow|findFirst|findFirstOrThrow|count|aggregate|groupBy)\s*\(/g;
/** Drizzle: `db.select().from(users)`, `db.query.users.findMany(…)`. */
const DRIZZLE_FROM = /\.\s*from\s*\(\s*([A-Za-z_$][\w$]*)\s*\)/g;
const DRIZZLE_QUERY = /\bquery\s*\.\s*([A-Za-z_$][\w$]*)\s*\.\s*(?:findMany|findFirst)\s*\(/g;
/** Kysely: `db.selectFrom("t")`. */
const KYSELY = /\.\s*selectFrom\s*\(\s*(['"`])([\w.]+)\1/g;

/** The literal starting at `open` (its quote), up to the matching close quote; templates may span lines. */
function literalAt(code: string, open: number): string {
  const q = code[open]!;
  let i = open + 1;
  while (i < code.length && code[i] !== q) i += code[i] === '\\' ? 2 : 1;
  return code.slice(open + 1, i);
}

const SQL_WORDS = new Set(['select', 'where', 'lateral', 'unnest', 'generate_series', 'jsonb_each', 'json_each']);
function sqlTables(sql: string): string[] {
  const out = new Set<string>();
  each(FROM, sql, (m) => {
    const t = m[1]!.split('.').pop()!;
    if (!SQL_WORDS.has(t.toLowerCase())) out.add(t);
  });
  return [...out];
}

/** Table reads in `code` (comments already blanked), in source order. */
export function findReads(code: string): WriteHit[] {
  const out: WriteHit[] = [];
  const seenSql = new Set<number>();
  if (/\bdb\s*\./.test(code)) each(SCOUT, code, (m) => out.push({ table: (m[1] ?? m[2] ?? m[3])!, via: 'db', at: m.index! }));
  if (/\.\s*(?:query|execute|raw|unsafe)\b|\b(?:db|pool|client)\s*\.\s*(?:all|get)\b/.test(code)) {
    each(QUERY, code, (m) => {
      const open = m.index! + m[0].length - 1;
      seenSql.add(open);
      for (const table of sqlTables(literalAt(code, open))) out.push({ table, via: 'sql', at: m.index! });
    });
  }
  if (/\b(?:SELECT|WITH)\s/.test(code)) {
    each(SQL_LITERAL, code, (m) => {
      if (seenSql.has(m.index!)) return;
      for (const table of sqlTables(literalAt(code, m.index!))) out.push({ table, via: 'sql', at: m.index! });
    });
  }
  if (/\b(?:prisma|tx)\s*\./.test(code)) each(PRISMA, code, (m) => out.push({ table: m[1]!, via: 'prisma', at: m.index! }));
  if (/\.\s*select\s*\(/.test(code)) each(DRIZZLE_FROM, code, (m) => out.push({ table: m[1]!, via: 'drizzle', at: m.index! }));
  if (/\bquery\s*\./.test(code)) each(DRIZZLE_QUERY, code, (m) => out.push({ table: m[1]!, via: 'drizzle', at: m.index! }));
  if (/\.\s*selectFrom\b/.test(code)) each(KYSELY, code, (m) => out.push({ table: m[2]!, via: 'kysely', at: m.index! }));
  return out.sort((x, y) => x.at - y.at);
}

const CONSTRAINT = /^(?:constraint|primary|foreign|unique|check|exclude|like|period)\b/i;
const CREATE = /\bcreate\s+(?:or\s+replace\s+)?(?:(?:global|local)\s+)?(?:temp(?:orary)?\s+|unlogged\s+)?table\s+(?:if\s+not\s+exists\s+)?([`"[]?[\w.]+[`"\]]?)\s*\(/gi;

/** `CREATE TABLE [IF NOT EXISTS] name (cols…)` statements: table names (schema prefix dropped) and column names. */
export function parseSqlTables(sql: string): { name: string; columns: string[] }[] {
  const text = sql.replace(/--[^\n]*/g, (c) => ' '.repeat(c.length)).replace(/\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\//g, (c) => c.replace(/[^\n]/g, ' '));
  const out: { name: string; columns: string[] }[] = [];
  each(CREATE, text, (m) => {
    const name = m[1]!.replace(/[`"[\]]/g, '').split('.').pop()!;
    let depth = 1;
    let i = m.index! + m[0].length;
    const start = i;
    const parts: string[] = [];
    let from = start;
    for (; i < text.length && depth > 0; i++) {
      const c = text[i];
      if (c === '(') depth++;
      else if (c === ')') depth--;
      else if (c === "'") { i++; while (i < text.length && text[i] !== "'") i++; }
      if ((c === ',' && depth === 1) || depth === 0) {
        parts.push(text.slice(from, i));
        from = i + 1;
      }
    }
    const columns = parts.map((p) => p.trim()).filter((p) => p && !CONSTRAINT.test(p)).map((p) => /^[`"[]?([\w$]+)/.exec(p)?.[1] ?? '').filter(Boolean);
    out.push({ name, columns });
  });
  return out;
}

/** Facts for a `.sql` schema file: the tables it defines (no symbols, calls or imports). */
export function sqlFacts(path: string, source: string): FileFacts {
  return { path, hash: hashText(source), imports: [], writes: [], reads: [], tables: parseSqlTables(source), symbols: [], calls: [], routes: [], entries: [] };
}
```

```bash
/** 1-based number of the current coding session ("decided in session 2"). */
function sessionNumber(bus: Bus): number {
  const seen: string[] = [];
  for (const e of bus.events) if (!seen.includes(e.session)) seen.push(e.session);
  if (!seen.includes(bus.session)) seen.push(bus.session);
  return seen.indexOf(bus.session) + 1;
}

/** Folders Alike can anchor for a glob it can't take: `vendor/llm-*` + `/**` → `vendor/llm-anthropic/`, … */
function concreteFolders(files: readonly string[], glob: string): string[] {
  const match = globMatcher(glob);
  const depth = glob.split('/').findIndex((seg) => /[*?[{]/.test(seg));
  const out = new Set<string>();
  for (const f of files) {
    if (!match(f)) continue;
    const parts = f.split('/');
    out.add(depth >= 0 && depth < parts.length - 1 ? `${parts.slice(0, depth + 1).join('/')}/` : f);
  }
  return [...out].sort();
}

 * Returns MCP fallback instructions for any decision the CLI couldn't record.
 */
export async function recordInAlike(repo: Repo, bus: Bus, items: { id: string; decision: AlikeDecision }[], exec?: ExecFn): Promise<string[]> {
  const fallback: string[] = [];
  for (const { id, decision } of items) {
    const rel = `decisions/${id}.md`;
    const path = join(repo.root, rel);
    if (!existsSync(path)) continue;
    const before = listDecisions(repo.root).find((d) => d.id === id);
    if (before?.alike_urn) continue;
    try {
      const urn = await recordDecision(decision, exec);
      const text = readFileSync(path, 'utf8');
      writeFileSync(path, text.replace(/\\n---\\n/, `\\nalike_urn: ${urn}\\n---\\n`));
      try { commitPaths(repo.root, [rel], `docs(decisions): ${id} recorded in Alike`); } catch { /* the URN stays in the working tree */ }
      const prev = bus.events.find((e) => e.kind === 'decision_recorded' && (e.data as { id: string }).id === id);
      if (prev) bus.emit('decision_recorded', { ...(prev.data as never), alike: true, urn }, { turn: prev.turn });
    } catch (e) {
      bus.emit('error', { message: `Alike didn't record ${id} (${(e as Error).message.split('\\n')[0]}); asking the session instead.` });
      fallback.push(mcpInstruction(decision));
    }
  }
  return fallback;
}"""+s[end:]
```

```typescript
// Table reads (Scout's db.get/where/all, SQL text in db.query, Prisma/Drizzle/Kysely) and `.sql` schema tables.
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { extractFacts } from '../src/facts/extract';
import { findReads, parseSqlTables } from '../src/facts/tables';

const tables = (code: string) => findReads(code).map((r) => `${r.via}:${r.table}`);

describe('findReads', () => {
  it('finds Scout reads with literal table names, type arguments included', () => {
    expect(tables('const r = await db.get<RunRow>("runs", id);\nreturn db.where<ContactRow>("contacts", { email }, { limit: 1 });\ndb.all(\'cost_log\');')).toEqual(['db:runs', 'db:contacts', 'db:cost_log']);
    expect(tables('db.insert("runs", row); db.update("runs", id, x);')).toEqual([]); // writes are not reads
  });

  it('reads FROM/JOIN tables out of db.query SQL, in any case, across template lines', () => {
    const code = 'await db.query<Pick<ContactRow, "name">>("select name from contacts where name <> \'\'");\n'
      + 'await db.query(`select n.*, 1 - (e.vector <=> $2) as score\n   from embeddings e\n   join notes n on n.id = e.note_id`, [a]);\n'
      + 'await db.query("select * from (select 1) x");';
    expect(tables(code)).toEqual(['sql:contacts', 'sql:embeddings', 'sql:notes']);
  });

  it('reads upper-case SQL literals elsewhere, but not prose', () => {
    expect(tables('const q = `SELECT id FROM public.runs JOIN steps ON true`;')).toEqual(['sql:runs', 'sql:steps']);
    expect(tables('const msg = "select a contact from the list";')).toEqual([]);
  });

  it('finds ORM reads', () => {
    expect(tables('await prisma.user.findMany({}); await tx.post.count();')).toEqual(['prisma:user', 'prisma:post']);
    expect(tables('db.select().from(users).where(eq(users.id, 1)); db.query.posts.findFirst({});')).toEqual(['drizzle:users', 'drizzle:posts']);
    expect(tables('db.selectFrom("pets").selectAll()')).toEqual(['kysely:pets']);
  });

  it('lands in FileFacts.reads with the enclosing symbol', () => {
    const f = extractFacts('src/outreach/crm-sync.ts', 'import { db } from "../shared/db";\nexport async function contactByEmail(email: string) {\n  const [c] = await db.where("contacts", { email });\n  return c;\n}\n', () => null);
    expect(f.reads).toEqual([{ table: 'contacts', symbol: 'src/outreach/crm-sync.ts#contactByEmail', via: 'db' }]);
  });
});

  const SQL = `-- Contacts. Owned by outreach.
create sequence if not exists contacts_id_seq;
create table if not exists contacts (
```

```txt
  writeFileSync(join(dir, 'domains.yaml'), mapYaml.replace('    to: outreach\n    exceptions: []', '    to: outreach\n    exceptions: []\n    decisions: [DR-4]'));
  mkdirSync(join(dir, 'decisions'));
  writeFileSync(join(dir, 'decisions/DR-4.md'), DR4);
  git(dir, 'init', '-q');
  git(dir, 'config', 'user.email', 'test@harness');
  git(dir, 'config', 'user.name', 'test');
  git(dir, 'add', '-A');
  git(dir, 'commit', '-qm', 'fixture');
  return dir;
}

/** Fake auditor: flags any added line in a tools file that reads an outreach table, citing DR-4 — if DR-4 was sent. */
function fakeAuditor(calls: AuditInput[]): Auditor {
  return async (input) => {
    calls.push(input);
    if (!input.decisions.some((d) => d.decision.id === 'DR-4')) return { findings: [], cost: 0 };
    let path = '';
    const findings = [];
    for (const l of input.diff.split('\n')) {
      const header = /^### (\S+)/.exec(l);
      if (header) { path = header[1]!; continue; }
      const m = /^\s*(\d+) \+ (.*)$/.exec(l);
      if (m && path.startsWith('src/tools/') && /"(outreach_log|contacts)"/.test(m[2]!)) {
        findings.push({ decision: 'DR-4', files: [path], lines: [{ path, line: Number(m[1]) }], confidence: 'high' as const, text: `DR-4 says outreach history reaches the brief through the run loop; ${path}:${m[1]} reads outreach_log directly.` });
      }
    }
    return { findings, cost: 0.02 };
  };
}

function setup() {
  const root = sandbox();
  const bus = new Bus(root, { fresh: true });
  const repo = new Repo(root, bus);
  repo.loadMapFile();
  bus.emit('map_confirmed', { map: repo.map, source: 'file' }, { turn: null });
  const calls: AuditInput[] = [];
  const named: NamerInput[] = [];
  const namer: Namer = async (input) => { named.push(input); return { names: input.journeys.map((j) => ({ id: j.id, name: 'Run research from the CLI' })), cost: 0.001 }; };
  const auditor = attachAuditor({ bus, repo, auditor: fakeAuditor(calls), plans: false });
  const journeys = attachJourneys({ bus, repo, namer });
  repo.scan();
  /** A coding turn as the session drives it: baseline, hook-reported edits, numstat at turn_ended, then the turn closes. */
  const turn = (id: string, write: () => string[], during?: () => void) => {
    const base = baseline(root);
    bus.turn = id;
    bus.emit('turn_started', { prompt: `turn ${id}`, head: base.head, baseline: base.snapshot });
    for (const p of write()) repo.fileChanged(p, { tool: 'Write' });
    during?.();
    bus.emit('turn_ended', { ...numstat(root, base), reason: 'success' });
    bus.turn = null;
  };
  const put = (p: string, text: string) => () => { writeFileSync(join(root, p), text); return [p]; };
  const of = <K extends keyof EventData>(kind: K) => bus.events.filter((e): e is HarnessEvent & { data: EventData[K] } => e.kind === kind).map((e) => e.data as EventData[K]);
  const idle = async () => { await auditor.idle(); await journeys.idle(); };
  return { root, bus, repo, auditor, journeys, calls, named, turn, put, of, idle };
}
```

```text
export function harnessTools(repo: Repo, bus: Bus, hooks: PlanHooks) {
  const store = semanticStore(repo, bus);
  const rel = (p: string) => repo.rel(p);
  const cellName = (domain: string, layer: string) =>
    `${repo.map.domains.find((d) => d.id === domain)?.name ?? domain} · ${repo.map.layers.find((l) => l.id === layer)?.name ?? layer}`;

  return createSdkMcpServer({
    name: 'harness',
    version: '0.1.0',
    tools: [
      tool(
        'submit_plan',
        'Submit your implementation plan before editing anything. Numbered steps; each lists the exact repo-relative file paths it will create or modify, and every new import it adds as { from: path, to: path }. Returns the architecture footprint and any rule violations.',
        {
          steps: z.array(z.object({
            n: z.number().int(),
            text: z.string(),
            files: z.array(z.string()),
            imports: z.array(z.object({ from: z.string(), to: z.string() })).default([]),
          })),
        },
        async ({ steps }) => {
          const norm = (p: string) => repo.rel(p) ?? p.replace(/^\.\//, '');
          const clean: PlanStep[] = steps.map((s) => ({
            n: s.n, text: s.text, files: s.files.map(norm),
            imports: s.imports.map((i) => ({ from: norm(i.from), to: i.to.startsWith('.') ? i.to : norm(i.to) })),
          }));
          const exists = withExtra(repo.exists, clean.flatMap((s) => s.files));
          const fp = planFootprint(repo.map, clean, exists, repo.mapper);
          bus.emit('planned', {
            steps: clean,
            cells: fp.cells.map((c) => ({ domain: c.domain, layer: c.layer, steps: c.steps, files: c.files })),
            edges: fp.edges.map((e) => ({ from: e.from, to: e.to, steps: e.steps, imports: e.imports })),
            unassigned: fp.unassigned,
          });
          for (const v of fp.violations) bus.emit('plan_violation', { violation: v }, { path: v.file, cell: repo.cellOf(v.file) });
          hooks.onPlan(clean, fp.violations);

          const lines = [
            `Plan recorded: ${clean.length} step(s).`,
            `Cells: ${fp.cells.map((c) => `${cellName(c.domain, c.layer)} (steps ${c.steps.join(', ')})`).join('; ') || 'none'}.`,
            `New cross-domain dependencies: ${fp.edges.map((e) => `${e.from} → ${e.to}`).join('; ') || 'none'}.`,
          ];
          if (fp.unassigned.length) lines.push(`Files outside every domain: ${fp.unassigned.join(', ')}.`);
          if (fp.violations.length) {
            lines.push('', `VIOLATIONS (${fp.violations.length}):`, violationText(fp.violations), '', ASK_RULE + ' Do not exit plan mode until the user has answered and you have resubmitted the plan.');
          } else {
            lines.push('No violations. Exit plan mode when ready.');
          }
          const notes = hooks.takeNotes();
          if (notes.length) lines.push('', ...notes);
          return text(lines.join('\n'));
        },
        { alwaysLoad: true },
      ),
      tool('cell_for', 'Which domain × layer cell a repo path belongs to.', { path: z.string() }, async ({ path }) => {
        const rel = repo.rel(path) ?? path;
        const p = repo.place(rel);
        return text(p.kind === 'cell' ? `${rel} → ${cellName(p.domain, p.layer)} (${p.domain}/${p.layer})` : `${rel} → ${p.kind}${'domain' in p ? ` (${p.domain})` : ''}`);
```

```text
import type { Tool } from "../shared/types";
import { tools } from "../tools/index";

/** "Filings," -> "filing", "10-K" -> "10-k". Plural-insensitive so tags read naturally. */
export function normalizeKeyword(word: string): string {
  const w = word.toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z0-9-]/g, "");
  return w.length > 3 && w.endsWith("s") && !w.endsWith("ss") ? w.slice(0, -1) : w;
}

export class ToolRegistry {
  private readonly byName = new Map<string, Tool>();
  private readonly byTag = new Map<string, Tool[]>();

  constructor(list: Tool[]) {
    for (const tool of list) this.register(tool);
  }

  register(tool: Tool): void {
    if (!/^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$/.test(tool.name)) throw new Error(`tool name must be snake_case: "${tool.name}"`);
    if (this.byName.has(tool.name)) throw new Error(`tool registered twice: ${tool.name}`);
    this.byName.set(tool.name, tool);
    for (const tag of tool.tags) {
      const key = normalizeKeyword(tag);
      this.byTag.set(key, [...(this.byTag.get(key) ?? []), tool]);
    }
  }

  get(name: string): Tool | undefined {
    return this.byName.get(name);
  }

  has(name: string): boolean {
    return this.byName.has(name);
  }

  list(): Tool[] {
    return [...this.byName.values()];
  }

  /** One line per tool, for the planner prompt. */
  describe(): string {
    return this.list()
      .map((t) => `- ${t.name} [${t.tags.join(", ")}]: ${t.description}`)
      .join("\n");
  }

  /** Tools with a tag that appears as a word in the goal, in registration order. */
  matchGoal(goal: string): Tool[] {
    const words = new Set(goal.split(/[\s,.;:!?()"']+/).filter(Boolean).map(normalizeKeyword));
    const matched = new Set<Tool>();
    for (const word of words) {
      for (const tool of this.byTag.get(word) ?? []) matched.add(tool);
    }
    return this.list().filter((t) => matched.has(t));
  }
}

export const registry = new ToolRegistry(tools);
```

```bash
## Verified capabilities and what was built (Oct 11, later)

Checked read-only against Alike's MCP schemas, the paired CLI, the installed runtime (`@alikeai/setup` 0.2.1, `~/.alike/runtime/*`) and alike.help.

| Question | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| Globs or folders in path anchors? | **Folders, not globs.** `'dir/'` matches a boundary-safe prefix (`hook.mjs` `isAtOrUnder`), new files included. `src/tools/**` would never match. |
| Server-side recording? | **Yes:** the paired CLI (`alike it "<title>" --json '{…}'`) or `POST https://alike.network/api-general/mcp` with the device token. The token covers 5 tools only: `record_decision`, `get_entity`, `get_briefing`, `resolve_work_item`, `inspect_injections`. |
| Repository identity in hooks? | The `origin` remote reduced to `owner/name`, **lowercased**. With no remote, Alike falls back to the bare folder name, which can't hold path anchors. A remote that isn't reachable is fine. |
| Update / supersede / delete? | `update_entity(status:'superseded')` and `dismiss_entity` work through **MCP only**. There's no delete, and **no dedupe** for decisions. |
| Read back by repository? | No server-side filter. `list_entities` or `query_entities` (MCP only) can be filtered by `anchors[].repository` client-side. With the device token, only `get_entity(urn)`. |
| Stable URL? | No per-item web URL is documented. The URN (`urn:alike:decision:<hex>`) is stable. |
| Situation anchors? | Accepted and matched on the server. Prompt grounding works mostly from the title, so put the principle in it. |
| **Blocker** | With transcript capture off for Claude (`capture_harnesses: []`), Alike's hooks are **completely silent**, including injection. The teammate moment needs `npx @alikeai/setup --capture=claude`. |

**Built (commit "record decisions in Alike from the server"):**
- The server records with `alike it` after the DR commit, never in the turn.
- Anchors: the cell folders of both sides of the invariant (`governs` / `context`), plus an `applies_when` situation.
- The title states the principle; the rationale names the refined rule and the rejected option.
- `alike_urn:` is written into the DR file and committed, so a decision is recorded once.
- `decision_recorded { alike: true, urn }` is emitted.
- The MCP instruction is kept as a fallback.
- `repoSlug` follows Alike: `HARNESS_REPO_SLUG`, or origin, lowercased; there's no git-user fallback any more.

- reading foreign decisions (needs an MCP client in the server);
- supersede on rule changes (MCP).
```

```text
  takeNotes(): string[];

export type PlanInput = {
  steps: { n: number; text: string; files: string[]; imports: { from: string; to: string }[] }[];
  avoided?: { from: string; to: string; decision: string; reason: string }[];
};

/** `submit_plan`: footprint, plan check (the one checker), `planned` + `plan_violation` events, and the tool's reply. */
export function submitPlan(repo: Repo, bus: Bus, hooks: PlanHooks, { steps, avoided: avoidedIn }: PlanInput): string {
  const cellName = (domain: string, layer: string) =>
    `${repo.map.domains.find((d) => d.id === domain)?.name ?? domain} · ${repo.map.layers.find((l) => l.id === layer)?.name ?? layer}`;
  const norm = (p: string) => repo.rel(p) ?? p.replace(/^\.\//, '');
  const clean: PlanStep[] = steps.map((s) => ({
    n: s.n, text: s.text, files: s.files.map(norm),
    imports: s.imports.map((i) => ({ from: norm(i.from), to: i.to.startsWith('.') ? i.to : norm(i.to) })),
  }));
  const exists = withExtra(repo.exists, clean.flatMap((s) => s.files));
  const fp = planFootprint(repo.map, clean, exists, repo.mapper);
  // Avoided approaches must cite a decision that exists in decisions/; unknown ids are dropped (and said so).
  const known = new Set(listDecisions(repo.root).map((d) => d.id));
  const end = (x: string) => (x.startsWith('domain:') ? x : norm(x));
  const avoided = (avoidedIn ?? []).filter((a) => known.has(a.decision.trim())).map((a) => ({ from: end(a.from), to: end(a.to), decision: a.decision.trim(), reason: a.reason }));
  const dropped = (avoidedIn ?? []).filter((a) => !known.has(a.decision.trim()));
  bus.emit('planned', {
    steps: clean,
    cells: fp.cells.map((c) => ({ domain: c.domain, layer: c.layer, steps: c.steps, files: c.files })),
    edges: fp.edges.map((e) => ({ from: e.from, to: e.to, steps: e.steps, imports: e.imports })),
    unassigned: fp.unassigned,
    ...(avoided.length ? { avoided } : {}),
  });
  for (const v of fp.violations) bus.emit('plan_violation', { violation: v }, { path: v.file, cell: repo.cellOf(v.file) });
  hooks.onPlan(clean, fp.violations);

  const lines = [
    `Plan recorded: ${clean.length} step(s).`,
    `Cells: ${fp.cells.map((c) => `${cellName(c.domain, c.layer)} (steps ${c.steps.join(', ')})`).join('; ') || 'none'}.`,
    `New cross-domain dependencies: ${fp.edges.map((e) => `${e.from} → ${e.to}`).join('; ') || 'none'}.`,
  ];
  if (fp.unassigned.length) lines.push(`Files outside every domain: ${fp.unassigned.join(', ')}.`);
  if (avoided.length) lines.push(`Avoided (per standing decisions): ${avoided.map((a) => `${a.from} → ${a.to} (${a.decision})`).join('; ')}.`);
  if (dropped.length) lines.push(`Not recorded as avoided (no such decision in decisions/): ${dropped.map((a) => `${a.from} → ${a.to} (${a.decision})`).join('; ')}.`);
  const { open, decided } = splitDecided(fp.violations);
  if (open.length) {
    lines.push('', `VIOLATIONS (${open.length}):`, violationText(open), '', ASK_RULE + ' Do not exit plan mode until the user has answered and you have resubmitted the plan.');
  }
  if (decided.length) {
    lines.push('', `ALREADY DECIDED (${decided.length}):`, ...decided.map((v) => v.reason), decidedText(repo.root, decided),
      'Do not exit plan mode until a resubmitted plan no longer crosses it.');
  }
  if (!fp.violations.length) lines.push('No violations. Exit plan mode when ready.');
  const notes = hooks.takeNotes();
  if (notes.length) lines.push('', ...notes);
  return lines.join('\n');
}
```

```typescript
// Syntactic stand-ins for dispatch that Tier 1 call facts can't see, so journeys can pass through registries and
// module-level clients (NAVIGATION_PLAN §3.1 "Tier 2" will produce typed `implements` and calls; when its edges are in the
// graph they are used as they are). Pure and browser-safe; used only for journeys, never by the gate or the map.
import type { FileFacts, SymbolFact } from '../contracts/facts';
import type { SourceFile } from './fetches';

/** An edge journeys add on a copy of the graph: interface dispatch (`calls` to a member, `implements` from each implementation) or a call through a module-level instance. */
export type InferredEdge = { kind: 'calls' | 'implements'; from: string; to: string; confidence: 'dispatch' | 'inferred' };

const last = (name: string) => name.slice(name.lastIndexOf('.') + 1);
const esc = (s: string) => s.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, '\\$&');

function innermost(symbols: readonly SymbolFact[], at: number): SymbolFact | null {
  let best: SymbolFact | null = null;
  for (const s of symbols) {
    if (s.kind === 'type' || s.span.end <= s.span.start || at < s.span.start || at >= s.span.end) continue;
    if (!best || s.span.end - s.span.start < best.span.end - best.span.start) best = s;
  }
  return best;
}

/**
 * 1. **Interface dispatch.** A method member `I.m` of an interface/type with at least two implementations — methods named
 *    `m` on a const or class in a file that is I's file or imports it — becomes a hub: each implementation `implements`
 *    it, and every symbol whose own code calls `.m(` from a file that imports I's file (directly or through one file)
 *    `calls` it (confidence `dispatch`). Scout: `runAgent` → `Tool.run` → each tool's `run`; `complete` → `ChatProvider.chat`.
 * 2. **Module-level instances.** `const client = new Anthropic()` at the top of a file: a symbol in that file that uses
 *    `client.` calls what the instance was made from (confidence `inferred`). Scout: `newsSummarize.run` → `Anthropic`.
 * Deterministic: edges sorted and deduplicated.
 */
export function inferDispatch(files: readonly SourceFile[], facts: Readonly<Record<string, FileFacts>>): InferredEdge[] {
  const out = new Map<string, InferredEdge>();
  const add = (e: InferredEdge) => { if (e.from !== e.to) out.set(`${e.kind}|${e.from}|${e.to}`, e); };
  const byId = new Map(Object.values(facts).flatMap((f) => f.symbols.map((s) => [s.id, s] as const)));
  const imports = (path: string) => new Set((facts[path]?.imports ?? []).map((i) => i.to));
  const sees = (path: string, target: string) => {
    if (path === target) return true;
    const direct = imports(path);
    return direct.has(target) || [...direct].some((d) => imports(d).has(target));
  };

  // 1. interface members with ≥ 2 implementations
  const members = Object.values(facts).flatMap((f) => f.symbols.filter((s) => s.kind === 'method' && s.parent && byId.get(s.parent)?.kind === 'type'));
  for (const member of members.sort((a, b) => (a.id < b.id ? -1 : 1))) {
    const m = last(member.name);
    const impls = Object.values(facts).filter((f) => f.path === member.file || imports(f.path).has(member.file)).flatMap((f) => f.symbols.filter((s) => {
      const owner = s.parent ? byId.get(s.parent) : undefined;
      return s.kind === 'method' && last(s.name) === m && s.id !== member.id && !!owner && (owner.kind === 'const' || owner.kind === 'class');
    }));
    if (impls.length < 2) continue;
    for (const s of impls) add({ kind: 'implements', from: s.id, to: member.id, confidence: 'dispatch' });
    const call = new RegExp(`\\??\\.\\s*${esc(m)}\\s*\\(`, 'g');
    for (const file of files) {
      if (!sees(file.path, member.file)) continue;
      for (const hit of file.source.matchAll(call)) {
        const at = innermost(file.symbols, hit.index);
        if (at && !impls.some((s) => s.id === at.id) && at.id !== member.id) add({ kind: 'calls', from: at.id, to: member.id, confidence: 'dispatch' });
      }
    }
  }

  // 2. module-level instances
  for (const file of files) {
    const f = facts[file.path];
    if (!f) continue;
    for (const d of file.source.matchAll(/^(?:export\s+)?(?:const|let|var)\s+([A-Za-z_$][\w$]*)\s*(?::[^=\n]+)?=\s*new\s+([A-Za-z_$][\w$]*)/gm)) {
      if (innermost(file.symbols, d.index)) continue; // only top-level declarations
      const [, v, ctor] = d as unknown as [string, string, string];
      const target = f.calls.find((c) => c.from === file.path && (c.to.endsWith(`#${ctor}`) || c.to.endsWith(`.${ctor}`)))?.to;
      if (!target) continue;
      for (const use of file.source.matchAll(new RegExp(`(?<![\\w$.])${esc(v)}\\s*\\??\\.`, 'g'))) {
        const at = innermost(file.symbols, use.index);
        if (at) add({ kind: 'calls', from: at.id, to: target, confidence: 'inferred' });
      }
    }
  }
  return [...out.values()].sort((a, b) => (`${a.kind}|${a.from}|${a.to}` < `${b.kind}|${b.from}|${b.to}` ? -1 : 1));
}
```

```text
140	      if (i === 0 || i >= p.length) continue;
141	      branches.push({ from: prefix.length + i - 1, steps: p.slice(i) });
142	    }
143	
144	    const slug = journeySlug(entry);
145	    const n = (used.get(slug) ?? 0) + 1;
146	    used.set(slug, n);
147	    out.push({
148	      id: `journey:${n > 1 ? `${slug}-${n}` : slug}`,
149	      name: route ? `${route.method} ${route.path}` : `${entry.kind} ${entry.label}`,
150	      inferred: true,
151	      entry: entry.id,
152	      steps,
153	      branches,
154	    });
155	  }
156	  return out.sort((a, b) => byId(a.id, b.id));
157	}
```

On the name: you want a word that works as an ordinary noun ("I'm building ___"), not a brand. The two strongest:

- **Oversight:** "I'm building oversight for coding agents." This is my pick. It's an everyday word, it names the human's new job in your thesis (supervising the agent instead of writing the code), and "sight" fits the map. It's easy to say on stage.
- **Interpretability:** "I'm building interpretability for coding agents." It's sharper for an AI-literate audience because it borrows a known research word and applies it to code. It needs "for coding agents" attached, or people will hear model interpretability.

They combine well in the pitch: "I'm building oversight for coding agents: human interpretability for the code they write."

On timing, agreed: the rename waits until the harness build session finishes. To make that quick, I wrote `RENAME.md` in the harness repo. It covers:
- **Two decisions first:**
  - The public noun, checked against existing products before it goes on a slide.

- **Size:** about 60 source files and hundreds of code references, so it really can't happen while three lanes edit those files. Scout itself needs no changes.
- **Done-when checks:** tests and typecheck pass, `npm run demo` works, a full plan, fork and build turn runs with the renamed tools, and a search finds only the leftovers you chose to keep.

```typescript
// Dev only. A synthetic 500-file repo as a real event log (map_confirmed + repo_scanned with Tier 1 facts), so the
// v2 renderer can be measured through the whole pipeline (reduce → graphOf → activityFor → project → ELK → React Flow):
//   npx tsx apps/shell/scripts/bench-events.ts [files]   →  /?fake=bench, then window.__v2.zoom() / .toggle('d0')
import { writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { dirname, join } from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import type { DomainMap, FileFacts, HarnessEvent } from '@harness/core/view';

const here = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
const N = Number(process.argv[2] ?? 500);
let seed = 7;
const rnd = () => (seed = (seed * 1664525 + 1013904223) >>> 0) / 2 ** 32;

const LAYERS = ['ui', 'entry', 'logic', 'data', 'external'];
const NAMES = ['Channels', 'Agent loop', 'Research tools', 'Model gateway', 'Memory', 'Outreach'];
const map = {
  version: 1,
  layers: LAYERS.map((id) => ({ id, name: id[0]!.toUpperCase() + id.slice(1) })),
  neutral: [],
  ignore: [],
  domains: NAMES.map((name, i) => ({ id: `d${i}`, name, purpose: 'Synthetic', cells: Object.fromEntries(LAYERS.map((l) => [l, { paths: [`src/d${i}/${l}/**`] }])) })),
  invariants: [],
} as unknown as DomainMap;

const files: { path: string; d: number; l: number }[] = [];
for (let i = 0; i < N; i++) {
  const d = i % 3;
  const l = Math.floor(rnd() * LAYERS.length);
  files.push({ path: `src/d${d}/${LAYERS[l]}/f${String(i).padStart(4, '0')}.ts`, d, l });
}
for (let i = 0; i < 60; i++) files.push({ path: `src/d${3 + (i % 3)}/${LAYERS[i % 5]}/o${i}.ts`, d: 3 + (i % 3), l: i % 5 });
files.sort((a, b) => a.path.localeCompare(b.path));

const facts: FileFacts[] = files.map((f) => {
  const imports = new Set<string>();
  const k = 1 + Math.floor(rnd() * 2);
  for (let j = 0; j < k; j++) {
    // mostly inside the same cell, sometimes another cell or domain
    const r = rnd();
    const pool = r < 0.7 ? files.filter((g) => g.d === f.d && g.l === f.l) : r < 0.9 ? files.filter((g) => g.d === f.d) : files;
    const t = pool[Math.floor(rnd() * pool.length)]!;
    if (t.path !== f.path) imports.add(t.path);
  }
  return { path: f.path, hash: `h${f.path}`, imports: [...imports].map((to) => ({ to, typeOnly: false })), writes: [], symbols: [], calls: [], routes: [], entries: [] };
});

const ev = (n: number, kind: HarnessEvent['kind'], data: Record<string, unknown>): HarnessEvent => ({ id: `bench-${n}`, t: 1000 + n, session: 'bench', turn: null, kind, data });
const out: HarnessEvent[] = [
  ev(0, 'map_confirmed', { map, source: 'fixture' }),
  ev(1, 'repo_scanned', {
    files: files.map((f) => ({ path: f.path, placement: { kind: 'cell', domain: `d${f.d}`, layer: LAYERS[f.l] } })),
    imports: [], writes: [], edges: [], fileFacts: facts,
  }),
];
writeFileSync(join(here, '../public/bench-events.json'), JSON.stringify(out));
console.log(`${files.length} files, ${facts.reduce((s, f) => s + f.imports.length, 0)} imports → public/bench-events.json`);
```

```txt
/** Most branches kept per journey (deterministic order: by divergence point, then by steps). */
export const MAX_BRANCHES = 16;
/** Most outside-service sinks traced one by one (trace stops after MAX_TRACE_PATHS sinks; deep services need their own run). */
const MAX_DEEP_SINKS = 50;

/**
 * One journey per entry, sorted by id.
 * - Route entries start at the route; when UI code fetches it, the journey starts there instead: the UI symbol that calls
 *   the fetch site (`page`), the site (`fetch`), then the route. Only the first site (syntactic before inferred, then by id)
 *   is drawn; a route nobody fetches starts at the route.
 * - Other entries start at the entry, then its symbol (or file).
 * - Paths come from core `trace` over calls ∪ handles ∪ implements, plus the fetch → route links and `inferred` dispatch
 *   edges (see dispatch.ts), on a copy of the graph: the nearest sinks, plus each outside service traced on its own.
 * - The main path is the best one by: most domains crossed, then ending at an outside service rather than a table, then
 *   length. When the flow reaches a dispatch hub (an interface member with several implementations, e.g. a tool
 *   registry's `Tool.run`), the main path goes through the hub and its best implementation, and every other
 *   implementation's best path is a branch at the hub. Other paths are branches where they leave the main path.
 * - A route that reaches no sink still shows its handler and what it calls.
 * Step confidence is that of the edge into the step (`handles` and the first step: syntactic; dispatch: `dispatch`;
 * an inferred instance call or a fetch link: its confidence).
 */
export function computeJourneys(graph: ContextGraph, facts: Readonly<Record<string, FileFacts>>, sites: readonly FetchSite[] = [], inferred: readonly InferredEdge[] = []): Journey[] {
  const links = linkFetches(sites, facts).filter((l) => graph.nodes[l.site.from] && graph.nodes[l.route.id]);
  const known = (e: { from: string; to: string }) => !!graph.nodes[e.from] && !!graph.nodes[e.to];
  // Fetch links ride along as `handles` edges so `trace` walks them; inferred dispatch as calls/implements. Never shown.
  const extra: GraphEdge[] = [
    ...links.map((l): GraphEdge => ({ id: edgeId('fetches', l.site.from, l.route.id), kind: 'handles', from: l.site.from, to: l.route.id, count: 1, owner: l.site.file })),
    ...inferred.filter(known).map((e): GraphEdge => ({ id: edgeId(e.kind, e.from, e.to), kind: e.kind, from: e.from, to: e.to, count: 1, owner: '', confidence: 'dispatch' })),
  ];
  const g: ContextGraph = extra.length ? { ...graph, edges: [...graph.edges, ...extra] } : graph;
  const sinks = journeySinks(graph);
  const deep = sinks.filter((s) => !s.startsWith('table:')).slice(0, MAX_DEEP_SINKS);

  const conf = new Map<string, StepConfidence>();
  const key = (a: string, b: string) => `${a}\u0000${b}`;
  const callers = new Map<string, string[]>();
  const callees = new Map<string, string[]>();
  const impls = new Map<string, string[]>(); // interface member → implementations
  for (const e of g.edges) {
    if (e.kind === 'calls') {
      if (!conf.has(key(e.from, e.to))) conf.set(key(e.from, e.to), e.confidence ?? 'syntactic');
      (callers.get(e.to) ?? callers.set(e.to, []).get(e.to)!).push(e.from);
      (callees.get(e.from) ?? callees.set(e.from, []).get(e.from)!).push(e.to);
    } else if (e.kind === 'handles') conf.set(key(e.from, e.to), 'syntactic');
    else if (e.kind === 'implements') {
      conf.set(key(e.to, e.from), 'dispatch');
      (impls.get(e.to) ?? impls.set(e.to, []).get(e.to)!).push(e.from);
    }
  }
  for (const e of inferred) if (e.kind === 'calls' && known(e)) conf.set(key(e.from, e.to), e.confidence);
  for (const l of links) conf.set(key(l.site.from, l.route.id), l.confidence);
  const siteIds = new Set(links.map((l) => l.site.from));
  const hubs = [...impls].filter(([, list]) => list.length >= 2).map(([h]) => h).sort(byId);

  /** Paths from `from` to sinks: the nearest few, plus one per outside service. Deduplicated, in a stable order. */
  const reach = (from: string): string[][] => {
    const all = [...trace(g, from, sinks), ...deep.flatMap((s) => trace(g, from, [s]))];
    return [...new Map(all.map((p) => [p.join('\n'), p])).values()];
  };
  const domains = (p: string[]) => new Set(p.map((id) => graph.nodes[id]?.domain).filter(Boolean)).size;
  const better = (a: string[], b: string[]) => {
    const d = domains(a) - domains(b);
    if (d) return d > 0;
    const v = (a.at(-1)!.startsWith('table:') ? 0 : 1) - (b.at(-1)!.startsWith('table:') ? 0 : 1);
    if (v) return v > 0;
    if (a.length !== b.length) return a.length > b.length;
    return a.join('\n') < b.join('\n');
  };
  const best = (ps: string[][]) => ps.reduce<string[] | null>((m, p) => (!m || better(p, m) ? p : m), null);

  const routes = new Map(Object.values(facts).flatMap((f) => f.routes).map((r) => [`entry:route:${r.method} ${r.path}`, r]));
  const entries = [...new Map(Object.values(facts).flatMap((f) => f.entries).map((e) => [e.id, e])).values()].sort((a, b) => byId(a.id, b.id));
  const used = new Map<string, number>();
  const out: Journey[] = [];

  for (const entry of entries) {
    const prefix: { node: string; kind: JourneyStepKind }[] = [];
    let start: string;
    const route = entry.kind === 'route' ? routes.get(entry.id) : undefined;
    if (route && graph.nodes[route.id]) {
      start = route.id;
      const hits = links.filter((l) => l.route.id === route.id)
        .sort((a, b) => (a.confidence === b.confidence ? 0 : a.confidence === 'syntactic' ? -1 : 1) || byId(a.site.from, b.site.from));
      const first = hits[0];
      if (first) {
        const page = pageFor(graph, callers, first.site.from);
        if (page) prefix.push({ node: page, kind: 'page' });
        prefix.push({ node: first.site.from, kind: 'fetch' });
      }
    } else {
      start = entry.symbol && graph.nodes[entry.symbol] ? entry.symbol : entry.file;
      prefix.push({ node: entry.id, kind: 'entry' });
    }

    // Where the flow starts: the start itself, or (an entry file with no top-level calls, e.g. a page whose component
    // isn't the default export) its first exported symbol that reaches anything, components first.
    let head = [start];
    let paths = graph.nodes[start] ? reach(start) : [];
    if (!paths.length && graph.nodes[start]?.kind === 'file') {
      const own = (graph.children[start] ?? []).filter((id) => graph.nodes[id]!.kind === 'symbol' && graph.nodes[id]!.symbol?.exported)
        .sort((a, b) => (graph.nodes[a]!.symbol!.kind === 'component' ? 0 : 1) - (graph.nodes[b]!.symbol!.kind === 'component' ? 0 : 1) || graph.nodes[a]!.order - graph.nodes[b]!.order);
      for (const id of own) {
        const found = reach(id);
        if (found.length) { paths = found; head = [start, id]; break; }
      }
    }
    const from = head.at(-1)!;

    // Through a dispatch hub: the hub's best implementation is the main path; the other implementations are branches.
    const alternatives: string[][] = [...paths];
    let main = best(paths);
    const toHub = hubs.length && graph.nodes[from] ? trace(g, from, hubs)[0] : undefined;
    if (toHub) {
      const viaImpl = (impls.get(toHub.at(-1)!) ?? []).slice().sort(byId)
        .map((i) => best(reach(i)))
        .filter((p): p is string[] => !!p)
        .map((p) => [...toHub, ...p]);
      const hubMain = best(viaImpl);
      if (hubMain && (!main || domains(hubMain) >= domains(main))) main = hubMain;
      alternatives.push(...viaImpl);
    }
    // No sink reached (reads aren't walked): a route still shows its handler and what it calls.
    main ??= route?.handler && graph.nodes[route.handler] && start === route.id ? [start, ...followCalls(graph, callees, route.handler)] : [from];

    const nodes = [...prefix.map((p) => p.node), ...head.slice(0, -1), ...main];
    const offset = nodes.length - main.length;
    const steps: Journey['steps'] = nodes.map((node, i) => {
      const pre = prefix[i];
      const isPage = entry.kind === 'page' && (i === prefix.length || (i === prefix.length + 1 && graph.nodes[node]?.symbol?.kind === 'component'));
      const kind: JourneyStepKind = pre?.kind ?? stepKind(graph, node, siteIds, isPage);
      const into = i === 0 ? 'syntactic' : (conf.get(key(nodes[i - 1]!, node)) ?? 'syntactic');
      return { node, kind, confidence: into };
    });
    const branches = new Map<string, Journey['branches'][number]>();
    for (const p of alternatives) {
      let i = 0;
      while (i < p.length && i < main.length && p[i] === main[i]) i++;
      if (i === 0 || i >= p.length) continue;
      const b = { from: offset + i - 1, steps: p.slice(i) };
      branches.set(`${b.from}\n${b.steps.join('\n')}`, b);
    }

    const slug = journeySlug(entry);
    const n = (used.get(slug) ?? 0) + 1;
    used.set(slug, n);
    out.push({
      id: `journey:${n > 1 ? `${slug}-${n}` : slug}`,
      name: route ? `${route.method} ${route.path}` : `${entry.kind} ${entry.label}`,
      inferred: true,
      entry: entry.id,
      steps,
      branches: [...branches.values()].sort((a, b) => a.from - b.from || byId(a.steps.join('\n'), b.steps.join('\n'))).slice(0, MAX_BRANCHES),
    });
  }
  return out.sort((a, b) => byId(a.id, b.id));
}
```

```mjs
}

// 3. the real Scout copy (live server), Research tools open

await browser.close();
```

  ## What was built

  - **Resolvers:** the `SemanticResolver` interface (`declarationsAt(file, positions)` and `update(changes)`) has two implementations:
    - TS 7 `typescript/unstable/sync`, pinned to exactly 7.0.2 and installed under the alias `typescript-7`, so the repo's own `tsc` stays on 5.9.
    - TS 6 through ts-morph 28, used automatically when TS 7 fails to load. `HARNESS_SEMANTIC_IMPL` can force either one.
  - **Resolution:** oxc finds every call and `new` site, attributed to the innermost Tier 1 symbol, plus every implementation site (`implements`, `extends`, `const x: I = {…}`, `satisfies I`). Answers are expressed as Tier 1 ids:
    - calls `typed`, or `dispatch` when the target is an interface, type-literal or abstract member;
    - `implements` edges.
  - **What Tier 2 keeps from Tier 1:** Tier 2 calls replace a file's syntactic calls in `buildGraph`. So it keeps Tier 1's vendor and table calls, and Tier 1's guesses inside symbols where the checker gave up.
  - **Runtime:** it runs in a forked child with a heap cap (`HARNESS_SEMANTIC_HEAP`, default 1536 MB).
    - On load it resolves file by file in the background.
    - Edits are debounced per file (150 ms) and batched into one snapshot update; the edited files and their importers are re-resolved.
    - Results are delivered only for the file's current hash. `HARNESS_SEMANTIC=0` turns it off.
  - **One Tier 1 change:** abstract methods are now symbols, so they can be dispatch targets.

  - `semantic.ts`: `repo_scanned` triggers a full load and `facts_changed` triggers an update. Results come back as `facts_resolved` events. Status is broadcast as an ephemeral `{type: 'semantic'}` message and served at `/api/semantic`.
    - `SemanticStore` caches `buildGraph(map, facts, semantic)` for the graph tools and the living map.
  - **Graph tools** in `harness-tools.ts` (implementation in `graph-tools.ts`): `graph_neighbors(id, kinds?, hops?)`, `trace(from, to?)` and `symbols_in(path)`.

  - I added `test/semantic-repo` to the exclude list in `packages/core/tsconfig.json`, and appended exports to `index.ts`. I edited `src/facts.ts` (`scanRepoFacts` now includes `.sql` files); the integrator asked for this, but that file belongs to the N1 lane.

  ## Risks
  - **TS 7 API:** it is unstable until 7.1, so it is pinned and accessed through local structural types. It reports paths in lower case on macOS; I compare in lower case and take the real path from `getSourceFile()`.
  - **Memory:** tsgo's Go process is not under the child's heap cap.
  - **Load vs. edits:** an edit made during the initial load waits until the load finishes, because the worker handles one message at a time.
  - **Relink cost:** relink runs synchronously on the main thread when exports or symbol names change. It is capped at 200 files, at about 0.5–1 ms each.
  - **ts-morph fallback:** it compiles files outside the root tsconfig (e.g. Scout's `web/`) with the root options, which gives 14 unresolved sites on Scout.
  - **Event volume:** load emits one `facts_resolved` per file, so large repos will grow the event log.
  - **Onboarding scoring:** candidates are scored without a churn term and without a margin over the skeleton; the lowest total wins.

```bash
  'src/registry.ts': 'import { a } from "./tools/a";\nimport { b } from "./tools/b";\nexport const tools = [a, b];\n',
  'src/agent.ts': 'import type { Tool } from "./types";\nimport { tools } from "./registry";\nexport async function runAgent(name: string) {\n  const tool: Tool | undefined = tools.find((t) => t.name === name);\n  return tool?.run(name);\n}\n',
  'src/gateway.ts': 'import { Client } from "../vendor/llm/index";\nexport function complete(text: string) {\n  return new Client().chat(text);\n}\n',
  'src/cli.ts': 'import { runAgent } from "./agent";\nvoid runAgent(process.argv[2] ?? "a");\n',
  'vendor/llm/index.ts': 'export class Client {\n  chat(text: string) { return text; }\n}\n',
};
const REGISTRY_MAP = `
version: 1
layers: [{ id: entry, name: Entry }, { id: logic, name: Logic }, { id: external, name: External }]
neutral: ["src/types.ts"]
domains:
  - { id: agent, name: Agent loop, purpose: Runs, cells: { entry: { paths: ["src/cli.ts"] }, logic: { paths: ["src/agent.ts", "src/registry.ts"] } } }
  - { id: tools, name: Tools, purpose: Tools, cells: { logic: { paths: ["src/tools/**"] } } }
  - { id: gateway, name: Gateway, purpose: Models, cells: { logic: { paths: ["src/gateway.ts"] }, external: { paths: ["vendor/llm/**"] } } }
`;

describe('computeJourneys through a registry (inferred dispatch)', () => {
  const root = mkdtempSync(join(process.env.HARNESS_TEST_TMP ?? tmpdir(), 'harness-registry-'));
  dirs.push(root);
  for (const [p, text] of Object.entries(REGISTRY_REPO)) { mkdirSync(dirname(join(root, p)), { recursive: true }); writeFileSync(join(root, p), text); }
  const map = parseDomainMap(REGISTRY_MAP);
  const { fileFacts } = scanRepoFacts(root, map);
  const sources = Object.values(fileFacts).map((f) => ({ path: f.path, source: REGISTRY_REPO[f.path]!, symbols: f.symbols }));

  it('infers interface dispatch (declared implementations only) and calls through a module-level client', () => {
    expect(inferDispatch(sources, fileFacts).map((e) => `${e.kind} ${e.from} → ${e.to} (${e.confidence})`)).toEqual([
      'calls src/agent.ts#runAgent → src/types.ts#Tool.run (dispatch)',
      'calls src/tools/b.ts#b.run → vendor/llm/index.ts#Client (inferred)',
      'implements src/tools/a.ts#a.run → src/types.ts#Tool.run (dispatch)',
      'implements src/tools/b.ts#b.run → src/types.ts#Tool.run (dispatch)',
    ]);
  });

  it('the main path goes through the registry and the best tool; the other tool is a branch at the hub', () => {
    const js = computeJourneys(buildGraph(map, fileFacts), fileFacts, [], inferDispatch(sources, fileFacts));
    expect(js.map((j) => j.id)).toEqual(['journey:cli-agent']);
    const [j] = js;
    expect(j!.steps.map((s) => `${s.kind}/${s.confidence} ${s.node}`)).toEqual([
      'entry/syntactic entry:cli:agent',
      'symbol/syntactic src/cli.ts',
      'symbol/syntactic src/agent.ts#runAgent',
      'symbol/dispatch src/types.ts#Tool.run',
      'symbol/dispatch src/tools/a.ts#a.run',
      'symbol/syntactic src/gateway.ts#complete',
      'vendor/syntactic vendor/llm/index.ts#Client',
    ]);
    expect(j!.branches).toEqual([{ from: 3, steps: ['src/tools/b.ts#b.run', 'vendor/llm/index.ts#Client'] }]);
    // Without inferred edges the flow stops at the agent: nothing past the dynamic call is visible.
    expect(computeJourneys(buildGraph(map, fileFacts), fileFacts)[0]!.steps.map((s) => s.node).at(-1)).not.toBe('vendor/llm/index.ts#Client');
  });
});
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-11 21:54:09Z)**_

Yes, it's architectural. And to be precise, the feature isn't rejected, only one way of building it. You still get the personalized opener; what memory blocks is building it as a research tool that reads outreach data.

**Why that matters in Scout:** the two areas handle very different data.
- **Research tools** handle public information about the company (filings, news, web results). Their output is sent to model providers, and it's saved as notes.
- **Outreach** holds private customer data: contacts' names, emails, phone numbers, and the bodies of emails you've sent.

**What actually goes wrong if a research tool reads past emails:**
1. **Private data leaks across contacts.** Every tool's output is saved as a note filed by company, not by contact, and the next research run on that company retrieves those notes. Your emails with Maya at Symbotic would turn up in a colleague's brief about a different Symbotic contact.
2. **It goes out to model providers.** Tool output feeds the brief and the planner's model calls. And as the news summarizer shows, a tool can call the model directly and skip redaction entirely.
3. **The planner pulls it in automatically.** Tools are chosen by matching words in the goal, so any goal mentioning "email" would bring private outreach data into research without anyone deciding to.
4. **The dependency points the wrong way.** Research would depend on CRM and email internals, so a change to the outreach tables could break research tools. That edge is exactly what DR-3 ("research tools never depend on outreach") exists to stop.

**The decided approach:** the run loop already knows who the contact is and coordinates everything. It hands outreach context only to the parts that should have it, here the email draft, which goes through the gateway's redaction. The private data then follows one path, in one place, which you can see on the map and audit.

**So on camera:**
- **Beat 3:** you set the principle. Say the reason in one breath when you choose A: "A. Research tools never touch customer data; the run loop decides where it goes."
- **Beat 4:** a different feature asks for the same shape, a research tool reading emails. Memory blocks that approach and builds the opener the decided way.

The weak spot in the current plan is that it states the rule without the reason, so a viewer could read it as arbitrary. Should I add the one-line reason to beat 3's answer and DR-4's rationale in `DEMO_PLAN.md`? The rationale is what Alike stores and shows on screen.

```mts
/** Tells the brief whether we've already emailed this contact, and when. */

  name: "contact_history",
  tags: ["outreach", "history", "emailed", "follow-up"],
  description: "Checks whether we've already emailed this contact and summarizes what we sent.",

  async run(input) {
    const [contact] = await db.where<{ id: string }>("contacts", { email: input.contact.email }, { limit: 1 });
    if (!contact) return { tool: this.name, summary: "We haven't emailed this contact before.", facts: [], sources: [] };
    const sent = await db.where<OutreachRow>("outreach_log", { contactId: contact.id, status: "sent" }, { orderBy: "createdAt desc", limit: 3 });
    if (sent.length === 0) return { tool: this.name, summary: "No emails sent to this contact yet.", facts: [], sources: [] };
    return {
      tool: this.name,
      summary: \`Emailed \${sent.length} time(s); last on \${sent[0]!.sentAt?.slice(0, 10)}: "\${sent[0]!.subject}".\`,
      facts: sent.map((row) => \`\${row.sentAt?.slice(0, 10)}: \${row.subject}\`),
      sources: sent.map((row) => \`outreach_log/\${row.id}\`),
    };
  },
};

writeFileSync(join(root, 'src/tools/index.ts'), idx);
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-11 21:56:57Z)**_

You're right, and that's a better frame. The map's strength is showing that a change duplicates something that already exists, or breaks how the system is put together. Privacy was my justification for the rule, not the point. Recast that way, each beat is about one idea: each capability has one home, and the map shows when a change would create a second one.

**Something Alike just surfaced in this session, which matters here:** it already holds a decision, apparently from the other session's test runs: "Rejected: allow filing-summarize to call OpenAI directly. Use the gateway with filings-specific redaction instead." It also holds a task to route `news_summarize` through the gateway. Two consequences:
- An agent arrived at exactly this architectural decision on its own while testing, which suggests the arc below is natural.
- That memory would be fed into the demo's sessions and could pre-empt the beats. So the per-take repository names the other session just added (`--take`) aren't optional: record every take and every baseline under a fresh one.

**The arc reframed around redundancy and architecture:**

| Beat | You do | The tempting plan | What the map and memory show |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 Ask | "Who in Scout calls the model provider?" | (a question) | Three callers where there should be one: the gateway, `news-summarize.ts`'s own client, and web search and news calling the SDK directly. Every second path is redundant, and the map shows each one |
| 2 Fix a bug | "Our Anthropic bill is higher than Scout's usage page says. Can we fix the cost tracking?" | A new cost tracker inside the search adapter, i.e. a second ledger, or writing the gateway's `cost_log` table from outside the gateway (DR-2, red) | You point at the gateway's existing ledger (`cost-ledger.ts#recordCost`): "use the one we have". The plan moves; one ledger |
| 3 Add a feature | "Can we add a tool that summarizes a prospect's latest 10-K?" | Copy `news-summarize`: its own model client, built around the gateway (redundant, and it breaks DR-1, red) | Fork. You pick A: "Extend the gateway; don't build around it." DR-4. The build adds a figures-safe mode to the gateway plus the tool: two columns, both planned |
| 4 Remember | Fresh session: "Can we add a tool that summarizes earnings call transcripts?" | Another direct client | It isn't built: struck through, "rejected in DR-4". The tool reuses the gateway mode from beat 3. Memory stopped a duplicate before it existed |
| 6 Audit | (recorded) a later tool calls the gateway without the filings mode | The rules can't see it | The auditor flags it, citing DR-4. This is the exact example already in NAVIGATION_PLAN's N9 |

**Why this is stronger:**
- Every beat is "don't build a second X". That's architecture and redundancy, judged on the map, not a policy debate.
- It reuses what Scout already has: the bypass, the uncounted search costs, and the 10-K fork (which works on real filings). Beat 4 becomes the Build Plan's original earnings-call memory beat, and the auditor case matches NAVIGATION_PLAN as written.
- **One trade-off:** the "revenue shows as phone 1" bug stops being a beat. Fixing redaction first would remove the 10-K tool's reason to go around the gateway. The bug stays visible in the app as the motivating symptom for beat 3: the gateway really does mangle figures.

**Beat 2 is the riskiest.** Fixing search costs properly means routing Claude's search calls through the gateway, which is a bigger change for the agent than the old formatting fix. It needs a rehearsal to check Claude's first plan is the redundant one and the turn stays short. If it's too slow, a quieter bug can take its place.

Should I rewrite `DEMO_PLAN.md` to this arc (beats 1–4 and 6, the rehearsal table, the harness needs) and update `DEMO_REPO_SPEC.md`'s list of what each beat depends on? No Scout code changes are needed.

That's a better beat than "don't build a duplicate". Your funnel story is a hidden dependency: your function relied on something another part of the system owned, nothing made that visible, so a reasonable change somewhere else quietly broke it. The decision behind your function lived only in your head.

That's exactly what the map plus memory should catch. A past architectural decision becomes a marker on the code it governs, so a later change that would undo it is flagged at plan time, before anything breaks.

**A Scout version of your story**, built on what's already there:

**Beat 3: the decision is made (gate and fork).**
- "Can we add a tool that summarizes a prospect's latest 10-K?"
- The tempting plan copies `news-summarize` and calls Claude directly, because the gateway's redaction turns filing figures into `[PHONE_n]`. The edge goes red under DR-1.
- You pick A: "Filings go through the gateway, in a filing mode that keeps figures intact."
- That becomes DR-4. The build adds a filing mode to the gateway's redaction, plus a test proving that mode keeps figures intact. The test is how the decision is enforced in code.

**Beat 4: the conflicting change** (your funnel moment), in a fresh session, maybe framed as a teammate.
- "We're seeing account numbers in briefs. Can we redact every long number, not just phone numbers?"
- Reasonable on its own. But the obvious change widens the shared redaction pattern for every caller, which silently breaks the 10-K summaries again: their figures come back as `[PHONE_n]`. Nobody would notice until a rep did.

```text
# Alike integration: current state and proposed redesign

Oct 11, 2026. A note for whoever owns the harness server. It proposes changes to how Interpretability uses Alike, motivated by demo beats 3 and 4 in `DEMO_PLAN.md`. Nothing here is decided. Check every Alike API detail against Alike's docs and `VERIFY.md` before building; items marked **unverified** are assumptions.

## The value we want to show

- **Alike on its own (basic memory):** it remembers what was decided, attaches it to code paths, and gives it to any agent working there. It is advisory: it can't tell whether the code still follows the decision, and a file created later has no anchor.
- **Alike plus Interpretability (architectural memory):** the decision is attached to the architecture, e.g. "research tools never read outreach data", not to the files involved that day. So:
  1. it covers code that doesn't exist yet;
  2. it shapes the plan before any code (the rejected approach shows struck through);
  3. it is checked against the code (load scan, edit gate, auditor);
  4. it has provenance on the map ("decided in session 1, DR-4").
```

```text
## Verified capabilities and what was built (Oct 11, later)

Checked read-only against Alike's MCP schemas, the paired CLI, the installed runtime (`@alikeai/setup` 0.2.1, `~/.alike/runtime/*`) and alike.help.

| Question | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| Globs or folders in path anchors? | **Folders, not globs.** `'dir/'` matches a boundary-safe prefix (`hook.mjs` `isAtOrUnder`), new files included. `src/tools/**` would never match. |
| Server-side recording? | **Yes:** the paired CLI (`alike it "<title>" --json '{…}'`) or `POST https://alike.network/api-general/mcp` with the device token. The token covers 5 tools only: `record_decision`, `get_entity`, `get_briefing`, `resolve_work_item`, `inspect_injections`. |
| Repository identity in hooks? | The `origin` remote reduced to `owner/name`, **lowercased**. With no remote, Alike falls back to the bare folder name, which can't hold path anchors. A remote that isn't reachable is fine. |
| Update / supersede / delete? | `update_entity(status:'superseded')` and `dismiss_entity` work through **MCP only**. There's no delete, and **no dedupe** for decisions. |
| Read back by repository? | No server-side filter. `list_entities` or `query_entities` (MCP only) can be filtered by `anchors[].repository` client-side. With the device token, only `get_entity(urn)`. |
| Stable URL? | No per-item web URL is documented. The URN (`urn:alike:decision:<hex>`) is stable. |
| Situation anchors? | Accepted and matched on the server. Prompt grounding works mostly from the title, so put the principle in it. |
| **Blocker** | With transcript capture off for Claude (`capture_harnesses: []`), Alike's hooks are **completely silent**, including injection. The teammate moment needs `npx @alikeai/setup --capture=claude`. |

**Built (commit "record decisions in Alike from the server"):**
- The server records with `alike it` after the DR commit, never in the turn.
- Anchors: the cell folders of both sides of the invariant (`governs` / `context`), plus an `applies_when` situation.
- The title states the principle; the rationale names the refined rule and the rejected option.
- `alike_urn:` is written into the DR file and committed, so a decision is recorded once.
- `decision_recorded { alike: true, urn }` is emitted.
- The MCP instruction is kept as a fallback.
- `repoSlug` follows Alike: `HARNESS_REPO_SLUG`, or origin, lowercased; there's no git-user fallback any more.
```
