```text
// computeJourneys (NAVIGATION_PLAN §2 "Journeys", phase N10): every entry (bin, script, cli, main, route, page) traced
// through the wiring to its sinks, with UI fetch sites linked to the routes they call. Pure, deterministic, browser-safe.
// Names are placeholders here; the server's namer replaces them (inferred until the user confirms).
import type { FileFacts, RouteFact } from '../contracts/facts';
import type { ContextGraph, GraphEdge } from '../contracts/graph';
import type { Journey, JourneyStepKind } from '../contracts/cartography';
import { edgeId } from '../contracts/graph';
import { EXTERNAL_LAYER } from '../graph/build';
import { trace } from '../graph/trace';
import { fnv1a } from '../cartography/util';
import { matchRoute, type FetchSite } from './fetches';
import type { InferredEdge } from './dispatch';

type StepConfidence = Journey['steps'][number]['confidence'];
export type FetchLink = { site: FetchSite; route: RouteFact; confidence: 'syntactic' | 'inferred' };

const byId = (a: string, b: string) => (a < b ? -1 : a > b ? 1 : 0);

/** `journey:<slug>` from an entry: routes use `<method> <path>`, others `<kind> <label>`; `{}` reads as `id`. */
export function journeySlug(entry: { kind: string; label: string }): string {
  const text = entry.kind === 'route' ? entry.label : `${entry.kind} ${entry.label}`;
  return text.toLowerCase().replace(/\{\}/g, 'id').replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, '-').replace(/^-+|-+$/g, '') || 'entry';
}

/** Content hash of a journey's step list (what a name describes); the name cache is keyed by it. */
export const journeyHash = (j: Pick<Journey, 'steps'>) => fnv1a(j.steps.map((s) => s.node).join('\n'));

/** Each fetch site matched to a route (sites without a match are dropped). */
export function linkFetches(sites: readonly FetchSite[], facts: Readonly<Record<string, FileFacts>>): FetchLink[] {
  const routes = Object.values(facts).flatMap((f) => f.routes).sort((a, b) => byId(a.id, b.id));
  const serving = new Set(routes.map((r) => r.file));
  const out: FetchLink[] = [];
  for (const site of sites) {
    if (serving.has(site.file)) continue; // a server calling its own routes is not a UI flow
    const m = matchRoute(site, routes);
    if (m) out.push({ site, ...m });
  }
  return out;
}

/**
 * Sinks a flow ends at: tables, vendor packages claimed by an `external` cell, and code inside `external` cells. Bare
 * packages nobody claimed (react, node builtins) are plumbing, not destinations; they count only when the map claims
 * no external at all (then every vendor except `node:` builtins).
 */
export function journeySinks(graph: ContextGraph): string[] {
  const all = Object.values(graph.nodes);
  const claimed = all.filter((n) => n.kind === 'table' || ((n.kind === 'vendor' || n.kind === 'file' || n.kind === 'symbol') && n.layer === EXTERNAL_LAYER));
  const chosen = claimed.some((n) => n.kind !== 'table') ? claimed : all.filter((n) => n.kind === 'table' || (n.kind === 'vendor' && !n.id.startsWith('vendor:node:')));
  return chosen.map((n) => n.id).sort(byId);
}

/** Most branches kept per journey (deterministic order: by divergence point, then by steps). */
export const MAX_BRANCHES = 16;
/** Most outside-service sinks traced one by one (trace stops after MAX_TRACE_PATHS sinks; deep services need their own run). */
const MAX_DEEP_SINKS = 50;

/**
 * One journey per entry, sorted by id.
 * - Route entries start at the route; when UI code fetches it, the journey starts there instead: the UI symbol that calls
 *   the fetch site (`page`), the site (`fetch`), then the route. Only the first site (syntactic before inferred, then by id)
 *   is drawn; a route nobody fetches starts at the route.
 * - Other entries start at the entry, then its symbol (or file).
 * - Paths come from core `trace` over calls ∪ handles ∪ implements, plus the fetch → route links and `inferred` dispatch
 *   edges (see dispatch.ts), on a copy of the graph: the nearest sinks, plus each outside service traced on its own.
 * - The main path is the best one by: most domains crossed, then ending at an outside service rather than a table, then
 *   length. When the flow reaches a dispatch hub (an interface member with several implementations, e.g. a tool
 *   registry's `Tool.run`), the main path goes through the hub and its best implementation, and every other
 *   implementation's best path is a branch at the hub. Other paths are branches where they leave the main path.
 * - A route that reaches no sink still shows its handler and what it calls.
 * Step confidence is that of the edge into the step (`handles` and the first step: syntactic; dispatch: `dispatch`;
 * an inferred instance call or a fetch link: its confidence).
 */
export function computeJourneys(graph: ContextGraph, facts: Readonly<Record<string, FileFacts>>, sites: readonly FetchSite[] = [], inferred: readonly InferredEdge[] = []): Journey[] {
  const links = linkFetches(sites, facts).filter((l) => graph.nodes[l.site.from] && graph.nodes[l.route.id]);
  const known = (e: { from: string; to: string }) => !!graph.nodes[e.from] && !!graph.nodes[e.to];
  // Fetch links ride along as `handles` edges so `trace` walks them; inferred dispatch as calls/implements. Never shown.
  const extra: GraphEdge[] = [
    ...links.map((l): GraphEdge => ({ id: edgeId('fetches', l.site.from, l.route.id), kind: 'handles', from: l.site.from, to: l.route.id, count: 1, owner: l.site.file })),
    ...inferred.filter(known).map((e): GraphEdge => ({ id: edgeId(e.kind, e.from, e.to), kind: e.kind, from: e.from, to: e.to, count: 1, owner: '', confidence: 'dispatch' })),
  ];
  const g: ContextGraph = extra.length ? { ...graph, edges: [...graph.edges, ...extra] } : graph;
  const sinks = journeySinks(graph);
  const deep = sinks.filter((s) => !s.startsWith('table:')).slice(0, MAX_DEEP_SINKS);

  const conf = new Map<string, StepConfidence>();
  const key = (a: string, b: string) => `${a}\u0000${b}`;
  const callers = new Map<string, string[]>();
  const callees = new Map<string, string[]>();
  const impls = new Map<string, string[]>(); // interface member → implementations
  for (const e of g.edges) {
    if (e.kind === 'calls') {
      if (!conf.has(key(e.from, e.to))) conf.set(key(e.from, e.to), e.confidence ?? 'syntactic');
      (callers.get(e.to) ?? callers.set(e.to, []).get(e.to)!).push(e.from);
      (callees.get(e.from) ?? callees.set(e.from, []).get(e.from)!).push(e.to);
    } else if (e.kind === 'handles') conf.set(key(e.from, e.to), 'syntactic');
    else if (e.kind === 'implements') {
      conf.set(key(e.to, e.from), 'dispatch');
      (impls.get(e.to) ?? impls.set(e.to, []).get(e.to)!).push(e.from);
    }
  }
  for (const e of inferred) if (e.kind === 'calls' && known(e)) conf.set(key(e.from, e.to), e.confidence);
  for (const l of links) conf.set(key(l.site.from, l.route.id), l.confidence);
  const siteIds = new Set(links.map((l) => l.site.from));
  const hubs = [...impls].filter(([, list]) => list.length >= 2).map(([h]) => h).sort(byId);

  /** Paths from `from` to sinks: the nearest few, plus one per outside service. Deduplicated, in a stable order. */
  const sinkSet = new Set(sinks);
  const reach = (from: string): string[][] => {
    // A single-sink trace walks through other sinks; such a path really ends at the first sink it meets (kept elsewhere).
    const all = [...trace(g, from, sinks), ...deep.flatMap((s) => trace(g, from, [s])).filter((p) => !p.slice(1, -1).some((id) => sinkSet.has(id)))];
    return [...new Map(all.map((p) => [p.join('\n'), p])).values()];
  };
  const domains = (p: string[]) => new Set(p.map((id) => graph.nodes[id]?.domain).filter(Boolean)).size;
  const better = (a: string[], b: string[]) => {
    const d = domains(a) - domains(b);
    if (d) return d > 0;
    const v = (a.at(-1)!.startsWith('table:') ? 0 : 1) - (b.at(-1)!.startsWith('table:') ? 0 : 1);
    if (v) return v > 0;
    if (a.length !== b.length) return a.length > b.length;
    return a.join('\n') < b.join('\n');
  };
  const best = (ps: string[][]) => ps.reduce<string[] | null>((m, p) => (!m || better(p, m) ? p : m), null);

  const routes = new Map(Object.values(facts).flatMap((f) => f.routes).map((r) => [`entry:route:${r.method} ${r.path}`, r]));
  const entries = [...new Map(Object.values(facts).flatMap((f) => f.entries).map((e) => [e.id, e])).values()].sort((a, b) => byId(a.id, b.id));
  const used = new Map<string, number>();
  const out: Journey[] = [];

  for (const entry of entries) {
    const prefix: { node: string; kind: JourneyStepKind }[] = [];
    let start: string;
    const route = entry.kind === 'route' ? routes.get(entry.id) : undefined;
    if (route && graph.nodes[route.id]) {
      start = route.id;
      const hits = links.filter((l) => l.route.id === route.id)
        .sort((a, b) => (a.confidence === b.confidence ? 0 : a.confidence === 'syntactic' ? -1 : 1) || byId(a.site.from, b.site.from));
      const first = hits[0];
      if (first) {
        const page = pageFor(graph, callers, first.site.from);
        if (page) prefix.push({ node: page, kind: 'page' });
        prefix.push({ node: first.site.from, kind: 'fetch' });
      }
    } else {
      start = entry.symbol && graph.nodes[entry.symbol] ? entry.symbol : entry.file;
      prefix.push({ node: entry.id, kind: 'entry' });
    }

    // Where the flow starts: the start itself, or (an entry file with no top-level calls, e.g. a page whose component
    // isn't the default export) its first exported symbol that reaches anything, components first.
    let head = [start];
    let paths = graph.nodes[start] ? reach(start) : [];
    if (!paths.length && graph.nodes[start]?.kind === 'file') {
      const own = (graph.children[start] ?? []).filter((id) => graph.nodes[id]!.kind === 'symbol' && graph.nodes[id]!.symbol?.exported)
        .sort((a, b) => (graph.nodes[a]!.symbol!.kind === 'component' ? 0 : 1) - (graph.nodes[b]!.symbol!.kind === 'component' ? 0 : 1) || graph.nodes[a]!.order - graph.nodes[b]!.order);
      for (const id of own) {
        const found = reach(id);
        if (found.length) { paths = found; head = [start, id]; break; }
      }
    }
    const from = head.at(-1)!;

    // Through a dispatch hub: the hub's best implementation is the main path; the other implementations are branches.
    const alternatives: string[][] = [...paths];
    let main = best(paths);
    const toHub = hubs.length && graph.nodes[from] ? trace(g, from, hubs)[0] : undefined;
    if (toHub) {
      const viaImpl = (impls.get(toHub.at(-1)!) ?? []).slice().sort(byId)
        .map((i) => best(reach(i)))
        .filter((p): p is string[] => !!p)
        .map((p) => [...toHub, ...p]);
      const hubMain = best(viaImpl);
      if (hubMain && (!main || domains(hubMain) >= domains(main))) main = hubMain;
      alternatives.push(...viaImpl);
    }
    // No sink reached (reads aren't walked): a route still shows its handler and what it calls.
    main ??= route?.handler && graph.nodes[route.handler] && start === route.id ? [start, ...followCalls(graph, callees, route.handler)] : [from];

    const nodes = [...prefix.map((p) => p.node), ...head.slice(0, -1), ...main];
    const offset = nodes.length - main.length;
    const steps: Journey['steps'] = nodes.map((node, i) => {
      const pre = prefix[i];
      const isPage = entry.kind === 'page' && (i === prefix.length || (i === prefix.length + 1 && graph.nodes[node]?.symbol?.kind === 'component'));
      const kind: JourneyStepKind = pre?.kind ?? stepKind(graph, node, siteIds, isPage);
      const into = i === 0 ? 'syntactic' : (conf.get(key(nodes[i - 1]!, node)) ?? 'syntactic');
      return { node, kind, confidence: into };
    });
    const branches = new Map<string, Journey['branches'][number]>();
    for (const p of alternatives) {
      let i = 0;
      while (i < p.length && i < main.length && p[i] === main[i]) i++;
      if (i === 0 || i >= p.length) continue;
      const b = { from: offset + i - 1, steps: p.slice(i) };
      branches.set(`${b.from}\n${b.steps.join('\n')}`, b);
    }

    const slug = journeySlug(entry);
    const n = (used.get(slug) ?? 0) + 1;
    used.set(slug, n);
    out.push({
      id: `journey:${n > 1 ? `${slug}-${n}` : slug}`,
      name: route ? `${route.method} ${route.path}` : `${entry.kind} ${entry.label}`,
      inferred: true,
      entry: entry.id,
      steps,
      branches: [...branches.values()].sort((a, b) => a.from - b.from || byId(a.steps.join('\n'), b.steps.join('\n'))).slice(0, MAX_BRANCHES),
    });
  }
  return out.sort((a, b) => byId(a.id, b.id));
}
/**
 * `from`, then up to `hops` calls onward, each the first callee (by id) in another file — the handler's real work,
 * when no sink is reachable (e.g. a GET that only reads). Stops at a cycle or when nothing is called outside the file.
 */
function followCalls(graph: ContextGraph, callees: Map<string, string[]>, from: string, hops = 2): string[] {
  const out = [from];
  for (let cur = from; out.length <= hops;) {
    const here = cur.split('#')[0];
    const next = [...new Set(callees.get(cur) ?? [])].sort(byId).find((id) => graph.nodes[id] && id.split('#')[0] !== here && !out.includes(id));
    if (!next) break;
    out.push(next);
    cur = next;
  }
  return out;
}

/** The UI symbol behind a fetch site: a caller of it (components first, then by id), or null when nothing calls it. */
function pageFor(graph: ContextGraph, callers: Map<string, string[]>, site: string): string | null {
  const list = [...new Set(callers.get(site) ?? [])].filter((c) => c !== site && graph.nodes[c]);
  list.sort((a, b) => {
    const ca = graph.nodes[a]!.symbol?.kind === 'component' ? 0 : 1;
    const cb = graph.nodes[b]!.symbol?.kind === 'component' ? 0 : 1;
    return ca - cb || byId(a, b);
  });
  return list[0] ?? null;
}

function stepKind(graph: ContextGraph, id: string, sites: ReadonlySet<string>, page: boolean): JourneyStepKind {
  if (id.startsWith('entry:')) return 'entry';
  if (id.startsWith('route:')) return 'route';
  if (id.startsWith('table:')) return 'table';
  const n = graph.nodes[id];
  if (id.startsWith('vendor:') || n?.layer === EXTERNAL_LAYER) return 'vendor';
  if (sites.has(id)) return 'fetch';
  return page ? 'page' : 'symbol';
}
// Syntactic stand-ins for dispatch that Tier 1 call facts can't see, so journeys can pass through registries and
// module-level clients (NAVIGATION_PLAN §3.1 "Tier 2" will produce typed `implements` and calls; when its edges are in the
// graph they are used as they are). Pure and browser-safe; used only for journeys, never by the gate or the map.
import type { FileFacts, SymbolFact } from '../contracts/facts';
import type { SourceFile } from './fetches';

/** An edge journeys add on a copy of the graph: interface dispatch (`calls` to a member, `implements` from each implementation) or a call through a module-level instance. */
export type InferredEdge = { kind: 'calls' | 'implements'; from: string; to: string; confidence: 'dispatch' | 'inferred' };

const last = (name: string) => name.slice(name.lastIndexOf('.') + 1);
const esc = (s: string) => s.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, '\\$&');

function innermost(symbols: readonly SymbolFact[], at: number): SymbolFact | null {
  let best: SymbolFact | null = null;
  for (const s of symbols) {
    if (s.kind === 'type' || s.span.end <= s.span.start || at < s.span.start || at >= s.span.end) continue;
    if (!best || s.span.end - s.span.start < best.span.end - best.span.start) best = s;
  }
  return best;
}

/**
 * 1. **Interface dispatch.** A method member `I.m` of an interface/type with at least two implementations — methods named
 *    `m` on a const or class in a file that is I's file or imports it — becomes a hub: each implementation `implements`
 *    it, and every symbol whose own code calls `.m(` from a file that imports I's file (directly or through one file)
 *    `calls` it (confidence `dispatch`). Scout: `runAgent` → `Tool.run` → each tool's `run`; `complete` → `ChatProvider.chat`.
 * 2. **Module-level instances.** `const client = new Anthropic()` at the top of a file: a symbol in that file that uses
 *    `client.` calls what the instance was made from (confidence `inferred`). Scout: `newsSummarize.run` → `Anthropic`.
 * Deterministic: edges sorted and deduplicated.
 */
export function inferDispatch(files: readonly SourceFile[], facts: Readonly<Record<string, FileFacts>>): InferredEdge[] {
  const out = new Map<string, InferredEdge>();
  const add = (e: InferredEdge) => { if (e.from !== e.to) out.set(`${e.kind}|${e.from}|${e.to}`, e); };
  const byId = new Map(Object.values(facts).flatMap((f) => f.symbols.map((s) => [s.id, s] as const)));

    if (path === target) return true;
    const direct = imports(path);
    return direct.has(target) || [...direct].some((d) => imports(d).has(target));
```

```text
# Alike integration: current state and proposed redesign

Oct 11, 2026. A note for whoever owns the harness server. It proposes changes to how Interpretability uses Alike, motivated by demo beats 3 and 4 in `DEMO_PLAN.md`. Nothing here is decided. Check every Alike API detail against Alike's docs and `VERIFY.md` before building; items marked **unverified** are assumptions.

## The value we want to show

- **Alike on its own (basic memory):** it remembers what was decided, attaches it to code paths, and gives it to any agent working there. It is advisory: it can't tell whether the code still follows the decision, and a file created later has no anchor.
- **Alike plus Interpretability (architectural memory):** the decision is attached to the architecture, e.g. "research tools never read outreach data", not to the files involved that day. So:
  1. it covers code that doesn't exist yet;
  2. it shapes the plan before any code (the rejected approach shows struck through);
  3. it is checked against the code (load scan, edit gate, auditor);
  4. it has provenance on the map ("decided in session 1, DR-4").
- **Alike's part:** carrying the decision to agents and teammates who never open Interpretability.

**Pitch line:** "Alike remembers what we decided. Interpretability makes it part of the architecture, so it holds for code nobody has written yet."

## What Interpretability does today

Code: `apps/server/src/decisions.ts` (`recordFork`, `repoAnchor`) and `apps/server/src/session.ts` (`notes`, `afterAlike`).

- **Write only.** After a fork is answered, `recordFork` writes `decisions/DR-n.md`, updates `domains.yaml` and commits both. It then queues an instruction asking Claude to call `mcp__alike__record_decision` with exact arguments. A PostToolUse hook re-emits `decision_recorded` with `alike: true`, and the inspector shows "in Alike".
- **Anchors are the files that broke the rule.** `anchors: [{ kind: 'path', label: 'governs', path, repository }]`, one per violating file. With option A that file usually never gets written (beat 3's planned `src/tools/outreach-history.ts`). So in Alike the decision points at a path that doesn't exist, and a teammate's agent touching any other research tool won't be shown it.
- **The decision text is mostly the violation**, not the principle. The title is the user's first sentence when it's long enough, otherwise "`<file>` follows DR-3: …".
- **Recording depends on the model.** Claude has to make the tool call, which adds a step to the coding turn and can silently not happen ("If the Alike tools are unavailable, skip this silently").
- **Nothing reads Alike back.** The session brief uses `decisions/` in git only. Alike's hooks are deliberately off in harness sessions (`settingSources: ['project','local']`, VERIFY.md item 4).
- **Repository identity:** `HARNESS_REPO_SLUG`, else the origin remote, else `<git user>/<folder>`. The demo's fresh copies (`scripts/fresh-scout.sh`) have no remote, so `npm run demo` passes `HARNESS_REPO_SLUG`.

## Proposed changes

Roughly in order of value for the demo.

1. **Anchor decisions to the architecture.** For a decision on an `only_via` or `no_edge` invariant, anchor to the path globs of the cells on both sides of the rule: for DR-4, `src/tools/**` (Research tools › Logic) and `src/outreach/**`. Add the files where the chosen approach lives (e.g. `src/orchestrator/agent.ts`). For `owns_writes`, anchor to the owner's data cell and its `schema.sql`. Then Alike surfaces DR-4 whenever any agent touches any research tool, including ones written later.
   - **Unverified:** whether Alike path anchors accept globs or folders. If not, anchor to every existing file in those cells, and re-anchor when the cell gains files (the cartographer's turn-end pass is a natural place).
2. **Record the principle, not the incident.**
   - Title and outcome come from the invariant plus the user's answer: "DR-4: Research tools never read outreach data; the run loop passes outreach context in."
   - The rationale names the rejected option explicitly ("Rejected: a research tool that imports outreach code") and the invariant it refines (DR-3).
   - Beat 3 has the user answer in that form; Interpretability should still compose a principle when they just type "A".
3. **Record deterministically, off the model.** Write to Alike from the server, not by asking Claude to make a tool call. The paired `~/.alike/bin/alike` CLI can call `record_decision` (VERIFY.md (d)), or use Alike's HTTP API if there is one (**unverified**).
   - Run it asynchronously after the commit, never in the hot path, and emit `decision_recorded { alike: true }` when it succeeds.
   - This removes a model step from the turn and makes "in Alike" reliable on camera.
   - Keep the MCP path as a fallback.
4. **Read decisions back.**
   - At session start, fetch this repository's standing decisions from Alike (the Build Plan suggested `resolve_work_item`; **unverified** which call fits). Merge them with `decisions/`.
   - **Decisions Interpretability made** (they carry a DR id) are already known; just confirm they match.
   - **Decisions made elsewhere,** e.g. a teammate's plain Claude Code conversation that Alike captured, show as *proposed* rules on the map: dashed, marked "from Alike". Accepting one turns it into an invariant through the cartographer's proposal flow (NAVIGATION_PLAN §4.5); rejecting it is recorded.

   That closes the loop. Alike's conversational memory becomes enforced architecture (with your consent), and goes back to Alike with exact anchors.
5. **Show it on the map.**
   - **Plans:** a planned edge that a standing decision rejects is drawn struck through: "rejected in DR-4, session 1" (beat 4). The ledger's `rejectedOptionsBlocked` already counts it.
   - **Inspector:** a decision links to its Alike page and lists where it's anchored.
   - **Turn summary:** "1 decision recorded in Alike" alongside the ledger.
6. **Repository identity for fresh copies and takes.**
   - **Teammate beat:** Alike's hooks in a plain Claude Code session probably identify the repository by its git remote, and the copy has none. `fresh-scout.sh` should give the copy an origin URL for `johnz4021/scout-agent` with pushing disabled (`git remote set-url --push origin no-push`).
   - **Per-take slug:** decisions outlive a copy reset, so each take adds another DR-4 to Alike. A `--take N` option should set `HARNESS_REPO_SLUG=johnz4021/scout-agent-takeN` and the matching origin.
   - **Baselines:** the plain Claude Code baselines (DEMO_PLAN "Baselines") must run under a slug that never received a decision. Otherwise Alike feeds them DR-4 and the "without harness" timings are wrong.
7. **Lifecycle (later).** When a rule is loosened, retired or excepted (NAVIGATION_PLAN §4.4 "rule erosion"), update or retire the Alike decision too (**unverified** whether Alike supports updates). Dedupe by DR id so replays and retries don't create copies.

## Open questions for Alike

- Do path anchors accept globs or folders?
- Is there a server-side or HTTP way to record and read decisions without an agent session? (This was on the Build Plan's "ask at the event" list.)
- How do Alike's hooks pick the repository: remote URL, folder, something else?
- Can decisions be updated, retired or deleted (for rule changes and take resets)?
- Is there a stable URL per decision, for linking from the inspector?

## Done when

- **Beat 3:** answering A shows "DR-4 in Alike" within a few seconds, recorded by the server. Alike's page shows the principle, the rejected option, and anchors covering `src/tools/**` and `src/outreach/**`.
- **Beat 4:** in a fresh session, "Can we build a research tool that reads our past emails…" plans without the tool, shows the struck-through edge citing DR-4, and the ledger counts one rejected option blocked.
- **Teammate moment:** plain Claude Code in a fresh copy (same take slug), touching any file in `src/tools/`, is given DR-4 by Alike.
- **Isolation:** a new take (`--take N+1`) starts with no DR-4 in Alike, and baselines run with no decisions.

## Verified capabilities and what was built (Oct 11, later)

Checked read-only against Alike's MCP schemas, the paired CLI, the installed runtime (`@alikeai/setup` 0.2.1, `~/.alike/runtime/*`) and alike.help.

| Question | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| Globs or folders in path anchors? | **Folders, not globs.** `'dir/'` matches a boundary-safe prefix (`hook.mjs` `isAtOrUnder`), new files included. `src/tools/**` would never match. |
| Server-side recording? | **Yes:** the paired CLI (`alike it "<title>" --json '{…}'`) or `POST https://alike.network/api-general/mcp` with the device token. The token covers 5 tools only: `record_decision`, `get_entity`, `get_briefing`, `resolve_work_item`, `inspect_injections`. |
| Repository identity in hooks? | The `origin` remote reduced to `owner/name`, **lowercased**. With no remote, Alike falls back to the bare folder name, which can't hold path anchors. A remote that isn't reachable is fine. |
| Update / supersede / delete? | `update_entity(status:'superseded')` and `dismiss_entity` work through **MCP only**. There's no delete, and **no dedupe** for decisions. |
| Read back by repository? | No server-side filter. `list_entities` or `query_entities` (MCP only) can be filtered by `anchors[].repository` client-side. With the device token, only `get_entity(urn)`. |
| Stable URL? | No per-item web URL is documented. The URN (`urn:alike:decision:<hex>`) is stable. |
| Situation anchors? | Accepted and matched on the server. Prompt grounding works mostly from the title, so put the principle in it. |
| **Blocker** | With transcript capture off for Claude (`capture_harnesses: []`), Alike's hooks are **completely silent**, including injection. The teammate moment needs `npx @alikeai/setup --capture=claude`. |

**Built (commit "record decisions in Alike from the server"):**
- The server records with `alike it` after the DR commit, never in the turn.
- Anchors: the cell folders of both sides of the invariant (`governs` / `context`), plus an `applies_when` situation.
- The title states the principle; the rationale names the refined rule and the rejected option.
- `alike_urn:` is written into the DR file and committed, so a decision is recorded once.
- `decision_recorded { alike: true, urn }` is emitted.
- The MCP instruction is kept as a fallback.
- `repoSlug` follows Alike: `HARNESS_REPO_SLUG`, or origin, lowercased; there's no git-user fallback any more.

**Still to do:** see the open decisions in the harness session. They cover:
- capture on or off;
- `fresh-scout.sh --take N` with an origin remote and pushing disabled;
- dismissing the stale test DR-4 in Alike;
- reading foreign decisions (needs an MCP client in the server);
- supersede on rule changes (MCP).
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# A fresh, disposable copy of Scout for one harness session.
#
# The original (../scout-agent) is never touched: each run clones it at a tag
# (default demo-start) into ../scout-run, so whatever the session changes
# (code, domains.yaml, decisions/, .harness/, the database) is thrown away next time.
#
# Usage: scripts/fresh-scout.sh [--map] [--with-data] [--keep] [--offline]
#   --map        start from fixtures/scout-agent.domains.yaml (skip the cartographer)
#   --with-data  copy the original's database (its runs and notes) instead of seeding a fresh one
#   --keep       keep the previous run as ../scout-run-<time> instead of deleting it
#   --offline    seed the offline sample companies instead of the live ones
#   --take N     give the copy its own Alike repository: origin https://github.com/johnz4021/scout-agent-takeN.git
#                (pushing disabled), so each recording take (and each baseline) starts with no decisions in Alike.
#                Without it the copy's origin is johnz4021/scout-agent, matching HARNESS_REPO_SLUG's default.
#
# Environment: SCOUT_SRC (original), SCOUT_RUN_DIR (copy), SCOUT_REF (tag or commit), SCOUT_PORT (default 8788)
set -euo pipefail

here="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
src="$(cd "${SCOUT_SRC:-$here/../scout-agent}" && pwd)"
dest="${SCOUT_RUN_DIR:-$(dirname "$src")/scout-run}"
ref="${SCOUT_REF:-demo-start}"
port="${SCOUT_PORT:-8788}"

map=0 with_data=0 keep=0 mode="live" take=""
while (( $# )); do
  case "$1" in
    --map) map=1 ;;
    --with-data) with_data=1 ;;
    --keep) keep=1 ;;
    --offline) mode="offline" ;;
    --take) shift; take="${1:?--take needs a value}" ;;
    --take=*) take="${1#--take=}" ;;
    -h|--help) sed -n '2,18p' "$0"; exit 0 ;;
    *) echo "unknown option: $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
  shift
done
slug="johnz4021/scout-agent${take:+-take$take}"

[[ "$dest" != "$src" ]] || { echo "refusing: the run directory is the original" >&2; exit 1; }
git -C "$src" rev-parse -q --verify "$ref^{commit}" >/dev/null || { echo "no $ref in $src" >&2; exit 1; }

# Copy-on-write where the filesystem supports it (APFS, btrfs), plain copy otherwise.
clone_path() {
  [[ -e "$1" ]] || return 0
  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$2")"
  cp -cR "$1" "$2" 2>/dev/null || cp -R --reflink=auto "$1" "$2" 2>/dev/null || cp -R "$1" "$2"
}

# Stop anything still serving the previous copy.
if pids="$(lsof -ti "tcp:$port" 2>/dev/null)" && [[ -n "$pids" ]]; then
  echo "stopping the process on :$port"
  kill $pids 2>/dev/null || true
  sleep 1
fi

if [[ -d "$dest" ]]; then
  if (( keep )); then
    mv "$dest" "$dest-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
  else
    rm -rf "$dest"
  fi
fi

echo "cloning $src @ $ref -> $dest"
git clone -q "$src" "$dest"
git -C "$dest" checkout -q -B session "$ref"
# Alike's hooks identify a repository by its origin remote (owner/name, lowercased), so the copy gets one that
# matches HARNESS_REPO_SLUG. Pushing is disabled: nothing in the session can push anywhere.
git -C "$dest" remote set-url origin "https://github.com/$slug.git"
git -C "$dest" remote set-url --push origin no-push

# Things git doesn't carry: dependencies, the API key, the SEC cache, the built web app.
clone_path "$src/node_modules" "$dest/node_modules"
clone_path "$src/.env" "$dest/.env"
clone_path "$src/.scout/cache" "$dest/.scout/cache"
clone_path "$src/web/dist" "$dest/web/dist"

cd "$dest"
if (( with_data )) && [[ -d "$src/.scout/pgdata" ]]; then
  if lsof -ti tcp:8787 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "note: something is running on :8787; if it's the original Scout, stop it first so its database is copied cleanly"
  fi
  clone_path "$src/.scout/pgdata" "$dest/.scout/pgdata"
  echo "copied the original's database"
else
  SCOUT_MODE="$mode" npm run --silent seed
fi
[[ -d web/dist ]] || npm run --silent build >/dev/null

if (( map )); then
  cp "$here/fixtures/scout-agent.domains.yaml" domains.yaml
  git add domains.yaml
  git -c user.name="Interpretability" -c user.email="interpretability@localhost" commit -qm "chore: add domains map"
  echo "added domains.yaml from fixtures"
fi

cat <<EOF

Fresh Scout at $dest (branch "session" at $ref; the original is untouched).

  Interpretability:  cd $here && HARNESS_REPO=$dest HARNESS_REPO_SLUG=$slug npm run dev
  Scout:    cd $dest && PORT=$port npm run dev:api      # app + API on http://localhost:$port, reloads server code

Run this script again for a clean slate. The web app is served prebuilt; after the agent edits web/, run "npm run build" in the copy.
EOF
```

```text
// project (NAVIGATION_PLAN §3.2): visible nodes with rolled-up activity, aggregated edges and ports for one view.
import type { TurnActivity } from '../contracts/api';
import type { CallConfidence } from '../contracts/facts';
import {
  NEUTRAL_ID, cellId, fileOf,
  type ContextGraph, type EdgeKind, type GraphEdge, type NodeKind, type Port, type Projection, type ProjectionGrid, type Rollup, type ViewState,
  type VisibleEdge, type VisibleNode, type ViolationState,
} from '../contracts/graph';
import { strongerMark } from './activity';
import { byId, subtreeCounts } from './util';

const SEVERITY = { new: 2, existing: 1 } as const;
/** The worse of two violation states ('new' > 'existing' > null). */
export const worse = (a: ViolationState, b: ViolationState): ViolationState => ((b ? SEVERITY[b] : 0) > (a ? SEVERITY[a] : 0) ? b : a);
const CONFIDENCE: Record<CallConfidence, number> = { dispatch: 0, syntactic: 1, typed: 2 };
/** Weakest call confidence (dispatch < syntactic < typed). */
const weaker = (a: CallConfidence | null, b: CallConfidence | undefined): CallConfidence | null =>
  !b ? a : !a || CONFIDENCE[b] < CONFIDENCE[a] ? b : a;

const emptyRollup = (leaves: number): Rollup => ({
  looked: false, edited: false, added: 0, removed: 0, ghostSteps: [], unplanned: false, violation: null,
  violationFiles: [], newViolationFiles: [], cursor: false, audit: 0, proposal: null, rules: [], plannedNew: false, leaves,
});

/** Containers whose collapsed node previews its first children (files and symbols are leaves at this level). */
const PREVIEWED = new Set<NodeKind>(['domain', 'cell', 'group', 'tests', 'unassigned', 'neutral']);
const PREVIEW = 4;

/** True when a rollup carries activity from the turn (what the turn lens keeps). */
export const isActive = (r: Rollup) =>
  r.looked || r.edited || r.ghostSteps.length > 0 || r.unplanned || r.violation === 'new' || r.cursor || r.added > 0 || r.removed > 0;

/**
 * Visible set: the root's children, plus the children of every expanded visible node. `view.focus` does not
 * change visibility (autoExpand does). Leaf activity rolls up to the nearest visible ancestor (and on to the
 * expanded containers above it, so a container's rollup always covers its whole subtree): booleans OR,
 * counts sum, violation MAX. Ghost and unplanned keep cellViews' cell semantics at every depth: a planned unit
 * (a cell, or a leaf outside cells) is a ghost only while nothing in it under the node is edited, and an edited
 * unit is unplanned only if nothing in it under the node is planned. Leaf edges map to their nearest visible
 * endpoints and aggregate by (from, to); self-loops and edges touching neutral code or the root are dropped.
 * Ghost (planned or gate-blocked) edges aggregate in their own lane. Edges between two cells of the same domain are
 * dropped (flow down a column is implied, SPEC §3); file edges inside an expanded domain are drawn. Ports mark where
 * an edge leaves or enters an expanded container, with the visible node at the other end. Collapsed containers carry
 * a preview of their first children. `cursor` is the visible node carrying the agent; `grid` the map's cells.
 * `lens.kinds` filters edge kinds (empty = all); `lens.turnOnly` keeps only nodes with turn activity.
 */
export function project(graph: ContextGraph, view: ViewState, activity: TurnActivity): Projection {
  const counts = subtreeCounts(graph);
  const expanded = new Set(view.expanded);

  // ---- visible tree (pre-order, siblings by order)
  const visible = new Map<string, VisibleNode>();
  const order: string[] = [];
  const walk = (parent: string, vparent: string | null, depth: number) => {
    for (const id of graph.children[parent] ?? []) {
      const n = graph.nodes[id]!;
      const kids = graph.children[id] ?? [];
      const expandable = kids.length > 0;
      const isOpen = expandable && expanded.has(id);
      const preview = !isOpen && PREVIEWED.has(n.kind) ? kids.slice(0, PREVIEW).map((k) => graph.nodes[k]!.label) : [];
      visible.set(id, {
        id, kind: n.kind, parent: vparent, label: n.label, depth, expanded: isOpen, expandable, order: n.order,
        ...(n.domain ? { domain: n.domain } : {}), ...(n.layer ? { layer: n.layer } : {}), ...(n.path ? { path: n.path } : {}),
        preview,
        rollup: emptyRollup(n.kind === 'file' ? counts(id).symbols : n.kind === 'symbol' ? counts(id).symbols + 1 : counts(id).files),
      });
      order.push(id);
      if (isOpen) walk(id, id, depth + 1);
    }
  };
  walk(graph.root, null, 0);

  const repMemo = new Map<string, string | null>();
  /** Nearest visible ancestor-or-self (null for the root and unknown ids). */
  const rep = (id: string): string | null => {
    let r = repMemo.get(id);
    if (r !== undefined) return r;
    const n = graph.nodes[id];
    r = !n || id === graph.root ? null : visible.has(id) ? id : n.parent ? rep(n.parent) : null;
    repMemo.set(id, r);
    return r;
  };
  const endMemo = new Map<string, string | null>();
  /** Edge endpoint: the nearest visible ancestor-or-self, or null inside neutral code (which never draws edges). */
  const end = (id: string): string | null => {
    let r = endMemo.get(id);
    if (r !== undefined) return r;
    const n = graph.nodes[id];
    if (!n || id === graph.root || id === NEUTRAL_ID || !n.parent) r = null;
    else if (n.parent === graph.root) r = id;
    else {
      const up = end(n.parent);
      r = up === null ? null : visible.has(id) ? id : up;
    }
    endMemo.set(id, r);
    return r;
  };
  /** Cell semantics unit: a leaf's cell, or the leaf's file outside cells. */
  const unit = (id: string) => {
    const n = graph.nodes[id]!;
    return n.domain && n.layer ? cellId(n.domain, n.layer) : fileOf(id) ?? id;
  };

  // ---- rollups
  type Unit = { ghost: Set<number>; edited: boolean; planned: boolean; unplanned: boolean };
  const units = new Map<string, Map<string, Unit>>();
  for (const [id, l] of Object.entries(activity.leaves)) {
    const k = unit(id);
    // the nearest visible ancestor, and every visible (hence expanded) container above it
    for (let r = rep(id); r; r = visible.get(r)!.parent) {
      const ro = visible.get(r)!.rollup;
      ro.looked ||= l.looked;
      ro.edited ||= l.edited;
      ro.added += l.added;
      ro.removed += l.removed;
      ro.violation = worse(ro.violation, l.violation);
      if (l.violation === 'new') ro.newViolationFiles.push(fileOf(id) ?? id);
      ro.cursor ||= l.cursor;
      ro.audit += l.audit;
      ro.proposal = strongerMark(ro.proposal, l.proposal);
      const byUnit = units.get(r) ?? units.set(r, new Map()).get(r)!;
      const u = byUnit.get(k) ?? byUnit.set(k, { ghost: new Set(), edited: false, planned: false, unplanned: false }).get(k)!;
      for (const s of l.ghostSteps) u.ghost.add(s);
      u.edited ||= l.edited;
      u.planned ||= l.planned;
      u.unplanned ||= l.unplanned;
    }
  }
  for (const [r, byUnit] of units) {
    const ro = visible.get(r)!.rollup;
    const ghost = new Set<number>();
    for (const u of byUnit.values()) {
      if (!u.edited) for (const s of u.ghost) ghost.add(s);
      if (u.unplanned && !u.planned) ro.unplanned = true;
    }
    ro.ghostSteps = [...ghost].sort((a, b) => a - b);
  }
  for (const f of activity.violations.files) {
    for (let r = rep(f); r; r = visible.get(r)!.parent) visible.get(r)!.rollup.violationFiles.push(f);
  }
  for (const [id, list] of Object.entries(activity.rules)) {
    for (let r = rep(id); r; r = visible.get(r)!.parent) visible.get(r)!.rollup.rules.push(...list);
  }
  for (const id of activity.plannedNew) {
    for (let r = rep(id); r; r = visible.get(r)!.parent) visible.get(r)!.rollup.plannedNew = true;
  }
  for (const v of visible.values()) {
    v.rollup.violationFiles = [...new Set(v.rollup.violationFiles)].sort(byId);
    v.rollup.newViolationFiles = [...new Set(v.rollup.newViolationFiles)].sort(byId);
    if (v.rollup.rules.length) v.rollup.rules = [...new Set(v.rollup.rules)].sort(byId);
  }

  const shown = view.lens.turnOnly ? new Set(order.filter((id) => isActive(visible.get(id)!.rollup))) : null;
  const nodes = order.filter((id) => !shown || shown.has(id)).map((id) => visible.get(id)!);

  // ---- edges
  const kinds = view.lens.kinds.length ? new Set<EdgeKind>(view.lens.kinds) : null;
  // index the few listed ids by their `from`, so the loop below only hashes ids of edges leaving those leaves
  const byFrom = (ids: readonly string[]) => {
    const m = new Map<string, Set<string>>();
    for (const id of ids) {
      const from = id.slice(id.indexOf('|') + 1, id.lastIndexOf('|'));
      (m.get(from) ?? m.set(from, new Set()).get(from)!).add(id);
    }
    return { has: (e: GraphEdge) => !!m.get(e.from)?.has(e.id) };
  };
  const added = byFrom(activity.addedEdges);
  const existing = byFrom(activity.violations.edges);
  /** Flow down a column is implied: no edge between two cells of one domain. */
  const sameColumn = (a: string, b: string) => {
    const na = visible.get(a)!;
    const nb = visible.get(b)!;
    return na.kind === 'cell' && nb.kind === 'cell' && na.domain === nb.domain;
  };
  const endpoints = (from: string, to: string): [string, string] | null => {
    const a = end(from);
    if (!a) return null;
    const b = end(to);
    if (!b || a === b) return null;
    if (shown && (!shown.has(a) || !shown.has(b))) return null;
    if (sameColumn(a, b)) return null;
    return [a, b];
  };
  type Solid = VisibleEdge & { kindSet: Set<EdgeKind> };
  const solid: Solid[] = [];
  const byPair = new Map<string, Map<string, Solid>>();
  for (const e of graph.edges) {
    if (kinds && !kinds.has(e.kind)) continue;
    const ends = endpoints(e.from, e.to);
    if (!ends) continue;
    const row = byPair.get(ends[0]) ?? byPair.set(ends[0], new Map()).get(ends[0])!;
    let v = row.get(ends[1]);
    if (!v) {
      v = { id: `${ends[0]}->${ends[1]}`, from: ends[0], to: ends[1], kinds: [], kindSet: new Set(), count: 0, status: 'existing', violation: null, confidence: null, steps: [], leafEdges: [] };
      row.set(ends[1], v);
      solid.push(v);
    }
    v.kindSet.add(e.kind);
    v.count += 1;
    v.leafEdges.push(e.id);
    if (added.has(e)) v.status = 'new';
    if (existing.has(e)) v.violation = worse(v.violation, 'existing');
    if (e.kind === 'calls') v.confidence = weaker(v.confidence, e.confidence);
  }
  const ghosts = new Map<string, VisibleEdge & { stepSet: Set<number> }>();
  if (!kinds || kinds.has('imports')) {
    for (const pe of activity.plannedEdges) {
      const ends = endpoints(pe.from, pe.to);
      if (!ends) continue;
      // a ghost a standing decision rules out keeps its own lane ("rejected in DR-4, session 1")
      const id = `${pe.decision ? 'rejected' : 'ghost'}:${ends[0]}->${ends[1]}`;
      let v = ghosts.get(id);
      if (!v) ghosts.set(id, (v = { id, from: ends[0], to: ends[1], kinds: ['imports'], count: 0, status: 'ghost', violation: null, confidence: null, steps: [], stepSet: new Set(), leafEdges: [], decision: pe.decision ?? null }));
      v.count += 1;
      v.leafEdges.push(`${pe.source ?? (pe.steps.length ? 'plan' : 'gate')}|${pe.from}|${pe.to}`);
      v.violation = worse(v.violation, pe.violation);
      for (const s of pe.steps) v.stepSet.add(s);
    }
  }
  const edges: VisibleEdge[] = [
    ...solid.map(({ kindSet, ...v }) => ({ ...v, kinds: [...kindSet].sort(byId) })),
    ...[...ghosts.values()].map(({ stepSet, ...v }) => ({ ...v, steps: [...stepSet].sort((a, b) => a - b) })),
  ].sort((a, b) => byId(a.id, b.id));

  // ---- ports: every expanded container an edge leaves (out) or enters (in)
  const ports: Port[] = [];
  const ancestors = (id: string) => {
    const out: string[] = [];
    for (let p = visible.get(id)!.parent; p; p = visible.get(p)!.parent) out.push(p);
    return out;
  };
  for (const e of edges) {
    const fa = ancestors(e.from);
    const ta = ancestors(e.to);
    const ts = new Set(ta);
    const fs = new Set(fa);
    for (const c of fa) if (!ts.has(c)) ports.push({ container: c, edge: e.id, peer: e.to, direction: 'out' });
    for (const c of ta) if (!fs.has(c)) ports.push({ container: c, edge: e.id, peer: e.from, direction: 'in' });
  }

  const cur = activity.cursor ? rep(activity.cursor) : null;
  const cursor = cur && (!shown || shown.has(cur)) ? { node: cur, leaf: activity.cursor!, verb: activity.verb ?? 'reading' } : null;
  return { nodes, edges, ports, cursor, grid: gridOf(graph) };
}

const grids = new WeakMap<ContextGraph, ProjectionGrid>();
/** Domains in map order, layers in map order (those with at least one cell), and the cell ids that exist. */
export function gridOf(graph: ContextGraph): ProjectionGrid {
  let g = grids.get(graph);
  if (g) return g;
  const domains: string[] = [];
  const layers = new Map<string, number>();
  const cells: string[] = [];
  for (const id of graph.children[graph.root] ?? []) {
    const d = graph.nodes[id]!;
    if (d.kind !== 'domain') continue;
    domains.push(d.domain!);
    for (const c of graph.children[id] ?? []) {
      const n = graph.nodes[c]!;
      if (n.kind !== 'cell') continue;
      cells.push(c);
      layers.set(n.layer!, n.order);
    }
  }
  g = { domains, layers: [...layers].sort((a, b) => a[1] - b[1]).map(([l]) => l), cells };
  grids.set(graph, g);
  return g;
}
// buildGraph (NAVIGATION_PLAN §3.2): one containment tree plus leaf edges, from domains.yaml and per-file facts.
// Pure and browser-safe (the mapper only needs picomatch).
import { createMapper, matchesAny, type Placement } from '../mapper';
import type { DomainMap } from '../schema';
import type { UIState } from '../events';
import type { CallConfidence, CallFact, FileFacts, SemanticFacts } from '../contracts/facts';
import {
  NEUTRAL_ID, ROOT_ID, UNASSIGNED_ID, cellId, domainId, edgeId, fileOf, groupId, tableId, testsId,
  type ContextGraph, type EdgeKind, type GraphEdge, type GraphNode, type NodeKind,
} from '../contracts/graph';

/** Top-level container for bare packages no `external` cell claims. */
export const VENDORS_ID = 'group:vendors';
/** A container holding more files than this is split into directory groups. */
export const GROUP_THRESHOLD = 12;
/** The layer whose cells hold external services; vendor packages and trace sinks live there. */
export const EXTERNAL_LAYER = 'external';

const KIND_RANK: Partial<Record<NodeKind, number>> = { group: 0, file: 1, table: 2, vendor: 3, symbol: 4, route: 5, entry: 6 };

const emptyFacts = (path: string): FileFacts => ({ path, hash: '', imports: [], writes: [], symbols: [], calls: [], routes: [], entries: [] });
const isPseudo = (id: string) => id.startsWith('vendor:') || id.startsWith('table:');
const normalize = (p: string) => p.replace(/\\/g, '/').split('/').filter((s) => s && s !== '.').join('/');

/**
 * Containment: repo → domain → cell → (group) → file → symbol (nested by `parent`), with routes and entries under
 * their file and tables under the cell that lists them. Test files sit in `tests:<domain>` under their domain;
 * files matching no cell in `unassigned`, shared code in `neutral` (both top-level, created when non-empty).
 * Bare packages (`vendor:<pkg>`) go into the `external` cell that claims them (a glob matching `<pkg>` or
 * `node_modules/<pkg>/…`, importing domains first), else into the top-level `group:vendors`.
 * A cell with confirmed `components` groups matching files by component; any container with more than
 * GROUP_THRESHOLD remaining files groups them by directory (recursively).
 * Leaf edges: imports (file→file), uses (file→vendor), calls, implements, handles (route→handler), writes (→table).
 * Tier 2 calls replace a file's syntactic calls when `semantic[path].hash === facts[path].hash`.
 */
export function buildGraph(
  map: DomainMap,
  facts: Readonly<Record<string, FileFacts>>,
  semantic: Readonly<Record<string, SemanticFacts>> = {},
): ContextGraph {
  const mapper = createMapper(map);
  const nodes: Record<string, GraphNode> = {};
  const children: Record<string, string[]> = {};
  const rank = new Map<string, number>();
  const add = (n: Omit<GraphNode, 'order'>, r: number): GraphNode => {
    const cur = nodes[n.id];
    if (cur) return cur;
    const node = n as GraphNode;
    node.order = 0;
    nodes[n.id] = node;
    rank.set(n.id, r);
    if (n.parent) (children[n.parent] ??= []).push(n.id);
    return node;
  };
  /** Copy a container's domain/layer onto a node (no spread: this runs per symbol). */
  const scoped = <T extends Omit<GraphNode, 'order'>>(n: T, from: GraphNode): T => {
    if (from.domain) n.domain = from.domain;
    if (from.layer) n.layer = from.layer;
    return n;
  };

  // ---- skeleton: domains in map order, cells in layer order (their order is the grid position)
  add({ id: ROOT_ID, kind: 'repo', parent: null, label: 'repo' }, 0);
  const layerIdx = new Map(map.layers.map((l, i) => [l.id, i]));
  map.domains.forEach((d, i) => {
    add({ id: domainId(d.id), kind: 'domain', parent: ROOT_ID, label: d.name, domain: d.id }, i);
    for (const l of map.layers) {
      if (l.id in d.cells) add({ id: cellId(d.id, l.id), kind: 'cell', parent: domainId(d.id), label: l.name, domain: d.id, layer: l.id }, layerIdx.get(l.id)!);
    }
  });
  const nd = map.domains.length;
  const ensureTop = (id: string) => {
    if (id === UNASSIGNED_ID) return add({ id, kind: 'unassigned', parent: ROOT_ID, label: 'Unassigned' }, nd);
    if (id === NEUTRAL_ID) return add({ id, kind: 'neutral', parent: ROOT_ID, label: 'Shared' }, nd + 1);
    return add({ id: VENDORS_ID, kind: 'group', parent: ROOT_ID, label: 'Vendors' }, nd + 2);
  };
  const ensureTests = (domain: string) =>
    add({ id: testsId(domain), kind: 'tests', parent: domainId(domain), label: 'Tests', domain }, map.layers.length);

  // ---- files: every path with facts plus every repo path they import
  const paths = new Set<string>();
  for (const [path, f] of Object.entries(facts)) {
    paths.add(path);
    for (const i of f.imports) if (!isPseudo(i.to)) paths.add(i.to);
  }
  const placement = new Map<string, Placement>();
  const byContainer = new Map<string, string[]>();
  for (const path of [...paths].sort()) {
    const p = mapper.place(path);
    if (p.kind === 'ignored') continue;
    placement.set(path, p);
    const c = p.kind === 'cell' ? cellId(p.domain, p.layer) : p.kind === 'test' ? ensureTests(p.domain).id : ensureTop(p.kind === 'neutral' ? NEUTRAL_ID : UNASSIGNED_ID).id;
    const list = byContainer.get(c) ?? [];
    list.push(path);
    byContainer.set(c, list);
  }

  const putFile = (path: string, parent: string) => {
    const p = placement.get(path)!;
    const n: Omit<GraphNode, 'order'> = { id: path, kind: 'file', parent, label: fileLabel(path), path };
    if (p.kind === 'cell' || p.kind === 'test') n.domain = p.domain;
    if (p.kind === 'cell') n.layer = p.layer;
    add(n, KIND_RANK.file!);
  };
  /** Directory groups for a container holding too many files; recursive, files directly in the common dir stay put. */
  const groupByDir = (parent: string, files: string[], gid: (dir: string) => string, scope: Pick<GraphNode, 'domain' | 'layer'>) => {
    if (files.length <= GROUP_THRESHOLD) { for (const f of files) putFile(f, parent); return; }
    const prefix = commonDir(files);
    const dirs = new Map<string, string[]>();
    for (const f of files) {
      const rest = prefix ? f.slice(prefix.length + 1) : f;
      const i = rest.indexOf('/');
      if (i < 0) { putFile(f, parent); continue; }
      const dir = (prefix ? `${prefix}/` : '') + rest.slice(0, i);
      const list = dirs.get(dir) ?? [];
      list.push(f);
      dirs.set(dir, list);
    }
    for (const [dir, list] of dirs) {
      const id = gid(dir);
      add({ id, kind: 'group', parent, label: `${dir.slice(prefix ? prefix.length + 1 : 0)}/`, path: dir, ...scope }, KIND_RANK.group!);
      groupByDir(id, list, gid, scope);
    }
  };
  for (const [container, files] of byContainer) {
    const n = nodes[container]!;
    if (n.kind === 'cell') {
      const { domain, layer } = n as Required<Pick<GraphNode, 'domain' | 'layer'>>;
      const comps = map.domains.find((d) => d.id === domain)?.cells[layer]?.components ?? [];
      const rest: string[] = [];
      for (const f of files) {
        const comp = comps.find((c) => matchesAny(c.paths, f));
        if (!comp) { rest.push(f); continue; }
        const id = groupId(domain, layer, comp.id);
        add({ id, kind: 'group', parent: container, label: comp.name, domain, layer }, KIND_RANK.group!);
        putFile(f, id);
      }
      groupByDir(container, rest, (dir) => groupId(domain, layer, dir), { domain, layer });
    } else {
      groupByDir(container, files, (dir) => `group:${container}/${dir}`, n.domain ? { domain: n.domain } : {});
    }
  }

  // ---- symbols, routes, entries (under their file; symbols nested by parent)
  for (const path of placement.keys()) {
    const f = facts[path];
    if (!f) continue;
    const file = nodes[path]!;
    const own = f.symbols.some((s) => s.parent) ? new Set(f.symbols.map((s) => s.id)) : null;
    for (const s of f.symbols) {
      const nested = !!s.parent && !!own?.has(s.parent);
      add(scoped({
        id: s.id, kind: 'symbol', parent: nested ? s.parent : path,
        label: nested ? s.name.slice(s.name.lastIndexOf('.') + 1) : s.name, symbol: { kind: s.kind, exported: s.exported },
      }, file), KIND_RANK.symbol!);
    }
    for (const r of f.routes) add(scoped({ id: r.id, kind: 'route', parent: path, label: `${r.method} ${r.path}` }, file), KIND_RANK.route!);
    for (const e of f.entries) add(scoped({ id: e.id, kind: 'entry', parent: path, label: e.label }, file), KIND_RANK.entry!);
  }

  // ---- tables: under the cell that lists them, else unassigned
  map.domains.forEach((d) => {
    for (const [layer, cell] of Object.entries(d.cells)) {
      for (const t of cell.tables ?? []) add({ id: tableId(t), kind: 'table', parent: cellId(d.id, layer), label: t, domain: d.id, layer }, KIND_RANK.table!);
    }
  });
  const ensureTable = (id: string) => nodes[id] ?? add({ id, kind: 'table', parent: ensureTop(UNASSIGNED_ID).id, label: id.slice(6) }, KIND_RANK.table!);

  // ---- table columns, from schema files (`CREATE TABLE`); the table stays under the cell that lists it
  for (const path of placement.keys()) {
    for (const t of facts[path]?.tables ?? []) ensureTable(tableId(t.name)).columns = [...t.columns];
  }

  // ---- vendors: claimed by an `external` cell (importing domains first), else the top-level Vendors group
  const callsOf = (path: string, f: FileFacts): CallFact[] => {
    const s = semantic[path];
    return s && s.hash === f.hash ? s.calls : f.calls;
  };
  const importers = new Map<string, Set<string>>();
  const noteVendor = (v: string, from: string) => {
    const set = importers.get(v) ?? new Set<string>();
    const d = mapper.domainOf(fileOf(from) ?? from);
    if (d) set.add(d);
    importers.set(v, set);
  };
  for (const path of placement.keys()) {
    const f = facts[path];
    if (!f) continue;
    for (const i of f.imports) if (i.to.startsWith('vendor:')) noteVendor(i.to, path);
    for (const c of callsOf(path, f)) if (c.to.startsWith('vendor:')) noteVendor(c.to, c.from);
  }
  const externals = map.domains.flatMap((d) => (d.cells[EXTERNAL_LAYER] ? [{ domain: d.id, globs: d.cells[EXTERNAL_LAYER]!.paths ?? [] }] : []));
  for (const [v, doms] of [...importers].sort(([a], [b]) => (a < b ? -1 : 1))) {
    const pkg = v.slice(7);
    const claims = (g: string[]) => matchesAny(g, pkg) || matchesAny(g, `node_modules/${pkg}`) || matchesAny(g, `node_modules/${pkg}/index.js`);
    const owner = externals.find((e) => doms.has(e.domain) && claims(e.globs)) ?? externals.find((e) => claims(e.globs));
    if (owner) add({ id: v, kind: 'vendor', parent: cellId(owner.domain, EXTERNAL_LAYER), label: pkg, domain: owner.domain, layer: EXTERNAL_LAYER }, KIND_RANK.vendor!);
    else add({ id: v, kind: 'vendor', parent: ensureTop(VENDORS_ID).id, label: pkg }, KIND_RANK.vendor!);
  }

  // ---- leaf edges, grouped by owner file (in path order) and sorted by id within it
  const edges: GraphEdge[] = [];
  const seen = new Map<string, Map<string, GraphEdge[]>>(); // from → to → edges (one per kind); avoids hashing new id strings
  const local: GraphEdge[] = [];
  const resolve = (id: string): string | null => {
    if (nodes[id]) return id;
    if (id.startsWith('table:')) return ensureTable(id).id;
    const f = fileOf(id);
    return f && nodes[f] ? f : null;
  };
  const edge = (kind: EdgeKind, from: string | null, to: string | null, owner: string, count: number, typeOnly?: boolean, confidence?: CallConfidence) => {
    if (!from || !to) return;
    const row = seen.get(from) ?? seen.set(from, new Map()).get(from)!;
    const same = row.get(to);
    const cur = same?.find((x) => x.kind === kind);
    if (cur) {
      cur.count += count;
      if (typeOnly === false) cur.typeOnly = false;
      return;
    }
    const e: GraphEdge = { id: edgeId(kind, from, to), kind, from, to, count, owner };
    if (typeOnly !== undefined) e.typeOnly = typeOnly;
    if (confidence) e.confidence = confidence;
    if (same) same.push(e);
    else row.set(to, [e]);
    local.push(e);
  };
  for (const path of placement.keys()) {
    const f = facts[path];
    if (!f) continue;
    for (const i of f.imports) edge(i.to.startsWith('vendor:') ? 'uses' : 'imports', path, resolve(i.to), path, 1, i.typeOnly);
    for (const c of callsOf(path, f)) edge('calls', resolve(c.from), resolve(c.to), path, c.count, undefined, c.confidence);
    const s = semantic[path];
    if (s && s.hash === f.hash) for (const im of s.implements) edge('implements', resolve(im.from), resolve(im.to), path, 1);
    for (const w of f.writes) edge('writes', w.symbol ? resolve(w.symbol) : path, ensureTable(tableId(w.table)).id, path, 1);
    for (const r of f.reads ?? []) edge('reads', r.symbol ? resolve(r.symbol) : path, ensureTable(tableId(r.table)).id, path, 1);
    for (const r of f.routes) if (r.handler) edge('handles', r.id, resolve(r.handler), path, 1);
    if (!local.length) continue;
    for (const e of local.sort((a, b) => (a.id < b.id ? -1 : 1))) edges.push(e);
    local.length = 0;
  }

  // ---- children, sorted by (rank, id); `order` is the sibling index (domains/cells: their grid index)
  for (const [parent, list] of Object.entries(children)) {
    list.sort((a, b) => rank.get(a)! - rank.get(b)! || (a < b ? -1 : a > b ? 1 : 0));
    const grid = parent === ROOT_ID || nodes[parent]!.kind === 'domain';
    for (let i = 0; i < list.length; i++) nodes[list[i]!]!.order = grid ? rank.get(list[i]!)! : i;
  }
  return { root: ROOT_ID, nodes, children, edges };
}

/** A file's label: its name, with the folder for index files (`vendor/news/index.ts` → `news/index.ts`). */
export function fileLabel(path: string): string {
  const parts = path.split('/');
  const name = parts.pop()!;
  return /^index\.[cm]?[jt]sx?$/.test(name) && parts.length ? `${parts.pop()}/${name}` : name;
}

/** Longest common directory of sorted paths (the common prefix of the first and last, cut at a `/`). */
function commonDir(sorted: string[]): string {
  const a = sorted[0]!;
  const b = sorted[sorted.length - 1]!;
  let i = 0;
  while (i < a.length && a[i] === b[i]) i++;
  return a.slice(0, Math.max(0, a.lastIndexOf('/', i - 1)));
}

/**
 * The facts the graph is built from: `ui.facts`, plus empty stubs for every file the log knows about but has no
 * facts for (placed files, files a turn touched or planned, planned import endpoints), so ghosts and fresh files
 * have a leaf. Cross-domain cell→cell imports follow `ui.edges` (the reducer's record of edge_added/removed), so
 * logs without `facts_changed` still project the same edges as `edgeViews`. A no-op when facts are current.
 */
export function graphFacts(ui: UIState): Record<string, FileFacts> {
  const out: Record<string, FileFacts> = { ...ui.facts };
  const stub = (path: string) => { if (!out[path] && !isPseudo(path)) out[path] = emptyFacts(path); };
  for (const [path, p] of Object.entries(ui.files)) if (p.kind !== 'ignored') stub(path);
  for (const t of ui.turns) {
    for (const p of Object.keys(t.paths)) stub(p);
    for (const c of Object.values(t.planned)) c.files.forEach(stub);
    t.unassigned.forEach(stub);
    for (const files of Object.values(t.tests)) files.forEach(stub);
    for (const s of t.steps) for (const f of [...s.files, ...s.imports.map((i) => i.from)]) stub(normalize(fileOf(f) ?? f));
    for (const e of Object.values(t.plannedEdges)) for (const i of e.imports) { stub(i.from); stub(i.to); }
    for (const e of t.edgesAdded) { stub(e.edge.from); stub(e.edge.to); }
  }
  if (!ui.map) return out;
  const mapper = createMapper(ui.map);
  const want = new Map<string, Set<string>>();
  for (const e of Object.values(ui.edges)) for (const f of e.files) { stub(f.from); stub(f.to); (want.get(f.from) ?? want.set(f.from, new Set()).get(f.from)!).add(f.to); }
  const cross = (a: string, b: string) => {
    const pa = mapper.place(a);
    const pb = mapper.place(b);
    return pa.kind === 'cell' && pb.kind === 'cell' && pa.domain !== pb.domain;
  };
  for (const [path, f] of Object.entries(out)) {
    const w = want.get(path);
    const keep = f.imports.filter((i) => isPseudo(i.to) || !cross(path, i.to) || !!w?.has(i.to));
    const extra = [...(w ?? [])].filter((to) => !f.imports.some((i) => i.to === to)).sort();
    if (keep.length !== f.imports.length || extra.length) out[path] = { ...f, imports: [...keep, ...extra.map((to) => ({ to, typeOnly: false }))] };
  }
  return out;
}

/** The context graph for a UI state (null before a map exists). */
export function graphOf(ui: UIState): ContextGraph | null {
  return ui.map ? buildGraph(ui.map, graphFacts(ui), ui.semantic) : null;
}
```

```text
// Journeys (NAVIGATION_PLAN §2, phase N10), server side: compute journeys from the repo's Tier 1 facts and fetch sites
// (pure, in @harness/core), name them with a small model (cached under .harness/journeys/<hash>.json by the hash of
// the step list; inferred until confirmed), and publish `journeys_updated` on load, after turns that change them, and on
// confirm. The namer never blocks anything: placeholder names go out first, model names follow.
import { existsSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { join } from 'node:path';
import { Hono } from 'hono';
import { query } from '@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk';
import {
  buildGraph, computeJourneys, findFetchSites, inferDispatch, journeyHash, reduce,
  type ContextGraph, type FileFacts, type Journey,
} from '@harness/core';
import type { Bus } from '../bus';
import type { Repo } from '../repo';

export type NamerInput = { root: string; journeys: { id: string; steps: string[] }[] };
export type Namer = (input: NamerInput) => Promise<{ names: { id: string; name: string }[]; cost: number | null }>;

const NAMES_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object', additionalProperties: false, required: ['names'],
  properties: {
    names: {
      type: 'array',
      items: { type: 'object', additionalProperties: false, required: ['id', 'name'], properties: { id: { type: 'string' }, name: { type: 'string' } } },
    },
  },
} as const;

export function namerPrompt(input: NamerInput): string {
  return [
    'Each block below is a user flow through a codebase: an entry point (UI page, HTTP route, CLI, script) followed by the code it runs, down to the services and tables it ends at.',
    'Give each flow a short product-language name a PM would use: 2–4 words, verb first, sentence case, no code names or URLs (e.g. "Start research", "Send a drafted email", "View usage").',
    'Return one name per id, using the exact ids given.',
    '',
    ...input.journeys.flatMap((j) => [`## ${j.id}`, ...j.steps.map((s, i) => `${i + 1}. ${s}`), '']),
  ].join('\n');
}

/** Real namer: a small, tool-less structured query. Model: `HARNESS_JOURNEY_MODEL` (default `claude-haiku-5-5`). */
export const sdkNamer: Namer = async (input) => {
  const q = query({
    prompt: namerPrompt(input),
    options: {
      cwd: input.root, model: process.env.HARNESS_JOURNEY_MODEL ?? 'claude-haiku-5-5', tools: [], settingSources: [], strictMcpConfig: true,
      outputFormat: { type: 'json_schema', schema: NAMES_SCHEMA as unknown as Record<string, unknown> }, maxTurns: 3,
    },
  });
  for await (const m of q) {
    if (m.type !== 'result') continue;
    if (m.subtype !== 'success' || !m.structured_output) throw Object.assign(new Error(`journey namer ${m.subtype}`), { cost: m.total_cost_usd });
    return { names: (m.structured_output as { names: { id: string; name: string }[] }).names ?? [], cost: m.total_cost_usd };
  }
  throw new Error('journey namer returned no result');
};

/** How a step reads in the namer's prompt: `<kind>: <label>` with the node's path or id for context. */
export function describeStep(graph: ContextGraph, step: Journey['steps'][number]): string {
  const n = graph.nodes[step.node];
  const where = step.node.includes('#') ? step.node : n?.path ?? step.node;
  return `${step.kind}: ${n?.label ?? step.node}${where !== n?.label ? ` (${where})` : ''}`;
}

/** Journeys for the repo's current facts and sources (deterministic; names are placeholders). */
export function journeysFor(repo: Repo): { journeys: Journey[]; graph: ContextGraph } {
  const facts: Record<string, FileFacts> = Object.fromEntries(repo.fileFacts);
  const sources = Object.values(facts).flatMap((f) => {
    const source = repo.current(f.path);
    return source === null ? [] : [{ path: f.path, source, symbols: f.symbols }];
  });
  const graph = buildGraph(repo.map, facts);
  return { journeys: computeJourneys(graph, facts, findFetchSites(sources), inferDispatch(sources, facts)), graph };
}

type Cache = { id: string; hash: string; steps: string[]; name: string };
type Confirmed = Record<string, { name: string; at: number }>;

export type JourneysOptions = { bus: Bus; repo: Repo; namer?: Namer | null };
export type Result = { ok: true; journey: Journey } | { ok: false; status: 404 | 409; error: string };

export function attachJourneys(opts: JourneysOptions) {
  const { bus, repo } = opts;
  const namer = opts.namer === undefined ? (process.env.HARNESS_JOURNEYS === '0' ? null : sdkNamer) : opts.namer;
  const dir = join(repo.root, '.harness', 'journeys');
  const confirmedPath = join(dir, 'confirmed.json');
  const work = new Set<Promise<unknown>>();
  const track = <T>(p: Promise<T>) => { work.add(p); const off = () => { work.delete(p); }; p.then(off, off); return p; };
  let naming = false;
  let again = false;
  let current: { journeys: Journey[]; graph: ContextGraph } | null = null;

  const readJson = <T>(p: string, fallback: T): T => { try { return existsSync(p) ? (JSON.parse(readFileSync(p, 'utf8')) as T) : fallback; } catch { return fallback; } };
  const cached = (hash: string) => readJson<Cache | null>(join(dir, `${hash}.json`), null);
  const confirmed = () => readJson<Confirmed>(confirmedPath, {});

  /** Confirmed names win (inferred: false); then cached model names; else the placeholder (both inferred). */
  function named(js: Journey[]): { journeys: Journey[]; unnamed: Journey[] } {
    const conf = confirmed();
    const unnamed: Journey[] = [];
    const journeys = js.map((j) => {
      const c = conf[j.id];
      if (c) return { ...j, name: c.name, inferred: false };
      const hit = cached(journeyHash(j));
      if (hit) return { ...j, name: hit.name, inferred: true };
      unnamed.push(j);
      return j;
    });
    return { journeys, unnamed };
  }

  const lastEmitted = () => JSON.stringify(reduce(bus.events).journeys);

  function publish(js: Journey[]) {
    if (JSON.stringify(js) !== lastEmitted()) bus.emit('journeys_updated', { journeys: js }, { turn: null });
  }

  /** Recompute, publish if anything changed, and name new journeys in the background. */
  function refresh(): Journey[] {
    if (!repo.map || !repo.hasMap()) return [];
    current = journeysFor(repo);
    const { journeys, unnamed } = named(current.journeys);
    publish(journeys);
    if (unnamed.length && namer) {
      if (naming) again = true;
      else track(name(unnamed));
    }
    return journeys;
  }

  async function name(list: Journey[]) {
    naming = true;
    const t0 = Date.now();
    const graph = current!.graph;
    try {
      const input = { root: repo.root, journeys: list.map((j) => ({ id: j.id, steps: j.steps.map((s) => describeStep(graph, s)) })) };
      const r = await namer!(input);
      mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });
      const byId = new Map(r.names.map((n) => [n.id, n.name.trim()]));
      for (const j of list) {
        const n = byId.get(j.id);
        if (!n) continue;
        const hash = journeyHash(j);
        writeFileSync(join(dir, `${hash}.json`), JSON.stringify({ id: j.id, hash, steps: j.steps.map((s) => s.node), name: n } satisfies Cache, null, 2));
      }
      bus.emit('maintenance_run', { agent: 'cartographer', trigger: 'journeys', ms: Date.now() - t0, cost: r.cost, ok: true }, { turn: null });
      if (current) publish(named(current.journeys).journeys);
    } catch (e) {
      bus.emit('maintenance_run', { agent: 'cartographer', trigger: 'journeys', ms: Date.now() - t0, cost: (e as { cost?: number }).cost ?? null, ok: false }, { turn: null });
      bus.emit('error', { message: `Journey naming failed: ${(e as Error).message}` }, { turn: null });
    } finally {
      naming = false;
      if (again) { again = false; schedule(); }
    }
  }

  /** Confirm a journey (optionally renaming it): it is no longer inferred. */
  function confirm(id: string, name?: string): Result {
    const js = reduce(bus.events).journeys;
    const j = js.find((x) => x.id === id);
    if (!j) return { ok: false, status: 404, error: `No journey ${id}.` };
    const text = (name ?? j.name).trim();
    if (!text) return { ok: false, status: 409, error: 'A journey name cannot be empty.' };
    mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });
    writeFileSync(confirmedPath, JSON.stringify({ ...confirmed(), [id]: { name: text, at: Date.now() } }, null, 2));
    const next = js.map((x) => (x.id === id ? { ...x, name: text, inferred: false } : x));
    publish(next);
    return { ok: true, journey: next.find((x) => x.id === id)! };
  }

  function schedule() {
    track(new Promise<void>((resolve) => setImmediate(() => {
      try { refresh(); }
      catch (e) { bus.emit('error', { message: `Journeys failed: ${(e as Error).message}` }, { turn: null }); }
      finally { resolve(); }
    })));
  }

  // After a scan (load, map accepted) and after every turn: recompute; emit only when the journeys changed.
  const off = bus.on((e) => { if (e.kind === 'repo_scanned' || e.kind === 'turn_ended') schedule(); });

  return {
    refresh() { schedule(); },
    confirm,
    /** Resolves once no recompute or naming job is in flight (for tests and shutdown). */
    async idle() { while (work.size) await Promise.allSettled([...work]); },
    detach: off,
  };
}

export type JourneysLoop = ReturnType<typeof attachJourneys>;

/** HTTP endpoints, mounted under /api by the server. */
export function journeyRoutes(j: JourneysLoop) {
  const r = new Hono();
  r.post('/journeys/:id/confirm', async (c) => {
    const body = await c.req.json<{ name?: string }>().catch(() => ({} as { name?: string }));
    const id = c.req.param('id');
    const res = j.confirm(id.startsWith('journey:') ? id : `journey:${id}`, body.name); // the bare slug works too
    return res.ok ? c.json(res) : c.json({ error: res.error }, res.status);
  });
  r.post('/journeys/refresh', (c) => { j.refresh(); return c.json({ ok: true }); });
  return r;
}

const PORT = Number(process.env.PORT ?? 4310);
const FALLBACK_MAP = resolve(here, '../../../fixtures/scout-agent.domains.yaml');

const bus = new Bus(REPO, { fresh: process.env.HARNESS_FRESH === '1' });
const sockets = new Set<WebSocket>();
const broadcast = (msg: unknown) => {
  const s = JSON.stringify(msg);
  for (const ws of sockets) if (ws.readyState === ws.OPEN) ws.send(s);
};
bus.on((event) => broadcast({ type: 'event', event }));

const repo = new Repo(REPO, bus);
// Tier 2 runs in a child process fed by repo_scanned / facts_changed; its status is ephemeral (not in the log).
const semantic = attachSemantic(bus, repo, { onStatus: (status) => broadcast({ type: 'semantic', status }), log: (l) => console.log(l) });
let session: Session | null = null;
let proposal: { yaml: string; source: 'cartographer' | 'fixture' } | null = null;
let busy = false;

function startSession() {
  repo.scan();
  repo.startWatcher();
  session = new Session(repo, bus, (m) => {
    if (m.type === 'busy') busy = m.busy;
    broadcast(m);
  });
  session.start();
}

/**
 * Load: use domains.yaml if present. Otherwise show the instant skeleton, then the best of the cartographer's K scored
 * candidates (HARNESS_CARTOGRAPHER=0, or a failed/empty run: the reference map), and wait for Confirm.
 */
async function load() {
  if (repo.hasMap()) {
    repo.loadMapFile();
    bus.emit('map_confirmed', { map: repo.map, source: 'file' }, { turn: null });
    startSession();
    return;
  }
  // ---- living map: the instant deterministic skeleton while the cartographer works (NAVIGATION_PLAN §4.2) ----
  showProposal(onboardingSkeleton(repo.root), 'cartographer');
  let yaml: string;
  let source: 'cartographer' | 'fixture' = 'cartographer';
  try {
    if (process.env.HARNESS_CARTOGRAPHER === '0') throw new Error('disabled');
    const k = Number(process.env.HARNESS_CARTOGRAPHER_K ?? 4);
    const best = await proposeOnboarding({ root: repo.root, bus, proposer: sdkProposer, k });
    if (!best) throw new Error('no valid candidate map');
    yaml = best.yaml;
    const s = best.score;
    bus.emit('chat', {
      role: 'system',
      text: `Cartographer: best of ${best.scored} scored candidate map(s): ${best.candidate.title} · a typical commit lights ${s.cellsLitMean.toFixed(1)} cells (skeleton ${best.skeleton.cellsLitMean.toFixed(1)}); ${s.unassigned} files unassigned.`,
    }, { turn: null });
  } catch (e) {
    if ((e as Error).message !== 'disabled') bus.emit('error', { message: `Cartographer failed, using the reference map: ${(e as Error).message}` }, { turn: null });
    yaml = readFileSync(FALLBACK_MAP, 'utf8');
    source = 'fixture';
  }

  if (session) return; // the user confirmed the skeleton before the cartographer answered
  showProposal(yaml, source);

function showProposal(yaml: string, source: 'cartographer' | 'fixture') {
  repo.setMap(yaml);
  proposal = { yaml, source };
  bus.emit('map_proposed', { map: repo.map, yaml }, { turn: null });
  // The shell plays the map assembling: one file_assigned per file, ~15 ms apart.
  const files = repo.listFiles();
  files.forEach((path, i) => setTimeout(() => bus.emit('file_assigned', { placement: repo.place(path) }, { path, turn: null }), i * 15));
}

const app = new Hono();

// ---- living map (NAVIGATION_PLAN §4): drift → cartographer proposals, accept/reject, survey ----
const living = attachLivingMap({ bus, repo });
app.route('/api', livingMapRoutes(living));
// ---- end living map ----
// ---- auditor + journeys (NAVIGATION_PLAN §4.6, N9/N10): advisory findings after each turn; journeys on load/turn end ----
const auditorLoop = attachAuditor({ bus, repo });
app.route('/api', auditorRoutes(auditorLoop));
const journeysLoop = attachJourneys({ bus, repo });
app.route('/api', journeyRoutes(journeysLoop));
// ---- end auditor + journeys ----
app.get('/api/info', (c) => c.json({ repo: REPO, session: bus.session, busy, proposal: !!proposal }));
app.get('/api/events', (c) => c.json(bus.events));
app.get('/api/semantic', (c) => c.json(semantic?.status() ?? { state: 'off' }));
app.post('/api/chat', async (c) => {
  const { text } = await c.req.json<{ text: string }>();
  if (!session) return c.json({ error: 'Confirm the map first.' }, 409);
  session.userMessage(text);
  return c.json({ ok: true });
});
app.post('/api/approve', (c) => { session?.approve(); return c.json({ ok: true }); });
app.post('/api/interrupt', (c) => { session?.interrupt(); return c.json({ ok: true }); });
app.post('/api/map/confirm', (c) => {
  if (!proposal) return c.json({ error: 'No proposal pending.' }, 409);
  writeFileSync(repo.mapPath, proposal.yaml);
  try { commitPaths(repo.root, ['domains.yaml'], 'docs: add domains.yaml architecture map'); }
  catch (e) { bus.emit('error', { message: `Could not commit domains.yaml: ${(e as Error).message}` }, { turn: null }); }
  repo.setMap(proposal.yaml);
  bus.emit('map_confirmed', { map: repo.map, source: proposal.source }, { turn: null });
  proposal = null;
  startSession();

  showProposal(readFileSync(FALLBACK_MAP, 'utf8'), 'fixture');

app.get('/api/file', (c) => {
  const p = c.req.query('path') ?? '';
  const rel = repo.rel(p);
  if (!rel || !existsSync(join(repo.root, rel))) return c.json({ error: 'not found' }, 404);
  return c.text(readFileSync(join(repo.root, rel), 'utf8'));

if (existsSync(shellDist)) app.use('/*', serveStatic({ root: shellDist }));

const server = serve({ fetch: app.fetch, port: PORT }, () => console.log(`Interpretability server on http://localhost:${PORT} · repo ${REPO}`));
const wss = new WebSocketServer({ server: server as never, path: '/ws' });
wss.on('connection', (ws) => {
  sockets.add(ws);
  ws.send(JSON.stringify({ type: 'hello', events: bus.events, busy, session: bus.session }));
  ws.on('close', () => sockets.delete(ws));

process.on('SIGINT', shutdown);
process.on('SIGTERM', shutdown);
```

```text
/** What the inspector shows: a cell, a v1 domain edge (cell pair), Unassigned; and in v2 a file, any other node, or a drawn edge. */

  | { unassigned: true }

/**
```
