```typescript
import { submitPlan, type PlanHooks } from '../../../apps/server/src/harness-tools';
import { listDecisions, recordProtects } from '../../../apps/server/src/decisions';
import type { EventData, HarnessEvent } from '../src/events';
import { linkDecision } from '../src/mapedit';
import { fixtureRepo, mapYaml } from './helpers';

const dirs: string[] = [];
const ENV = ['GIT_AUTHOR_NAME', 'GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL', 'GIT_COMMITTER_NAME', 'GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL'] as const;
beforeAll(() => { for (const k of ENV) process.env[k] = k.endsWith('EMAIL') ? 't@t' : 't'; });
afterAll(() => {
  for (const d of dirs) rmSync(d, { recursive: true, force: true });
  for (const k of ENV) delete process.env[k];
});

const DR4 = `---
id: DR-4
title: Filings go through the gateway, in a filing mode that keeps figures intact
outcome: Route it through the Model gateway (every model call, with redaction and cost logging) instead of importing vendor/llm-anthropic/index.ts directly
status: made
type: standing
invariant: DR-1
anchors:
  paths:
    - src/tools/filing-summarize.ts
rejected: Add an exception for src/tools/filing-summarize.ts and record why
session: 1
---

The user chose A.
`;

function setup() {
  const root = realpathSync(mkdtempSync(join(process.env.HARNESS_TEST_TMP ?? tmpdir(), 'harness-b4-')));
  dirs.push(root);
  cpSync(fixtureRepo, root, { recursive: true });
  writeFileSync(join(root, 'domains.yaml'), linkDecision(mapYaml, 'DR-1', 'DR-4'));
  mkdirSync(join(root, 'decisions'));
  writeFileSync(join(root, 'decisions/DR-4.md'), DR4);
  execFileSync('git', ['init', '-q'], { cwd: root });
  execFileSync('git', ['add', '-A'], { cwd: root });
  execFileSync('git', ['commit', '-qm', 'init'], { cwd: root });
  const bus = new Bus(root, { fresh: true });
  const repo = new Repo(root, bus);
  repo.loadMapFile();
  repo.scan();
  const of = <K extends keyof EventData>(kind: K) => bus.events.filter((e): e is HarnessEvent & { data: EventData[K] } => e.kind === kind).map((e) => e.data);
  return { root, bus, repo, of };
}

const hooks: PlanHooks = { onPlan: () => {}, takeNotes: () => [] };

/** Beat 3's build in the decision turn: the tool through the gateway, a filing mode in redact.ts, a gateway test. */
function beat3Turn(root: string, bus: Bus, repo: Repo) {
  bus.turn = 't1';
  bus.emit('turn_started', { prompt: 'Can we add a tool that summarizes a prospect\'s latest 10-K?', head: '', baseline: '' });
  bus.emit('decision_recorded', { id: 'DR-4', title: 'Filings go through the gateway, in a filing mode that keeps figures intact', invariant: 'DR-1', option: 'A', paths: ['src/tools/filing-summarize.ts'], alike: false });
  const edit = (path: string, text: string, append = false) => {
    if (append) appendFileSync(join(root, path), text); else writeFileSync(join(root, path), text);
    return repo.fileChanged(path, { tool: 'Edit' });
  };
  const redact = readFileSync(join(root, 'src/gateway/redact.ts'), 'utf8');
  edit('src/gateway/redact.ts', redact.replace('export function redact(text: string, _names: unknown[]): string {', 'export function redact(text: string, _names: unknown[], mode: "default" | "filing" = "default"): string {\n  if (mode === "filing") return text;'));
  edit('src/tools/filing-summarize.ts', 'import { complete } from "../gateway/complete";\nexport async function filingSummarize(text: string) { return complete({ purpose: "filing", messages: [text] }); }\n');
  edit('test/gateway/complete.test.ts', '\ndescribe("filing mode", () => it("keeps figures intact", () => expect(1).toBe(1)));\n', true);
}

describe('recordProtects (decision turn end)', () => {
  it('writes protects into the DR file, commits only it, and re-emits decision_recorded with protects', () => {
    const { root, bus, repo, of } = setup();
    beat3Turn(root, bus, repo);
    bus.emit('turn_ended', { added: 0, removed: 0, files: [], reason: 'success' });
    const done = recordProtects(repo, bus, 't1');
    const protects = { paths: ['src/gateway/redact.ts', 'test/gateway/complete.test.ts'], symbols: ['src/gateway/redact.ts#redact'] };
    expect(done).toEqual([{ id: 'DR-4', protects }]);
    const text = readFileSync(join(root, 'decisions/DR-4.md'), 'utf8');
    expect(parseYaml(/^---\n([\s\S]*?)\n---/.exec(text)![1]!)).toMatchObject({ id: 'DR-4', session: 1, protects });
    expect(text).toContain('\n---\n\nThe user chose A.\n');
    expect(execFileSync('git', ['log', '-1', '--format=%s', '--name-only'], { cwd: root, encoding: 'utf8' }).trim().split('\n').filter(Boolean))
      .toEqual(['docs(decisions): what DR-4 protects', 'decisions/DR-4.md']);
    expect(of('decision_recorded').at(-1)).toMatchObject({ id: 'DR-4', protects, option: 'A' });
    expect(listDecisions(root)[0]!.protects).toEqual(protects);
    // Once: a later call (e.g. a replayed turn end) leaves it alone.
    expect(recordProtects(repo, bus, 't1')).toEqual([]);
  });
});

/** A repo whose DR-4 already protects beat 3's filing mode and test (a later session). */
function protectedSetup() {
  const s = setup();
  beat3Turn(s.root, s.bus, s.repo);
  s.bus.emit('turn_ended', { added: 0, removed: 0, files: [], reason: 'success' });
  recordProtects(s.repo, s.bus, 't1');
  s.bus.turn = null;
  return s;
}

describe('plans that touch protected code (submit_plan)', () => {
  it('emits decision_touched per step and adds the reminder to the tool result; never a violation or a fork', () => {
    const { repo, bus, of } = protectedSetup();
    bus.turn = 't2';
    bus.emit('turn_started', { prompt: 'Redact every long number', head: '', baseline: '' });
    const out = submitPlan(repo, bus, hooks, {
      steps: [
        { n: 1, text: 'Widen the number pattern', files: ['./src/gateway/redact.ts'], imports: [] },
        { n: 2, text: 'Unrelated', files: ['src/orchestrator/agent.ts'], imports: [] },
        { n: 3, text: 'Extend the test', files: ['test/gateway/complete.test.ts'], imports: [], symbols: [] },
      ],
    });
    expect(of('decision_touched')).toEqual([
      { decision: 'DR-4', principle: 'Filings go through the gateway, in a filing mode that keeps figures intact', paths: ['src/gateway/redact.ts'], symbols: ['src/gateway/redact.ts#redact'], source: 'plan', step: 1 },
      { decision: 'DR-4', principle: 'Filings go through the gateway, in a filing mode that keeps figures intact', paths: ['test/gateway/complete.test.ts'], symbols: [], source: 'plan', step: 3 },
    ]);
    expect(out).toContain('No violations.\n\nThis plan touches what DR-4 protects: Filings go through the gateway, in a filing mode that keeps figures intact. Route it through the Model gateway (every model call, with redaction and cost logging) instead of importing vendor/llm-anthropic/index.ts directly. Keep it true (decided in session 1): scope the change so it still holds, and extend its test. Protected code here: src/gateway/redact.ts#redact, test/gateway/complete.test.ts.');
    expect(out).toContain('do not ask the user');
    expect(out).not.toContain('Exit plan mode when ready');
    expect(of('plan_violation')).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  it('a step naming only other symbols in the file does not touch it', () => {
    const { repo, bus, of } = protectedSetup();
    bus.turn = 't2';
    bus.emit('turn_started', { prompt: 'x', head: '', baseline: '' });
    const out = submitPlan(repo, bus, hooks, { steps: [{ n: 1, text: 'Add a helper', files: ['src/gateway/redact.ts'], imports: [], symbols: ['src/gateway/redact.ts#maskAccount'] }] });
    expect(of('decision_touched')).toHaveLength(0);
    expect(out).toContain('No violations. Exit plan mode when ready.');
    expect(of('planned').at(-1)!.steps[0]!.symbols).toEqual(['src/gateway/redact.ts#maskAccount']);
  });
});

type HookOut = { hookSpecificOutput?: { hookEventName: string; additionalContext?: string } };
type Inner = { afterEdit: (i: unknown, id: undefined, o: { signal: AbortSignal }) => Promise<HookOut> };

describe('edits that touch protected code (PostToolUse)', () => {
  it('returns additionalContext once per decision per turn, emits decision_touched for every touching edit', async () => {
    const { root, repo, bus, of } = protectedSetup();
    const session = new Session(repo, bus, () => {});
    const s = session as unknown as Inner;
    session.userMessage('We\'re seeing account numbers in briefs. Can we redact every long number?');
    const hook = (path: string) => s.afterEdit({ tool_name: 'Edit', tool_input: { file_path: join(root, path) } }, undefined, { signal: new AbortController().signal });

    // An edit that changes no protected symbol: nothing.
    appendFileSync(join(root, 'src/gateway/redact.ts'), '\nexport const LONG_NUMBER = /\\d{8,}/g;\n');
    expect(await hook('src/gateway/redact.ts')).toEqual({});
    expect(of('decision_touched')).toHaveLength(0);

    // The protected function's body changes: reminder.
    const text = readFileSync(join(root, 'src/gateway/redact.ts'), 'utf8');
    writeFileSync(join(root, 'src/gateway/redact.ts'), text.replace('if (mode === "filing") return text;', 'if (mode === "filing") return text;\n  text = text.replace(LONG_NUMBER, "[NUMBER]");'));
    const first = await hook('src/gateway/redact.ts');
    expect(first.hookSpecificOutput).toEqual({
      hookEventName: 'PostToolUse',
      additionalContext: 'This edit touches what DR-4 protects: Filings go through the gateway, in a filing mode that keeps figures intact. Route it through the Model gateway (every model call, with redaction and cost logging) instead of importing vendor/llm-anthropic/index.ts directly. Keep it true (decided in session 1): scope the change so it still holds, and extend its test. Protected code here: src/gateway/redact.ts#redact.',
    });

    // The protected test changes too: an event (marker), but no second reminder this turn.
    appendFileSync(join(root, 'test/gateway/complete.test.ts'), '\n// long numbers\n');
    expect(await hook('test/gateway/complete.test.ts')).toEqual({});
    expect(of('decision_touched').map((t) => [t.source, t.paths, t.symbols])).toEqual([
      ['edit', ['src/gateway/redact.ts'], ['src/gateway/redact.ts#redact']],
      ['edit', ['test/gateway/complete.test.ts'], []],
    ]);
    expect(of('edited').at(-1)).toMatchObject({ tool: 'Edit' });
  });
});
```

```typescript
import { useEffect, useLayoutEffect, useMemo, useRef } from 'react';
import { fileOf, sessionNumber, type UIState } from '@harness/core/view';
import { api, fakeMode } from '../connection';
import { useView } from '../derive';
import { useStore } from '../store';
import { reveal } from '../v2/reveal';
import { useLinks } from './links';
import { Markdown, type Links } from './Markdown';

export function ChatPane() {
  const v = useView();
  const delta = useStore((s) => s.delta);
  const busy = useStore((s) => s.busy);
  const conn = useStore((s) => s.conn);
  const scroller = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const chat = v.ui.chat;
  const replaying = !v.live;
  const links = useLinks(v.ui);

  useLayoutEffect(() => {
    const el = scroller.current;
    if (el) el.scrollTop = el.scrollHeight;
  }, [chat.length, delta, v.ui.errors.length, v.ui.pendingFork, v.ui.awaitingApproval]);

  const empty = !chat.length && !delta;
  return (
    <aside className="chat">
      <div className="chat-head">
        <span className="chat-title">Claude Code</span>
        <span className={`chat-state ${busy ? 'is-busy' : ''}`}>
          {replaying ? 'Replaying' : conn === 'down' ? 'Offline' : busy ? 'Working' : 'Ready'}
        </span>
      </div>

      <div className="chat-log" ref={scroller}>
        {empty && (
          <div className="chat-empty">
            <p>Ask Claude to change something. The map shows what it plans and what it does.</p>
            <p className="chat-example">“Add a tool that summarizes a prospect's latest 10-K.”</p>
            <p className="chat-tip">Shift-click anything on the map to point at it in your message.</p>
          </div>
        )}
        {chat.map((m, i) => (
          <div key={i} className={`msg msg-${m.role}`}>
            {m.context?.length ? <Chips ids={m.context} ui={v.ui} /> : null}
            {m.role === 'assistant' ? <Markdown text={m.text} links={links} /> : <p>{m.text}</p>}
          </div>
        ))}
        {busy && v.live && delta && (
          <div className="msg msg-assistant msg-streaming">
            <Markdown text={delta} links={links} />
          </div>
        )}
        {v.ui.errors.map((e, i) => (
          <div key={`e${i}`} className="msg msg-note">{e}</div>
        ))}
      </div>

      {v.ui.pendingFork && <ForkCard />}
      {v.ui.awaitingApproval && !v.ui.pendingFork && <ApprovalCard plan={v.ui.awaitingApproval.plan} turn={v.ui.awaitingApproval.turn} disabled={replaying} links={links} />}
      <Composer disabled={replaying || conn === 'down'} busy={busy && v.live} why={replaying ? 'Replaying. Go live to send.' : 'Waiting for the server.'} />
    </aside>
  );
}

/** A short name for a pointed-at map node: a symbol's name, a file's name, "Domain › Layer" for a cell. */
export function chipLabel(ui: UIState, id: string): { label: string; kind: string } {
  const map = ui.map;
  let m = id.match(/^cell:([^/]+)\/(.+)$/);
  if (m) {
    const d = map?.domains.find((x) => x.id === m![1]);
    const l = map?.layers.find((x) => x.id === m![2]);
    return { label: `${d?.name ?? m[1]} › ${l?.name ?? m[2]}`, kind: 'cell' };
  }
  m = id.match(/^domain:(.+)$/);
  if (m) return { label: map?.domains.find((x) => x.id === m![1])?.name ?? m[1]!, kind: 'domain' };
  m = id.match(/^(vendor|table|route):(.+)$/);
  if (m) return { label: m[2]!, kind: m[1]! };
  m = id.match(/^group:.*\/([^/]+)$/);
  if (m) return { label: `${m[1]}/`, kind: 'folder' };
  const file = fileOf(id);
  if (file && id.includes('#')) return { label: `${file.slice(file.lastIndexOf('/') + 1)} › ${id.slice(id.indexOf('#') + 1)}`, kind: 'symbol' };
  if (file) return { label: file.slice(file.lastIndexOf('/') + 1), kind: 'file' };
  return { label: id, kind: 'node' };
}

function Chips({ ids, ui, onRemove }: { ids: string[]; ui: UIState; onRemove?: (id: string) => void }) {
  return (
    <span className="chips" aria-label="Pointing at">
      {ids.map((id) => {
        const c = chipLabel(ui, id);
        return (
          <span key={id} className={`chip chip-${c.kind}`} title={id}>
            <button type="button" className="chip-go" onClick={() => reveal(id)}>
              <span className="chip-kind">{c.kind === 'symbol' ? 'ƒ' : c.kind === 'cell' ? '▦' : c.kind === 'file' ? '▤' : '·'}</span>
              {c.label}
            </button>
            {onRemove && <button type="button" className="chip-x" aria-label={`Stop pointing at ${c.label}`} onClick={() => onRemove(id)}>×</button>}
          </span>
        );
      })}
    </span>
  );
}

function ForkCard() {
  const v = useView();
  const setDraft = useStore((s) => s.setDraft);
  const fork = v.ui.pendingFork!;
  const first = fork.violations[0];
  if (!first) return null;
  return (
    <section className="card card-fork" aria-label="Choose how to proceed">
      <p className="card-kicker">{first.invariant} would be crossed</p>
      <p className="card-reason">{first.reason}</p>
      <div className="fork-options">
        {(['A', 'B'] as const).map((opt, i) => (
          <button key={opt} className="fork-option" disabled={!v.live} onClick={() => setDraft(`${opt} — `, true)}>
            <span className="fork-letter">{opt}</span>
            <span>{first.options[i]}</span>
          </button>
        ))}
      </div>
      <p className="card-hint">Pick one and add your reason. It becomes a decision later sessions follow.</p>
    </section>
  );
}

/** Beat 4: one line per standing decision whose protected code the awaiting plan touches. */
function touchedLines(ui: UIState, turnId: string | null) {
  const turn = turnId ? ui.turns.find((t) => t.id === turnId) : ui.turns.at(-1);
  const out: { id: string; principle: string; session: number; where: string[] }[] = [];
  for (const t of turn?.touched ?? []) {
    const d = ui.decisions.find((x) => x.id === t.decision);
    let line = out.find((x) => x.id === t.decision);
    if (!line) out.push((line = { id: t.decision, principle: t.principle || d?.title || '', session: d ? sessionNumber(ui, d.session) : 0, where: [] }));
    for (const w of [...t.symbols, ...t.paths]) if (!line.where.includes(w) && !line.where.some((x) => x.startsWith(`${w}#`))) line.where.push(w);
  }
  return out;
}

function ApprovalCard({ plan, turn, disabled, links }: { plan: string; turn: string | null; disabled: boolean; links: Links }) {
  const v = useView();
  const touched = useMemo(() => touchedLines(v.ui, turn), [v.ui, turn]);
  const steps = (turn ? v.ui.turns.find((t) => t.id === turn) : v.turn)?.steps ?? [];
  return (
    <section className="card card-approve" aria-label="Plan waiting for approval">
      <p className="card-kicker">Plan ready</p>
      {plan.trim() && (
        <div className="card-plan">
          <Markdown text={plan} links={links} />
        </div>
      )}
      {steps.some((s) => s.files.length || s.symbols?.length) && (
        <ol className="card-where" aria-label="Where each step lands">
          {steps.map((s) => {
            const refs = [...new Set([...(s.symbols ?? []), ...s.files.filter((f) => !(s.symbols ?? []).some((x) => x.startsWith(`${f}#`)))])];
            if (!refs.length) return null;
            return (
              <li key={s.n}>
                <span className="card-where-n">{s.n}</span>
                {refs.map((r) => (
                  <button key={r} type="button" className="md-link" title={`Show ${r} on the map`} onClick={() => links.open(r)}>
                    <code>{r.includes('#') ? `${r.slice(r.lastIndexOf('/') + 1, r.indexOf('#'))}#${r.slice(r.indexOf('#') + 1)}` : r.slice(r.lastIndexOf('/') + 1)}</code>
                  </button>
                ))}
              </li>
            );
          })}
        </ol>
      )}
      {touched.map((t) => (
        <div key={t.id} className="card-touched" role="note">
          <svg className="card-touched-mark" viewBox="0 0 12 14" width="13" height="15" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M6 0.6 11.2 2.6v4.1c0 3.1-2.2 5.6-5.2 6.7C3 12.3 0.8 9.8 0.8 6.7V2.6Z" /></svg>
          <p>
            Touches what <strong>{t.id}</strong> protects: {t.principle}
            {t.session ? <span className="card-touched-when"> (decided in session {t.session})</span> : null}
            {t.where.length > 0 && (
              <span className="card-touched-where">
                {t.where.map((w) => (
                  <button key={w} type="button" className="md-link" onClick={() => links.open(w)}><code>{w.slice(w.lastIndexOf('/') + 1)}</code></button>
                ))}
              </span>
            )}
          </p>
        </div>
      ))}
      <div className="card-actions">
        <button className="btn btn-primary" disabled={disabled} onClick={() => void api.approve()}>Approve plan</button>
        <span className="card-hint">or reply with changes</span>
      </div>
    </section>
  );
}

function Composer({ disabled, busy, why }: { disabled: boolean; busy: boolean; why: string }) {
  const draft = useStore((s) => s.draft);
  const focusTick = useStore((s) => s.focusTick);
  const setDraft = useStore((s) => s.setDraft);
  const pointing = useStore((s) => s.pointing);
  const togglePoint = useStore((s) => s.togglePoint);
  const clearPoint = useStore((s) => s.clearPoint);
  const ui = useView().ui;
  const ta = useRef<HTMLTextAreaElement>(null);

  useEffect(() => {
    const el = ta.current;
    if (!el || !focusTick) return;
    el.focus();
    el.setSelectionRange(el.value.length, el.value.length);
  }, [focusTick]);

  useLayoutEffect(() => {
    const el = ta.current;
    if (!el) return;
    el.style.height = 'auto';
    el.style.height = `${Math.min(160, el.scrollHeight)}px`;
  }, [draft]);

  const send = () => {
    const t = draft.trim();
    if (!t || disabled) return;
    void api.chat(t, pointing);
    setDraft('');
    clearPoint();
  };

  return (
    <div className={`composer ${pointing.length ? 'has-chips' : ''}`}>
      {pointing.length > 0 && <Chips ids={pointing} ui={ui} onRemove={togglePoint} />}
      <div className="composer-row">
        <textarea
          ref={ta}
          rows={1}
          value={draft}
          disabled={disabled}
          placeholder={disabled ? why : fakeMode ? 'Fake log loaded; sending is off.' : pointing.length ? 'Say what to do with these' : 'Message Claude'}
          onChange={(e) => setDraft(e.target.value)}
          onKeyDown={(e) => {
            if (e.key === 'Enter' && !e.shiftKey && !e.nativeEvent.isComposing) {
              e.preventDefault();
              send();
            }
          }}
        />
        {busy ? (
          <button className="btn btn-stop" onClick={() => void api.interrupt()}>Stop</button>
        ) : (
          <button className="btn btn-primary" disabled={disabled || !draft.trim()} onClick={send}>Send</button>
        )}
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

```css
/* Wave 3 lane B: world-space overlays (journey, trace, proposal ghosts, inferred labels) and the node badge slot.
   Uses the v2 theme tokens; the agent indigo is the only saturated colour, red and amber mean a rule or the plan. */

.ov-svg { position: absolute; left: 0; top: 0; overflow: visible; pointer-events: none; z-index: 1450; }
.ov-svg.is-under { z-index: 1300; }
.ov-wash { fill: var(--v2-ground); opacity: 0.66; animation: ov-fade 260ms var(--ease, ease) both; }
@keyframes ov-fade { from { opacity: 0; } }

/* labels at constant screen size */
.ov-tag rect { fill: var(--v2-file); stroke: var(--v2-line); stroke-width: 1px; vector-effect: non-scaling-stroke; }
.ov-tag text { font-family: var(--v2-sans); font-weight: 600; fill: var(--v2-ink); }
.ov-tag.is-click { pointer-events: auto; cursor: pointer; }
.ov-tag.is-quiet rect { fill: var(--v2-cell); }
.ov-tag.is-quiet text { fill: var(--v2-ink-2); font-weight: 500; }
.ov-tag.is-hub rect { fill: var(--v2-agent-wash); stroke: var(--v2-agent); }
.ov-tag.is-hub text { fill: var(--v2-agent); }
```

```typescript
// Real Scout facts (fixtures/scout-real.json: Tier 1 facts, fetch sites, inferred dispatch, violations and journeys
// of scout-agent@demo-start under the reference map): provider paths (beat 1), `fetches` edges, and journeys unchanged
// by them.
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import type { FileFacts } from '../src/contracts/facts';
import type { Journey } from '../src/contracts/cartography';
import type { Violation } from '../src/rules';
import { buildGraph, trace } from '../src/graph';
import { computeJourneys, fetchEdges, providerPaths, type FetchSite, type InferredEdge } from '../src/journeys';
import { createMapper } from '../src/mapper';
import { overviewText } from '../../../apps/server/src/graph-tools';
import { loadMap } from './helpers';

type Fixture = { fileFacts: Record<string, FileFacts>; sites: FetchSite[]; inferred: InferredEdge[]; violations: Violation[]; journeys: Journey[] };
const fx = JSON.parse(readFileSync(new URL('./fixtures/scout-real.json', import.meta.url), 'utf8')) as Fixture;
const map = loadMap();

describe('providerPaths on real Scout (beat 1)', () => {
  it('classifies the three kinds of path to the model provider', () => {
    const paths = providerPaths(buildGraph(map, fx.fileFacts), map, fx.violations);
    expect(paths.map((p) => [p.class, p.invariant ?? null, p.nodes.join(' → ')])).toEqual([
      ['violation', 'DR-1', 'src/tools/news-summarize.ts → vendor/llm-anthropic/index.ts#Anthropic → vendor:@anthropic-ai/sdk'],
      ['uncosted', null, 'vendor/news/index.ts#transcriptLive → vendor:@anthropic-ai/sdk'],
      ['uncosted', null, 'vendor/search/index.ts#liveClient → vendor:@anthropic-ai/sdk'],
      ['gateway', null, 'src/gateway/embed.ts#embedMany → vendor/embeddings/index.ts#createEmbeddings'],
      ['gateway', null, 'src/gateway/providers.ts#AnthropicProvider → vendor/llm-anthropic/index.ts#Anthropic → vendor:@anthropic-ai/sdk'],
      ['gateway', null, 'src/gateway/providers.ts#OpenAIProvider → vendor/llm-openai/index.ts#OpenAI'],
    ]);
    expect(paths.every((p) => p.provider === p.nodes.at(-1))).toBe(true);
  });

  it('without a current violation the bypass reads as uncosted, and a map with no only_via rule has no provider paths', () => {
    const g = buildGraph(map, fx.fileFacts);
    expect(providerPaths(g, map, []).find((p) => p.nodes[0] === 'src/tools/news-summarize.ts')?.class).toBe('uncosted');
    expect(providerPaths(g, { ...map, invariants: map.invariants.filter((i) => i.kind !== 'only_via') }, fx.violations)).toEqual([]);
  });

  it('the overview tool states domains, edges, the violation and the provider paths', () => {
    const files = Object.keys(fx.fileFacts);
    const imports = Object.values(fx.fileFacts).flatMap((f) => f.imports.filter((i) => !i.to.startsWith('vendor:')).map((i) => ({ from: f.path, to: i.to })));
    const text = overviewText(buildGraph(map, fx.fileFacts), map, { files, imports, writes: [] }, createMapper(map), fx.violations);
    expect(text).toContain('6 domains × 5 layers (ui, entry, logic, data, external)');
    expect(text).toContain('- Model gateway (domain:gateway): Every model call, with redaction and cost logging.');
    expect(text).toContain('Rule violations now (1):\n- DR-1: src/tools/news-summarize.ts → vendor/llm-anthropic/index.ts (Model providers are only called through the model gateway)');
    expect(text).toContain('- RULE VIOLATION DR-1: src/tools/news-summarize.ts → vendor/llm-anthropic/index.ts#Anthropic → vendor:@anthropic-ai/sdk');
    expect(text).toContain('- outside the gateway, no rule broken (not redacted or cost-logged): vendor/search/index.ts#liveClient → vendor:@anthropic-ai/sdk');
    expect(text).toMatch(/- Research tools → Model gateway: \d+/);
  });
});

describe('fetches edges', () => {
  const edges = fetchEdges(fx.sites, fx.fileFacts);
  const g = buildGraph(map, fx.fileFacts, {}, edges);

  it('link UI symbols to the routes they call', () => {
    const fetches = g.edges.filter((e) => e.kind === 'fetches');
    expect(fetches.length).toBe(edges.length);
    expect(fetches.length).toBeGreaterThan(5);
    expect(fetches.every((e) => e.to.startsWith('route:') && g.nodes[e.from] && e.owner.startsWith('web/'))).toBe(true);
    expect(fetches.find((e) => e.to === 'route:POST /api/runs')).toBeTruthy();
    expect(buildGraph(map, fx.fileFacts).edges.some((e) => e.kind === 'fetches')).toBe(false);
  });

  it('trace walks them: from the UI call to the run loop', () => {
    const start = g.edges.find((e) => e.kind === 'fetches' && e.to === 'route:POST /api/runs')!.from;
    const paths = trace(g, start);
    expect(paths.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    expect(paths[0]![1]).toBe('route:POST /api/runs');
  });

  it('journeys are identical whether the graph carries the fetches edges or not (and to the recorded output)', () => {
    const withEdges = computeJourneys(g, fx.fileFacts, fx.sites, fx.inferred);
    const without = computeJourneys(buildGraph(map, fx.fileFacts), fx.fileFacts, fx.sites, fx.inferred);
    expect(withEdges).toEqual(fx.journeys);
    expect(without).toEqual(fx.journeys);
    expect(fx.journeys.length).toBe(14);
  });
});
```

```typescript
// CodeMirror 6 for the code pane (N6 Code level), loaded on first open only. Read-only. Gutters: this turn's diff
// (added / changed / deleted-here bars), then marks (plan step badges, a decision shield on protected code, a rule
// mark on a crossing), then line numbers. Inline: the reason a line crosses a rule, under that line.
import { EditorState, RangeSetBuilder, type Extension } from '@codemirror/state';
import { Decoration, EditorView, GutterMarker, WidgetType, gutter, lineNumbers, type DecorationSet } from '@codemirror/view';
import { defaultHighlightStyle, syntaxHighlighting } from '@codemirror/language';
import { javascript } from '@codemirror/lang-javascript';

export type DiffMark = 'added' | 'changed' | 'deleted';
export type LineMark =
  | { kind: 'step'; steps: number[]; title: string }
  | { kind: 'decision'; id: string; title: string; touched: boolean }
  | { kind: 'violation'; rule: string; title: string; isNew: boolean };
/** Everything the pane draws, by 1-based line number. */
export type Marks = {
  diff: Map<number, DiffMark>;
  marks: Map<number, LineMark[]>;
  /** Lines inside code a decision protects (a faint ink band). */
  protectedLines: Set<number>;
  /** Inline reasons, shown as a block under the line. */
  notes: Map<number, { text: string; kind: 'violation' | 'decision' }>;
  /** Lines of the symbol the pane was opened at. */
  focus: { from: number; to: number } | null;
};

class DiffMarker extends GutterMarker {
  constructor(readonly kind: DiffMark) { super(); }
  eq(o: GutterMarker) { return o instanceof DiffMarker && o.kind === this.kind; }
  toDOM() {
    const el = document.createElement('span');
    el.className = `cm-diff cm-diff-${this.kind}`;
    el.title = this.kind === 'added' ? 'Added this turn' : this.kind === 'changed' ? 'Changed this turn' : 'Lines removed here this turn';
    return el;
  }
}

class MarksMarker extends GutterMarker {
  constructor(readonly list: LineMark[]) { super(); }
  eq(o: GutterMarker) { return o instanceof MarksMarker && JSON.stringify(o.list) === JSON.stringify(this.list); }
  toDOM() {
    const el = document.createElement('span');
    el.className = 'cm-marks';
    for (const m of this.list) {
      const b = document.createElement('span');
      b.title = m.title;
      if (m.kind === 'step') {
        b.className = 'cm-mark cm-mark-step';
        b.textContent = m.steps.join(',');
      } else if (m.kind === 'decision') {
        b.className = `cm-mark cm-mark-decision ${m.touched ? 'is-touched' : ''}`;
        b.innerHTML = '<svg viewBox="0 0 12 14" width="9" height="11" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M6 0.6 11.2 2.6v4.1c0 3.1-2.2 5.6-5.2 6.7C3 12.3 0.8 9.8 0.8 6.7V2.6Z"/></svg>';
        b.append(m.id);
      } else {
        b.className = `cm-mark cm-mark-violation ${m.isNew ? 'is-new' : ''}`;
        b.textContent = m.rule;
      }
      el.append(b);
    }
    return el;
  }
}

class NoteWidget extends WidgetType {
  constructor(readonly text: string, readonly kind: 'violation' | 'decision') { super(); }
  eq(o: WidgetType) { return o instanceof NoteWidget && o.text === this.text && o.kind === this.kind; }
  toDOM() {
    const el = document.createElement('div');
    el.className = `cm-note cm-note-${this.kind}`;
    el.textContent = this.text;
    return el;
  }
}

function decorations(state: EditorState, m: Marks): DecorationSet {
  const b = new RangeSetBuilder<Decoration>();
  const lines = state.doc.lines;
  for (let n = 1; n <= lines; n++) {
    const line = state.doc.line(n);
    const cls: string[] = [];
    const d = m.diff.get(n);
    if (d === 'added' || d === 'changed') cls.push(`cm-line-${d}`);
    if (m.protectedLines.has(n)) cls.push('cm-line-protected');
    if (m.marks.get(n)?.some((x) => x.kind === 'violation')) cls.push('cm-line-violation');
    if (m.focus && n >= m.focus.from && n <= m.focus.to) cls.push('cm-line-focus');
    if (cls.length) b.add(line.from, line.from, Decoration.line({ class: cls.join(' ') }));
    const note = m.notes.get(n);
    if (note) b.add(line.to, line.to, Decoration.widget({ widget: new NoteWidget(note.text, note.kind), block: true, side: 1 }));
  }
  return b.finish();
}

function extensions(m: Marks, path: string): Extension[] {
  const ts = /\.[cm]?tsx?$/.test(path);
  const jsx = /x$/.test(path);
  return [
    EditorState.readOnly.of(true),
    EditorView.editable.of(false),
    gutter({
      class: 'cm-gutter-diff',
      markers: (view) => {
        const b = new RangeSetBuilder<GutterMarker>();
        for (let n = 1; n <= view.state.doc.lines; n++) {
          const d = m.diff.get(n);
          if (d) b.add(view.state.doc.line(n).from, view.state.doc.line(n).from, new DiffMarker(d));
        }
        return b.finish();
      },
    }),
    gutter({
      class: 'cm-gutter-marks',
      markers: (view) => {
        const b = new RangeSetBuilder<GutterMarker>();
        for (let n = 1; n <= view.state.doc.lines; n++) {
          const list = m.marks.get(n);
          if (list?.length) b.add(view.state.doc.line(n).from, view.state.doc.line(n).from, new MarksMarker(list));
        }
        return b.finish();
      },
    }),
    lineNumbers(),
    ...(/\.(m|c)?[jt]sx?$/.test(path) ? [javascript({ typescript: ts, jsx })] : []),
    syntaxHighlighting(defaultHighlightStyle, { fallback: true }),
    EditorView.decorations.of((view) => decorations(view.state, m)),
    EditorView.theme({ '&': { height: '100%' }, '.cm-scroller': { overflow: 'auto' } }),
  ];
}

export type Editor = { destroy(): void; scrollTo(line: number): void };

export function mountEditor(parent: HTMLElement, text: string, path: string, marks: Marks): Editor {
  const view = new EditorView({ parent, state: EditorState.create({ doc: text, extensions: extensions(marks, path) }) });
  return {
    destroy: () => view.destroy(),
    scrollTo: (line) => {
      const n = Math.max(1, Math.min(view.state.doc.lines, line));
      view.dispatch({ effects: EditorView.scrollIntoView(view.state.doc.line(n).from, { y: 'start', yMargin: 48 }) });
    },
  };
}
```

```text
// Drives one demo turn against a running server: prompt → (fork → answer A) → approve → wait for turn_ended.
const base = process.argv[2] ?? 'http://localhost:4320';
const prompt = process.argv[3] ?? "Add a tool that summarizes a prospect's latest 10-K. Base it on src/tools/news-summarize.ts, which is the closest existing example.";
const answer = process.argv[4] ?? 'A — route it through the gateway like the other tools.';
const post = (p, b) => fetch(base + p, { method: 'POST', headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' }, body: JSON.stringify(b ?? {}) });
let seen = 0;
const t0 = Date.now();
const show = (e) => {
  const d = e.data ?? {};
  const extra = e.kind === 'chat' ? `${d.role}: ${String(d.text).slice(0, 300).replace(/\n/g, ' ⏎ ')}`
    : e.kind === 'planned' ? `cells=${d.cells.map((c) => `${c.domain}/${c.layer}[${c.steps}]`).join(',')} edges=${d.edges.map((x) => `${x.from}->${x.to}`).join(',')} unassigned=${d.unassigned}`
    : e.kind.includes('violation') || e.kind === 'gate_blocked' ? (d.violation ? d.violation.reason : `${(d.violations ?? []).length} violations`)
    : e.kind === 'edited' ? `${e.path} +${d.added} -${d.removed}${d.unattributed ? ' UNATTRIBUTED' : ''} cell=${e.cell ? e.cell.domain + '/' + e.cell.layer : '-'}`
    : e.kind === 'turn_ended' ? `+${d.added} -${d.removed} ${d.files} (${d.reason})`
    : e.kind === 'decision_recorded' ? `${d.id} ${d.title} alike=${d.alike}`
    : ['edge_added', 'edge_removed'].includes(e.kind) ? `${d.from}->${d.to} ${d.edge.from}`
    : e.path ? `${e.path} ${e.cell ? e.cell.domain + '/' + e.cell.layer : ''}` : '';
  console.log(`${((Date.now() - t0) / 1000).toFixed(1).padStart(6)}s ${e.kind.padEnd(18)} ${extra}`);
};
const sleep = (ms) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms));
async function poll(until) {
  while (true) {
    const ev = await (await fetch(base + '/api/events')).json();
    for (const e of ev.slice(seen)) { show(e); const r = until(e); if (r) { seen = ev.indexOf(e) + 1; return r; } }
    seen = ev.length;
    await sleep(500);
  }
}
seen = Math.max(0, (await (await fetch(base + '/api/events')).json()).length - 1);
// (no startup wait)
await post('/api/chat', { text: prompt });
let answered = false;
while (true) {
  const e = await poll((e) => ['fork_asked', 'approval_requested', 'turn_ended', 'error'].includes(e.kind) && e);
  if (e.kind === 'fork_asked' && !answered) { answered = true; await sleep(300); console.log('>>> answering', answer); await post('/api/chat', { text: answer }); }
  else if (e.kind === 'approval_requested') { await sleep(300); console.log('>>> approve'); await post('/api/approve'); }
  else if (e.kind === 'turn_ended') break;
  else if (e.kind === 'error' && /Session ended/.test(e.data.message)) break;
}
process.exit(0);
```

```typescript
// What the code pane marks on one file, as a pure function of the reduced log, the file's text and its diff against
// the turn baseline: diff bars, plan step badges, rule crossings (on the import line, with the reason inline) and
// decision shields on the code a standing decision protects (beat 4). No React, no CodeMirror: tested in node.
import { fileOf, type TurnState, type UIState, type Violation } from '@harness/core/view';
import type { DiffMark, LineMark, Marks } from './editor';

export type Hunk = { oldStart: number; oldLines: number; newStart: number; newLines: number; lines: string[] };

/** 1-based line of a string offset. */
export function lineAt(text: string, offset: number): number {
  let n = 1;
  for (let i = 0; i < Math.min(offset, text.length); i++) if (text.charCodeAt(i) === 10) n++;
  return n;
}

/** Diff bars: lines a hunk adds (no old lines) are `added`, lines it replaces `changed`, a pure deletion marks the line after. */
export function diffMarks(hunks: readonly Hunk[], lines: number): Map<number, DiffMark> {
  const out = new Map<number, DiffMark>();
  for (const h of hunks) {
    if (h.newLines > 0) {
      for (let n = h.newStart; n < h.newStart + h.newLines; n++) out.set(n, h.oldLines === 0 ? 'added' : 'changed');
    } else {
      const at = Math.min(Math.max(1, h.newStart + 1), Math.max(1, lines));
      if (!out.has(at)) out.set(at, 'deleted');
    }
  }
  return out;
}

/**
 * Lines of a symbol: its span in the current facts, else (a planned symbol Tier 1 doesn't list, like a module-level
 * regex const) the first line that declares its last name segment.
 */
export function symbolLines(ui: UIState, text: string, id: string): { from: number; to: number } | null {
  const file = fileOf(id);
  if (!file || !id.includes('#')) return null;
  const s = ui.facts[file]?.symbols.find((x) => x.id === id);
  if (s && s.span.end > s.span.start && s.span.end <= text.length + 1) return { from: lineAt(text, s.span.start), to: lineAt(text, Math.max(s.span.start, s.span.end - 1)) };
  const name = id.slice(id.indexOf('#') + 1).split('.').pop()!.replace(/~\d+$/, '');
  if (!/^[\w$]+$/.test(name)) return null;
  const decl = new RegExp(`(?:^|[\\s(])(?:export\\s+)?(?:default\\s+)?(?:async\\s+)?(?:const|let|var|function\\*?|class|type|interface|enum)\\s+${name.replace(/\$/g, '\\$')}\\b|^\\s*(?:(?:public|private|protected|static|readonly|async|get|set)\\s+)*${name.replace(/\$/g, '\\$')}\\s*[(:=<]`, 'm');
  const m = decl.exec(text);
  if (!m) return null;
  const line = lineAt(text, m.index + (m[0].startsWith('\n') ? 1 : 0));
  return { from: line, to: line };
}

/** The import line a violation is about (its target's module name), else line 1. */
function violationLine(text: string, v: Violation): number {
  if (!v.target) return 1;
  const parts = v.target.replace(/\.[cm]?[jt]sx?$/, '').split('/');
  const last = parts.at(-1) === 'index' ? parts.at(-2) : parts.at(-1);
  if (!last) return 1;
  const lines = text.split('\n');
  const i = lines.findIndex((l) => /\b(import|require|from)\b/.test(l) && l.includes(last));
  return i >= 0 ? i + 1 : 1;
}

export function computeMarks(ui: UIState, turn: TurnState | null, path: string, text: string, hunks: readonly Hunk[], focusId: string | null): Marks {
  const lineCount = text.split('\n').length;
  const marks = new Map<number, LineMark[]>();
  const push = (n: number, m: LineMark) => { const l = marks.get(n) ?? []; l.push(m); marks.set(n, l); };
  const notes: Marks['notes'] = new Map();
  const protectedLines = new Set<number>();

  // plan steps: a step naming symbols here badges their lines; a step naming only the file badges line 1
  const byLine = new Map<number, Set<number>>();
  for (const s of turn?.steps ?? []) {
    const syms = (s.symbols ?? []).filter((x) => fileOf(x) === path);
    const lines = syms.map((x) => symbolLines(ui, text, x)?.from).filter((x): x is number => !!x);
    const names = s.files.includes(path) || s.imports.some((i) => i.from === path);
    if (!lines.length && (names || syms.length)) lines.push(1);
    for (const n of lines) (byLine.get(n) ?? byLine.set(n, new Set()).get(n)!).add(s.n);
  }
  for (const [n, set] of [...byLine].sort((a, b) => a[0] - b[0])) {
    const steps = [...set].sort((a, b) => a - b);
    push(n, { kind: 'step', steps, title: steps.map((k) => `Step ${k}: ${turn!.steps.find((s) => s.n === k)?.text ?? ''}`).join('\n') });
  }

  // rule crossings: load-time ones, and this turn's plan and gate ones
  const seen = new Set<string>();
  const vios: { v: Violation; isNew: boolean }[] = [
    ...ui.violations.filter((v) => v.file === path).map((v) => ({ v, isNew: false })),
    ...[...(turn?.planViolations ?? []), ...(turn?.gateBlocks ?? [])].filter((v) => v.file === path && !ui.violations.some((x) => x.file === v.file && x.invariant === v.invariant)).map((v) => ({ v, isNew: true })),
  ];
  for (const { v, isNew } of vios) {
    const k = `${v.invariant}|${v.target ?? ''}`;
    if (seen.has(k)) continue;
    seen.add(k);
    const n = violationLine(text, v);
    push(n, { kind: 'violation', rule: v.invariant, title: v.reason, isNew });
    if (!notes.has(n)) notes.set(n, { text: `${v.invariant}${isNew ? ' (new)' : ''}: ${v.reason}`, kind: 'violation' });
  }

  // decisions: shields on the code each standing decision protects; stronger when this turn touches it
  const touched = new Set((turn?.touched ?? []).map((t) => t.decision));
  for (const d of ui.decisions) {
    const p = d.protects;
    if (!p) continue;
    const ranges: { from: number; to: number }[] = [];
    for (const sym of p.symbols) if (fileOf(sym) === path) { const r = symbolLines(ui, text, sym); if (r) ranges.push(r); }
    if (!ranges.length && p.paths.includes(path)) ranges.push({ from: 1, to: 1 });
    for (const r of ranges) {
      for (let n = r.from; n <= r.to; n++) protectedLines.add(n);
      push(r.from, { kind: 'decision', id: d.id, title: `${d.id} protects this: ${d.title}`, touched: touched.has(d.id) });
      if (touched.has(d.id) && !notes.has(r.from)) notes.set(r.from, { text: `${d.id} protects this: ${d.title}. This turn's plan touches it.`, kind: 'decision' });
    }
  }
  // what this turn touches here that a decision protects, when the decision's own lines aren't in this file
  for (const t of turn?.touched ?? []) {
    for (const sym of t.symbols) {
      if (fileOf(sym) !== path) continue;
      const r = symbolLines(ui, text, sym);
      if (!r || marks.get(r.from)?.some((m) => m.kind === 'decision' && m.id === t.decision)) continue;
      push(r.from, { kind: 'decision', id: t.decision, title: `Touches what ${t.decision} protects: ${t.principle}`, touched: true });
      if (!notes.has(r.from)) notes.set(r.from, { text: `Touches what ${t.decision} protects: ${t.principle}`, kind: 'decision' });
    }
  }

  return { diff: diffMarks(hunks, lineCount), marks, protectedLines, notes, focus: focusId ? symbolLines(ui, text, focusId) : null };
}

```

```typescript
// The code pane (NAVIGATION_PLAN §2, Code level): docked right of the map, read-only, opened from a symbol (double-
// click) or a path link in chat, scrolled to the symbol. Gutters show this turn's diff against the turn baseline, plan
// step badges, rule crossings and decision shields on protected code. CodeMirror loads on first open.
import { useEffect, useMemo, useRef, useState } from 'react';
import { fileOf, type HarnessEvent } from '@harness/core/view';
import { api } from '../../connection';
import { useView } from '../../derive';
import { useStore } from '../../store';
import { computeMarks, type Hunk } from './marks';
import type { Editor } from './editor';

export const CODE_W = 560;

/** The baseline a turn started from (`turn_started.baseline`), for the diff route when the server doesn't know the turn. */
function baselineOf(events: readonly HarnessEvent[], turn: string | null): string | null {
  if (!turn) return null;
  const e = events.find((x) => x.kind === 'turn_started' && x.turn === turn);
  return ((e?.data as { baseline?: string } | undefined)?.baseline) ?? null;
}

export function CodePane() {
  const code = useStore((s) => s.code);
  if (!code) return null;
  return <Pane key={code.path} path={code.path} symbol={code.symbol} nonce={code.nonce} />;
}

function Pane({ path, symbol, nonce }: { path: string; symbol: string | null; nonce: number }) {
  const v = useView();
  const events = useStore((s) => s.events);
  const close = useStore((s) => s.closeCode);
  const turn = v.turn;
  const edits = turn?.paths[path]?.edits ?? 0;
  const [text, setText] = useState<string | null | undefined>(undefined);
  const [hunks, setHunks] = useState<Hunk[]>([]);
  const [created, setCreated] = useState(false);
  const host = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const editor = useRef<Editor | null>(null);
  const base = baselineOf(events, turn?.id ?? null);

  // text and diff: refetched when this turn edits the file again
  useEffect(() => {
    let live = true;
    void api.file(path).then((t) => live && setText(t)).catch(() => live && setText(null));
    void api.diff(path, turn?.id ?? null, base).then((d) => {
      if (!live) return;
      setHunks(d?.hunks ?? []);
      setCreated(!!d?.created);
    });
    return () => { live = false; };
  }, [path, turn?.id, base, edits]);

  const marks = useMemo(() => (typeof text === 'string' ? computeMarks(v.ui, turn, path, text, hunks, symbol) : null), [v.ui, turn, path, text, hunks, symbol]);

  useEffect(() => {
    const el = host.current;
    if (!el || typeof text !== 'string' || !marks) return;
    let live = true;
    void import('./editor').then(({ mountEditor }) => {
      if (!live) return;
      editor.current?.destroy();
      el.textContent = '';
      editor.current = mountEditor(el, text, path, marks);
      if (marks.focus) editor.current.scrollTo(marks.focus.from);
    });
    return () => { live = false; };
  }, [text, marks, path]);
  useEffect(() => () => editor.current?.destroy(), []);
  // a repeated request for the same file re-scrolls
  useEffect(() => { if (marks?.focus) editor.current?.scrollTo(marks.focus.from); }, [nonce]); // eslint-disable-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps

  const p = v.ui.files[path];
  const map = v.ui.map;
  const where = p?.kind === 'cell' ? `${map?.domains.find((d) => d.id === p.domain)?.name ?? p.domain} › ${map?.layers.find((l) => l.id === p.layer)?.name ?? p.layer}`
    : p?.kind === 'test' ? `${map?.domains.find((d) => d.id === p.domain)?.name ?? p.domain} tests` : p?.kind === 'neutral' ? 'Shared' : 'Unassigned';
  const added = hunks.reduce((n, h) => n + h.lines.filter((l) => l.startsWith('+')).length, 0);
  const removed = hunks.reduce((n, h) => n + h.lines.filter((l) => l.startsWith('-')).length, 0);
  const sym = symbol && fileOf(symbol) === path ? symbol.slice(symbol.indexOf('#') + 1) : null;
  const decisions = marks ? [...new Set([...marks.marks.values()].flat().filter((m) => m.kind === 'decision').map((m) => (m as { id: string }).id))] : [];

  return (
    <aside className="v2-code" aria-label={`Code: ${path}`} onKeyDown={(e) => { if (e.key === 'Escape') { e.stopPropagation(); close(); } }}>
      <header className="v2-code-head">
        <div className="v2-code-title">
          <span className="v2-code-path">{path}{sym && <b>#{sym}</b>}</span>
          <span className="v2-code-where">{where}</span>
        </div>
        <button type="button" className="v2-code-close" onClick={close} aria-label="Close code">×</button>
      </header>
      <div className="v2-code-sub">
        {created ? <span className="v2-code-diff">Created this turn · +{added}</span> : added || removed ? <span className="v2-code-diff">This turn <span className="plus">+{added}</span> <span className="minus">−{removed}</span></span> : <span className="v2-code-quiet">{turn ? `Unchanged in turn ${v.turnIndex}` : 'No turn yet'}</span>}
        {decisions.map((d) => <span key={d} className="v2-code-dr">{d}</span>)}
      </div>
      {text === undefined && <p className="v2-code-note">Loading…</p>}
      {text === null && <p className="v2-code-note">Not on disk yet. {turn?.steps.some((s) => s.files.includes(path) || (s.symbols ?? []).some((x) => fileOf(x) === path)) ? 'The plan creates it.' : 'It may be planned but not created.'}</p>}
      <div ref={host} className="v2-code-body" />
    </aside>
  );
}
```

```mjs
// Drives one turn against a running server: prompt → (fork → answer) → approve → wait for turn_ended. Prints events.
const base = process.argv[2];
const prompt = process.argv[3];
const answer = process.argv[4] ?? 'A';
const post = (p, b) => fetch(base + p, { method: 'POST', headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' }, body: JSON.stringify(b ?? {}) });
let seen = 0;
const t0 = Date.now();
const show = (e) => {
  const d = e.data ?? {};
  const extra = e.kind === 'chat' ? `${d.role}: ${String(d.text).replace(/\n/g, ' ⏎ ')}`
    : e.kind === 'planned' ? `steps=${JSON.stringify(d.steps.map((s) => ({ n: s.n, text: s.text, files: s.files, symbols: s.symbols, imports: s.imports })))} cells=${d.cells.map((c) => `${c.domain}/${c.layer}[${c.steps}]`).join(',')} edges=${d.edges.map((x) => `${x.from}->${x.to}`).join(',')} avoided=${JSON.stringify(d.avoided ?? [])}`
    : e.kind.includes('violation') || e.kind === 'gate_blocked' ? (d.violation ? d.violation.reason : `${(d.violations ?? []).length} violations`)
    : e.kind === 'edited' ? `${e.path} +${d.added} -${d.removed}${d.unattributed ? ' UNATTRIBUTED' : ''} symbols=${JSON.stringify(d.symbols ?? null)}`
    : e.kind === 'turn_ended' ? `+${d.added} -${d.removed} ${d.files} (${d.reason})`
    : e.kind === 'decision_recorded' ? `${d.id} ${d.title} protects=${JSON.stringify(d.protects ?? null)}`
    : e.kind === 'decision_touched' ? JSON.stringify(d)
    : e.kind === 'approval_requested' ? String(d.plan).replace(/\n/g, ' ⏎ ')
    : e.kind === 'fork_asked' ? `${d.violations.length} violation(s): ${d.text.replace(/\n/g, ' ⏎ ')}`
    : e.kind === 'error' ? d.message
    : ['edge_added', 'edge_removed'].includes(e.kind) ? `${d.from}->${d.to} ${d.edge.from}→${d.edge.to}`
    : e.path ? `${e.path}` : '';
  if (['facts_changed', 'call_added', 'call_removed', 'facts_resolved', 'cursor'].includes(e.kind)) return;
  console.log(`${((Date.now() - t0) / 1000).toFixed(1).padStart(6)}s ${e.kind.padEnd(18)} ${extra}`);
};
const sleep = (ms) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms));
async function poll(until) {
  while (true) {
    const ev = await (await fetch(base + '/api/events')).json();
    for (let i = seen; i < ev.length; i++) { const e = ev[i]; show(e); const r = until(e); if (r) { seen = i + 1; return r; } }
    seen = ev.length;
    await sleep(500);
  }
}
seen = (await (await fetch(base + '/api/events')).json()).length;
await post('/api/chat', { text: prompt });
let answered = false;
while (true) {
  const e = await poll((e) => ['fork_asked', 'approval_requested', 'turn_ended', 'error'].includes(e.kind) && e);
  if (e.kind === 'fork_asked' && !answered) { answered = true; await sleep(300); console.log('>>> answering', answer); await post('/api/chat', { text: answer }); }
  else if (e.kind === 'approval_requested') { await sleep(300); console.log('>>> approve'); await post('/api/approve'); }
  else if (e.kind === 'turn_ended') break;
  else if (e.kind === 'error' && /Session ended/.test(e.data.message)) break;
}
await sleep(1500); // decision_recorded { protects } follows turn_ended
await poll(() => true).catch(() => {});
process.exit(0);

```

```text
  25.1s chat               assistant: Scout is a research-and-outreach agent built as 6 domains. Every request comes in through one of two entry points and flows down to vendors. ⏎  ⏎ ## Shape ⏎  ⏎ - **Channels**: requests come in through `src/channels/routes.ts` (HTTP) and `src/channels/cli.ts`. The React app (`web/src/app/**`) sits on top and has one page per domain. ⏎ - **Agent loop**: `src/orchestrator/agent.ts` and `planner.ts` plan each run. They pick tools through `tool-registry.ts` and save progress to the `runs` table via `run-state.ts`. ⏎ - **Research tools** (`src/tools/**`): company, news and SEC-filing lookups, backed by `vendor/search`, `vendor/news`, `vendor/sec-edgar` and `vendor/enrichment`. ⏎ - **Model gateway**: the intended single route to any model. `complete.ts` and `embed.ts` go through `redact.ts`, then `providers.ts` (OpenAI or Anthropic), and log spend to `cost_log` via `cost-ledger.ts`. ⏎ - **Memory**: notes and embeddings for each company (`notes-store.ts`, `vector-index.ts`, `retrieve.ts`). ⏎ - **Outreach**: email drafts (`draft-email.ts`), sending (`send.ts`), CRM sync and the `outreach_log`. ⏎  ⏎ Dependencies mostly point one way: Channels → Agent loop → Tools/Memory/Outreach → Gateway. There are no cycles. ⏎  ⏎ ## Risky ⏎  ⏎ 1. **Live rule violation (DR-1).** `src/tools/news-summarize.ts:1` creates its own `Anthropic` client instead of going through the gateway. Its prompt includes the contact's **name, title, email and phone**, so personal data goes to the provider without redaction, and the call isn't recorded in `cost_log`. It's also the newest commit (5d9e6d5), so it's likely a regression. ⏎ 2. **Model calls hidden inside vendor adapters.** `vendor/search/index.ts:48` (`liveClient`) and `vendor/news/index.ts:69` (`transcriptLive`) call `@anthropic-ai/sdk` directly in live mode. No rule is broken because they're in the external layer, but they get no redaction or cost tracking. That makes the Usage page under-report spend. ⏎ 3. **Channels reaches past the logic layer.** `routes.ts` imports data modules directly: `cost-ledger`, `notes-store`, `run-state`, `crm-sync` and `outreach-log`. The `POST /api/outreach/:id/send` route (`routes.ts:114`) calls `sendDraft` straight from HTTP. Whether a real email goes out depends on the sandbox flags (`routes.ts:136`), so check how that route is authenticated and gated before anything is deployed. ⏎ 4. **Shared config inside vendor code.** The vendor adapters import `src/shared/config`, so the "external" layer isn't a clean boundary. ⏎  ⏎ ## Over-engineered (mildly) ⏎  ⏎ - **`ToolRegistry`** (`src/orchestrator/tool-registry.ts:10`): a class with `register`, `get`, `has`, `list`, `describe` and keyword-based `matchGoal`, all for about 5 tools. A plain map or array would do the job, and keyword matching sits awkwardly next to a planner. ⏎ - **Two-provider gateway** (`providers.ts`: a `ChatProvider` interface, two classes, a cached factory): it's only justified if you really switch between OpenAI and Anthropic. If you only use Anthropic, it's extra weight. It's still the right place to put the fix for items 1 and 2. ⏎  ⏎ Overall it's a modest codebase (72 files) and the layering is reasonable. The real issue is that model calls are getting around the gateway, not that there's too much abstraction. ⏎  ⏎ If you want, I can plan the fix: move `news-summarize` onto `src/gateway/complete.ts` and send the vendor search/news model calls through the gateway too.
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-11 22:39:18Z)**_

You're right, and it's a structural problem, not a polish problem. Today Claude does the work in the chat pane and the map watches. To make Interpretability the center, the map has to become where the work happens: Claude's moves show as navigation on it, and your decisions are made on it.

**1. The map is the conversation; chat steps back.**
- The map goes full screen. Chat shrinks to a **command bar** at the bottom, plus a **one-line narrator** generated from events, not from Claude's prose:
  - "Reading `news-summarize.ts`"
  - "Plan: 3 steps across Research tools → Model gateway"
  - "Stopped: this crosses DR-1"
- Claude's full text is one click away, never the main thing. Claude is also told its replies are captions, so it writes one-sentence messages.
- **Follow is always on.** The camera travels with Claude through the graph, so you watch it navigate rather than read about it.
- **You decide on the map:**
  - **Fork:** the two options appear as two routes, and you click one.
  - **Approve:** you click Build on the planned path.
  - **Point:** you click a node.

  Typing stays for real instructions.

**2. Replace the grid with a flow.**
- The domain × layer grid is a filing cabinet. It shows where code sits, not how the app works. The defining shape of Scout is a request flowing through it: UI/routes → run loop → tools → gateway → Claude, with stores and services hanging off it.
- So the layout should run left to right in the direction of calls, like a service map or C4 container view, built deterministically from the call graph:
  - **domains are regions;** zooming into one shows its own internal flow;
  - **journeys are literally the paths you watch,** and the agent's plan lights its route through them.

**3. Minimalism.** Remove the turn tabs, the always-on ledger, the legend, step bars, and zero counts like "0 lines changed". The ledger becomes a short card at the end of a turn, showing only non-zero counts. One accent colour for Claude, red for rules, everything else quiet grey.

**What I'd do with the running lanes:**
- **Keep lane C (server).** Model pinning, the graph-first brief, `overview`, the protect markers and the path classifier all serve the new direction.
- **Pause lanes A and B (UI).** They're building panels, chips and grid-based views for the current layout. Their logic is reusable (function-level ghosts, journey data, marker roll-ups), but continuing spends effort polishing a direction you don't like.
- **Then a short design spike before rebuilding:** two or three flow-layout prototypes on real Scout data, screenshotted, for you to react to, as with the D1 comps.

**Which shape should replace the grid as the main map?**

Options:
- **Flow map (Recommended)** - Left-to-right in the direction of calls: entry points on the left, the run loop and tools in the middle, gateway/providers and stores on the right. Domains are regions; journeys are the paths you watch light up. Built deterministically from the call graph.
- **Service map** - Domains as large nodes laid out by dependency (layered, not force-directed), external services as satellites; edges thick by traffic/calls. Closer to Datadog/Kiali. Less 'request story', more 'system at a glance'.
- **Prototype both** - The design spike builds both on real Scout data (plus the map-first conversation) and you pick from screenshots.

**Pause the two UI lanes (A and B) while we redesign? Server lane C keeps going either way.**

Options:
- **Pause A and B (Recommended)** - Stop them now; their committed logic (symbol ghosts, marker rollups, journey/overlay data) is salvaged into the new UI. Saves usage on the old layout.
- **Let them finish** - They complete their current scope on the grid UI; we port what's useful afterwards. More spend, nothing lost.


**Answer:** Flow map (Recommended)" selected preview:

# Frontend Design

Approach this as the design lead at a design studio known for giving every client a distinct visual identity that is not mistaken for anyone else's. This client has already rejected proposals that felt cliché or templated, and is paying for a distinctive point of view: make deliberate, opinionated choices about palette, typography, and layout that are specific to this brief, and take aesthetic risk if justified.

## Ground your designs in the subject matter

If the brief does not identify what the product or subject matter is, identify it yourself before designing, and confirm with the client. You can come up with one concrete subject, the design's audience, and the design's primary job, as a proposal. If there's any information in your memory about the client's preferences or context about what they're building, use that as a hint. The subject's industry, subject matter, materials, and vernacular are where distinctive visual choices come from — a design for a toy for girls aged 8–11 will be very aesthetically different from a dashboard for financial analysts. Build with the brief's real content and subject matter throughout.

## Design principles

For web designs, the hero is the first thing viewers will see. Open with the most characteristic thing in the subject's world, in the form that is most appropriate: a headline, an image, an animation, a live demo, an interactive moment, or other treatments. Be deliberate with your choice: a big number with a small label, supporting stats, and a gradient accent is the default treatment, so only use it if that's truly the best option.

Typography carries the personality of the page. You don't need a different typeface for display or headline text and body content: use one family or two, and if two, make them clearly distinct.

Choose your typefaces deliberately, not the default families you would reach for on any other project, and set a clear type scale following the default guidance of The Elements of Typographic Style with intentional weights, widths, and spacing. When type is used as a headline or visual element, use the type treatment itself as an active part of the design, not a neutral delivery vehicle for the content.

Default to line lengths of less than 80 characters. Serif typefaces can have slightly longer line lengths; give serif body text slightly more line-height than a sans-serif.

Avoid these default typographic treatments; they are the commonest tells of a generated page:
- Accenting just a single word or phrase in a headline, like putting one word in italic/bold or a different color.
- Using all caps for labels.
- Adding unnecessary typographic labels above content.

Visual structure is information. Structural devices like outlines, borders, numbering, eyebrows, dividers, labels, etc., encode useful information about the content rather than decorate it. Many generic designs use numbered markers (01 / 02 / 03), but that's only appropriate if the content actually is a sequence — like a stepped process or a timeline. Before adding numbered markers, check the content really is a sequence.

Use non-user-triggered motion sparingly and deliberately, only to draw attention. A single orchestrated moment — one page-load sequence or one reveal — lands better than scattered effects; fade-and-slide-up entrances on each section and hover transitions on every card are the generic default and read as AI-generated. Motion that answers a person's action (opening, expanding, confirming) is welcome when it shows what changed.

Consider written content carefully. Often a design brief may not contain real content, and it's up to you to come up with copy and placeholder content. Copy can make a design feel as templated as the design itself. See the below section on writing for more guidance.

## Process: plan, review against the brief, build, critique

For calibration, AI-generated design right now clusters around some traits:
1. a warm cream background (near #F4F1EA) with a high-contrast serif display and a terracotta or warm-clay accent (often near #D97757 — Anthropic's own Claude-interaction accent, so on a user's brief it reads as a tell);
2. a near-black background with a single bright acid-green or vermilion accent;
3. a broadsheet-style layout with hairline rules, zero border-radius, and dense newspaper-like columns;
4. the SaaS-card kit: content chopped into identical rounded cards, one border-radius on everything regardless of hierarchy, the same soft grey shadow (rgba(0,0,0,.1)) under each, and gradient washes as decoration;
5. template chrome that appears whatever the subject: a tracked-out ALL-CAPS eyebrow label above every heading; meta strings joined with middle dots ('A · B · C'); labels built as 'WORD — fragment' with a spaced em dash; tinted near-black (#0B0B0B, #111) standing in for black; a monospace face for small data labels; a '→' appended to link and button text.

All traits are legitimate for some briefs, but they are defaults rather than choices, and they appear regardless of subject. Where the brief pins down a visual direction, follow it exactly — the brief's own words always win, including when it asks for one of these looks. Where it leaves an axis free, don't spend that freedom on one of these defaults. As with a hired human designer, there's often a careful balance between doing what you're good at and taking each project as a chance to experiment and learn.

Work in two passes. First, brainstorm a short design plan based on the client's design brief: create a compact token system with color, type, layout, and principles.
- Color: describe the core base palette as 4–6 named hex values.
- Type: the typefaces and their roles.
- Layout: a layout concept, using one-sentence prose descriptions and ASCII wireframes to ideate and compare. Include alignment guidance; should the content be left aligned, center aligned, justified?
- Principles: the high-level guidance for what makes this page unique.

Then review that plan against the brief before building: if any part of it reads like the generic default you would produce for any similar page (work through a similar prompt to see if you arrive somewhere similar) rather than a choice made for this specific brief — revise that part, say what you changed and why. Only after you've confirmed the relative uniqueness of your design plan should you start to write the code, following the revised plan.

When writing the code, be careful of structuring your CSS selector specificities. It's easy to generate CSS classes that cancel each other out (especially with a type-based selector like .section and an element-based selector like .cta). This can happen often with padding/margin between sections.

## Restraint and self-critique

Spend your boldness in one place. Let one element be the memorable thing, keep everything around it quiet and disciplined, and cut any decoration that does not serve the brief. Build to a quality floor without announcing it: responsive down to mobile, visible keyboard focus, reduced motion respected, visually accessible, harmonious color palettes. Critique your own work as you build, taking screenshots to review if your environment supports it — a picture is worth 1000 tokens. Consider Chanel's advice: before leaving the house, take a look in the mirror and remove one accessory. Human creatives have memory and always try to do something new, so if you have a space to quickly jot down notes about what you've tried, it can help you in future passes.

## More on writing in design

Words appear in a design for one reason: to make it easier to understand and use. They are design content, not decoration. Bring the same intentionality and minimalism to copywriting that you would bring to spacing and color. Before writing anything, ask what the design needs to say, and how it can best be said to help the person navigate the experience.

Write from the end user's perspective. Name things by what users will understand in simple language, not by how the system is built. A user manages notifications, not webhook config. Describe what something is or does in plain terms rather than selling it. Being specific and legible to new users is always better than being clever.

Use active voice as default. A CTA says exactly what happens when it is used: "Save changes," not "Submit." An action keeps the same name through the whole flow, so the button that says "Publish" produces a toast that says "Published." The vocabulary of an interface is the signposting for someone navigating the product. Cohesion and consistency are how people learn their way around.

Treat failure and emptiness as moments for direction, not mood. Explain what went wrong and how to fix it, in the interface's voice rather than a person's. Errors don't apologize, and they are never vague about what happened. An empty screen is an invitation to act.

Keep the tone conversational: plain verbs, sentence case, no filler, with tone matched to the brand and the audience. Let each written element do exactly one job.

**UI lanes A and B are paused.** Their in-progress work is committed as WIP on their own branches, so the useful logic can be salvaged into the new UI: function-level ghosts, decision-marker roll-ups, journey overlay data. Server lane C keeps going (model pinning, graph-first brief, `overview`, protect markers, three-path classifier, beat rehearsal), since all of that serves the new direction.

**The spike, one lane, running.** It builds a working prototype at `?ui=flow` on real Scout data, driven by scripted playback (no live Claude), with screenshots and a recording:
1. **Flow map instead of the grid.** Laid out left to right in the direction of calls: entry points → run loop → registry → tools → gateway → Claude, with stores and services hanging off. Domains are soft labelled regions, and the overview rolls up to about 15–30 components. The design path reads as one spine; the red bypass and the amber uncosted SDK calls stand out against it.
2. **Map-first conversation.** The map is full screen.
   - **Command bar:** you type requests at the bottom.
   - **Narrator line:** one sentence generated from events, e.g. "Reading `news-summarize.ts`", "Stopped: crosses DR-1, choose a route", "Building 2 of 3".
   - **Claude's full text:** one click away, never the main surface.
   - **Follow mode:** on by default, so the camera travels with Claude.
3. **Agent activity you can follow, including your annotation idea.** A fading trail of where Claude has been, its cursor, notes it pins on nodes, paths it highlights to show you something, and its plan drawn as a ghost route with step numbers on it.
   - I've added the events for this: `annotation`, `highlight`, `focus`.
   - The spike also writes a short spec for the MCP tools Claude will use to act on the map (`annotate`, `highlight`, `focus`), with a brief rule that says "show, don't tell".
4. **Decide on the map.**
   - **Fork:** the two options appear as two routes, and you click one.
   - **Approve:** a Build button sits on the ghost route.
   - **Beat 4:** the DR-4 marker on the node it protects.
   - **Beat 4b:** the rejected route drawn struck through.
5. **Minimal chrome.** No turn tabs, always-on ledger, legend, step bars or zero counts. A small card at the end of each turn shows only non-zero counts.

**When it's back** you'll get screenshots of the overview, beat 1 mid-answer with notes and highlighted paths, the beat 3 fork as two routes, building, and beat 4's marker. React to those before anything is built out for real. Then we rebuild the default UI on the chosen design and turn the annotation tools into real MCP tools.
