/** Top-level container for bare packages no `external` cell claims. */
export const VENDORS_ID = 'group:vendors';
/** A container holding more files than this is split into directory groups. */
export const GROUP_THRESHOLD = 12;
/** The layer whose cells hold external services; vendor packages and trace sinks live there. */
export const EXTERNAL_LAYER = 'external';

const KIND_RANK: Partial<Record<NodeKind, number>> = { group: 0, file: 1, table: 2, vendor: 3, symbol: 4, route: 5, entry: 6 };

const emptyFacts = (path: string): FileFacts => ({ path, hash: '', imports: [], writes: [], symbols: [], calls: [], routes: [], entries: [] });
const isPseudo = (id: string) => id.startsWith('vendor:') || id.startsWith('table:');
const normalize = (p: string) => p.replace(/\\/g, '/').split('/').filter((s) => s && s !== '.').join('/');

/**
 * Containment: repo → domain → cell → (group) → file → symbol (nested by `parent`), with routes and entries under
 * their file and tables under the cell that lists them. Test files sit in `tests:<domain>` under their domain;
 * files matching no cell in `unassigned`, shared code in `neutral` (both top-level, created when non-empty).
 * Bare packages (`vendor:<pkg>`) go into the `external` cell that claims them (a glob matching `<pkg>` or
 * `node_modules/<pkg>/…`, importing domains first), else into the top-level `group:vendors`.
 * A cell with confirmed `components` groups matching files by component; any container with more than
 * GROUP_THRESHOLD remaining files groups them by directory (recursively).
 * Leaf edges: imports (file→file), uses (file→vendor), calls, implements, handles (route→handler), writes (→table).
 * Tier 2 calls replace a file's syntactic calls when `semantic[path].hash === facts[path].hash`.
 */
export function buildGraph(
  map: DomainMap,
  facts: Readonly<Record<string, FileFacts>>,
  semantic: Readonly<Record<string, SemanticFacts>> = {},
): ContextGraph {
  const mapper = createMapper(map);
  const nodes: Record<string, GraphNode> = {};
  const children: Record<string, string[]> = {};
  const rank = new Map<string, number>();
  const add = (n: Omit<GraphNode, 'order'>, r: number): GraphNode => {
    const cur = nodes[n.id];
    if (cur) return cur;
    const node = n as GraphNode;
    node.order = 0;
    nodes[n.id] = node;
    rank.set(n.id, r);
    if (n.parent) (children[n.parent] ??= []).push(n.id);
    return node;
  };
  /** Copy a container's domain/layer onto a node (no spread: this runs per symbol). */
  const scoped = <T extends Omit<GraphNode, 'order'>>(n: T, from: GraphNode): T => {
    if (from.domain) n.domain = from.domain;
    if (from.layer) n.layer = from.layer;
    return n;
  };

  // ---- skeleton: domains in map order, cells in layer order (their order is the grid position)
  add({ id: ROOT_ID, kind: 'repo', parent: null, label: 'repo' }, 0);
  const layerIdx = new Map(map.layers.map((l, i) => [l.id, i]));
  map.domains.forEach((d, i) => {
    add({ id: domainId(d.id), kind: 'domain', parent: ROOT_ID, label: d.name, domain: d.id }, i);
    for (const l of map.layers) {
      if (l.id in d.cells) add({ id: cellId(d.id, l.id), kind: 'cell', parent: domainId(d.id), label: l.name, domain: d.id, layer: l.id }, layerIdx.get(l.id)!);
    }
  });
  const nd = map.domains.length;
  const ensureTop = (id: string) => {
    if (id === UNASSIGNED_ID) return add({ id, kind: 'unassigned', parent: ROOT_ID, label: 'Unassigned' }, nd);
    if (id === NEUTRAL_ID) return add({ id, kind: 'neutral', parent: ROOT_ID, label: 'Shared' }, nd + 1);
    return add({ id: VENDORS_ID, kind: 'group', parent: ROOT_ID, label: 'Vendors' }, nd + 2);
  };
  const ensureTests = (domain: string) =>
    add({ id: testsId(domain), kind: 'tests', parent: domainId(domain), label: 'Tests', domain }, map.layers.length);

  // ---- files: every path with facts plus every repo path they import
  const paths = new Set<string>();
  for (const [path, f] of Object.entries(facts)) {
    paths.add(path);
    for (const i of f.imports) if (!isPseudo(i.to)) paths.add(i.to);
  }
  const placement = new Map<string, Placement>();
  const byContainer = new Map<string, string[]>();
  for (const path of [...paths].sort()) {
    const p = mapper.place(path);
    if (p.kind === 'ignored') continue;
    placement.set(path, p);
    const c = p.kind === 'cell' ? cellId(p.domain, p.layer) : p.kind === 'test' ? ensureTests(p.domain).id : ensureTop(p.kind === 'neutral' ? NEUTRAL_ID : UNASSIGNED_ID).id;
    const list = byContainer.get(c) ?? [];
    list.push(path);
    byContainer.set(c, list);
  }

  const putFile = (path: string, parent: string) => {
    const p = placement.get(path)!;
    const n: Omit<GraphNode, 'order'> = { id: path, kind: 'file', parent, label: fileLabel(path), path };
    if (p.kind === 'cell' || p.kind === 'test') n.domain = p.domain;
    if (p.kind === 'cell') n.layer = p.layer;
    add(n, KIND_RANK.file!);
  };
  /** Directory groups for a container holding too many files; recursive, files directly in the common dir stay put. */
  const groupByDir = (parent: string, files: string[], gid: (dir: string) => string, scope: Pick<GraphNode, 'domain' | 'layer'>) => {
    if (files.length <= GROUP_THRESHOLD) { for (const f of files) putFile(f, parent); return; }
    const prefix = commonDir(files);
    const dirs = new Map<string, string[]>();
    for (const f of files) {
      const rest = prefix ? f.slice(prefix.length + 1) : f;
      const i = rest.indexOf('/');
      if (i < 0) { putFile(f, parent); continue; }
      const dir = (prefix ? `${prefix}/` : '') + rest.slice(0, i);
      const list = dirs.get(dir) ?? [];
      list.push(f);
      dirs.set(dir, list);
    }
    for (const [dir, list] of dirs) {
      const id = gid(dir);
      add({ id, kind: 'group', parent, label: `${dir.slice(prefix ? prefix.length + 1 : 0)}/`, path: dir, ...scope }, KIND_RANK.group!);
      groupByDir(id, list, gid, scope);
    }
  };
  for (const [container, files] of byContainer) {
    const n = nodes[container]!;
    if (n.kind === 'cell') {
      const { domain, layer } = n as Required<Pick<GraphNode, 'domain' | 'layer'>>;
      const comps = map.domains.find((d) => d.id === domain)?.cells[layer]?.components ?? [];
      const rest: string[] = [];
      for (const f of files) {
        const comp = comps.find((c) => matchesAny(c.paths, f));
        if (!comp) { rest.push(f); continue; }
        const id = groupId(domain, layer, comp.id);
        add({ id, kind: 'group', parent: container, label: comp.name, domain, layer }, KIND_RANK.group!);
        putFile(f, id);
      }
      groupByDir(container, rest, (dir) => groupId(domain, layer, dir), { domain, layer });
    } else {
      groupByDir(container, files, (dir) => `group:${container}/${dir}`, n.domain ? { domain: n.domain } : {});
    }
  }

  // ---- symbols, routes, entries (under their file; symbols nested by parent)
  for (const path of placement.keys()) {
    const f = facts[path];
    if (!f) continue;
    const file = nodes[path]!;
    const own = f.symbols.some((s) => s.parent) ? new Set(f.symbols.map((s) => s.id)) : null;
    for (const s of f.symbols) {
      const nested = !!s.parent && !!own?.has(s.parent);
      add(scoped({
        id: s.id, kind: 'symbol', parent: nested ? s.parent : path,
        label: nested ? s.name.slice(s.name.lastIndexOf('.') + 1) : s.name, symbol: { kind: s.kind, exported: s.exported },
      }, file), KIND_RANK.symbol!);
    }
    for (const r of f.routes) add(scoped({ id: r.id, kind: 'route', parent: path, label: `${r.method} ${r.path}` }, file), KIND_RANK.route!);
    for (const e of f.entries) add(scoped({ id: e.id, kind: 'entry', parent: path, label: e.label }, file), KIND_RANK.entry!);
  }

  // ---- tables: under the cell that lists them, else unassigned
  map.domains.forEach((d) => {
    for (const [layer, cell] of Object.entries(d.cells)) {
      for (const t of cell.tables ?? []) add({ id: tableId(t), kind: 'table', parent: cellId(d.id, layer), label: t, domain: d.id, layer }, KIND_RANK.table!);
    }
  });
  const ensureTable = (id: string) => nodes[id] ?? add({ id, kind: 'table', parent: ensureTop(UNASSIGNED_ID).id, label: id.slice(6) }, KIND_RANK.table!);

  // ---- table columns, from schema files (`CREATE TABLE`); the table stays under the cell that lists it
  for (const path of placement.keys()) {
    for (const t of facts[path]?.tables ?? []) ensureTable(tableId(t.name)).columns = [...t.columns];
  }

  // ---- vendors: claimed by an `external` cell (importing domains first), else the top-level Vendors group
  const callsOf = (path: string, f: FileFacts): CallFact[] => {
    const s = semantic[path];

  const importers = new Map<string, Set<string>>();
  const noteVendor = (v: string, from: string) => {
    const set = importers.get(v) ?? new Set<string>();
    const d = mapper.domainOf(fileOf(from) ?? from);
    if (d) set.add(d);
    importers.set(v, set);
  };
  for (const path of placement.keys()) {
    const f = facts[path];
    if (!f) continue;
    for (const i of f.imports) if (i.to.startsWith('vendor:')) noteVendor(i.to, path);
    for (const c of callsOf(path, f)) if (c.to.startsWith('vendor:')) noteVendor(c.to, c.from);
  }
  const externals = map.domains.flatMap((d) => (d.cells[EXTERNAL_LAYER] ? [{ domain: d.id, globs: d.cells[EXTERNAL_LAYER]!.paths ?? [] }] : []));
  for (const [v, doms] of [...importers].sort(([a], [b]) => (a < b ? -1 : 1))) {
    const pkg = v.slice(7);
    const claims = (g: string[]) => matchesAny(g, pkg) || matchesAny(g, `node_modules/${pkg}`) || matchesAny(g, `node_modules/${pkg}/index.js`);
    const owner = externals.find((e) => doms.has(e.domain) && claims(e.globs)) ?? externals.find((e) => claims(e.globs));
    if (owner) add({ id: v, kind: 'vendor', parent: cellId(owner.domain, EXTERNAL_LAYER), label: pkg, domain: owner.domain, layer: EXTERNAL_LAYER }, KIND_RANK.vendor!);
    else add({ id: v, kind: 'vendor', parent: ensureTop(VENDORS_ID).id, label: pkg }, KIND_RANK.vendor!);
  }

  // ---- leaf edges, grouped by owner file (in path order) and sorted by id within it
  const edges: GraphEdge[] = [];
  const seen = new Map<string, Map<string, GraphEdge[]>>(); // from → to → edges (one per kind); avoids hashing new id strings
  const local: GraphEdge[] = [];
  const resolve = (id: string): string | null => {
    if (nodes[id]) return id;
    if (id.startsWith('table:')) return ensureTable(id).id;
    const f = fileOf(id);
    return f && nodes[f] ? f : null;
  };
  const edge = (kind: EdgeKind, from: string | null, to: string | null, owner: string, count: number, typeOnly?: boolean, confidence?: CallConfidence) => {
    if (!from || !to) return;
    const row = seen.get(from) ?? seen.set(from, new Map()).get(from)!;
    const same = row.get(to);
    const cur = same?.find((x) => x.kind === kind);
    if (cur) {
      cur.count += count;
      if (typeOnly === false) cur.typeOnly = false;
      return;
    }
    const e: GraphEdge = { id: edgeId(kind, from, to), kind, from, to, count, owner };
    if (typeOnly !== undefined) e.typeOnly = typeOnly;
    if (confidence) e.confidence = confidence;
    if (same) same.push(e);

    const f = facts[path];
    if (!f) continue;
    for (const i of f.imports) edge(i.to.startsWith('vendor:') ? 'uses' : 'imports', path, resolve(i.to), path, 1, i.typeOnly);
    for (const c of callsOf(path, f)) edge('calls', resolve(c.from), resolve(c.to), path, c.count, undefined, c.confidence);
    const s = semantic[path];
    if (s && s.hash === f.hash) for (const im of s.implements) edge('implements', resolve(im.from), resolve(im.to), path, 1);

    for (const r of f.reads ?? []) edge('reads', r.symbol ? resolve(r.symbol) : path, ensureTable(tableId(r.table)).id, path, 1);
    for (const r of f.routes) if (r.handler) edge('handles', r.id, resolve(r.handler), path, 1);

  for (const [parent, list] of Object.entries(children)) {
    list.sort((a, b) => rank.get(a)! - rank.get(b)! || (a < b ? -1 : a > b ? 1 : 0));
    const grid = parent === ROOT_ID || nodes[parent]!.kind === 'domain';
    for (let i = 0; i < list.length; i++) nodes[list[i]!]!.order = grid ? rank.get(list[i]!)! : i;

}

/** A file's label: its name, with the folder for index files (`vendor/news/index.ts` → `news/index.ts`). */
export function fileLabel(path: string): string {
  const parts = path.split('/');
  const name = parts.pop()!;
  return /^index\.[cm]?[jt]sx?$/.test(name) && parts.length ? `${parts.pop()}/${name}` : name;
}

/** Longest common directory of sorted paths (the common prefix of the first and last, cut at a `/`). */
function commonDir(sorted: string[]): string {
  const a = sorted[0]!;
  const b = sorted[sorted.length - 1]!;
  let i = 0;
  while (i < a.length && a[i] === b[i]) i++;
  return a.slice(0, Math.max(0, a.lastIndexOf('/', i - 1)));
}

/**
 * The facts the graph is built from: `ui.facts`, plus empty stubs for every file the log knows about but has no
 * facts for (placed files, files a turn touched or planned, planned import endpoints), so ghosts and fresh files
 * have a leaf. Cross-domain cell→cell imports follow `ui.edges` (the reducer's record of edge_added/removed), so
 * logs without `facts_changed` still project the same edges as `edgeViews`. A no-op when facts are current.
 */
export function graphFacts(ui: UIState): Record<string, FileFacts> {
  const out: Record<string, FileFacts> = { ...ui.facts };
  const stub = (path: string) => { if (!out[path] && !isPseudo(path)) out[path] = emptyFacts(path); };
  for (const [path, p] of Object.entries(ui.files)) if (p.kind !== 'ignored') stub(path);
  for (const t of ui.turns) {
    for (const p of Object.keys(t.paths)) stub(p);
    for (const c of Object.values(t.planned)) c.files.forEach(stub);
    t.unassigned.forEach(stub);
    for (const files of Object.values(t.tests)) files.forEach(stub);
    for (const s of t.steps) for (const f of [...s.files, ...s.imports.map((i) => i.from)]) stub(normalize(fileOf(f) ?? f));
    for (const e of Object.values(t.plannedEdges)) for (const i of e.imports) { stub(i.from); stub(i.to); }
    for (const e of t.edgesAdded) { stub(e.edge.from); stub(e.edge.to); }
  }
  if (!ui.map) return out;
  const mapper = createMapper(ui.map);
  const want = new Map<string, Set<string>>();
  for (const e of Object.values(ui.edges)) for (const f of e.files) { stub(f.from); stub(f.to); (want.get(f.from) ?? want.set(f.from, new Set()).get(f.from)!).add(f.to); }
  const cross = (a: string, b: string) => {
    const pa = mapper.place(a);
    const pb = mapper.place(b);
    return pa.kind === 'cell' && pb.kind === 'cell' && pa.domain !== pb.domain;
  };
  for (const [path, f] of Object.entries(out)) {
    const w = want.get(path);
    const keep = f.imports.filter((i) => isPseudo(i.to) || !cross(path, i.to) || !!w?.has(i.to));
    const extra = [...(w ?? [])].filter((to) => !f.imports.some((i) => i.to === to)).sort();
    if (keep.length !== f.imports.length || extra.length) out[path] = { ...f, imports: [...keep, ...extra.map((to) => ({ to, typeOnly: false }))] };
  }
  return out;
}

/** The context graph for a UI state (null before a map exists). */
export function graphOf(ui: UIState): ContextGraph | null {
  return ui.map ? buildGraph(ui.map, graphFacts(ui), ui.semantic) : null;
}
// trace (NAVIGATION_PLAN §2 "Wiring trace"): shortest call chains from a symbol, route or file to its sinks.
import type { ContextGraph } from '../contracts/graph';
import { EXTERNAL_LAYER } from './build';
import { byId } from './util';

export const MAX_TRACE_PATHS = 5;

const adjacency = new WeakMap<ContextGraph, Map<string, { to: string; sinkOnly: boolean }[]>>();

/** calls and handles forward, implements from the interface member to each implementation, writes into tables. */
function adjacencyOf(g: ContextGraph) {
  let adj = adjacency.get(g);
  if (adj) return adj;
  adj = new Map();
  const link = (a: string, b: string, sinkOnly: boolean) => {
    const list = adj!.get(a) ?? adj!.set(a, []).get(a)!;
    if (!list.some((x) => x.to === b)) list.push({ to: b, sinkOnly });
  };
  for (const e of g.edges) {
    if (e.kind === 'calls' || e.kind === 'handles') link(e.from, e.to, false);
    else if (e.kind === 'implements') link(e.to, e.from, false);
    else if (e.kind === 'writes') link(e.from, e.to, true);
  }
  for (const list of adj.values()) list.sort((x, y) => byId(x.to, y.to));
  adjacency.set(g, adj);
  return adj;
}

/**
 * BFS over calls ∪ implements ∪ handles (plus writes into a table sink). Default sinks: vendor and table nodes,
 * and anything inside an `external` cell. Sinks end a chain. Returns at most MAX_TRACE_PATHS shortest chains
 * (one per sink, nearest first, ties by sink id), each starting at `from`. Dispatch through a registry shows up
 * as an interface member followed by an implementation (`implements` walked backwards).
 */
export function trace(graph: ContextGraph, from: string, sinks?: readonly string[]): string[][] {
  if (!graph.nodes[from]) return [];
  const adj = adjacencyOf(graph);
  const given = sinks ? new Set(sinks) : null;
  const isSink = (id: string) => {
    if (given) return given.has(id);
    const n = graph.nodes[id];
    return id.startsWith('vendor:') || id.startsWith('table:') || n?.layer === EXTERNAL_LAYER;
  };
  const parent = new Map<string, string | null>([[from, null]]);
  const found: string[] = [];
  let frontier = [from];
  while (frontier.length && found.length < MAX_TRACE_PATHS) {
    const next: string[] = [];
    const reached: string[] = [];
    for (const id of frontier) {
      for (const { to, sinkOnly } of adj.get(id) ?? []) {
        if (parent.has(to) || (sinkOnly && !isSink(to))) continue;
        parent.set(to, id);
        if (isSink(to)) reached.push(to);
        else next.push(to);
      }
    }
    found.push(...reached.sort(byId));
    frontier = next;
  }
  return found.slice(0, MAX_TRACE_PATHS).map((sink) => {
    const path: string[] = [];
    for (let n: string | null = sink; n !== null; n = parent.get(n) ?? null) path.push(n);
    return path.reverse();
  });
}

// Lazy per-graph indexes, cached by identity (graphs are treated as immutable once built).
import type { ContextGraph, GraphEdge } from '../contracts/graph';

const memo = <T>(build: (g: ContextGraph) => T) => {
  const cache = new WeakMap<ContextGraph, T>();
  return (g: ContextGraph): T => {
    let v = cache.get(g);
    if (v === undefined) cache.set(g, (v = build(g)));
    return v;
  };
};

/** from → leaf edges, in graph order. */
export const outEdges = memo((g) => {
  const out = new Map<string, GraphEdge[]>();
  for (const e of g.edges) {
    const list = out.get(e.from);
    if (list) list.push(e);
    else out.set(e.from, [e]);
  }
  return out;
});

export const edgeIds = memo((g) => new Set(g.edges.map((e) => e.id)));

/** An exported interface's member (a property or method under a `type` symbol): kept in the graph, never counted. */
export function isMember(g: ContextGraph, id: string): boolean {
  const n = g.nodes[id];
  if (n?.kind !== 'symbol' || (n.symbol?.kind !== 'property' && n.symbol?.kind !== 'method')) return false;
  const p = n.parent ? g.nodes[n.parent] : undefined;
  return p?.kind === 'symbol' && p.symbol?.kind === 'type';
}

/** Files in a subtree (a file counts itself) and symbols strictly below a node (interface members excluded); memoized for containers only. */
export const subtreeCounts = memo((g) => {
  const cache = new Map<string, { files: number; symbols: number }>();
  const count = (id: string): { files: number; symbols: number } => {
    const kids = g.children[id];
    const self = g.nodes[id]!.kind === 'file' ? 1 : 0;
    if (!kids?.length) return { files: self, symbols: 0 };
    let c = cache.get(id);
    if (c) return c;
    c = { files: self, symbols: 0 };
    for (const k of kids) {
      if (isMember(g, k)) continue;
      const s = count(k);
      c.files += s.files;
      c.symbols += s.symbols + (g.nodes[k]!.kind === 'symbol' ? 1 : 0);
    }
    cache.set(id, c);
    return c;
  };
  return count;
});

export function pathTo(g: ContextGraph, id: string): string[] {
  const out: string[] = [];
  for (let n: string | null = id; n; n = g.nodes[n]?.parent ?? null) out.push(n);
  return out.reverse();
}

export type DriftSignalKind =
  | 'unassigned'
  | 'wide_turns'
  | 'co_change'
  | 'coupling_growth'
  | 'rule_erosion'
  | 'rule_reinforcement'
  | 'bloated_cell'
  | 'new_top_level'
  | 'stale_label';

export type DriftSignal = {
  signal: DriftSignalKind;
  metric: string; // human-readable metric name, e.g. "median cells lit per turn (last 10)"
  value: number;
  threshold: number;
  scope: string[]; // graph node ids (domains, cells, files, invariant ids as `rule:<id>`)
  persisted: number; // consecutive turn ends it has held for; triggers at >= 2
};

/** A unit of history to score maps against: a Interpretability turn or a git commit. */
export type HistoryTurn = { id: string; source: 'turn' | 'commit'; files: string[] };

export type MapScore = {
  cellsLitMean: number;
  cellsLitMedian: number;
  modularity: number; // Newman Q of the file import graph partitioned by domain
  unassigned: number;
  cellSizeGini: number;
  decisionsBroken: number;
  churnFiles: number; // files whose cell changes vs the current map
  churnIds: number; // domain/cell ids removed or renamed-by-id vs the current map
  total: number; // weighted, lower is better
};

export type ProposalChange =
  | { kind: 'place'; path: string; domain: string; layer: string }
  | { kind: 'move'; path: string; from: { domain: string; layer: string }; to: { domain: string; layer: string } }
  | { kind: 'add_domain'; domain: string; name: string }
  | { kind: 'remove_domain'; domain: string }
  | { kind: 'rename_domain'; domain: string; from: string; to: string }
  | { kind: 'purpose'; domain: string; purpose: string }
  | { kind: 'add_cell'; domain: string; layer: string }
  | { kind: 'remove_cell'; domain: string; layer: string }
  | { kind: 'add_rule'; invariant: string; rule: string }
  | { kind: 'retire_rule'; invariant: string }
  | { kind: 'change_rule'; invariant: string; rule: string };

export type MapProposal = {
  id: string; // `MP-<n>`
  trigger: DriftSignal[];
  scope: string[]; // node ids the proposal touches
  candidates: { yaml: string; score: MapScore }[];
  chosen: number; // index into candidates

# Reference map for the Scout demo repo.
# Live, the cartographer proposes this on load and the user confirms it.
# This copy is the test fixture for packages/core and the fallback if the
# cartographer's proposal is off on stage.

version: 1

layers:
  - { id: ui,       name: UI }
  - { id: entry,    name: Entry }
  - { id: logic,    name: Logic }
  - { id: data,     name: Data }
  - { id: external, name: External }

# Paths that belong to no domain and never create cross-domain edges.
neutral: ["src/shared/**", "vendor/_calllog.ts", "web/src/shared/**"]
ignore: ["node_modules/**", ".git/**", ".harness/**", "fixtures/**", "scripts/**", "decisions/**", "*.json", "*.md", "*.config.ts", ".*", "domains.yaml", "web/dist/**", "web/public/**", "web/vite.config.ts", "web/tsconfig.json", ".scout/**"]

domains:
  - id: channels
    name: Channels
    purpose: Take requests from HTTP and the CLI
    cells:
      ui:    { paths: ["web/index.html", "web/src/main.tsx", "web/src/app/**"] }
      entry: { paths: ["src/channels/routes.ts", "src/channels/cli.ts"] }
      logic: { paths: ["src/channels/validate.ts"] }
    tests: ["test/channels/**"]

  - id: orchestrator
    name: Agent loop
    purpose: Plan each run and call tools in order
    cells:
      ui:    { paths: ["web/src/features/runs/**"] }
      logic: { paths: ["src/orchestrator/agent.ts", "src/orchestrator/planner.ts", "src/orchestrator/tool-registry.ts"] }
      data:  { paths: ["src/orchestrator/run-state.ts", "src/orchestrator/schema.sql"], tables: ["runs"] }
    tests: ["test/orchestrator/**"]

  - id: tools
    name: Research tools
    purpose: Look up companies, news and filings
    cells:
      ui:       { paths: ["web/src/features/tools/**"] }
      logic:    { paths: ["src/tools/**"] }
      external: { paths: ["vendor/search/**", "vendor/news/**", "vendor/sec-edgar/**", "vendor/enrichment/**"] }
    tests: ["test/tools/**"]

  - id: gateway
    name: Model gateway
    purpose: Every model call, with redaction and cost logging
    cells:
      ui:       { paths: ["web/src/features/usage/**"] }
      logic:    { paths: ["src/gateway/complete.ts", "src/gateway/embed.ts", "src/gateway/redact.ts", "src/gateway/providers.ts"] }
      data:     { paths: ["src/gateway/cost-ledger.ts", "src/gateway/schema.sql"], tables: ["cost_log"] }
      external: { paths: ["vendor/llm-openai/**", "vendor/llm-anthropic/**", "vendor/embeddings/**"] }
    tests: ["test/gateway/**"]

    cells:

      logic: { paths: ["src/memory/retrieve.ts", "src/memory/vector-index.ts"] }
      data:  { paths: ["src/memory/notes-store.ts", "src/memory/schema.sql"], tables: ["notes", "embeddings"] }
    tests: ["test/memory/**"]

    purpose: Draft emails and keep the CRM in sync
    cells:

      logic:    { paths: ["src/outreach/draft-email.ts", "src/outreach/send.ts"] }

# Seeded by the cartographer on load (source: cartographer), confirmed by the user.

invariants:

      if (s.events.length && s.events[s.events.length - 1]!.id === e.id) return s;
      const clear = e.kind === 'chat' && (e.data as { role?: string } | undefined)?.role === 'assistant';
      return { events: [...s.events, e], ...(clear ? { delta: '' } : {}) };
    }),
  addDelta: (text) => set((s) => ({ delta: s.delta + text })),
  setBusy: (busy) => set(busy ? { busy } : { busy, delta: '' }),
  setConn: (conn) => set({ conn }),
  setRepo: (repo) => set({ repo }),
  setDraft: (draft, focus) => set((s) => ({ draft, focusTick: focus ? s.focusTick + 1 : s.focusTick })),
  select: (selection) => set({ selection }),
  setTurn: (turn) => set({ turn }),
  setReplay: (replay) => set({ replay }),
  setHover: (hover) => set({ hover }),
}));
import type { HarnessEvent } from '@harness/core/view';
import { useStore } from './store';

type ServerMsg =
  | { type: 'hello'; events: HarnessEvent[]; busy: boolean; session: string }
  | { type: 'event'; event: HarnessEvent }
  | { type: 'delta'; text: string }
  | { type: 'busy'; busy: boolean };

const params = new URLSearchParams(location.search);
/** Dev-only: `?fake=1` loads /fake-events.json at once, `?fake=play` streams it; `&at=N` opens the replay at N. */
export const fakeMode = params.get('fake');

export function connect() {
  if (fakeMode) return loadFake(fakeMode === 'play', fakeMode);
  void fetch('/api/info')
    .then((r) => r.json() as Promise<{ repo: string }>)
    .then((i) => useStore.getState().setRepo(i.repo))
    .catch(() => {});
  openSocket(500);
}

function openSocket(delay: number) {
  const ws = new WebSocket(`${location.protocol === 'https:' ? 'wss' : 'ws'}://${location.host}/ws`);
  let opened = false;
  ws.onopen = () => {
    opened = true;
    useStore.getState().setConn('open');
  };
  ws.onmessage = (m) => {
    const msg = JSON.parse(String(m.data)) as ServerMsg;
    const s = useStore.getState();
    if (msg.type === 'hello') s.hello(msg.events, msg.busy);
    else if (msg.type === 'event') s.append(msg.event);
    else if (msg.type === 'delta') s.addDelta(msg.text);
    else if (msg.type === 'busy') s.setBusy(msg.busy);
  };
  ws.onclose = () => {
    useStore.getState().setConn('down');
    const next = opened ? 500 : Math.min(delay * 2, 8000);
    setTimeout(() => openSocket(next), opened ? 500 : delay);
  };
}

async function loadFake(play: boolean, fakeMode: string) {
  const st = useStore.getState();
  st.setConn('fake');
  st.setRepo('scout-agent (fake turn)');
  const file = fakeMode === '1' || fakeMode === 'play' ? 'fake' : fakeMode; // `?fake=comp` → /comp-events.json
  const events = (await (await fetch(`/${file}-events.json`)).json()) as HarnessEvent[];
  const at = params.get('at');
  if (!play) {
    st.hello(events, false);
    if (at !== null) st.setReplay(Math.max(0, Math.min(events.length, Number(at))));
    return;
  }
  st.hello([], false);
  for (let i = 0; i < events.length; i++) {
    const e = events[i]!;
    const prev = events[i - 1];
    const gap = prev ? Math.max(20, Math.min(900, (e.t - prev.t) / 3)) : 0;
    await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, e.kind === 'file_assigned' ? 15 : gap));
    useStore.getState().append(e);
  }
}

async function post(path: string, body?: unknown) {
  if (fakeMode) return;
  await fetch(path, { method: 'POST', headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' }, body: JSON.stringify(body ?? {}) });
}

export const api = {
  chat: (text: string) => post('/api/chat', { text }),
  approve: () => post('/api/approve'),
  interrupt: () => post('/api/interrupt'),
  confirmMap: () => post('/api/map/confirm'),
  fallbackMap: () => post('/api/map/fallback'),
  async file(path: string): Promise<string | null> {
    const r = await fetch(`/api/file?path=${encodeURIComponent(path)}`);
    return r.ok ? r.text() : null;
  },
};

// The browser's ELK: elkjs's own worker script, loaded on the first layout only (v1 never pulls it in).
import type { ElkNode } from 'elkjs/lib/elk-api';
import { cachedLayout, type ElkApi } from './containers';

let elk: Promise<ElkApi> | null = null;

function getElk(): Promise<ElkApi> {
  elk ??= Promise.all([import('elkjs/lib/elk-api.js'), import('elkjs/lib/elk-worker.min.js?url')]).then(([api, url]) => {
    const ELK = api.default;
    return new ELK({ workerFactory: () => new Worker(url.default) }) as unknown as ElkApi;
  });
  return elk;
}

export const layoutContainer = cachedLayout(getElk);
export const clearLayoutCache = () => layoutContainer.cache.clear();

/** Boot the worker and JIT ELK before the first expand (the cold first layout took ~160 ms on the M1). */
export const warmElk = () =>
  getElk().then((api) => api.layout({ id: 'warm', layoutOptions: { 'elk.algorithm': 'layered' }, children: [{ id: 'a', width: 10, height: 10 }, { id: 'b', width: 10, height: 10 }], edges: [{ id: 'e', sources: ['a'], targets: ['b'] }] } as ElkNode));
// The real pipeline wired to the stores: ui = reduce(events, upTo) → graph = graphOf(ui) (memoized) →
// activity = activityFor(ui, graph, turn) → projection = project(graph, view, activity).
import { useMemo } from 'react';
import { useView } from '../derive';
import { graphMemo, sceneOf, type Scene } from './scene';
import { useV2 } from './store';

export { hotLabels, type Scene } from './scene';

const memoGraph = graphMemo();

/** The scene for the current events, replay index, selected turn and open set. */
export function useScene(): Scene | null {
  const v = useView();
  const open = useV2((s) => s.open);
  const graph = useMemo(() => memoGraph(v.ui), [v.ui]);
  return useMemo(() => (graph ? sceneOf(v.ui, graph, v.turn?.id ?? null, open) : null), [v.ui, v.turn, graph, open]);
}
// Staged, interruptible transitions between two laid-out frames (NAVIGATION_PLAN §3.3):
//   0–150 ms   fade out edges that will change and nodes that will go
//   150–450 ms one commit, then FLIP the moved nodes with the Web Animations API; the camera flies in parallel
//   450–650 ms new nodes fade in and changed edges draw in (CSS, keyed on the commit)
// A new request at any point cancels the pending stage and starts from what is on screen.
import type { Frame } from './layout/frame';

export const reducedMotion = () => typeof matchMedia !== 'undefined' && matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches;

export const T_FADE = 150;
export const T_MOVE = 300;
export const T_ENTER = 200;
const EASE = 'cubic-bezier(0.25, 0.8, 0.3, 1)';
const FADE_ID = 'v2-fade';

/** What enters with a commit: new nodes, changed edges, and edges that just became new (one pulse each, never looping). */
export type Enter = { nodes: Set<string>; edges: Set<string>; pulse: Set<string>; seq: number };
export type TransitionStats = { commitMs: number; commitToFrameMs: number; moved: number; entered: number; removed: number; animated: boolean };

export type TransitionHooks = {
  root(): HTMLElement | null;
  /** Must commit synchronously (flushSync): content and positions land in one React commit. */
  commit(next: Frame, enter: Enter): void;
  camera(next: Frame, prev: Frame | null, animate: boolean): void;
};

const sel = (attr: string, id: string) => `[${attr}="${CSS.escape(id)}"]`;

export class Transitioner {
  private timers: number[] = [];
  private seq = 0;
  shown: Frame | null = null;
  last: TransitionStats | null = null;
  onDone: ((s: TransitionStats) => void) | null = null;

  constructor(private hooks: TransitionHooks) {}

  cancel() {
    for (const t of this.timers) clearTimeout(t);
    this.timers = [];
    const root = this.hooks.root();
    if (!root) return;
    root.classList.remove('is-moving');
    for (const a of root.getAnimations({ subtree: true })) {
      if (a.id === FADE_ID) a.cancel();
      else if (a instanceof CSSAnimation || a instanceof CSSTransition) continue;
      else a.finish();
    }
  }

  go(next: Frame) {
    this.cancel();
    const prev = this.shown;
    const root = this.hooks.root();
    const animate = !!prev && !!root && !reducedMotion();
    const prevEdges = new Map(prev?.edges.map((e) => [e.id, e.d]) ?? []);
    const nextEdges = new Map(next.edges.map((e) => [e.id, e.d]));
    const changedEdges = [...prevEdges].filter(([id, d]) => nextEdges.get(id) !== d).map(([id]) => id);
    const removed = prev ? prev.nodes.filter((n) => !next.boxes[n.id]).map((n) => n.id) : [];
    const prevStatus = new Map(prev?.edges.map((e) => [e.id, e.status]) ?? []);
    const enter: Enter = {
      nodes: new Set(prev ? next.nodes.filter((n) => !prev.boxes[n.id]).map((n) => n.id) : []),
      edges: new Set(prev ? next.edges.filter((e) => prevEdges.get(e.id) !== e.d).map((e) => e.id) : []),
      pulse: new Set(prev ? next.edges.filter((e) => e.status === 'new' && prevStatus.get(e.id) !== 'new').map((e) => e.id) : []),
      seq: ++this.seq,
    };
    // Strata's depth fade, for transitions only: while the view changes, everything outside the focus recedes.
    if (animate && root && prev && prev.key !== next.key) {
      root.classList.add('is-moving');
      this.timers.push(window.setTimeout(() => root.classList.remove('is-moving'), T_FADE + T_MOVE + T_ENTER));
    }

    if (animate && root) {
      for (const id of changedEdges) root.querySelector(sel('data-edge', id))?.animate([{ opacity: 1 }, { opacity: 0 }], { duration: T_FADE, fill: 'forwards', easing: 'ease-out', id: FADE_ID });
      for (const id of removed) root.querySelector(`.react-flow__node${sel('data-id', id)}`)?.animate([{ opacity: 1 }, { opacity: 0 }], { duration: T_FADE, fill: 'forwards', easing: 'ease-out', id: FADE_ID });
    }
    const run = () => this.commit(prev, next, enter, animate, removed.length);
    if (animate && (changedEdges.length || removed.length)) this.timers.push(window.setTimeout(run, T_FADE));
    else run();
  }

  private commit(prev: Frame | null, next: Frame, enter: Enter, animate: boolean, removed: number) {
    const root = this.hooks.root();
    if (root) for (const a of root.getAnimations({ subtree: true })) if (a.id === FADE_ID) a.cancel();
    const t0 = performance.now();
    this.hooks.commit(next, enter);
    const commitMs = performance.now() - t0;
    this.shown = next;

    let moved = 0;
    if (animate && prev && root) {
      for (const n of next.nodes) {
        const a = prev.boxes[n.id];
        if (!a) continue;
        const posChanged = Math.abs(a.x - n.x) > 0.5 || Math.abs(a.y - n.y) > 0.5;
        const sizeChanged = Math.abs(a.w - n.w) > 0.5 || Math.abs(a.h - n.h) > 0.5;
        if (!posChanged && !sizeChanged) continue;
        const el = root.querySelector<HTMLElement>(`.react-flow__node${sel('data-id', n.id)}`);
        if (!el) continue;
        moved++;
        const from: Keyframe = { transform: `translate(${a.x}px, ${a.y}px)` };
        const to: Keyframe = { transform: `translate(${n.x}px, ${n.y}px)` };
        if (sizeChanged) Object.assign(from, { width: `${a.w}px`, height: `${a.h}px` }), Object.assign(to, { width: `${n.w}px`, height: `${n.h}px` });
        el.animate([from, to], { duration: T_MOVE, easing: EASE });
      }
    }
    this.hooks.camera(next, prev, animate);
    const stats: TransitionStats = { commitMs, commitToFrameMs: 0, moved, entered: enter.nodes.size, removed, animated: animate };
    requestAnimationFrame(() => {
      stats.commitToFrameMs = performance.now() - t0;
      this.last = stats;
      const done = () => this.onDone?.(stats);
      if (animate) this.timers.push(window.setTimeout(done, T_MOVE + T_ENTER));
      else done();
    });
  }
}
import { create } from 'zustand';
import type { ProjectionCursor, VisibleEdge, VisibleNode } from '@harness/core/view';

export type Theme = 'atlas' | 'control' | 'strata';
const params = new URLSearchParams(location.search);
const themeParam = params.get('theme');
export const initialTheme: Theme = themeParam === 'control' || themeParam === 'strata' ? themeParam : 'atlas';

/** Where you are: the containers you opened (domains, cells, groups) and the node you are on. View-only state. */
export type Place = { open: string[]; focus: string | null };

const readMinimap = () => {
  try { return localStorage.getItem('harness.minimap') !== '0'; } catch { return true; }
};

/**
 * View-only state for the v2 map: what is open, the focused node, history, chrome toggles. Plus the current
 * projection's nodes and edges published by id with structural sharing, so each node component re-renders only when
 * its own slice changes. Nothing here duplicates what the event log says.
 */
type V2Store = {
  open: string[];
  focus: string | null;
  back: Place[];
  forward: Place[];
  theme: Theme;
  minimap: boolean;
  palette: boolean;
  /** A node to fly the camera to once it is laid out (⌘K, breadcrumbs). */
  fly: string | null;
  nodes: Record<string, VisibleNode>;
  edges: Record<string, VisibleEdge>;
  hot: Record<string, string[]>;
  /** File id → how many of its symbols this turn changed. */
  symbols: Record<string, number>;
  /** Table id → its columns, from the schema file that defines it. */
  columns: Record<string, string[]>;
  cursor: ProjectionCursor | null;

  /** Navigate to a place (pushes history unless it is the same place). */
  go(next: Partial<Place>, fly?: string | null): void;
  setFocus(id: string | null): void;
  goBack(): void;
  goForward(): void;
  setPalette(open: boolean): void;
  toggleMinimap(): void;
  publish(p: { nodes: VisibleNode[]; edges: VisibleEdge[]; hot: Record<string, string[]>; symbols: Record<string, number>; columns: Record<string, string[]>; cursor: ProjectionCursor | null }): void;
};

const same = (a: unknown, b: unknown) => a === b || JSON.stringify(a) === JSON.stringify(b);
const samePlace = (a: Place, b: Place) => a.focus === b.focus && a.open.join() === b.open.join();
const HISTORY = 50;

export const useV2 = create<V2Store>((set, get) => ({
  open: (params.get('expand') ?? '').split(',').filter(Boolean).map((d) => (d.includes(':') ? d : `domain:${d}`)),
  focus: null,
  back: [],
  forward: [],
  theme: initialTheme,
  minimap: readMinimap(),
  palette: false,
  fly: null,
  nodes: {},
  edges: {},
  hot: {},
  symbols: {},
  columns: {},
  cursor: null,

  go: (next, fly = null) => {
    const s = get();
    const cur: Place = { open: s.open, focus: s.focus };
    const to: Place = { open: next.open ?? s.open, focus: next.focus === undefined ? s.focus : next.focus };
    if (samePlace(cur, to)) { if (fly) set({ fly }); return; }
    set({ ...to, back: [...s.back, cur].slice(-HISTORY), forward: [], fly });
  },
  setFocus: (focus) => set({ focus }),
  goBack: () => {
    const s = get();
    const prev = s.back.at(-1);
    if (!prev) return;
    set({ ...prev, back: s.back.slice(0, -1), forward: [{ open: s.open, focus: s.focus }, ...s.forward], fly: prev.focus });
  },
  goForward: () => {
    const s = get();
    const next = s.forward[0];
    if (!next) return;
    set({ ...next, forward: s.forward.slice(1), back: [...s.back, { open: s.open, focus: s.focus }], fly: next.focus });
  },
  setPalette: (palette) => set({ palette }),
  toggleMinimap: () => set((s) => {
    try { localStorage.setItem('harness.minimap', s.minimap ? '0' : '1'); } catch { /* private mode */ }
    return { minimap: !s.minimap };
  }),
  publish: (p) => {
    const prev = get();
    const nodes: Record<string, VisibleNode> = {};
    for (const n of p.nodes) {
      const o = prev.nodes[n.id];
      nodes[n.id] = o && same(o, n) ? o : n;
    }
    const edges: Record<string, VisibleEdge> = {};
    for (const e of p.edges) {
      const o = prev.edges[e.id];
      edges[e.id] = o && same(o, e) ? o : e;
    }
    const hot: Record<string, string[]> = {};
    for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(p.hot)) hot[k] = prev.hot[k] && same(prev.hot[k], v) ? prev.hot[k]! : v;
    set({ nodes, edges, hot, symbols: same(prev.symbols, p.symbols) ? prev.symbols : p.symbols, columns: same(prev.columns, p.columns) ? prev.columns : p.columns, cursor: same(prev.cursor, p.cursor) ? prev.cursor : p.cursor });
  },
}));
import {
  cellKey, cellViews, edgeViews, ledger, reduce, turnLedger,
  type CellView, type EdgeView, type HarnessEvent, type Ledger, type TurnLedger, type TurnState, type UIState, type Violation,
} from '@harness/core/view';
import { useStore } from './store';

/** Everything the UI shows, as a pure function of (events, replay index, selected turn). */
export type View = {
  ui: UIState;
  upTo: number;
  live: boolean;
  turn: TurnState | null;
  turnIndex: number; // 1-based, 0 when no turn
  cells: Record<string, CellView>;
  edges: EdgeView[];
  ledger: Ledger;
  turnLedger: TurnLedger | null;
  /** cellKey → files placed there (product files only; tests are listed under their domain). */
  cellFiles: Record<string, string[]>;
  testFiles: Record<string, string[]>;
  unassigned: string[];
  proposal: { domains: number; rules: number } | null;
  steps: { done: number; total: number };
  turnStarts: number[];
};

let reduceCache: { events: readonly HarnessEvent[]; upTo: number; ui: UIState } | null = null;
let viewCache: { ui: UIState; turnSel: string | null; view: View } | null = null;

function reduced(events: readonly HarnessEvent[], upTo: number): UIState {
  if (reduceCache && reduceCache.events === events && reduceCache.upTo === upTo) return reduceCache.ui;
  const ui = reduce(events, upTo);
  reduceCache = { events, upTo, ui };
  return ui;
}

export function deriveView(events: readonly HarnessEvent[], replay: number | null, turnSel: string | null): View {
  const upTo = replay ?? events.length;
  const ui = reduced(events, upTo);
  if (viewCache && viewCache.ui === ui && viewCache.turnSel === turnSel) return viewCache.view;

  const turn = (turnSel && ui.turns.find((t) => t.id === turnSel)) || ui.turns.at(-1) || null;
  const cellFiles: Record<string, string[]> = {};
  const testFiles: Record<string, string[]> = {};
  const unassigned: string[] = [];
  for (const [path, p] of Object.entries(ui.files)) {
    if (p.kind === 'cell') (cellFiles[cellKey(p)] ??= []).push(path);
    else if (p.kind === 'test') (testFiles[p.domain] ??= []).push(path);
    else if (p.kind === 'unassigned') unassigned.push(path);
  }
  for (const list of Object.values(cellFiles)) list.sort();

  let proposed = -1;
  let confirmed = -1;
  const turnStarts: number[] = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < events.length; i++) {
    const k = events[i]!.kind;
    if (k === 'turn_started') turnStarts.push(i);
    if (i >= upTo) continue;
    if (k === 'map_proposed') proposed = i;
    if (k === 'map_confirmed') confirmed = i;
  }
  const proposal = proposed > confirmed && ui.map ? { domains: ui.map.domains.length, rules: ui.map.invariants.length } : null;

  const l = ledger(ui);
  const view: View = {
    ui,
    upTo,
    live: replay === null,
    turn,
    turnIndex: turn ? ui.turns.indexOf(turn) + 1 : 0,
    cells: cellViews(ui, turn?.id ?? null),
    edges: edgeViews(ui, turn?.id ?? null),
    ledger: l,
    turnLedger: turn ? turnLedger(ui, turn) : null,
    cellFiles,
    testFiles,
    unassigned,
    proposal,
    steps: turn ? stepProgress(turn) : { done: 0, total: 0 },
    turnStarts,
  };
  viewCache = { ui, turnSel, view };
  return view;
}

/** "3 of 6 steps": a step is done when every cell it plans has been edited (or, for a step with no cells, its files). */
function stepProgress(turn: TurnState) {
  const editedFiles = new Set([
    ...Object.values(turn.edited).flatMap((c) => c.files),
    ...Object.values(turn.tests).flat(),
    ...turn.unassigned,
  ]);
  let done = 0;
  for (const step of turn.steps) {
    const cells = Object.entries(turn.planned).filter(([, c]) => c.steps.includes(step.n)).map(([k]) => k);
    const ok = cells.length ? cells.every((k) => !!turn.edited[k]) : step.files.length > 0 && step.files.every((f) => editedFiles.has(f));
    if (ok) done++;
  }
  return { done, total: turn.steps.length };
}

export function useView(): View {
  const events = useStore((s) => s.events);
  const replay = useStore((s) => s.replay);
  const turnSel = useStore((s) => s.turn);
  return deriveView(events, replay, turnSel);
}

/** Violations relevant to the selected turn (load-time plus this turn's plan and gate), for the inspector. */
export function turnViolations(v: View): { v: Violation; source: 'load' | 'plan' | 'gate' }[] {
  const out: { v: Violation; source: 'load' | 'plan' | 'gate' }[] = v.ui.violations.map((x) => ({ v: x, source: 'load' as const }));
  for (const x of v.turn?.planViolations ?? []) out.push({ v: x, source: 'plan' });

}

export type Insets = { top: number; right: number; bottom: number; left: number };
const DEFAULT_INSETS: Insets = { top: 116, right: 28, bottom: 24, left: 96 };

type Shown = { frame: Frame; enter: Enter };
type Stats = { layoutMs: number; pipelineMs: number; elk: { id: string; files: number; ms: number }[]; transition: TransitionStats | null };

export default function MapV2({ insets = DEFAULT_INSETS, chrome = true }: { insets?: Insets; chrome?: boolean }) {
  return (
    <ReactFlowProvider>
      <Inner insets={insets} chrome={chrome} />
    </ReactFlowProvider>

/**
 * Fit a box, but never below `minZoom` (projector legibility: 16 px file labels stay at 13 px or more). When the box
 * does not fit at that zoom, centre on `anchor` (the agent, or the target) and keep the box's top-left in view.
 */
function viewportFor(b: Box, W: number, H: number, ins: Insets, opts: { maxZoom?: number; minZoom?: number; anchor?: Box } = {}): Viewport {
  const aw = Math.max(50, W - ins.left - ins.right);
  const ah = Math.max(50, H - ins.top - ins.bottom);
  const fit = Math.min(opts.maxZoom ?? 1.25, aw / b.w, ah / b.h);
  const zoom = Math.max(0.08, opts.minZoom ? Math.max(fit, opts.minZoom) : fit);
  if (zoom === fit || !opts.minZoom) return { zoom, x: ins.left + (aw - b.w * zoom) / 2 - b.x * zoom, y: ins.top + (ah - b.h * zoom) / 2 - b.y * zoom };
  const a = opts.anchor ?? b;
  const axis = (start: number, size: number, aStart: number, aSize: number, avail: number, inset: number) => {
    if (size * zoom <= avail) return inset + (avail - size * zoom) / 2 - start * zoom;
    const centred = inset + avail / 2 - (aStart + aSize / 2) * zoom;
    return Math.min(inset - start * zoom, Math.max(inset + avail - (start + size) * zoom, centred));
  };
  return { zoom, x: axis(b.x, b.w, a.x, a.w, aw, ins.left), y: axis(b.y, b.h, a.y, a.h, ah, ins.top) };
}

/** Zoom floor for views below System level (16 px file labels at 0.82 are about 13 px). */
const READABLE = 0.82;

/** Roots of the focus region: the selected node, else what is open, else everything (null). */
function regionOf(scene: Scene, sel: string | null): string[] | null {
  const ids = new Set(scene.projection.nodes.map((n) => n.id));
  if (sel && ids.has(sel)) return [sel];
  const open = scene.open.filter((id) => ids.has(id));
  if (open.length) return open;
  // A plan that declines an approach (beat 4): the struck-through edge leads; quiet edges recede to trunks.
  return scene.projection.edges.some((e) => e.decision) ? [] : null;
}

  const [shown, setShown] = useState<Shown | null>(null);
  const stats = useRef<Stats>({ layoutMs: 0, pipelineMs: 0, elk: [], transition: null });
  const insetsRef = useRef(insets);
  insetsRef.current = insets;
  const sel = useStore((s) => selectedNode(s.selection));
  const sceneRef = useSceneRef;
  sceneRef.current = scene;

  const flyTo = useCallback((b: Box, animate: boolean, opts?: Parameters<typeof viewportFor>[4]) => {
    const el = rootRef.current;
    if (!el) return;
    const { width: W, height: H } = el.getBoundingClientRect();
    if (!W || !H) return;
    const ins = insetsRef.current;
    const inspector = useStore.getState().selection ? 400 : 0; // the inspector panel covers the right of the stage
    void rf.setViewport(viewportFor(b, W, H, { ...ins, right: ins.right + inspector }, opts), { duration: animate && !reducedMotion() ? T_MOVE + 150 : 0, interpolate: "smooth" });
  }, [rf]);

  const camera = useCallback((next: Frame, prev: Frame | null, animate: boolean) => {
    const fly = useV2.getState().fly;
    const target = fly ? next.boxes[fly] : undefined;
    if (target) {
      useV2.setState({ fly: null });
      flyTo(pad(next.focus ? union(next.focus, target) : target, 30), animate, { minZoom: READABLE, anchor: pad(target, 40) });
      return;
    }
    if (prev && prev.key === next.key) return; // the camera moves when the view changes, not on every event
    if (!next.focus) return flyTo(next.bounds, animate);
    const c = useV2.getState().cursor;
    const at = c ? next.boxes[c.node] : undefined;
    const inFocus = !!at && at.x >= next.focus.x && at.x <= next.focus.x + next.focus.w;
    flyTo(pad(next.focus, 30), animate, { minZoom: READABLE, anchor: inFocus && at ? pad(at, 60) : { ...next.focus, h: 1 } });
  }, [flyTo]);

  const tr = useMemo(() => new Transitioner({
    root: () => rootRef.current,
    commit: (frame, enter) => flushSync(() => {
      const s = sceneRef.current;
      if (s) publish(s);
      setShown({ frame, enter });
    }),
    camera,
  }), [camera]);

  // Lay out every expanded container (worker, cached, bottom-up), then hand the frame to the transitioner.
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!scene || !v.ui.map) return;
    let live = true;
    const map = v.ui.map;
    const t0 = performance.now();
    void layoutAll(scene.projection, layoutContainer).then((layouts) => {
      if (!live) return;
      stats.current.layoutMs = performance.now() - t0;
      stats.current.elk = [...layouts.values()].map((l) => ({ id: l.id, files: Object.keys(l.nodes).length, ms: +l.ms.toFixed(1) }));
      const meta = { domains: map.domains.map((d) => ({ id: d.id, name: d.name, purpose: d.purpose })), layers: map.layers.map((l) => ({ id: l.id, name: l.name })) };
      tr.go(buildFrame({ projection: scene.projection, meta, layouts, region: regionOf(scene, sel), key: scene.key }));
    });
    return () => { live = false; };
  }, [scene, sel, tr, v.ui.map]);

  // A fly request for a node already on screen (history, breadcrumbs to the same layout).
  const fly = useV2((s) => s.fly);
  useEffect(() => {
    const f = tr.shown;
    if (!fly || !f?.boxes[fly] || f.key !== sceneRef.current?.key) return;
    useV2.setState({ fly: null });
    flyTo(pad(f.focus ? union(f.focus, f.boxes[fly]!) : f.boxes[fly]!, 30), true, { minZoom: READABLE, anchor: pad(f.boxes[fly]!, 40) });
  }, [fly, tr, flyTo, shown]);

  useEffect(() => () => tr.cancel(), [tr]);
  useEffect(() => { void warmElk(); }, []);
  useKeys(tr, rootRef);
  useBenchApi(tr, stats, rf);

  const rfNodes = useMemo<Node[]>(() => {
    if (!shown) return [];
    const { frame, enter } = shown;
    return frame.nodes.map((n) => ({
      id: n.id,
      type: n.type,
      position: { x: n.x, y: n.y },
      data: {},
      width: n.w,
      height: n.h,
      style: { width: n.w, height: n.h },
      zIndex: n.z,
      draggable: false,
      selectable: false,
      connectable: false,
      focusable: n.type !== 'band',
      ariaLabel: ariaFor(n),
      className: enter.nodes.has(n.id) ? 'v2-enter' : undefined,
    }));
  }, [shown]);

  const select = useStore((s) => s.select);
  const onNodeClick = useCallback((ev: React.MouseEvent, node: Node) => {
    ev.stopPropagation();
    const n = useV2.getState().nodes[node.id];
    if (!n) return;
    useV2.getState().setFocus(node.id);
    const cur = useStore.getState().selection;
    select(selectedNode(cur) === node.id ? null : selectionFor(n));
  }, [select]);
  const onNodeDoubleClick = useCallback((_: unknown, node: Node) => {
    const s = sceneRef.current;
    if (!s) return;
    const st = useV2.getState();
    const id = node.id.startsWith('band:') ? UNASSIGNED : node.id;
    st.go(dive(s.graph, { open: st.open, focus: st.focus }, id));
  }, []);

  const theme = useV2((s) => s.theme);
  const minimap = useV2((s) => s.minimap);
  const open = useV2((s) => s.open);
  return (
    <div ref={rootRef} className={`v2-map theme-${theme}`} data-theme={theme}>
      <ReactFlow
        nodes={rfNodes}
```

# Frontend Design

Approach this as the design lead at a design studio known for giving every client a distinct visual identity that is not mistaken for anyone else's. This client has already rejected proposals that felt cliché or templated, and is paying for a distinctive point of view: make deliberate, opinionated choices about palette, typography, and layout that are specific to this brief, and take aesthetic risk if justified.

## Ground your designs in the subject matter

If the brief does not identify what the product or subject matter is, identify it yourself before designing, and confirm with the client. You can come up with one concrete subject, the design's audience, and the design's primary job, as a proposal. If there's any information in your memory about the client's preferences or context about what they're building, use that as a hint. The subject's industry, subject matter, materials, and vernacular are where distinctive visual choices come from — a design for a toy for girls aged 8–11 will be very aesthetically different from a dashboard for financial analysts. Build with the brief's real content and subject matter throughout.

## Design principles

For web designs, the hero is the first thing viewers will see. Open with the most characteristic thing in the subject's world, in the form that is most appropriate: a headline, an image, an animation, a live demo, an interactive moment, or other treatments. Be deliberate with your choice: a big number with a small label, supporting stats, and a gradient accent is the default treatment, so only use it if that's truly the best option.

Typography carries the personality of the page. You don't need a different typeface for display or headline text and body content: use one family or two, and if two, make them clearly distinct.

Choose your typefaces deliberately, not the default families you would reach for on any other project, and set a clear type scale following the default guidance of The Elements of Typographic Style with intentional weights, widths, and spacing. When type is used as a headline or visual element, use the type treatment itself as an active part of the design, not a neutral delivery vehicle for the content.

Default to line lengths of less than 80 characters. Serif typefaces can have slightly longer line lengths; give serif body text slightly more line-height than a sans-serif.

Avoid these default typographic treatments; they are the commonest tells of a generated page:
- Accenting just a single word or phrase in a headline, like putting one word in italic/bold or a different color.
- Using all caps for labels.
- Adding unnecessary typographic labels above content.

Visual structure is information. Structural devices like outlines, borders, numbering, eyebrows, dividers, labels, etc., encode useful information about the content rather than decorate it. Many generic designs use numbered markers (01 / 02 / 03), but that's only appropriate if the content actually is a sequence — like a stepped process or a timeline. Before adding numbered markers, check the content really is a sequence.

Use non-user-triggered motion sparingly and deliberately, only to draw attention. A single orchestrated moment — one page-load sequence or one reveal — lands better than scattered effects; fade-and-slide-up entrances on each section and hover transitions on every card are the generic default and read as AI-generated. Motion that answers a person's action (opening, expanding, confirming) is welcome when it shows what changed.

Consider written content carefully. Often a design brief may not contain real content, and it's up to you to come up with copy and placeholder content. Copy can make a design feel as templated as the design itself. See the below section on writing for more guidance.

## Process: plan, review against the brief, build, critique

For calibration, AI-generated design right now clusters around some traits:
1. a warm cream background (near #F4F1EA) with a high-contrast serif display and a terracotta or warm-clay accent (often near #D97757 — Anthropic's own Claude-interaction accent, so on a user's brief it reads as a tell);
2. a near-black background with a single bright acid-green or vermilion accent;
3. a broadsheet-style layout with hairline rules, zero border-radius, and dense newspaper-like columns;
4. the SaaS-card kit: content chopped into identical rounded cards, one border-radius on everything regardless of hierarchy, the same soft grey shadow (rgba(0,0,0,.1)) under each, and gradient washes as decoration;
5. template chrome that appears whatever the subject: a tracked-out ALL-CAPS eyebrow label above every heading; meta strings joined with middle dots ('A · B · C'); labels built as 'WORD — fragment' with a spaced em dash; tinted near-black (#0B0B0B, #111) standing in for black; a monospace face for small data labels; a '→' appended to link and button text.

All traits are legitimate for some briefs, but they are defaults rather than choices, and they appear regardless of subject. Where the brief pins down a visual direction, follow it exactly — the brief's own words always win, including when it asks for one of these looks. Where it leaves an axis free, don't spend that freedom on one of these defaults. As with a hired human designer, there's often a careful balance between doing what you're good at and taking each project as a chance to experiment and learn.

Work in two passes. First, brainstorm a short design plan based on the client's design brief: create a compact token system with color, type, layout, and principles.
- Color: describe the core base palette as 4–6 named hex values.
- Type: the typefaces and their roles.
- Layout: a layout concept, using one-sentence prose descriptions and ASCII wireframes to ideate and compare. Include alignment guidance; should the content be left aligned, center aligned, justified?
- Principles: the high-level guidance for what makes this page unique.

Then review that plan against the brief before building: if any part of it reads like the generic default you would produce for any similar page (work through a similar prompt to see if you arrive somewhere similar) rather than a choice made for this specific brief — revise that part, say what you changed and why. Only after you've confirmed the relative uniqueness of your design plan should you start to write the code, following the revised plan.

When writing the code, be careful of structuring your CSS selector specificities. It's easy to generate CSS classes that cancel each other out (especially with a type-based selector like .section and an element-based selector like .cta). This can happen often with padding/margin between sections.

## Restraint and self-critique

Spend your boldness in one place. Let one element be the memorable thing, keep everything around it quiet and disciplined, and cut any decoration that does not serve the brief. Build to a quality floor without announcing it: responsive down to mobile, visible keyboard focus, reduced motion respected, visually accessible, harmonious color palettes. Critique your own work as you build, taking screenshots to review if your environment supports it — a picture is worth 1000 tokens. Consider Chanel's advice: before leaving the house, take a look in the mirror and remove one accessory. Human creatives have memory and always try to do something new, so if you have a space to quickly jot down notes about what you've tried, it can help you in future passes.

## More on writing in design

Words appear in a design for one reason: to make it easier to understand and use. They are design content, not decoration. Bring the same intentionality and minimalism to copywriting that you would bring to spacing and color. Before writing anything, ask what the design needs to say, and how it can best be said to help the person navigate the experience.

Write from the end user's perspective. Name things by what users will understand in simple language, not by how the system is built. A user manages notifications, not webhook config. Describe what something is or does in plain terms rather than selling it. Being specific and legible to new users is always better than being clever.

Use active voice as default. A CTA says exactly what happens when it is used: "Save changes," not "Submit." An action keeps the same name through the whole flow, so the button that says "Publish" produces a toast that says "Published." The vocabulary of an interface is the signposting for someone navigating the product. Cohesion and consistency are how people learn their way around.

Treat failure and emptiness as moments for direction, not mood. Explain what went wrong and how to fix it, in the interface's voice rather than a person's. Errors don't apologize, and they are never vague about what happened. An empty screen is an invitation to act.

Keep the tone conversational: plain verbs, sentence case, no filler, with tone matched to the brand and the audience. Let each written element do exactly one job.

import { cellKey, type Cell, type TurnState, type UIState } from './events';
import type { Violation } from './rules';

export type Severity = 1 | 2 | 3 | 4;

export type Finding = {
  severity: Severity;
  kind: 'invariant' | 'new_edge' | 'new_external' | 'unplanned' | 'planned';
  cell: Cell | null;
  text: string;
  files: string[];
  invariant?: string;
};

export type TurnLedger = {
  turn: string;
  linesChanged: number | null; // null until turn_ended brings the git numstat
  cellsToReview: number;
  forksCaughtBeforeCode: number;
  rejectedOptionsBlocked: number;
  findings: Finding[];
};

export type Ledger = {
  turns: TurnLedger[];
  session: { linesChanged: number; cellsToReview: number; forksCaughtBeforeCode: number; rejectedOptionsBlocked: number };
};

const vkey = (v: Violation) => `${v.invariant}|${v.file}|${v.target ?? ''}`;

function cellOf(s: UIState, turn: TurnState, file: string): Cell | null {
  const p = s.files[file];
  if (p?.kind === 'cell') return { domain: p.domain, layer: p.layer };
  const edited = Object.entries(turn.edited).find(([, c]) => c.files.includes(file));
  if (edited) { const [domain, layer] = edited[0].split('/') as [string, string]; return { domain, layer }; }
  return Object.values(turn.planned).find((c) => c.files.includes(file))?.cell ?? null;
}

/** Severity-ranked findings for one turn (SPEC §9): 1 invariant hit · 2 new edge / new external · 3 unplanned · 4 planned. */
export function turnFindings(s: UIState, turn: TurnState): Finding[] {
  const out: Finding[] = [];
  const seen = new Set<string>();
  for (const { v } of turn.violationsSeen) {
    if (seen.has(vkey(v))) continue;
    seen.add(vkey(v));
    out.push({ severity: 1, kind: 'invariant', cell: cellOf(s, turn, v.file), text: v.reason, files: [v.file], invariant: v.invariant });
  }
  const edges = new Map<string, { from: string; to: string; files: string[] }>();
  for (const e of turn.edgesAdded) {
    const k = `${e.from}->${e.to}`;
    const cur = edges.get(k) ?? { from: e.from, to: e.to, files: [] };
    if (!cur.files.includes(e.edge.from)) cur.files.push(e.edge.from);
    edges.set(k, cur);
  }
  for (const e of edges.values()) {
    const cell = cellOf(s, turn, e.files[0]!);
    out.push({ severity: 2, kind: 'new_edge', cell, text: `New dependency: ${name(s, e.from)} → ${name(s, e.to)}`, files: e.files });
  }
  const hasPlan = Object.keys(turn.planned).length > 0;
  for (const [k, c] of Object.entries(turn.edited)) {
    const [domain, layer] = k.split('/') as [string, string];
    const cell = { domain, layer };
    if (layer === 'external' && c.created.length) {
      out.push({ severity: 2, kind: 'new_external', cell, text: `New external service in ${name(s, domain)}`, files: c.created });
    }
    if (hasPlan && !turn.planned[k]) {
      out.push({ severity: 3, kind: 'unplanned', cell, text: `Edited ${name(s, domain)} · ${layer} without planning it`, files: c.files });
    } else {
      out.push({ severity: 4, kind: 'planned', cell, text: `${name(s, domain)} · ${layer}: ${c.files.length} file(s), +${c.added} −${c.removed}`, files: c.files });
    }
  }
  for (const file of turn.unassigned) {
    if (hasPlan && !Object.values(turn.planned).some((c) => c.files.includes(file))) {
      out.push({ severity: 3, kind: 'unplanned', cell: null, text: `Edited ${file}, which belongs to no domain`, files: [file] });
    }
  }
  return out.sort((a, b) => a.severity - b.severity);
}

function name(s: UIState, domain: string) {
  return s.map?.domains.find((d) => d.id === domain)?.name ?? domain;
}

export function turnLedger(s: UIState, turn: TurnState): TurnLedger {
  const findings = turnFindings(s, turn);
  const review = new Set(findings.filter((f) => f.severity <= 3).map((f) => (f.cell ? cellKey(f.cell) : `file:${f.files[0]}`)));
  // A fork counts once per distinct plan violation it resolved, if it was answered before any edit in the turn.
  let forks = 0;
  for (const f of turn.forks) {
    if (f.answered === null || !f.beforeCode) continue;
    forks += new Set(f.violations.map(vkey).filter((k) => turn.violationsSeen.some((x) => x.source === 'plan' && vkey(x.v) === k))).size;
  }
  // A rejected option is blocked when a violation cites a decision, or when the plan avoids it citing one (beat 4) —
  // but only decisions made in an earlier turn: avoiding what you just decided is the fork itself, counted above.
  const earlier = (id: string | undefined) => !!id && s.decisions.some((d) => d.id === id && d.turn !== turn.id);
  const rejected = new Set([
    ...turn.violationsSeen.filter((x) => earlier(x.v.decision)).map((x) => `${x.v.decision}|${x.v.file}`),
    ...(turn.avoided ?? []).filter((a) => earlier(a.decision)).map((a) => `${a.decision}|${a.from}->${a.to}`),
  ]).size;
  return {
    turn: turn.id,
    linesChanged: turn.numstat ? turn.numstat.added + turn.numstat.removed : null,
    cellsToReview: review.size,
    forksCaughtBeforeCode: forks,
    rejectedOptionsBlocked: rejected,
    findings,
  };
}

export function ledger(s: UIState): Ledger {
  const turns = s.turns.map((t) => turnLedger(s, t));
  const sum = (f: (t: TurnLedger) => number) => turns.reduce((a, t) => a + f(t), 0);
  return {
    turns,
    session: {
      linesChanged: sum((t) => t.linesChanged ?? 0),
      cellsToReview: sum((t) => t.cellsToReview),
      forksCaughtBeforeCode: sum((t) => t.forksCaughtBeforeCode),
      rejectedOptionsBlocked: sum((t) => t.rejectedOptionsBlocked),
    },
  };
}
import { withExtra, type Exists, type FactDelta, type ImportEdge } from './facts';
import { isRelative, normalizePath, resolveImport, resolvePath } from './imports';
import { createMapper, type Mapper } from './mapper';
import { check, type Violation } from './rules';
import type { DomainMap } from './schema';

/** One step of a `submit_plan` call. Import `to` is a repo path (extension optional) or a specifier relative to `from`. */
/** `symbols`: optional `path#qualified.name` ids the step changes or adds (drives symbol-level ghosts). */
export type PlanStep = { n: number; text: string; files: string[]; imports: { from: string; to: string }[]; symbols?: string[] };

export type PlanFootprint = {
  cells: { domain: string; layer: string; steps: number[]; files: string[] }[];
  tests: { domain: string; files: string[] }[];
  unassigned: string[];
  edges: { from: string; to: string; steps: number[]; imports: ImportEdge[] }[];
  delta: FactDelta;
  violations: Violation[];
};

/** Ghost footprint of a plan: the cells and tests it touches, its new cross-domain edges, and the violations its imports would cause. */
export function planFootprint(map: DomainMap, steps: PlanStep[], exists: Exists, mapper: Mapper = createMapper(map)): PlanFootprint {
  const norm = (p: string) => normalizePath(p) ?? p;

// packages/core/src/journeys/provider-paths.ts (exported from @harness/core/view) against the `ProviderPaths` contract.
// Swap the import in ./trace.ts (`providerPaths`) for the core one and delete this file. Same signature, same output type;
// this version only looks one import hop deep, which is enough to draw beat 1's three classes on Scout.
import type { ContextGraph, DomainMap, ProviderPath, ProviderPaths, Violation } from '@harness/core/view';

const PROVIDER_PKG = /(^|\/)(@anthropic-ai\/sdk|openai|@google\/genai)$/;

export const providerPaths: ProviderPaths = (graph: ContextGraph, map: DomainMap, violations: readonly Violation[]): ProviderPath[] => {
  const via = map.invariants.find((i) => i.kind === 'only_via');
  const gateway = via && via.kind === 'only_via' ? via.allowed_from[0] ?? 'gateway' : 'gateway';
  const isProviderFile = (id: string) => /^vendor\/llm-[^/]+\//.test(id) && graph.nodes[id]?.kind === 'file';
  const isProviderPkg = (id: string) => id.startsWith('vendor:') && PROVIDER_PKG.test(id.slice(7));
  const out: ProviderPath[] = [];
  const seen = new Set<string>();
  for (const e of graph.edges) {
    if (e.kind !== 'imports' && e.kind !== 'uses') continue;
    const sink = isProviderFile(e.to) || isProviderPkg(e.to);
    if (!sink || isProviderFile(e.from)) continue;
    const from = graph.nodes[e.from];
    if (!from) continue;
    const v = violations.find((x) => x.file === e.from && (!x.target || x.target === e.to));
    const cls = from.domain === gateway ? 'gateway' : v ? 'violation' : 'uncosted';
    const key = `${e.from}|${e.to}`;
    if (seen.has(key)) continue;
    seen.add(key);
    if (cls !== 'gateway') { out.push({ class: cls, nodes: [e.from, e.to], provider: e.to, ...(v ? { invariant: v.invariant } : {}) }); continue; }
    // Through the gateway: start where callers enter it (code outside the gateway importing the gateway file that imports this one).
    const importers = (to: string) => graph.edges.filter((x) => x.kind === 'imports' && x.to === to).map((x) => x.from);
    const entries = importers(e.from).filter((y) => graph.nodes[y]?.domain === gateway)
      .flatMap((y) => importers(y).filter((x) => { const n = graph.nodes[x]; return !!n?.domain && n.domain !== gateway && n.layer !== 'ui'; }).map((x) => [x, y]));
    if (!entries.length) out.push({ class: 'gateway', nodes: [e.from, e.to], provider: e.to });
    for (const [x, y] of entries) out.push({ class: 'gateway', nodes: [x!, y!, e.from, e.to], provider: e.to });
  }
  return out.sort((a, b) => (a.nodes.join() < b.nodes.join() ? -1 : 1));
};

But to keep filing figures intact, it skipped anything after a `$` and didn't count commas as part of a number. It also never counted `/` or `_`. So numbers like `4532/1234/5678`, `1234_5678_9012` and `123,456,789` reached the model unchanged. ⏎  ⏎ **What changed:** ⏎ - **`src/gateway/redact.ts`:** by default, any 7+ digit number with any of those separators is replaced. Phone-shaped ones (at most 11 digits, phone separators only) become `[PHONE_n]`; everything else, such as account and card numbers, becomes `[NUMBER_n]`. A comma only joins digits when one comes right after it, so a list like `1234567, 7654321` stays two numbers. My first version merged those into one; a test caught it. ⏎ - **Filing mode:** `complete()` in `src/gateway/complete.ts` takes `mode: "filing"`, and `src/tools/filing-summarize.ts` uses it. In that mode `$` amounts and comma-grouped figures pass through as before, which keeps your earlier decision that filings keep their figures. Emails, phone numbers and names are still redacted in filing mode, and a new test checks that. ⏎ - **Note to the model:** the placeholder note it gets now lists `[NUMBER_1]` too. ⏎ - **Tests:** the account-number formats above are covered. The "keeps financial figures" test now runs in filing mode, and the filing tool's test also checks that no `[NUMBER_` tokens are sent. ⏎  ⏎ **Trade-off:** outside filing mode, large dollar figures are redacted as well, because that's what "every long number" means. For example, `$2,148,900,000` revenue in the brief prompt becomes `$[NUMBER_1]`. And a 7–11 digit amount with no commas, like `$1234567890`, gets the `[PHONE_n]` label, since it's still matched by shape.
