```typescript
// Tier 1 for Python and Go (N11): web-tree-sitter (pinned runtime + grammars from @vscode/tree-sitter-wasm) producing
// the same FileFacts as TypeScript, the same gate facts, and a graph that traces from a route to a table.
import { beforeAll, describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { deltaForEdit, fileExistsIn, scanRepoFacts } from '../src/facts';
import { check } from '../src/rules';
import { parseDomainMap } from '../src/schema';
import { buildGraph, trace } from '../src/graph';
import { diffSymbols } from '../src/facts/diff';
import { diskLangContext, extractTreeSitter, initTreeSitter, treeSitterReady } from '../src/facts/treesitter';
import type { FileFacts } from '../src/contracts/facts';

const PY = fileURLToPath(new URL('./fixture-py', import.meta.url));
const GO = fileURLToPath(new URL('./fixture-go', import.meta.url));
const map = parseDomainMap(`version: 1
layers: [{ id: entry, name: Entry }, { id: logic, name: Logic }, { id: data, name: Data }]
domains:
  - { id: api, name: API, purpose: HTTP, cells: { entry: { paths: ["app/api/**", "app/main.py", "app/legacy/**", "internal/api/**", "cmd/**"] } } }
  - { id: core, name: Core, purpose: Runs and storage, cells: { logic: { paths: ["app/services/**"] }, data: { paths: ["app/models.py", "app/db.py", "internal/store/**"], tables: [runs, cost_log] } } }
invariants:
  - { id: DR-1, rule: Storage never depends on the API, kind: no_edge, from: core, to: api, exceptions: [] }
  - { id: DR-2, rule: Only core writes runs, kind: owns_writes, owners: { runs: core }, exceptions: [] }
`);

beforeAll(async () => { await initTreeSitter(); });

const summary = (f: FileFacts) => ({
  imports: f.imports.map((i) => i.to),
  symbols: f.symbols.map((s) => `${s.kind} ${s.name}${s.exported ? '' : ' (private)'}`),
  calls: f.calls.map((c) => `${c.from} -> ${c.to}`),
  routes: f.routes.map((r) => `${r.id} => ${r.handler}`),
  entries: f.entries.map((e) => e.id),
  writes: f.writes.map((w) => `${w.table} ${w.symbol} ${w.via}`),
  reads: (f.reads ?? []).map((w) => `${w.table} ${w.symbol} ${w.via}`),
});

describe('Python (FastAPI, Flask, SQLAlchemy, Django)', () => {
  const scan = () => scanRepoFacts(PY, map);

  it('is loaded once and parses synchronously', () => {
    expect(treeSitterReady()).toBe(true);
  });

  it('imports resolve to repo modules (absolute, relative, package submodules), else vendor packages', () => {
    const { fileFacts, imports } = scan();
    expect(summary(fileFacts['app/main.py']!).imports).toEqual(['vendor:fastapi', 'app/api/runs.py', 'app/db.py', 'vendor:uvicorn']);
    expect(summary(fileFacts['app/services/runner.py']!).imports).toEqual(['vendor:anthropic', 'app/db.py', 'app/models.py']);
    expect(imports).toContainEqual({ from: 'app/api/runs.py', to: 'app/services/runner.py' });
    expect(imports.some((i) => i.to.startsWith('vendor:'))).toBe(false); // gate facts: repo files only
  });

  it('symbols, calls through import bindings (aliases, modules, self), routes and entries', () => {
    const { fileFacts } = scan();
    const runner = summary(fileFacts['app/services/runner.py']!);
    expect(runner.symbols).toEqual(['function start_run', 'class Planner', 'method Planner.plan', 'method Planner.score', 'function _private (private)']);
    expect(runner.calls).toEqual(expect.arrayContaining([
      'app/services/runner.py#start_run -> app/models.py#Run',
      'app/services/runner.py#start_run -> app/services/runner.py#Planner',
      'app/services/runner.py#Planner.plan -> app/services/runner.py#Planner.score',
      'app/services/runner.py -> vendor:anthropic',
    ]));
    const runs = summary(fileFacts['app/api/runs.py']!);
    expect(runs.calls).toContain('app/api/runs.py#create_run -> app/services/runner.py#start_run'); // `start_run as begin`
    expect(runs.routes).toEqual(['route:POST /api/runs => app/api/runs.py#create_run', 'route:GET /api/runs/{} => app/api/runs.py#get_run']);
    expect(runs.entries).toEqual(['entry:route:POST /api/runs', 'entry:route:GET /api/runs/{}']);
    expect(summary(fileFacts['app/legacy/views.py']!).routes).toEqual(['route:GET /legacy/{} => app/legacy/views.py#item', 'route:DELETE /legacy/{} => app/legacy/views.py#item']);
    expect(summary(fileFacts['app/main.py']!).entries).toEqual(['entry:main:app/main.py']);
  });

  it('writes and reads: SQLAlchemy session.add(Model(...)), Django Model.objects…, raw SQL; table names from __tablename__ / Meta.db_table', () => {
    const { fileFacts, writes } = scan();
    expect(summary(fileFacts['app/services/runner.py']!).writes).toEqual(['runs app/services/runner.py#start_run sqlalchemy', 'cost_log app/services/runner.py#start_run sqlalchemy']);
    expect(summary(fileFacts['app/legacy/views.py']!).writes).toEqual(['legacy_items app/legacy/views.py#item django', 'audit_log app/legacy/views.py#item sql']);
    expect(summary(fileFacts['app/api/runs.py']!).reads).toEqual(['runs app/api/runs.py#get_run django']);
    expect(writes).toContainEqual({ file: 'app/services/runner.py', table: 'runs' });
  });

  it('the gate sees Python imports and writes (same checker)', () => {
    const exists = fileExistsIn(PY);
    const old = readFileSync(`${PY}/app/models.py`, 'utf8');
    const delta = deltaForEdit('app/models.py', old, `from app.api.runs import router\n${old}`, exists);
    expect(delta.imports).toEqual([{ from: 'app/models.py', to: 'app/api/runs.py' }]);
    expect(check(map, delta).map((v) => `${v.invariant} ${v.detail}`)).toEqual(['DR-1 app/models.py → app/api/runs.py']);
    const views = readFileSync(`${PY}/app/legacy/views.py`, 'utf8');
    const w = deltaForEdit('app/legacy/views.py', views, views.replace('return "ok"', 'cursor.execute("UPDATE runs SET x = 1")\n    return "ok"'), exists);
    expect(check(map, w).map((v) => `${v.invariant} ${v.detail}`)).toEqual(['DR-2 app/legacy/views.py writes "runs"']);
  });

  it('symbol diffs work on Python (body vs signature)', () => {
    const ctx = diskLangContext(PY);
    const src = readFileSync(`${PY}/app/services/runner.py`, 'utf8');
    const a = extractTreeSitter('app/services/runner.py', src, ctx).facts;
    const b = extractTreeSitter('app/services/runner.py', src.replace('return len(goal)', 'return len(goal) * 2').replace('def plan(self, goal)', 'def plan(self, goal, depth=1)'), ctx).facts;
    const d = diffSymbols(a.symbols, b.symbols);
    expect(d.sig).toEqual(['app/services/runner.py#Planner.plan']);
    expect(d.body).toEqual(expect.arrayContaining(['app/services/runner.py#Planner', 'app/services/runner.py#Planner.score']));
    expect(extractTreeSitter('x.py', 'def broken(:\n', ctx).parsed).toBe(false);
  });

  it('the graph traces a route to its table through the handler and the service', () => {
    const { fileFacts } = scan();
    const g = buildGraph(map, fileFacts);
    expect(trace(g, 'route:POST /api/runs', ['table:runs'])).toEqual([['route:POST /api/runs', 'app/api/runs.py#create_run', 'app/services/runner.py#start_run', 'table:runs']]);
  });
});

describe('Go (net/http, chi, gin, database/sql)', () => {

    expect(summary(fileFacts['internal/api/routes.go']!).imports).toEqual(['vendor:net/http', 'internal/store/store.go', 'vendor:github.com/gin-gonic/gin', 'vendor:github.com/go-chi/chi/v5']);
    expect(imports).toContainEqual({ from: 'internal/api/routes.go', to: 'internal/store/store.go' });

    const routes = summary(fileFacts['internal/api/routes.go']!);
```

```bash
async function playFlow(file: string) {
  const st = useStore.getState();

  st.setRepo('scout-agent');

  const at = params.get('at');
  if (!params.has('play')) {

    return;
  }
  const from = params.get('from');
  let start = events.findIndex((e) => e.kind === 'turn_started' && (!from || e.turn === from));
  if (start < 0) start = events.length;
  st.hello(events.slice(0, start), false);
  const speed = Number(params.get('speed') ?? '1') || 1;
  const auto = params.get('auto');
  await sleep(Number(params.get('delay') ?? '1200'));
  st.setBusy(true);
  for (let i = start; i < events.length; i++) {
    const e = events[i]!;
    const prev = events[i - 1];
    if (e.pause) {
      st.setBusy(false);
      await new Promise<void>((r) => {
        resumeFake = r;
        if (auto) setTimeout(r, Number(auto) || 2500);
      });
      resumeFake = null;
      st.setBusy(true);
    } else if (prev && e.kind !== 'turn_started') {
      await sleep(Math.max(0, Math.min(4000, (e.t - prev.t) / speed)));
    } else if (prev) {
      await sleep(Math.min(2500, 1500 / speed));
    }
    const { pause: _p, ...clean } = e;
    useStore.getState().append(clean as HarnessEvent);
  }
  useStore.getState().setBusy(false);
}

const sleep = (ms: number) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms));

async function post(path: string, body?: unknown) {
```

```text
        let cell = cells.get(key);
        if (!cell) cells.set(key, (cell = { domain: p.domain, layer: p.layer, steps: new Set(), files: new Set() }));
        cell.steps.add(step.n);
        cell.files.add(file);
      } else if (p.kind === 'test') {

    for (const imp of stepImports) {

      if (!seen.has(k)) {
        seen.add(k);
        imports.push(imp);
      }
      const a = mapper.place(imp.from);
      const b = mapper.place(imp.to);
      if (a.kind !== 'cell' || b.kind !== 'cell' || a.domain === b.domain) continue;
      const key = `${a.domain}\u0000${b.domain}`;
      let edge = edges.get(key);

      if (!edge.imports.some((i) => i.from === imp.from && i.to === imp.to)) edge.imports.push(imp);
```

```typescript
// Dev only. Recorded-style logs for the map-first prototype (`?ui=flow&fake=flow-beat1|flow-beat3|flow-beat4&play`),
// built on the load events of a real Scout copy (flow-base-events.json: map, scan with Tier 1 facts, violations,
// journeys and Tier 2 facts, captured from `apps/server` with the cartographer, labels, auditor and Alike off).
// Plans go through the real `planFootprint` (so the fork's violation and options are the checker's own); edits carry
// `facts_changed` like the server's. Events marked `pause` wait for you during playback (fork, Build).
//
//   npx tsx apps/shell/scripts/flow-events.ts
import { readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { dirname, join } from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import {
  createMapper, planFootprint,
  type DomainMap, type EventData, type EventKind, type FileFacts, type HarnessEvent, type PlanStep, type Violation,
} from '@harness/core';

const here = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
const base = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(here, 'flow-base-events.json'), 'utf8')) as HarnessEvent[];
const map = (base.find((e) => e.kind === 'map_confirmed')!.data as EventData['map_confirmed']).map as DomainMap;
const scan = base.find((e) => e.kind === 'repo_scanned')!.data as EventData['repo_scanned'];
const mapper = createMapper(map);
const facts: Record<string, FileFacts> = Object.fromEntries((scan.fileFacts ?? []).map((f) => [f.path, f]));
const S1 = base[0]!.session;

type Ev = HarnessEvent & { pause?: string };

class Log {
  out: Ev[];
  t: number;
  n = 0;
  session = S1;
  turn: string | null = null;
  known = new Set(scan.files.map((f) => f.path));
  constructor(private tag: string) {
    this.out = [...base];
    this.t = (base.at(-1)?.t ?? 0) + 5000;
  }
  ev<K extends EventKind>(kind: K, data: K extends keyof EventData ? EventData[K] : never, o: { path?: string; gap?: number; pause?: string } = {}) {
    this.t += o.gap ?? 900;
    const p = o.path ? mapper.place(o.path) : null;
    const cell = p && p.kind === 'cell' ? { domain: p.domain, layer: p.layer } : undefined;
    const e: Ev = { id: `${this.tag}-${String(++this.n).padStart(3, '0')}`, t: this.t, session: this.session, turn: this.turn, kind, data: data as Record<string, unknown> };
    if (o.path) e.path = o.path;
    if (cell) e.cell = cell;
    if (o.pause) e.pause = o.pause;
    this.out.push(e);
  }
  start(turn: string, session: string, prompt: string) {
    this.turn = turn;
    this.session = session;
    this.ev('turn_started', { prompt, head: 'demo-start', baseline: 'demo-start' }, { gap: 0 });
    this.ev('chat', { role: 'user', text: prompt }, { gap: 60 });
  }
  read(path: string, gap = 900) {
    this.ev('looked', { tool: 'Read' }, { path, gap });
  }
  note(id: string, node: string, text: string, tone: EventData['annotation']['tone'] = 'note', gap = 650) {
    this.ev('annotation', { id, node, text, tone }, { gap });
  }
  say(text: string, gap = 900) {
    this.ev('chat', { role: 'assistant', text }, { gap });
  }
  /** A plan through the real footprint; its violations follow as `plan_violation`s. */
  plan(steps: PlanStep[], avoided?: EventData['planned']['avoided'], gap = 1400): Violation[] {
    const fp = planFootprint(map, steps, (p) => this.known.has(p) || !!facts[p]);
    this.ev('planned', { steps, cells: fp.cells, edges: fp.edges, unassigned: fp.unassigned, ...(avoided ? { avoided } : {}) }, { gap });
    for (const v of fp.violations) this.ev('plan_violation', { violation: v }, { gap: 40 });
    return fp.violations;
  }
  edit(path: string, added: number, removed: number, o: { created?: boolean; imports?: string[]; symbols?: string[]; gap?: number } = {}) {
    this.ev('cursor', { verb: 'editing' }, { path, gap: o.gap ?? 700 });
    this.ev('edited', { added, removed, created: !!o.created, tool: o.created ? 'Write' : 'Edit', ...(o.symbols ? { symbols: { added: [], removed: [], sig: [], body: o.symbols, renamed: [] } } : {}) }, { path, gap: 1200 });
    if (o.imports || o.created) {
      const prev = facts[path];
      const imports = [...(prev?.imports ?? []), ...(o.imports ?? []).filter((to) => !prev?.imports.some((i) => i.to === to)).map((to) => ({ to, typeOnly: false }))];
      const next: FileFacts = { path, hash: `${this.tag}-${this.n}`, imports, writes: prev?.writes ?? [], symbols: prev?.symbols ?? [], calls: prev?.calls ?? [], routes: prev?.routes ?? [], entries: prev?.entries ?? [], ...(prev?.reads ? { reads: prev.reads } : {}) };
      facts[path] = next;
      this.known.add(path);
      this.ev('facts_changed', { facts: next }, { path, gap: 20 });
      for (const to of o.imports ?? []) {
        const a = mapper.place(path);
        const b = mapper.place(to);
        if (a.kind === 'cell' && b.kind === 'cell' && a.domain !== b.domain) this.ev('edge_added', { edge: { from: path, to }, from: a.domain, to: b.domain }, { gap: 20 });
      }
    }
  }
  end(files: string[], gap = 700) {
    let added = 0;
    let removed = 0;
    for (const e of this.out) if (e.turn === this.turn && e.kind === 'edited') { added += (e.data as EventData['edited']).added; removed += (e.data as EventData['edited']).removed; }
    this.ev('turn_ended', { added, removed, files, reason: 'success' }, { gap });
  }
  write(name: string) {
    writeFileSync(join(here, `../public/${name}-events.json`), JSON.stringify(this.out));
    console.log(`${this.out.length} events → public/${name}-events.json`);
  }
}

const FS = 'src/tools/filing-summarize.ts';
const TS = 'src/tools/transcript-summarize.ts';
const ANTHROPIC = 'vendor/llm-anthropic/index.ts';
const SDK = 'vendor:@anthropic-ai/sdk';
const DR4 = 'Filings go through the gateway, in a filing mode that keeps figures intact';

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- beat 1: a question, answered on the map
function beat1(l: Log) {
  l.start('t-beat1', S1, "Describe Scout's architecture, and anything risky or over-engineered.");
  l.read('src/channels/routes.ts', 1400);
  l.note('doors', 'src/channels/routes.ts', 'Eleven routes and a CLI: two doors into one run loop');
  l.read('src/orchestrator/agent.ts');
  l.note('loop', 'src/orchestrator/agent.ts', 'Plans each run, then calls tools in order through the registry');
  l.read('src/orchestrator/tool-registry.ts', 800);
  l.read('src/gateway/complete.ts');
  l.note('door', 'src/gateway/complete.ts', 'The one door the design intends: redact, then log the cost');
  l.read('src/tools/news-summarize.ts', 1000);
  l.note('bypass', 'src/tools/news-summarize.ts', "Calls Claude directly: the contact's name goes out unredacted and uncosted", 'finding');
  l.read('vendor/search/index.ts', 1000);
  l.note('search', 'vendor/search/index.ts', 'Uses the Anthropic SDK itself, so web searches never reach cost_log', 'finding');
  l.read('vendor/news/index.ts', 700);
  l.read('vendor/llm-openai/index.ts', 800);
  l.note('openai', 'vendor/llm-openai/index.ts', 'A second provider nothing selects by default: keep it?', 'question');
  l.ev('highlight', {
    nodes: ['src/tools/web-search.ts', 'src/gateway/complete.ts', 'src/gateway/providers.ts', ANTHROPIC, SDK, 'src/tools/news-summarize.ts', 'vendor/search/index.ts', 'vendor/news/index.ts'],
```

```mjs
  if (a.wait) await page.waitForTimeout(a.wait);
  if (a.waitFor) await page.waitForSelector(a.waitFor, { timeout: a.timeout ?? 60000 });
  if (a.shot) await page.screenshot({ path: a.shot });
}
await page.screenshot({ path: out });
if (logs.length) console.log(logs.slice(0, 10).join('\n'));
await browser.close();
```

  For each kept file, the protected symbols are what the turn added or changed there: `added`, `sig`, `body`, and the new name of a rename. Removed symbols and `<cbN>` callbacks are never included. A file with no such symbol is protected whole.
  
  `recordProtects` (in `decisions.ts`) writes `protects:` into the DR front matter, commits only that file, and re-emits `decision_recorded { protects }`. `recordFork` now also writes `session:` into the DR file.
  
  **A plan step touches protected code when:**
  - it names a protected symbol, or one containing it or inside it;
  - or it edits or names anything in a whole-file protection;
  - or it edits a file holding protected symbols without naming any symbol in that file.
  
  Naming only other symbols in that file does not touch it.
  
  **An edit touches protected code when:**
  - its symbol diff changes a protected symbol (`sig`, `body`, `removed`, or the old name of a rename);
  - or the file is protected whole;
  - or it changed code outside every symbol span. Imports and comments don't count.
  
  The third case exists because Tier 1 lists no symbol for module-level consts like `PHONE_PATTERN`, so beat 4's widening would otherwise produce an empty diff.
  
  **What a touch does:**
  - `submit_plan` emits `decision_touched { source: 'plan', step }` and adds "This plan touches what DR-n protects: <title>. <outcome>. Keep it true (decided in session N): scope the change so it still holds, and extend its test." It is never a block or a fork.
  - The PostToolUse hook is now synchronous. It returns `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext` once per decision per turn; I checked in `sdk.d.ts` that this field is honoured only on synchronous responses.
  - The brief lists each decision's protected code.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-11 23:07:34Z)**_

Mostly yes, with a few things to know.

**What reloads by itself:** Scout's server code. Both copies serve Scout with `npm run dev:api`:
- `../scout-run` via `npm run demo`;
- `../scout-cc` via the command I gave you.

That uses `tsx watch`, which restarts the API within a second or two whenever a file it loads changes, including new files the agent wires in. Every planned beat is a server-side change (the gateway's redaction, a new tool, cost recording), so you don't need to restart or rebuild anything.

**What doesn't happen automatically:**
1. **Results only change in new research runs.** Old runs in the database keep their old output. After the change, start a fresh Symbotic run (about 75 s) and look at that one.
2. **The goal has to call the new tool.** Tools are picked by the planner and by words in the goal, so for beat 3's after shot write something like "Prep for the renewal call; check recent news and their latest 10-K". A plain "check recent news" won't run the 10-K tool.
3. **Some pages need a manual refresh.** A run's page and the research list update themselves while a run is going. The Model usage page (beat 2's "Web search" row) doesn't, so refresh it after the new run.
4. **Don't let the agent edit while a run is in progress.** The server restart kills a run mid-flight, and it stays stuck as "Researching". Run the research after the agent finishes.
5. **UI changes need a rebuild.** If an agent ever edits the web app itself (none of the planned beats should), run `npm run build` in that copy and refresh the browser. New tools show up in the trail without any UI change.
6. **Schema changes need a manual restart.** `schema.sql` isn't watched, and existing tables aren't altered. That only matters for the optional "encrypt phone numbers" beat, which also needs a migration.

So the routine after each change is: wait for the agent to finish, then start a new research run whose goal mentions what you just built.

```bash
const NOTE_S = 1.45;

export function placeNotes(frame: FlowFrame, o: FlowOverlay): NotePlace[] {
  const placed: NotePlace[] = [];
  const nodes = frame.nodes;
  const hit = (r: Box, list: Box[]) => list.some((q) => r.x < q.x + q.w && r.x + r.w > q.x && r.y < q.y + q.h && r.y + r.h > q.y);

}
```

Right on the main point: plain Claude Code started with `--safe-mode` can't get DR-4 from Alike. Safe mode switches off its hooks and MCP servers, so nothing from Alike can reach that session. (With capture still off, Alike's hooks are silent anyway.) Interpretability doesn't rely on Alike for this either: it puts DR-4 in front of Claude from the repo's `decisions/` folder. Alike only matters for the teammate moment.

Two caveats:
- **The decision is still in the repo as a file.** The copy contains `decisions/DR-4.md` and beat 3's test. Plain Claude Code could stumble on either and avoid the trap. That's honest ("a decision in a file only helps if the agent happens to read it"), but rehearse it.
- **Beat 1 needs no second repo,** as you said: it's read-only.

**Beat 4 from one copy works too, with two steps:**
1. **Stop Interpretability while recording take A.** Otherwise its file watcher records plain Claude Code's edits into the session as unexplained edits, polluting the map and ledger for take B. Since `npm run demo` also stops Scout's app, run that alone during take A: `cd ../scout-run && PORT=8788 npm run dev:api`.
2. **Reset to the checkpoint before take B.** Plain Claude Code's edits need undoing:
   ```
   git -C ../scout-run reset -q --hard && git -C ../scout-run clean -fdq -e .harness
   ```
   This assumes you made the "checkpoint after beat 3" commit. The broken research run from take A stays in the app's history, which you can leave or ignore.

The separate `../scout-cc` already exists and avoids both steps, at the cost of one sync command and a second app on :8789. Either works. If you'd rather go single-copy as you said, I'll delete `../scout-cc` and change the plan's beat 4 comparison to the stop-then-reset steps above. Which do you prefer?

```text
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# One command for a session against Scout: a fresh copy of Scout, Scout's app on :8788,
# and the harness (:4310 server, :5173 shell) pointed at the copy.
#
# Usage: npm run demo [-- options]
#   --no-map    let the cartographer propose the map (default: start from fixtures/scout-agent.domains.yaml)
#   --replace   stop a harness that is already running on :4310 / :5173 first
#   --take N    a separate Alike repository for this take (johnz4021/scout-agent-takeN); see fresh-scout.sh
#   --with-data, --keep, --offline   passed to scripts/fresh-scout.sh
#
# Ctrl+C stops everything. Run it again for a clean slate; the original ../scout-agent is never touched.
set -euo pipefail

here="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
src="$(cd "${SCOUT_SRC:-$here/../scout-agent}" && pwd)"
run_dir="${SCOUT_RUN_DIR:-$(dirname "$src")/scout-run}"
port="${SCOUT_PORT:-8788}"
slug="${HARNESS_REPO_SLUG:-johnz4021/scout-agent}"

map="--map" replace=0 pass=()
while (( $# )); do
  case "$1" in
    --no-map) map="" ;;
    --replace) replace=1 ;;
    --take) shift; take="${1:?--take needs a value}"; pass+=(--take "$take") ;;
    --take=*) take="${1#--take=}"; pass+=(--take "$take") ;;
    -h|--help) sed -n '2,12p' "$0"; exit 0 ;;
    *) pass+=("$1") ;;
  esac
  shift
done
[[ -z "${take:-}" ]] || slug="johnz4021/scout-agent-take$take"

listening() { lsof -nP -iTCP:"$1" -sTCP:LISTEN -t 2>/dev/null || true; }

busy=""
for p in 4310 5173; do [[ -n "$(listening "$p")" ]] && busy="$busy :$p"; done
if [[ -n "$busy" ]]; then
  if (( replace )); then
    echo "stopping the harness already running on$busy"
    for p in 4310 5173; do pids="$(listening "$p")"; [[ -z "$pids" ]] || kill $pids 2>/dev/null || true; done
    sleep 1
  else
    echo "A harness is already running on$busy (maybe another session's)." >&2
    echo "Stop it, or run: npm run demo -- --replace" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
fi

SCOUT_RUN_DIR="$run_dir" SCOUT_PORT="$port" "$here/scripts/fresh-scout.sh" ${map:+"$map"} ${pass[@]+"${pass[@]}"} >/dev/null
echo "fresh Scout ready at $run_dir (from demo-start)"
echo "  Scout app  http://localhost:$port"
echo "  Interpretability    http://localhost:5173"
echo

cd "$here"
exec npx concurrently -k -n scout,harness -c green,blue \
  "cd '$run_dir' && PORT=$port npm run --silent dev:api" \
  "HARNESS_REPO='$run_dir' HARNESS_REPO_SLUG='$slug' npm run dev"
```
</details></tool-use>

Here's an overview you can talk through. I checked it against what's in the shell today, and the honest status of each piece is at the end.

## The idea in one breath

"You still program in plain language, but you read, point and decide on a live map of the system instead of a transcript. The agent works on the same map. That's the visual programming: not drawing boxes, but steering the design where you can see it."

## The loop, which is the spine of the talk

1. **Ask:** type a question or request in chat.
2. **Plan:** the agent's plan appears on the map as ghost cells and edges, numbered by step, before any code exists.
3. **Steer:** shift-click the right place to redirect it, or answer an A/B fork when the plan crosses a rule.
4. **Approve:** one click on the plan card.
5. **Watch:** the ghosts fill in as edits land, an avatar shows where the agent is, line counts tick up, and anything unplanned turns amber.
6. **Remember:** your answers become decisions that live on the code and constrain future plans.

## What's on screen

| Region | What it is | What you do there |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Chat** (left) | The conversation with real Claude Code | Type requests; pointed-at nodes arrive as chips in your message |
| **Map** (centre) | Columns are product domains (Channels, Agent loop, Research tools, Model gateway, Memory, Outreach); rows are layers (UI, Entry, Logic, Data, External); edges are real dependencies between domains | Read it; double-click to go into a domain, then a file, then a function; Esc to come back up |
| **Inspector** (right) | Whatever you clicked: its files, tables, rules, and history ("added in turn 3, DR-4") | Answers "why is this here?" |
| **Ledger** (top) | Counts for the session: lines changed, cells to review, forks caught before code, rejected options blocked | Counts only, never estimated minutes |
| **Turn summary and replay** (bottom) | Findings, loudest first, and a scrubber over everything that happened | Scrub back to re-watch any turn |
| **Find** (⌘K) | Search domains, files, functions, routes, decisions and turns | Jump anywhere |

## The visual language (say it once, then it's obvious)

- **Ghost (dashed, numbered):** what the agent plans to do.
- **Filled:** what it actually changed.
- **Amber:** something it did that it didn't plan.
- **Red:** a change that crosses a rule. You see it before code exists, and the agent stops to ask.
- **Struck-through edge:** an approach you already rejected ("rejected in DR-4").
- **Avatar on a cell:** where the agent is reading or editing right now.
- **Motion only when something changes.** Nothing loops, so movement always means news.

## The agent's side (what makes this more than a dashboard)

- Claude queries the same graph you see, so its answers point at the map instead of pasting file contents.
- Its plan isn't prose. It's a list of steps naming the exact files and functions it will touch, which is why the plan can be drawn.
- Rules and your past decisions reach it at plan time, so it designs within the architecture rather than discovering it in review.

## A 45-second talk track

"On the left is Claude Code, the agent you already use. On the right is your system: product areas across, layers down, and the real dependencies between them. When I ask for something, the plan shows up here as ghosts before a line of code exists. I can see it's about to touch the model gateway and cross a rule, in red, so it stops and asks me. I answer in a sentence, approve, and watch it build: ghosts fill in, and anything it didn't plan turns amber. My answers don't disappear into chat history. They become decisions that sit on the code, so the next time anyone, or any agent, plans a change there, the design is already in the room."

## Built today vs still coming

- **Built in the shell:**
  - chat, the grid, the inspector, the ledger, turn summary and replay;
  - ghosts with step numbers, amber and red states, the fork's A/B choice, the approval card;
  - the v2 map with drill-down, breadcrumbs, the minimap, ⌘K search and keyboard navigation;
  - shift-click pointing, follow-the-agent, the struck-through rejected edge.
- **Not in the shell yet:**
  - the journey and trace overlay (beat 1; the core logic exists, but it isn't drawn yet);
  - decision markers on protected code (beat 4);
  - audit badges (beat 6);
  - the agent drawing on the map itself (annotate, highlight, focus: the events were just added to core).

Want this as a one-page visual (the layout plus the legend) that you can show while you talk, or put up as a slide?

## The one-liner

"The map isn't drawn by an AI. It's computed from the code, labelled with a confirmed map file, and animated by what the agent does."

## Three layers, each with one owner

| Layer | What it holds | Who produces it | How often |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Facts** | Every file's imports, functions, calls, database writes and reads, routes, and external services | Plain code, no AI: a fast parser (oxc for TypeScript, tree-sitter for Python and Go), plus TypeScript's own type checker in the background for precise calls | On every edit, in milliseconds |
| **Meaning** | Which folders form which product area and layer, what the areas are called, and the rules between them | A map file in the repo (`domains.yaml`). An AI "cartographer" proposes it once and you confirm; later it proposes updates when the code drifts, and you accept or reject | Once at setup, then occasionally |
| **Intent and activity** | What the agent plans, reads and edits, and what you decide | The coding agent's plan (steps naming exact files and functions), hooks on every tool call, a file watcher, and your answers | Live |

**The rule that makes it trustworthy:** facts win on structure, you win on meaning, and the agent only states intent, which is checked against the facts. Anything an AI produced (labels, proposals, audit findings) is marked as inferred.

## The pipeline (draw this on a whiteboard)

```
code ──parse──▶ facts ─┐
                       ├─▶ one graph ──▶ projection for your view ──▶ map on screen
map file ──────────────┘   (product area › layer      (what's expanded; edges
                             › file › function)         roll up to visible boxes)
                                    ▲
agent's tool calls ──hooks──▶ event log ──▶ the overlay: ghosts, fills, amber, red, cursor
```

1. **One graph.** Facts plus the map file build a single graph: repo, product area, cell, file, function, joined by edges for imports, calls and writes. Every zoom level is a view of that same graph, so nothing is maintained twice.
2. **A projection for your view.** The graph is filtered by what you've expanded and focused. Hidden detail rolls up into the nearest visible box. If something three levels down is red, the box you can see is red; status rolls up as the worst case, never an average.
3. **Rendering.** React Flow draws the boxes; ELK lays out the inside of each box. The top grid of product areas and layers is fixed, so the map never reshuffles and you don't lose your place.
4. **Live overlay.** Every tool call Claude makes passes through hooks. Each becomes an event (looked, planned, edited, blocked, decided) appended to a log in the repo. The UI is just a function of that log, which is why replay is free: it's the same log read up to an earlier point.

## Why it can be live and safe

- **No AI in the fast path.** Mapping a file, re-reading its imports and checking a rule are plain code, under about 20 ms. So the map updates before the agent's next step, and the gate can stop an edit instantly.
- **The gate uses the same facts as the picture.** What turns red is exactly what gets blocked, because it's one check used in three places: on load, on the plan, and on each edit.
- **Decisions are data, not chat.** Each decision is a file in the repo, linked in the map file and recorded in Alike. It lists the functions it protects, so when a plan or edit touches one, the marker lights up and the agent is told.

## Stack, in one sentence for judges

"A TypeScript monorepo: oxc, tree-sitter and TypeScript 7 for the facts; a Node server running real Claude Code through the Agent SDK, with hooks and a small tool server; and React with React Flow and ELK for the map, streamed over a websocket."

## 30-second talk track

"Nothing on this map is guessed. A parser reads every file and extracts the facts: who imports what, who calls what, who writes which table. That runs in milliseconds, on every edit. A small map file, which an AI proposed and I confirmed, groups those facts into product areas and layers. Then every action Claude takes passes through hooks and lands in an event log, and the map is just a live view of facts plus that log. Ghosts are its plan, fills are its edits, and red is a rule it's about to cross, checked by the same plain code that blocks the edit."
